An exact noise-filter representation explains why: a quantity computable from the graph and stepsize decides whether the endpoint is asymptotically Gaussian, and when the number of clients outgrows the inverse stepsize on networks with summable return probabilities, such as lazy tori of dimension at least three and expanders, a few recent noise terms at nearby clients keep a fixed share of local variance. On these tori the limit is a non-Gaussian local field plus an independent Gaussian consensus term, and no reference distribution built from finitely many noise moments, including Edgeworth and Cornish--Fisher corrections, is calibrated at all levels uniformly over noise laws. We propose a hybrid reference that resamples the influential noise terms from their empirical law and replaces the rest by a Gaussian; its non-asymptotic coverage bound allows noise laws and curvature estimated from fresh gradients or the client's trajectory, and extends to nonlinear vector objectives. In full-network simulations it restores tail balance at essentially unchanged interval length, also under rare large shocks that break Cornish--Fisher intervals; gains vanish, as predicted, when consensus dominates.

authors.name: Xiaoli Li, Qianqian Lei, Wei Biao Wu

papers.title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle with high-frequency and high-order partial differential equations (PDEs) due to optimization stiffness and spectral bias, despite possessing sufficient approximation capacity. Existing remedies, including modified feature representations, domain decomposition, higher floating-point precision, and curvature-aware optimizers, can improve convergence but largely act as workarounds for optimization difficulties arising from deep architectures rather than addressing their underlying source. We investigate Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions, retaining high approximation capacity within a shallow computational graph. On a high-frequency Helmholtz benchmark, PI-SUPNs are the only architecture to successfully recover the solution, while all competing models fail even under FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization. However, experiments on higher vibrational modes of a fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli beam reveal that architectural improvements alone are insufficient: accurate solutions require the combination of PI-SUPNs, FP64 precision, and curvature-aware optimization. Additionally, Allen-Cahn experiments show that PI-SUPNs achieve lower solution and derivative errors at reduced computational cost, with more favorable loss landscapes than competing architectures. We also establish quasi-local approximation properties and spline-based convergence bounds for SUPNs. Our results show that shallow network architectures are an important mechanism for improving physics-informed trainability, but accurate solutions to the most challenging PDEs can still require FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization.

authors.name: Zachary Morrow, Yucheng Fu, Pratanu Roy, Michael Penwarden

papers.title: Targeted Learning for Externally Controlled Trials and Beyond
papers.summary: This paper focuses on externally controlled trials (ECTs), which consist of a single-arm clinical trial supplemented by an external control arm (ECA). Potential data sources for the ECA can be broadly classified into three categories: (i) the control arm of a historical clinical trial, (ii) a concurrent cohort study, and (iii) external real-world data (RWD). In this paper, we consider a broad class of estimands defined through balancing weights. For a given estimand in the class, we discuss the efficient influence function (EIF) and the targeted maximum likelihood estimator (TMLE), together with practical implementation algorithms. Within the targeted learning framework, TMLE is a substitution estimator that enjoys several desirable theoretical properties and favorable finite-sample performance. Finally, the proposed framework is extended to two additional settings: (1) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) augmented with external covariate information to define a target population, and (2) indirect treatment comparisons (ITCs) that combine individual patient data (IPD) from an internal RCT with aggregate data (AgD) from an external RCT.

authors.name: Yixin Fang, Weili He

papers.title: A hybrid Graph-based Machine Learning Model for predicting Delivery Times in Supply Chain Logistics
papers.summary: Global supply chains are increasingly vulnerable to disruptions arising from external events, such as natural disasters and geopolitical crises, and from internal operational inefficiencies, including supplier delays and bottlenecks in order shipping. This work, conducted within the Horizon Europe project M4ESTRO, introduces a hybrid modelling approach combining graph theory and machine learning to represent supply chain logistics operations, with a focus on predicting delays in inbound flows between industrial suppliers and manufacturing entities. The various stages of order fulfilment are modelled through a formal mathematical framework, by defining disruption indicators computed from both historical and real-time data drawn from heterogeneous sources, including traffic and weather conditions and supplier dispatch readiness. Building on a graph-based representation of the supply chain, stochastic methods based on Markov chains are applied to estimate delivery times, detect schedule deviations, quantify prediction uncertainty, and produce interpretable metrics to support operational decision-making. Within the M4ESTRO project, the proposed framework was applied to build a web application for real-time tracking of inbound logistics, and was validated in a use case with an industrial project partner. The web application successfully enabled early detection of logistics disruptions along the supply chain and provided stakeholders with the visibility needed to act before delays propagated. The underlying model proved effective as the basis of a resilient, data-driven logistics tracking system, aligned with the digital transformation objectives of industry and with Manufacturing-as-a-Service paradigms.

authors.name: Mattia Volpato, Andrea Giuseppe Landella, Bruno Puzzolante

papers.title: Digital Knockoffs
papers.summary: Social simulations often use language model agents to represent people who differ on several measurable traits. However, describing a trait profile in a prompt does not guarantee the agent will express each trait at its intended level. We propose a method that calibrates agents to multidimensional profiles using activation steering: (i) extract steering directions for each trait, (ii) learn a shared mapping from steering strengths to measured trait scores, and (iii) search for a steering intervention for each target. We use Bayesian optimization for this search and evaluate the method on the Big Five personality scores of 500 OpenPsychometrics respondents. In each of five rounds, the assigned interventions yield lower mean absolute error across respondents than the prompting and steering baselines. Further, the model's responses to a given intervention yield the same trait profile regardless of whose target motivated it, so a poor match for one respondent can be the best match for another. When we match each respondent to the closest profile found across all tested interventions, Bayesian optimization yields 16.6% lower mean absolute error than uniform random search at the same evaluation budget. Our method thus offers a way to build social agents whose measured traits dovetail with those of the people they seek to represent. Whether this closer fit translates to improved predictions of downstream behavior remains an open question.

authors.name: Niuniu Zhang

papers.title: Accelerating wave-scattering simulations with learned search directions
papers.summary: Wave-scattering simulation requires solving a dense boundary-element system for every frequency, incidence and design. Krylov solvers build each search space from scratch, and it grows with problem size. Here we present BEMFormer, a solver that learns to generate search directions across systems of one integral equation and supplies geometry-specific directions through a coarse-grid correction. BEMFormer generalizes to unseen geometries, meshes and excitations, and to acoustic scattering after fine-tuning on eight geometries. It reproduces the measured radar cross-sections of benchmark targets. On a quadcopter with 1.04 million unknowns, 38 times the largest training problem, BEMFormer solves each system 30 times faster than a preconditioned Krylov solver. Both reach a radar cross-section deviation of about 1 dB, comparable to the difference between independent measurements and acceptable for engineering applications. These results show that solving million-unknown scattering problems in minutes is possible when the search space is learned rather than built from scratch.

authors.name: Haoran Sun, Tao Shan, Hongyu Zhou, Rui Guo, Shenheng Xu, Fan Yang, Maokun Li

papers.title: An equivariant classical density functional for ionic fluids at complex interfaces
papers.summary: Predicting the combined effects of ionic packing and long-range electrostatics at complex interfaces is technologically important, but remains challenging without atomistic simulations. Here we present a machine-learned classical density functional for ionic fluids that combines a symmetry-adapted neural free energy for short-range correlations with explicit long-range electrostatics. Trained on three-dimensional equilibrium densities and bulk correlations of the full-Coulomb restricted primitive model, a single functional transfers to charge-patterned particles and atomically structured electrodes. Around anisotropic charged solutes, it reproduces the ionic structure and mean forces from molecular dynamics, including reversals of the bare electrostatic force. At metal electrodes, self-consistent coupling to metal atoms captures the redistribution of ionic and electrode charge and the loading-dependent capacitance enhancement produced by steps and bumps. Combined with mobilities determined independently from bulk molecular dynamics, the same functional describes the main features of charging dynamics and resolves geometry-dependent spatial relaxation. This framework can be extended to more complex ionic fluids, enabling efficient exploration of how composition and geometry control structure and response.

authors.name: Bingqing Cheng

papers.title: Shoonya: Zero-Socket In-Process Small Language Models for Graph Databases with Schema-Epoch KV Caching, Live Catalog Logit Masking, and Verifier-Advantage Distillation
papers.summary: Coupling a property-graph database to an external language-model server imposes a three-part socket tax: serialization overhead dwarfing microsecond graph reads, repeated prefill of verbose schemas, and blind decoding divorced from the live catalog and multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) engine. We present Shoonya, from-scratch commercially clean (0.0% non-commercial or share-alike data) tri-modal (Python, Rust, OpenCypher) small language models (16.8M to 1.07B parameters) co-designed with shoonya-infer, a zero-dependency pure-Rust runtime embedded inside the samyama-graph-enterprise address space. Direct GraphStore references unlock three database-native primitives: (1) an epoch-invalidated SchemaPrefixCache over a copy-on-write PagedKvArena accelerating warm CPU time-to-first-token by 4.91x--13.68x with O(1) DDL invalidation; (2) a 36 us columnar catalog and source-span logit mask enforcing valid ontology identifiers and verbatim spans; and (3) a sub-65 us read-only MVCC gate serving Tier-0 queries inside 389.8 MiB INT8 RSS (59.8--67.9 tok/s) with 0.0% hallucination leak. Rank-factorized tied embeddings (-74.5% vocabulary weights), atomic indentation tokens (0/421 indentation errors), 4:1 grouped-query attention with 2:1 cross-layer KV sharing (-93.75% INT8 KV memory), Warmup-Stable-Decay training, KnOTS SVD merging, Step-GRPO, and Rust Jacobi SVD governance keep 100% of layers heavy-tailed ($\alpha \in [1.88, 2.20]$). Finally, we synthesize nine lessons across v0.1--v1.0, resolving a Reverse-Token-Density Distillation Trap via teacher scaling and zero-VRAM Verifier-Advantage-Gated Knowledge Distillation (AdvKD), recovering +13.61 MBPP points (33.07%) while reaching 100% validity on enrichment, grounded extraction, and tool planning.

authors.name: Madhulatha Mandarapu, Sandeep Kunkunuru

papers.title: When and Where to Transfer: Learning Transferable Historical Contexts for Short-History Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
papers.summary: Related sources can improve multivariate time series forecasting when the target history is short, but their usefulness varies across source groups and historical periods. A key challenge is to identify informative historical contexts from the sources. This paper proposes Hierarchical Context Transfer (HiCT), a framework that adaptively weights source groups and their historical contexts to determine both \emph{where} and \emph{when} to transfer. A shared context encoder and cross-attention are used to learn weights over source groups and historical contexts. These weights guide regularized transfer estimation, followed by an optional target-specific correction. This paper establishes a target excess-risk bound for the context-weighted transfer estimator. Experiments demonstrate competitive predictive performance across four multivariate forecasting datasets and a favorable accuracy--runtime trade-off against the evaluated baselines. Source-corruption ablations illustrate the roles of group-level and within-group weighting in adapting to unreliable source histories.

authors.name: Huiling Yuan, Yize Wang, Guodong Li

papers.title: Complex band-limited maximum likelihood: estimating the wave behind detected quanta
papers.summary: Detected photons and electrons land at positions drawn from $|\psi|^2$, yet it is $\psi$, phase included, that a wave equation propagates, and the state that produced the particles is often known only in part. A density estimator can recover $|\psi|^2$ directly from the positions, without any wave equation, but it discards the phase, and with it the state. We introduce complex band-limited maximum likelihood (complex BLML), which estimates $\psi$ itself by maximising the likelihood of the detected positions over exactly the intensities the physics allows: squared moduli of complex functions whose spectrum lies in a given set, such as a band, the shape of the aperture, or several modes for a partially coherent source. A single eigenvalue can certify a global maximum. On simulated two-slit far fields we measure what each prior is worth: a band reaches a given accuracy with seven times fewer photons than a kernel density estimate and already gives the fringe contrast and the relative phase, and the shape of the aperture adds the slit geometry. Some quantities need a prior at any number of photons: for slits of one profile the intensity fixes only the contrast $2\rho V/(1+\rho^2)$, and on a line two different apertures can produce the same particles. Cutting a pattern to a few fringes, as published records are, removes the slit width. On four public single-particle double-slit records it predicts held-out particles best among the methods we tested, kernel estimators and two-slit optical models included, and it recovers the fringe contrast without a model of the optics. On fluorescent beads it finds the resolution limit of the microscope, $2\mathrm{NA}/\lambda$, from the photons alone.

authors.name: Rahul Agarwal, Ankit Agarwal

papers.title: Can Ideologues Agree on Quality? From Non-identifiable Latent Factors to Collective Outcomes
papers.summary: To surface "objective" fact-check notes, X's Community Notes uses Biased Matrix Factorization (BMF) on crowd-sourced ratings to separate note quality from reviewer ideology. We show that for any correctly specified model that decomposes ratings into quality and ideological alignment, this separation requires fixing an ideological anchor: a reference point for what counts as neutral. We give a characterization for the standard implementation: with $L_2$ regularization, BMF anchors quality at a point proportional to the mean reviewer ideology, recovering objective quality if and only if the mean reviewer is neutral, assuming note quality is uncorrelated with note leaning. This parallels the Condorcet Jury Theorem: collective judgment recovers truth when the pool is unbiased on average. When that assumption fails, BMF's recovered ranking shifts toward maximizing aggregate reviewer satisfaction, which coincides with social welfare only when the pool is representative. This is not specific to BMF; the rating matrix admits a continuous family of gauge-equivalent decompositions, each implying a different quality ranking, so no mechanism based on ratings alone can recover quality without implicitly choosing such an anchor. What appears to be routine hyperparameter tuning is in fact a normative choice about whose preferences define quality.

authors.name: David Gamba, Seura Ha, Daniel M. Romero, Grant Schoenebeck

papers.title: Neural Schr\"{o}dinger Bridge via Yasue Action with Applications to Generative Modeling
papers.summary: We propose a novel neural solver for inferring the continuous state evolution of the Schr\"{o}dinger bridge problem. The proposed solver builds on a saddle point formulation involving the Yasue action functional. This allows us to realize the continuous state evolution by learning the optimal velocity for an ordinary differential equation, as opposed to learning the optimal drift for a stochastic differential equation. The proposed solver only uses the source and the target samples, and not the source and target distributions per se, which makes it particularly suitable for high dimensional applications arising in generative modeling. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solver using several numerical experiments in low and high dimensions, using both real and synthetic datasets.

authors.name: Yan-Han Chen, Abhishek Halder, Hailiang Liu

papers.title: Self-prediction residuals improve single-pass detection of wrong-object boxes in grounded vision-language models
papers.summary: Grounded vision-language models write boxes as text, and the mean probability of their coordinate tokens says little about whether a box is right. We study a single-pass signal for boxes on another object, which matter when only the object counts. A linear map, fitted per model to its own answers without labels, reads a box from the hidden state before writing. Its disagreement with the written box, the self-prediction residual, flags boxes on another object although the read-out is far less accurate; the residual's weight was fixed with labels on two models. On a replication list of 1,200 RefCOCOg test items, the residual, averaged over six models, raises the detection of these errors for each of fifteen single-pass scores, by 0.026 to 0.049 in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) on a label-free probe and probes trained on 2,000 labelled items. Over all errors, adding it to the label-free probe moves AUROC, averaged over the models, by less than 0.02 (95% interval). With a fifth of answers reviewed, the share of all errors caught moves from 0.518 to 0.524, that of boxes on another object from 0.505 to 0.607 (post hoc): the residual changes which errors are found, not how many, and in cost-weighted recall it breaks even when such a box costs about 0.86 times another error, and its gain is positive in point estimate at equal costs. These gains come from RefCOCOg lists of MS-COCO images.

authors.name: Enhao Cui, Junzhi Yang, Yaoshun Lin, Yuhan Feng, Zijian Chen

papers.title: UACR: Uncertainty-Aware Collaborative Routing for Explainable Industrial Anomaly Inspection
papers.summary: Industrial anomaly inspection requires not only accurate anomaly discrimination but also trustworthy explanations for operators, while satisfying the strict latency constraints of online inspection. Existing methods, however, typically apply a fixed computational path to all samples, making it difficult to strike a good balance among detection accuracy, inference efficiency, and interpretability. To address this issue, we propose UACR, an uncertainty-aware collaborative routing framework for explainable industrial anomaly inspection. UACR aims to deliver reliable anomaly decisions together with operator-facing explanations under the online inspection budget, while adaptively allocating computation so that ambiguous cases receive deeper scrutiny. The framework consists of two stages. Stage I, Offline Training and Routing Hyperparameter Search, learns the anomaly inspection modules and calibrates the uncertainty estimator that drives routing. Stage II, Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Routing, collaboratively dispatches each input across inspection paths according to its estimated uncertainty. Experimental results on multiple public datasets show that UACR achieves over 5.16% improvement in accuracy compared to the baseline method, while reducing latency by over 31.5%. It also enhances the interpretability of industrial detection by over 15%.

authors.name: Yiwei Li, Qiyang Chen, Zheming Yang

papers.title: Wavelet-CFM for the extragalactic millimeter-wave sky
papers.summary: We develop a Wavelet-factorized Conditional Flow Matching (Wavelet-CFM) framework to generate fast, accurate simulations of correlated astrophysical fields including gravitational lensing convergence ($\kappa$), the kinetic and thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ and tSZ) effects, and cosmic infrared background (CIB) emission. Together these make up every bright extragalactic component of the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) sky apart from radio sources. Our approach combines multi-scale wavelet decomposition with conditional flow matching models, trained on $\sim$9$\times$9 deg$^2$ patches at 1-arcminute resolution. The four fields are generated jointly, including their cross couplings, and the model has a tractable likelihood, which to our knowledge has not previously been achieved for this set of components. The power spectra, one-point distributions and Minkowski functionals of the generated maps match a validation set to a few percent. These results show promise for enabling field-level cosmological analyses of mm-wave data.

authors.name: M. Mebratu, W. L. K. Wu, S. Gasiorowski

papers.title: Training speech deepfake detectors against worst-case filters: Gains, Costs and Limits
papers.summary: Speech deepfake detectors make few errors on standard benchmarks, yet a simple attack defeats them: the attacker passes fake speech through one short filter, tuned against the detector, and many fakes then pass as real. Training with random filters does not stop this attack, because the attacker uses the worst filter, not a random one. We therefore train the detector against the worst case: during training, a small set of filters is updated to fool the current detector, at about the cost of random filters. In a preregistered study, this made the detector more robust to filter attacks on real-world recordings than random filters did. It also lowered the in-domain attack error of the standard detector, and beat one-step adversarial training with additive noise on real-world recordings. The price is a higher error on unfiltered speech, and a validation study shows that choosing the checkpoint on held-out spoofing systems made the standard detector about as robust.

authors.name: Ali Alavi

papers.title: Routing Collapse in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts: Cross-Modal Conditioning Restores Expert Diversity Without Improving Accuracy
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) classifiers are increasingly applied to multimodal emotion recognition, yet the health of their routing distributions is rarely measured. We study a seven-expert MoE head on IEMOCAP under two conditions that differ only in how modality embeddings are fused before reaching it: a learned scalar gate alone, and the same gate preceded by pairwise cross-modal attention. Under scalar fusion the router collapses, concentrating on 1.88 of seven experts at a normalised entropy of 0.241. Cross-modal fusion raises entropy to 0.537 and utilisation to 3.25 experts, a 2.23x increase (p=0.035, Cohen's d=2.55), and induces emotion-differentiated routing absent in the scalar case. This recovered diversity confers no detectable benefit: across six seeds per condition, weighted accuracy (p=0.646) and run-to-run variance (p=0.768) are statistically indistinguishable. We further observe a 13-point accuracy spread under identical configuration. In this regime, router health and task performance are decoupled, and diagnosing collapse does not by itself justify fixing it.

authors.name: Syed Hussamuddin, Mubashra Fayyaz

papers.title: UNIFY: Unified Learning with One Model via Batch Norm Switching
papers.summary: Neural networks are typically trained separately for individual datasets or tasks, resulting in many task-specific models. This redundancy increases memory footprint, deployment costs, and energy consumption limiting their scalability. We propose UNIFY, a unified learning framework that enables a single model to jointly learn and perform inference across multiple datasets via Batch Normalization Switching (BNS). Instead of maintaining separate models for each dataset, UNIFY shares the parameter-intensive backbone while maintaining dataset-specific BN statistics and parameters, along with dataset-specific classification heads. We validate our framework using five datasets (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet) across six Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) of different sizes (SqueezeNet 1.1, WideResNet-40-2, WideResNet-16-8, ResNet-18, ResNet-34, ResNet-50). Notably, a single UNIFIED ResNet-34 trained on these datasets achieves accuracies of 99.53%, 94.84%, 96.12%, 80.32%, and 67.67%, respectively, outperforming the average performance of the corresponding independently trained task-specific models while reducing the memory footprint by approximately 4.94x, from 428.30 MB (five separate models) to 86.71 MB (one unified model). UNIFY aims not only to consolidate (K) models into a single model but also to enhance model-effectiveness by leveraging complementary knowledge across datasets. It paves the way for scalable, efficient, and unified learning capable of handling diverse image classification tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/saktx/UNIFY.

authors.name: Shaharyar Ahmed Khan Tareen, Xiaojing Yuan

papers.title: Analytical Modeling and Optimal GPU Provisioning for Disaggregated LLM Inference
papers.summary: We present OSplit, an exact analytical method that enables efficient partitioning of a GPU L1 domain into prefill and decode workers, including sharding for classical and advanced GPUs. OSplit takes into consideration model parameters, enabling any inference model to be partitioned into prefill and decode workers with a goal of producing the maximum throughput possible. OSplit is based on a capacity model that takes as inputs the model, the loading scheme (batch size, max sequence length), and models an inference serving framework (vLLM) and computes the efficiency of each GPU. For this, we model H100 and GB300 GPUs, and model a scale-up domain, along with FlashAttention-based kernels. OSplit first computes an optimal collective generation policy, which gives inputs to the capacity model that enables optimal split of prefill and decode GPUs. We evaluate our scheme over H100 (NVL8) and GB300 (NVL72) using vLLM inference serving and show throughput, predicted and measured latency, showing near-perfect theoretical-to-measured values over leading LLMs (Llama and Qwen)

authors.name: Akshat Pandey, Dominic Cheng, Sidharth Sharma, Ashwin Gumaste

papers.title: Contrastive Gradient Guidance for Test-Time Multi-Preference Alignment of Diffusion Models
papers.summary: Aligning pre-trained diffusion models with multiple context-dependent preferences requires adapting generation at test time rather than relying on offline fine-tuning, which requires hyperparameter tuning and a new training run for each preference trade-off. Existing approaches compress diverse preferences into a single scalar reward objective for fine-tuning or test-time guidance rather than directly reusing existing generative experts released for different purposes and obtained through different fine-tuning methods. In this work, we propose Contrastive Gradient Guidance (CGG), a test-time compositional generative framework that reformulates multi-preference alignment as a composition of distributions. CGG represents each preference as a contrastive preference pair of favored experts and unfavored anti-experts, whose score difference forms a contrastive gradient guidance signal that combines denoising directions (gradients) from off-the-shelf diffusion models during sampling. Experiments show that CGG reuses pre-trained and fine-tuned models as favored experts or anti-experts to control output style and safety, and that it can be combined with existing sampling-based reward guidance. With a single fixed scale per pair, CGG composes five preferences at once and gives a more balanced trade-off across text-image preference, concept control, photographic fidelity, and safety than offline fine-tuning, weight-space merging, and reward steering.

authors.name: Po-Yi Lu, Jui-Chao Lu, Paul Kuo-Ming Huang, Shih-Hsin Wang, Chun-Liang Li, Hsuan-Tien Lin

papers.title: Multi-Order Passive Macromodeling from Layouts via Nested Port-Hamiltonian Learning
papers.summary: Compact, passive state-space macromodels of interconnects and power-delivery networks are essential for stable transient signal- and power-integrity simulations. However, conventional flows require costly per-layout full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, while both traditional fitting and prior learning surrogates rely on post-hoc fitting or passivity perturbation that degrades accuracy without guaranteeing convergence. In this work, we propose an end-to-end macromodeling framework that learns directly in the passive space, mapping physical layout graphs to multi-order port-Hamiltonian (pH) macromodels. Specifically, our network encodes each layout graph into unconstrained matrix blocks and assembles them via a complete, prefix-nested pH parameterization that guarantees continuous-frequency passivity and stability by construction, yielding valid $k$-state macromodels via direct state slicing in one forward pass. To train all orders without reference realizations, we supervise the network directly on S-parameters through a progressive order-growth curriculum. Evaluated on 27k unseen test structures from a 270k-structure advanced-packaging dataset, our framework reduces mean S-parameter error by $42\%$ on average (up to $65\%$) over established macromodeling tools fitted to ground-truth EM responses, achieves zero passivity violations across $459{,}000$ exported models, and accelerates macromodel generation by $11{,}000$--$39{,}000\times$ ($36$--$85$~ms per layout).

authors.name: Benchao Zhu, Keren Zhu

papers.title: Learning free energy across a differentiable temperature range by deep generative modeling
papers.summary: Free energy governs the directionality, stability, and temperature sensitivity of physical, chemical, and biological transformations. Conventional free energy calculations, such as thermodynamic integration and free energy perturbation, often have to be performed at individual temperatures and are limited by the high cost of sampling an extensive set of thermodynamic states. Here, we introduce learned temperature-differentiable free energy perturbation (TD-FEP), a deep generative framework that learns a temperature-conditioned, invertible mapping between reference and target systems through data-free, energy-based optimization. TD-FEP thereby unifies one-shot state generation and free energy calculation across a continuous temperature range. We validated TD-FEP across a broad range of applications, including isolated molecules, periodic materials, and chemical reactions.

authors.name: Yaowen Zhang, Chen Chen, Wanyu Lin, Shuo-Hui Li, Ding Pan

papers.title: Beyond Raw IQ: Compact Semantic Representations for Task Oriented Automatic Modulation Classification
papers.summary: Automatic modulation classification (AMC) is an important component of modern wireless communication systems, but conventional signal representations can be expensive to store, process, and communicate, particularly under noisy channel conditions. This work investigates whether learned semantic representations can provide a compact alternative to high-dimensional in-phase and quadrature (IQ) representations while retaining robustness to noise. Starting from a 2048-dimensional IQ representation, we evaluate learned semantic representations with dimensions of 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64. Across the evaluated configurations, a 16-dimensional representation provides the strongest overall trade-off between classification performance, robustness, and representation size. The resulting representation achieves a 128x compression ratio and a 99.22% reduction in dimensionality. We further evaluate representation stability across signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), compare semantic representations with a raw-IQ CNN, analyze per-class robustness, and perform five-seed validation. The five-seed evaluation produces an average accuracy of (49.22 +- 0.52)% and Macro-F1 of (49.27 +- 0.53)% across the evaluated SNR range. These results indicate that learned semantic compression can produce a substan- tially smaller representation while preserving useful classification information and improving geometric stability under noise.

authors.name: Omm Swarup, Shrishail M. Hiremath

papers.title: Statistical mechanics of linear classification on hierarchical tree data
papers.summary: Deep networks owe much of their success to their ability to exploit the structure in data, from the grammar of language to the multi-scale organization of images. Yet, many statistical mechanics approaches to structured data rely on Gaussian equivalence, whose assumptions can fail when a few latent variables influence all input coordinates. In this work, we take a step beyond this setting with a simple setup, in which a linear classifier is trained to infer the root of the classical broadcast process on a tree from its $N$ leaves. Despite this simplicity, the data already display non-Gaussian statistics along the direction carrying the label, as well as strong finite-size effects. By retaining the exact law along this direction and approximating the transverse fluctuations as Gaussian, we obtain a finite-depth replica theory that accurately describes the measured learning curves. At large depth and sufficiently weak regularization, we uncover a double descent whose two stages are separated in scale. In a range of broadcast noise below the reconstruction threshold, the first descent occurs at a number of samples scaling as $N^\omega$, with $0<\omega<1$ set by the data statistics, whereas the overfitting peak occurs at order $N$ samples. Beyond linear classifiers, this setup could serve as a controlled starting point to study deeper architectures and generative models on hierarchical data.

authors.name: Jerome Garnier-Brun, Federica Kulka, Carlo Lucibello

papers.title: More Is Never Less: Affordable Robustness to Additive Attacks via Monotone Multiple-Instance Learning
papers.summary: Static malware detectors that represent each sample as a bag of extracted features, such as permissions, API calls, or imported functions, are cheap to deploy and remain state-of-the-art under temporal drift and in selective classification. Yet, attackers can evade them by adding benign-looking content that outweighs malicious evidence. Canonically, detectors encode the presence of a few thousand features, selected during training, as sparse multi-hot vectors over a fixed vocabulary. Features that emerge after training remain invisible. We show that linear models and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) over this input are sum-pooled set models in disguise. Sum-pooling lets added benign features cancel malicious evidence. Instead, we cast malware detection with set-shaped static features as a multiple-instance learning (MIL) problem. To this end, we propose MalSets, which uses max-pooled Deep Sets models with a monotone head to ensure that any malicious evidence remains undiluted; thus, more is never less. Under MIL, a general text encoder maps any feature string to an embedding, thus eliminating the long-standing out-of-vocabulary problem at test time. Max-pooling retains the malicious evidence regardless of how many benign features an attacker adds. Since max-pooling can only grow when features are added, constraining the head alone makes the malware score monotone under additions, even against a white-box attacker adapted to this architecture. While monotone detectors are never evaded by state-of-the-art black-box or white-box attacks, they often significantly pay for this robustness in clean performance since benign features cannot count as evidence. However, by combining a non-monotone set encoder with max-pooling and a monotone head, MalSets maintains the robustness of prior monotone classifiers while achieving state-of-the-art performance.

authors.name: Alexander Herzog, Shae McFadden, Lorenzo Cavallaro

papers.title: Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation for Synthetic Segmentation Data
papers.summary: Synthetic images sharing a segmentation label can differ in their training value. We propose Task-Conditioned Detail Allocation (TCDA) to select useful candidates and locally edit some remaining images. We ask whether image details provide class-specific cues in the regions marked by the label. We train a small task reference on frozen image features from real training images. We compare its class responses before and after blurring each candidate, and score how well these response changes align with the labeled regions. This detail allocation score ranks candidates from the same source. Comparing their response--label alignment with that of the real source image also guides repair decisions and, in multiclass tasks, the choice of regions to edit. Selected candidates and accepted repairs are used for training with the original labels and the unchanged downstream segmenter. Experiments on camouflaged object detection, degraded salient object detection, and adverse-condition semantic segmentation show that our selection outperforms equally sized random and label-agreement subsets. Combining selection and repair improves over real-only training by up to 0.019 in $S_\alpha$ on COD10K and 2.86 mIoU points on ACDC.

authors.name: Chunming He, Dingming Zhang, Jifan Zhang, Yuhan Dong, Longxiang Tang, Youwei Pang, Xiaoqi Zhao, Fengyang Xiao, Sina Farsiu

papers.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters
papers.summary: Two visually identical animated characters can respond differently to the same action command because their body dynamics differ. For example, a stiff blob and its bouncy twin reach different heights when both receive the jump command. Given only the first frame and the action command, a visual world model has no information to distinguish these twins, because their initial appearances are identical. We therefore propose an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation, using a contrastive loss to separate look-alike characters. We introduce ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters that run, jump, fall, turn and crouch. Its characters form look-alike groups of four that differ only in their dynamics profile, and we also evaluate the model on 32 animated animals from DeformingThings4D. Even with a body code from these clips, the latent pixel world model we tested recovered at most 25 percent of the twins' jump height difference. On new shapes, our model identified the correct twin in 85.9 percent of cases, compared with 76.7 percent for a transformer baseline that reads the same clips without a body summary, and in a controlled ablation the contrastive loss gave more than half of this gain. On the animated animals, it reduced the mean path prediction error by 8.5 percent against a model without body information.

authors.name: Amarnath R

papers.title: Twisted Block Particle Filters: A Local Particle-System Change of Measure for High-Dimensional State-Space Models
papers.summary: Block particle filters mitigate weight degeneracy in high-dimensional state-space models, but their normalizer estimates can remain highly variable. We introduce a twisted block particle filter (TBPF) that incorporates predictive guidance through an exact change of measure at blockwise resampling. The method guide-tilts one uniformly selected offspring per block, leaves the state-transition kernel unchanged, and computes the resampling correction using finite empirical guide averages. We prove that this correction exactly preserves the finite-particle block particle filter normalizer expectation, separating the effect of guided sampling from the approximation introduced by spatial blocking. Our analysis provides exact conditional local moments and a one-step conditional central limit result. We further derive explicit bounds on the correction accumulated across blocks and time, establish fixed-horizon consistency of the block filter and corrected normalizer under suitable regularity and guide-range conditions, and identify conditional criteria for guide perturbations that reduce variance. Experiments on coupled linear Gaussian and stochastic-volatility models with up to 256 latent dimensions show lower measured log-normalizer variance. For stochastic volatility with a five-step guide, the median reduction is $38\%$. An application to a 100-dimensional financial portfolio panel extends the evaluation to real data.

authors.name: Ning Ning

papers.title: Beyond Invoice Volumes: Temporal Network Structure, Maturity Concentration, and Systemic Liquidity Exposure in SME Trade-Credit Networks
papers.summary: Trade-credit invoices encode directed obligations whose temporal synchronization and counterparty concentration are obscured by annual volume totals. We audit 749,952 atomic B2B invoices from 2012-2023 (EUR 99.705B; 75,343 firms) from the pseudonymized Mendeley Data corpus (Esteva de la Rosa, 2026), separating 1,240 terminal 2024 bridge records (EUR 630.12M; 9 bridge-only firms) and 13 extreme-duration contracts (>3,650 days; EUR 297.75k). Using directed weighted graphs, HHI, Shannon entropy, CR1 shares, spectral centralities, and multi-cadence temporal operators, we formulate and benchmark a Maturity-Aware Network Exposure (MANE) indicator. Invoice values are heavily skewed: the top 1% hold 81.41% of value (Gini = 0.9742). Two-way fixed-effects panels with circular block bootstrapping ($B=999$, 12-month blocks) and Holm-Bonferroni control show higher lagged debtor counterparty concentration is associated with lower MANE ($\hat{\beta}=-0.494$, 95% CI $[-0.752,-0.248]$, $p_{\mathrm{Holm}}=0.004$). Robustness audits (R1-R4) confirm stability under 2021 exclusion ($-0.402$, $p=0.004$), Shannon entropy ($+0.257$), CR1 ($-0.515$), 1%-99% Winsorization ($-0.462$, all $p=0.001$), and multi-invoice debtors (count $\ge 2$, $-0.334$, $p=0.031$). Conversely, within-FE diagnostics expose severe joint-concentration multicollinearity (VIF = 22.22) that vanishes for multi-invoice debtors ($p=0.719$), while regime splits reveal a macro reciprocity sign reversal between 2012-2019 ($-0.706$) and 2020-2023 ($+0.232$, both $p=0.001$). In 12-month purged forecasting, MANE does not reliably improve over maturity seeds ($\Delta\mathrm{MSE}=2.668$, 95% CI $[-0.027,7.954]$; trimmed $0.067$, $[-0.035,0.194]$), positioning MANE as a reproducible screening and auditing diagnostic, rather than a default proxy, for supply-chain finance, multilateral clearing, and RWA tokenization.

authors.name: Sai Srikanth Madugula, Peplluis Esteva de la Rosa, Daya Shankar

papers.title: Correlation-aware sequential sampling for multi-output polynomial chaos expansions
papers.summary: The interaction of multiple physical processes in complex engineering systems is often characterized by several quantities of interest (QoIs) with non-negligible cross-correlations. Accurate uncertainty quantification of these responses requires repeated model evaluations, which can be computationally expensive. As an alternative, polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) provides an efficient surrogate modeling framework for reducing this computational cost owing to its natural structure for statistical analysis, while adaptive sequential sampling can further improve sampling efficiency under a limited model evaluation budget. However, adaptive sampling strategies specifically designed for multi-output PCE remain limited, and existing approaches commonly aggregate information from individual outputs without explicitly accounting for their statistical dependence. When strong correlations exist among QoIs, output-wise aggregation can give greater combined influence to response patterns shared by several outputs. To reduce the influence of such repeated representation on sample allocation, this study develops a principal component analysis-based extension of the multi-output criterion for adaptive construction of PCE. The sampling criterion combines component-wise normalization with the retention of selected principal directions, thereby adjusting the relative influence of shared response patterns while preserving distance-based exploration. The method is verified through numerical examples with different levels of output coupling and is compared with the conventional multi-output criterion and reference sampling strategies. The results demonstrate that accounting for output dependence improves the allocation of new samples among multiple response features and enhances the efficiency of multi-output PCE surrogate construction, particularly for strongly correlated QoIs.

authors.name: Qitian Lu, Miroslav Vo\v{r}echovsk\'y, Luk\'a\v{s} Nov\'ak

papers.title: A Novel Approach to Clustering Shape Data Using Iteratively Weighted Vectors with k-Means
papers.summary: Topological data analysis provides a collection of methods for analyzing data with shape structure, including point clouds, graphs, and images. Recent advances in topological vectorization have enabled the embedding of shape data into Euclidean spaces, facilitating comparisons and machine learning tasks. Vector summaries that effectively capture topological structures are particularly useful for shape classification and unsupervised learning tasks such as clustering. We investigate the use of vectorized topological data for clustering through k-means, which partitions observations into a fixed number of groups by minimizing a squared-error loss function. By incorporating an element-wise weight-update step into the iterative k-means algorithm, we improve clustering performance on both simulated and real-world shape datasets. We show that estimating these weights reduces to a least-squares problem, requiring minimal additional computation while allowing flexible coefficient constraints. Our approach also substantially strengthens the negative correlation between the loss and clustering accuracy, improving the effectiveness of selecting among multiple clustering solutions based on the lowest loss. These improvements remain robust to changes in vector length and the number of initializations. Furthermore, weighted topological vector summaries exhibit stability under small structural perturbations, particularly when weight constraints are imposed. The proposed method offers a flexible alternative for clustering topological data, accommodating different k-means variants, vectorization methods, and weight constraints.

authors.name: Jason Turk, Umar Islambekov

papers.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
papers.summary: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. Numerical predictions are validated against analytical solutions and established BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes. Applications to complex three-dimensional geometries are demonstrated using single-fin, double-fin, and arrayed fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) configurations. Gradient-based inverse learning enables single- and multi-parameter identification, including simultaneous recovery of mode-resolved phonon relaxation times and spatially distributed heat-generation rates in steady-state and transient problems. GPU performance and scalability are evaluated with respect to spatial resolution, angular discretization, and phonon bands, including comparisons with an MPI-based BTE solver. JAX-Nano provides a unified computational framework for three-dimensional phonon transport, automatic differentiation, and inverse parameter identification, enabling sensitivity analysis and optimization of nanoscale thermal systems.

authors.name: Bo Zhang, Amy Zhaomei Zhang

papers.title: Elicitation format changes zero-shot classification accuracy in a medical vision-language model: a two-center evaluation on colorectal histopathology
papers.summary: Background. Verbalized confidence from a hosted medical vision-language model is usually treated as packaging around an unchanged prediction. Methods. We held a nine-class colorectal histopathology prompt fixed except for the requested response format and evaluated MedGemma-27b-it on 10,004 validation and 7,180 external-center PathMNIST patches, with preregistered endpoints, randomized ties, and random floors recomputed for each patch set. Results. Requesting probabilities over all nine classes instead of a ranked top-3 reduced accuracy by 14.8 points on validation, -0.1475 [-0.1594, -0.1353], and 13.4 at the external center, -0.1341 [-0.1484, -0.1196], against chance accuracy of 0.1111. The nine-class prompt uniquely forbade commentary, reasoning, and a chosen answer; removing that prohibition at matched cardinality and token budget recovered +0.1878 [+0.1623, +0.2134] and +0.1911 [+0.1648, +0.2181], while changing cardinality with the prohibition absent moved accuracy by -0.0013 [-0.0300, +0.0280] and -0.0214 [-0.0494, +0.0071]. The nine-class format returned no parseable distribution on 7.6 and 7.7 percent of patches, mostly zero vectors in the two least-textured classes, and deferring these failures first explained its measurable selective-prediction gain. Across four vision-capable models, accuracy did not grade the cost: two models matched on accuracy differed five- to sevenfold. First-token logit entropy routed better than any elicited signal, +0.1820 [+0.1722, +0.1974] versus +0.0493 [+0.0377, +0.0649] relative to each signal's random floor. Conclusions. Response format changes a medical vision-language classifier, and the operative component here was the instruction suppressing an answer. Use logits when available; otherwise request a short ranked list without prohibiting reasoning or a chosen answer.

authors.name: Anay Sinhal, Amit Sinhal, Arpana Sinhal

papers.title: Sub-Gaussian HDLSS Principal Component Analysis: High-Probability Theory and Numerical Evidence for NRM, CDM, and Block Noise Reduction
papers.summary: We study principal component analysis when the dimension d is much larger than the sample size n under an independent-factor sub-Gaussian model. The dual sample covariance is decomposed into a finite-rank score matrix, an isotropic bulk shift, and a high-probability remainder governed by the bulk trace \tau_0, Frobenius scale q_0, and largest noise eigenvalue b_0 = ||\Lambda_0||_{op}. This decomposition separates fixed-score HDLSS limits from joint limits in which n also grows. It shows that sequential noise reduction generally targets a score oracle containing a later-spike subtraction, while an oracle block correction avoids that subtraction when the signal rank is known. A parallel cross-data-matrix bound explains the benefit and cost of sample splitting. Reproducible Gaussian-factor simulations with 1,000 replications per configuration confirm the score-oracle approximation, the multi-spike subtraction, the separation between eigenvalue and eigenvector scales, and the population transition when n grows.

authors.name: Yugo Nakayama

papers.title: TrustFlow-ECG: Reliability-Aware ECG Restoration with Calibrated Risk Estimation
papers.summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) restoration models can reduce noise and motion artifacts, but they rarely estimate whether the restored waveform is reliable for downstream analysis. We propose TrustFlow-ECG, a reliability-aware restoration framework that combines a one-step conditional rectified-flow restorer with a lightweight window-level risk predictor. The predictor uses the noisy ECG, restored ECG, and correction residual, then applies validation-set isotonic calibration for selective ECG analysis. We evaluate on MIT-BIH ECG windows corrupted with NSTDB artifacts, powerline interference, and mixed noise across multiple SNRs, with an external 9,675-window PTB-XL stress check without retraining. TrustFlow achieves 0.862 Spearman correlation with true risk and 0.911 AUROC for failure detection, while calibration reduces ECE from 0.0385 to 0.0098. At 80% coverage, selective rejection reduces RMSE from 0.1848 to 0.1345, improves R-peak F1 from 0.8778 to 0.9175, and reduces HR MAE from 6.26 to 4.88 bpm.

authors.name: Mohamed Kamel, Tamer Nadeem

papers.title: Neural Costate Guidance for Autonomous Cislunar Low-Thrust Trajectory Generation
papers.summary: Future missions will benefit from onboard autonomous low-thrust trajectory generation to correct deviations from the nominal flight path caused by navigation errors and thruster outages. Onboard computing resources rarely allow the solution of a cold-started, long-duration nonconvex optimal control problem, especially in dynamically challenging regions such as the cislunar to translunar corridor of the Earth-Moon system. This paper develops data augmentation and training techniques that enable a neural network to predict accurate initial costates of the indirect method. A recovery trajectory is then built from repeated network queries in a computationally efficient guidance algorithm. Training data are produced by the backward generation of optimal examples method, extending prior approaches to the circular restricted three-body problem. A novel anchor trajectory approach is developed to cover the relevant state space, and costate rescaling and a Hamiltonian loss term are used to improve learning. The method is demonstrated on Earth-Moon transfers from a high Earth orbit to halo orbits about L1 and L2. Under navigation errors and thruster outages, a spacecraft reaches the target orbit more often with the proposed method than with nominal-trajectory tracking or fully numerical reoptimization. Onboard computation is reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared with reoptimization.

authors.name: Jannik Graebner, Ryne Beeson

papers.title: DUO Policy: Bridging Human Video Coverage and Robot Precision for Fine-Grained Manipulation
papers.summary: Human videos promise a scalable way to reduce expensive robot data collection, but the embodiment gap limits the resulting policies to coarse behaviors, and they fail at precise tasks such as insertion. Existing methods co-train or finetune a single policy on both data sources, treating each source as equally useful in every state: the policy either absorbs the embodiment error at precision-critical steps or spends scarce robot data relearning free-space motion. We observe that the value of each source depends on the state: human data is useful where precision requirements are low, while robot data is disproportionately valuable near precision-critical states. We therefore propose \textbf{DUO Policy} (Dual-Actor Policy), which decouples a manipulation skill into a hand policy, pretrained on human videos for global free-space motion, and a robot policy, trained on sparse in-hand data for local precise corrections, with a gate learned from human interventions switching between them. This design is robust to moderate embodiment error in human data and generalizes to scene layouts beyond the coverage of the robot data. On tasks such as K-cup coffee making, desk cleanup, and cluttered candy sorting, DUO Policy outperforms the baseline with the highest average success by 12.9 percentage points over four simulated tasks and by 51.7 points over three real-world tasks, and matches robot-only training with 2.75$\times$ less data-collection time. Project Webpage: https://mingxi-jia.github.io/duo_policy_site/

authors.name: Mingxi Jia, Patton Jiyang Yin, Haojie Huang, Ivy Xiao He, Xuanru Liu, Gefei Liu, Dian Wang, Stefanie Tellex

papers.title: Handover Cost Optimization in LEO Satellite Networks using an RL-based Multiple-Column Selection Strategy via Branch-and-Price
papers.summary: Next-generation wireless networks increasingly rely on low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites for broad coverage and low latency, making efficient handover management essential. We formulate satellite handover as a combinatorial optimization problem, assigning each ground user to exactly one capacity-limited, visible satellite while minimizing network handover costs. We propose a reinforcement learning (RL)-based branch-and-price (B&P) framework with learned multiple-column selection (MCS) to accelerate column generation while retaining exact dynamic programming pricing. We also develop two lightweight heuristic policies: handover-aware visibility duration (HAVD) for online decisions and congestion-aware predictive (CAP) for offline planning. Additionally, a local-search repair algorithm adapts precomputed B&P or MCS-B&P solutions to demand perturbations through single-flip and per-user trajectory re-optimization, avoiding complete re-optimization. Simulations using realistic large scale constellations, including Starlink Gen-1, demonstrate that MCS-B&P achieves solution quality comparable to exact B&P with fewer column-generation iterations, fewer branch-and-bound nodes, and reduced computation time. HAVD and CAP offer effective online and offline cost-latency trade-offs, while local-search repair recovers most performance losses due to demand perturbations at a fraction of the computational cost of full re-optimization.

authors.name: Mandar R. Nalavade, Gaurav S. Kasbekar, Koushik Kar

papers.title: ATLAS: Autoregressive Trajectories for Longitudinal Analysis of Survival
papers.summary: Dynamic survival prediction requires estimates that reflect a patient's observed clinical history. We introduce ATLAS (Autoregressive Trajectories for Longitudinal Analysis of Survival), a framework that trains a sequence model on longitudinal data and autoregressively samples possible futures conditional on an individual's covariates and observed history. These trajectories form a patient-specific synthetic cohort from which Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Aalen-Johansen cumulative incidence curves are estimated. We evaluate ATLAS using two stochastic finite-state automaton benchmarks with exact conditional reference curves: a single-covariate process with duration dependence and a late rule change, and a three-covariate Markov process with recovery and competing causes of death. Comparisons include eight direct survival models, including validation-optimized DRSA and Dynamic-DeepHit and history-aware SurvTRACE adaptations, with each neural model trained nine times in the first experiment and five times in the second. After baseline, every ATLAS configuration had lower mean survival-curve error than every fitted direct comparator in both experiments. With a common Sobol sampler and 10,000 trajectories per patient, the best ATLAS model did so in every individual training run, and its mean error was 62% to 84% lower than that of the strongest direct comparator. Baseline advantages were smaller and less consistent in the duration-dependent experiment. ATLAS provides a generative framework for history-conditioned survival estimation, while the accompanying benchmarks enable direct assessment of individual survival and competing-risk predictions against known reference curves.

authors.name: Morgan Nissen, Chunyang Li, Seth Glazier, Julia Bohman, Ahmad Halwani, Jeffrey Humpherys

papers.title: Why Adaptive Optimizers Struggle with Large Convolution Kernels
papers.summary: Large convolution kernels enlarge the receptive fields of ConvNets at a modest computational cost, but they are notoriously difficult to train. Existing large-kernel networks therefore rely on costly training techniques, such as parallel small-kernel branches with batch normalization. In this paper, we trace this difficulty to adaptive optimizers such as Adam, which normalize the update of every weight separately. Since input features rarely average to zero, all weights of a kernel share a common gradient, and these optimizers move the mean of a $k\times k$ kernel $k$ times as far as a single parameter. We find this mean amplification in widely used ConvNets and vision transformers, and show that it can force the maximal learning rate to fall as $1/k^2$. We further prove that the basis of the discrete cosine transform (DCT) isolates the mean and is the only orthonormal basis that diagonalizes every stationary gradient statistic with mirrored boundaries. We therefore train large kernels through their DCT coefficients and convert them back after training. The resulting method, DCT-Rep, requires only a few lines of code and adds no parameters, no inference cost and negligible training overhead. Extensive experiments on image classification, object detection, semantic segmentation and image restoration show that DCT-Rep consistently improves large-kernel ConvNets and vision transformers, by $+0.79\%$ top-1 accuracy for a large-kernel ConvNeXt-T and $+0.43\%$ for ViT-S/16 on ImageNet-1K, $+1.4$ box AP on COCO, $+1.2$ mIoU on ADE20K and up to $+0.4$ dB on image deblurring, where the gain grows with the kernel size.

authors.name: Tianyu Ding, Jiachen Jiang, Jinxin Zhou, Yong Ma, Zhihui Zhu, Luming Liang

papers.title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds
papers.summary: Exact k-nearest-neighbor vector search lies on the critical path of machine learning systems, from sparse attention in the latest large language models (LLMs) to long-context memories and training-data deduplication. Exhaustive GPU search scans the whole dataset for every query, while approximate indexes return inexact neighbors. Recent methods skip almost every vector with a cheap half-precision proof that it lies too far away, but only on one GPU that holds the whole dataset. Our insight is to keep only the short rows of these proofs in GPU memory and to fetch the few remaining full vectors from host memory. Our system, Zarc, answers Euclidean, cosine, inner-product, and filtered queries exactly under updates. On four H100 GPUs, it answers 10,000 exact queries over one billion vectors in 1.1 seconds instead of five minutes. On eleven open LLMs, it retrieves the exact top-10 attention keys 2.2x to 13.1x faster than exhaustive search. In sparse attention over one million tokens, it runs 3.1x faster than bf16 selection with FlashInfer, which misses the exact top-64 for most queries.

authors.name: Dongfang Zhao

papers.title: Benchmarking Web Agent Defenses Against Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
papers.summary: Multimodal web agents automate website interactions but remain vulnerable to visual prompt injection (VPI), where malicious webpage content manipulates their visual processing and induces unintended actions. Although several defenses focus on detecting injected instructions in screenshots, malicious destinations such as phishing URLs embedded in HTML can remain hidden yet accessible through agent interactions. Existing evaluations have also not sufficiently examined adaptive attackers who know the defense mechanisms. To address these limitations, we introduce AdaptiveVPI, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating adaptive VPI threats in web agents. Specifically, we present a dataset of 360 webpage instances spanning 6 distinct hijack strategies across 10 real-world websites, with malicious destinations not visible in screenshots. We design an adaptive attack framework that iteratively refines malicious instructions based on feedback from the defense mechanism being evaluated. We also introduce three metrics to measure the extent of agent hijacking at three different levels. Across 10 defense configurations for computer-use agents and 11 defense configurations for browser-use agents, our adaptive attacks achieve average success rates of 91.87% and 91.99%, respectively. These results reveal a gap between current VPI defenses and realistic threats and highlight the need for defenses designed with adaptive attackers in mind.

authors.name: Haichuan Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhong, Shih-Chieh Dai, Xinyu Sun, Guanhong Tao

papers.title: A comparison of knot point screening algorithms for highly adaptive lasso
papers.summary: Highly adaptive lasso (HAL) is a nonparametric regression estimator with a rate of convergence $n^{-1/3}(\log n)^{d/2}$, where the data dimension $d$ only appears in the power of the log of sample size. This fast rate is crucial for many causal inference tasks, where efficient estimation typically requires nuisance parameters to be estimated at a specific rate. HAL achieves this rate and, when paired with semiparametrically efficient estimators -- such as those constructed using targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE) -- can be used to develop efficient estimators. Beyond causal inference, HAL is applicable to a wide range of supervised machine learning tasks. The procedure for HAL involves first performing a basis expansion on the original design matrix $X$ and then computing a lasso solution path. Cross-validation is used to select the optimal $L_1$-norm for the coefficients. For datasets with all continuous covariates and no ties, the HAL design matrix can reach a dimension as large as $n \times n(2^d-1)$, imposing a significant computational and memory burden. To address this, screening algorithms are applied at both the variable and knot-point levels to make HAL practical for datasets of moderate to large sizes. In this work, we propose outcome-blind knot point screening based on center-based clustering -- $k$-means and partitioning around medoids (PAM) -- and compare it with the quantile-based screening implemented in the hal9001 R package at matched design-matrix sizes. Across 153 simulation settings, $k$-means and PAM significantly improved test $R^2$ in 97 and 111 settings, respectively, with gains that grow with covariate skewness, while producing slightly smaller design matrices. On nine real-world datasets, they reduced the cross-validated mean squared error by 35-36% on the dataset with the most skewed predictors and performed comparably on the others.

authors.name: Yadi Weng, Sky Qiu

papers.title: $\zeta_0$: A Framework for World Action Models with Joint Scene and Body Foresight in Humanoid Control
papers.summary: World Action Models anticipate visual outcomes to guide robot actions, yet humanoid interaction also depends on how the robot's body responds. Visual foresight alone can miss body motion, while latent-distance losses do not directly supervise action responses. We present $\zeta_0$, a framework that turns vision-language-action policies into World Action Models by foreseeing future visual features and measured joint trajectories in a shared latent representation. During training, a teacher conditioned on recorded futures provides a reference action response, and dual-response transfer trains the causal predictor to match it through the teacher and the executing policy. All components are trained jointly, and deployment uses only causally predicted futures. On seven HumanoidArena tasks, $\zeta_0$ built on $\Psi_0$ and GR00T N1.7 reaches 63.6% and 79.5% mean success, 18.8 and 9.0 points above these bases. On six real-world tasks, it reaches 78.3% and 85.0%, gains of 16.7 and 10.0 points. On GR00T, its 79.5% tops all compared seven-task joint policies. Project page: https://chenyizhi123.github.io/zeta0-project/

authors.name: Yizhi Chen, Zhanxiang Cao, Yitong Wang, Junyu Liu, Hongchu Zeng, Xinyi Peng, Chuxuan Huang, Yicheng Su, Zihao Zhou, Shengcheng Fu, Haoyang Li, Liyun Yan, Tianyue Zhan, Jianming Ma, Yang Zhang, Keqi Zhu, Xiaxi Si, Jinming Yao, Qiao Sun, Shizeng Zhang, Jiangwei Zhong, Yue Gao

papers.title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
papers.summary: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. Within known energy decades below 10^16 eV, gradient boosting on nine reconstructed features is within 2.2% of the estimated floor under every estimator setting, so more capacity is not expected to gain more than about 2%. The floor is an estimate, accurate to about 1% in a semi-synthetic benchmark with intervals that under-cover, and not a bound on the true Bayes risk. Replacing reconstructed by true particle numbers removes 70 to 72% of the error variance below 10^15 eV and 24 to 26% between 10^16 and 10^17 eV on all three models, yet simulated station signals close about a tenth of that gap. On GRAPES-3, networks given images rendered from the fit do no better than the fit. In measured data, the mean muon size at fixed electron size lies within every model's proton-to-iron bracket and a label-free probe finds the muon channel used as in simulation; neither fixes the energy scale. Energy-labelled results are simulated.

authors.name: Mugdha Raje Ashiya, Samarjeet Malik

papers.title: Optimal Labelling Designs for Sequential Decisions on Language Model Updates
papers.summary: When a large language model (LLM) is updated, its developer must decide whether accuracy improved, worsened or stayed within a tolerance. An LLM judge can assess every prompt cheaply but imperfectly, while human labels are costly. We propose Sequential Decisions with Optimal Labelling Designs (SOLD), which labels one prompt at a time, uses the judge to correct the estimate of the change in accuracy and to choose the prompts, and stops once the evidence is conclusive. A wrong decision has probability at most a prespecified level whenever labelling stops. The commonly used Neyman allocation minimises the variance of the estimate and therefore rarely labels prompts that the judge is confident about. It can need far more draws when the outcomes of these prompts could still fall far below the judge's prediction. We instead derive the design that gathers evidence fastest, which labels each prompt with probability at least proportional to how far its outcome could fall below the prediction. As the level tends to zero, no procedure based on the judge-corrected estimates needs fewer draws than SOLD. In simulations and on the EVOUNA and MMLU-Pro datasets, SOLD needed fewer labels than the other methods.

authors.name: Doudou Zhou, Jiahui Xie, Yue Liu

papers.title: Phase-Conditioned Action Contracts for Auditable Microsurgical Control
papers.summary: Staged robotic procedures may reuse a fixed-dimensional policy output even though the admissible motions and physical meanings of its coordinates change across phases. We call this action-semantic shift. To address it, we propose a phase-conditioned executable policy that separates learned action proposal from deterministic command formation. Phase-specific heads generate proposals, while an action contract removes inadmissible components, enforces state-dependent bounds, and decodes the remaining action into phase-dependent task-space commands. We further introduce failure-focused local repair and a read-only provenance trace for exact command replay and rule-level auditing. Across three held-out retinal-injection evaluation blocks, our method achieves $94.27\pm0.64\%$ procedural completion and $64.40\pm2.43\%$ success within $35\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, with no hard violations. Applying the contract and decoder to the same frozen Correction network raises completion from $12.27\%$ to $90.47\%$. The trace exactly reconstructs 96,350 commands, and all 1,996 binding interventions follow their declared effects. These results show the importance of explicit executable action semantics for auditable staged microsurgical control.

authors.name: Jiaxi You, Yiwei Shi, Yanlin Li, Rihui Song, Weibing Li, Kai Huang, Weiru Liu

papers.title: A Closed-Form Soft Spectral Partition for Adaptive Mode Decomposition
papers.summary: Density-based Adaptive Mode Decomposition (DAMD) shows that the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) objective, restricted to hard binary partitions, is equivalent to weighted K-means clustering, enabling automatic mode detection. The equivalence concerns detection only; extraction with hard Voronoi masks introduces boundary artefacts. This paper develops a soft extraction theory independent of the detector. First, the hard-partition equivalence is shown to be an algebraic identity that holds if and only if the weights are binary; hard and soft extraction are optima of two different functionals (linear K-means and regularised quadratic VMD) over the same simplex. Second, the regularised soft VMD problem is proved to have a closed-form global optimum, unique on the support of the spectrum: the Lorentzian-weighted partition $s_k^*(\omega)\propto[1+2\alpha(\omega-\omega_k)^2]^{-1}$. Every fixed point of the VMD ADMM mode update is proportional to $|\omega-\omega_k|^{-2}$; when the dual ascent enforces reconstruction, it is the $\alpha\to\infty$ endpoint of this family. The Lorentzian shape at finite $\alpha$ is therefore a consequence of the regulariser, and $\alpha$ controls how closely the allocation approaches that fixed point. Third, under a Lorentzian spectral prior the partition equals the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) estimator of each mode in the low-noise limit, tying $\alpha$ to the inverse squared mode bandwidth. Since the partition needs only detected centre frequencies, the extraction rule can be switched without recomputing detection. Synthetic experiments with known ground truth test the predictions; four categories of real signals show how much the two allocations differ.

authors.name: Hao Jia, Chunyu Yang, Fan Feng, Cesar F. Caiafa, Feng Duan, Jordi Sol\'e-Casals

papers.title: What Test-Time Training Corrects in Latent World Models? A Slow-Fast Approach
papers.summary: Latent world models plan toward a goal by predicting the outcomes of candidate actions, but under the distribution shift, prediction errors can lead the planner astray. Test-time training using executed actions helps, yet what it corrects and whether its updates should persist across episodes remains unclear. We address both by analyzing the world model's prediction error. On PushObj, an object-pushing task, we probe multiple actions from the same state and decompose the error into an offset shared across actions and an action-dependent component. The offset effectively shifts the planner's goal, and AdaJEPA mainly tracks it: the common shift alone recovers 91% of its planning gain. Part of the offset is episode-specific, so carrying its correction into the next episode does not help and may even hurt. The remaining offset recurs across episodes and action-dependent error can be or needs to be learned and retained from many episodes. Our sft-JEPA therefore uses two learners on different timescales: a fast learner that tracks the offset and resets each episode, and a slow LoRA learner that accumulates recurring knowledge across episodes. Across PushObj, PointMaze, zero-shot planning on RoboCasa (with DINO-WM), and OGBench (with LeWAM), sft-JEPA leads all benchmark averages, improving planning success over AdaJEPA by up to 22 points.

authors.name: Shuaicheng Niu, Guohao Chen, Kevin Z. Shen, Yunbei Zhang, Peilin Zhao, Yinan Zhang, Cyril Leung

papers.title: PAWP-TTS: Phoneme-Aware Weight Programming for Compact Bilingual English-Nepali Speech Synthesis
papers.summary: This paper presents PAWP-TTS, a compact non-autoregressive text-to-speech system for English, Nepali, and English-Nepali code-mixed speech at 24 kHz, with no language model at inference. Deterministic pronunciation knowledge lives in a rule- and lexicon-based bilingual frontend that preserves native Nepali contrasts and avoids Hindi phonology, so the network only models acoustics. Counting every learned inference tensor, including the waveform decoder, PAWP-1.5M (1,490,390 parameters, 5.98 MB) reaches 1.50% English and 1.75% Nepali character error rate under a single ASR recognizer, and 5.04% / 4.02% Nepali / English phoneme error rate (PER) on 600 untouched test utterances. Decoder-centric 281K-parameter models (1.1 MB) stay intelligible across three independent seeds, with equal-budget dense models (5.53 +/- 0.08% NE, 5.34 +/- 0.28% EN PER) outperforming K=2 cross-layer shared-basis models (6.35 +/- 0.11% NE, 6.57 +/- 0.47% EN PER). Fixing a frontend/label version mismatch nearly halved Nepali PER, more than any architectural or weight-level change. The paper then studies weight-space programming: inspection-guided, zero-training weight edits.
