Despite large shifts in absolute mIoU, most of the reported improvement of later CLIP-only methods over SCLIP remains under the unified protocol (roughly 79% of the published gain). Decomposing official background handling shows that it combines numeric settings and class-name files whose dominant component reverses across benchmarks, while no tested tuning-free rule transfers reliably across all datasets. Moreover, exact collisions between background words and target names---present in six of seven official COCO-Object configurations through "bed"---make affected classes unpredictable under official post-processing, while the main per-class drops under language-model-generated vocabularies on VOC21 are largely attributable to a few generated terms. We offer reporting recommendations and release our evaluation code, frozen configurations, contracts, and a collision-check tool.

authors.name: Wendong Yao, Binhua Huang, Soumyabrata Dev

papers.title: AlignHand: Multi-View Hand Reconstruction from a Frozen Monocular Prior
papers.summary: Modern monocular hand estimators recover detailed 3D meshes from individual images, yet effectively leveraging their predictions across multiple views remains challenging. Independently predicted meshes can disagree in scale, placement, and articulation, limiting the integration of complementary multi-view information. Hence, we present AlignHand, a calibrated multi-view framework that builds on a frozen monocular hand reconstruction prior to align and enhance its predictions. Specifically, AlignHand refines cross-view joint observations and estimates their reliability to establish a shared metric reference for alignment. Once the meshes are brought into a common frame, their complementary surface evidence is selectively fused across anatomical regions, followed by pixel-aligned refinement that predicts bounded residual displacements from local image features. This global-to-local integration enables AlignHand to exploit complementary observations while preserving the strong monocular prior. Extensive experiments on DexYCB-MV, HanCo, and HO3D-Eval-MV demonstrate that AlignHand achieves the lowest MPVPE and MPJPE among the compared methods under the respective evaluation protocols, reducing MPVPE by 30.1%, 29.1%, and 8.0%, respectively, compared with a matched geometry baseline.

authors.name: Zhilu Yang, Kun Yang, Shiyan Wang, Anqi Xu, Xinran Huang, Yizheng Jiao, Huan Yang, Rolandos Alexandros Potamias

papers.title: Diagnosing Verbalized Confidence in a Medical Vision-Language Model for Selective Prediction on Colorectal Histopathology Patches
papers.summary: Flagging uncertain histopathology patches for specialist review needs a confidence that is higher when the model is right. We test whether an open medical vision-language model emits one. MedGemma-27b-it and its base Gemma-3-27b-it were run zero-shot under one prompt on 10,004 PathMNIST validation patches and 7,180 patches of a patient-disjoint external cohort. Both are too inaccurate to deploy (40.6% and 35.5%); the object of study is the confidence. MedGemma's verbalized confidence puts 96% of patches at one value; its confidence-correctness AUROC is 0.499 and 0.528, and routing by it moves selective-accuracy AUC by -0.004 and +0.037. Gemma-3 spreads its confidence over nine values, reaches AUROC 0.70, and gains +0.114 and +0.115. MedGemma's label-token probabilities do not rescue it: their validation advantage reverses where the top-20 alternatives include every class. On 1,800-patch subsets of each cohort, stratified on correctness and reweighted to the full splits, agreement across five prompt variants beats random by +0.123 and +0.106, and wording-only paraphrases give +0.100 and, externally and in direction only, +0.054; agreement's external margins over confidence do not survive slide-level clustering. Under one restructured prompt variant, MedGemma's stated confidence routes (+0.112, +0.141), so the failure is tied to a prompt chosen for macro F1.

authors.name: Anay Sinhal, Amit Sinhal, Ashish Pandey, Arpana Sinhal

papers.title: RAGA: Refreshable Animatable Gaussian Avatars from a Single Photo
papers.summary: Avatars created from a single photo are fixed once made: regions the photo never showed, such as the back of a garment, are hallucinated and remain that way. We present Refreshable Animatable Gaussian Avatars (RAGA), a full-body Gaussian avatar that is created from a single image in about one second and can be refreshed whenever new images of the same person become available, without retraining or gradient-based optimization. RAGA maps each new observation into canonical UV space, accumulates it as visibility- and angle-weighted running sums, and re-decodes the fused map with the same decoder used for the photo. Although this decoder is trained only on single images, it makes use of the fused evidence. On 163 clips from five datasets, RAGA created from one photo outperforms LHM, LHM++ and IDOL, including on three datasets never used in training. Refreshing from later frames adds 0.49 dB PSNR overall and 0.68 dB on views turned at least 135{\deg} from the photo, where SSIM and LPIPS also improve. Given the same 16 images on all clips, LHM++ gains 0.15 dB, against 0.48 dB for RAGA. Creating an avatar takes 1.08 s and animating it 48.1 ms per frame on a laptop RTX 3080 GPU, with body fitting and matting included in creation and pose estimation included in animation. Code will be released on GitHub.

authors.name: Sadia Mubashshira, John Quarles, Kevin Desai

papers.title: T2ISpec: Benchmarking Speculative Decoding for Text-to-Image Generation
papers.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) generators produce detailed images but remain slow at inference. Speculative decoding can reduce this cost, yet its behavior across the rendering requirements of T2I prompts remains insufficiently understood. We introduce T2ISpec, a benchmark of 1,400 prompts balanced across seven rendering topics and two difficulty levels. It evaluates autoregressive and diffusion/flow accelerators by latency, work performed by the target model, and image quality. Our study reveals three key findings: (1) aggregate results hide large differences between topics, (2) alignment and preference scores can disagree with prompt constraint satisfaction, and (3) large reductions in target work can yield limited latency gains. Motivated by these findings, we propose TopicRoute, a plugin that combines prompt routing with speculative and cache controls without retraining the generator. Across six model--method pairs, it achieves a geometric mean speedup of 1.0308x over the native methods, and the speedup carries over to external prompts with the same settings, while quality gains and losses vary across configurations.

authors.name: Yifan Zhang, Shatong Zhu, Hui Shen, Yunta Hsieh, Jianing Ma, Muxin Fu, Xin Wang, Ping Zhang, Qian Chen, Chaofan Tao

papers.title: Recurrent Point Transformer via Test-Time Training
papers.summary: Real-world point clouds are not naturally bounded: 3D scans grow as sensors move through rooms, LiDAR surveys extend across forest plots, and 4D captures can span thousands of frames. Yet most point-cloud encoders are designed for fixed-size inputs, forcing inference-time cropping or tiling that loses long-range context and requires ad-hoc output stitching. We formulate arbitrary-extent point-cloud segmentation as recurrent sequence-of-chunks processing and introduce PoinTTT, a recurrent point-cloud encoder built on Point Transformer V3 (PTv3). PoinTTT augments PTv3 with residual Large Chunk Test-Time Training (LaCT) layers in both the encoder and decoder. Each LaCT layer maintains compact fast weights as recurrent state: tokens from each chunk update the fast weights, which are then applied to produce chunk features and passed to the next chunk. This design allows PoinTTT to train on fixed-size chunks while processing scenes of arbitrary spatial or temporal extent, with activation memory bounded by the chunk size. A pilot study on ScanNet and nuScenes shows that recurrent TTT improves segmentation over PTv3 baselines. On FOR-instanceV2, PoinTTT achieves state-of-the-art forest semantic segmentation of 87.9 mIoU with nearly constant memory. On HOI4D, online full-sequence recurrent inference carries state across clips rather than resetting at benchmark boundaries, reaching 42.6 mIoU; a matched full-sequence Mamba control reaches approximately 39.9. These results suggest that test-time training is a practical primitive for scalable spatial and temporal point-cloud understanding.

authors.name: Wentao Zhou, Xuweiyi Chen, Charles Saunders, Aruni RoyChowdhury, Zezhou Cheng

papers.title: Single-Transformer Latent Diffusion
papers.summary: Latent generative models typically rely on three separate networks: an encoder that tokenizes pixels, a generator that models the latent distribution, and a decoder that maps latents back to pixels. UNITE recently merged the first two into a single generative encoder trained in one stage, but its decoder remains a separate network. We ask whether this last network can be folded in too, so that one diffusion transformer encodes, generates, and decodes. Simply letting the shared backbone decode does not help. What makes it work is to cast all three modes as position-aligned sequence maps over one fully shared backbone, distinguished only by a mode token and the timestep. The resulting model, UNIFIED, is simple: one network trained from scratch in a single stage with only reconstruction and flow-matching losses, without adversarial losses or pretrained encoders (e.g., DINO). On ImageNet-1K 256x256 at matched parameters, UNIFIED improves gFID over UNITE at three sizes (~60M, ~115M, and ~215M) and reaches 2.08 with 215M parameters, the lowest among compared models under 250M parameters. On text-to-image generation, UNIFIED-B (218M) reaches a GenEval score of 0.87 at 512x512, exceeding single-stage pixel diffusion models with around one billion parameters. Full unification of latent diffusion is thus not merely feasible but beneficial.

authors.name: Hao-Yu Hsu, Shenlong Wang, Alexander G. Schwing

papers.title: Projecting Beauty: Transferring Image Aesthetic Analysis onto 3D Heritage and Urban Scenes
papers.summary: Judgments about the beauty of buildings and streets inform architectural design, urban planning, and heritage conservation, yet increasingly rely on scanned 3D models over material fabric. Automatic aesthetic assessment remains largely confined to 2D photographs. We ask what survives when image aesthetic assessment crosses this dimensional gap to produce dense, per-point aesthetic descriptions of heritage and urban point clouds. We examine three routes that sidestep costly, and sometimes ethically dubious, human labeling at scale: (1) lifting scalar scores from image aesthetic models (NIMA, SAAN) onto geometry; (2) training Aesthetic Visual Analysis (AVA) regression heads on frozen vision backbones (DINOv3, TIPS, SigLIP2, PE, RADSeg) or, in a 3D-native variant, a generalist point encoder on feed-forward AVA reconstructions; and (3) querying lifted vision-language features with a natural-language aesthetic label, taking similarity as a score. The two supervised routes transfer poorly: heads fitting AVA in-domain produce architectural class profiles that neither reproduce one another nor track other signals, while the 3D-native probe stays near chance due to reconstruction geometry quality. Text querying is markedly more coherent. Projecting out the class-text direction from point features raises mean cross-model agreement on architectural part profiles from +0.035 to +0.352, and from +0.113 to +0.293 per point; the four backbones passing a semantic sanity check correlate at 0.31-0.73, while the failing one remains an outlier. Since model agreement is not agreement with human aesthetic perception, we detail a part-aware rating protocol to clarify where human and automatic ratings disagree. We provide a reproducible transfer protocol, an account of which pseudo-labeling routes carry signal, and dense aesthetic pseudo-labels meant as hypotheses rather than ground truth.

authors.name: Sophia Kovalenko, Alexander M. Rusnak, Vittoria Meroni, Yasmine Kroknes-Gomez, Fr\'ed\'eric Kaplan

papers.title: GAG-Net: Graph-Based Anatomical Guidance Network for Pharyngeal Area Segmentation in VFSS Images
papers.summary: Diagnosing sarcopenic dysphagia typically requires costly supplementary imaging such as CT or MRI to assess muscle atrophy, burdening elderly patients. The pharyngeal area at rest (PA_rest), measurable directly from videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) images, is a promising biomarker that could eliminate this dependency, but repeated manual measurement has limited its adoption. PA_rest segmentation is further complicated by indistinct soft-tissue boundaries and clinical rule-based delineation criteria that data-driven models capture only imprecisely. We formulate automated PA_rest segmentation as a clinically defined measurement task, translating an implicit clinical measurement into an explicit landmark specification and annotation protocol developed with a rehabilitation medicine specialist. Applying this protocol, we constructed, to our knowledge, the first dataset for this task: 2,255 single-center VFSS frames from 137 patients, with PA_rest contours and seven landmarks verified by a senior specialist. We then introduce GAG-Net, an automated rest-frame measurement pipeline combining deformable convolutions, for irregular pharyngeal boundaries, with a graph-based anatomical guidance module that models the geometric dependencies among landmarks prescribed by the delineation rules. On a patient-level held-out test set (237 frames, 67 patients), GAG-Net achieved the lowest area measurement error (mean absolute percentage error: 8.17% against specialist-verified references; patient-level ICC 0.97) and the highest Dice score (0.8862) among all evaluated methods, with 67.2% fewer parameters and 74% less training memory than the two-stage JOINED model. Integrating clinician-defined anatomical knowledge may enable automated PA_rest measurement from VFSS images alone, supporting quantitative assessment of sarcopenic dysphagia without supplementary imaging.

authors.name: JunYeong Park, Myung Woo Park, Byung Chan Lee, Hyung Jin Chang, Sang-Il Choi

papers.title: SilentWAM: Planning in the Masked State of a Diffusion World Model
papers.summary: World-action models learn from future prediction, but accessing their future representations directly at test time can require costly frame generation. Methods that generate future frames before planning incur additional forward passes, while future co-training methods omit explicit future predictions at inference. We introduce \method, a planner that reads the hidden states of masked future tokens without decoding future frames. We pretrain MMaDA-Parallel-M on driving video using frame-level masked world modeling, which predicts a masked suffix of future frames and explicitly includes inputs with all future frames masked. Learned planning queries attend to these masked positions and the observed context, and a continuous head predicts the trajectory in the same forward pass. With a single front camera, \method reaches 92.0 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 89.3 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, with an end-to-end latency of 60.3\,ms.

authors.name: Ziyu Zhao, Casey Sun, Zeyu Wang, Shicong Ma, Emily T Zhang, Cheng Lu

papers.title: Supply the Global, Supervise the Local: Combining Representation Conditioning and Alignment in Diffusion Transformers
papers.summary: A pretrained image representation helps train a diffusion transformer in several roles, including as an alignment target, which the model's hidden states learn to match, as in representation alignment (REPA), and as a condition, an extra input describing the image to be generated. Combined, they would give the model an input and a target, but whether they conflict is unknown. To test this, we let the condition carry only part of REPA's target: we split the representation of each image patch into an image-level (global) part, shared by all patches of the image, and a within-image (local) part, the patch's difference from the image-level part, and use one token carrying the image-level part as the condition. Then, the two roles overlap on the image-level part, where they could conflict, while only REPA supervises the within-image part, where we can see whether the token helps REPA. We find that the token and REPA together teach both the image-level part and the within-image part, the main source of REPA's FID improvement, far more than the sum of what each teaches alone, so they cooperate rather than conflict. These findings give one design rule for combining REPA with an image-level condition, supply the global, supervise the local, which we implement as Global-Condition REPA (GC-REPA): REPA with the token as an extra input; the token carries no information beyond REPA's target and is drawn at sampling from a separately trained token prior. GC-REPA greatly accelerates convergence: on ImageNet 256*256, SiT-XL/2 + GC-REPA reaches REPA's 4M- and SiT-XL/2's 7M-iteration FIDs within 200K and 100K iterations (20 and 70 fewer).

authors.name: Chaojie Ji, Sergio Quiroga-Sandoval, Ruxin Wang, Zheju Zheng, Yankai Cao

papers.title: RAVEC: Reward-Aligned Visual Evidence Correction
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves multimodal reasoning, but response-level feedback provides limited guidance on which intermediate decisions to correct. Visual interventions reveal sensitivity to image content, yet this sensitivity alone does not establish reward alignment or support across questions. We introduce RAVEC (Reward-Aligned Visual Evidence Correction), which selects visual corrections using local and cross-question reward support and jointly determines their strengths within each response. Paired Visual Evidence Contrast (PVEC) compares predictions from an exponential moving average teacher at the same sampled response prefix under the original image and a version with its annotated evidence region suppressed, yielding signed correction directions. Credit-Risk Allocation (CRA) screens these directions using local reward alignment and reward support from other questions, excluding all responses to the source question. It then solves a response-level budgeted allocation problem, assigning additional cost to directions that locally reduce predictive entropy. The resulting signed visual loss augments Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) during training. Inference uses only the original image and question. Across ten multimodal benchmarks, RAVEC achieves the highest average accuracy among the compared methods with both 3B and 7B Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct models, outperforming GRPO by 2.67 and 1.39 percentage points, respectively. Component ablations support the combined design of evidence alignment, credit qualification, and risk-aware allocation. The project is available at https://yangjj007.github.io/ravec/.

authors.name: Junjie Yang, Rui Qian, Xutao Mao, Yuhe Wu, Mingda Zhang, Jiaxuan Luo, Yang Tan, Qiang Huang, Zhisheng Chen, Yanfeng Li, Dawen Tian, Changmiao Wang, Tao Tan

papers.title: RVLM: Fewer Tokens, Better Resolution Scaling, Fine-Grained Spatial Grounding
papers.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) tokenize images using fixed spatial grids, so visual token count grows with pixel area rather than scene content. We propose to group neighboring patches based on their visual appearance, allowing tokens to represent coherent image regions rather than fixed spatial windows. We introduce RVLM, a VLM trained to use regions rather than patches as its visual units. Analyzing region construction for general-purpose VLMs, we find that regions must cover the full image, stay spatially connected during end-to-end training, and preserve fine structure such as small text, while semantic grouping adds little. RVLM therefore partitions images using training-free Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher segmentation, assigns each ViT patch to a region, and pools patches within each region into a variable-length sequence of visual tokens. The patch-to-region assignment is retained to support spatially precise prediction through coarse-to-fine decoding. Across tasks spanning VQA, pointing, counting, segmentation, and depth estimation, RVLM matches or improves example-weighted task performance while using 21.5% fewer visual tokens than an identically trained patch baseline. The advantage grows with image resolution, reaching a 5.3-point gain while using 51.8% fewer visual tokens at the highest-resolution setting. The gains are largest on spatially demanding tasks, where prior token-reduction methods degrade most sharply. RVLM adds no model parameters and improves inference throughput by up to 35.9%. On unseen pathology and satellite images and on video benchmarks without any video training, RVLM performs on par with the patch baseline while using 2-3$\times$ fewer visual tokens. These results establish regions as a scalable alternative to patch-based visual representations while preserving the spatial precision required for grounded prediction.

authors.name: Savya Khosla, Chris Dongjoo Kim, Alex Schwing, Derek Hoiem, Christopher Clark, Sangho Lee

papers.title: ArborNet: Volume- and skeleton-aware completion of tree quantitative structure models from incomplete point clouds using anchor-conditioned graph learning
papers.summary: Terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) enables 3D reconstruction of trees and quantitative structure models (QSMs) for estimating woody volume and structural traits. However, occlusion in single-station or sparsely sampled TLS causes incomplete branch observations and biased volume estimates. Existing point-cloud completion methods recover plausible geometry but do not explicitly preserve branch topology, cylinder radii, or woody volume. We propose ArborNet, a volume- and skeleton-aware framework for completing tree structures in the QSM domain. Each tree is represented as a TreeQSM cylinder graph encoding cylinder geometry, branch level, parent-child topology, and branch identity. A multi-relation graph encoder propagates information across parent, child, and intra-branch connections. An anchor-conditioned decoder generates missing cylinders through terminal-branch continuation and new-branch generation. Geometry, existence, branch, radius, axis-smoothness, and volume losses encourage structural consistency. During inference, generated cylinders are selected under predicted level-wise missing-volume budgets. We evaluate ArborNet on DART-simulated TLS trees and urban TLS trees from Hong Kong, using single-station QSMs as partial inputs and multi-station QSMs as references. Under budget-constrained inference, ArborNet achieves mean total-volume relative error of 0.081% and mean level-wise volume error of 0.676% against reference QSMs, while reducing skeleton geometry error relative to evaluated point-cloud completion baselines. These errors quantify agreement with reference QSMs, not accuracy against destructively measured woody volume. Ablation results show that joint volume supervision is particularly important for volume control. These results demonstrate the potential of QSM-domain completion to recover explicit woody structure while constraining geometry and volume.

authors.name: Ge Jiang, Tiangang Yin, Wei Yao, Wai Yeung Yan, Qi Chen, Jinhong Wang, Qihao Weng

papers.title: Inclusive Hand Pose Estimation via Topology-Aware Distillation and Progressive Kinematic Reasoning
papers.summary: Hand pose estimation aims to recover the spatial configuration of hand joints from visual observations and serves as a fundamental perception module for downstream systems that rely on complete and topologically consistent hand representations. Most existing methods are developed under the assumption of fully articulated hand structures and tend to produce unstable or implausible predictions when parts of the kinematic structure are persistently absent, resulting in degraded performance or even system failure despite available partial observations. To study this challenge, we construct IncNYU, a physiologically constrained benchmark that simulates structural incompleteness through morphological modification of complete hand models and retains reference locations for both intact and synthetically removed regions. Based on this benchmark, we propose InsHaPE, an Inclusive Hand Pose Estimation framework designed to remain robust under structural incompleteness while preserving performance on standard, fully articulated hands. Built on hierarchical kinematic modeling, InsHaPE introduces two complementary components. First, a topology-aware distillation strategy transfers joint-level and relational priors from fully articulated hand representations, providing anatomically consistent initialization under missing structures. Second, a progressive kinematic reasoning module performs structured inference along the kinematic chain, enabling complete and anatomically consistent pose estimation under severe structural variations. Extensive experiments on NYU/IncNYU, together with external validation on MSRA, demonstrate that InsHaPE improves robustness under structural incompleteness while maintaining competitive performance on complete hands. System-level evaluations further show that InsHaPE improves robustness for downstream applications that require fixed-topology hand pose representations.

authors.name: Kanglei Zhou, Zikai Hao, Liyuan Wang, Xiaohui Liang

papers.title: Training-Free 3D Editing via Feature-Divergence Localization and Trajectory Correction
papers.summary: Modifying 3D assets requires enacting targeted structural transformations while strictly preserving the geometric identity of unedited regions. While recent probability flow models enable training-free editing, bounding these modifications within a high-dimensional latent space presents severe mathematical challenges. Current inversion-free trajectories rely on global velocity updates, which often cause spatial bleed into preserved structures and induce trajectory under-commitment, causing edits to stall mid-path. To resolve these dual failures, we introduce FocusFlow, a segmentation-free framework that structures the integration trajectory into two disjoint phases. During early coarse structure formation, FocusFlow applies Feature-Divergence Localization (FDL) to spatially gate the velocity field using intrinsic cross-attention. Once coarse structure has formed, FocusFlow applies Reference Generation Guidance (RGG), a trajectory-correction term that drives convergence to the target shape by pulling the trajectory toward an explicit clean-latent target. Evaluated on the joint Google Scanned Objects and PartObjaverse-Tiny benchmarks, FocusFlow obtains the best preservation scores and the largest edit magnitude among compared methods, suggesting that it can reduce the traditional preservation-modification trade-off. By providing stable, localized geometric control without manual spatial annotations, this phase-scheduled approach lowers technical barriers to the modification of synthetic 3D media.

authors.name: Tri Ton, Siwoo Lim, Joshua Tian Jin Tee, Chang D. Yoo

papers.title: Decoupling Perception from Generation for Agentic 3D CT Report Generation
papers.summary: Chest CT reports repeatedly assess the same anatomical regions for findings and their attributes, such as whether a lung nodule is present and where it is located. These assessments suggest learning to answer visual questions directly, rather than coupling perception to open-ended text generation. Yet current CT report generation models largely follow generic vision-language modeling, which may miss subtle abnormalities when training data are limited. We therefore formulate report generation as a set of visual question-answering decisions coordinated by a large language model (LLM) agent. This decouples visual perception from reasoning and report writing: perception can be learned as a discriminative, non-generative task, while the LLM focuses on reasoning over patient context and posing relevant visual queries. We introduce Rad-VL-JEPA, which unifies report retrieval, finding recognition, and fine-grained attribute characterization through vision-language joint-embedding prediction. Building on this perception module, an agent trained with reinforcement learning (RL) acquires patient-specific visual evidence, while a separate editor incorporates the evidence into the final report, further separating evidence acquisition from report realization. Experiments show that Rad-VL-JEPA achieves strong performance on fine-grained CT understanding tasks with lower amortized per-query inference time than a generative VLM baseline trained with the same CT encoder and VQA data. The resulting reporting system outperforms strong VLM-based and agentic baselines.

authors.name: Chenyu Wang, Mingyu Chen, Wenchao Li, Kayhan Batmanghelich

papers.title: SpatialDuet: Bayesian task routing between a metric expert and a geometry expert for spatial intelligence
papers.summary: Embodied assistants and wearable devices need 3D spatial reasoning, and their limited hardware restricts them to small vision-language models (VLMs). Small spatial VLMs acquire different abilities from their training: a model trained on large spatial question sets estimates object and room sizes well, whereas a model with a 3D geometry encoder is better at relative directions and absolute distances. Instead of training a single model for all spatial tasks, as published methods do, we build one system that uses each frozen model for the tasks it handles best. We propose SpatialDuet, which pairs a metric expert with a geometry expert under a Bayesian task router. The metric expert is a data-driven spatial VLM run with three training-free modules: training-aligned sampling, metric-aware minimum Bayes risk decoding and per-type metric calibration. The geometry expert is a VLM with a 3D geometry encoder. For each question type, the router estimates from labelled development questions how likely each expert is to be better, and pools their answers with that probability as weight, in log space for numeric answers and over the option distributions for multiple-choice answers. Extensive experiments on four spatial benchmarks covering video and single images validate SpatialDuet; it outperforms the best published small VLMs by 3.17% on VSI-Bench and, excluding a model trained on CV-Bench-style data, by 1.44% on CV-Bench, without training any model weight.

authors.name: Duy Tran Thanh

papers.title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics
papers.summary: Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit. Existing evaluations with counterfactual target videos mainly cover object removal or specific rigid-body motions, although real scenes also involve elastic deformation, fluid flow, and interactions among rigid bodies, elastic solids, and fluids. We introduce PhyCoVE, a benchmark of 533 cases on 110 source videos that covers rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics in five interaction patterns, with edits that remove an object, change a physical quantity, or insert a new object. For the simulated cases, a language model proposes scene designs, coding agents build them with solvers suited to each material and physically based rendering and then simulate each edit from the source scene state, and humans check every stage. For the real cases, we record continuously from one camera position before and after each edit. We also propose counterfactual fidelity, a metric that applies across materials and their interactions and measures how much of the physical change from the source video to the target video a generated video reproduces. We evaluate seven open-source and commercial video editing models and find that counterfactual fidelity ranks them nearly as human preference does, but even the best model reproduces only about one seventh of the physical change. The models change how a scene looks but rarely how it evolves, whereas a physical edit requires understanding the dynamics that it changes. Physical counterfactual video editing thus remains far from solved, and PhyCoVE provides a foundation for developing and evaluating methods for it.

authors.name: Conghan Yue, Yuanjie Chen, Yunyan Xiao, Zeyu Peng, Xingsong Ye, Ya Gao, Yanglin Huang, WeiYao Zhang, Yue Han, Zhineng Chen, Yu-Gang Jiang

papers.title: Unleashing the Value of Raw Point Clouds for 3D Understanding with LLMs
papers.summary: Standard 3D point cloud language models typically rely on pretrained point encoders to extract 3D features and project them into representations processable by large language models (LLMs). However, these encoders are often originally optimized for pre-defined tasks, resulting in a representation bottleneck that may lead to a substantial mismatch with downstream 3D understanding. Moreover, existing models largely follow a single pass closed-book generation, limiting their ability to actively inspect task-relevant 3D regions or retrieve necessary external knowledge. In this work, we present PointTool, an encoder-free and tool-augmented framework for 3D reasoning. PointTool introduces Alignment-Free Patch Tokenization (AFPT) to locally aggregate raw point clouds while preserving fine-grained geometric structure, and Decoupled Point-Text LoRA (DPL) to facilitate global aggregation and 3D knowledge internalization within a frozen LLM. Building upon these designs, Program-Supervised Tool Reasoning (PSTR) enables the model to explicitly operate on raw 3D data and external resources through executable tools, supporting interactive 3D reasoning grounded in spatial evidence. We further introduce PointCloud-TR, a benchmark comprising 13K 3D objects, 39.8K questions, and 35.6K tool trajectories to facilitate training and evaluation of complex 3D reasoning. Experiments demonstrate that PointTool achieves strong performance on both standard and complex 3D understanding tasks, validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

authors.name: Tailai Chen, Jiawei Yu, Yiming Cheng, Ping Nie, Yongyong Chen, Tao Zhou, Zheng Zhu, Ming Li

papers.title: PartPO: Part-Level Policy Optimization for Shape-to-Program Generation
papers.summary: We present PartPO, a reinforcement learning method for generating structured shape programs from 3D point clouds. Existing shape-to-program models are trained with supervised learning on procedurally generated data and generalize poorly to more diverse shapes, while reinforcement learning from execution feedback assigns a single scalar reward to a long program that builds many parts, making credit assignment difficult. PartPO instead builds on a core property of the task: shape programs are self-describing, with each semantically named part produced by its own code block. It segments each generated program by its parts and applies part-level rewards only to the code of the corresponding part, a category reward only to the object name, and a shape-level reward to the whole program. The required part supervision is obtained without manual annotation, by grounding part names on target meshes with an open-vocabulary segmentation model prompt-tuned on the model's own outputs. Applied to MeshCoder, PartPO improves reconstruction accuracy and execution success on ShapeNetCore and ABO over the base model, rejection-sampling fine-tuning and trajectory-level RL, and generalizes to the unseen HSSD dataset. Code will be released at https://github.com/HannuoZ/PartPO.

authors.name: Hannuo Zhang, Zhixiang Chi, Xuanchen Li, Yiqun Zhou, Yang Wang, Xinxin Zuo

papers.title: Complementary Geometry in Gaussian Splatting
papers.summary: Gaussian Splatting has achieved high visual quality in novel view synthesis, but the accuracy of its rendered geometry remains a challenge. In particular, the rendered depth is computed as an opacity-weighted average along each ray, which may not correspond to the actual scene surface. In this paper, we observe that depth predictions from different views of the same frozen Gaussian representation exhibit complementary errors, allowing us to improve novel-view geometry using information from other views without modifying the original representation. Based on this observation, we propose REVEAL, a general framework that selectively refines novel-view depth using complementary geometric information. Specifically, we first reproject depth predictions from source views to the target view and combine them using robust multi-view consensus. We then introduce a learned selection mechanism to determine whether the candidate depth is more accurate than the original prediction, based on the expected reduction in depth error. In addition, we introduce RIG, a real-world benchmark captured with synchronized RGB-D cameras, which provides ground-truth depth for evaluating both static and dynamic reconstruction models. Experiments on 6 Gaussian Splatting backbones across 3 benchmarks show that REVEAL consistently improves depth accuracy while maintaining comparable rendering quality.

authors.name: Mingle Jiang, Jikui Zhou, Chenghan Lyu, Rui Xu, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

papers.title: MM-DataLoop: Closing the Data-Side Loop for Recursive Self-Improvement in MLLM Post-Training
papers.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a path toward improving models through repeated evaluation and revision. We study its data side in multimodal language model (MLLM) post-training, where heterogeneous operations and cross-round evidence must be coordinated. MMDataLoop organizes data interventions into five operation families and connects them through an Observe-Diagnose-Plan-Execute-Verify-Reflect cycle with shared rule memory. Across 34 candidate rounds on Qwen3.5-0.8B and five benchmarks, we hold the base initialization, shared training schedule and evaluation protocol fixed while varying data recipes. The five-benchmark mean reaches 63.04 at R33, up 5.32 points from the zero-shot baseline; R29, R32, and R33 form a close top cluster within 0.09 points. In eightcandidate comparisons, guided search reaches the preselected target in six candidates and identifies the top observed candidate, while random arms show higher means and lower dispersion. The selected R29 recipe also scores above two full-pool baselines under the same epoch schedule. Together, these findings establish MM-DataLoop as a traceable workflow and provide an empirical basis for studying how data-side decisions shape outcomes across MLLM post-training recipes.

authors.name: Likang Peng, Chen Ju, Xu Chen, Xiangyang Wu, Jinsong Lan, Haihong Tang, Ying Chen

papers.title: CFANet: Learning Conflict-Free Weather Adapters for All-Weather Image Restoration
papers.summary: All-weather image restoration aims to recover clean images from diverse weather degradations such as rain, haze, and snow. Most existing all-in-one methods handle different weather types with a unified network or rely on single-label weather modeling. However, real-world adverse weather is often compositional, where multiple known weather primitives may coexist in a single image. To this end, we propose Conflict-Free Adapter Network (CFANet) for open-compositional all-weather image restoration. CFANet first employs a Weather Mixture Router (WMR) to predict non-exclusive composition weights for rain, haze, and snow from shallow features. Guided by these weights, a Shared-Private Weather Adapter (SPWA) dynamically composes a common adapter with weather-private adapters inside each Conflict-Free Adapter Block, preserving shared restoration capability while providing weather-specific residual adaptation. Moreover, a lightweight Natural Color Adapter (NCA) performs constrained color calibration to improve color fidelity and visual naturalness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive adverse weather image restoration performance and benefits downstream visual tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/wenchao-tech/CFANet-main

authors.name: Minglong Xue, Wenchao Yan, Guoan Guan, Palaiahnakote Shivakumara, Yirui Wu

papers.title: ContinuLoc: Continuous Pose Inference over Neural Fields for UAV Geo-Localization
papers.summary: Cross-view UAV geo-localization involves three design choices: how to represent the UAV observation, how to represent the geo-referenced map, and how to infer pose from their interaction. The dominant paradigm organizes the map as a discretized 2DoF candidate library, coupling map representation to pose inference and thus bounding spatial localization precision by candidate sampling resolution. We decouple map representation from pose inference by encoding the geo-referenced map as a continuously queryable semantic neural field, enabling localization to be formulated as explicit optimization over a continuous 4DoF pose space parameterized by 2D ground position, in-plane heading, and viewing scale. Pose hypotheses are evaluated on demand using global descriptors in a shared semantic feature space, bypassing the sampling bottleneck of retrieval. We learn 4DoF pose-sensitive visual representations under full 4DoF supervision provided by ContinuScenes, a multi-city benchmark with dense near-nadir UAV imagery and complete pose annotations. Inference proceeds hierarchically, progressing from broad pose-space coverage to adaptive concentration on high-compatibility regions. Experiments demonstrate substantial gains over representative localization paradigms under progressively stricter 4DoF accuracy criteria. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhouWeikun/ContinuLoc/

authors.name: Weikun Zhou, Jinliang Lin, Yu Zang, Lin Xie, Haiqing Fu, Sheng Ao, Shangshu Yu, Zhiming Luo, Cheng Wang

papers.title: One-shot is Enough: Boosting SAM for Medical Image Segmentation through Structured Information Modeling
papers.summary: In recent years, Foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization capabilities, but because they are primarily pre-trained on natural images, they perform poorly when faced with medical images. With sufficient labeled medical data, this challenge is somewhat alleviated. However, the difficulty and high cost of acquiring large amounts of labeled data make one-shot learning a highly attractive research paradigm. But within this paradigm, SAM struggles to fully extract its potential multi-granular information, leading to a sharp decline in performance. To address this, we propose OB-SAM, a one-shot enhancement framework for medical image segmentation. It aims to maximize the utilization of information from a single sample from the perspective of structured modeling. Specifically, we first designed a Multi-Frequency Decoupling (MFD) module, which divides features into different frequency domain components, allowing each branch to focus on information expression at different semantic levels, thereby alleviating overfitting and enhancing feature representation capabilities. Secondly, we introduce a Progressive Feature Integrator (PFI) module to promote complementary fusion among multi-level features, thereby avoiding the dominant effect of a certain level of feature in the fusion process. Furthermore, we propose an Selective Context Filtering (SCF) Module that adaptively selects key contextual information by modeling the contrast relationship between the foreground and background, thereby achieving precise localization of the lesion area. Extensive experiments across seven diverse datasets validate that OB-SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance.

authors.name: Guilin Guan

papers.title: RadioWorld: Transferring World Models to Radio-Frequency Radiance Fields
papers.summary: Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation in the physical world constitutes a Radio-Frequency (RF) radiance field, providing rich information for 6G communication and sensing. However, existing neural RF field methods suffer from three fundamental limitations: (1) they predominantly rely on per-scene optimization and cannot generalize to unseen scenes; (2) they require costly reference RF measurements in each target scene; and (3) they degrade severely when extrapolating beyond the vicinity of reference measurements. To overcome these limitations, we present RadioWorld, a general framework that adapts a world model to synthesize RF radiance fields directly from physical scene geometry and transceiver locations, without requiring any reference RF measurements at inference. Specifically, RadioWorld couples two specialized modules within a dual-stream Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture: a Scene-Understanding Transformer that encodes 3D scene geometry and transceiver locations to extract environment-aware global EM propagation features, and a Field-Generation Transformer that attends to these features to synthesize the RF radiance field with the local query conditions. We also establish UrbanRF-Bench, a large-scale ray-traced benchmark spanning 657 urban scenes and 32,850 RF radiance fields across seven global cities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RadioWorld significantly outperforms specialized baselines and accurately synthesizes RF fields at arbitrary locations in unseen cities. Code, datasets, and checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.

authors.name: Hu Zhou, Jiazhou Zhou, Shuowen Zhang, Ying-Chang Liang, Liang Liu

papers.title: Robust Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Models via Simulating Brain Functional Localization
papers.summary: Concept erasure in text-to-image models aims to prevent a target concept from appearing in generated images while preserving general image generation capability. However, erased concepts can still be reactivated by attacks. Prior attacks mainly search text or image input spaces, leaving the initial latent space underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce IVO (Initial latent Variable Optimization), a new concept reactivation attack that changes the starting point of image generation by optimizing the initial latent. Comprehensive experiments across 8 erasure methods show that IVO reactivates erased concepts more effectively than the attack baselines, revealing a blind spot in erasure robustness evaluation. This motivates us to localize model components associated with the target concept and then treat them as intervention sites for more robust concept erasure. We propose CeFlune (Concept Erasure via Functional Localization of Unit Neurons), which adapts brain functional localization to text-to-image models. CeFlune defines linear modules as Unit Neurons and localizes concept-responsive ones by comparing their response trajectories in the model's task and resting states. It then updates the localized Unit Neurons to constrain their responses and the erased model's predictions. Across U-Net diffusion and flow-matching transformer architectures, CeFlune achieves a favorable balance between concept erasure and general image generation capability in comparisons with up to 15 baseline methods. Under IVO and 4 other evaluated attacks, CeFlune also shows lower concept reactivation.

authors.name: Manyi Li, Yufan Liu, Bing Li, Xia Wu, Ziyu Li, Weiming Hu

papers.title: CT-Navigator: Towards Interpretable and Generalizable CT Understanding through Agentic Perception and Tool-Invocation
papers.summary: Clinical computed tomography (CT) interpretation inherently requires progressive visual exploration, where radiologists navigate from whole scans to individual slices and regions of interest and interact with external tools when necessary. However, existing 3D medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) typically connect a specialized 3D visual encoder to a language model, without fully leveraging the native 2D visual and agentic capabilities of generalist MLLMs. Trained on large-scale one-hop CT instruction-following data, these models also have limited ability to perform iterative reasoning and explicitly ground their conclusions in visual evidence, limiting their support for traceable CT interpretation. To solve these problems, we propose \textbf{agentic perception} as an alternative paradigm inspired by radiologists' interpretation workflows. We introduce \textbf{CT-Navigator}, a framework that harnesses generalist MLLMs' 2D visual and agentic capabilities to progressively ground CT interpretation in explicit, traceable visual evidence through hierarchical visual exploration and radiology tool invocation. To build these capabilities, we curate 8,904 visual chain-of-thought (V-CoT) trajectories for cold-start agentic supervised fine-tuning. We then optimize the policy through reinforcement learning on 33,219 questions, with data selection and dynamic rollout sampling prioritizing informative learning signals. Finally, we introduce CTNavi-Bench, a 3D CT visual question answering benchmark comprising 7,000 questions spanning anatomical regions throughout the human body. CT-Navigator achieves 79.50\% accuracy on CTNavi-Bench, surpassing the strongest baseline by 17.59\%, and demonstrates strong generalization across three external CT benchmarks. The code, model, and benchmark will be released on \href{https://github.com/fyb99/ct_navigator}{GitHub}.

authors.name: Yibing Fu, Huidong Xie, Yihao Niu, Wei Ji, Heming Dong, Ziyue Wang, Jingyu Chen, Jun Zhao, Haoyuan Hu, Hongming Shan, Lai Jiang, Mai Xu, Yueming Jin

papers.title: Where Does Personalization Reside in Photo Editing? Evidence from One Photographer's Lightroom History
papers.summary: Personalized photo-editing systems must infer both a photographer's recurring preferences and the intent of a particular shoot, yet these signals are rarely evaluated separately. We study interpretable Lightroom adjustments in a longitudinal, private dataset of 3,193 edited photographs from 41 catalogs by one professional photographer, with holdouts formed at the batch level. We compare absolute and prior-relative targets, image-conditioned predictors, and estimators that receive a small set of edits from the target batch. Residual prediction improves validation error, but its advantage on held-out batches is small and not significant under a batch-clustered bootstrap (0.592 vs 0.582 EV exposure MAE). In a batch-shared protocol, closed-form shrinkage using 4, 8, or 16 same-batch anchors reaches 0.466, 0.457, or 0.453 EV with the best estimator at each k, compared with 0.586-0.592 EV for the prior-only baseline; the paired reductions are significant under a batch-clustered bootstrap. Learned anchor-conditioned heads do not improve on this closed-form estimator, and a negative-trained prior already yields a low cold-image false-edit rate, leaving little benefit for an additional gate. The recommended estimator is closed-form and auditable, and it requires only a handful of same-batch edits. A render-space check against 383 native Lightroom exports reproduces the ranking: at k=8, online EB lowers Delta E00 against the prior by 0.41 (p=0.042), and the photographer's true parameters lower it by 0.78 (p=0.034). An appendix extends the action space from six to thirteen global controls: a same-batch median look lowers rendered chroma toward the export, while a per-photograph residual head again fails to transfer. The study is limited to one photographer and does not claim that slider accuracy measures aesthetic preference.

authors.name: Dongwu Qian

papers.title: Prompt-Consistent Cross-View Object Geo-Localization
papers.summary: Cross-view object geo-localization (CVOGL) aims to locate an object indicated by a click point in a ground or drone query image within a satellite reference image. Through a quantitative prompt-sensitivity evaluation, we find that existing CVOGL methods suffer from a prompt-disobeying overfitting problem: when the click point is moved or removed, their predictions barely respond, indicating that the models rely on spurious feature correlations rather than genuinely following the prompt semantics. We trace this behavior to the limited scale of the benchmark dataset, which contains only 4,343 prompt-object pairs per task, so that the models simply memorize the object associated with each scene instead of learning the true prompt-to-object correspondence. To address this, we propose two plug-and-play components. First, we construct the CVOGL-MO dataset by expanding the existing training and test sets with diverse multi-object annotations, mitigating the memorization that induces shortcut learning. Second, we propose the Cross-View Co-Scene Multi-Object Contrastive Loss (CVMCL), which enforces distinct feature representations for different click points within the same scene, compelling the model to follow prompt instructions. We further design a prompt-sensitivity evaluation protocol with prediction-shift metrics, providing the first quantitative measurement of prompt-following capability for CVOGL. Both components are architecture-agnostic and can be integrated into existing methods without any architectural modification. Experiments on three representative backbones show that our components substantially improve prompt-following accuracy on the new multi-object test sets and markedly increase prompt sensitivity. Our dataset and code will be publicly released at https://github.com/Sunny-Fresher/CVOGL-MO.

authors.name: Lingyun Xing, Wenning Hao, Kai Jiang, Dawei Jin, Xiaohan Zhang, Xiaoxiong Zhang

papers.title: SKIA: Spatial-Knowledge Informed Attention for Robust Remote Photoplethysmography under Lower-Face Motion Artifacts
papers.summary: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) enables contactless physiological monitoring from facial videos, but facial motion, particularly mouth and jaw movements during cognitive and communicative tasks, can severely degrade signal reconstruction. We present SKIA, a lightweight, mask-guided framework that suppresses motion-prone lower-face regions while preserving physiological cues from the forehead and cheeks. Using the UBFC-rPPG benchmark, we first investigate static lower-face suppression in the classical CHROM pipeline. Static masking improves waveform Pearson correlation from 0.3507 to 0.4166 (p < 0.001) and reduces heart-rate mean absolute error (MAE) from 33.50 to 23.44 bpm. Building on this finding, we introduce SKIA-Net, a compact spatiotemporal architecture that combines raw facial frames, statically masked representations, and temporal motion differences to reconstruct blood volume pulse (BVP) waveforms. The full model achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.7522 and a heart-rate MAE of 3.73 bpm on UBFC-rPPG, outperforming single-stream variants. Ablation studies show that the static mask provides complementary information to raw appearance and that static anatomical priors outperform the tested dynamic optical-flow-based masking strategy. These results suggest that spatially informed, temporally stable masking can improve motion-robust rPPG estimation. Code: https://github.com/lee-vtruong/SKIA-rPPG

authors.name: Van-Truong Le, Viet-Tham Huynh, Minh-Triet Tran

papers.title: Probe Before You Learn: Allocating Prompts from Initial Gradients under Label Noise
papers.summary: Prompt learning provides a parameter-efficient way to adapt pretrained vision--language models through text and visual prompts, but noisy labels prevalent in real-world data inevitably bias prompt updates and thereby undermine adaptation effectiveness. Prior work on robust prompt learning focuses on suppressing unreliable updates under noisy supervision. We uncover a pivotal yet overlooked aspect--prompt allocation: shifting the parameter budget between text and visual prompts can substantially enhance robustness while keeping the training objective and total budget fixed. However, suitable prompt allocations vary across tasks and are unknown a priori, rendering brute-force candidate training computationally prohibitive. We propose GPrompt, a training-free method that derives allocation between text and visual prompts using only loss gradients at initialization before prompt optimization. Using a small sample of images and generated pseudo-labels as shared supervision, GPrompt performs an initialization probe to extract paired text and visual loss gradients, and characterizes the geometry of their trace-normalized Gram matrices through both concentration within each modality and overlap between modalities. GPrompt then derives a closed-form allocation, and projects it onto feasible prompt counts under the exact parameter budget, enabling task-specific selection without training candidate configurations. Experiments across eleven datasets show that GPrompt outperforms the strongest baseline by up to 7.75% while selecting configurations close to the best allocation identified through exhaustive training. The average runtime of gradient probe across datasets is 99.9% lower than that of exhaustive candidate training.

authors.name: Jiazhe Zhang, Zibin Geng, Qiang Ma, Xuefeng Jiang, Yijun Lin, Jingyi Wang, Yu Yan, Xingzhou Zhang, Min Liu, Yuwei Wang, Sheng Sun

papers.title: MIMORPHEUS: Rethinking Cross-Modal Supervision for Human Pose Estimation from Radar Signals
papers.summary: Deep learning has shown promise for estimating human pose with multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar through walls. Building paired radar and pose datasets demands considerable time and manual effort, while large visual pose datasets provide no corresponding radar echoes. Physical simulation can supply synthetic signals, but requires expertise in scattering models and can leave a gap between simulated and real data. To address this challenge, we introduce MIMORPHEUS, a framework that generates radar echoes from 3D human poses through conditional diffusion. To prepare echo and pose representations, MIMO-VAE compresses the echoes according to their channel and fast time sample structure, while SkeleCoder learns pose features through contrastive alignment with echo features. These pose features then guide diffusion in the MIMO-VAE latent space, and the VAE decoder reconstructs echoes from the generated latents. Once trained, the generator augments radar data by producing different echoes for a recorded pose and supplies the radar modality for pose annotations in existing visual datasets. In data augmentation experiments, our method reduces MPJPE by 6.8%-11.2% across four radar pose estimators. Transfer experiments with three public pose datasets also show that visual pose annotations can supply useful radar training data. Code will be made publicly available on GitHub.

authors.name: Shizhao Zhang, Yanyan Zhang, Deshui Yu, Jun Pan, Guangyou Fang

papers.title: A Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Color Normalization Methods in Histopathology: Nuclei Preservation, Artifact Sensitivity, Background Fidelity, and Downstream Performanc
papers.summary: Deep learning models for nuclei detection and classification may generalize poorly across medical centers because of variations in staining and scanning. Although color normalization aims to reduce these variations, its effects on nuclear structure, background preservation, artifact sensitivity, and nuclei detection and classification performance have not been systematically evaluated. We present a procedure to benchmark 11 classical and deep learning normalization methods using 7 public and private nuclei datasets. Additionally, we investigate the effect of 7 input color spaces. The normalization methods differed in their effects on nuclear structure, background, and sensitivity to artifacts. However, detection and classification performance varied more across datasets than across normalization methods, and the input color space had limited influence. No single method performed best on all criteria, and image-level metrics did not reliably predict downstream performance, highlighting the need for nuclei- and structure-aware normalization methods. To support this work, we introduce WSI Quality Control and Normalization (WSI-QCN), a publicly available pipeline for robust whole-slide image quality assessment and color normalization; the source code is available on GitHub.

authors.name: Falah Jabar, Aria Torkpour, Pasquale Lombardi, Masoud Tafavvoghi, Per Niklas Benzler Waaler, Sigve Andersen, Ilona Urbarova, David J. Pinato, Mehrdad Rakaee, Tom Donnem, Lill-Tove Rasmussen Busund, Elin Richardsen

papers.title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?
papers.summary: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. We introduce Polytropos, a benchmark that measures what model descriptions of cultural objects keep of the particular object by turning each description back into an image and comparing it with the original photograph. On 374 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty, with 1,870 descriptions from five models and 230 written by curators, reconstructions are recognised as the recorded culture more often than the photographs, at 54.55% to 59.09% against 52.14%, yet 16% to 21% of objects change outcome and only 0.49% of reconstructions are identified as the specific object. On the same objects, models lose recorded cultures at a rate similar to curators but gain more. Model descriptions give each object many faces, each typical of its culture and almost none the object itself.

authors.name: Yuechen Jiang, Enze Zhang, Yuyan Wang, Mohsinul Kabir, Chenying Lin, Sijia Li, Qianqian Xie, Stavroula Golfomitsou, Konstantinos Arvanitis, Sophia Ananiadou

papers.title: Beyond Attention Maps: Understanding and Improving Medical MLLMs via Visual Values
papers.summary: Current MLLM methods largely focus on whether models attend to the right visual regions, implicitly treating spatial attention map as the primary key of effective visual perception. To examine this assumption, we introduce a medical VQA dataset with paired non-contrast (NC) and contrast-enhanced (CE) images that share corresponding anatomy while providing different cues. We show that this view is incomplete: across paired NC and CE medical images, MLLMs often exhibit similar attention patterns despite producing contrasting answers, while controlled bidirectional interventions induce substantially larger prediction changes on visual values than attention weights. These results identify the visual content retrieved through values as a critical factor in improving perception beyond spatial attention alone. Guided by this finding, we propose VIVID (VIsual Value Intervention Distillation), which uses enhanced visual values to identify and refine teacher corrections aligned with useful visual evidence to improve on-policy distillation from CE to NC images. Across six internal and external test sets, VIVID consistently outperforms existing on-policy distillation methods across different model scales and architectures, requires only NC images at inference, and maintains strong zero-shot performance on general-domain VQA benchmarks. The project page is available at https://qiuzyc.github.io/VIVID.

authors.name: Yichen Zhao, Fenghe Tang, Wenxin Ma, Rongsheng Wang, Zihao Wan, Shaohua Kevin Zhou

papers.title: Scenario Compliant Indoor Pedestrian Trajectory Reconstruction from Partial Observation
papers.summary: Pedestrian trajectory reconstruction is vital for applications ranging from security surveillance to indoor navigation. While existing probabilistic and generative frameworks have shown success in outdoor GPS-based trajectory imputation, they often fail in indoor settings where movement is strictly governed by dense geometric constraints such as walls and corridors. Standard models typically treat trajectories as unconstrained coordinate sequences, leading to physically infeasible paths with high collision rates. To address this, we propose a map-conditioned generative framework based on conditional diffusion models. Our approach explicitly integrates dense scenario maps as structured spatial inputs via a CNN-based encoder, allowing environmental geometry to guide the iterative denoising process. Furthermore, we employ an endpoint-aware mechanism by embedding observations (start and end points) directly into the scenario map, providing critical spatial anchors through image-level features. Experiments on simulated indoor trajectories and the real-world Shopper trajectory dataset, with three training seeds, show that our method achieves the lowest errors among the compared generative methods. Scene conditioning reduces the collision and invalid rates by 19\% and 46\% on the simulated dataset, whereas on real shopper data the gains are consistent but small, mainly because the model rarely learns to route around obstacles between the endpoints. Compared with a shortest-path planner, which never collides, our method better captures the variability of real motion (31\% lower CRPS), but the timing of stops is reconstructed only partially. These results show that explicit environmental context improves physical consistency, while reconstructing realistic human motion in real indoor spaces remains challenging. Our code is available at https://github.com/dang-qi/trajectory_reconstruction

authors.name: Qi Dang, Luis Quintero, Shibo Zhu, Oskar Juhlin, Xiaodan Shi

papers.title: ClothCast: Generative Cloth World Modeling under Partial Observability
papers.summary: World models support robotic manipulation by predicting how the scene evolves under a planned action. For garments this prediction is notoriously difficult: deformations are complex, and self-occlusion leaves much of the cloth unobserved. Planned gripper trajectories provide a useful motion prior because cloth held by a gripper moves with it, while the remaining deformation must be predicted. We introduce ClothCast, a world model that applies this prior to the cloth's points and learns the residual motion. ClothCast takes one RGB-D observation, the camera pose, the robot's own model and the planned gripper trajectories, with no cloth mesh or material parameters. It lifts the observation to a layered point set that includes hypothesized occluded layers, carries the points with a blended rigid prior derived from the gripper poses, and predicts the residual motion with a video-diffusion point-flow model. Over entire 4- to 11-second episodes at 10 Hz, the moved points are rendered into depth, from which a geometry-conditioned completion model synthesizes RGB; after release, a hand-designed settling step replaces the learned motion. We further release ClothCastBench, 10,000 simulated dual-arm cloth-manipulation episodes with the ground-truth cloth mesh, including occluded layers, at every frame. On 492 held-out episodes, ClothCast achieves 2.5x lower sequence-averaged visible-surface Chamfer distance than Flex-{\pi}, the strongest baseline in geometry (14.0 mm vs. 35.6 mm), and 3.7 dB higher cloth-region PSNR than Cosmos-Predict2.5, the strongest baseline in cloth PSNR. On a 50-episode ablation subset, the rigid prior alone, applied to ClothCast's learned initial geometry with the same post-processing, already outperforms both geometry-capable baselines, and the learned residual lowers its error by about a third.

authors.name: Yushen Hu, Yilong Song, Zhen Zhou, Apurv Kushwaha, Harshvardhan Chandirasekar, Zhu-Tian Chen

papers.title: SpectralGS: Spectral Gaussian Splatting for Unsupervised Spectral Super-Resolution
papers.summary: Unsupervised spectral super-resolution aims to recover spectral information from RGB images without paired hyperspectral data. However, the limited spectral information in RGB observations makes learning an effective spatial-spectral representation challenging, requiring the incorporation of structured spectral modeling with sensor imaging. In this paper, we propose SpectralGS, a spectral Gaussian splatting framework comprising two components: Shared Spectral Gaussian Representation and Spectral Response Projection Rendering. The representation module constructs a continuous spatial-spectral representation via shared spectral and local spatial Gaussian primitives, exploiting the low-rank spectral structure of hyperspectral images. The rendering module utilizes the spectral response function (SRF) to apply integral projection to the continuous representation, blending it to generate an RGB image. Consistency between the rendered and observed RGB images provides training supervision. Our main contribution is a Gaussian splatting framework that integrates structured continuous spatial-spectral representation with imaging response-based rendering, enabling unsupervised spectral reconstruction. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

authors.name: Qiaoying Qu, Bin Pan, Chen Jia, Haiyang Xu, Xia Xu, Zhenwei Shi

papers.title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model
papers.summary: Understanding a scene requires both geometry and semantics: geometry recovers its spatial structure, and semantics separates it into objects. Current models obtain the two from separate networks or separate passes. We present PINE, a one-step Omni Diffusion Transformer that predicts the point map, the surface normals, and the instance map of an image in one forward pass. PINE treats each map as a token stream, and a stream mask decides which streams interact. A camera-aware ray encoding positions every token by its camera ray rather than its pixel. Grounding attention adds the affinity of pretrained DINOv3 features to the attention logits. Trained on only 139K synthetic images for geometry, PINE achieves state-of-the-art point maps whether or not intrinsics are given and the best average rank on surface normals. It also exceeds SAM on large objects with less than 1 percent of its training images, and it predicts all three maps 5.7x faster than MoGe-3 with SAM.

authors.name: Zeyu Ren, Jie Ni, Rui Qian, Jiahao Wei, Hao Tang, Yongtai Liu, Zeyu Zhang

papers.title: AgroVG+: Generalized Visual Grounding in Agriculture with Region-Supervised Action Generation
papers.summary: Generalized visual grounding in agriculture requires localizing all objects that match a natural-language description and recognizing when no matching target is present. We introduce AgroVG+, a dataset whose referring expressions are all written and reviewed by agricultural experts based on image content and corresponding target sets. The dataset comprises 7,404 images and 10,081 query records across six agricultural scene families, covering single-target, multi-target, and target-absent cases. We also propose ReSAG (Region-Supervised Action Generation), a framework that couples regional evidence supervision with explicit box-generation and termination decisions. ReSAG assigns each target an equally weighted supervision term on a shared spatial evidence distribution computed before answer generation. The BOX/END protocol exposes a choice between generating another box and terminating the response at box boundaries, while coordinates are generated using the original language vocabulary. Regional and sequence objectives jointly train a shared language decoder. On AgroVG+, ReSAG outperforms coordinate-only fine-tuning on single- and multi-target exact-set accuracy, and achieves higher aggregate accuracy than either component alone in ablations.

authors.name: Haocheng Li, Juepeng Zheng, Guilong Xiao, Kaiqi Du, Gengmeng Pu, Haohuan Fu, Jianxi Huang

papers.title: MSBench: Benchmarking Script-Controlled Multi-Shot Text-to-Video Generation
papers.summary: Text-to-video (T2V) models can now generate visually plausible short clips, but multi-shot generation requires a different set of skills: composing multiple shots with intended cut timing, transition style, camera language, and cross-shot continuity. How far this multi-shot output can be controlled from text remains unmeasured: existing benchmarks either evaluate single shots or, when they provide shot-level scripts, typically check whether the requested shots appear but not when they change or how they are joined. We introduce MSBench, a benchmark for controllable text-driven multi-shot video generation built around structured Scene-Entity-Shot mini-scripts that specify each shot's time span, camera state, content, and outgoing transition. MSBench defines a four-dimensional hybrid evaluation framework spanning Visual Quality, Dynamic Quality, Semantic Alignment, and Cross-Shot Consistency with 11 sub-metrics. Experiments on 14 commercial and open-source systems show that visual quality does little to separate the systems, whereas multi-shot control does: many models cut mainly on scene changes and render requested gradual transitions as hard cuts. Human evaluations further validate MSBench, with its system ranking reaching a Spearman correlation of 0.87 with human preferences. The project page is available at https://totalhuang.github.io/MSBench-page/.

authors.name: Tao Huang, ZiHao Liang, Junhao Liu, Junzhe Li, Yuancheng Wei, Sifan Zuo, Beiming Yu, Taojin Liu, Zhuoyang Li, Bing Cao

papers.title: A colour-marker tracker for pose estimation of slender surgical instruments: vision-language-model-guided adaptive colour calibration
papers.summary: Slender surgical instruments need small, narrow markers for camera-based pose estimation. A colour-stripe marker fits this requirement, but its colours in the image drift from the design values with lighting, printing and camera settings. Because the colours can only be corrected after the marker has been found, methods that rely on the design colours face a circular problem. We propose vision-language-model (VLM)-based adaptive colour calibration and compare it with two rule-based methods, which re-measure the colours from detections made with the design colours: Initial colour update does so once after tracking starts, and Colour adaptation continuously during tracking. VLM guidance uses a fine-tuned VLM to find the markers without relying on the design colours and builds the colour profile from their pixels. Recall/F1 (%) for Initial colour update, Colour adaptation and VLM guidance were 92.0/95.7, 87.8/93.3 and 98.2/99.1 on 672 synthetic image pairs; 51.3/67.2, 48.8/65.0 and 83.8/87.0 on eight degraded laboratory videos; and 38.9/55.2, 19.7/29.7 and 100/100 on a surgical-robot (da Vinci) video with strongly shifted colours. In that video the rule-based methods never found the purple/cyan marker, whereas VLM guidance found all 234 markers with no false positives. In a simulation, the hue boundary between the two stripes moved by less than 0.1 pixel for exposure gains of 0.5-2.0, compared with 2.9-4.0 pixels for a boundary found with a fixed brightness threshold. When the degradation is mild, the rule-based methods, which need no training and no GPU, are sufficient. When the colours change greatly, the gain comes from a VLM-guided candidate search that does not rely on the design colours. Combining colour-stripe markers with adaptive colour calibration enables tracking of slender surgical instruments with small markers.

authors.name: Jaesung Hong, Dong Won Lee

papers.title: HorizonFlow: Few-Step Video Distillation in 600 Iterations
papers.summary: Distribution matching distillation (DMD) enables fast video generation by distilling a multi-step teacher into a few-step student. However, DMD-based methods often suffer from unnatural motion and costly training. We trace these limitations to the DMD gradient, which jointly optimizes appearance, layout, and motion without distinguishing their learning dynamics. Its static component, which carries appearance and layout, has a much higher signal-to-noise ratio than its motion component. As a result, per-frame quality converges within a few hundred iterations, whereas motion lags far behind. Beyond being noisy, the gradient also lacks two signals. (1) Video VAEs encode several frames into one latent frame (four in Wan2.1), and the gradient provides little guidance for spreading motion over these frames, causing periodic stutter. (2) DMD does not constrain the final sampling step to preserve the layout set by earlier steps, so objects merge and drift once the video moves. We propose HorizonFlow, which decouples the correction of motion from that of layout. It keeps the DMD loss and only shifts its regression target, with one training-only correction in the motion component and one in the orthogonal layout component. Chunk Evenness addresses (1) by spreading the motion of each latent chunk evenly over its frames, and Semantic Commitment addresses (2) by anchoring the coarse layout to the teacher's completion of the student's last step. In only 600 iterations, HorizonFlow distills Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B into a 4-step model using 8.4k training samples, 4.6-304$\times$ fewer than prior work. On VBench, HorizonFlow outperforms all released few-step Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B models. The same recipe transfers to Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B, where our student outperforms NVIDIA's distilled model. Code: https://github.com/XIANGLONGGUO/HorizonFlow-repo

authors.name: Xianglong Guo, Haobo Xu, Zanyi Wang, Zhen Lei, Chang Yu

papers.title: Ride on Anything: Contact-Coupled Monocular 4D Reconstruction of a Rider and Horse in Camera and World Frames
papers.summary: We address the reconstruction of a horse and its rider from a single video. When a human estimator and a horse estimator are applied independently, both meshes can fit their silhouettes well while the rider hovers beside or passes through the horse, slides along its back and jitters relative to it. These errors lie along the camera axis and are not visible in the input view. We present Ride on Anything (RoA), a general, training-free methodology for reconstructing a person riding an animal, which couples frozen estimators of the rider and the mount at test time. We instantiate it for horseback riding with SAM 3D Body and 4DEquine. RoA aligns both estimators on a common frame index, projects both subjects through one pixel-isotropic camera initialized from the horse estimator, and jointly optimizes bounded corrections under interaction terms defined in the horse's body frame, including a collision term based on generalized winding numbers that remains valid on the non-watertight horse mesh. The result is lifted to a levelled world frame using the camera rotation from the background and the field of view from MoGe-2. On our riding clips, the raw outputs of the two estimators leave the rider's pelvis 15 cm from the horse's back on average. RoA reduces this seat gap to 1 cm, the drift of the seat along and across the spine by 64% and 89%, the 90th-percentile penetration depth by 57%, and the share of rider surface inside the horse from 12.1% to 7.9%. The motion is markedly smoother (94% lower acceleration of the rider relative to the horse, 80% lower horse jerk), while the rider's silhouette IoU decreases from 0.59 to 0.52. Qualitatively, the rider stays seated on the horse and moves together with it. A quantitative evaluation of 3D accuracy awaits calibrated recordings of ridden animals. We also test a clip outside the task, a horse led on foot, and analyse the failure modes.

authors.name: Zehang Weng, Ci Li
