Fatemighomi, D. Gallacher, A. Gaur, W. Gillis, F. Girard, R. Gornea, G. Gratta, C. A. Hardy, M. Heffner, E. Hein, A. Iverson, A. Karelin, D. Keblbeck, P. Knauss, A. Kuchenkov, K. S. Kumar, A. Larson, M. B. Latif, S. Lavoie, B. G. Lenardo, D. S. Leonard, H. Lewis, X. Li, Z. Li, C. Licciardi, R. Lindsay, R. MacLellan, S. Majidi, M. Marquis, J. Masbou, M. Medina-Peregrina, S. Mngonyama, B. Mong, X. E. Ngwadla, K. Ni, I. Nitu, A. Nolan, J. C. Nzobadila Ondze, A. Odian, J. L. Orrell, G. S. Ortega, C. T. Overman, L. Pagani, H. Peltz Smalley, A. Piepke, A. Pocar, R. Rai, H. Rasiwala, D. Ray, S. Rescia, F. Reti\`ere, R. Ross, P. C. Rowson, S. Sangiorgio, T. Shetty, L. Si, V. Stekhanov, Tanmay, M. Todd, T. Totev, S. Triambak, O. A. Tyuka, E. van Bruggen, S. Viel, M. Wehrfritz, S. Wilde, H. Xu, L. Yang, M. Yu, O. Zeldovich

papers.title: Physical co-presence of workers is linked with the evolution of interfirm networks
papers.summary: Inter-firm transaction networks underpin modern economies and are critical for economic growth and resilience. Previous studies have largely explained the formation of inter-firm ties through spatial proximity. Yet people routinely move across space, creating opportunities for encounters that extend beyond geographical proximity. How these opportunities relate to inter-firm transaction relationships remains poorly understood. Here, we combine large-scale mobile phone mobility data with a multi-year panel of transactions among 196,317 firms in Tokyo to quantify encounter opportunities between workers and examine their association with inter-firm transaction ties. We find that pairs of areas with greater opportunities for encounters one another are more likely to have transaction links and new link formation between previously unconnected firms. This association is particularly pronounced in information- and service-intensive industries, reflecting the importance of encounter opportunities for exchange involving intangible knowledge and service. Indirect connections through shared neighbors in the encounter network are also positively associated with subsequent transaction formation across industries, but not within industries. These findings suggest that urban policies shaping connectivity formed through human mobility could play a significant role in the development and resilience of economic networks.

authors.name: Ketian Chen, Hiroyasu Inoue, Yoshihide Sekimoto, Yoshiki Ogawa, Takahiro Yabe

papers.title: Analysis of Geometric Eigenmode Splitting in Planar Microwave Resonators
papers.summary: A traditional challenge in planar microwave resonator design is to find geometric mechanisms that can control individual resonant frequencies - or tune coupling between specific eigenmodes - without affecting other system parameters, such as the center frequency. Achieving this capability can be transformative for the design of microwave sensors, filters, antennas and resonant networks. Starting from first principles, we outline the development of an analytical method that guides practical design by suggesting specific perturbation shapes capable of achieving resonant mode-splitting while keeping the center frequency nearly stationary. This approach opens the door to novel designs that were previously difficult to discover or optimize. Independent numerical simulations and measurements of stripline resonators validate the effectiveness of this approach. The demonstrated tuning effect shows that the first-order estimate suggested by the theory persists in practice over a relatively wide splitting bandwidth (exceeding 54% of center frequency), increasing the utility of the proposed method.

authors.name: Hagen Papenburg, Jason Corn, Romain Speciel, Adham Naji

papers.title: Polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
papers.summary: High-refractive-index dielectric metasurfaces supporting optical modes are ideal candidates for achieving strong coupling with transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) materials. However, optical illumination with a specific polarization is always required to estimate the maximal coupling strength in such coupled systems due to the polarization-dependent optical modes. Here, we propose a self-hybridized strong coupling between Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBICs) mode and A excitons in the same bulk WS2 metasurface. By changing the thickness of the bulk WS2 metasurfaces, a typical anticrossing behavior with Rabi splitting of 165.9 meV is observed. Such Rabi splitting is unchanged when changing the polarization of the incident light from linearly to circularly polarizations, demonstrating the polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling. This work provides a novel method for realizing robust polarization-independent polaritons in bulk TMDCs metasurface and offers new insights for expanding the applications of polaritonic devices with arbitrary polarizations.

authors.name: Xiongwei Guo, Fu Liu, Jinhai Si, Xun Hou, Kuidong Wang

papers.title: Diffusion Posterior Sampling for Mitigation of Spatially-Variant System Blur in Ultra-High-Resolution CT of Trabecular Bone
papers.summary: Objective: CT spatial resolution degrades with distance from isocenter. We evaluate diffusion posterior sampling (DPS) deblurring for restoring structural detail and harmonizing texture features (TFs) of off-center trabecular bone to isocenter in ultra-high resolution CT (UHR CT). Methods: DPS pairs a diffusion prior, trained on isocenter UHR CT patches of trabecular bone from four human femora, with a likelihood term enforcing consistency with the observed image. Two variants were tested on a held-out femur at radial shifts of 90, 130 and 160 mm: KnownBlurDPS, with an anisotropic Gaussian kernel derived from modulation transfer function measurements, and BlindDPS, which estimated the kernel jointly with the image. Restored patches were compared with isocenter ground truth by structural similarity (SSIM), gradient magnitude similarity deviation (GMSD), and concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) of 40 gray-level co-occurrence and run-length TFs. Results: Both DPS variants improved SSIM and GMSD by 1-10% and mean TF CCC by 30-130%. The number of reproducible TFs (CCC > 0.80) at 90/130/160 mm rose from 13/2/1 without deblurring to 33/35/29 (KnownBlurDPS) and 40/36/16 (BlindDPS). At 90 mm, the accuracy of a linear classifier predicting the shift from TFs dropped from 79% to chance level with BlindDPS. Conclusion: DPS partly restores trabecular detail and TF reproducibility lost to spatially-variant blur in UHR CT; the blind variant matches the measured-kernel variant up to 130 mm. Significance: DPS deblurring can standardize trabecular bone TFs against patient mis-centering, potentially improving the robustness of TF-based CT radiomics; its blind form needs no CT system characterization.

authors.name: T. Ye, G. Shi, A. Sivakumar, F. J. Quevedo Gonzalez, K. F. Moseley, J. A. Carrino, J. H. Siewerdsen, W. Zbijewski

papers.title: Generation and characterization of unsteady inflows in a fan-vane wind tunnel
papers.summary: Wind-tunnel experiments often require inflows with specific combinations of turbulence intensity and integral length scale because both can influence the measured response. To broaden the range of attainable inflows, this study uses pseudorandom vane excitation to generate large-scale turbulence and examines how both quantities vary with the amplitude and spectral shape of the vane-angle command. In each test, the 15 servo-driven vanes downstream of a 768-fan array received the same angle command, and all fans operated at a common, constant duty cycle. Hot-wire measurements covered twenty heights and selected spanwise and downstream positions. At a fan-control duty cycle of 60%, increasing vane angular amplitude raised profile-mean turbulence intensity from 7.3% to 31.8% under periodic forcing and from 6.2% to 23.0% under pseudorandom forcing. With the normalized pseudorandom command spectrum held fixed, larger angular amplitudes increased the low-frequency share of velocity variance, accompanied by longer correlation times and larger integral scales. At a root-mean-square angular amplitude of 15 degrees, changing the command spectrum yielded profile-mean integral length scales of 0.88-1.67 m at similar turbulence intensities. The principal features of the velocity spectra persisted between 2 and 4 m downstream, while integral scales continued to change. Both forcing types exhibited middle-region minima in turbulence intensity and integral scale. Regional analysis of a representative pseudorandom case linked these minima to weaker low-frequency fluctuations and shorter correlation times. These findings provide a basis for selecting vane inputs according to the turbulence-intensity and integral-scale requirements of the intended test region.

authors.name: Yutong Liu, Gang Hu, Hongwei Zhang

papers.title: Electron Parameters in H2:Ar:CH4 Plasma Maintained by Microwave and Laser Radiation
papers.summary: Electron parameters in an atmospheric-pressure hybrid plasma in the 95H2:3Ar:2CH4 mixture maintained by pulsed-periodic microwave radiation (2.47 GHz) and CO2 laser radiation (10.6 {\mu}m) were studied. The plasma was generated in a quasi-cylindrical reactor, which was a resonator for TM011-mode microwave radiation. It was shown that in the hybrid plasma emission spectra the H{\alpha} and H{\betta} lines are strongly broadened and can be approximated by the sum of two Lorentzian contours (dual-Lorentzian approximation). The Stark broadening of the H{\alpha} and H{\betta} lines was used to measure the electron density in the plasma, and the ratio of their intensities allowed to estimate the electron temperature. To simplify the description of the hybrid plasma properties the concept of two plasma states caused by the pulsed injection of laser energy into the plasma was introduced. The hybrid plasma state, corresponding to the plasma state during the laser pulse, is characterized by a high electron density of (1-2.5)*10^17 cm-3 and an electron temperature of ~0.5-0.6 eV. The electron density in the state corresponding to the time intervals between laser pulses (1.8*10^14-5*10^15 cm-3) is more than an order of magnitude lower than the electron density in the first state, but it is 2-10 times higher than the electron density in microwave plasma ((1-5)*10^14 cm-3). The electron temperature in this state is 0.16-0.24 eV. The radius of the dense plasma region with an electron density of ~10^17 cm-3 is estimated to be ~0.5-1 mm.

authors.name: Svetlana Avtaeva, Alexey Medvedev

papers.title: Hyperbolic network embedding via dimensional annealing and Barnes--Hut approximation
papers.summary: Common features observed in complex networks from various domains can be explained by network geometry in hyperbolic space. Inferring the latent coordinates of nodes enables efficient navigation, link prediction, and geometric renormalization. However, the loss landscape of the hyperbolic model is extremely rugged due to the topological constraints of the low-dimensional embedding space. To overcome this, we introduce the dimensional annealing framework, which bypasses these constraints by introducing an auxiliary dimension. We show that dimensional annealing achieves higher-quality embeddings than existing energy-based embedding methods. Additionally, we incorporate the Barnes--Hut approximation for computational scalability.

authors.name: Bukyoung Jhun, Gangmin Son, Hoyun Choi, Sang Hoon Lee

papers.title: Giant thermal transduction via feedback-phase engineering in a thin-film lithium-niobate opto-electro-mechanical oscillator
papers.summary: Conventional resonant MEMS thermometry typically relies on the intrinsic temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) of mechanical resonances. Here we show that embedding a suspended thin-film lithium-niobate mechanical resonator in an opto-electro-mechanical (OEM) feedback loop enhances the intrinsic coefficient by two orders of magnitude. By using laser--cavity detuning to control the loop's round-trip phase, and thus the Barkhausen-selected oscillation frequency, we engineer an effective TCF of $+1.24\times10^{4}$~ppm/K: a 100-fold enhancement and a sign reversal relative to its intrinsic TCF of $-124$~ppm/K. Temperature-dependent and open-loop phase measurements confirm that this giant response originates from feedback phase selection rather than from the passive resonator itself. This interpretation is further supported by the independently measured closed-loop oscillation frequencies and a detuning-dependent delay model. The same architecture also supports 2:1 subharmonic injection locking, yielding sub-6~Hz linewidths, reference-limited frequency stability, and tunable operation from $76.71$ to $76.82$~MHz. These results establish feedback-phase engineering as a general, post-fabrication route to both giant thermal transduction and low-noise yet tunable mechanical oscillation.

authors.name: Ran Yin, Yue Yu, Ian Christen, Mengjie Yu

papers.title: Ultrabroadband, high-sensitivity time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy enabled by a Yb-based laser system
papers.summary: Ultrafast optical fields have introduced numerous novel light-induced states in quantum materials. Identifying these states and elucidating their formation mechanisms require comprehensive, quantitative access to nonequilibrium electrodynamics across relevant energy scales. Here, we develop a Yb-laser-based time-resolved terahertz spectroscopy (TRTS) platform combining multi-pass-cell pulse compression, spintronic terahertz generation, and air-biased coherent detection. A single time-domain waveform scan provides continuous phase-resolved spectral coverage to 25 THz ($\sim$100 meV) with a Fourier resolution of 0.1 THz ($\sim$0.4 meV). This capability enables the characterization of both low-frequency charge dynamics and higher-energy resonant excitations in quantum materials under a common temporal reference. The system achieves a single-scan time-domain signal-to-noise ratio of 72 dB with long-term waveform stability, while preserving most of the laser pulse energy for tunable excitation. Measurements on intrinsic GaAs resolve extremely weak phonon features above 23 THz and demonstrate quantitative retrieval of equilibrium and transient complex optical properties. The resulting platform can provide a more complete microscopic picture of light-induced states in quantum materials.

authors.name: Hong-Yuan Wu, Si-Jia Li, Jing-Long Ma, Guo-Qian Liao, Alexander Holm Ohrt, Long Cheng, Peter Uhd Jepsen, Bin-Bin Zhou, Si-Jie Zhang, Yu-Tong Li

papers.title: Development of a Hybrid Scintillator Strip-Drift Tube Muon Detector for the FCC-ee
papers.summary: The Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee) is a proposed high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ collider for precision measurements at the electroweak, Higgs, and top-quark energy scales. A high-performance, cost-effective muon system is essential for muon identification, triggering, momentum measurement, and long-lived particle detection. We present the R&D of a hybrid muon detector concept combining fast extruded plastic scintillator strips with precision drift tubes. The scintillator strips were produced at Fermilab, while detector prototypes with SiPM readout and pressurized drift tubes were designed, constructed, and integrated at the University of Michigan. The hybrid detector was tested at the CERN test beam facility in 2025 and 2026. The scintillator strips achieved a position resolution of 1.6 mm and a time resolution of approximately 350 ps, while the drift tubes provided a single-hit spatial resolution better than 100 $\mu$m. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a high-performance hybrid muon spectrometer for the FCC-ee.

authors.name: Jiajin Ge (on behalf of the University of Michigan FCC-ee R&D team)

papers.title: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
papers.summary: It has been established that electron (phase-space) holes, i.e., EHs, can arise from the nonlinear relaxation of the electron beam instability. Excitation of electromagnetic waves related to the EHs is, however, still not fully understood. Using 2.5-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, we systematically investigate the nonlinear evolution of the (moderately relativistic) electron bi-stream instability (a special case of the electron beam instability where the densities of the two counter-propagating energetic electron beams are equivalent) in charge- and current-neutralized plasmas under weak and strong magnetizations. This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions, the formation of non-Maxwellian features, and the anisotropic electron heating in magnetized plasmas, with potential implications for coherent radio emission in astrophysical plasmas (e.g., solar zebra-pattern bursts).

authors.name: Xiaowei Zhou, Dejin Wu, Ling Chen, Zongjun Ning

papers.title: Transient Impact Force and Spreading Dynamics of Droplets Impacting Spherical Surfaces
papers.summary: Droplet impacts on spherical surfaces are encountered in processes such as spray cooling, anti-icing, and spray deposition. The curvature of the impact target changes the spreading path of the droplet and the impact force, leading to more complex kinematic and transient force dynamics. This study employs a numerical model utilizing the volume of fluid approach to investigate the spreading, retraction, rebound and deposition characteristics of droplets impinging on spherical surfaces. The roles of wall wettability, spherical curvature, Weber number, and Ohnesorge number on droplet spreading and wall impact force are analyzed. The results show that the wall impact force exhibits two peaks in the complete rebound and partial rebound modes, whereas the second peak disappears in the complete deposition mode. Further parametric analysis shows that increasing the contact angle, i.e., decreasing wettability, reduces both the maximum spreading length and the contact time, and significantly changes the second peak of the impact force. Under complete rebound mode, the relationship between the contact time and the contact angle can be expressed as ${{{t}_{\text{c}}}}/{{{t}_{\sigma }}}\;={{C}_{1}}\left[ {{\left( 1-\cos {{\theta }_{\text{eq}}} \right)}^{{-1}/{2}\;}}-{1}/{\sqrt{2}} \right]+{{C}_{2}}$, where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are constants. Within the investigated curvature range, increasing the dimensionless curvature reduces the critical contact angle required for complete rebound. The dimensionless first peak of the impact force decreases with increasing the Weber number and finally approaches a constant, following a relationship of $F_{\text{t}1}^{*}={{\beta }_{1}}+{{\beta }_{2}}W{{e}^{-1}}$, where ${{\beta }_{1}}$ and ${{\beta }_{2}}$ are constants. Increasing the Ohnesorge number reduces the maximum spreading length, prolongs the contact time, and slightly increases the first peak of impact force.

authors.name: Mengqi Ye, Tianyou Wang, Zhizhao Che

papers.title: Dynamic Renewal for Hydrodynamic Coupling in Ciliary Mucus Transport
papers.summary: Mucociliary clearance in large mammalian airways involves millimetric MUC5B-rich mucus strands that emerge from submucosal glands approximately aligned with the direction of transport. These strands are observed downstream in cross-flow networks. Recently, Bos et al. [PNAS Nexus 2, pgad388 (2023)] modeled single strand reorientation using a free-draining coupling for the flow induced by cilia. This leaves unresolved whether the strand's own disturbance of the surrounding liquid assists or frustrates the turning. Here, we develop the methodology to address this question. An immersed-boundary coupling is combined with a Fourier-space Stokes solver and a bespoke dynamic-renewal algorithm that exposes the strand to new ciliary domain without enlarging the simulation volume. This allows us to overcome one of the multiscale challenges posed by mucociliary clearance. We find that hydrodynamic interactions result in only a limited decrease in the rate of reorientation, which supports the use of the free-draining approximation. Future work can build on the methodological foundation introduced here to study collective strand dynamics.

authors.name: Jeroen Bechtold, Valentijn van Zwieten, Iris Verkuil, Meike F. Bos, Georg Rempfer, Mae Nesenberend, Pieter Michels, Florian K. R. Gaeremynck, Bart Stam, Debabrata Panja, Joost de Graaf

papers.title: Turbulence Strength Estimation from Multiplexed Orbital Angular Momentum Beams Using Multimode Fibre Speckle
papers.summary: The strength of atmospheric turbulence governs how much the modes of a free-space optical link mix together. It is usually measured with a separate instrument or with a Gaussian probe beam, neither of which uses the beams that a structured-light link already carries. Here we show that the turbulence strength, expressed as the Fried parameter, can be estimated directly from multiplexed orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams without knowing which modes are present. The beams pass through a passive multimode fibre that turns them into speckle on a camera, and a trained weighted sum of the camera pixels (known as an extreme learning machine), averaged over a few tens of frames, gives the Fried parameter. In the laboratory with emulated turbulence, superpositions of up to eleven OAM modes give an estimate as accurate as that from a Gaussian probe beam sent through the same fibre. In all but weak turbulence the estimate is also more accurate than an ideal Strehl meter or an ideal tip/tilt sensor, providing an efficient way to estimate turbulence strength in mode-division multiplexed systems.

authors.name: Warwick G. C. Brown, Mitchell A. Cox

papers.title: Nonempirical Determination of the Optimal TAO-DFT Fictitious Temperature for Molecular Systems in the Lowest Singlet State
papers.summary: Thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) [J.-D. Chai, J. Chem. Phys., 2012, ${\bf 136}$, 154104] has been developed to investigate the ground-state properties of large electronic systems exhibiting varying multi-reference (MR) character. As a central parameter in TAO-DFT, the fictitious temperature $\theta$ is closely linked to the degree of static correlation in an electronic system. While the conventional system-independent $\theta$-scheme is computationally efficient and broadly applicable, a fixed, preassigned $\theta$ can be overly large for single-reference (SR) systems yet too small for strongly MR systems. To overcome this limitation, we propose a nonempirical scheme based on spin-symmetry restoration to determine the optimal system-dependent fictitious temperature $\theta^{*}$ for molecular systems in their lowest singlet states. Across benchmark tests encompassing both MR systems (the bond dissociation of H$_{2}$, N$_{2}$, Li$_{2}$, and LiH, as well as the torsional rotation of twisted ethylene) and pure SR systems (the dissociation of He$_{2}$ and Ne$_{2}$), our nonempirical approach demonstrates superior overall accuracy compared with the conventional fixed-$\theta$ scheme. Furthermore, relative to standard Kohn-Sham density functional theory (TAO-DFT with $\theta = 0$), TAO-DFT employing $\theta^{*}$ yields substantial improvements for MR systems while preserving comparable accuracy in SR systems.

authors.name: Bing-Ying Li, Jeng-Da Chai

papers.title: RxnScope: Accurate joint generation of product and transition-state pairs from reactants via flow matching
papers.summary: Reaction networks are central to understanding chemical reactivity and guiding reaction design. Constructing them when products are unknown remains a major challenge in computational chemistry, requiring the identification of products and their corresponding transition states (TSs) across elementary steps. Here, we introduce RxnScope, a flow-matching framework that jointly generates paired product-TS geometries from reactants, conditioned on a potentially reactive region. Directed product-to-TS coupling allows evolving rather than fixed product geometries to guide TS generation, while paired outputs enable product-topology ranking to prioritize candidates for validation. RxnScope recovered and validated 95.8% of reference pathways on Transition1x, performed robustly on multicomponent reactions and enabled multistep pathway exploration. In automatic reaction discovery, it achieved low-energy pathway coverage comparable to that of the single-ended growing string method while using only about 2% of its computational cost. These results establish joint product-TS generation as a new strategy for exploring reaction networks from reactants.

authors.name: Yanyang Li, DaoJing Li, Manyi Yang, Shuhua Li

papers.title: Polarization-cloaked spatiotemporal topological knots
papers.summary: Spatiotemporally localized topological knots encode global connectivity within a moving space-time optical wavepacket, circumventing the requirement for spatial-only eigenmodes that extend throughout three-dimensional space-filling. In conventional modalities, this connectivity is identified directly from a scalar complex field. However, knotting optical knots with the polarization state of light proves difficult to realize for ultrafast localized wavepackets. In this work, we combine oppositely wound toroidal vortex modes with orthogonal circular polarization states on the higher-order Poincar\'e sphere to construct vectorial electromagnetic spatiotemporal wavepackets, in which the topological connectivity is encoded in the relative phase between the polarization components. Stokes analysis shows that S_0 retains a common toroidal envelope, whereas the phase sensitive Stokes parameters S_1 and S_2 reveal winding-dependent linked and knotted trajectories; numerical simulations verify their closure, and time-sliced off-axis interferometry experimentally reconstructs the corresponding three-dimensional S_2 textures. This separation of topological connectivity from the scalar intensity envelope extends the control of spatiotemporal topology to the polarization degree of freedom and provides a versatile framework for controlling how topological information is accessed in multidimensional structured light.

authors.name: Yaning Zhou, Nianjia Zhang, Zhao Zhang, Chunhao Liang, Qian Cao, Houan Teng, Qiwen Zhan, Sergey A. Ponomarenko, Xu Guo, Yangjian Cai, Xin Liu

papers.title: Restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham theory for arbitrary genealogical spin coupling
papers.summary: We introduce a generalization of restricted open-shell Kohn-Sham (ROKS) theory to a single configuration state function (CSF) with arbitrary genealogical spin coupling. This CSF-ROKS theory establishes a spin-pure density functional extension of the recently developed CSF-based restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock (CSF-ROHF) theory, providing a computationally efficient route to incorporate dynamic electron correlation. The energy is expressed as a weighted sum over unrestricted determinants built from a common set of restricted orbitals, and the number of determinants grows quadratically with the number of open shells. Numerical calculations for N$_2$ and the polyacene series show that CSF-ROKS solutions retain chemically interpretable character. Exchange-correlation functionals preferentially stabilize low-seniority configurations, shifting the onset of polyradical character in polyacenes to longer chains than predicted by CSF-ROHF. Furthermore, CSF-ROKS can be used to target state-specific spin-pure excitations in the vinyl and allyl radicals, and the [Cr(ddpd)$_2$]$^{3+}$ molecular ruby. However, CSF-ROKS incorrectly predicts ferromagnetic coupling in a set of bridged transition metal dimers, indicating that kinetic exchange requires more advanced correlated methods.

authors.name: Hugh G. A. Burton, Cameron Y . Z. Brown

papers.title: A shock-fitting approach to high-order simulation of viscous hypersonic flows based on inviscid implicit shock tracking
papers.summary: This work presents a framework for computing viscous, shock-dominated flows at high Mach and Reynolds numbers in which the bow shock is located by inviscid implicit shock tracking and then treated as a boundary of the viscous computation. The high-order implicit shock tracking (HOIST) method is applied to the Euler equations on a coarse, shock-agnostic mesh to produce a shock-aligned mesh and the shock geometry; the elements upstream of the shock are discarded, the post-shock domain is remeshed to resolve the boundary layer, and the compressible Navier-Stokes equations are solved on it with a high-order interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method, with the post-shock state prescribed along the shock boundary by the oblique shock relations. Because the shock structure is never resolved, the approach requires neither the extreme element compression nor the specialized formulations that fully coupled viscous shock tracking demands at these conditions; the tracking optimization is confined to the coarse inviscid mesh, and the viscous computation involves no mesh unknowns and no additional nonlinear stabilization. The framework is demonstrated on a Mach 10.6 axisymmetric blunt cone, a Mach 17.6 cylinder, and a Mach 5 sphere in three dimensions, with surface pressure and heat flux in good agreement with experimental measurements and reference computations.

authors.name: Huijing Dong, Alexander M. Perez Reyes, Matthew J. Zahr

papers.title: Radial Evolution of Correlation Anisotropy in PUNCH Observations of the Young Solar Wind
papers.summary: Solar wind turbulence, evolving in the presence of a mean magnetic field, large-scale shear, and expansion, exhibits several types of anisotropy, including wavevector anisotropy and variance anisotropy. As the solar wind expands from the corona into the interplanetary space, the magnetically controlled outer corona transitions into the dynamic and less constrained solar wind, and fluctuations may evolve toward isotropy. This is suggestive of an evolution of anisotropy with distance from the Sun, a feature observed in earlier results using surveys of in-situ data, as well as more limited images of solar wind density from STEREO. Here we confirm and expand on those results employing data from the PUNCH mission, whose wide-field, high-cadence imaging enables anisotropy tracking at different heliospheric positions. We evaluate a two-dimensional (2D) correlation function $C(\ell_{\perp}, \ell_{\parallel})$ of polarized white-light brightness as a function of radial $\ell_\parallel$ and transverse $\ell_\perp$ scales to infer the nature of density anisotropy and its development in space. At larger heliocentric distances ($\sim 100 R_\odot$), circular contours of the correlation function indicate a transition toward approximate isotropy. The correlation structure at heliocentric distances from $30R_\odot$ to $60R_\odot$ preferentially extends along the radial direction, which might imply the possible dominance of the two-dimensional variation in the transverse plane. In this way, the very large field of view of PUNCH images reveal a fundamental transition of solar wind turbulence toward isotropy.

authors.name: Zhuoran Gao, Yan Yang, Francesco Pecora, Rohit Chhiber, Riley Amos, Steven R. Cranmer, Jiaming Wang, William H. Matthaeus, Craig E. DeForest, Sarah E. Gibson, Nicholeen Viall, Chris R. Gilly, Ronnie Killough, Jillian Redfern, William L. Wells, Matthew N. Beasley, Glenn T. Laurent, Robin C. Colaninno, Nick R. Waltham, J. Marcus Hughes, Daniel B. Seaton, Samuel Van Kooten, Ritesh Patel, Chris Lowder, Derek Lamb

papers.title: Political Orientation and Participation in Prediction Markets: Large Stakes Converge, Small Stakes Diverge
papers.summary: Prediction markets offer a way to study collective expectations and beliefs: people express their views on various events and, by putting money behind their predictions, take on the risks of their judgments. As a result, the scale of investment can reveal additional dimensions of individual behavior and beliefs. In this study, we use a complex network approach to examine the structure of user participation, drawing on roughly 1.14 billion transaction records from the Polymarket platform, covering more than 3.1 million wallet addresses and 764,000 prediction events. To do this, we build a bipartite network of users and events and analyze patterns of investment concentration, connections between topics, and the network's community structure. Our findings show a highly skewed distribution of financial participation: 1\% of events account for 64\% of total transaction volume, while 1\% of wallets account for 79.2\% of total financial participation. We also examine how investment scale and political orientation shape user participation patterns. Focusing on the 2024 U.S. presidential election, we compare users who invested exclusively in a Trump victory or exclusively in a Harris victory, grouping wallets by purchase size rather than by retail or institutional status. The results show that among large-scale investors, capital allocation patterns across topics are more similar between the two political groups; in contrast, these patterns diverge more and vary more among small-scale investors. This result holds across six different ways of representing and comparing the networks, and four of these differences are also statistically supported.

authors.name: Ali Hosseinzadeh, Ali Hosseiny, Reza Jafari

papers.title: Stable eigenmodes of the Large-scale circulation in Turbulent Convection
papers.summary: Turbulent Rayleigh-B\'enard convection (RBC) is a canonical system for studying buoyancy-driven turbulence. Its defining feature is a system-size large-scale circulation (LSC), whose dynamics reflect the coupling between coherent motion and turbulent fluctuations. Starting from the Boussinesq Navier-Stokes and temperature equations, we derive three coupled stochastic equations for the LSC angular velocity and its associated dipolar temperature field. The deterministic dynamics contain an unstable no-LSC set and two symmetry-related stable finite-LSC states. Linearization about either finite-LSC state yields one purely relaxational eigenmode and a pair of damped oscillatory eigenmodes whose frequency is set by the LSC turnover rate. Turbulent fluctuations continually excite the latter, providing a dynamical origin for the observed quasi-periodic oscillations. Experiments in a thin-disk cell directly resolve both eigenmodes and show their predicted Rayleigh-number scalings. The same stochastic dynamics also provide a route to rare cessations and reversals. This theory-experiment framework provides a tractable example of how coherent circulation states, intrinsic modes, and fluctuation-driven transitions emerge in turbulent convection, with broader relevance to geophysical and astrophysical flows.

authors.name: Yin Wang, Pik-Yin Lai, Penger Tong

papers.title: Initial Field Test of a Quadrupedal Robot at SLAC Beam Dump East (BDE): A Sandbox for Robotics in Accelerator Operations
papers.summary: Deploying field robotics in large scale particle accelerator facilities offers significant potential to enhance operational efficiency, promote facility sustainability, and reduce personnel exposure to radiation and other hazards. As key underlying technologies mature, field robotics are seeing broader deployment across various industrial sectors. However, accelerator facilities have remained cautious in adopting these systems, primarily due to concerns regarding cost versus return on investment and the risk of equipment collisions. In addition, operational experience with SLAC's Remotely Operated Accelerator Monitoring platform, ROAM highlighted critical technical challenges, including radiation tolerance and poor network connectivity in enclosed accelerator areas. This paper presents the findings from a recent test drive of a Boston Dynamics SPOT quadrupedal robot equipped with a SPOT Arm payload conducted at SLAC's Beam Dump East facility. We evaluate the technical feasibility and operational considerations of deploying quadrupedal field robotics within accelerator environments. Furthermore, we report key practical challenges, such as protective suits that impede navigation sensors and low light infrared navigation in unlit spaces. Finally, we outline potential development pathways toward adaptive learning and autonomous execution for future routine field robotics operations in accelerator facilities.

authors.name: M. Bai (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory), M. A. Montironi (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory), A. Saad (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory), T. Thayer (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory)

papers.title: A Theoretical Investigation of Magnetic Susceptibility Measurement of Diamagnetic Liquids Using a Michelson Interferometer
papers.summary: We examine the theoretical use of a Michelson interferometer to infer the magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic liquid from a magnetically induced surface deformation. A ring magnet changes the liquid thickness along the sample beam, producing a signed phase shift relative to a fixed optical reference. For a double traversal of the sample, the fringe displacement is $m = 2(n_{\ell} - n_a)\Delta z/\lambda$. We derive the susceptibility inversion both in a local gravity approximation and with surface tension included through the linearized Young-Laplace equation. The treatment distinguishes a finite reference field from a zero-field reference, specifies the displacement sign and susceptibility contrast, and identifies calibration and uncertainty requirements. Reproducible illustrative calculations use a uniformly magnetized annulus. The results establish a theoretical measurement relation and its assumptions; they do not constitute an experimental demonstration or a verified accuracy claim.

authors.name: David Shulman

papers.title: Coarse-Grained Description of Stochastic Neutron Transport in Highly Heterogeneous Reactor Media via Non-Local Feller Boundary Functionals
papers.summary: This paper presents a novel hierarchical coarse-graining framework to model non-Markovian neutron transport within the ultra-heterogeneous, multi-phase subcooled nucleate boiling layer of a nuclear reactor core. By applying Feller's subordination theory to continuous-time random walks, microscopic fluid fluctuations and vapor bubble dynamics are rigorously integrated into macroscopic transport operators through the apparatus of Complete Bernstein Functions (CBF). A modified non-local Fick's law is derived using a $P_1$-Legendre polynomial expansion, mapping the fractal porosity and structural phase boundaries into a stochastically renormalized effective diffusion coefficient. The thermodynamic consistency of the model is grounded within Chentsov's statistical manifolds, demonstrating that granular Poisson-like shot noise yields a geometric-exponential family of distributions characterized by a constant negative information curvature. To evaluate operational safety margins under transient conditions, a generalized Lyapunov functional with a quadratic memory kernel is constructed, and a complex decomposition of the transfer function $H(\omega)$ is performed. The resulting analytical limits are parameterized for a WWER-1000 core layout and translated into an engineering computational sequence suitable for implementation in Mathcad Prime 8 to diagnose the onset of Hopf bifurcations and spatial power oscillations.

authors.name: V. V. Ryazanov

papers.title: Experimental study of the Reynolds number effect on the mean flow and coherent structures in a 180-degree bent pipe flow using PIV
papers.summary: In this work, we study the effect of Reynolds number on the flow in a 180{\deg} pipe bend with a curvature of {\gamma} = 0.2. We perform planar particle image velocimetry (PIV) in the symmetry plane of the pipe for bulk Reynolds numbers ReD from 10 000 to 60 000 with water as the working fluid. To remove the refraction at the pipe wall, a hybrid method is employed. A mixture of water, glycerol and sodium iodide is used to match the refractive index of the pipe at its outer interface. The refraction at the inner interface is corrected using reverse ray tracing. The measurements are validated against direct numerical simulations at ReD = 10 000 and 20 000 and against hot-wire data from the literature at 60 000. As the Reynolds number increases, the mean velocity profiles in and downstream of the bend become flatter. Furthermore, a second vortex pair, with the opposite direction of rotation to the Dean vortices, forms further downstream, between bend angles of 116{\deg} and 126{\deg}. A modal decomposition of the planar velocity fields shows that the coherent structures keep their spatial features at all Reynolds numbers. Their Strouhal numbers remain nearly unchanged and show no monotonic trend.

authors.name: Eman Bagheri, Christoph Heigl, Felix Czwielong, Stefan Becker, Philipp Schlatter

papers.title: Collision of a sphere and a prolate spheroid settling in a quiescent ambient
papers.summary: The collision rate of a prolate spheroid and a sphere settling through a quiescent fluid at small Reynolds number is computed for randomly oriented spheroids and for spheroids turned broadside by weak fluid inertia. Without hydrodynamic interactions, the collision cross-section is the projection of the spheroid enlarged by the radius of the sphere. The ideal kernel then follows in closed form for aligned spheroids and from a one-dimensional quadrature for isotropic ones. Alignment raises the ideal kernel by at most a factor of 4/{\pi}, but extinguishes it on the extinction locus, where an isolated broadside spheroid settles as fast as the sphere. Hydrodynamic interactions are computed from pair trajectories in a first-reflection slender-body model, in which the interaction velocity is proportional to the difference of the buoyant weights and only the flow of the sphere rotates the spheroid. A strongly aligned spheroid weathervanes, whereas a freely rotating one feathers and glides. Weathervaning lowers the collision efficiency, as does feathering far from the extinction locus, but gliding raises it near the locus. There, the collision rate of spheroids aligned at a finite rate lies far above both the strong-alignment result and the ideal isotropic kernel. Just above the extinction locus, where strongly aligned spheroids are blocked, collisions persist at all the finite alignment rates computed. A boundary-element solution shows that the model overestimates the rate at which the gap closes near contact. A lubrication film largely corrects this and reduces the collision efficiencies from their interception values. Simple fits for the ideal kernels, the efficiencies and the near-contact correction are provided for use in collision models.

authors.name: Arnab Choudhury, Anubhab Roy

papers.title: Monogenic signal analysis for wavefield characterisation in distributed acoustic sensing
papers.summary: The spatio-temporal wavefield sampled by distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) contains intertwined information about signal strength, oscillatory structure and propagation. We introduce a methodology to disentangle these properties, with applications to the analysis of weak arrivals obscured by noise or stronger wave trains. The method is based on the monogenic signal, a two-dimensional extension of the analytic signal defined via the Riesz transform. In DAS, the monogenic signal decomposes locally dominant arrivals into their amplitude, phase and apparent slowness along the fibre. Moreover, the consistency of the wavefield orientation, quantified using the notion of directional coherency, allows coherent arrivals to be identified and enhanced. In this work, we apply the monogenic signal to analyse submarine T-wave recordings following the magnitude 3.5 earthquake of 5 October 2023 in the western Alboran Sea, acquired along approximately 60 km of the Estepona-Tetouan fibre-optic cable. Directional coherency allows us to enhance coherent wave trains, attenuating the incoherent background while preserving their oscillatory structure. Combining the monogenic attributes, we track individual oscillations across the fibre, obtaining spatially consistent apparent-slowness estimates. Together with varying cable geometry, these estimates allow us to infer the incoming directions of two wave trains, revealing distinct backazimuths. We extend the methodology to direction-selective enhancement, revealing a weaker third wave train with opposite moveout that is obscured by stronger arrivals. Beyond these examples, we show that monogenic analysis offers new possibilites for wavefield comparison, with promising applications to lossy data compression and inversion. Our results highlight the versatility of monogenic analysis and its potential to become a central tool for interpreting DAS recordings.

authors.name: Aleix Segui, Arantza Ugalde, Andreas Fichtner, Huynh Van Luong, Wes Armour

papers.title: Low Vibration Closed-Cycle Flow Cryostat for Ion-Cavity Experiments
papers.summary: Cryogenic operation below 10 K suppresses trap-electrode and dielectric heating of trapped ions while cryopumping residual gases to ultra-high vacuum (UHV) without requiring a bakeout. These advantages are particularly important for cavity-integrated ion traps, where nearby dielectric surfaces can increase motional heating and rapid design-build-test iterations benefit from eliminating bakeout cycles. We have developed a custom 4 K cryostat cooled by a ColdEdge Technologies (CET) Stinger closed-cycle $^{4}\text{He}$ flow cryogenic system to study various ion trap optical cavity structures designed to serve as a photonic interconnect between remote, compute-capable trapped $^{171}\text{Yb}^{+}$ ion quantum processors, enabling long baseline entanglement distribution $(>10\text{ km})$. We integrate an Alpine Quantum Technologies (AQT) Paul trap and Fabry-P\'erot optical cavity at the 4 K stage. The cooling capacities of the cryostat 40 K and 4 K stages were measured to be 5 W at 45 K and 0.5 W at 6.1 K. Vibrations of the 4 K stage relative to the optical table are less than $12\text{ nm}_{\text{RMS}}$ in three dimensions, as measured using a Michelson interferometer. An ultra-high vacuum (UHV) is inferred by studying the rate of hydrogen-$\mathrm{Yb}^{+}$ ion collisions. Ion storage times exceeding 5 days without laser cooling have been reported and the position of the trapped ions are reproducible within $\sim10\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ following repeated thermal cycles to room temperature. The uptime of this system is 72 days and offers convenient access to the 4 K stage for in-vacuum maintenance and system modifications. Using this platform, we demonstrate spatial overlap and interaction between a trapped $^{174}\text{Yb}^{+}$ ion and the optical cavity mode on the 1345 nm transition, establishing preliminary experimental validation of the integrated cryogenic ion-cavity structure.

authors.name: Andrew Laugharn

papers.title: The replication-energy limit of PQG reduced-density-matrix theory from a single-fragment semidefinite program
papers.summary: Variational two-electron reduced-density-matrix calculations are not size extensive: the energy per fragment can decrease when identical, strictly noninteracting fragments are replicated [M. Nakata and K. Yasuda, Phys. Rev. A 80, 042109 (2009)]. For the $P$, $Q$, and $G$ conditions (PQG) we prove the following. (i) The energy per fragment converges to the minimum of a semidefinite program (SDP) on one fragment. The limit is reached through negative interfragment covariances of order $1/(k-1)$ for $k$ replicas, which cancel the local electron number and spin fluctuations consistently with a global singlet. (ii) The energy per fragment is nonincreasing in the replica count. (iii) It reaches the limit exactly at a finite replica count. (iv) The defect is tied to the local electron-number variance: a sharp local electron number restores additivity without a spin constraint. (v) In chains of identical units the energy per unit has a limit that tends to the same minimum as the coupling vanishes. The key tool is that the $G$ condition [C. Garrod and J. K. Percus, J. Math. Phys. 5, 1756 (1964)] keeps the variances and covariances of one-body operators positive semidefinite without a representing state, so that the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applies. PQG therefore admits explicitly constructed replicated points whose compensated local fluctuations lower the energy per fragment below the isolated value. Be, CH$_4$, N$_2$, and H$_2$O (STO-6G) and a four-site Hubbard fragment illustrate the results; in these examples the gap to the isolated value persists with three-index conditions $T_1$ and $T_2$.

authors.name: Maho Nakata

papers.title: Electric polarizabilities with phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
papers.summary: While projector quantum Monte Carlo methods are known for producing accurate ground-state energies, the prediction of other properties that encode the electronic response to applied electric and magnetic fields has historically been challenging. In this work we demonstrate that the electric (static) polarizability tensor, which is formally a second-derivative of the energy with respect to electric fields, can be efficiently computed with phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo using a correlated sampling finite-difference strategy. With simple Hartree-Fock trial wave functions, we investigate a series of small molecules (some of which are difficult for approximate density functionals), polyacenes of increasing size, and ferrocene as a representative organometallic complex. The methodology is scalable to relatively large molecules involving thousands of basis functions, and with appropriate trial wave functions remains robust for strongly correlated electronic states, as we show for the stretched dinitrogen molecule. This work opens the door to the computation of a host of other second-order molecular properties with auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, which will inform the ongoing search for optimal trial wave functions and extend benchmark-quality training data sets for the refinement of semi-empirical and machine learning models for quantum chemistry and molecular simulation.

authors.name: Leon Otis, Jo Kurian, James Shee

papers.title: Infrared Relaxation Modes and the Emergence of Collective Order in Neural Dynamics
papers.summary: We develop a microscopic field theory of collective order formation in interacting nonlinear neural systems. Integrating out microscopic neural degrees of freedom yields an effective action whose quadratic kernel determines the ordering threshold, while higher-order connected responses govern nonlinear stabilization. Spectral decomposition reveals that relaxation rates and collective-mode overlaps control collective instability and memory dynamics. Enhanced infrared spectral weight lowers the critical coupling and generates long-time memory, revealing a common spectral origin of collective ordering and persistent dynamics. Controlled numerical constructions verify the spectral dependence of collective instability and response, while nonlinear mean-field scaling follows from the microscopic Landau expansion. Transformer Jacobian spectra further reveal learning-induced infrared organization and transient memory enhancement consistent with critical-like response. Our results establish a microscopic framework linking neural interactions, collective order, and long-time memory.

authors.name: Byung Gyu Chae

papers.title: An eight-channel RFSoC waveform digitizer with AC- and DC-coupled front ends and transparent dual-DDR event memory
papers.summary: We present Transparent Dual-DDR Event Memory (TDEM) for the triggered readout of an eight-channel radio-frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) digitizer. With either an AC- or a DC-coupled front end, each accepted trigger records 4096 samples per channel at 5 GSa/s. Two pulses 100 ns apart produced separate, overlapping records. On one DC-coupled input, interleaving calibration reduced an eight-sample periodic residual by a factor of 29 at +100 mV, but not at zero input. After a power cycle, the digitizer restored the coefficients for all eight DC-coupled inputs without a training tone. TDEM assigns complete events to 64- and 32-bit DDR4 memory interfaces in a 2:1 ratio. With this allocation alone, host page requests still determined which memory served each read. In two runs of approximately 6 s at 160 kHz, the peak receiver backlog fell from 20 140 events with the earlier readout to 1457 with event-level prefetch. Prefetch raised the sustained rate of the DC-coupled system from 150 to 170 kHz under repeated host readout pauses. With the same receiver design and a revised host buffer allocation, the AC-coupled system passed three 30 min tests at 175 kHz, each with 48 readout pauses and no rejected triggers. Without imposed pauses or background load, the host verified all 323 452 631 events in 30 min at 179.7 kHz. At 180 kHz, triggers were first rejected at the digitizer, consistent with a modelled transmitter capacity of 179.730 kHz for this event format.

authors.name: Tao Xue

papers.title: QuakeConsensus: Reducing false detections in automatic earthquake catalogs through consensus phase association
papers.summary: Automatic earthquake catalogs rely on phase associators to group the picks of a phase picker into events. Associators also produce false events that inflate the catalog. We measure the false events of five associators, PyOcto, GaMMA, REAL, GENIE, and backprojection, on two benchmarks built from observed phase picks in Taiwan. The first benchmark isolates 28,129 cataloged earthquakes in 20-minute windows, adding noise by shifting unassociated picks independently. The second evaluates 11,917 earthquakes from the 2024 $M_w$ 7.4 Hualien aftershock sequence, shifting unassociated P and S pairs together. We also propose a consensus association strategy that keeps an event found by at least two associators. With noise picks, single associators produce 5.3% to 10.2% false positives on the regional benchmark and 11.8% to 46.8% on the Hualien benchmark, whereas the consensus catalog reduces these false positive percentages to 4.2% and 11.5%, respectively. The consensus has the highest F1 score and the smallest percentage of false positives on both benchmarks.

authors.name: Wu-Yu Liao, En-Jui Lee

papers.title: XTCP: an open-source FPGA TCP endpoint for readout over 10 and 25 Gigabit Ethernet
papers.summary: XTCP is an open-source implementation of the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for high-rate detector readout. It targets sustained single-connection throughput near the TCP payload limit. In separate 10 Gigabit Ethernet transfers on the same Kintex UltraScale+ KU5P card and Linux host, XTCP and SiTCP-XG each delivered a median application-level throughput of 9.49 Gbit/s towards the host. Towards the FPGA, the medians were 9.49 Gbit/s for XTCP and 5.76 Gbit/s for the tested SiTCP-XG configuration. The XTCP prototype used more lookup tables and on-chip memory. In a 96 GiB echo test spanning repeated sequence-number wraps, recording when an acknowledgement first crossed the recovery boundary allowed four fast recoveries that the earlier signed comparison would have blocked. On one 25 Gigabit Ethernet bitstream, increasing the IP maximum transmission unit from 1500 to 9000 bytes raised median one-way throughput from 23.30 to 24.70 Gbit/s towards the host and from 22.09 to 24.08 Gbit/s towards the FPGA. At 9000 bytes these rates reached 99.7% and 97.1% of the TCP payload limit, respectively. In a separate echo test, the host verified all 8.77 TB returned by a jumbo-frame prototype over one connection in 3595 s, averaging 19.51 Gbit/s per direction.

authors.name: Tao Xue

papers.title: China daily CO2 emission estimates 2019-2025
papers.summary: Near-real-time CO2 estimates enable timely tracking of emission changes, but broad sectoral classifications limit their ability to resolve industrial dynamics across China's provinces. Here, we update Carbon Monitor to estimate daily CO2 emissions across five sectors in 31 mainland Chinese provinces during 2019-2025 and monthly emissions from 40 industrial and construction subsectors in 30 provinces, combining historical inventories with industrial production indicators. National emissions increased from 10.83 Gt CO2 in 2019 to 12.15 Gt CO2 in 2023, before declining slightly to 12.08 Gt CO2 in 2025. The 2024-2025 national reduction of 0.23% reflected opposing sectoral trends, with industrial emissions increasing by 48.8 Mt CO2 while power generation and ground transport emissions decreased by 46.6 Mt CO2 and 27.7 Mt CO2, respectively. Provincial trajectories also diverged, with emissions rising in 16 provinces and falling in 15. Industrial disaggregation revealed increases of 102.3 Mt CO2 in nonferrous-metal smelting and pressing and decreases of 108.1 Mt CO2 in nonmetal mineral products during 2019-2024. Comparison with a historical provincial inventory yielded a median absolute relative difference of 9.4%. These findings demonstrate that national emission stabilization masks divergent regional and industrial changes, highlighting the need for temporally updated, sector-specific evidence to assess progress toward sustained reductions and identify mitigation priorities.

authors.name: Xiaoting Huang, Zhu Deng, Ling Ye, Peng Lu, Xuanren Song, Yuli Shan, Zhu Liu

papers.title: Friendship paradoxes in networks
papers.summary: Since Scott L. Feld's seminal paper entitled ``Why your friends have more friends than you do'' [Am.~J.~Sociol.~\textbf{96}, 1464 (1991)], the friendship paradox (FP) has been extensively studied in network science and related fields over the last decades. In this paper we survey the literature on the FP and its generalizations. We first introduce definitions and general results of the FPs defined in networks, and then overview their results on model networks. Empirical results using various social network data as well as applications to real-world problems, such as early detection of outbreaks and network sampling, are also summarized. Finally, we conclude by discussing several directions of possible future works.

authors.name: Eun Lee, Hang-Hyun Jo

papers.title: Global Patterns and Drivers of Terrestrial Surface Albedo Dynamics from 2001 to 2025
papers.summary: Terrestrial surface albedo is a fundamental determinant of the global radiative balance, yet a spatially integrated understanding of its long-term trajectories and multi-sphere environmental drivers remains lacking. Utilizing MODIS observations (2001-2025), this study integrates Theil-Sen trend analysis, standardized anomaly diagnostics, and a pixel-wise multiple linear regression framework to quantify global albedo dynamics and attribute them to biophysical drivers. Our results reveal that global albedo change is characterized by profound spatial heterogeneity rather than a uniform trend, with 23.3% of the land surface exhibiting significant brightening, while 18.9% showed significant darkening. Multi-driver attribution demonstrates a clear zonal organization of controls: snow cover dominates albedo variability in northern high latitudes (46.9% of classified area), while NDVI (41.0%) and soil moisture (12.1%) govern tropical vegetated regions and moisture-limited transitional zones, respectively. These findings underscore that while terrestrial albedo is a robust indicator of Earth system change, its interpretation depends strongly on regional cryospheric, biophysical, and hydrological contexts.

authors.name: Xiaoting Huang, Zhu Liu

papers.title: A Constrained Coupled Cluster Approach for Strongly Correlated Electrons
papers.summary: We introduce constrained coupled cluster (cCC), a general framework for imposing arbitrary physical constraints on conventional single-reference coupled cluster amplitudes without rederiving or replacing the underlying coupled cluster residual equations. As a first application, we derive a constraint from the spin-symmetry requirement for an exact wavefunction and demonstrate the resulting approach on strongly correlated problems. Across benchmark Hubbard models, nitrogen and chromium bond breaking, and iron--sulfur cluster spin gaps, the constraint strongly suppresses spin contamination, repairs qualitative failures of conventional coupled cluster, and often brings CCSDT, and in several cases CCSD, into quantitative agreement with exact diagonalization or high-accuracy density matrix renormalization group calculations. The derived constraint adds only a mean-field cost contraction to the coupled cluster calculation and is compatible with any cluster truncation. These results identify numerical constraints as a promising route for extending single-reference coupled cluster machinery into strongly correlated regimes conventionally associated with more complicated electronic structure methods.

authors.name: Chenghan Li, Garnet K. -L. Chan

papers.title: Pseudo-Altermagnetism in Non-Hermitian Systems
papers.summary: Altermagnetism has attracted growing attention, and its analogs have been actively explored across classical platforms. Here, we introduce pseudo-altermagnetism in non-Hermitian systems, where balanced gain and loss plays the role of the altermagnetic spin, and the opposite gain and loss sublattices are related by an antiunitary symmetry $O$ with $O\bm k\neq \bm k$ for generic momentum $\bm k$. Using a two-dimensional non-Hermitian system with $O=C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$ symmetry as a representative example, we find that pseudo-altermagnetism not only leads to a momentum-dependent gain and loss distribution analogous to the momentum-dependent spin splitting of altermagnets, but also exhibits intrinsic non-Hermitian properties. The bands of $C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$-invariant non-Hermitian systems are either isolated or paired by $C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$, and both cases are guaranteed to host movable but unremovable nodal structures, characterized by the zeros of two distinct quantities. An isolated band exhibits two movable but unremovable Hermitian spectral lines, whose generic points are not invariant under $C_{4z}\mathcal{T}$, in sharp contrast to the conventional Hermitian spectra enforced only at the fixed points of an antiunitary symmetry. The paired bands, in turn, feature a movable but unremovable nodal network formed by the union of real-part and imaginary-part degeneracy lines, whose intersections are generally exceptional points. We further demonstrate these findings in a non-Hermitian photonic crystal. Our results establish a symmetry-based bridge between non-Hermitian physics and altermagnetism, and provide novel mechanisms of Hermitian spectra beyond $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry.

authors.name: Chang-Yin Ji, Runze Li, Zhi-Ming Yu, Yugui Yao

papers.title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
papers.summary: The aerodynamic performance of motorsport vehicles relies on understanding the unsteady flow dynamics around complex geometries at high Reynolds numbers. Extracting the dominant 3D coherent structures from high-fidelity simulations is often intractable due to the high dimensionality of the state-space, and standard modal decompositions, such as proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), do not give interpretable meaning to the temporal dynamics of the modes. This study demonstrates a scalable POD and Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) method, implemented in the open-source pyLOM framework, that can identify coherent structures and their temporal dynamics in high-fidelity simulations of Formula 1 aerodynamics, specifically the Imperial Front Wing (IFW), a publicly available benchmark based on the McLaren MP4-17D, at Reynolds number $Re = 2.2 \times 10^5$. DMD is applied to large eddy simulation (LES) results of the flow field that is resolved using spectral/hp element method via Nektar++, producing $49.72 \times 10^6$ degrees of freedom at polynomial order p=4. The simulation captures four dominant vortical structures (endplate, canard, main, and footplate), with time-averaged force coefficients showing 2.24% and 2.87% differences in $C_L$ and $C_D$ compared to the reference data. DMD extracts the frequencies, amplitudes and damping ratios of the coherent structures, and modes at chord-based Strouhal numbers of 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 are associated, through point-probe spectra, with the main-element laminar separation bubble, canard vortex core pulsation and endplate vortex meander, respectively. The DMD allows for both a model reduction technique and a compression scheme, here reducing approximately 6 TB of snapshots to 200 GB of modal data.

authors.name: Parv Khurana, Benet Eiximeno, Alexandra Liosi, Spencer Sherwin, Athanasios Chatzopoulos, Julien Hoessler, Arnau Mir\'o, Oriol Lehmkuhl, Ivette Rodriguez, J. Nathan Kutz

papers.title: A Steady Theory for Highly Unsteady Thin Airfoil Motions
papers.summary: A generalized steady thin airfoil theory is built not from steady flow, but from flows in which there exists a frame of reference where the absolute vorticity field is steady. We specialize this general idea to construct a foliation of a domain of phase space for thin airfoil motions in which staying on a leaf of the foliation maintains zero absolute vorticity in the fluid indefinitely. The phase space is described by the airfoil's total rotation rate, speed, and angle of attack. It is found using this definition that one of the preeminent unsteady stall conditions is equivalent to the traditional steady stall condition for this class of flows, various other classical results can be re-interpreted as steady in the absolute vorticity field, and insight is also provided into the surprising experimental results of McGowan et al. (AIAA J. 49, 2011). We show parts of existing quasi-steady flow and Theodorsen unsteady flow theory can be built from a planar approximation of our foliation, making the quasi-steady extension of our theory trivial, and suggesting how an unsteady extension can be created as well. Furthermore, pure unsteady effects in the new theory amount to a transversal of the leaves, occupying just one dimension, inviting interesting prospects for future experimental and theoretical work.

authors.name: Scott A. Bollt

papers.title: Designing Incoherent Multispectral Diffractive Optical Networks for Satellite Image Classification
papers.summary: Optical neural networks and diffractive optical computing provide a promising route for performing task-specific inference with high parallelism and lightweight electronic post-processing. These advantages are especially attractive for multispectral satellite imaging, where conventional workflows rely on transmitting high-dimensional image cubes to the ground for downstream electronic analysis. Here, we introduce a computationally efficient surrogate model-guided framework for designing incoherent multispectral diffractive optical networks that directly output class probabilities onboard, eliminating the need to capture and transfer the full multispectral data cube for ground-side inference. We first train a physically compatible surrogate model, represented by a non-negative fully connected model that accommodates a generalized detector readout, yielding a task-specific non-negative multispectral intensity transformation that can be transferred to an optical processor. We then synthesize its diffractive counterpart through data-free point-spread-function-based optimization under spatially incoherent illumination. Using this approach, we numerically demonstrate a six-spectral-channel diffractive classifier for tri-class satellite-scene recognition, achieving a blind-testing accuracy of 79.8% for artificial surface, water body, and vegetated land images, closely approaching the 81.8% accuracy of its surrogate. We further demonstrate a more compact three-spectral-channel design that numerically achieves 72.7% blind-testing accuracy, compared with 75.1% for its corresponding surrogate model. This surrogate model-guided strategy provides a practical pathway for designing compact, task-specific incoherent multispectral optical processors for resource-constrained remote-sensing inference.

authors.name: Xilin Yang, Md Sadman Sakib Rahman, Ryan Lee, Aydogan Ozcan

papers.title: Relativistic Harmonic Generation in Spatiotemporal Plasma Photonic Crystals
papers.summary: Spatiotemporal photonic crystals offer a route to controlling the frequency, momentum, and energy of light. Extending this capability to relativistic laser intensities calls for a plasma-based platform. Here we propose a spatiotemporal plasma photonic crystal (SPPC) formed at a solid surface driven by intense pump pulses, with a separate probe interacting with the resulting modulation. The spatial and temporal periodicity of the SPPC determines the allowed harmonic frequencies and emission angles, while its complex Floquet bands explain how the probe draws energy from the modulation. Beyond harmonic generation, this picture predicts wavelength-dependent probe amplification as the probe accesses amplifying modes of the SPPC, providing an experimentally testable connection between the band structure and energy transfer. Agreement with particle-in-cell simulations supports this interpretation.

authors.name: Haojie Zhang, Boyuan Li, Xiangyan An, Rong Huang, Feng Liu, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Min Chen

papers.title: A Novel Multi-Target Approach for simultaneous enhancement of brightness, intensity, and bi-spectral performance of cold neutron sources
papers.summary: Increasing the brightness of cold neutron beams is a central objective in modern cold neutron source development, since it largely governs the sample intensity for high-resolution neutron instruments. Raising accelerator beam power is constrained by the target heat-removal limit of 0.5-1 kW/cm2, and increasing the moderator length beyond about 20-30 cm becomes inefficient owing to the finite mean free path of cold neutrons. We propose reversing the conventional design logic: rather than tailoring the cryogenic moderator to a fixed target-premoderator source, we tailor the thermal-neutron source geometry to a high-performance moderator configuration. The concept is realized as a staircase moderator assembly of several shorter compressed moderators, each with its own target-premoderator unit, which distributes neutron production among multiple units and thus enables higher accelerator powers while preserving the brightness advantages of compressed moderators. This approach can provide additional brightness and intensity gains relative to a single low-dimensional or conventional voluminous moderator at the desired transverse beam size and may naturally generate bi-spectral neutron beams, thereby extending the dynamic range of neutron instruments.

authors.name: A. Ioffe, P. Konik, D. Shapiro

papers.title: Flow-induced vibration of an array of circular cylinders in a square enclosure due to thermal buoyancy
papers.summary: Flow-induced oscillations of heated cylinder arrays in a square enclosure driven solely by natural convection are investigated in the current study at Prandtl number of 7 and Raleigh number of $10^7$ (based on side of square enclosure). This is accomplished by a coupled thermal-fluid-structure-interaction formulation based on body-fitted arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework, implemented using variational finite element methodology. Study on stationary array shows asymmetry in the $3\times 3$ configuration, along with a non-dimensional wall-gap plume oscillation frequency of 0.183 on the left column cylinders. When elastically mounted, these cylinders synchronize and lock-in with the frequency at reduced velocity of 15.7. The remaining cylinders undergo broadband buffeting that grows monotonically with reduced velocity and exceeds the synchronized response. The $4\times 4$ array shows symmetric behavior with no synchronization. The response is observed to be forced buffeting for all the cylinders, and dominated by the slow plume forcing for the inner column cylinders. The motion of the cylinders also influence the heat transfer characteristics. The $3\times 3$ array shows negligible change in heat transfer for the whole array, while measurable enhancement is observed for $4\times 4$ array.

authors.name: Amit Pramod Joshi, Nishit Gupta, Unnat Agarwal, Vaibhav Joshi

papers.title: COSIMA Cookbook: a community-driven resource for ocean and sea-ice modelling science
papers.summary: The COSIMA Cookbook is an open educational resource for analysing ocean and sea-ice model output in Jupyter notebooks. It has been developed by the Consortium for Ocean--Sea Ice Modelling in Australia (COSIMA) as a community resource for researchers, students, and practitioners working with large gridded datasets, especially output from the ACCESS ocean--sea ice model configurations. The Cookbook is organised around a gastronomy theme: ``Cooking Tutorials'' teach generic, transferable techniques for handling model output, while "Easy Recipes", "Advanced Recipes" and "Regional Specialties" are self-contained notebooks that show how to perform concrete diagnostics and analyses. Along the way, the notebooks demonstrate open-source tools for the scientific analysis of large data, including Intake catalogues, Xarray, Dask, xgcm, xESMF, eofs, Parcels, matplotlib and Cartopy. The Cookbook addresses the steep entry cost of analysing climate model output: it packages expert, often tacit, knowledge into complete, well-documented and reusable workflows, in the same medium in which researchers actually work. It is developed openly on GitHub, is published as a documentation website, and is continuously reviewed and extended by its community through pull requests and regular hackathons. The easy access to data and analysis it provides has contributed to the international adoption of ACCESS ocean and sea-ice model configurations, and has facilitated well over 100 peer-reviewed papers and more than 20 PhD projects.

authors.name: Navid C. Constantinou, Julia Neme, Wilton Aguiar, Matthis Auger, Ashley J. Barnes, Romain Beucher, Dhruv Bhagtani, Christopher Yit Sen Bull, Hannah Dawson, Noah Day, Fabio Boeira Dias, Edward W. Doddridge, Anupiya Ellepola, Denisse Fierro-Arcos, Angus Gibson, Aidan Heerdegen, Andy McC. Hogg, Ryan M. Holmes, Maurice F. Huguenin, Wilma Huneke, Jemma Jeffree, Andrew E.
