At pH 4, however, p(NIPAm-co-AA) microgels are weakly charged and exhibit a volume phase transition near the lower critical solution temperature of pNIPAm; the magnitude of the size change is greater for the less-crosslinked microgel. Above the volume phase transition temperature, the volume change from hydrodynamic radius decouples from that from viscosity. The ratio of the radius of gyration and hydrodynamic radius R_g/R_h of p(NIPAm-co-AA) microgels at high temperature exceeds the value theoretically predicted for homogeneous spheres and the deviation increases with the extent of crosslinking, suggesting that a non-uniform internal distribution of polymer gives rise to the anomalous decoupling at high temperatures. Our results indicate that care must be taken in extrapolating packing fractions for multi-responsive copolymer microgels, and suggest that copolymer composition and crosslink density may be used to tune bulk properties such as rheology through the internal microstructure.

authors.name: Peter Edimeh, Howard Chen, Jacinta C. Conrad

papers.title: How a Prediction Dies: A Challenge-Driven, Rule-Bound Self-Refutation in an LLM Agent Society
papers.summary: Persistent societies of large language model agents now make empirical claims about their own collective behaviour, yet the fate of such claims is rarely observable. We document one claim, from registration to death, on AITRAP, a multi-agent platform whose public, append-only ledger records every action. The claim (0495d171, registered 19 October 2026) asserted that a majority of bridges between problem domains would remain attached to a single exploration lineage. Three community challenges forced its judgment criterion through four versions, from an ambiguous statement to an executable protocol with a fixed threshold, a minimum-frame-size gate, and a baseline calibration gate. When the first frame with at least 20 bridges arrived, support stood at 9 of 79 (11.4%; Wilson 95% CI [6.1%, 20.3%]); the author, bound by the registered clause, refuted the claim and relinquished the associated stake. Three findings emerge. The criterion became executable only under community pressure, which we document version by version. The calibration gate caught a fault in the author's own recalculation that would otherwise have published a spuriously perfect 0/79 result. The failure itself traces to a denominator that grew 8.8-fold in five days while the numerator grew 1.8-fold, coinciding with a change in platform incentives; we report this mechanism as a hypothesis, not a rescuing condition. A claim whose termination is carried out exactly as written carries more evidential weight than one that survives, and this case provides initial empirical grounds for treating voluntary self-refutation as a candidate indicator of epistemic accountability in incentive-coupled agent societies.

authors.name: Lei Zhenbing, Lei Chang

papers.title: Louis Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation: Circulation and Reception
papers.summary: Louis Bachelier's Theorie de la speculation (1900) introduced a probabilistic model of Brownian motion in a study of financial fluctuations, five years before Einstein's physical theory. By connecting probability distributions with the heat equation and studying speculation and option valuation, Bachelier anticipated central developments in probability, physics, and mathematical finance. How widely did the thesis circulate before its broader significance was recognized? Drawing on library correspondence, surviving copies, accession registers, provenance marks, historical catalogues, and acquisition lists, this article reconstructs its international circulation and reception in two forms: the separate Gauthier-Villars dissertation and its publication in the Annales scientifiques de l'Ecole normale superieure. It identifies thirty-eight foreign academic institutions in the official dissertation exchange network for 1900 and documents its operation. University exchanges, commercial purchases, journal distribution, and personal presentations provided complementary channels. American holdings reveal its geographical reach, including receipt at Cornell in April 1900. Contemporary reviews and subsequent uses establish selective engagement in mathematics, actuarial science, and economics, including transmission without attribution. An examination of probability composition and diffusion clarifies the thesis's place in the history of stochastic processes and its relationship to physical Brownian motion. Columbia's journal volume, accessioned in 1901 and borrowed by Mandelbrot in 1961, connects early dissemination with renewed interest. Distinguishing availability from documented reading and use, the study shows that delayed recognition coexisted with early international circulation and a dispersed readership across scientific traditions.

authors.name: Hector Giacomini

papers.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
papers.summary: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.

authors.name: Athul S. Rema, Adri\'an E. Rubio L\'opez, Felipe Herrera

papers.title: photon number correlations in harmonics driven with classical and quantum light
papers.summary: Recent reports of nonclassical intensity correlations in harmonic generation raised questions about whether strong harmonic correlations necessarily imply genuinely quantum behaviour. Here, we compare the low-photon-number perturbative harmonic generation driven by classical and bright squeezed vacuum sources. The latter generates strong auto- and cross-correlations in the harmonic spectrum. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and heralding measurements show that the cross-correlations are fully classical and can be explained by the common fluctuations from the driving field. A visible scaling of the measured correlation function with mean harmonic flux is observed, which is well-explained by a click detector-response model.

authors.name: Katarzyna M. Kowalczyk, Michael T. Weil, Kevin Murzyn, Andr\'e Staudte, Jeff S. Lundeen, David M. Villeneuve, Giulio Vampa

papers.title: Interstitial Magnetoelectricity in Altermagnetic Electrides
papers.summary: Electrides and altermagnets are two distinct yet intriguing classes of quantum materials, characterized by interstitial anionic electrons and nonrelativistic spin splitting, respectively. The recent prediction of Stoner-instability-driven altermagnetic electride provides a natural bridge between these two fields. Here, we investigate the magnetoelectric response and its related spin-polarized transport in the altermagnetic electride Zr$_2$N monolayer. Using the tight-binding Hubbard model and first-principles calculations, we find that the electric field can break the magnetic compensation between the two interstitial anionic electrons, inducing a finite net magnetization and giving rise to an interstitial electron mediated magnetoelectric response. The magnetoelectric response is further demonstrated through the electrical control of spin conductivity. Our results reveal a magnetoelectric effect in altermagnetic electrides, paving a way towards electride-based spintronic devices.

authors.name: Yue Li, Shibo Fang, Jianhua Wang, Qiang Li, Weizhen Meng, Haiyu Meng, Xiong-Xiong Xue, Jianfeng Wang, Yi Du, Jing Lu, Yee Sin Ang

papers.title: Large Deviations and Critical Scaling in the Finite-Population Granovetter Threshold Model
papers.summary: We develop a systematic asymptotic analysis of the exact finite-population solution of Granovetter's threshold model, in which a single initial instigator triggers a cascade among agents with independently distributed adoption thresholds. By expressing the propagation probability as an order-statistic boundary-crossing event, we formulate its macroscopic large-deviation rate as a constrained relative-entropy minimization problem. For Beta-distributed thresholds, we obtain explicit solutions for all shape parameters $\alpha$ and $\beta$, identifying four possible optimal empirical threshold profiles: fully free, fully pinned, pinned--free, and free--pinned. These profiles determine both the exponential probability of macroscopic cascades and the threshold configurations responsible for their occurrence. Importance-sampling estimates confirm the analytical rate functions, while sequential Monte Carlo simulations independently reproduce the predicted optimal profiles. We also revisit the critical scaling near $\alpha_c=1$ and confirm the principal finite-size scaling laws: the mean active fraction decays as $N^{-1/2}$ for uniform thresholds and as $N^{-1}$ for $\alpha=1$ and $0<\beta<1$. In the latter regime, we further derive an explicit scaling function for the logarithmic critical window from the microscopic branching-process limit. Our results provide a general framework for determining the probabilities and characteristic configurations of rare collective events in threshold-driven cascade processes

authors.name: Jos\'e F. Fontanari

papers.title: Observation of nonadiabatic quantum tunneling in a driven correlated insulator
papers.summary: Many emerging solid-state platforms for Floquet engineering, nonlinear transport, and high harmonic generation operate near the Keldysh crossover, where optical fields are sufficiently strong and fast to reshape electronic states on sub-cycle timescales. Despite its importance, the microscopic pathways for photocarrier generation in this regime remain poorly understood, as neither perturbative multiphoton absorption nor adiabatic tunneling provides an adequate description. Here, we perform time-resolved optical spectroscopy on the correlated van der Waals insulator NiPS$_3$ while systematically tuning the drive electric field and frequency over a wide range. In the crossover regime, we observe multiphoton-like resonances that are blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects within an otherwise tunneling-dominated absorption channel - a clear spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown. Hubbard-model simulations based on a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach qualitatively reproduce these features. Together, our results elucidate the microscopic mechanisms of charge excitation in the Keldysh crossover regime and identify a key ingredient for controlling strong-field nonlinear dynamics in correlated materials.

authors.name: Mingyao Guo, Radu Andrei, Jaena Park, Je-Geun Park, Eugene Demler, David Hsieh

papers.title: Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications
papers.summary: We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.

authors.name: Vladimir Mikhalev

papers.title: Multi-Sensor Fusion for False-Alarm Reduction by Timed Electromechanical Corroboration
papers.summary: A physician checks the clinical electrocardiogram against other observations. A wearable monitor has no physician. This paper shows that a mechanical sensor worn beside the electrocardiogram can take over that check, and that the right added sensors lower false alarms further. A beat is accepted only when a mechanical contraction follows at the delay learned for the wearer. Beat-shaped artifacts injected into resting and exercise recordings passed the electrocardiogram alone almost every time. A seismocardiogram or phonocardiogram as the second channel rejected most while keeping nearly all true beats, strongly at rest and partly during exercise. Shifting the mechanical signal in time removed the benefit. A detection criterion scores an added sensor by the part of its response that the sensors in place cannot predict. With four sensors, this score ranked the sets as their measured false-alarm rates did. With the two sensors it selected, 6.2 percent of the artifacts passed while 95 percent of true beats were kept, half the rate of the best single sensor. In integer arithmetic on a low-cost microcontroller, the detector made the same decisions as the software. These rates come from injected artifacts, not alarms in patients. Natural motion and clinical events remain untested.

authors.name: Zixuan Fu, Anthony Raffaele, Unnikrishna Pillai

papers.title: An informational interpretation of the reverse nonequilibrium molecular dynamics
papers.summary: Reverse nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (RNEMD) is an efficient simulation method for determining transport coefficients. In this method, a flux is imposed by a seemingly artificial nonlocal exchange operation and the corresponding thermodynamic gradient is induced as a result, apparently reversing the usual force-flux causality. Although this method is well studied as a simulation technique, developing an information-thermodynamic interpretation of its Maxwell-demon-type operation and the associated apparent reversal of force-flux causality would provide a solid physical foundation for algorithms of this type. Here, we develop an information-reservoir interpretation for a representative RNEMD scheme for determining self-diffusivity. We show that the statistical bias of the information reservoir defines an information affinity that sustains a concentration gradient and a diffusive flux in the steady state. We further derive the linear transport coefficient corresponding to the information affinity in the linear response regime. Using the large deviation functional for the steady-state densities and currents, we also establish a fluctuation theorem for entropy production and the thermodynamic uncertainty relation linking entropy production to the fluctuations of the particle current. Computer simulations are performed to corroborate our theoretical results.

authors.name: Yuxing Jiao, Mingcheng Yang

papers.title: CLFF: Automated Framework for Concurrent Learning Force Fields and Material Property Calculations
papers.summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer an efficient paradigm for large-scale atomistic simulations with near first-principles accuracy. However, developing and deploying these potentials often involves intricate procedures that require substantial manual effort and domain expertise. In this work, we present CLFF, an open-source Python framework designed to automate concurrent learning workflows for MLIPs. CLFF integrates model training, MLIP-driven sampling, uncertainty-based candidate selection, quantum-mechanical labeling, and dataset augmentation into a unified workflow. The framework currently supports several modern graph-based MLIP architectures and is compatible with widely used computational chemistry and materials science tools. A distinguishing feature of CLFF is its ability to asynchronously distribute computational tasks across multiple heterogeneous remote computing resources, enabling users to aggregate fragmented hardware infrastructure within a single controllable workflow. In addition to concurrent learning, CLFF provides automated workflows for initial data generation and material property calculations, including phonon dispersion and potential energy surface scans. By minimizing manual intervention and enhancing reproducibility, CLFF offers a flexible platform for developing and deploying MLIPs in computational materials research.

authors.name: Cao Thang Nguyen, Sung Youb Kim

papers.title: Bogoliubov-picture thermofield dynamics in anharmonic environments
papers.summary: Thermofield dynamics (TFD) describes finite-temperature quantum relaxation through a purified wavefunction, without sampling thermally populated initial states. For harmonic environments, TFD is typically combined with a thermal Bogoliubov transformation to obtain a compact wavefunction representation. This transformation can also be useful for anharmonic baths, but preparing the corresponding thermal state in the transformed representation poses additional numerical challenges. Here, we explore TFD approaches tailored to anharmonic potentials and compatible with efficient tensor network methods for quantum propagation. We show that the conceptually appealing route of converting a harmonic-reference thermal state into the target anharmonic state by imaginary-time propagation can be numerically ill-conditioned. As a practical alternative, we formulate a multilayer multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (ML-MCTDH) protocol that separates thermal-state preparation from the harmonic-reference Bogoliubov transformation. We prepare the thermal purification in the bare representation and then apply finite-basis Bogoliubov unitaries to the physical--auxiliary mode pairs. For independent bath modes, direct construction of the thermal amplitude provides a complementary initialization procedure. We illustrate this protocol through vibrational relaxation and spatial-superposition decoherence of a harmonic subsystem coupled to a Morse-oscillator bath. We find non-monotonic energy relaxation, shifts in the dominant resonant response, and oscillatory energy exchange at zero and finite temperature. For decoherence, we recover the expected harmonic-bath scaling and find a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of the decay rate on anharmonicity at finite temperature in a low-frequency model, with a weaker dependence in a high-frequency model.

authors.name: Rocco Martinazzo, Bartosz B{\l}asiak, Irene Burghardt

papers.title: An Annular Spiral Construction for Anomalous Dissipation in the Forced Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.summary: Kolmogorov's 1941 theory of turbulence (K41) predicts that the rate of kinetic energy dissipation in a turbulent flow can remain positive as viscosity tends to zero. In 2023, Bru\`e and De Lellis used quasi-self-similar mixing to construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations exhibiting anomalous dissipation. In this paper, we show that anomalous dissipation can still occur for a flow with spiral geometry in an annulus. In the horizontal plane, we wind a radial segment into a two-turn spiral and then apply alternating shears. After each pair of shears, the image of the segment shares a subarc of positive length with the original spiral. We compare the vertical velocity with sine profiles whose angular period halves with each pair. After the horizontal flow stops, diffusion damps the final profile. By embedding this planar construction into the $(2+\frac{1}{2})$-dimensional framework, we obtain smooth solutions of the three-dimensional equations with the same smooth initial datum. For a sequence of viscosities tending to zero, their dissipation over a fixed subannulus and one vertical period has a uniform positive lower bound, and their forces converge in $C^\alpha$ uniformly in time for every $0<\alpha<1$. We use this spiral construction to produce solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations that exhibit anomalous dissipation.

authors.name: Changhong Li

papers.title: Pharmacy stock and post-earthquake access to medicines in Tokyo: modeling choices that change recovery judgments
papers.summary: Community pharmacies sustain access to medicines after an earthquake only while open, staffed and stocked. Accessibility models rarely represent stock depletion, and the assumptions this requires may change conclusions about recovery. We examine these assumptions for over-the-counter (OTC) medicines supplied by 4,748 registered pharmacies in Tokyo's 23 wards during the first week after a magnitude-7.3 scenario earthquake. A two-step floating catchment area model computes walking accessibility for 2,651 grid cells (500 m) under 10,000 sampled combinations of stock duration, staffing, operation and demand. Results are expressed as Retention: post-disaster accessibility divided by the same cell's pre-disaster accessibility. First, the assumed link between stock and service, the supply a pharmacy can still provide, determines the recovery verdict. If service falls in proportion to remaining stock, mean Retention declines from 0.479 (days 2-3) to 0.273 (days 4-7). If service is maintained until stock falls below one quarter, the mean rises instead, although low-end (10th-percentile) outcomes still decline. Measuring at the start of each period rather than averaging over it also reverses the trend. Second, a simple model that rescales a fixed map by citywide supply and demand reproduces citywide patterns but cannot evaluate where pharmacies close or where capacity is added; a spatial model run once on average inputs can. Third, four floating catchment methods agree on overall rankings (rank correlation 0.81), but their lowest-ranked 10% of cells overlap only partially (Jaccard index 0.56). Disaster assessments should report stock assumptions and low-end outcomes, and treat local priority areas as method-dependent.

authors.name: Juanning Liang, Hiroki Baba

papers.title: Analysis of the Cosmos 2612 - ICEYE-X36 rendezvous and proximity operation from public orbital element data
papers.summary: We analyse the October 2026 close approach between Cosmos 2612 (NORAD 68762) and the commercial radar satellite ICEYE-X36 (NORAD 59103), both in sun-synchronous low Earth orbit, to determine whether it was a rendezvous and proximity operation (RPO) or the result of natural orbital evolution. The public general perturbations (GP) element history from April to October 2026 was propagated with SGP4, and the prediction error was measured empirically for each object. The null hypothesis of natural evolution, tested with manoeuvre-free propagations, is rejected for all 18 parameter combinations: the encounter required manoeuvres by Cosmos 2612, whereas those of ICEYE-X36 are not needed to reproduce it. Closest approach occurred on 18 October at 06:33 UTC, below 0.79 km (95th percentile), with a local relative velocity of about 0.08 m/s and 41.4 h continuously within 5 km. It was the final stage of a sequence that began in May with a plane match, followed by a phasing drift, the approach and a manoeuvred retreat, with a minimum cumulative $\Delta v$ of 174-180 m/s. The data cannot resolve the minimum distance below their accuracy, nor establish whether the operation was cooperative or its purpose.

authors.name: Brayan Nicolas Buitrago Montenegro

papers.title: Exact superdiffusion exponents and hull exploration of chiral random walkers on critical percolation clusters
papers.summary: Generalizing de Gennes' ant-in-the-labyrinth concept, we consider a chiral random walker on a percolation cluster at criticality. The fully chiral ant clings to obstacle boundaries and traces the fractal hulls of the cluster, spreading with the exact walk dimension $7/4$ until its orbit closes. Because the cluster contains holes on all scales, the ensemble spreads superdiffusively, $\langle r^2\rangle\sim t^{89/84}$, carried by a diminishing fraction of walkers whose orbits are still open. Both exponents follow from percolation geometry alone, and agree well with large-scale numerical simulations. When the walker turns chirally only with probability $\chi<1$, superdiffusion gives way to the subdiffusion of the ant at a crossover time set by both exponents, with a diffusion coefficient enhanced by $(1-\chi)^{-2/d_w}$. The relation between crossover time and diffusion coefficient does not depend on how chirality is realized, offering a direct test for chiral tracers in disordered media.

authors.name: Joshua Uhlig, Ralf Metzler, Erik Kalz

papers.title: AmorphGen: A Python package for amorphous structure generation with machine-learning and classical interatomic potentials
papers.summary: AmorphGen is an open-source Python package for generating and analyzing amorphous structures from a composition or a crystal. Chemically informed rules estimate initial densities and assign separation and coordination constraints. Three routes are available: random placement followed by relaxation, melt-quench from a crystal, and a hybrid route that anneals and quenches random structures. ASE provides access to classical and machine-learning potentials, with GPU batching for selected backends. Analysis tools compute coordination numbers, bond angles, rings, and X-ray or neutron structure factors for comparison with measurements. An optional interface to the FEFF code computes extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra. For amorphous Ga2O3, TiO2 and InGaZnO4, the cation coordination numbers are close to reference models and measurements, and the X-ray structure factors reproduce the main measured peaks. The EXAFS spectra for Ga2O3 and InGaZnO4 also capture the dominant first-shell features observed experimentally. The hybrid route reduces bonding defects in SiO2 and As and builds the first sharp diffraction peak of SiO2. By simplifying ensemble generation and standardizing structural assessment, AmorphGen makes it practical to compare amorphous models across compositions, potentials, and preparation routes, and to screen new amorphous compositions.

authors.name: Chaiyawat Kaewmeechai, Louie Slocombe, Alexis G. Manche, David O. Scanlon

papers.title: Ballistic propagation-mediated super-resolution light-element imaging: in-situ tracking dynamic hydrogen migration
papers.summary: Transmission electrons - with few-picometer wavelengths - can theoretically resolve all atoms in solids. However, constrained by factors such as lens aberrations, Z-contrast dependence and poor temporal resolution, the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) fails to tackle the long-standing challenge of hydrogen dynamics on atomic scale. Here, our experiment-guided simulations reveal that unlike heavy-atom imaging - governed by wave-based imaging process - ballistic propagation of particle-like electrons in Cs-corrected TEM enables super-resolution imaging (SRI) of light atoms, achieving a resolution down to 14 pm and a robust hydrogen contrast of ~24%. Our in-situ SRI study not only uncovers polymetric hydrogen aggregation in TiHx and H-LaAlO3, but also inter-site migration, rotational displacement of hydrogen species and collective hydrogen tunneling-induced polarization surge in the oxide. By exploiting the novel electron-matter interactions, our findings offer an unparalleled approach to probe hydrogen dynamics and establish accurate structure-property relationships in diverse functional materials.

authors.name: Zhiyao Liang, Feng Liu, Linyuan Chen, Zhiwei Lv, Shiya Chen, Xinyu Liao, Yuzhou He, Yi Wang, Pengpeng Liu, Hua Bing Tao, Nianpeng Lu, Changlin Zheng, Yang Sun, Qinghua Zhang, Rafal E. Dunin-Borkowski, Xian-Kui Wei

papers.title: MagPot: A magnetoelastic potential generator for molecular dynamics simulations
papers.summary: Magnetoelastic phenomena originate from the coupling between atomic displacements and magnetic degrees of freedom, and their atomistic simulation requires interatomic models in which magnetic interactions depend explicitly on interatomic distance. This paper presents MagPot, a Python program that generates Bethe-Slater parameter sets for spin-lattice molecular dynamics simulations using the SPIN package of the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). From a compact set of material properties, the program determines the radial functions describing Heisenberg exchange and the dipole and quadrupole contributions of the two-ion N\'eel interaction. Version 1.0 supports simple-cubic, body-centred-cubic and face-centred-cubic lattices with ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations. A central feature of MagPot is its modular architecture, which allows the magnetic contribution it generates to be combined additively with a broad range of compatible non-magnetic interatomic potentials. The parameterisation workflow is assessed through equation-of-state, Curie-temperature, volume-magnetostriction, pressure-dependent magnetocrystalline-anisotropy and anisotropic-magnetoelastic tests. By automating the construction of the magnetic contribution to the interatomic model, MagPot offers a straightforward and reproducible route from material properties to LAMMPS-ready magnetic interactions, facilitating large-scale atomistic simulations of magnetoelasticity and magnetostriction, as well as physical phenomena associated with magnon-phonon coupling.

authors.name: P. Nieves, I. Korniienko, S. Arapan, A. Fraile, R. Iglesias, D. Legut

papers.title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
papers.summary: We derive an improved upper bound on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability $\gamma$, given by $\log_2[1+(1-\gamma)\gamma^{\gamma/(1-\gamma)}]$. It applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement, and, for every $0<\gamma<1$, strictly improves the PLOB relative-entropy bound, the analytic max-relative-entropy bound, and the optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bound. At high damping, a known triple-rail protocol attains more than $99.54\%$ of its leading coefficient. Our method extends sector teleportation simulation to qubits: phase rotations and permutations give exact simulations within fixed-excitation subspaces while preserving the two-level input structure. We determine the exact, additive relative entropy of entanglement of the amplitude-damping resources and the exact regularized entanglement gain at fixed input population. We then derive explicit bounds for generalized amplitude damping, which includes thermal excitation. Combining the amplitude-damping gain with unital and entanglement-breaking channels gives a closed expression that recovers the zero-temperature result and vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region. It improves established benchmarks over broad parameter ranges, while the exact entanglement of the generalized resources remains open. Both results admit refinements under an average-excitation constraint. The bounds provide quantitative limits for adaptive communication through relaxing qubits and show how a sector simulation can remain useful beyond channels whose resource entanglement is known exactly.

authors.name: Stefano Pirandola

papers.title: Pyroelectric Harvesting from Steady Heat Sources via Active Piezoelectric Thermal Switching
papers.summary: This study demonstrates pyroelectric energy harvesting from a steady heat source using active piezoelectric thermal switching in a PZT/Si bimorph cantilever. The same PZT layer serves as both the mechanical actuator and the pyroelectric energy-conversion element. Dual output electrodes enable separation of the pyroelectric and piezoelectric signals. Pyroelectric energy harvesting is experimentally demonstrated at frequencies up to 110 Hz and temperature differences as small as 5 K. Comparison with the response predicted from the independently measured pyroelectric coefficient, together with transient thermal simulations, identifies dynamic interfacial heat transfer as a key limitation to high-frequency operation. This work demonstrates a compact MEMS approach for higher-frequency pyroelectric energy harvesting from low-grade steady heat sources.

authors.name: Jun Usami, Yuki Okamoto, Shimpei Saito, Saeko Tachikawa, Soumei Baba, Takeshi Fujii, Sucheta Gorwadkar, Natsumi Makimoto, Takeshi Kobayashi

papers.title: Integrable discretization of the Maxwell-Bloch equations
papers.summary: Numerical schemes for the Maxwell-Bloch equations keep the length of the Bloch vector but not the integrable structure, so that solitons are only approximate solutions. We write an integrable discretization, in both time and space, of these equations for a complex field in a resonant two-level medium in the physical variables and use it as a numerical scheme. The lattice follows from a discrete Lax pair with the analytic structure of the continuous one; an auxiliary field variable is fixed by an isospectral normalization, and the resulting scheme is explicit, a $2\times2$ similarity transformation of the density matrix per grid node. It conserves the length of every Bloch vector and satisfies an exact energy balance between field and medium. The lattice coincides with a known fully discrete integrable system, which we use to obtain closed-form solitons and breathers; they are reflectionless potentials with energy $16\sum_j\mathrm{Im}\,\lambda_j$ and converge to the McCall-Hahn soliton and Lamb's breather. Inhomogeneous broadening is included through ordered sublayers that keep integrability. On a finite time window the scattering data evolve by a closed map, with the final state of the medium given by the data at one point of the spectral plane. On the infinite line, if the medium returns to its ground state behind the pulse (which we show on the first row and observe numerically on later rows), the transmission coefficient is conserved and the reflection coefficient evolves linearly, with the multiplier of the linearized lattice. As a numerical method the lattice is explicit and second order, with a cost per accuracy comparable to that of Cayley and exponential-midpoint schemes, and an area-preserving input map with a calibrated medium coupling makes it exact for a chosen soliton.

authors.name: I. Kuk, I. Gabitov

papers.title: Plasma-enabled magnet-free LSW search for eV-scale axions with laser-stimulated regeneration
papers.summary: In conventional light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) experiments, strong magnetic fields mediate the conversion of photons into axions and their subsequent reconversion into photons. At eV-scale axion masses, however, photon--axion phase mismatch causes these conversions to lose coherence, substantially reducing the experimental sensitivity. We propose a magnet-free LSW scheme that addresses this limitation via plasma-based axion generation and laser-stimulated regeneration. At low laser intensity, a two-color dispersion-matched source generates axions in a narrow mass range set by the plasma dispersion. At relativistic laser intensity, a single-pulse plasma-broadened source generates axions over a broad mass range, as shown by particle-in-cell simulations. The Fourier spectrum of the source term $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ broadens around the laser branch, consistent with mixing between the laser and low-frequency plasma waves. For axion detection behind the wall, a counter-propagating laser stimulates axion decay into a detectable signal photon and a second photon emitted into the laser mode, with the laser frequency chosen to satisfy phase matching. For representative parameters, the requirement of at least one regenerated photon yields projected upper limits on the axion-photon coupling on the order $10^{-7}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ over $m_a=0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{eV}$.

authors.name: Xiangyan An, Min Chen, Yipeng Wu, Boyuan Li, Wenchao Yan, Peng Yuan, Binbin Yan, Feng Liu, Zhengming Sheng, Jie Zhang

papers.title: A Unified Energy-Density Framework for Moir\'e Interface Energetics and Mechanics
papers.summary: The mechanical response of moir\'e interfaces depends on how atomic registry combines with contact size and boundary geometry. An analytical description must retain this discrete lattice information while connecting microscopic interactions to the energetics of finite contacts. Here, we develop a unified energy-density framework for rigid van der Waals interfaces by expressing registry-dependent pair potentials and atomic densities in reciprocal space. The resulting formulation accommodates different lattice bases and atomic species, linking single-atom and molecular adsorption to infinite bilayers and finite crystalline contacts. Explicit expressions for circular and regular polygonal flakes separate the area contribution from boundary-dependent terms and connect microscopic corrugation coefficients to energy barriers, rotational torques, and interlayer shear stiffnesses. The boundary analysis recovers the quarter-power area scaling of the barrier envelope for circular flakes and distinguishes bounded oscillations from square-root area scaling for polygonal contacts according to edge orientation. A dimensionless criterion characterizes the polygon-to-circle crossover in terms of moir\'e wavelength, flake size, and side number. Direct-summation benchmarks support the finite-domain expressions, while calculations for two-dimensional ice on graphene demonstrate the corresponding boundary-scaling trends in a molecular lattice. Applications to interlayer shear and graphite compression connect the same microscopic interaction description to tangential and normal mechanical responses. The framework establishes an analytical connection between microscopic registry, moir\'e periodicity, and finite-domain geometry, providing a basis for understanding and tailoring the energetics and mechanics of van der Waals contacts.

authors.name: Zhangke Lei, Weidong Yan, Zhicheng Feng, Wengen Ouyang

papers.title: Growing Knot Embeddings into Spherical Graphs
papers.summary: Knotted structures occur throughout soft matter and biology, where topological constraints can shape relaxation and spatial organization. Here, we introduce a computational construction that maps a specific 3D knot embedding to a graph embedded on the sphere through growth and interfacial-energy relaxation. For standard 3D embeddings of prime knots with at most seven crossings, we obtain a family of growth-based graphs that generally differ from the corresponding Tait graphs. We further identify an empirical growth-graph reconstruction rule based on polygonal regions with alternating crossing structure in a knot diagram. Non-minimal diagrams demonstrate that these graphs are not knot invariants, while selected connected sums suggest that graph features associated with their prime factors can remain recognizable. Determining how these graphs transform under isotopy may reveal invariant features, which we leave for future study.

authors.name: Eren G\"ulmez, Joost de Graaf

papers.title: Stellar Temporal Intensity Interferometry with Adaptive Optics at the Palomar Observatory
papers.summary: Spatial intensity interferometry has seen a major resurgence in astronomy due to its immunity to atmospheric phase turbulence, but its temporal counterpart - a cornerstone of quantum optics - has remained largely unexplored for astronomical sources. Here, we demonstrate that high-visibility temporal photon bunching signatures from stellar sources are now accessible by combining ultra-narrowband spectral filtering with high-speed single-photon counting detectors. Leveraging the adaptive optics architecture at the Palomar Observatory, we report the first observation of resolved stellar temporal photon bunching, with a peak of $g^{(2)}(\tau=0) = 1.3 \pm 0.1$, from the red supergiant $\alpha$ Her. This advance establishes stellar temporal intensity interferometry as a viable observational modality, bridging quantum optics with high-resolution stellar astrophysics.

authors.name: Darren Ming Zhi Koh, Xi Jie Yeo, Sam Halverson, Rebecca Oppenheimer, Gautam Vasisht, Christian Kurtsiefer, Peng Kian Tan

papers.title: Apparent thermal conductivity governed by interface-injected phonon spectra
papers.summary: Thermoreflectance techniques such as time- and frequency-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR and FDTR) are widely used to measure the thermal conductivity of bulk materials, thin films, and interfaces. When phonon mean free paths $\Lambda_\omega$ become comparable to the thermal penetration depth, a Fourier analysis yields an apparent thermal conductivity $\kappa_{\rm app}$ that deviates from the bulk value $\kappa_{\rm bulk}$. Recent studies have highlighted the role of the phonon spectrum injected through the transducer interface, which is generally out of equilibrium owing to frequency-dependent transmission, and have shown that accounting for this nonequilibrium distribution can yield $\kappa_{\rm app}>\kappa_{\rm bulk}$, unlike conventional suppression-function analyses that predict only $\kappa_{\rm app}\leq\kappa_{\rm bulk}$. However, the spectral characteristics governing whether $\kappa_{\rm app}$ is enhanced or reduced remain unclear. Here, we resolve the surface-temperature response of semi-infinite Si mode by mode and show that short-$\Lambda_\omega$-weighted injection raises the surface temperature, whereas long-$\Lambda_\omega$-weighted injection lowers it. This behavior is governed by how deep the injected phonons travel before thermalizing with the lattice, which is set by their mean free paths, and by how effectively the substrate conducts the injected energy away, which is limited by its long-mean-free-path phonons. For an Al (70 nm)/Si structure, Fourier fits of synthetic TDTR phase signals give $\kappa_{\rm app}$ of Si from about 93 to 360 W/(m K) for different interfacial transmission spectra, and $\kappa_{\rm app}$ correlates with the heat-flux-weighted $\Lambda_\omega$ of the transmitted phonons. Thus, $\kappa_{\rm app}$ from thermoreflectance reflects not only the substrate thermal properties but also the phonon spectrum injected across the transducer interface.

authors.name: D. G. Jeong, Terumasa Tadano, J. S. Lee

papers.title: Atomistic insight into defect-mediated boron redistribution and high-temperature strengthening in TiAl alloys
papers.summary: Boron (B) microalloying can effectively refine microstructures of as-cast TiAl alloys and regulate their mechanical properties. Yet, how dilute B exists in TiAl and interacts with defects and how these interactions govern high-temperature deformation remain elusive. Here, we systematically elucidate defect-mediated B redistribution in TiAl alloys and its consequences for their deformation using hybrid grand-canonical Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics simulations augmented with a newly developed high-fidelity machine-learning potential. As a typical product of B microalloying, borides are markedly stiffer than the TiAl matrix and act as brittle reinforcing phases, while borides/matrix interfacial adhesion depends on surface termination and stacking sequence. In the bulk, interstitial B tends to be trapped at Ti-rich octahedral sites by high migration barriers but can kinetically evolve into substitutional dopants upon approaching Al vacancies. Increased tensile stress and vacancy concentration further promote B enrichment in the bulk. B is enriched at semi-coherent $\gamma/\alpha_2$ boundaries and preferentially partitions into the $\alpha_2$ phase. In polycrystalline TiAl, B accumulates primarily in disordered regions, raising the average flow stress by 9.4% at 1 at.% B and 900 K. This strengthening is accompanied by reduced shear strain accumulation. Simulated microstructural evolution and stacking-fault energetics indicate that B impedes dislocation glide via local pinning and suppresses deformation twinning, thereby increasing resistance to plastic deformation. By linking solute redistribution to defect interactions and deformation, these findings establish an atomistic framework for understanding and designing high-performance alloys based on interstitial solutes.

authors.name: Xiang Meng, Shuhei Shinzato, Zhiqiang Zhao, Linfeng Yu, Jian Guo, Liangli Chu, Kepeng Ouyang, Shigenobu Ogata, Zhuhua Zhang

papers.title: High-Throughput Screening of Phononic Bandgap in Experimentally Realized Materials
papers.summary: Materials with a phonon band gap offer a unique mechanism to restrict phonon scattering, making them promising candidates for developing functional materials for targeted thermal applications. Unlocking this mechanism across broad material classes requires systematic exploration, but first-principles methods and experiments are too expensive. Here, we used the universal machine-learning interatomic potential to quantify phonons and thermodynamic properties. We validated the accuracy of machine-learning-calculated results by comparing them with density-functional theory. We screened 154,879 materials and performed phonon calculations for 42,347 thermodynamically stable and experimentally observed compounds. We then performed phonon band gap analysis for dynamically stable materials and identified 11,176 materials with a phononic gap, including 10,960 materials with optical-optical gaps and 270 with acoustic-optical gaps. We also analyzed the lattice thermal conductivity of materials with phonon band gaps to identify candidates with acoustic-optical gaps and low thermal conductivity. Finally, by solving the linearized phonon Boltzmann equation from first principles, we demonstrate low room-temperature lattice thermal conductivities in three Li-metal binaries.

authors.name: Mohammad Bagheri, Kameyab Raza Abidi, Pekka Koskinen

papers.title: Bypassing the Nanoampere Limit: A Thick-Target Methodology for Ultra-Low-Energy Resonances in the $^{11}$B(p,$\alpha$)2$\alpha$ Reaction
papers.summary: Precise measurements of the low-energy cross section for the $^{11}$B(p,$\alpha$)2$\alpha$ reaction is critical for nuclear astrophysics and fusion energy research, yet such measurements are experimentally demanding due to the reaction's extremely small cross section. Conventional thin-target experiments are fundamentally limited to nanoampere beam currents, which restrict count rates to impractical levels at ultra-low proton energies. To overcome this limitation, we report a correction-free thick-target methodology capable of operating at beam currents of 20-60 microamperes, corresponding to a gain of over three orders of magnitude. Monte Carlo simulations of the full reaction kinematics are employed to determine the absolute reaction yield, eliminating the requirement for empirical normalization factors. At the well-known 148~keV (c.m.) resonance peak, our extracted resonance energy ($E_{\mathrm{r}} = 148.0$~keV) and level width ($\Gamma_{\mathrm{cm}} = 5.3$~keV) are demonstrated in good agreement with published data. A scheme via comparing the measured reaction probability with a theoretical extrapolation result is furtherly presented to probe low-energy resonances below 100~keV region. Preliminary measurements at proton energies of 75~keV and 100~keV reveal no evidence for additional low-energy resonances. This work provides a robust new methodology to measure cross section and resonance parameters for the p$^{11}$B reaction and offers a highly efficient tool for systematic resonance searches in the ultra-low-energy regime.

authors.name: Xu-Yang Luo, Wen-Qing Wei, Shi-zheng Zhang, Wen Jiang, Bu-bo Ma, Zi-qian Zhao, Zhao Wang, Guo-Dong Wang, Lu-Lin Shi, Rui Cheng, Yan-Shi Zhang, Di Luo, Xiao Xiao, Guan-Chao Zhao, Bing Liu, Dieter H. H. Hoffmann, Jie-Ru Ren, Yong-Tao Zhao

papers.title: Femtosecond laser-controlled production of functional titanium niobate layers from TiO$_{2}$/Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders
papers.summary: Conventional synthesis methods of titanium niobates (TNO) require prolongated high-temperature treatments. To overcome this limitation, in this work, we have developed a confined powder-bed femtosecond (fs) laser-based technique to sinter TNO films starting from a mixture of TiO$_{2}$ and Nb$_{2}$O$_{5}$ powders, avoiding furnace-based approaches. The influence of laser-processing conditions on film formation, phase composition, and microstructure is systematically investigated, demonstrating that different TNO phases and morphologies can be obtained by controlling the laser pulse energy. A comprehensive characterization of the processed films has been performed, providing insights into the mechanisms governing their formation, which appear to share key features with laser-induced backward transfer (LIBT) processes. Our findings establish the relationship between laser-processing conditions and TNO film formation, highlighting the potential of confined powder-bed fs-laser processing as an alternative route for manufacturing functional oxide layers. Tentative applications of these layers are finally discussed.

authors.name: Gonzalo Gomez-Munoz, Aar\'on Calvo-Villoslada, Inmaculada \'Alvarez-Serrano, Mar\'ia Luisa L\'opez, Paloma Fern\'andez, Javier Solis, Bel\'en Sotillo

papers.title: Asymmetrical transport distribution function: skewness as a key to enhance thermoelectric performance
papers.summary: How to achieve high thermoelectric figure of merit is still a scientific challenge. By solving the Boltzmann transport equation, thermoelectric properties can be written as integrals of a single function, the transport distribution function (TDF). In this work, the shape effects of transport distribution function in various typical functional forms on thermoelectric properties of materials are systematically investigated. It is found that the asymmetry of TDF, characterized by skewness, can be used to describe universally the trend of thermoelectric properties. By defining symmetric and asymmetric TDF functions, a novel skewness is then constructed for thermoelectric applications. It is demonstrated, by comparison with ab initio calculations and experiments, that the proposed thermoelectric skewness not only perfectly captures the main feature of conventional skewness, but also is able to predict the thermoelectric power accurately. This comparison confirms the unique feature of our proposed thermoelectric skewness, as well as its special role of connection between the statistics of TDF and thermoelectric properties of materials. It is also found that the thermoelectric performance can be enhanced by increasing the asymmetry of TDF. Finally, it is also interesting to find that the thermoelectric transport properties based on typical quantum statistics (Fermi-Dirac distributions), can be well described by typical shape parameter (skewness) for classical statistics.

authors.name: Jin-Cheng Zheng

papers.title: A new frequency-time hybrid RPML-BIE solver with few-mode corrections for the wave-equation problems in nonuniform closed waveguides
papers.summary: This paper is devoted to proposing a novel FTH integral equation solver for wave-equation problems in two-dimensional nonuniform closed waveguides with multiple channels. The FTH methodology, which combines the Fourier transform with frequency-domain BIE formulations, has demonstrated its effectiveness in solving time-dependent wave scattering problems. However, when applied to waveguide problems, the modal expansions arising from multiple scattering introduce cut-off frequencies. Such frequencies pose significant challenges, requiring both a frequency-robust solver for frequency-domain waveguide problems and an efficient treatment of the solution's non-smooth behavior near the cut-off frequencies for the evaluation of the inverse Fourier transform. The first issue is addressed by developing a new frequency-domain BIE method based on the free-space fundamental solution and regionalized perfectly matched layer truncation, together with a few-mode Dirichlet-to-Robin modification. The method is rigorously proved to achieve uniform exponential convergence, even at frequencies arbitrarily close to the cut-off frequencies. To address the second issue---the recovery of the time-domain solution via the inverse Fourier transform---a sine-transform based stationary-point Filon--Clenshaw--Curtis quadrature is introduced to accurately handle the non-smoothness and square-root singularities of frequency-domain solutions. Additionally, theoretical result shows that the complex resonances closing to the real axis may significantly effect the convergence of the Fourier transform algorithm and then a novel strategy of complex resonance extraction based on AAA rational approximation and singularity subtraction is utilized to avoid this influence. Numerical experiments for both frequency-domain and time-domain problems illustrate the efficiency and high accuracy of the proposed method.

authors.name: Yan Tan, Liwei Xu, Tao Yin

papers.title: Geometry-conditioned differentiable surrogate with adjoint Monte Carlo sampling for scintillator detector co-design
papers.summary: Optimizing light-guide geometries for scintillator-based imaging detectors requires repeated photon-transport evaluations, making direct Monte Carlo simulation computationally costly. Differentiable surrogates can accelerate these evaluations and support detector readout co-design aimed at improving information extraction from particle interactions. In this work we describe a surrogate model for photon transport. We develop it starting from a modular, event-driven Monte Carlo model for the generation and transport of scintillation photons, and a reciprocal Monte Carlo construction (an adjoint model) of a spatially and temporally resolved optical response field. The latter evaluates the collectible light output and its temporal structure from a scintillator volume by launching weighted photon trajectories from the light-guide readout face. We apply this approach to a scintillator cell with two mirrored, curved, single-clad light guides. We employ the adjoint model to train a geometry-conditioned neural surrogate that predicts collection probabilities and conditional transport-time distributions across a constrained guide-design family. The surrogate is natively differentiable, lending itself to be an element of a differentiable pipeline for gradient-based optimization. A forward-reciprocal benchmark and validation on held-out geometries establish the accuracy of the trained model and identify its limitations. The developed tools provide a foundation for rapid optical-response studies and detector readout co-design.

authors.name: Lorenzo Pepa, Mohammad Ali Marashli, Nicolas Babio Elguero, Tommaso Dorigo, Irene Fagnani, Carlo Gulizia, Pablo Martinez Ruiz del Arbol, Fredrik Sandin, Pietro Vischia

papers.title: Computational Complexity and Energy Landscapes of Coulomb Crystals
papers.summary: Simulated annealing is widely used to search for ground states of trapped-ion Coulomb crystals and of charges on a sphere (the Thomson problem). Elementary nonuniform bounds clarify the role of the input encoding. For identical ions in a fixed trap, unary ion count and a binary energy threshold define a decision problem in P/poly; NP-hardness would imply a collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. The same holds on the unit sphere. With unary ion count and logarithmic precision parameter, approximate configuration search on the sphere and in a fixed positive-definite harmonic trap admits a solution function in FP/poly. These advice bounds provide no uniform search algorithm. In simulations of up to 100 ions, the number of distinct minima found and the time to reach the best-known minimum both grow approximately exponentially. When ions are pinned to prescribed candidate sites, choosing which sites to occupy to minimize the Coulomb energy is NP-hard in two and three dimensions; a finite-precision promise version is NP-complete. All ions are identical, the interaction is bare Coulomb repulsion, and the hardness is carried by the site positions alone. We extend a previous inverse-square reduction to the Coulomb interaction by deriving its angular law, including the quartic field term, and sharpening two estimates. The construction is an array of quadrupoles whose common monopole term cancels from energy differences between legal configurations. Its energy landscapes exhibit large barriers between nearly degenerate minima. Barrier trees resolve this structure, and simulated annealing becomes trapped above the ground state in the cube example. At laboratory parameters, with individually tunable well depths, the encoding survives numerically on a half-filled square lattice. For Doppler-cooled strontium ions, this requires stiff wells a few to tens of micrometers apart, as in electrode trap arrays.

authors.name: Paco Navarro, Michael Emmerich

papers.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
papers.summary: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.

authors.name: Jos\'e Antonio Carrillo, Timon Gutleb, Andrea Medaglia, Yijia Tang

papers.title: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
papers.summary: While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.

authors.name: Zhenyu Du, Xiongfeng Ma, Vlatko Vedral, Jinzhao Sun

papers.title: Molecular Pawns on a Surface Chessboard: Computational Investigation of Nanographenes with Atomistic Methods
papers.summary: Atomically precise nanographenes combine tunable electronic topology with localized, coherent spin states, making them candidate platforms for molecular quantum technologies. This review examines the multiscale theoretical framework governing these systems: the hierarchy of computational methods for describing magnetic properties, the substrate-molecule interface, on-surface synthetic kinetics, and supramolecular self-assembly. We highlight how density functional theory, automated reaction-path discovery, and spin-aware machine-learned interatomic potentials connect static electronic structure to mesoscale dynamics, and how magnetic exchange, optical excitations, and spin transport can be predicted before synthesis.

authors.name: Antonio Lorenzo Mariano, Jacopo Lupi, Emilio Lorini, Matteo Briganti

papers.title: Donnan Grand Canonical Monte Carlo Simulations with Fast Ewald Summation for Calculating Individual Ionic Chemical Potentials
papers.summary: We present a Donnan Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulation method using fast Ewald summation to accurately and efficiently calculate the individual ionic excess chemical potentials of $\alpha_+:\alpha_-$ electrolyte solutions. By introducing a dynamic inner electrostatic potential that acts to penalize net charge fluctuations and maintain average charge neutrality ($\langle Q_t \rangle = 0$), the method enables single-ion GCMC trial moves without sacrificing convergence speed or breaking thermodynamic consistency. Unlike the Widom particle insertion method---which suffers from severe phase-space sampling bottlenecks and requires separate virtual insertions for each ionic species---the Donnan GCMC protocol simultaneously yields the individual excess chemical potentials $\mu_+^{\text{ex}}$ and $\mu_-^{\text{ex}}$ corresponding to a resulting bulk concentration $c_b$ with rapid numerical convergence. Varying the reference activity parameter $c_r$ allows us to efficiently construct the complete $\mu_\pm^{\text{ex}}(c_b)$ curves. Comparison with the Mean Spherical Approximation (MSA) demonstrates excellent agreement for size-symmetric electrolytes, while highlighting the failure of linear-response theories for size-asymmetric ions where electrostatic correlations and cavity effects become strongly coupled.

authors.name: Alexandre P. dos Santos, Amin Bakhshandeh, Yan Levin

papers.title: Fifth-order KdV solitary waves in a nonlinear electrical transmission line
papers.summary: We report the controlled experimental observation of solitary waves governed by the fifth-order dispersion Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. To achieve vanishing cubic dispersion, we use a mutual inductive coupling between nearest-neighbor inductors within a nonlinear electrical transmission line. We then experimentally characterize the resulting solitary waves through direct spatiotemporal measurements of the dispersion relation, its oscillatory tail profiles, amplitude-width scaling, and amplitude-velocity relation, finding good agreement with semi-analytical predictions. Collision experiments between two (co- or counter-propagating) solitary waves also show that their self-similar profile persists after interaction, up to a time shift. Dissipation effects are also quantified.

authors.name: Loic Fache, Filip Novkoski, Eric Falcon

papers.title: Lincege.jl: LINked Cluster Expansions on a GEneral GEometry
papers.summary: The numerical linked-cluster expansion (NLCE) is a powerful tool for studying properties of quantum lattice models directly in the thermodynamic limit. Here, we introduce Lincege.jl, a versatile, efficient, and easy-to-use package for generating the clusters needed to perform the NLCE on a general finite or infinite lattice. Lincege.jl takes as input only the Bravais lattice vectors, the basis information, and the expansion unit and uses a depth-first search to efficiently generate clusters, their lattice constants, and the sub-cluster information. It outputs final coefficients of the series, expressed in terms of the extensive properties of the clusters, in different orders. The package also contains tools for visualizing the lattice and the generated clusters as well as a classical Ising model solver that can be used as a template for interfacing Lincege.jl with solvers of other lattice models. This package can be installed using the Julia package manager and utilized with example scripts from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/rightleftspin/Lincege.jl. The online documentation, including examples, can be found at https://rightleftspin.github.io/Lincege.jl/stable/.

authors.name: Pranav Seetharaman, Francisco Correia, Ehsan Khatami

papers.title: Self-similar Inequality Dynamics in Biased Competition for a Conserved Resource
papers.summary: In many complex systems the redistribution of a conserved resource can generate strong inequality. Important examples are cities exchanging inhabitants, farms competing for farmland, or agents for wealth in saturated markets. Here we model such systems as agents competing for a fixed total resource, and show that coupling agent extinction to a bias favoring richer agents dynamically amplifies this inequality over time. Drawing on an analogy with emulsions, where droplets compete for a conserved quantity, we introduce a dynamical critical resource size that determines an agent's fate. Crucially, this threshold grows in time, continuously raising the bar for survival and further reinforcing inequality. Increasing the bias strength, we find a transition from a continuous resource concentration towards a winner-takes-all outcome. Furthermore, the case of continuous resource concentration is characterized by a self-similar dynamics accompanied by a power-law or exponential increase in inequality, quantified by the Gini coefficient. We derive these results analytically in a mean-field model and compare them to agent-based simulations, showing excellent agreement.

authors.name: Giacomo Bartolucci, Jonathan Bauermann

papers.title: Shaderous: A Browser-based Hydrodynamics Code for Physics Research and Teaching
papers.summary: Shaderous is a three-dimensional code for compressible gas dynamics and magnetohydrodynamics that runs in WebGPU compute shaders in a web browser on any vendor's GPU. It combines an unsplit MUSCL-Hancock scheme and HLLC fluxes with a multigrid Poisson solver, block-structured adaptive mesh refinement with per-block timesteps, constrained transport with HLLD fluxes, point masses with sinks, gray radiation transport with the M1 closure, implicit pressure for low Mach numbers, tabulated equations of state from degenerate electrons to rock and iron, cooling, viscosity, conduction, resistivity, mixtures of gases, and nuclear burning by a neural network trained on a 13-isotope reaction network. A setup is shared as a link and runs on a student's own laptop or phone, so the code suits teaching at every level. A run is limited to one GPU: the largest adaptive mesh so far held about 175 million cells on an NVIDIA H200. It therefore suits parameter studies, run as sweeps from the command line, rather than the largest single simulations. Three aspects of the design are, as far as we can find, new. First, the hydrodynamic solver stores no face flux. The two cells that share a face compute bit-identical fluxes, so cells at boundaries between levels and between timesteps recompute their neighbors' fluxes instead of keeping a flux register. Mass, momentum and energy are conserved to round-off on the adaptive mesh, and compensated sums keep the divergence of the magnetic field at round-off. Second, the whole step runs on the GPU: the timestep and the assignment of blocks to time bins are reduced there, and ghost cells are computed as they are loaded rather than exchanged. Third, the code computes in single precision yet reproduces a range of astrophysical systems accurately, from stars and atmospheres in hydrostatic balance to shocks, gravitational collapse and magnetized flows, in 206 validation tests.

authors.name: James Guillochon

papers.title: Solute-Aware Stochastic Korhonen Model of Electromigration in Wide vs Near-Bamboo Al-Cu Lines
papers.summary: We couple an evolving Cu field to the one-dimensional Korhonen stress equation on random grain maps for wide (10 $\mu$m), narrow (3 $\mu$m) and near-bamboo Al-Cu lines. Earlier random-microstructure simulations fixed the Cu effect, and most continuum solute models used prescribed structures with all Cu mobile; we join the two and let only dissolved Cu move, the excess staying as immobile precipitate. With $10^3$ maps per condition at 200 $^\circ$C, we report nucleation times and sites, immortal fractions and Black's-law parameters. In cathode-limited lines Cu depletion shortens the median nucleation time 1.15- to 1.20-fold relative to immobile Cu for the cited Cu diffusivity; treating all Cu as mobile overstates this a further 2.24- to 2.36-fold at 2 wt%; the exponent stays near 2. In wide lines with reservoir ends, Cu steps left by the immobile precipitate become the failure sites, removing their Cu-free immortality if a quarter or more of the precipitate blocks Al diffusion. With Cu above the solvus the lifetime is not Arrhenius, as the dissolved fraction rises with temperature: a Black's-law fit at 250 to 300 $^\circ$C overestimates the median nucleation time at 150 $^\circ$C up to 2.33-fold at 2 wt% Cu with an exponent near 2. At the test durations the model qualitatively matches the cathode-side damage in narrow lines and the Cu build-up and mid-line peaks in wide lines but not the cathode-side Cu peaks or longer lives of narrow lines.

authors.name: Narahara Chari Dingari, David R. Heskett

papers.title: Simple design of adaptive protocols for quantum metrology with limited data
papers.summary: Recent sensing experiments have used a Bayesian notion of precision gain to adapt control parameters for fixed measurements. Here, we advocate a simple design principle based on Personick's minimum mean square loss formalism to extend this procedure in order to include measurement optimisation, determining the optimal measurement for each probe and providing a prior-dependent precision gain to optimise the probe itself. This offers a Bayesian counterpart to protocol design based on the Fisher information, with a similar algebraic structure but incorporating the full prior. We apply this principle to adaptive phase estimation with single-mode Gaussian probes, showing that joint optimisation outperforms both adaptive homodyne detection and a fixed-probe strategy optimised for the initial prior, with a maximum reduction of 32% in mean posterior variance relative to homodyne detection. Our results illustrate the potential of simple Bayesian design for quantum metrology with limited data when measurement bases can be controlled.

authors.name: Ricard Ravell Rodr\'iguez, Jes\'us Rubio

papers.title: Transverse deflecting cavities
papers.summary: Transverse deflecting cavities are used for a number of applications in modern accelerators. In this paper we discuss the fields of these cavities, some of their applications, and some important aspects of their design.

authors.name: G. Burt (Lancaster University)

papers.title: Newton's second law: not so elementary (as it may seem)
papers.summary: Introductory courses present Newton's second law either as a definition of force or as a law of nature, and in both cases leave unexplained why it holds only in a special class of reference frames. We give an operational reading of the law built on a single instrument, the spring balance. Its reading is a local fact on which all observers agree; in a given laboratory it defines the masses of bodies and a vector {\gamma} characterising the laboratory. Laboratories with $\gamma$ = 0 are, by definition, inertial. The empirical content of the second law is then the statement {\gamma} = -KA, where A is the acceleration of the laboratory measured kinematically from any inertial laboratory, and K is a universal constant that the choice of the newton as unit of force makes invisible. In this reading a spring balance is an accelerometer and an accelerometer is a dynamometer: both measure the specific force a-g familiar from inertial navigation. We discuss the hypotheses involved (universality of free fall, absence of rotation, locality) and the relation with Newton's own formulation.

authors.name: Ledo Stefanini, Giancarlo Reali

papers.title: Can Satellite Mega-Constellations Justify Their Impact on Astronomy?
papers.summary: Private space companies are increasingly commercializing near-earth space. Some estimates show that more than 100,000 satellites may orbit the Earth by 2030. This increase in the number of satellites has many consequences for science, particularly astronomy. Satellite mega-constellations for satellite Internet connectivity are one of the main drivers behind the explosion in the number of satellites. Here, we briefly note whether such satellite mega-constellations can justify their impact on astronomy.

authors.name: Sai Charan Petchetti

papers.title: Wavescan: Multiresolution Time-Frequency Transform of Gravitational-Wave Data
papers.summary: Identifying transient signals embedded in non-stationary noise requires analyzing the time-dependent spectral components of the observed time series. The time-frequency distribution of the signal power can be estimated with Gabor atoms, or wavelets, localized in time and frequency by a window function. Such analysis is constrained by the Heisenberg-Gabor uncertainty principle, which limits the simultaneous time and frequency localization achievable with individual wavelets. Moreover, the resulting time-frequency distribution is subject to temporal and spectral leakage, limiting the identification of sharp or rapidly varying features in the power spectrum. This paper introduces a time-frequency transform that uses a stack of wavelets to scan local power across multiple scales. At each time-frequency location, a wavelet least affected by the leakage is selected from the stack to obtain high-resolution localization of power. The resulting wavelet scan ("wavescan") extends conventional multiresolution analysis by enhancing time-frequency localization and mitigating local power distortions caused by temporal and spectral leakage. The paper describes the principal components of the wavescan framework, including the estimation of the time-varying spectrum, identification of transient signals in the time-frequency data, and reconstruction of the corresponding time-domain waveforms. To demonstrate the performance of the method, the wavescan transform is applied to gravitational-wave data from the LIGO detectors.

authors.name: Sergey Klimenko

papers.title: Twisted light affects ultrafast demagnetization
papers.summary: Irradiation with an ultrashort laser pulse can completely destroy the magnetic order of ferromagnetic thin films on the femtosecond timescale. This phenomenon holds great potential for ultrafast spintronics and information processing and is an active field of research. It is still an open question if the angular momentum of light can support this effect. While it has been shown that the spin of light only has a negligible influence, we experimentally demonstrate the influence of photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) on the magnetization dynamics of a thin nickel film. Our results reveal that the photonic OAM affects the demagnetization behavior by a non-coherent, secondary process within the first hundreds of femtoseconds depending on the handedness of the OAM with respect to the direction of the sample magnetization.

authors.name: Eva Prinz, Paul Herrgen, Jonas Hoefer, Benjamin Stadtm\"uller, Martin Aeschlimann

papers.title: Depth-multiplexing spectral domain OCT for full eye length imaging with a single modulation unit
papers.summary: Clinical measurement of a patient's axial eye length is emerging as a crucial approach to track progression and monitor management of myopia. However, the preferred method for such measurements is swept-source OCT, whose cost prohibits broad use, especially in lower-income communities. Spectral domain (SD) OCT is a more affordable option, but it has limited imaging depth range, so is not suitable for full eye length measurement. Depth-multiplexing (DM) techniques for SD-OCT provide a workaround by capturing images at multiple depths within the eye. However, these methods typically require multiple light modulation units or detectors for simultaneous imaging across depths, adding complexity and cost. In response, we propose a novel DM-SD-OCT approach that utilizes a single light modulation unit for depth encoding. We capture images at multiple depths within the eye simultaneously with a single line scan camera, then computationally demix the contributions from different depths. Here, we demonstrate acquisition and demixing of signals from three distinct depths within the eye and validate experimentally in human subjects. Our method thus offers a cost-effective solution for comprehensive eye length measurement in clinical myopia research.

authors.name: Xue Dong, Aster Zhang, Fabio Feroldi, Sarah Singh, Austin Roorda, Laura Waller, Guanghan Meng

papers.title: Self organisation of invasive breast cancer driven by the interplay of active and passive nematic dynamics
papers.summary: In invasive breast cancer, cell clusters of varying sizes and shapes are embedded in the fibrous extracellular matrix (ECM). Although the prevailing view attributes this structure to increasing disorder resulting from loss of function and dedifferentiation, our findings reveal that it arises through a process of active self-organization driven by cancer cell motility. Simulations and histological analyses of tumours from over 2,000 breast cancer patients reveal that motile, aligned cancer cells within clusters move as active nematic aggregates through the surrounding highly aligned ECM fibres, which form a confining, passive nematic phase. Cellular motion leads to cluster splitting and coalescence. The degree of cluster activity, combined with heterogeneity in cell motility, is reflected in specific scaling behaviours for cluster shape, size distribution, and the distance between cluster boundaries and nematic defects in ECM alignment. Increased activity estimates correlate with tumour progression and are associated with a poorer prognosis for patients.

authors.name: Pablo Gottheil, Saraswat Bhattacharyya, Philip Friedrich, Kilian Roth, Mario Merkel, Kolya Lettl, Kudor Harb, Salvador Rivera-Moreno, Assal Daneshgar, Jonas Wieland, Bahriye Aktas, Jens-Uwe Blohmer, Hans Kubitschke, Anne-Sophie Wegscheider, Christine Sers, Igor M. Sauer, Armin Jarosch, Axel Niendorf, Julia M. Yeomans, Josef A. K\"as

papers.title: Incoherent Diffraction Imaging with a Pseudo-Thermal Light Source
papers.summary: Incoherent Diffraction Imaging - IDI - is a diffraction-based imaging technique that has been recently proposed to exploit the partial coherence of incoherently scattered light to retrieve structural information from the scattering centers. Similar to the stellar intensity interferometry of Hanbury Brown and Twiss, the signal builds up on the second-order spatial correlations of the emitted light.
