The complex spatial distribution of the target is thereby encoded in the spatial intensity fluctuations of the scattered light. The first experimental realisations of this imaging technique have been realised using the fluorescence excited by an ultra-short X-ray pulse at Free Electron Laser (FEL) facilities. Here, we propose an alternative set-up based on a table-top Pseudo-Thermal Light Source. This set-up allows us to explore IDI under a wide range of physically relevant conditions as well as to benchmark numerical and analytical models currently used to determine the imaging capabilities of this technique.

authors.name: Pablo San Miguel Claveria, Sesbasti\~ao Antunes, Peer Biesterfeld, Matilde Fernandes, Matilde Garcia, Matilde Nunes, Lucas Ansia Fernandez, Gareth O. Williams, Sven Froehlich, David Theidel, Philip Mosel, Ihsan Fsaifes, Andrea Trabattoni, Marco Piccardo, Jean-Christophe Chanteloup, Milutin Kovacev, Hamed Merdji, Marta Fajardo

papers.title: Lagrangian Attention Tensor Networks for Velocity Gradient Statistical Modeling
papers.summary: Direct numerical simulation of turbulence at realistic Reynolds numbers is still beyond current computational capability, necessitating models that reduce the number of resolved spatial scales. Improving these models requires better models of the statistical dynamics of the Velocity Gradient Tensor (VGT) at the Kolmogorov scale. Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) has found considerable success in exploiting large datasets generated from direct numerical simulation (DNS) of Navier-Stokes to improve models for the evolution of the VGT. Using the intimate connection between VGT evolution and fluid deformation, we augment a Tensor Basis Neural Network (TBNN) closure with learned Lagrangian memory kernels, and name the result Lagrangian Attention Tensor Networks (LATN). Trained on single-time (tangent) data, Lagrangian memory is strongly predictive: it lowers the error of the pressure Hessian by 43% and markedly improves its eigenvector alignment, with the most useful history spanning about half a Kolmogorov time. These \textit{a-priori} gains, however, do not translate into improved \textit{a-posteriori} prediction. We therefore inject the memory features into the first layer of a frozen, pre-trained TBNN and train \textit{only the memory} on model rollouts, against a distributional objective. We integrate the model for nine Kolmogorov times from DNS initial conditions and evaluate it with single- and multi-time statistics of the DNS. The resulting LATN retains the trunk's single-time accuracy while improving the long-time statistics: the topology, magnitude and tail distributions of the VGT, and the alignment of vorticity with the strain rate.

authors.name: Criston Hyett, Yifeng Tian, Michael Woodward, Misha Stepanov, Chris Fryer, Daniel Livescu, Michael Chertkov

papers.title: Towards Higher Order Oscillatory Ising Machines
papers.summary: Ising machines as hardware solvers of combinatorial optimization problems (COPs) can efficiently explore large solution spaces due to their inherent parallelism and physics-based dynamics. Many important COP classes such as satisfiability (SAT) assume arbitrary interactions between problem variables, while most Ising machines only support pairwise (second-order) interactions. This necessitates translation of higher-order interactions to pair-wise, which typically results in extra variables not corresponding to problem variables, and a larger problem for the Ising machine to solve than the original problem. This in turn can significantly increase time-to-solution and/or degrade solution accuracy. In this paper, considering a representative CMOS-compatible class of Ising machines, we propose a practical design to enable direct hardware support for higher order interactions. By minimizing the overhead of problem translation and mapping, our design leads to up to 4x lower time-to-solution without compromising solution accuracy.

authors.name: Nafisa Sadaf Prova, H\"usrev C{\i}lasun, Abhimanyu Kumar, Ahmet Efe, Sachin S. Sapatnekar, Ulya R. Karpuzcu

papers.title: Nonequilibrium protein complexes as molecular automata
papers.summary: Biology stores information and computes at the molecular scale, yet the ways in which it does so are often distinct from human-engineered computers. Mapping biological computation onto architectures familiar to computer science remains an outstanding challenge. Here, inspired by Crick's proposal for molecular memory, we analyse a thermodynamically-consistent model of a protein complex subject to driven, nonequilibrium enzymatic reactions. In the strongly driven limit, we find that the system maps onto a stochastic, asynchronous variant of cellular automata, where each rule corresponds to a different set of enzymes being present. We find a broad class of phenomena in these 'molecular automata' that can be exploited for molecular computation, including error-tolerant memory via multistable attractors, and long transients that can be used as molecular stopwatches. By systematically enumerating all possible dynamical rules, we identify those that allow molecular automata to implement simple computational architectures such as finite-state machines. Overall, our results provide a framework for engineering synthetic molecular automata, and offer a route to building protein-based computation in living cells.

authors.name: Jan Kocka, Kabir Husain, Jaime Agudo-Canalejo

papers.title: A multi-physics Eulerian framework for long-term contrail evolution (MultiCon): Single plume analysis
papers.summary: We present MultiCon, a reduced order, multi-physics Eulerian framework for simulating long term evolution of individual aircraft contrail plumes while retaining essential microphysical processes at low computational cost. The model resolves vertical plume evolution through a coupled PDE system, while horizontal spread is tracked using the method of characteristics and a quasi Gaussian kernel. The current implementation adopts a locally monodisperse approximation. The framework couples the transport of ice particle number and mass, as well as water-vapor transport, with an equation for particle-shape evolution. It also accounts for a- ice-crystal habit evolution and b- turbulence-modulated bulk settling. Habit-dependent growth and sublimation are represented through an approximate inherent growth factor parameterization and a diffusion-limited formulation including latent heat effects. Furthermore, the model incorporates a reduced-order closure for the effective bulk settling velocity, using a Burgers-type model to describe the transition from turbulence-reduced settling towards the terminal velocity of individual particles. We compare MultiCon with CoCiP and APCEMM for a common reference case and a parametric sweep. Across the parameter sweep, MultiCon and APCEMM exhibit similar distributions for most plume diagnostics. In terms of computational cost, CoCiP and MultiCon both operate in the range of tenths of a second to a few seconds per plume simulation. By comparison, for comparable temporal and vertical resolutions, APCEMM requires runtimes on the order of minutes, potentially approaching an hour or more depending on the particle-size bin resolution. Finally, owing to MultiCon's spatially resolved quasi 2D cross-sectional dynamics, selected microphysical processes, and computational efficiency, the solver provides a basis for future global-scale contrail assessments.

authors.name: Amin Jafarimoghaddam, Manuel Soler

papers.title: An Innovative Photon-Driven Subcritical Reactor Concept Powered by Synchrotron Radiation Source
papers.summary: Most reactors are fuelled with enriched uranium, whose production is proliferation-sensitive and concentrated in a few suppliers, and discharge fuel that still contains fissile material and accumulates in storage. Accelerator-driven subcritical reactors relax the requirements on the fuel, but proton beams must travel in vacuum to a spallation target inside the core. Here we show that synchrotron radiation can drive a subcritical heavy-water reactor fuelled with natural uranium or with spent fuel loaded without reprocessing. A photon beam with a critical energy of 10 MeV, from a proposed 32 GeV electron storage ring, releases neutrons in a uranium converter at the centre of the core. Coupled photon-neutron Monte Carlo simulations show that the two cores, loading different fuels but being at a multiplication factor close to 0.985, reach the same gain: one 400 kW beamline drives each of them close to 4.4 MW of fission power, about 11 times the beam power. A storage ring with 50 beamlines could drive one core from each beamline, every core controlled through its own photon beam. These results make synchrotron radiation a candidate driver for thermal subcritical reactors that need neither enrichment nor reprocessing, complementary to proton-driven fast systems for transmutation.

authors.name: Antonio Cammi, Lorenzo Loi, Andrea Missaglia, David Alesini, Hans-Heinrich Braun

papers.title: Decarbonization without deindustrialization in future pathways for European industry
papers.summary: Decarbonizing European industry while maintaining international competitiveness are two central objectives of European Union (EU) policy, yet they may conflict. This study investigates trade-offs between these goals across alternative industrial production pathways, from continued decline to policy-driven reindustrialization, focusing on steel, cement, methanol, ammonia, and high-value chemicals. Using an extended PyPSA-Eur energy system model with detailed process-level representation, we compare domestic low-carbon production costs against imported alternatives and evaluate three policy strategies: intra-European relocation, selective green intermediate imports, and targeted subsidies. Deep industrial decarbonization is technically feasible, with electrification playing a central role, but cost competitiveness peaks during the investment-intensive transition phase around 2040. Intra-European relocation delivers limited savings and faces significant real-world constraints. Strategic imports of green intermediates substantially reduce system costs while preserving downstream industrial activity. Overall, European industrial policy should prioritize decarbonizing existing capacity, leveraging green intermediate imports to retain high-value domestic production, supported by targeted, time-limited public support.

authors.name: Alice Di Bella, Toni Seibold, Tom Brown, Massimo Tavoni

papers.title: Mathematical basis, phase transitions and singularities of (3+1)-dimensional phi4 scalar field model
papers.summary: The lambda phi4 scalar field model can be applied to interpret pion-pion scattering and properties of hadrons. In this work, the mathematical basis, phase transitions and singularities of a (3+1)-dimensional (i.e., (3+1)D) phi4 scalar field model are investigated. It is found that as a specific example of topological quantum field theories, the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model must be set up on the Jordan-von Neumann-Wigner framework and dealt with the parameter space of complex time (or complex temperature). The use of the time average and the topologic Lorentz transformation representing Reidemeister moves ensure the integrability, which takes into account for the contributions of nontrivial topological structures to physical properties of the many-body interacting system. The ergodic hypothesis is violated at finite temperatures in the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model. Because the quantum field theories with ultraviolet cutoff can be mapped to the models in statistical mechanics, the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model with ultraviolet cutoff is studied by inspecting its relation with the three-dimensional (3D) Ising model. Furthermore, the direct relation between the coupling K in the 3D Ising model and the bare coupling lambda0 in the (3+1)D phi4 scalar field model is determined in the strong coupling limit. The results obtained in the present work can be utilized to investigate thermodynamic physical properties and critical phenomena of quantum (scalar) field theories.

authors.name: Zhidong Zhang

papers.title: Equivalent bounded confidence processes
papers.summary: In the bounded confidence model the opinions of a set of agents evolve over discrete time steps. In each round an agent averages the opinion of all agents whose opinions are at most a certain threshold apart. Here we assume that the opinions of the agents are elements of the real line. The details of the dynamics are determined by the initial opinions of the agents, i.e. a starting configuration, and the mentioned threshold -- both admitting uncountably many possibilities. Recently it was conjectured that for each starting configuration the set of thresholds can be partitioned into a finite number of intervals such that the evolution of opinions does not depend on the precise value of the threshold within one of the intervals. So, we may say that, given a starting configuration of initial opinions, there is only a finite number of equivalence classes of bounded confidence processes (and an algorithm to compute them). Here we systematically study different notions of equivalence. Under our broadest notion of equivalence we can also get rid of the initial starting configuration and end up with a finite number of equivalent bounded confidence processes for each given (finite) number of agents. This allows to precisely study the occurring phenomena for small numbers of agents without the jeopardy of missing interesting cases by performing numerical experiments. We exemplarily study the freezing time, i.e. number of time steps needed until the process stabilizes, and the degree of fragmentation, i.e. the number of different opinions that survive once the process has reached its final state.

authors.name: Sascha Kurz

papers.title: A Polarization Hall Effect in Hydrated DNA
papers.summary: We report magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent transverse-voltage phenomena in hydrated genomic DNA. The sample is confined beneath a glass coverslip in a quasi-two-dimensional geometry and subjected to perpendicular magnetic fields, revealing sharp thresholds, staircase-like voltage plateaus, and oscillatory structures approximately periodic in inverse magnetic field. Fixed-field cooling reveals longitudinal reorganizations near 20.6 and 12.0 $^\circ$C, while a separate experiment shows large-amplitude transverse oscillations below approximately 12 $^\circ$C. Water controls and buffer-free DNA measurements support an association between the structured response and the hydrated DNA system. We propose a polarization-based interpretation of the transverse response, termed a ``polarization Hall effect,'' and discuss the observed regimes within a phenomenological framework of nonlinear dynamics and metastable configurations. These findings identify hydrated DNA as a soft-matter system exhibiting structured electrical responses jointly regulated by magnetic field and temperature.

authors.name: Mariusz Pietruszka

papers.title: Maximal spreading of impacting viscoelastic droplets
papers.summary: Droplet impact and spreading on solid substrates are well understood for Newtonian fluids, yet how viscoelasticity alone modifies the maximal spreading remains unclear. Here, we isolate the role of viscoelasticity by performing impact experiments with Boger fluids of comparable viscosity and surface tension but different relaxation times. For a wide range of conditions, viscoelastic droplets follow a similar behavior to Newtonian ones{, showcasing the same leading-order inertia--capillary scalings}; however, their maximal spreading diameter is significantly reduced compared with the Newtonian behavior when the Deborah number is of order unity. This reduction is non-monotonic in the relaxation time: droplets with larger relaxation times recover Newtonian-like maximal spreading within experimental uncertainty. We rationalize these observations using an energy-balance model that includes a viscoelastic energy-storage term. The scaling argument obtained from this model explains the reported reduction in maximal spreading and identifies the range of fluid properties for which the strongest viscoelastic effects emerge.

authors.name: Orr Avni, Dongyue Wang, Mithun Ravisankar, Roberto Zenit

papers.title: Physics-Based Learning of the Wave Speed Landscape in Complex Media
papers.summary: The propagation of waves through complex, inhomogeneous media is a fundamental challenge across scales, from optics to geophysics. In such environments, the waves reflected by the medium are typically dominated by a random speckle pattern, a complex interference resulting from multiple scattering by fine-scale heterogeneities. While this speckle is traditionally viewed as a source of noise that blurs the medium's structure, it contains rich information about the underlying wave speed landscape. Here, we introduce a physics-based learning framework that reconstructs the velocity distribution from the reflection matrix of the medium. We show how the speckle wave-field can be exploited to probe the focusing quality, serving as an intrinsic guide star to evaluate the local consistency of the velocity model. By representing wave propagation as a differentiable multi-layer network, we leverage optimization tools to solve the inverse problem and infer the wave speed map. We validate this approach through ultrasound experiments in highly scattering tissue-mimicking phantoms and human breast tissues, demonstrating its potential for tumor detection and characterization where standard methods fail. This synergy between wave physics and gradient-based optimization provides a general paradigm for non-invasive tomography in any complex environment where reflection data is available.

authors.name: Baptiste H\'eriard-Dubreuil, Emma Brenner, Benjamin Rio, William Lambert, Foucauld Chamming's, Mathias Fink, Alexandre Aubry

papers.title: Preconditioned Adjoint Data Assimilation for Two-Dimensional Decaying and Forced Turbulence
papers.summary: Adjoint-based data assimilation for turbulent Navier-Stokes flows is limited by backward adjoint growth and increasing dominance of small-scale structures, which degrade reconstruction of initial conditions from sparse measurements. We show that the relative weighting of spectral components can be systematically controlled by redefining the inner product under which the adjoint operator is defined. The resulting Fourier-space weighting kernel acts as a preconditioner for the optimization. Specific kernels correspond to fractional integration or diffusion operators on the initial condition. Numerical experiments show that flow-dependent kernel selection substantially improves reconstruction stability and accuracy: exponential kernels suppress high-wavenumber contributions, whereas a fractional integral kernel is particularly effective for forced Kolmogorov flow. Ensemble statistics of adjoint fields reveal scale-dependent backward growth rates, explaining the instability of the standard formulation and how spectral preconditioning attenuates incoherent small-scale amplification.

authors.name: Hongyi Ke, Zejian You, Qi Wang

papers.title: Fluctuation imaging of disorder in monolayer semiconductors
papers.summary: Monolayer semiconductors hold great potential for nanoscale electronics, optoelectronics, and photonics. Excitons dominate their optical properties. As their electric fields extend outside the monolayer, they are sensitive to their surroundings. Thus, disorder can cause exciton instability, which is detrimental to device performance and critical for scalability and reproducibility. Here, we adapt a super-resolution fluorescence fluctuation microscopy technique to image localized exciton fluctuations in monolayer semiconductors, allowing us to identify unstable spots in an otherwise continuous monolayer with constant fluorescence. These spots correspond to interfacial disorder measured by atomic force microscopy. We examine how different material interfaces influence the fluctuations by comparing several substrates and provide additional insight into the disorder behind the fluctuations using hyperspectral imaging. We also assess the reduction of disorder upon thermal annealing, evidenced by a decrease in fluctuations. Our results show that fluorescence fluctuation imaging can detect disorder features similar to those of atomic force microscopy and hyperspectral imaging, while being faster and easier to implement. Therefore, it is a promising method for evaluating the quality of monolayer semiconductors, particularly when integrated with nanostructures and heterostructures found in nano-optoelectronic devices.

authors.name: Tom T. C. Sistermans, Rasmus H. Godiksen, Sara A. Elrafei, Alberto G. Curto

papers.title: From description to design: Automated engineering of complex systems with desirable emergent properties
papers.summary: Across the sciences, researchers have developed hundreds of statistics that describe the collective behavior of complex systems. These statistics are typically used passively, to describe a system after the fact, so it is rarely learned whether the patterns captured actually matter. The problem of engineering systems that display desirable emergent properties is a less developed area, as the very nature of emergent phenomena challenges the typical bottom-up approach to engineering. Here we propose a top-down approach, re-purposing the large number of descriptive statistics as objective functions in an optimization pipeline. Since this method lets a collective property instantiated directly, it makes long-standing correlational questions amenable to experimentation. We demonstrate this concept on four models taken from four different areas of science: a Kuramoto coupled-oscillator model (physics), a Wilson-Cowan network of excitatory and inhibitory processes (neuroscience), an SIRS pandemic spread model (epidemiology), and an echo-state network (machine learning). In each case, we take measures commonly used to describe behavior and feed those descriptive statistics back into the system to sculpt desirable macro-scale properties into the fundamental generative dynamics. We find that this approach is successful across domains and systems, and the inclusion of ``emergent" measures can actually improve the ability of some systems to perform tasks. We argue these threads can be unified into a general practice of emergent engineering that combines traditional task-oriented, bottom-up approaches to engineering with top-down guidance of collective, emergent properties to build resilient, capable, complex systems.

authors.name: Thomas F. Varley, Josh Bongard

papers.title: Precision Spectroscopy of a Trapped Ion Using a Bath of Ultracold Atoms
papers.summary: We perform laser spectroscopy of a trapped ion that is not directly laser cooled. An ultracold atomic bath continuously cools the internal degrees of freedom of the ion to its hyperfine ground state via spin-exchange collisions, while a cotrapped $^{174}$Yb$^+$ ion sympathetically cools the external degrees of freedom. Successful laser excitation is detected via state-selective charge transfer following a collision with an atom and subsequent ion loss. As a demonstration of this spectroscopic technique, we probe the $6^2S_{1/2}\rightarrow 6^2P_{3/2}$ transition at 329 nm in $^{173}$Yb$^+$ and measure the magnetic and electric hyperfine interaction constants for the $6^2P_{3/2}$ state to be A = -241(1) MHz and B = 1460(8) MHz, respectively. Our results are in agreement with a previous measurement obtained in a hollow-cathode discharge experiment but are a factor of 6-9 more precise. The techniques demonstrated in this work may be extended to perform precision spectroscopy on ions with complex level structures, with applications in fundamental physics.

authors.name: Egor Kovlakov, Rene Gerritsma

papers.title: Toward Neutrino and Dark Matter Detection with Ancient Minerals: TEM Study of Heavy-Ion Tracks in Olivine
papers.summary: Solar, supernova, and atmospheric neutrinos, and possibly weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter, have been interacting in the Earth beneath our feet for billions of years. The ''paleo-detector'' technique seeks to detect and characterize the induced crystalline defects from these events, in particular from energetic nuclear recoils, which in some minerals can be preserved on these timescales. Such defects can manifest as nuclear recoil tracks, on the order of a few nanometers wide and extending up to hundreds of microns in length, which can be detected with nanoscale-resolution microscopy. In order to test the feasibility of the paleo-detector technique and to study the formation and morphology of track defects in promising mineral candidates like olivine, we use ion irradiation to artificially implant tracks to effectively mimic astrophysical particle interactions. We present a study of heavy-ion track width as a function of depth, which we relate to ion energy, in an olivine crystal irradiated with 15 MeV Au$^{+5}$ using scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). Unlike previous studies, which measure tracks at the surface of the irradiated sample, we instead take measurements at various target depths via focused ion-beam sectioning of the irradiated sample. No etching techniques are used to enhance the tracks. In addition, we provide a comparison to predictions from simulations using SRIM software and previous results with a variety of ion species and energies. Notably, we find that a significant change in track continuity across the energy range studied (0.4-12.9 MeV) is indicative of the transition between electronic and nuclear stopping power dominance, consistent with the simulations' predictions. Overall, the tracks produced in olivine indicate that this mineral is an attractive candidate for paleo-detection, with robust track creation at the MeV scale.

authors.name: Andrew Calabrese-Day, Emilie LaVoie-Ingram, Kathryn Ream, Hannah Ross, Joshua Spitz, Patrick Stengel, Kai Sun, Alexander Takla

papers.title: Iterative approach for high-quality binary intensity hologram generation in augmented reality applications
papers.summary: Binary amplitude spatial light modulators, such as digital micromirror devices (DMDs), are increasingly relevant for computer generated holography due to their high refresh rates, low cost, and due to the emergence of subwavelength pixel architectures. However, the binary constraint limits the reconstruction quality, as conventional approaches rely on a binarization applied as a final step after hologram computation which leads to reduced efficiency and contrast. We introduce an iterative estimation approach for the generation of off axis binary amplitude holograms, in which the binarization constraint is applied at each iteration. We validate the approach through numerical simulations and experimental reconstruction using a DMD based optical setup. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons with random superposition and Gerchberg Saxton methods demonstrate significant improvements in image contrast, light efficiency, and reconstruction fidelity, with comparable computational cost. The proposed method provides a practical route toward high quality CGH using binary modulators and supports emerging applications requiring high speed and high resolution holographic projection.

authors.name: Anik Ghosh, Matteo Ziliani, Marco Astarita, Samuele Trezzi, Alessandro Cerioni, Anna Cesaratto, Mara Galli, Gianluca Valentini, Andrea Bassi, Giulio Cerullo, Paolo Pozzi

papers.title: Thin-Film AlN Microbolometer for Very-Long-Wave Infrared Detection
papers.summary: We demonstrate a suspended thin-film aluminum nitride (AlN) microbolometer for narrowband very-long-wave infrared detection. The device uses a 100 nm-thick AlN membrane suspended above a Pt back reflector by a 1 $\mu$m air gap. Resonant absorption near 15.4 $\mu$m is set by the AlN transverse optical phonon and is strengthened by suspension above the reflector. A periodic perforation pattern reduces membrane thermal mass, facilitates release, and tunes the effective optical thickness without requiring a thinner deposited film. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) reflection measurements on the released bolometer show approximately 95% peak cavity absorptance near 15.4 $\mu$m with a 0.772 $\mu$m FWHM. DC resistance measurements under tunable infrared illumination verify bolometric operation, with a peak normalized resistive responsivity of 252 ppm/mW at 15.48 $\mu$m. This platform can enable compact wavelength-selective thermal detectors for multispectral imaging, on-chip infrared spectroscopy, and chemical sensing.

authors.name: Vivek Tallavajhula, Zarko Sakotic, Ian Anderson, Yinan Wang, Daniel Wasserman, Ruochen Lu

papers.title: Temporal connection probabilities in real networks
papers.summary: Principled prediction of when and where links form in complex networks is a fundamental problem. We derive a closed-form non-Markovian expression for next-step connection probabilities that unifies latent hyperbolic geometry with long-range memory of past interactions. This expression yields interpretable forecasts governed by a small set of parameters. Applied to large-scale real networks, the framework explains how interaction history changes the distance dependence of connectivity: repeated interactions can remain probable at large distances, whereas first-contact probabilities are consistent with a nonmonotonic distance dependence. The framework's predictions agree quantitatively with empirical connection probabilities. These results provide a common probabilistic description of first contacts and repeated interactions, linking the latent geometry of networks to their temporal connectivity.

authors.name: Fragkiskos Papadopoulos

papers.title: Dynamically Reconfigurable Optical Skyrmions Enabled by a Silicon Microring Optical Phased Array for Robust Free-Space Communication
papers.summary: Optical skyrmions can encode information in the skyrmion number for free-space communication through atmospheric turbulence. However, programming both the skyrmion number and type on a compact chip remains challenging. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate a skyrmion generator based on a silicon optical phased array with optimized inner- and outer-grating microring emitters. The two emitter types provide orthogonal circularly polarized components and generate optical skyrmions through coherent superposition. The on-chip phase shifters configure the azimuthal phase distribution, enabling the $4\times4$ array to generate states with target skyrmion numbers of $-2$, $-1$, 1, and 2. Adjustment of the relative phase bias continuously switches states with target skyrmion numbers of $\pm1$ between the N\'eel and Bloch types. Increasing the array size to $12\times12$ extends the target range from $-8$ to 8. Laser wavelength tuning and calibration of the microring input phases and amplitudes recover target states within a range of simulated fabrication errors, which shows the robustness of the generator. Furthermore, we evaluate four-symbol communication using skyrmion-number decoding over a simulated 100 m turbulent link and observe no symbol errors in $10^4$ trials at Rytov variances up to 0.12. These results demonstrate the potential of this generator as a compact, programmable transmitter for turbulence-tolerant free-space optical communication.

authors.name: Zili Cai, Tian Zhang, Qi Chen, Jubo Hao, Jian Dai, Kun Xu

papers.title: Comparison of Proton, Helium-Ion, and Carbon-Ion CT Imaging for Hadron Radiotherapy Using Monte Carlo Simulations
papers.summary: Objective: To perform a comprehensive comparative analysis of proton, helium-ion, and carbon-ion computed tomography (CT) as direct imaging modalities for hadron therapy treatment planning, focusing on Relative Stopping Power (RSP) reconstruction accuracy and patient radiation dose. Approach: High-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations were conducted using the GATE/Geant4 platform to model a standard CTP404 phantom. RSP maps were reconstructed using two iterative algorithms: the Simultaneous Algebraic Reconstruction Technique (SART) and the Richardson-Lucy (RL) deconvolution. Imaging performance was evaluated by comparing reconstructed RSP values against ground truth data for various tissue-equivalent inserts, while integral doses were estimated for a human head geometry using a Shepp-Logan-like phantom. Main results: All investigated particle modalities demonstrated a significant dose reduction compared to conventional X-ray CT protocols (which are approximately 40 mGy). The estimated imaging doses were 0.5 mGy for protons, 1.3 mGy for helium ions, and 7.5 mGy for carbon ions. In terms of accuracy, carbon-ion imaging achieved promising accuracy for soft-tissue materials (mean absolute error <0.5%). Helium ions offered a balanced performance with sub-1% errors for most materials and a dose burden significantly lower than carbon ions. Protons exhibited the widest range of RSP deviations. Significance: Direct particle imaging eliminates the systematic uncertainties inherent in photon-to-hadron conversion, which typically introduce RSP deviations of 1.6%-3.5% in standard single-energy X-ray CT. While carbon ions provide better RSP reconstruction precision essential for complex treatment plans in heterogeneous anatomy, helium and proton imaging offer exceptional dose sparing, making them particularly advantageous for pediatric patients and frequent adaptive replanning scenarios.

authors.name: Zs\'ofia J\'olesz, G\'abor B\'ir\'o, G\'abor Papp, Gergely G\'abor Barnaf\"oldi

papers.title: Enabling quantum communication in ultra-large-scale networks
papers.summary: The recent development of small-scale quantum networks poses the question of which network-level mechanisms could enable quantum communication to operate at scale in a future Quantum Internet. The question can be answered within a well-established framework where a quantum network is mapped into a classical weighted graph, and communication reliability is assessed using methods from network theory. Previous work relied on this framework to determine sufficient conditions for viable network-wide communication only on special network topologies, such as regular lattices, and to devise communication protocols applicable only to small- and moderate-sized real networks. Here, we overcome both limitations by introducing a family of quantum communication protocols that scale to networks with hundreds of millions of nodes. We show that the competition between increasing communication distance and path redundancy determines their large-scale behavior, and that degree heterogeneity can provide sufficient redundancy to sustain communication in small-world networks. These conclusions are supported by a systematic analysis of both real network topologies and synthetic networks, and an analytical treatment in the limit of infinitely large random scale-free graphs.

authors.name: Filippo Radicchi

papers.title: Programmable Synthetic Motion at a Time-Varying Interface
papers.summary: Space-time metamaterials that exhibit synthetic motion promise arbitrary control over the momentum, frequency and energy of scattered light, but realising the required space-time modulation in a programmable way remains a challenge. Here we program synthetic motion using a single spatial light modulator in a 4f geometry which imprints a continuously tunable pulse-front tilt onto a high-intensity pump pulse, inducing reflectivity modulations at a sub-wavelength indium tin oxide thin film with synthetic velocities spanning the sub- and superluminal regimes. The angle-resolved spectrum of a scattered probe pulse reveals space-time diffraction patterns whose gradient and bandwidth vary continuously with synthetic velocity, in excellent agreement with theory. Splitting the shaped pump into two independently controlled pulses yields space-time double-slit diffraction with tunable fringe separation and frequency-momentum gradient. This programmable platform opens a path towards non-linear and periodic space-time trajectories for tabletop analogue studies of relativistic phenomena and space-time metasurfaces.

authors.name: A. C Harwood, D. Cielecki, T. V. Raziman, S. A. Maier, S. Vezzoli, R. Sapienza

papers.title: Resonant lunar tides of Earth's core and basal magma ocean
papers.summary: Earth's magnetic field is generated by fluid motion in the liquid-metal core and has been active for billions of years. However, prior to the onset of inner-core growth, the sources of mechanical power that drove the geodynamo remain uncertain. During this period, the core may have been overlain by a basal magma ocean (BMO), creating two immiscible fluid layers separated by a density interface, beneath the solid mantle. We develop a theory for lunar tides in this core--BMO system, in which the tidal potential acts on the density contrast between the two layers. The resulting dynamics differ fundamentally from previous models driven by imposed deformation of the core's bounding envelope. In the inviscid limit, the response transitions from an equilibrium tide to an interfacial gravity wave as forcing frequency increases. The two regimes are separated by a resonance that occurs when the forcing frequency matches the natural frequency of the degree-2, order-2 interfacial mode. The inviscid core flow is formally identical to the canonical elliptical vortex, linking the problem to the theory of elliptical instability. Finite viscosity regularises the resonance, introduces phase lag and generates oscillatory boundary layers. Combined with parameterised models of lunar recession and BMO crystallisation, the theory predicts enhanced core-boundary ellipticity, core-flow speed, magnetic Reynolds number and instability metrics, particularly near resonance. These results identify a previously unexplored mechanism for tidally driven flow in differentiated planetary bodies and show that a BMO can enhance tidal coupling to the core, potentially contributing to dynamo action.

authors.name: Murray B. C. Kiernan, Hamish C. F. C. Hay, David W. Rees Jones, James F. J. Bryson, Richard F. Katz

papers.title: Dictionary learning approach to analytic continuation of imaginary-time quantum Monte Carlo data
papers.summary: Many fields of physics use quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations to simulate quantum systems in imaginary-time $\tau$ and estimate imaginary-time correlation functions (ITCF). However, extracting dynamic $\omega$-dependent quantities from ITCFs is a notoriously difficult task, known as analytic continuation (AC), that amounts to solving an exponentially ill-conditioned inverse problem. Within the AC literature, there are competing stochastic and regularized approaches, as well as an emerging collection of works using parameterized models like neural networks. Here we transcend the traditional divides between the communities, introducing the regularized stochastic optimization method (RSOM). This method reformulates AC as a dictionary learning problem, discovering a sparse dictionary to represent the solution. Our approach is motivated by the astounding results dictionary learning has produced in many scientific fields. Remarkably, RSOM discovers a sparse dictionary that maps a high-dimensional ill-conditioned inverse problem to a low-dimensional problem. We demonstrate that the method yields competitive results for common synthetic test problems as well as for authentic QMC data from the finite temperature electron gas. Due to the low dimensionality, there is reasonably finite uncertainty in the dictionary, which is leveraged to create an \textit{ad hoc} post-processing estimate of the dictionary coefficients' sensitivity to perturbations. This work exposes that a dictionary exists within all stochastic and regularized methods and that dictionary learning provides a new angle of attack for future AC methods.

authors.name: Thomas Chuna, Phil-Alexander Hofmann, Alexander Benedix-Robles, Tobias Dornheim

papers.title: High-Power Laser Drives Motion in Ultra-thin Photonic Crystal Lightsails
papers.summary: Laser-driven lightsails require reflectors that are ultralight, highly reflective and robust under intense illumination. These demands point to the thinnest reflectors that dielectric optics allows, photonic crystals, in which a perforated membrane thinner than the wavelength of light acts as a mirror. Such mirrors reflect by confining light inside the membrane, but this confinement also amplifies absorption, making ultralow-loss, tension-bearing materials essential. Stoichiometric high-stress silicon nitride uniquely meets both requirements, yet its ~1 GPa stress makes large, compliant structures difficult to release intact, and such sails have never been pushed by high-power lasers. Here we demonstrate millimeter-wide, 200-nm-thick photonic-crystal trampolines in this material, with 99% design reflectivity at 1070 nm and a static stiffness of 0.53 N/m. Radiation pressure displaces them by more than a micrometer within 50 microseconds. In air, they withstand several times the irradiance found at the Sun's surface, delivered as a coherent beam. Light reshapes the sail more than it pushes it, since modest temperature differences buckle the membrane and collapse its stiffness, so thermal deformation outpaces radiation pressure within milliseconds. The interaction and compliance that make lightsails movable also let light deform them. These results establish a testbed for high-power nanophotonics, directed-energy systems and light-driven propulsion.

authors.name: Lucas Norder, Ata Ke\c{s}kekler, Richard A. Norte

papers.title: The Sustainability Paradox of Biodegradable Packaging Through a Life Cycle Perspective on Chitosan Based Food Packaging
papers.summary: Chitosan-based packaging systems are being studied as alternatives to traditional food packaging made from petroleum sources. The research that has been carried out so far has mostly focused on analyzing their material properties, formulation strategies, or biodegradable behavior. However, as a result, there is a gap left in understanding how the upstream impacts affect the functional advantages of food packaging and the end-of-life results of the formulation process. This review evaluates what trade-offs exist as well as what factors affect the sustainability of chitosan-based packages. Beginning with chitin extraction from crustacean waste, key processing steps, including demineralization, deproteinization, and nanoparticle synthesis, are assessed in terms of chemical intensity, energy demand, and associated emissions. Manufacturing routes, including solvent-based and green synthesis approaches, are compared with those of conventional plastics to identify relative environmental burdens. The use phase is analyzed with respect to antimicrobial functionality, shelf life extension, and potential reductions in food waste. End-of-life pathways, including biodegradation and composting, are evaluated alongside uncertainties related to degradation behavior and nanoparticle fate. The review takes into account life-cycle issues and offers a scientifically based viewpoint on how to differentiate between packaging applications whose environmental benefits can be determined and those whose ecological footprint, lack of functionality, and uncertainty regarding disposal make it impossible to assess sustainability.

authors.name: Maria Cosic, Milena Cosic, Amy Kim, Siddhartha Pahari, Grace Wu, Rayna Zhou, Trisha Daftari, Shaily Gupta, Reyna Michelle Suneel, Srinivasan Latha, Rashi Sharma, Utkarsh Chadha

papers.title: Classical diamagnetism: How adiabatic change of field makes it work
papers.summary: Many textbooks discuss the diamagnetic response of a ``classical atom'' to a small and slowly (adiabatically) applied magnetic field. Here we show that the small-field assumption is not essential, whereas the slow rate of field change is crucial: it preserves the circular nature of the orbit regardless of the applied field magnitude. The latter property follows from the existence of an adiabatic invariant of electron's motion. Orbit circularity allows us to solve the problem for arbitrarily large fields. Resulting diamagnetic response exhibits symmetries that unexpectedly persist beyond the small-field limit, and provides a nice illustration of the range of applicability of Larmor's theorem.

authors.name: Ya. B. Bazaliy, Ammar Kasem

papers.title: Uniaxial poroelastic tendon model with crimped fibre recruitment reveals hysteresis
papers.summary: Fibre recruitment plays an important role in tendon. Due to their large water content, a popular modelling approach for tendons is poroelasticity. Within this framework some tendon studies have included fibres, though none have included crimped fibre recruitment. We present a one dimensional poroelastic model in which the solid skeleton is composed of a soft neo-Hookean background matrix and crimped fibrils which do not bear load (FIB model). As the tissue is stretched, fibrils are straightened and contribute to load bearing. The fibre-reinforced tissue is compared to a tissue with a purely neo-Hookean (NH) skeleton in response to a uniaxial constant applied load (loading) and release of the load (unloading). The system dynamics are governed by a diffusion equation where the diffusion coefficient depends on stiffness. Within tendon parameter ranges, the FIB model is softer than the NH model, and so approaches steady state more slowly during loading. The presence of stiff, crimped fibrils increases bulk extension without excessively straining the fibrils, providing a natural protection mechanism for the tendon's structural components to load, in agreement with experiments. During unloading, the FIB model is much slower to relax as the tissue softens due to fibril re-crimping. This asymmetry in loading and unloading manifests as a hysteresis loop in the stress-strain curve averaged over the tendon. The hysteresis is reduced with increasing applied load. To the authors' knowledge, the finding of hysteresis within this framework is novel. The inclusion of fibrils allows for clearer biological interpretation and potential comparison to data. While the stress law employed in this study is bespoke for the application at hand by accounting for crimp and fibril recruitment, other fibril constitutive laws can readily be considered and incorporated into this framework.

authors.name: Zoe C. Godard, Sarah L. Waters, Derek E. Moulton

papers.title: Solar System and Atomic Clock Bounds on Locally Coupled Swampland Scalars
papers.summary: We study how local measurements constrain light scalar fields that are relevant in late time cosmic acceleration and are often discussed in connection with swampland criteria. Starting from a scalar-tensor framework, we define the swampland slope and curvature variables in the canonically normalized Einstein frame and relate them to Solar System tracking, Lunar Laser Ranging, equivalence principle tests and atomic clock comparisons. These measurements do not constrain the scalar velocity by itself, but products of that velocity with microscopic couplings to matter, gravity and atomic parameters. For coupling directions visible to local experiments, the scalar is driven into an ultra slow present regime. This severely restricts the possibility of realizing an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ de Sitter gradient through unscreened visible sector couplings alone. The refined de Sitter alternative remains possible, but in the single field hilltop realization it requires proximity to the maximum or a tuned suppression of the growing mode.

authors.name: Suraj Gavhale, Maxim Khlopov, Oem Trivedi, Maxim Krasnov

papers.title: Quantum frequency comb with pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading in a lithium niobate microresonator
papers.summary: Integrated quantum photonics requires bright, high-fidelity photon-pair sources capable of spectral multiplexing, correlation control, and circuit-compatible extraction. Cavity-enhanced spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) increases pair generation, but triply resonant operation imposes stringent pump-signal-idler spectral-alignment constraints. Moreover, the trade-off between intrinsic generation and coincidence-to-accidental ratio (CAR) does not capture the usable output flux, which depends on photon extraction. Here, we demonstrate a single-pass-pumped, resonator-enhanced quantum frequency comb (QFC) source based on a periodically poled lithium niobate photonic-crystal Fabry-P$\'e$rot microresonator. The device yields intrinsic and loaded brightnesses of 69.9 and 1.88 MHz/$\mu$W, respectively, and a maximum CAR of 16,000. Frequency-resolved measurements reveal 461 cavity-defined bins spanning 1495-1570 nm, and loaded spectral brightness approaching $2.22\times10^9$ pairs/(s$\cdot$mW$\cdot$nm). Heralded autocorrelation measurements yield a second-order autocorrelation $g_H^{(2)}(0)$ as low as $4.0\times10^{-4}$ for a selected high-CAR cavity-defined bin pair. In particular, tuning the single-pass pump deterministically selects correlated frequency-bin pairings within the fixed QFC grid while preserving brightness and pairwise coincidence rates. We further separate intrinsic generation from output photon-pair flux, revealing the loaded-brightness-CAR relation. Together, pump-selectable bin pairing and extraction-aware loading point to tailored SPDC QFCs as chip-integrated nonclassical light resources for multichannel quantum-state transport and information processing.

authors.name: Mohamad Reza Nurrahman (Department of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Hyeon Hwang (Department of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Nuri Han (Department of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Guhwan Kim (Quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Hong-Seok Kim (Quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Kiwon Moon (Quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Jung Jin Ju (Quantum Optics Research Section, Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Hansuek Lee (Department of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Min-Kyo Seo (Department of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, Daejeon, Republic of Korea)

papers.title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
papers.summary: The analytical modeling of a plasma wakefield driven by a relativistic proton beam is an element in optimizing advanced plasma-based acceleration schemes. In this work, we present a 1D nonlinear fluid framework under the quasi-static approximation to describe the wake potential excited by a positively charged proton driver which attracts background electrons into a density compression rather than expelling them. We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using a two-bunch scheme, our piecewise-event integration model is validated to high numerical accuracy ($\sim 10^{-11}~\mathrm{GV/m}$) against independent phase-space quadrature of cold-fluid solutions, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ ramped micro-bunch train with fixed $2\pi$ spacing, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a piecewise analytical scaling model. This formulation maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic post-train residual wake plateau, which is determined exactly by the conserved vacuum Hamiltonian invariant evaluated at the final bunch-train exit state. Furthermore, the framework estimates the onset of nonlinear phase-slippage that arrests growth and causes the transient wakefield overshoot to decay toward the residual horizon. Providing immediate 1D analytical benchmarks, this computationally inexpensive tool offers a reproducible baseline for verifying 1D fluid and multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) codes. It also provides a tractable starting point for exploring asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles relevant to transformer-ratio optimization.

authors.name: D. Tsiklauri

papers.title: Probing Extended Recognition Sites in Zn-Metalloproteins via Quantum Chemistry and Polarizable Molecular Dynamics
papers.summary: Zn-metalloproteins play vital roles in numerous metabolic processes, making them high-value targets for structure-based drug design. To advance these efforts, it is useful to unravel the individual components of the intermolecular interaction energies ($\Delta E$) that stabilize the Zn-binding cavity, both in the absence and presence of bound protein ligands. Here, we utilize quantum chemistry (QC) to decompose $\Delta E$ into distinct physical contributions. The relative magnitudes of these components vary significantly depending on the coordination number (four to six) and the chemical nature ('hard' vs. 'soft') of the Zn-coordinating ligands. These high-level QC analyses serve to calibrate and validate polarizable molecular mechanics potentials, effectively extending the accurate description of electronic effects beyond the immediate Zn-binding cavity to enlarged recognition sites and, ultimately, entire protein systems over long molecular dynamics (MD) simulation timescales. We focus here on a QC-grounded molecular mechanics procedure, denoted as SIBFA. Following a concise overview of our QC methodology used for its calibration, we present validation studies on complexes containing up to 300 atoms and discuss the prospects of applying this framework to large-scale simulations of Zn-metalloprotein-ligand complexes. Finally, the structural and energetic roles of discrete, highly polarizable water molecules are highlighted.

authors.name: Nohad Gresh, Jean-Philip Piquemal

papers.title: Single-Photon Detection via Enhanced Cross-Phase Modulation in Topology-Optimized Epsilon-Near-Zero Dual-Wavelength Nanocavities
papers.summary: We use the Green's tensor quantization theory for open resonant nanostructures with absorption losses to study cross-phase modulation (XPM) at the single-photon level in nanoscale Kerr-type epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials with an effective nonlinear susceptibility integrated inside dual-wavelength nanocavities. We obtain analytical formulas for the XPM frequency shifts in hybrid nanocavities that simultaneously trap a classical probe beam at 1.5 $\mu$m and single-photon pump at 3 $\mu$m wavelengths. We present a comprehensive analysis of the fundamental limits for mid-infrared single-photon detection in the quantum nondemolition modality for nanostructured cadmium oxide (CdO) regions with ENZ-enhanced nonlinearity embedded in a silicon (Si) environment inversely designed by free-form topology optimization. We numerically implement our theoretical results using finite element simulations within the rigorous framework of quasi-normal modes, demonstrating a single-photon XPM frequency shift $\Delta f_s \approx 5.71 \text{ GHz}$ with fractional shift (i.e., frequency pulling) $\Delta f_s / f_s \approx 2.85 \times 10^{-5}$ and addressing the feasibility of detection in the hybrid Si-CdO dual-wavelength nanocavity, either with a classical probe beam or a squeezed probe state, including the contributions of traditional limitations from self-phase modulation noise, thermorefractive noise, shot noise, and free-carrier absorption effects. Finally, we present a comparative size scaling analysis of the XPM phase shift and phase noise contributions for dual-wavelength nanocavities based on CdO and indium tin oxide (ITO) nonlinear ENZ materials. This work establishes a robust benchmark for the engineering of mid-infrared single-photon nonlinear devices such as nondemolition quantum detectors, sensors, and all-optical gates on a solid state photonic platform.

authors.name: Luca Dal Negro, Riccardo Franchi, Marco Ornigotti

papers.title: Investigating planar Proca metamaterials in nonlinear (2+1)-Electrodynamics
papers.summary: The present work pursues the investigation of the physics of a planar electromagnetic system incorporating nonlinear effects, as well as de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass terms in vacuum, which can be tuned to describe new planar metamaterials (MTMs) potentially suitable for technological applications. As a result, we observe interesting effects generated by a spatially dispersive profile that emerges from non-linearity. This characterizes the three-dimensional QED vacuum as a nonlocal metamaterial. The constitutive relations are derived, and the dielectric function of the metamaterial (MTM) exhibits spatial dispersion due to the Chern-Simons mass. The dispersion relations are analyzed in terms of applied external electromagnetic fields and both the de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass parameters. We also notice that, in the special case in which only a background magnetic field is present, this field gives no contribution neither to the dielectric function nor to the spatial dispersion profile, as is the case when both the electric and magnetic fields are present.

authors.name: Widervan de Deus Morais, Stamatios Strikos, Ronaldo Thibes, Jos\'e Abdalla Helay\"el-Neto

papers.title: Comparative qualification of advanced plasma-facing materials for fusion pilot plants through public- and private-sector experiments in DIII-D
papers.summary: A coordinated DIII-D campaign involving four private fusion developers and 12 participating institutions comparatively assessed 44 advanced plasma-facing materials, including the first DIII-D divertor exposure of neutron-irradiated W, to support fusion pilot plant wall and divertor material qualification. Samples were exposed using the Divertor Materials Evaluation System (DiMES) under Ohmic, L-mode, and H-mode conditions with edge-localized modes, at 0.2-2.5 MW m$^{-2}$ on flush geometries and 10-15 MW m$^{-2}$ on 10$^\circ$ angled geometries. Engineered tungsten architectures retained integrity; long-fiber Wf/W showed the clearest crack-arrest behavior. W-Re and K-doped W showed near-ITER-W-like responses, while additively manufactured W-Ta showed heat-flux-sensitive mass losses of 0.64 mg for the flat sample and 2.19-2.87 mg for angled samples. After irradiation to 0.3 dpa at 550$^\circ$C, neutron-irradiated ITER-grade W retained 2.8 times more deuterium than pristine W, while TiB$2$ showed the lowest D$2$ release in the Ohmic set. VTaHfMo was the most stable refractory multi-principal-element alloy. NbC and (Nb${0.5}$Ta${0.5}$)C retained integrity with 0.02-0.03 mg mass loss, whereas ZrC lost 7 mg. CVD SiC retained macroscopic integrity but exhibited an effective Si erosion yield of 0.5, about 5-10 times above prior DIII-D trends. Renewable boron pebble rods underwent plasma-driven recession; 13% of released boron was ionized near the outer strike point and up to 50% was recovered locally. Initial in-situ Cr gross-erosion measurements yielded effective erosion yields of order $10^{-2}$. Together, these results provide cross-material benchmarks for fusion pilot plant down-selection and future AI/ML-assisted plasma-facing-material development.

authors.name: Florian Effenberg, Jonathan D. Coburn, Luca Cappelli, Simon D. Corah, Amoolya Grandhi, Jerome Guterl, Charlie Hirst, Mike Jackson, Dylan A. Kohler, Rob Kolasinski, Erick Martinez-Loran, Ria Meston, Lauren Nuckols, Angelica Ottaviano, Zana Popovic, Sergey Tsurkan, Tessa Van Volkenburg, Daniel Velazquez, Aaliyah Zuniga, Arunodaya Bhattacharya, Jose Boedo, Kent Christian, Giacomo Dose, Eric Hollmann, Mykola Ialovega, Florian M. Laggner, Samara Levine, Xavier Navarro, Andrew Shone, Lance L. Snead, David Sprouster, Jason Trelewicz, Jayson Barr, Ryan Hood, Charlie Lasnier, Yan-Ru Lin, Vincent Mazon, Jun Ren, Gilson Ronchi, Dmitry Rudakov, Dinh Truong, Cedric Tsui, Shawn Zamperini, Weicheng Zhong, Tyler Abrams, Anthony W. Leonard, Roberto Maurizio

papers.title: Rotational spectra and de-perturbation analysis for ground state ytterbium oxide, YbO
papers.summary: A combination difference analysis of Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (FTMW) measurements of $^{174}$YbO combined with earlier near-infrared chemiluminescence data have resulted in much improved YbO rotational and centrifugal distortion constants. These have been confirmed in a multi-isotopologue analysis of further FTMW measurements of $^{172}$YbO and $^{176}$YbO and an analysis of nuclear-size-dependent Born-Oppenheimer breakdown effects in the molecule. Multiple excited electronic states overlap with low-lying excited vibrational levels of the electronic ground state leading to irregularities in its vibrational spacings and other previously observed electronic manifolds. This has been modeled with a matrix of the vibrational levels of the ground and multiple interacting states assuming Morse potentials and including electronic Hamiltonian matrix elements mixing the states. Vibrational level overlaps were calculated numerically assuming Morse vibrational wavefunctions. The resulting de-perturbed potentials for the states inform continuing experimental and theoretical work on this and other ytterbium-containing molecules.

authors.name: Richard J. Mawhorter, Sean Jackson, Charles Brainin, Trevor J. Sears, Peter F. Bernath, Philipp Buschmann, Jens-Uwe Grabow

papers.title: Newton's Second Law: A Structural Necessity of Mechanics Constrained by Excluded Perpetual Motion and Universal Free Fall
papers.summary: For over three centuries, Newton's second law (F = ma) has governed mechanics with extraordinary success, while its epistemic warrant has remained empirical. That merely empirical contingency vanishes once mechanics is constrained by two principles: the principle of excluded perpetual motion (PEPM) with its pre-Newtonian phenomenological content and the weak equivalence principle (WEP) with universal free fall as its primitive content. The PEPM secures the applicability of Suppes' measurement-theoretic framework to gravitational mass and force, exposing the formal structure latent in their empirical manifestations and establishing both as independent primitives. Gravity bridges statics and kinematics in Stevin's and Galileo's inclined-plane arguments, where the common sine factor in force and acceleration cancels in F/a. Cycle arguments under the PEPM extend this result to arbitrary force mechanisms, establishing F/a as object-intrinsic and securing inertial mass as a well-defined physical quantity. Further constrained by universal free fall, the resulting quantitative structure compels the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass, with Newton's second law as the operational expression of that equivalence. Direct implications include constraints on modified-inertia MOND that follow from the PEPM alone. The PEPM also places free-fall and torsion-balance experiments on equal footing as tests of the WEP. Together with the WEP, the derivation further grounds both the dimensional reduction of mechanics and the location-invariance of the Kibble-balance realization of the SI kilogram. Deeper still, Newton's second law derives its necessity from exclusion and invariance principles whose scope extends beyond mechanics itself.

authors.name: Lars Nordmann

papers.title: Quantum Theory of Third-harmonic Generation in Epsilon-Near-Zero Materials
papers.summary: We present a theoretical framework, based on the Green's tensor quantisation method, to describe third-harmonic generation in epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials and derive analytical, closed-form solutions for the generation efficiency. We validate our model against experimental measurements of wavelength- and angle-resolved third-harmonic generation efficiency from 30 nm-thin ITO nano layers at low pump intensity, described under the undeleted pump approximation. Our results provide a local and scalar model for quantum nonlinear processes in dispersive and lossy ENZ media, and establishes a simple and reliable framework for investigating a variety of nonlinear optical phenomena with applications to quantum sensing, quantum information, and quantum non demolition measurements.

authors.name: Sonia Alipour, Riccardo Franchi, Tornike Shubitidze, Smridhi Chawla, Luca Dal Negro, Marco Ornigotti

papers.title: 3D trapping of a meta-atom in an intensity minimum
papers.summary: High-refractive-index particles have recently attracted a growing interest in optical manipulation, enabling to engineer optical forces through electromagnetic Mie resonances. Unlike standard silica particles, which exhibit trap frequencies mainly determined by material density, resonant meta-atoms formed by high-index particles enable qualitatively new trapping behaviors. In this work, we experimentally investigate the trapping of resonant silicon particles in an optical standing wave. A direct comparison of silicon and silica highlights the fundamental differences in their optical force scaling and trapping dynamics. Beyond conventional trapping at intensity-maxima, we demonstrate deterministic and stable three-dimensional trapping of silicon nanoparticles in optical intensity minima, a regime that remains inaccessible for silica particles. Drawing a mesoscopic analogy with blue-detuned atom trapping, our results establish meta-atoms as a versatile approach to further extend the optical manipulation tool box towards accessing novel trapping regimes e.g. in close proximity to a surface.

authors.name: Bin Lu, Adeel Afridi, Nadine Meyer, Romain Quidant

papers.title: Geometry-Encoded Multireceiver Fluorometry Affords Full-Range Nonlinear Quantification under the Primary Inner Filter Effect
papers.summary: The inner filter effect (IFE) transforms the nominally linear fluorescence-concentration relationship into a geometry-dependent and often nonmonotonic response, resulting in reduced sensitivity, concentration ambiguity, and inaccurate underestimation at high optical densities. Here, we introduce a spatially encoded multireceiver fluorometric strategy that does not eliminate or correct the IFE, but instead harnesses the spatial fluorescence attenuation induced by IFE as an additional quantitative encoding dimension. Fluorescence generated along the excitation axis is integrated over independently positioned receiver windows, and concentration is recovered by nonlinear optimization of the joint fluorescent intensity vector. Tryptophan was selected as a biomedically relevant model fluorophore to validate the proposed strategy. Single-window calibration exhibited vanishing-gradient boundary and two-valued concentration inversions, whereas two spatially separated receiver windows restored global identifiability across the full concentration range. Screening of 35 two-receiver geometries identified the minimum-uncertainty configuration, achieving an average 95% error half-width of mean E_95= 0.884 mg/L, and the maximum-sensitivity configuration, reaching a noise-normalized response sensitivity of mean S_N=3.832 a.u./(mg/L). By converting spatial attenuation into a multidimensional concentration coordinate, this approach extends quantitative fluorescence analysis without dilution, a separate absorbance measurement, or piecewise calibration and provides a general metrology framework for fluorescence metrology even under strong IFE conditions.

authors.name: Shuiyi Tan, Yuchao Fu, Nai-Quan Zhu, Olivier J. F. Martin

papers.title: Photonic Weyl Points and Fermi Arc Surface States in a Self-Assembling Zinc-Blende Colloidal Crystal
papers.summary: We characterize the design, photonic band structure, and self-assembly of a colloidal crystal capable of supporting robust topological Weyl points and Fermi arc surface states in 3D. To achieve this, we propose a new zinc-blende structure, built off of recent progress in self-assembling diamond photonic crystals, which lacks inversion symmetry and supports photonic Weyl points. Furthermore, we show that the geometry can be optimized to make the Weyl point and its Fermi arc surface states experimentally observable in the photonic crystal's projected band structure. Finally, we perform molecular dynamics simulations to demonstrate that the geometry we propose for observing Weyl points is capable of being self-assembled with realistic interparticle interactions. Together, these results provide a platform for the assembly of large-scale photonic crystals supporting topological degeneracies and robust Fermi arc surface states in the visible and near-infrared.

authors.name: Johnathon P. Gales, Hengbin Cheng, David J. Pine, Mikael C. Rechtsman

papers.title: Quantifying AI data center nitrogen oxide (NO$_x$) emissions from space
papers.summary: AI data center power demand is spurring rapid deployment of on- and near-site natural gas turbines. The resulting nitrogen oxide NO$_x$ pollution is a growing concern but has not previously been quantified with atmospheric observations. Here we demonstrate space-based detection and quantification of NO$_x$ emissions from the SpaceXAI Colossus 2 power plant in Southaven, Mississippi. Using observations from the geostationary TEMPO satellite instrument, we detect a strong increase in local mean NO$_2$ column concentrations after the plant began operations in late 2025. We then use TEMPO to estimate two-week-average NO$_x$ source rates from August 2025 to August 2026, calibrating against continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) data from US power plants. TEMPO first detected NO$_x$ emissions in December 2025 at 530$\pm$220 kg h$^{-1}$. We find that emissions increased through August 2026, averaging 870$\pm$165 kg h$^{-1}$ after February 2026, roughly 19$\pm$4 times higher than expected from the facility's March 2026 permit for 41 turbines operating under best available control technology (BACT) requirements ($\sim$47 kg h$^{-1}$). Emissions at the expected level would be undetectable by our TEMPO analysis.

authors.name: Kevin D. Gauld, Daniel J. Varon, Nicholas Balasus, Daniel H. Cusworth

papers.title: Direct, Collision-Operator-Free Simulation of Electron-Ion Transport in Magnetized and Unmagnetized Plasmas
papers.summary: Accurate electron-ion collision models are central to predicting transport in fusion and space plasmas, yet collision operators and Monte Carlo collision models assume that a charged particle meets one partner at a time and that its successive encounters are independent. However, an electron that turns back along the magnetic field passes the same ions again. We solve the Newton-Lorentz equations for test electrons among static ions with a prescribed Debye-screened potential. The method combines force summation within an interaction radius, a time-symmetric particle pusher, and adaptive time stepping, enabling stable and scalable simulations in unmagnetized and magnetized plasmas. Using simulation-based measures of momentum relaxation and cross-field diffusion, we compare the simulations with a reference in the same model that treats every encounter as independent. Without a magnetic field the scattering rate reproduces the binary-collision rate for the same potential to within 2%. When the gyroradius is smaller than the Debye length, the scattering rate stays within 10% of the reference, but the cross-field diffusion coefficient exceeds it by a factor that grows with the field, up to 17. The excess comes from repeated passes of the same ions, whose guiding-center displacements add up: when the ions are replaced by new random ones many times per scattering time, so that a returning electron meets different ions, most of the excess disappears. The framework therefore provides a computational benchmark for testing and improving reduced collision operators and transport models.

authors.name: Keheng Zhu, Jian Liu, Chaozhou Mou, Senran Lin, Wei Zhang

papers.title: Requirements for Synthetic-Frequency Switching in Integrated Photonic Fabrics
papers.summary: Electro-optic synthetic-frequency coupling can coherently transfer light between the frequency modes of an integrated resonator, but its value in a multiport photonic switch depends on how connections share spatial paths, frequency channels, and control signals. Here we identify two distinct architectural roles of synthetic-frequency coupling in switching fabrics and the device requirements associated with each. As a channel-assignment resource, it cannot increase the number of orthogonal channels per port, but it recovers connections blocked by fixed input frequencies or unavailable output channels. A short coupling range is sufficient. In an 8x8 fabric with eight channels per port, coupling over the first three frequency spacings achieves 95.2% of the blocking reduction of unrestricted inter-mode coupling, and the range of coupled separations matters more than the specific choice of radio-frequency tones, consistent with limited-range wavelength conversion in wavelength-division-multiplexed networks. As a spatial-switching resource, frequency control can reduce the number of spatial switching elements only through a nonseparable joint element whose spatial state is programmable for each frequency channel, whereas a separate frequency-conversion stage cannot replace missing spatial connectivity. Finally, a thin-film lithium niobate resonator model with experimentally reported coupling and decay rates, embedded in a multistage Mach-Zehnder interferometer fabric, shows that with a single shared drive the power redistributed to non-target modes and the reduced transmission of frequency-preserving paths outweigh the added connectivity. These results define the through-channel transmission, mode selectivity, and control requirements for useful synthetic-frequency switching.

authors.name: Jorge Parra

papers.title: Seismic P- and S-wave attenuation inversion in time-frequency domain based on Kramers-Kronig relations
papers.summary: Seismic attenuation (inverse quality factor) inversion is important for gas reservoir prediction. Two key issues in seismic attenuation inversion are the development of a physically consistent reflection coefficient equation and stable inversion of seismic attenuation from seismic data. To address these issues, this study, within the framework of isotropic linear viscoelastic media, starts from the Kramers-Kronig relations and expresses the viscoelastic stiffness matrix as a function of seismic attenuation. Under the assumptions of weak attenuation and small elastic and attenuation contrasts across the interface, a frequency-dependent PP-wave reflection coefficient equation explicitly containing P- and S-wave attenuation terms is derived using scattering theory. The derived equation not only satisfies the causality constraint but also preserves a compact mathematical form. Based on this equation, P- and S-wave attenuation are estimated by a time-frequency domain Bayesian inversion. To improve resolution and stability, the inversion adopts a recursive frequency strategy with half-power overlapping Gaussian windows, in which the result at the previous frequency serves as the prior model for the next frequency, and prior models are built from well-log rock-physics modeling to provide low-frequency constraints. Synthetic seismic data tests show that the inversion resolution and accuracy improve as the inversion frequency increases and that the method remains robust at a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 dB. Application to field seismic data further demonstrates that the P-wave attenuation anomalies effectively identify gas reservoirs, whereas S-wave attenuation is insensitive to gas reservoirs. This study provides a new approach for extracting P- and S-wave attenuation information from seismic data and achieving high-resolution prediction of gas reservoirs.

authors.name: Shengyi Wang, Xuehua Chen, Xingyu Luo, Kaixing Huang

papers.title: Thresholdless IBW Emission and Alpha-to-Thermal-Ion Energy Channeling via Pole Resonance of Fusion-Product Ions
papers.summary: Fusion reactions can release a substantial fraction, and in aneutronic reactions nearly all, of their energy as the kinetic energy of fusion-product ions. In magnetized plasmas, these energetic ions can form ring distributions in velocity space. Such distributions can drive Dory-Guest-Harris (DGH) electrostatic instabilities, but these self-instabilities require a finite energetic-ion density and can be stabilized by a thermal background. We show that the same background can instead enable a distinct instability mechanism: a cyclotron pole of the minority energetic-ion susceptibility destabilizes a stable ion Bernstein wave (IBW) eigenmode. When the energetic-ion harmonic is distinct from the thermal-ion harmonics, exact root-pole resonance is thresholdless in the ideal collisionless limit. A species-resolved power balance shows that the energetic ions supply the free energy while the thermal plasma receives it. In the LAPD proton--alpha example, $99.96\%$ of the alpha-particle power loss enters the coherent proton response. This self-excited, ion-directed transfer provides a possible linear building block for alpha-particle energy channeling in proton-Boron11 fusion.

authors.name: Hong Qin, Nathaniel J. Fisch

papers.title: Proposing, never assigning: fair allocation of shifts in experimental particle physics collaborations from ranked wishes under institutional quotas
papers.summary: Experimental particle physics collaborations staff the operation of their detectors with shifts, taken in the control room or remotely by members drawn from dozens of institutions. The established practice for filling them is a credit system with self sign-up: institutions owe a quota of credit, and people take the seats they want when booking opens. This paper describes a method in which seats are instead allocated from ranked wishes under institutional quotas, the result is issued as offers that each person accepts or declines, and an independent checker recomputes every rule before anything is published: the platform proposes, never assigns, and proves that it kept the rules. The credit and quota model is inherited from current practice. Around that core the paper adds a quota rule that keeps indivisible blocks fair to institutions whose share of a period is smaller than one block, and four rules that make fairness visible beyond the count: shares of owl, weekend and holiday blocks, seats shown in the laboratory's clock and the institution's own, reachable pools for institutions that cannot travel, and booking order by balance. On a synthetic collaboration of 48 institutions and 256 eligible members, the method allocates 70 to 72 of 72 seats per period in two rounds, with a mean rank satisfaction of 84 to 95% and no rule broken; after a year of running every institution of four members or more is within 13% of its cumulative share, and the smallest institutions, which one block overshoots by arithmetic, are brought within the same range by pooling in pairs.
