Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schr\"odinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction method.Our results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their interplay.To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. These estimates illustrate the potential signatures of quantum corrections in gravitational-wave ringdown.

authors.name: Nikola Herceg, Tajron Juri\'c, A. Naveena Kumara, Andjelo Samsarov, Ivica Smoli\'c, Kumar S. Gupta

papers.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
papers.summary: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

authors.name: Nikola Savi\'c, Filippo Vernizzi

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
papers.summary: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and E\"ot-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the E\"ot-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

authors.name: Federico Huxhagen, Diana L\'opez Nacir

papers.title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$\mu_5$ matching in the NJL model
papers.summary: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $\delta\Omega_r=c_r\mu_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$\mu_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$\mu_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $\mu_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $\mu_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$\mu_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.

authors.name: Jingyi Chao

papers.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states on $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ fermionic quantum algebra
papers.summary: We study the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states with two Grassmann variables $(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)$ built on the superalgebra $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ associated with the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli-Kyemba, the two dilation parameters $\phi_1(p,q)$ and $\phi_2(p,q)$ being meromorphic functions of two variables evaluated at $(p,q)$. The graded super-Fock space splits into four sectors: bosonic, $\phi_1-$fermionic, $\phi_2-$fermionic and bi-fermionic. In each of them we establish the diagonal representation of the density operator by means of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$derivative, angular integration and Berezin integration, and we give a unified compact form in terms of sectorial parametric functions. The total density operator is obtained in explicit form as the sum of the four sectorial contributions, and can be read as a mixture of the four sectors. We define the sectorial reproducing kernels, obtained from the resolution of the identity, we compute the matrix elements of the density operator in the super-coherent state basis, and we prove the hermiticity, positivity and matrix multiplication properties of the kernels, together with the series expansion of their diagonal values. An integral formulation relates the density operator, its density function and the reproducing kernel, the latter being the function associated with the identity operator. Berezin quantization in the bosonic sector yields the quantized operators associated with $z$, $\bar z$, $|z|^2$, $z^2$ and $\bar z^2$ and their mean values; the dispersions of the super-position and super-momentum operators show that the super-coherent states are intelligent states.

authors.name: Kaw\`eyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph D\'esir\'e Bukweli Kyemba, Bienvenu Gnim Adewi

papers.title: Central charges as black-hole hair in weakly coupled trace-anomaly gravity
papers.summary: We study black holes in Gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the Euler and the Weyl central charges. We prove that a constant anomalyon on any Ricci-flat geometry, the Kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. Otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the Standard Model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a universal window. Electric charge separates the two anomaly invariants: the hair reverses sign at a critical charge-to-mass ratio set by the ratio of central charges, its extremal value retains only the Weyl charge, and the Euler charge governs the near-horizon growth of the anomalyon. For every unitary matter sector, the hair regular at the event horizon diverges at the Cauchy horizon. Finally, once the higher-derivative Weyl operator is order-reduced, the background, the anomalyon-graviton mixing and all propagation speeds depend only on the difference of central charges, which extends the no-ghost and Laplacian stability conditions to the full anomaly.

authors.name: Francisco Tello-Ortiz, A. V\'asquez, Kazuharu Bamba, Ghulam Mustafa

papers.title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
papers.summary: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.

authors.name: El\'eana Berteaux, Florian Nortier

papers.title: From joint attention to shared symbols: A free-energy principle account
papers.summary: Joint attention precedes vocabulary acquisition. How can attending to the same object help two people with different sensory experiences come to use a shared word? In a free-energy principle account, marginalizing the common object induces a statistical dependence between private perceptual states. In a categorical world, the joint prior inherits a mixture structure whose component index provides a candidate for shared reference. The collective predictive coding model approximates this prior by representing the dependence through that shared index. An established Metropolis-Hastings naming game lets agents infer and exchange words using private evidence. Toy and multiview image experiments illustrate how word exchange can coordinate private categories and improve the fit of collective models. The account connects joint attention to shared symbols through the coupling of private inference.

authors.name: Tadahiro Taniguchi, Koji Hashimoto, Ryuichiro Ishikawa

papers.title: Multipartite entanglement structure of crystal quenches
papers.summary: Understanding how entanglement emerges and spreads in out-of-equilibrium quantum many-body systems is a fundamental problem. In this paper, we investigate multipartite entanglement after quantum quenches. In particular, we study the entanglement structure and dynamics of quasiparticle multiplets generated by crystal quenches in the tight-binding chain. We identify zero-configurations for which a multiplet shared between three parties has no irreducible tripartite entanglement---these configurations consist entirely of pairwise distributed bipartite-entangled states. The existence of zero-configurations has important implications on the entanglement structure and dynamics of crystal quenches. For example, we show that it can further delay the production of tripartite entanglement. We build the quasiparticle picture for the Markov gap, and prove that it is a faithful witness of irreducible tripartite entanglement for crystal quenches. We discuss several key aspects of their tripartite entanglement dynamics through the lens of the Markov gap. We confront our results with exact lattice numerics and find perfect agreement in the hydrodynamic regime.

authors.name: Paul Gaudin, Cl\'ement Berthi\`ere

papers.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
papers.summary: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dot{\phi}^2=\gamma H^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

authors.name: V. K. Oikonomou

papers.title: New analytic constraints for the soft anomalous dimension bootstrap at three loops
papers.summary: The soft anomalous dimension governs the universal long-distance singularities of gauge theory amplitudes. It exhibits a highly constrained analytic structure and has been shown to be amenable to bootstrap methods. In this paper we revisit the relation between unitarity cuts and sequential discontinuities of Feynman integrals and use it to derive new constraints on the soft anomalous dimension. At three loops, we show that certain sequential discontinuities in non-overlapping two-particle channels vanish for every web contributing to the quadrupole function that correlates four coloured partons. These constraints hold for arbitrary parton masses, and we explicitly verify them for the known massless and one-mass cases. We then demonstrate their constraining power by substantially strengthening the massless bootstrap and carrying out the first bootstrap construction of the one-mass quadrupole function. The new constraints are largely complementary to those arising from the absence of unphysical branch points, symmetries, and collinear and Regge limits. With their help, we determine each quadrupole function within the assumed function space up to a single coefficient, which we fix by matching to existing diagrammatic results. These results open the way to bootstrapping the three-loop soft anomalous dimension for amplitudes with several massive partons.

authors.name: Einan Gardi, Luke Lippstreu, Andrew J. McLeod, Laura Walsh, Zehao Zhu, Enrico Zunino

papers.title: The AdS/$\mathsf{C}$-$\mathsf{P}$-${\mathsf T}$ Correspondence
papers.summary: We study the realization of $\mathsf{C}$, $\mathsf{P}$, $\mathsf{T}$ in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM -- corresponding to charge conjugation, parity, and time-reversal -- and identify the $\mathsf{C}$, $\mathsf{P}$, $\mathsf{T}$ global symmetries of ${\cal N}=4$ SYM with bulk (gauge) symmetries of string theory on $AdS_5\times S^5$. The dual bulk transformations are symmetries of Type IIB string theory on $AdS_5\times S^5$ that combine string worldsheet symmetries, with geometric transformations acting on $AdS_5\times S^5$. We show that $\mathsf P$ and $\mathsf T$ map to $\mathsf{CP}$ and $\mathsf{CT}$ under $S$-duality (combined with an $SU(4)$ R-symmetry outer automorphism),while $\mathsf C$ and $ \mathsf{CPT}$ are invariant. We define codimension-two charge conjugation monodromy defects in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM, which have an unusual large $N$ expansion, and discuss their bulk dual description. We elucidate the relation between symmetries on the string worldsheet and symmetries of target space string field theory, global vs gauge symmetries in quantum gravity, among related topics. Defects in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM and in quantum gravity play a central role in this work.

authors.name: Jaume Gomis

papers.title: Non-Abelian Casimir energy in the Curci-Ferrari model through a functional approach
papers.summary: Using functional integral methods, we investigate the non-Abelian Casimir energy in the Curci-Ferrari model, which offers an effective description of the infrared regime of Yang-Mills theory. We consider a 3+1D (resp.\ 2+1D) system of two infinite parallel plates (resp.\ wires) at a fixed distance from each other, with either perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) or perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary conditions. Imposing the boundary conditions directly in the functional integral by the introduction of suitable auxiliary fields that act as Lagrange multipliers, we obtain a boundary effective action that captures the dynamics of this system. The Casimir energy is then computed both directly from the functional integral and via the energy-momentum tensor, providing equivalent results. We find that the Casimir energy for PEC and PMC conditions differs by a constant factor, which can be traced back to a van Dam--Veltman--Zakharov-like discontinuity (both in 3+1D and 2+1D). Lastly, we show that our analytical results are compatible with a variety of recent numerical lattice simulations of the non-perturbative Yang-Mills Casimir energy, in which a novel non-perturbative mass scale emerges.

authors.name: David Dudal, Philipe De Fabritiis, Sebbe Stouten

papers.title: Localisation with on-shell supersymmetry algebras via the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism: Localisation as gauge fixing
papers.summary: The Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism provides a powerful technique to deal with gauge and global (super)symmetries that may only hold on shell. We argue that, since global (super)symmetries and gauge symmetries appear on an equal footing in the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism, similarly localisation with respect to global (super)symmetries appears on an equal footing with gauge fixing of gauge symmetries; in general, when the gauge-fixing condition is not invariant under the global symmetries, localisation (with respect to a localising fermion) and gauge fixing (with respect to a gauge-fixing fermion) combine into a single operation. Furthermore, this perspective enables supersymmetric localisation using only on-shell supermultiplets, dispensing with auxiliary fields, extending an insight first discovered by Losev and Lysov arXiv:2312.13999. We provide the first examples of on-shell localisation for quantum field theories (together with a companion paper by Arvanitakis arXiv:2511.00144).

authors.name: Leron Borsten, Dimitri Kanakaris, Hyungrok Kim

papers.title: IR/UV mixing from higher-order interactions in a Scalar Field
papers.summary: The observed vacuum energy lies far below the usual quantum-field-theoretic estimate. We construct a preferred-frame reduced scalar Hamiltonian in which a nonlocal quartic field derivative interaction produces a wavevector dependence proportional to $|\vec k|^8$ for modes below a smoothly defined scale. Within the quartic oscillator regime, the ground-state energy and excitation gaps are $\propto |\vec k|^{8/3}$. The preferred frame is characterized by a timelike clock-field background. The Planck energy is reached at a substantially smaller value of the spatial wavevector due to its supra-linear mode-energy dependence. The proposed interaction is instantaneous in the preferred frame and yields a Hamiltonian bounded below. Normalizing the peak of the ground-state energy to the Planck scale, together with Cohen-Kaplan-Nelson (CKN) saturation, applied as a matching recipe rather than as an {\it {ab initio}} calculation, fixes the cutoff scale at $k_G\sim k_{Pl}^{1/3}k_{box}^{2/3}$. Modes above the smooth cutoff scale retain their ordinary scalar dynamics. We assume that the interaction-induced ground-state energy shift gravitates, as do other contributions. CKN saturation is imposed on the total vacuum energy, comprising this shift and the other vacuum contributions. Identifying the inferred infrared scale phenomenologically with the cosmic event horizon reproduces the holographic-dark-energy relation $\rho_{vac}\propto\frac{M_{Pl}^2}{R_h^2}$, provided the coupling tracks the horizon; the resulting holographic fluid has $w_0\simeq-0.89$.

authors.name: Satish Ramakrishna

papers.title: Modified gravity at large scales on quantum spacetime in the IKKT model
papers.summary: The gravitational dynamics of 3+1 dimensional covariant quantum spacetime in the IKKT or IIB matrix model is studied at one loop, combining the Yang-Mills-type matrix action with the induced Einstein-Hilbert action. This combined action leads to interesting modifications of the gravitational dynamics at long distances, governed by modified Einstein equations including an extra geometrical tensor interpreted as ''mirage matter''. In particular we find extra non-Ricci flat geometric modes with a non-standard dispersion relation, with features reminiscent of dark matter and/or dark energy.

authors.name: Harold C. Steinacker

papers.title: Integrability from Homotopy Algebras
papers.summary: Homotopy algebraic methods have become increasingly influential in the study of field theories. We consider semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory and its relation with the principal chiral model. The semi-classical equivalence of the two theories is expected on general grounds, as the principal chiral model arises by eliminating trivial pairs and gauge fixing. We construct this equivalence explicitly as an off-shell, cyclic quasi-isomorphism between the cyclic $L_\infty$-algebras governing the two theories, and show that it directly encodes the Lax connection. This provides a concrete example for studying integrability of a two-dimensional system through the homotopy algebraic lens.

authors.name: Luigi Alfonsi, Leron Borsten, Mehran Jalali Farahani, Hyungrok Kim, Martin Wolf, Charles Alastair Stephen Young

papers.title: Quasi-Local Celestial Charges and Multipoles
papers.summary: We extend Penrose's quasi-local mass definition to include higher-spin charges associated with the celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetries and relate them to traditional definitions of multipoles. The resulting formulae provide explicit expressions that can be computed on finite 2-surfaces, given a choice of null hypersurface. They yield a geometric definition of celestial symmetries and multipoles in generic spacetimes in terms of higher-valence solutions to the twistor equations. This, in turn, gives rise to natural flux-balance laws along the null hypersurface. We also present a first-principles phase-space derivation of these charges, starting from a twistor space action for self-dual gravity that can be identified with the standard gravitational asymptotic phase space at null infinity, performing a large gauge transformation analysis and using the Penrose transform to connect with the corresponding spacetime expressions. Finally, we formulate the spacetime analysis in the Plebanski gauge and relate the celestial symmetries to the integrability of self-dual gravity in the case of a self-dual background.

authors.name: Adam Kmec, Lionel Mason, Romain Ruzziconi

papers.title: Rotating End of the World
papers.summary: We study the thermodynamics and interior structures of dynamical end of the world (EoW) branes in the rotating BTZ black hole. By mapping the induced metric of the branes to an effective Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) system, we derive the first law of thermodynamics for the boundary conformal field theory (BCFT), incorporating boundary degrees of freedom. To construct this thermodynamics, we adopt two frameworks of black hole chemistry and the duality between the JT black hole and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. In addition, we verify that the shadow entropy is equivalent to the boundary entropy via Hubeny-Ryu-Takayanagi (HRT) surfaces. Furthermore, we explore the possible interior configurations of the EoW brane inside the horizon. Two representative configurations, namely single and double-joint EoW branes, are considered. These disparate configurations share the same exterior brane configuration outside the horizon. By comparing their energies, we show that a transition could occur within the horizon.

authors.name: Kyung Kiu Kim, Hwajin Eom, Jung Hun Lee, Yunseok Seo

papers.title: Classifying double copies and multicopies in AdS
papers.summary: In this paper, we draw a parallel between solutions of pure three-dimensional gravity with a negative cosmological constant and classical double copies in four dimensions. In the former case, topological solutions, such as the BTZ black hole, deficit angles, and naked singularities, emerge from identifying points in AdS using elements from its isometry algebra $so(2,2)$. The type of solution corresponds one-to-one with the orbits of $so(2,2)$. We demonstrate how various double copies of four-dimensional AdS gravity similarly arise from the $so(2,3)$ isometry elements, which also correspond one-to-one with their orbits through a Penrose-type transform. We classify all such elements and generate the corresponding double copies, which include AdS black holes, black branes, and many others. The double-copy isometries originate from the centralizer of a given AdS isometry, allowing us to define canonical coordinates associated with its Abelian part. Additionally, the two Casimir invariants of $so(2,3)$ feature in the metrics via the characteristic polynomial of the AdS symmetry parameter. Our classification naturally extends to higher spins, providing nonequivalent multicopies at the linearized level.

authors.name: V. E. Didenko, N. K. Dosmanbetov

papers.title: Anomalous Transport from Effective Field Theory
papers.summary: A systematic study of chiral effects is presented using an Effective Field Theory framework. By integrating out a massive Dirac fermion at finite temperature in presence of vector and axial background fields, the currents and their anomalies are computed from the path-integral. Chiral effects previously considered separately naturally arise in a unified computation, including new mass corrections. The link between each anomalous transport effect and the anomalies is clearly established, beyond the identification of their coefficients. In particular, we can appreciate how these effects are sourced by the anomalous nature of the theory even in configurations where the anomaly itself vanishes. The consistent and covariant anomalies are both encapsulated in master formulae for the currents which result from a careful treatment of the regularisation. It is finally found that, at finite temperature, the physical currents cannot be inferred simply from the Chern-Simons terms whose divergence reproduce the chiral anomalies.

authors.name: R\'emy Larue, Amaury Marchon, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot

papers.title: On the large N convergence of the supermembrane matrix model
papers.summary: In this paper, the large N behavior of a supersymmetric matrix model is compared with its exact continuum description. We prove that the complete spectrum of a $SU(N)$ regularized compactified M2-brane theory in the semiclassical approximation converges, in the large $N$ limit, to the exact spectrum in the same approximation. To this end, we concentrate on the large $N$ limit of a supersymmetric matrix model describing a supermembrane with central charge on a toroidally compactified target space. We analyze, on the one hand, the supermembrane model formulated on a differentiable compact torus, with structure group given by the area-preserving diffeomorphisms, and, on the other hand, its associated regularized $SU(N)$ model. We emphasize in our analysis the structure of the local and global constraints of the regularized model, which generate the $SU(N)$ algebra and reproduce the area-preserving diffeomorphism algebra in the large N limit, together with the topological information associated with the central charge condition and the topology of the model. We explain the role of the central charge in the compactified supermembrane and how it allows a top-down $SU(N)$ regularization. It is known that its $SU(N)$ regularized model has a purely discrete spectrum with finite multiplicity. We prove that, in the semiclassical approximation, the spectrum of the Hamiltonian of the supersymmetric matrix model converges in the large-$N$ limit to that of the Hamiltonian of the supermembrane (M2-brane) with central charge.

authors.name: M. P. Garcia del Moral, P. Le\'on, A. Restuccia

papers.title: Non-relativistic limits of $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory and S-duality
papers.summary: We investigate non-relativistic limits of four-dimensional maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory (4d MSYM) and their relation to the nonperturbative $\operatorname{SL}(2;\mathbb Z)$ S-duality of the relativistic theory. We construct a general family of non-relativistic limits using a Type IIB brane set-up with a D3-brane and $(p,q)$-strings and show that the resulting theories are topological deformations of supersymmetric Galilean Yang-Mills theory or quantum mechanics on the moduli space of BPS monopoles. The deformations of the Galilean Yang-Mills theory are the familiar $\theta$-term and a coupling to the monopole charge, while in the moduli space theory the only deformation is a $\theta$-term. This family of theories fit together into a three-dimensional moduli space with nontrivial topology, on which $\operatorname{PSL}(2;\mathbb Z)$-valued dualities act in a richer and more complex way than in the relativistic parent theory. In the Abelian case, we establish the duality directly using the path integral, while in the non-Abelian case we support our claim by matching the one-particle spectrum as well as the Galilean spacetime symmetries and electric/magnetic invertible one-form symmetries.

authors.name: Hyungrok Kim, Joseph Smith

papers.title: Poisson-Lie T-duality and D-brane Configurations of $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ Backgrounds
papers.summary: We construct a non-Abelian dual pair for the $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ background via Poisson-Lie T-duality on a semi-Abelian double. Using a specific parameterization of the six-dimensional Lie group ${A}_2 \times {A}_2 \times A_2$, we formulate the original $\sigma$-model incorporating the $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ metric with a vanishing Kalb-Ramond field ($B$-field), and derive its dual background, which features a non-vanishing $B$-field and a physical singularity. We investigate the conformal properties and test the generalized supergravity equations for the complete geometry; although a generalized Killing vector exists, the full background fails to satisfy these equations. We then analyze the asymptotic structure and coordinate domains, revealing distinct exterior and interior sectors separated by curvature-singular boundaries, alongside an asymptotic approach to the original background. Finally, we investigate the transformation of $D$-brane boundary conditions under Poisson-Lie T-duality for the semi-Abelian Drinfeld double $({\A}_2 \oplus {\A}_2 \oplus {\A}_2 , 6{\A}_1)$. By analyzing seven classes of gluing matrices, we examine the eigenvalue spectra, identify candidate dual D-brane configurations, and construct the corresponding Dirichlet and Neumann projectors. We also investigate the integrability of the Neumann distributions and determine the associated gauge-invariant two-forms and world-volume field strengths, providing a systematic framework for studying the geometric and boundary condition properties of the dual branes.

authors.name: Ali Eghbali

papers.title: Superconformal mechanics from N-extended Euler-Calogero-Moser and Calogero models
papers.summary: We investigate two-particle variants of the N-extended Euler-Calogero-Moser and Calogero models. Oving to translational invariance, the center-of-mass degrees of freedom and the associated fermions decouple, yielding specific systems of superconformal mechanics. Additional bosonic spin variables are straightforwardly incorporated into the supercharges and the Hamiltonian. For the Euler-Calogero-Moser model, the two-particle supersymmetry exhibits an unexpected extension from $Osp(N|2)$ to $SU(1,1|N)$ superconformal symmetry, whereas the Calogero model reduces to purely $Osp(N|2)$ superconformal mechanics. Finally, we demonstrate that introducing a larger number of fermions into the system provides a consistent pathway to overcoming well-known pathologies with higher supersymmetries inherent to these framework.

authors.name: S. Krivonos, A. Sutulin

papers.title: Group Theory and the CFT Distance Conjecture: $\mathcal{N}=2$ Tensionless Strings Have No (Co)Weight
papers.summary: We perform a systematic survey of the Hagedorn behaviour at infinite-distance points in the conformal manifold of four-dimensional large-$N$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ Superconformal Field Theories admitting a Lagrangian description. Many properties of these theories can be understood in terms of the Lie algebra encoding the shape of their quiver. We find that in the overall-free limit, the Hagedorn temperature is determined by the largest eigenvalue of an affine or finite Cartan adjacency matrix. This defines two types of universality classes of theories sharing the same high-energy exponential growth of states characteristic of string-like spectra. The first and largest is the affine case, corresponding to orbifold and orientifold projections of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills, and all share the same temperature. The others fall into universality classes following an ADE classification with a temperature set by the dual Coxeter number, and can be obtained by deforming the affine case. Our results apply to all large-$N$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ quivers with any classical gauge symmetry, including those with matter charged beyond bifundamental representations. We further discuss the string-theoretic construction of these theories and some of the holographic implications, as well as how our methods extend to broad families of theories with less supersymmetry. We also consider limits where only part of the theory becomes free, and find lower and upper bounds on the exponential rate predicted by the CFT Distance Conjecture. Both these bounds and the Hagedorn temperature are set by the same eigenvalue, and when the quiver has a single gauge node the lower bound is saturated, giving a natural explanation for the three universality classes recently found in the literature.

authors.name: Florent Baume, Fabio Mantegazza

papers.title: A discrete series gauge field at the late-time boundary of $dS_4$
papers.summary: We study the free Maxwell field on the planar patch of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime ($dS_4$). We review its bulk canonical quantization in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, and we give a representation-theoretic viewpoint by studying the transformation properties of single-particle states under infinitesimal dS transformations. By taking the late-time limit, we identify two late-time operators with scaling dimensions $\Delta=1$ (leading) and $\Delta=2$ (subleading). We introduce CFT-inspired inner products invariant under the dS group ($SO(4,1)$) for states created by late-time operators acting on the Bunch-Davies vacuum. We explain how the unitary discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ associated with the photon are furnished by both operators, in contrast with the Maxwell field on $AdS$ where the $\Delta=1$ operator corresponds to a non-normalizable mode. We also explain how the corresponding discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ split into a direct sum of representations corresponding to two helicities $+1$ and $-1$. This is achieved by taking advantage of the dS invariance of the self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors of the photon field strength. In our outlook, we draw inspiration from a recent proposal for the microscopic description of $dS_4$ higher-spin gravity where conformal gauge fields in 3 dimensions play a central role, and we investigate a possible connection of the $\Delta=1$ late-time operator with a conformal spin-1 gauge field in 3 dimensions.

authors.name: Manizheh Botshekananfard, Elif B\"u\c{s}ra G\"uraks{\i}n, Vasileios A. Letsios, Gizem \c{S}eng\"or

papers.title: Matrix Multiverses Meet Multiple Mythologies
papers.summary: We present a model in which asymptotically de Sitter universes of various types, and de Sitter (dS) radii $R_n$, live in the interiors of black holes in a maximally entropic flat $p = \rho$ Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe. These dS universes clearly have many quantum states. We argue that they decay and equilibrate with the maximal entropy universe on time scales of order $\alpha_n R_n {\rm ln} (R_n /\delta_n)$, where $\alpha_n$ are model-dependent dimensionless constants and $\delta_n$ are the initial distances between the shell, satisfying the Israel junction conditions, and the dS horizon. These are time-scales as viewed by a detector following a trajectory far from the would-be cosmological horizon. These times are all exponentially shorter than dS recurrence times, which have no meaning in this model. It is impossible for a detector inside one of the dS universes to determine whether it is actually part of such a structure. This model could be used as the basis for claiming that certain constants of nature or cosmological initial conditions were chosen to have mathematically unnatural values because other values could not lead to any form of intelligent life.

authors.name: Sidan A, Tom Banks, Willy Fischler

papers.title: False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
papers.summary: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $\phi^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $\phi^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.

authors.name: Manuel A. Mart\'inez S\'anchez, Christoph Adam, Danial Saadatmand

papers.title: Algebraic versus physical uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators
papers.summary: We give explicit determinant counterexamples to the uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators from their degrees and simultaneous pair zeros. At seven points the solution space has dimension seven; Bose symmetry removes six directions and leaves the Hodges line. At eight points a two-dimensional Bose-symmetric space remains. Regular integer-spinor configurations distinguish these deformations from the Hodges numerator. On the eight-point plane, collinear factorization, the leading positive-helicity soft coefficient and ordinary BCFW decay each select the Hodges line. For $n\ge5$, we prove two results on the full fixed-degree, common-denominator ansatz, without pair-zero conditions. Complete collinear residue functions on all pairs determine at most one numerator; Bose symmetry makes one channel sufficient. The splitting law and a normalized lower-point amplitude supply the boundary function, starting from an explicit five-point seed. With Bose symmetry, $O(Z^{-1})$ decay under one fixed same-helicity shift at generic conserving kinematics also selects the Hodges line. Normalized collinear and soft data fix the eight-point scale; the homogeneous shift condition leaves one constant per multiplicity.

authors.name: Lin Mai, Yaobo Zhang

papers.title: History-Dependent Mode Selection in a Driven Holographic Superfluid
papers.summary: We study finite-rate mode selection among competing Landau-unstable modes in a holographic superfluid. The first mode to reach a prescribed amplitude need not be the instantaneously fastest-growing one. Time-dependent linear evolution on the driven homogeneous background closely reproduces the modal amplitudes obtained from full bulk evolution. Protocols with identical present driving conditions can reverse the relative ordering of two modes. For the controlled histories studied here, the change in their logarithmic amplitude ratio is well approximated by the excess accumulated differential QNM gain.

authors.name: Bo-Xuan Ge

papers.title: Teleparallel formulation of $E_{8(8)}$ Exceptional Field Theory
papers.summary: The potential of $E_{8(8)} \times \mathbb{R}^+$ exceptional field theory, suited for studying three-dimensional maximally supersymmetric compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, is derived in teleparallel formulation. This means that, starting from an ansatz of the most general combination of the quadratic scalar contractions of the intrinsic torsion, which is manifestly invariant under generalised diffeomorphisms, one selects the potential by imposing the invariance under infinitesimal rotation of the maximal compact subgroup of the duality group. The teleparallel formulation makes manifest at geometric level the preeminent role of the intrinsic torsion in studying compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, where the intrinsic torsion is identified with the embedding tensor of the resulting gauged supergravity.

authors.name: Davide Rovere

papers.title: Timelike Entanglement from Spacetime Density Matrices: A Lattice Realization
papers.summary: We develop a systematic framework for timelike entanglement in a two-dimensional free real scalar field, connecting spacetime density matrices with Lorentzian twist-operator correlators through independent microscopic and continuum calculations. Extending Gaussian diagonalization to generally non-Hermitian reduced operators, we determine their complete nonzero spectra in the generic regular case, together with all integer R\'enyi moments. The real-time replica construction relates these moments to twist correlators, with quantitative agreement in both magnitude and phase for the full four-point function on a circle, the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary two-point functions, and the massive form-factor predictions. In the massless continuum theory with Dirichlet boundaries, we further establish a finite causally connected window in which all integer moments are real, while the even moments are strictly positive for arbitrary initial states. For Gaussian states, all integer moments are strictly positive, and the resulting R\'enyi entropies are real. These results demonstrate that causal connectedness alone is not sufficient for a nonzero imaginary part of timelike R\'enyi entropy.

authors.name: Hao-yu Wang, Wu-zhong Guo

papers.title: A Geodesic Route toward Holography beyond AdS: Tessellating the Schwarzschild Black Hole
papers.summary: In vacuum anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, the geometry admits a perfect tessellation by a geodesic network. This tessellation characterizes the background exactly, and a partial entanglement entropy (PEE) tensor-network toy model of AdS/CFT can be defined on it. It has so far been unclear whether this construction can be extended beyond vacuum AdS. In this paper we take the first step in this direction. We show that the exterior region of the Schwarzschild black hole and its Einstein--Rosen bridge are perfectly tessellated by a specific geodesic gas emitted from the boundary, so that Crofton reconstruction holds in these regions. We then prove that such a geodesic tessellation and the Crofton reconstruction it defines extend to more generic Riemannian manifolds. This allows us to construct a PEE tensor-network model of holographic duality on more generic geometric backgrounds. In the case of the PEE tensor-network model for the Schwarzschild background, we can concretely realize the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy, the Ryu--Takayanagi formula and the ER=EPR proposal. Our approach opens a new route towards holographic toy models beyond AdS/CFT.

authors.name: Shi Gu, Qiang Wen, Haocheng Zhong, Yiwei Zhong

papers.title: Generalized eigenstate thermalization beyond leading order in 2D large $c$ CFTs
papers.summary: We develop a Fock-space formulation that reduces expectation values of vacuum-family quasi-primaries in quantum Korteweg--de Vries (qKdV) eigenstates to a free-bosonic problem, and employ it to test the generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (GETH) in 2D conformal field theories with a large central charge. We prove that the first two qKdV charges $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ lift all degeneracies except along at most countably many curves in the $(c,\,\Delta)$ plane, where $c$ is the central charge and $\Delta$ denotes the highest weight of the conformal family, so that the full-qKdV simultaneous eigenstates are unambiguously determined by $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. Based on this, a comprehensive toolkit for testing GETH within the scope of vacuum-family observables, i.e. equating qKdV eigenstates and thermal states of the generalized Gibbs ensemble in the sense of expectation values of vacuum-family local observables, is provided in this paper. We argue that GETH is satisfied when the infinite tower of qKdV charges is considered. A more restrictive form of the GETH, namely that all expectations of local observables of a definite level should be expressible in terms of the first few qKdV charges, is directly falsified at subleading order in the large-$c$ expansion. Specifically, at levels 6 and 8 in the vacuum family, expectation values of quasi-primaries in simultaneous eigenstates of the qKdV charges are not determined by any finite number of the lowest-index qKdV charges. The question of whether additional microscopic information about the eigenstate is required is left for future work.

authors.name: Ziyuan Wang, Shaojie Wang, Jiaju Zhang

papers.title: Massive de Sitter Correlators as Finite Mellin-Barnes Integrals
papers.summary: Using the Mellin-Barnes representation of de Sitter propagators, we reduce tree-level heavy-particle exchange to finite integrals that converge at physical kinematics on mass-independent contours, and one-loop diagrams to the same integrand times a flat-space momentum factor. We compute the complete one-loop triangle at general masses, with its collider signal in closed form to all orders in the squeezed-limit expansion, and give the triple-exchange bispectrum at arbitrary heavy masses as a double series that converges at every physical shape. The loop reduction also applies at strong mixing.

authors.name: Amara McCune

papers.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
papers.summary: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.

authors.name: Arsen R. Melikyan, Aleksandr Pinzul

papers.title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
papers.summary: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $\xi$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $\xi$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.

authors.name: John F. Dawson

papers.title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
papers.summary: We derive the primordial $\langle\zeta\zeta h\rangle$, $\langle\zeta hh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.

authors.name: Y. A. Ageeva, M. A. Stepanov

papers.title: BPS Chaos and Fortuity in Higgs Branches I: The Gepner Point
papers.summary: The BPS states in Calabi-Yau compactifications of type II string theory can sometimes be described using quiver quantum mechanics whose Higgs branch is a complete intersection manifold. Their degeneracy resembles that of BPS black holes. A small fraction of these states corresponds to multi-center supergravity brane configurations and can be continued to the (near-Higgs) Coulomb branch. We identify them as monotone states. The overwhelming majority of states, known as pure-Higgs states, are fortuitous states, which concentrate at a particular $R$-charge. This division has a precise mathematical meaning as two different types of cohomologies of the Higgs branch target space. We argue that a natural probe of BPS chaos in these models is the Berry/Chern curvature. In the case of the Gepner model, we use localization techniques in an auxiliary two-dimensional CFT to compute the curvature, its RMT properties, and deviations from it.

authors.name: Micha Berkooz, Trivko Kukolj, Ohad Mamroud, Josef Seitz

papers.title: Tachyon and massless sectors of the bosonic string effective action
papers.summary: Recently, it has been observed that in certain schemes of the bosonic string effective action, the non-derivative tachyon appears only in the tachyon potential, while all other couplings involve covariant derivatives of the tachyon and massless fields. Within these schemes, a minimal basis can be found whose coupling constants are constrained by T-duality upon circle reduction. Using this constraint, one obtains sets of couplings at each order of \(\alpha'\) that are invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the tachyon. In this paper, we observe that consistency of these T-dual sets with S-matrix elements requires an appropriate field redefinition, such that each set becomes invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the metric, dilaton, and tachyon. This separates the couplings into a massless sector and a tachyon sector. We determine the six-derivative couplings in the massless sector, with all coupling constants fixed, and find two T-dual couplings in the tachyon sector with arbitrary coupling constants. We show that the leading-order action and the massless-sector couplings exactly reproduce the expansion of the sphere-level S-matrix element of two tachyons and two massless vertex operators at six-momentum order, and that the coupling constant of the four-tachyon coupling in the tachyon sector is fixed by the expansion of the four-tachyon S-matrix element at six-momentum order.

authors.name: Mohammad R. Garousi

papers.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
papers.summary: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cveti\v{c}-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-St\"ackel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.

authors.name: Di Wu, Shuang-Qing Wu

papers.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
papers.summary: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.

authors.name: Jie Gu

papers.title: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
papers.summary: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives of finite duration can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate comparisons, some protocols reach a prescribed entropy tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. At criticality, a slow scalar field can persist even when little horizon entropy remains available for preparation and subsequent relaxation. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of order $\varepsilon^4$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient governs the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow mode on the normal side. This weight vanishes in proportion to the mode's decay rate near the transition. Horizon area growth is quadratic in the covariant scalar flux. When the horizon remains smooth and its area growth uniformly controls the radial drift of the scalar field, the time needed to suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$. Charge transfer fixes the signed area swept out by the time integral of this same flux, raising the minimum flux cost and strengthening the time bound.

authors.name: Yu Shi, Sheng Long

papers.title: Lie-Poisson Formulation of Dissipative Spin Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: Covariance and the second law cannot fix how fluid flow couples to spin, since reversible couplings produce no entropy. We show that the spin commutation relations and the Poincar\'e algebra fix these couplings. Reversibly, a flow exerts no torque on the spin: its magnitude per particle is conserved, its direction is Fermi--Walker transported, and spin--shear couplings reflect a deforming triad. The magnitude changes only through higher multipoles, as in spinor condensates, or dissipation, whose first-order spin--shear coupling reorients the spin away from the vorticity above a critical shear rate.

authors.name: Zi-Hao Liu, Mei Huang

papers.title: Holomorphic Feynman diagrams in four dimensions and the quantum BPS ring
papers.summary: We compute at all loop orders the kernels of the holomorphic Feynman graphs governing loop corrections to supersymmetry transformations and regularized operator products in the holomorphic twist of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric gauge theories. Interpreting their current equations as those of an electrical network---with Schwinger parameters as resistances and holomorphic momenta as injected currents---we iterate series, parallel and star-triangle reductions on Schwinger space to obtain the fan, spider and cubic product-forest kernels at all loop orders. Assuming that twisting commutes with quantization for composite operators, we obtain every perturbative correction to the supersymmetry transformation in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, acting on operators with arbitrary holomorphic derivatives. Using the marked higher operations of Gaiotto, Kulp and Wu, we construct the quantum product and prove that on cohomology of the quantum supercharge it is associative, graded commutative and unital, furnishing the multiplication of the quantum BPS ring; in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory every multi-graviton operator thus admits an explicit finite all-order completion. For the classical gauge groups, every perturbative differential image in the multi-trace ring vanishes upon Cartan restriction. In $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, we find new fortuitous classes and one-loop lifts across several gauge groups, no two-loop lift in the sectors tested, and rationally certified three-loop lifts in $SO(11)$, $SO(12)$ and $SO(13)$. The lowest example we find lies in the level-$34$ BMN sector of $SO(13)$. The glueball lifts in $SO(11)$ and $SO(13)$ remove the excess classical powers relative to their symplectic duals. Beyond $\mathcal N=4$, we find two-loop lifts in the Leigh-Strassler and $\beta$-deformations, and two- to four-loop lifts in abelian and $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theories.

authors.name: Botao Li, Kangning Liu, Chi-Ming Chang

papers.title: Holographic Tessellations Tensor Networks $\{p,q\}$ from Entangled Quantum Tetrahedron in Loop Quantum Gravity
papers.summary: The relationship between spin network states in loop quantum gravity and bulk--boundary duality is further explored using the tessellated holographic tensor network. We develop a holographic tensor network construction based on quantum entanglement between tetrahedra in loop quantum gravity (LQG). This construction relates four-valent intertwiner spaces and Bell states dressed with $SU(2)$ holonomies to effective tensors on hyperbolic $\{p,q\}$ tessellations. For the $\{5,4\}$ tessellation, six tetrahedra are assembled into a single effective cell with five network legs and one logical index. Provided that the microscopic transfer map has full row rank, a right inverse and a completion on the kernel space are employed to construct an isometric embedding, yielding an effective tensor proportional to a perfect tensor. The construction is generalized to the $p=2k-1$ family, with local dimensions supporting absolutely maximally entangled states. On finite networks satisfying a radial orientation condition, an appropriate normalization produces an isometric bulk--boundary map. For cuts satisfying the isometry condition on both sides, the boundary entropy decomposes into a link contribution $\sum_{\ell}\log(2j_{\ell}+1)$ and the bulk entropy, thereby providing a discrete realization of the quantum Ryu--Takayanagi structure. Applications to the black hole interior are formulated via postselection-based non-isometric encoding. Assuming additional Haar statistics, this framework is used to analyze the preservation of overlaps on average and the competition between entropy branches underlying the Page Curve. These results establish a constructive link between the geometric degrees of freedom of LQG and holographic codes, while clarifying the conditions required to connect them to geometric area in LQG, the location of the quantum extremal surface, and evaporation of black hole.

authors.name: Deden M. Akbar, Freddy P. Zen, Jusak S. Kosasih

papers.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
papers.summary: We establish a geometric framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms that are beyond standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. We also propose a generalized class Chern character and three conjectures: (i) the finite dimensionality of independent couplings at fixed derivative order, (ii) the representation of all-order mixed RR-gauge-scalar interactions through finitely many effective even forms, and (iii) the generation of higher-derivative contact terms from finitely many primitive tensor structures. Our framework provides a systematic mathematical foundation for reconstructing D-brane effective actions and exploring their underlying geometric and cohomological structures. We also introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity and their constraints.

authors.name: Armin Hatefi, Ehsan Hatefi

papers.title: Orthosymplectic Satake equivalence, II
papers.summary: This is a companion paper of arXiv:1909.11492 and arXiv:1912.01930. We prove an equivalence relating representations of a degenerate orthosymplectic supergroup with the category of twisted $Sp(2n,{\mathbb C}[\![t]\!])$-equivariant $D$-modules on the so called mirabolic affine Grassmannian of $Sp(2n)$. We also discuss (conjectural) extension of this equivalence to the case of quantum supergroups and to some exceptional supergroups.

authors.name: Alexander Braverman, Michael Finkelberg, Roman Travkin

papers.title: A Majorana Relativistic Quantum Spectral Approach to the Riemann Hypothesis in (1+1)-Dimensional Rindler Spacetimes
papers.summary: We present a Hilbert--P\'olya approach to the Riemann zeta function via a Mellin--Barnes integral for massive Majorana modes in $(1+1)$-dimensional Rindler spacetime. The boost spectrum is continuous on the full wedge and discrete with a reflecting wall. Summing positive momentum modes on a transverse circle yields $\zeta(2s)$ in the radial Mellin transform. Building on our one-sided Ces\`aro criterion for additive correlations of $\Lambda(n)-1$, we assign each prime $p$ a chiral channel of optical length $\tfrac12\log p$. Its $k$th return at $u=k\log p$ carries weight $\log p$. The centered correlation obeys $C(u)\le C(0)$ for all real $u$ exactly when the Riemann hypothesis (RH) holds. For a Majorana oscillator with linear mass profile, a bounded self-adjoint function of its Hamiltonian assigns period $kT_1$ to mode pair $k$. The first $n$ pairs have least common period $T_n=T_1\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)$, so $\log(T_n/T_{n-1})=\Lambda(n)$ for $n\ge2$. Set $m=\lceil\sqrt{x}\rceil$, $N=\lfloor mx\rfloor$, and $\psi(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$. The signed revival mean $A(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}(N/j-\psi(N/j))$ satisfies $A(x)=R(x)+o(\sqrt{x})$, where $R(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\Lambda(n)(x/n-1)-x\log x+(1+\gamma_{\mathrm E})x$. At each zeta zero $\rho$ of multiplicity $d$ with $\Re(\rho)>1/2$, the meromorphic continuation of $\int_2^\infty A(x)x^{-s-1}\,dx$ has a simple pole of residue $d/[\rho(1-\rho)]$. For fixed $\lambda>1$, $1/20$, the Kaczorowski--Pintz theorem gives $A(x)>Kx^\theta$ at some $x\in[Y,Y^\lambda]$ for all large $Y$. Thus RH follows if for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $C_\varepsilon$ with $A(x)\le C_\varepsilon x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ throughout $[Y,Y^\lambda]$ for arbitrarily large $Y$. For $\lambda=3/2$, the independent theta-lift estimate reported by Alp\"oge and Claude for $G=R$ gives this bound for $A$.

authors.name: Fabrizio Tamburini (Rotonium - Quantum Computing, Le Village by CA, Padova, Italy)

papers.title: Strange correlator and string order parameter for non-invertible symmetry protected topological phases in 1+1d
papers.summary: We construct strange correlators and string order parameters for non-invertible symmetry protected topological phases (NISPTs) in 1+1d spin chains. These diagnostics and the entanglement spectrum are connected to the interface algebra between two NISPTs. To compare phases, we first use finite-depth circuits of locally symmetric gates to minimize the bond dimension of each matrix product state. The resulting action tensors determine local strange charged operators and the charge decorations of truncated symmetry operators. The strange correlator probes the representation of the interface algebra realized by the two states. Higher-dimensional irreducible components yield nontrivial strange charged operators. For the distinct phases studied here, we identify such operators with long-range strange correlations. The full interface algebra admits a one-dimensional representation precisely when the phases coincide. For an on-site symmetry with a symmetric product reference state, the dimensions of the irreducible representations of the interface algebra also constrain degeneracies in the entanglement spectrum. We use unitary Drinfeld twists of a finite-dimensional Hopf $C^*$-algebra $H$ to construct general fixed point $\mathrm{Rep}(H)$ SPTs, action tensors and string order parameters. Our examples include the three $\mathrm{Rep}(D_8)$ NISPTs and intrinsically mixed $G\times\mathrm{Rep}(G)$ SPTs with explicit Hamiltonians for $G=S_3$. For the self-dual Hopf algebra $A_{12}$, we construct Hamiltonians and string order parameters for the two $\mathrm{Rep}(A_{12})$ SPT phases and evaluate a strange correlator between them. We also outline a geometric extension to higher dimensions.

authors.name: Da-Chuan Lu, Fu Xu, Yi-Zhuang You

papers.title: Quantum cosmological perturbations in bouncing models with mimetic dark matter
papers.summary: We calculate the power spectrum of cosmological perturbations originated from quantum vacuum fluctuations in bouncing scenarios proposed in Ref.~\cite{chamseddine2014cosmology} in the framework of mimetic cosmology. We show that all physically relevant models produce scale-invariant spectral indices and amplitudes compatible with observations, provided that the bounce occurs at length scales $t_0$ inside the physically reasonable interval $10^5 l_p < t_0 < 10^9 l_p$. We also show that by slightly modifying the scalar field potential proposed in Ref.~\cite{chamseddine2014cosmology}, we can obtain the observed red-tilted spectral index, with the same amplitude constraints. The underlying theory contains instability problems yet to be solved. However, the methods we constructed and the results we obtained may be sufficiently general to be applied to the infrared limit of some yet to be constructed healthy mimetic cosmology, providing reasonable bouncing cosmological models without the need for any background quantum effect.

authors.name: Idaiane L. Machado, D\^eivid R. da Silva, Nelson Pinto-Neto

papers.title: Interaction-enhanced quantum to classical transport crossover temperature in a Luttinger liquid
papers.summary: Strange metals are highly entangled gapless states of matter that exhibit anomalous transport, such as linear in temperature resistivity, over more than a decade of temperature. Why a single power law should be so robust is an open question. We propose a scenario in which interactions enhance the domain of certain scattering regimes, effectively suppressing other ``would-be regimes." We test this proposal in a one-dimensional Luttinger liquid coupled to a one-dimensional acoustic phonon. We use the memory matrix formalism to calculate the dc electrical and thermal conductivities at low and high temperatures, relative to the Debye cutoff on phonon frequencies, in both the ``clean" (umklapp scattering) and ``dirty" (disorder scattering) limits. We find the crossover temperature separating the low and high temperature regimes to be interaction-dependent, with repulsive interactions substantially increasing it, generally by more than an order of magnitude. This provides a concrete illustration for how interactions can extend a single transport regime over a wider temperature range.

authors.name: Yen-Wen Lu, Michael Mulligan

papers.title: Solving the Domain Wall Problem: Primordial Magnetic Fields as a Dynamical Solution
papers.summary: To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay-a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source that drives the axion field. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its efficacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. In particular, the axion emitted from the decaying domain-wall network can contribute to the dark matter abundance, and the associated gravitational-wave signal lies in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing array experiments.

authors.name: Zizhuo Zhao, Yuefeng Di, Ligong Bian, Jing Shu

papers.title: Entanglement, equivalence principle, and HBAR entropy, in a new bumblebee black hole
papers.summary: We investigate quantum correlations, atomic excitation, and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) entropy near a recently proposed bumblebee black hole with spacelike or lightlike Lorentz violating vacuum configurations. Using localized scalar field packets and the near horizon Rindler correspondence, we evaluate the logarithmic negativity and mutual information as functions of observer position, packet frequency, and geometric deformation. Configurations with the same geometry yield identical correlation measures. Positive geometric deformations partially counteract entanglement degradation, with the largest differences occurring at low frequencies. We also compute the excitation probability of a freely falling two level atom using the time coordinate normalized at spatial infinity. At leading near horizon order and within the frequency hierarchy adopted, its thermal factor agrees with the local flat spacetime acceleration radiation result. Finally, we derive the HBAR entropy flux and its relation to the radiative horizon area loss using the canonical conserved energy. The area coefficient depends on the causal character of the vacuum even for configurations with identical geometries: the spacelike case acquires a factor set by the bumblebee coupling, while the lightlike case gives the usual one quarter coefficient. These coefficients reproduce the corresponding thermodynamic entropy factors.

authors.name: A. A. Ara\'ujo Filho, Wentao Liu

papers.title: A single field inflationary model consistent with recent observations: reheating and radiative stability
papers.summary: We study single field inflation with the inverse exponential potential, which has one free parameter besides the energy scale. For a wide range of parameter space, its predictions for the scalar spectral index and the tensor to scalar ratio lie within the $1\sigma$ region of the combined SPA$+$BK$+$DESI data, and the wider family of inverse power law exponential potentials behaves similarly. We compare these predictions with those of the $R^2$ model, monomial potentials, $\alpha$-attractors, non-minimally coupled Higgs like inflation and a radiatively corrected plateau potential. The $R^2$ and monomial predictions lie near or outside the $2\sigma$ boundary of the same data, whereas the non-minimally coupled Higgs like and radiatively corrected plateau families overlap the favoured contours over part of their parameter space. To describe reheating, we add a steep exponential term that is negligible during inflation and, together with the inverse exponential term, creates a minimum about which the inflaton oscillates. The maximum reheating temperatures are $T_{\rm rh}\sim10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,{\rm GeV}$, consistent with the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis bound. Coupling the inflaton to a Dirac fermion through a Yukawa interaction, these temperatures require couplings comparable to the standard model charged lepton Yukawa couplings. Nonperturbative fermion production transfers negligible energy, and perturbative decay completes reheating. The same coupling induces a one loop correction to the inflationary potential, which limits the radiatively safe reheating temperature to $T_{\rm rh}\lesssim10^{12}\,{\rm GeV}$.

authors.name: Md. Wali Hossain

papers.title: Mixed-state Phases from Higher-order SSPTs with Kramers-Wannier Symmetry
papers.summary: Mixed-state phases have recently attracted significant attention as a generalization beyond their pure-state counterparts. Prominent examples include mixed-state symmetry-protected topological (mSPT) phases and the strong-to-weak symmetry breaking (SWSSB) phases. It has been shown recently that mSPT phases admit a holographic dual description in terms of higher-order subsystem SPT phases. In this work, we investigate the mixed-state phases obtained by tracing out the bulk degrees of freedom of higher-order subsystem SPT phases protected by non-invertible symmetries. We find that the resulting mixed-states exhibit the coexistence of the symmetry-protected topological order and SWSSB. We also use the interface as a probe to characterize the mixed-state phases, and specifically, when there is no local modification to preserve the symmetries across the interface, the two sides of the interface are in distinct phases.

authors.name: Aswin Parayil Mana, Zijian Song, Fei Yan, Tzu-Chieh Wei

papers.title: Fracton Topological Holography
papers.summary: Topological Holography (TH) is a framework of representing $(d-1)$-dimensional quantum systems with a $d$-dimensional sandwich, consisting of a topological order bulk, a gapped top boundary and a dynamical bottom boundary. Dualities and non-invertible symmetries are represented by the change of top boundary in the TH framework. Existing studies have focused on sandwiches with liquid topological bulk, in this paper we examine some fracton bulks, where we call the framework Fracton Topological Holography (FTH). In particular, the X-cube FTH induces the transverse field plaquette Ising model (TFPIM) version Kramers--Wannier duality, the duality between TFPIM and the two-dimensional $90^\circ$ quantum compass model, and the self-duality of quantum compass model. Haah's code FTH induces a duality of transverse-field generalized Ising models (TFGIMs). The two examples illustrate at least a part of type-I fracton (X-cube) and a part of type-II fracton (Haah's code) models can be used to construct FTH sandwiches. Moreover, we construct an explicit Sequential Quantum Circuit (SQC) switching the top boundary of X-cube sandwich, realizing the TFPIM version KW duality.

authors.name: Yu-Tao Hu, Jie-Yu Zhang, Peng Ye

papers.title: No classical particle limit for massless quanta
papers.summary: We investigate whether relativistic massless classical particles may emerge as the classical limit of massless quanta. To address this question independently of any specific dynamics, environment, or pointer basis, we develop an axiomatic and operational framework for the coarse-graining approach. In this formulation, a candidate classical phase space is taken as the outcome space of a POVM subject to minimal classicality and covariance requirements. Applying this framework to the Poincar\'e group, we prove a no-go theorem for massless particles: the covariance requirement is incompatible with the operational conditions for classicality. Conversely, we show that the obstruction can be avoided for massive particles by constructing coarse-graining schemes satisfying the minimal classicality requirements. The no-go theorem leaves open field-like limits of massless quanta, such as the emergence of the electromagnetic field, while ruling out classical massless particles, such as classical photons.

authors.name: Riccardo Falcone, Simon Fuchs

papers.title: 70 years of Double-Logarithmic Approximation
papers.summary: Existence of Double-Logarithmic (DL) contributions to scattering amplitudes in QED was discovered by V.V. Sudakov in 1956 and total summation of DL contributions to electron-photon scattering resulted in appearance of famous Sudakov exponentials. Then, thanks to contributions of V.G. Gorshkov, V.N.
