Gribov, G.V. Frolov and L.N. Lipatov, the pattern of calculations in Double- Logarithmic Approximation (DLA) was constructed. Since then, DLA has become one of basic ways of describing various high-energy processes in the framework of QED, QCD and theory of EW interactions. In the present paper, we remind the history of DLA and present a brief overview of application of DLA to various objects like form factors, scattering amplitudes, DIS structure functions.

authors.name: B. I. Ermolaev

papers.title: Possibility of the antibottom-strange molecular pentaquarks near $ B\Sigma$ and $ B^*\Sigma$ thresholds
papers.summary: The molecular states in coupled channel system of $B_s^0N- B\Lambda- B^*\Lambda- B\Sigma- B^*\Sigma$ are investigated within one-boson-exchange model that includes $S$-$D$ wave mixing and a tunable short-range $\delta(r)$ term. Bound, resonant, and virtual states are searched by analytically continuing the $S$ matrix in the complex energy plane. In the single-channel analysis, the $ B\Sigma$ and $ B^*\Sigma$ systems with $J^P=1/2^-$ and $3/2^-$ are found to be attractive and form three bound states with reasonable cutoff region, corresponding to $1/2^-( B\Sigma)$, $1/2^-( B^*\Sigma)$, and $3/2^-( B^*\Sigma)$ . When coupled-channel dynamics is included, these states evolve into near-threshold poles that produce enhancements in the $B_s^0N$, $ B\Lambda$, and $ B^*\Lambda$ invariant mass spectra. The pole below the $ B^*\Sigma$ threshold in the $J^P=1/2^-$ system depends strongly on the treatment of the short-range $\delta(r)$ term and becomes a virtual state when this contribution is removed, while the other two resonant poles and their line shapes are only moderately affected. The influences of $B^{(*)}\Sigma^*$ channels on these states are also investigated. For representative parameter region, the predicted masses of these states lie in the $6.44-6.70$ GeV region and have widths of a few to several MeV. The pole coupling and partial-width analyses indicate that the invariant mass spectrum of the $B_s^0N$ and $ B^{(*)}\Lambda$ channels are the best place to hunt the predicted states. These results support the existence of near-threshold molecular pentaquark $P_{ \bar b s}$ and provide useful guidance in future experimental searches.

authors.name: Jian-Kang Zhao, Nijiati Yalikun

papers.title: A Small-Throat Boundary Condition for the Tunneling Wave Function of the Universe
papers.summary: We propose a small-throat prescription for the wave function of a closed universe in the semiclassical approximation, motivated by the idea that universe creation may be obtained as the decoupling, or pinch-off, limit of a tunneling geometry connected to another universe through a small throat. Instead of retaining the parent-universe side explicitly, we describe the remaining half-geometry by a minisuperspace model with boundary conditions imposed at the throat. To model the finite throat, we introduce a small radiation component parametrized by $\epsilon$ in a closed minisuperspace model with a positive cosmological constant. The radiation term produces two turning points, an inner one $q_-\sim O(\epsilon)$ and an outer one $q_+\sim H^{-2}$, where $q$ is the square of the scale factor. Our prescription imposes the Neumann condition $\dot q(0)=0$ on the classical solutions and restricts the initial size $q_i=q(0)$ to the small-throat domain $0<|q_i|<\sqrt{\epsilon}/H$. This domain contains the inner turning point $q_-$ and excludes the unsuppressed outer-turning-point saddle at $q_i=q_+$. We choose the steepest-descent lapse contour through the inner tunneling saddle in the semiclassical approximation. Taking the limit $\epsilon\to0$ after this finite-throat saddle problem has been defined, the inner turning point approaches $q_i=0$, and the saddle action reduces to that of the standard tunneling saddle. Other choices of lapse contour can instead select Hartle-Hawking-type growing branches. In this sense, the tunneling exponent and outgoing WKB phase can be obtained as the limiting form of tunneling from an arbitrarily small universe, rather than by imposing a boundary condition directly at a vanishing geometry.

authors.name: Masaki Yamada

papers.title: Formation and scaling of $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings for global $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry
papers.summary: We numerically investigate networks of global $\mathbb{Z}_N$ strings with multi-string junctions in a scalar field model whose vacuum manifold is $\mathrm{PSU}(N)=\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathbb{Z}_N$. The construction of the model is motivated by the Higgs vacua of mass-deformed $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory, commonly known as $\mathcal{N}=1^*$ theory, and provides a tractable effective description of string networks with baryon-vertex-like junctions. We perform classical lattice simulations of the formation and evolution of these networks in a radiation-dominated universe. For $N=2,3,$ and $4$, the time histories suggest that the total winding-length density approaches approximate scaling over the simulated interval, with no evidence for frustration. For $N=5$ and $8$, we report densities at selected times. For the parameters studied, the density normalization grows approximately in proportion to $N^2-1$, while non-minimal-charge components remain subdominant.

authors.name: Masaki Yamada

papers.title: CFT-Inspired Two-Horizon Thermodynamics as a Diagnostic for the Bi-Hair Organization of NUT Charge
papers.summary: After decades without a fully self-consistent thermodynamic formulation, recent proposals for Lorentzian Taub-NUT spacetime have yielded several inequivalent descriptions, each satisfying its own first law and Smarr relation, leaving unresolved which formulation is physically preferred. In this Letter, we introduce a two-horizon diagnostic whose left- and right-moving thermodynamic temperatures are fixed via the harmonic mean relations before the thermodynamic variables are chosen. For uncharged Taub-NUT spacetime, the left-moving first law closes with the mass and NUT charge, whereas, within the restricted homogeneous class examined here, the right-moving first law requires an additional thermodynamic secondary hair $J_n = mn$. This result supports a bi-hair thermodynamic organization of the NUT parameter through $N = n$ and $J_n = mn$. Furthermore, this two-horizon framework offers a new opportunity toward addressing similar thermodynamic non-uniqueness in other two-horizon NUT-charged systems when the first law and Smarr relation alone do not identify a physically preferred formulation.

authors.name: Di Wu, Robert B. Mann, Shuang-Qing Wu

papers.title: Removability criterion for radiative corrections to the Starobinsky attractor in weakly nonlocal gravity
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate how the one-loop running of local couplings in weakly nonlocal, super-renormalizable completions of $R+R^{2}$ gravity affects the predictions of the Starobinsky model. Our study is motivated by the larger scalar spectral index $n_s$ preferred by recent data. For a canonical inflaton at first order in slow roll, we derive the response of the observables to an arbitrary fractional deformation $\Delta$ of the Einstein-frame potential $V$. We find that it is governed by $\mathcal{R}[\Delta]=(V/V')\Delta'$, and that the shift of the logarithm of the slow-roll parameter is twice the logarithmic derivative of the trajectory average of $\mathcal{R}$. This provides a test which requires one differentiation only. Deformations with constant $\mathcal{R}$, which we call removable, change the E-model exponent and shift $n_s$ at $O(\ln N/N^{2})$ only, where $N$ is the number of $e$-folds, while $\mathcal{R}\propto N^{k}$ gives $\Delta n_s=[2k^{2}/(k+1)]\mathcal{R}/N$. When the running is improved at the Einstein-frame Hubble rate, the renormalization-group time is half the logarithm of the tree-level potential and the gravitational flow is removable. Under a naturalness condition, a matching to the nonlocality scale yields $|\Delta n_s|\lesssim3\times10^{-4}$, a factor of about $30$ below the shift preferred by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). However, for a scale tied to the Jordan-frame curvature, the same flow is not removable and $\Delta n_s\simeq K/3$, where $K$ is a linear combination of the running parameters. Removability is a property of the flow together with the scale prescription. None of the deformations proposed since ACT DR6 that raise $n_s$ to the preferred value is removable. These results hold within a projected truncation of the local couplings and a first-order improvement of the potential.

authors.name: Ekapob Kulchoakrungsun, Phongpichit Channuie, Daris Samart

papers.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
papers.summary: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction \xi of the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming \xi\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.

authors.name: M. G. Belyakova, R. Nevzorov

papers.title: Fermion mass hierarchies in a three-generation Clifford model
papers.summary: We examine whether an algebraic model of three fermion generations based on the complex Clifford algebra $\mathbb C\ell(10)$, in which an $S_3$ family symmetry relates the generations, can reproduce the observed mass hierarchies of the charged leptons and down quarks. Taking the internal Gram matrix as the fermion kinetic metric, we show that the original Yukawa interaction, with complex coefficients, gives precisely those ordered mass triples $0\leq m_1\leq m_2\leq m_3$ for which $m_3\leq m_1+2m_2$. This restriction excludes the observed hierarchies in both sectors and persists when the right-acting Higgs operator is allowed to range over the full Clifford algebra. This obstruction motivates a second Yukawa contraction in which a projector, constructed from the difference between an internal charge operator and its family average, acts from the left. The resulting interaction preserves the gauge and family symmetries and uses the same three Higgs doublets. With both contractions present, there is a fixed coupling ratio at which the two successive mass ratios in a single sector become arbitrarily large along a real vacuum path. Separately, a rational interval calculation establishes that one real Higgs vacuum, with different coupling ratios in the two sectors, reproduces the chosen running masses of the charged leptons and down quarks. A softly broken three-doublet potential realises this vacuum as a global minimum at tree level. The additional neutral scalars have flavour-changing couplings, and their exchange at a common mass of $2000\,\mathrm{TeV}$ satisfies the neutral-meson mixing criterion and the $\mu\to3e$ contact-interaction test considered here.

authors.name: Ye Zhou, Niels Gresnigt

papers.title: Covariant linear response theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime
papers.summary: To overcome the failure of the conventional non-relativistic description of photon statistics in strong gravitational fields and for non-comoving observers, we develop a covariant theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime, starting from the relativistic Boltzmann equation and employing the relaxation time approximation. The transport coefficients are computed up to second order in the relaxation time. The results reveal novel phenomena absent in flat space. At second order, the gravitational field renders the transport coefficients tensor-valued and induces transverse particle and energy fluxes, analogous to the Hall effect in electromagnetism. Using the first-order results, we derive the relativistic generalizations of Fick's and Fourier's laws and obtain the radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks around Schwarzschild black holes. This provides a covariant description of radiative transport in strong gravitational fields for high-energy astrophysical applications.

authors.name: Jianan Wang, Long Cui, Bin Wu

papers.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
papers.summary: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $\gamma$, scaling as $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR). For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} - \beta_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $\beta$-$\gamma$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $\sigma_{2\gamma-\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $\sigma_{\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $\gamma$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $\sigma_\beta\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $\gamma$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $\sigma_{\gamma}\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.

authors.name: Mohsen Khodadi, Salvatore Capozziello

papers.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
papers.summary: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the R\'enyi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.

authors.name: M. A. Rajabpour

papers.title: Relic Neutrinos Probing Small Scale Primordial Non-Gaussianity
papers.summary: Relic neutrinos retain a record of electromagnetic entropy production after neutrino decoupling, probing primordial modes erased from the primary CMB. We derive the cubic photon number source from acoustic damping and its leading folded sensitive bispectrum window, with neutrino decoupling, thermalization, and acoustic coherence combined in a single response kernel. For excited initial states, this kernel filters the physical folded profile and yields a sharpness dependent transmission condition, directly connecting small scale primordial non-Gaussianity to relic neutrino capture rates.

authors.name: Suraj Gavhale, Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov, Oem Trivedi

papers.title: Propagation and horizon formation in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet scalar collapse. I. Characteristic conditions, bounds and formation
papers.summary: We study scalar collapse in five- and six-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling as an exact classical theory. On spherical scalar backgrounds, gravitational characteristic conditions reduce to inequalities in two local invariants. In five dimensions, they imply $R_h^2>\tilde\alpha$ for regular marginal spheres on the GR branch and the sharp Kretschmann bound $\tilde\alpha^2\mathcal R_{abcd}\mathcal R^{abcd}<28$ for nonnegative mass. Under the stated finite-domain hypotheses, spherical continuation places the first characteristic degeneration on a smooth background. Within this setting, a future marginal sphere formed while the characteristic conditions hold throughout the preceding evolution forces their later failure. For every allowed radius, separately chosen complete smooth data form marginal spheres with mass arbitrarily close to the sharp lower bound; in six dimensions both radius and mass can be arbitrarily small. At sufficiently large scale, complete nonspherical data with weak curvature contain marginal surfaces with prescribed $S^3$ metrics under a spectral condition. These surfaces are outermost and strictly stable. A separate Berger family has arbitrarily small area at one common ADM mass; formation from untrapped data remains open. Exact nonspherical developments have smoothly convergent initial data but tidal tensors that fail to converge to the reference values at a chosen time after the reference core loses hyperbolicity. Under local geometric uniqueness for developments of the same data on overlaps connecting the initial slice to the observers, classical existence on a common region and continuous dependence of the tidal tensor cannot both hold. The constructed solutions themselves extend smoothly. Fixed time averages converge on the controlled interval, but this does not establish a predictive effective-field-theory continuation.

authors.name: Cendikiawan Suryaatmadja

papers.title: Fractal phase structure of QCD under imaginary rotation
papers.summary: We show that in hot QCD rotating at an imaginary angular velocity $\tilde\Omega_I$, the angular velocity selects not only the temperature of the bulk but whether charge conjugation $C$ is broken there. For QCD at temperature $T$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta$, with $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi=p/q$ in lowest terms, the bulk far from the rotation axis is in the same thermal equilibrium state as nonrotating QCD at temperature $T/q$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $\theta'=q\theta+\pi(p+q+1)$; this follows from the Euclidean boundary conditions and locality alone, and holds nonperturbatively whenever the equivalent nonrotating system has a finite correlation length. Consequently, even at zero quark chemical potential, the bulk is placed at the Roberge-Weiss (RW) point whenever $p$ and $q$ are both odd, and $C$ is spontaneously broken there for $T>qT_{\rm RW}$, with $T_{\rm RW}$ the RW endpoint temperature. The bulks at $\tilde\Omega_I=2\pi/3$ and $4\pi/3$, for example, are both at temperature $T/3$, yet only the former can break $C$. The set of imaginary angular velocities at which $C$ is broken has a fractal structure: raising $T$ adds rationals of ever larger denominator. At irrational $\tilde\Omega_I/2\pi$ the bulk corresponds to zero-temperature QCD at any $T$ and remains confined.

authors.name: Rin Takada

papers.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Pleba\'nski--Demia\'nski spacetimes
papers.summary: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.

authors.name: Finnian Gray, Hryhorii Ovcharenko

papers.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
papers.summary: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about 6.6%.

authors.name: Jing Zhou, Ligong Bian

papers.title: A hyperbolicity obstruction near regular charged centers
papers.summary: A conserved charge creates a tension at a spherical center: the flux remains fixed while the area of the symmetry spheres shrinks. We ask whether curvature-dependent electromagnetic responses can reconcile bounded central curvature with hyperbolic propagation in four-dimensional Einstein gravity when both parity-even and parity-odd couplings are allowed. The background equations force a positive charge potential and its first curvature derivative to vanish at the central curvature endpoint. On branches with a positive electromagnetic kinetic coefficient and a positive effective gravitational coefficient, this endpoint flattening produces a physical extraordinary mode of the fully coupled equations whose squared angular characteristic speed is strictly below minus one at radii arbitrarily close to the center. Its characteristic cone has no hyperbolicity direction in common with the ordinary photon and graviton modes. The result requires no central curvature expansion, remains valid at points where the curvature Legendre Hessian vanishes, and extends to positive-definite mixing of finitely many Abelian fields. An exact analytic example with a nonlinear gravitational curvature sector admits a real, subluminal extraordinary photon cone near the center. In a fixed-action black-hole family, the obstruction extends outside the outer horizon over a near-extremal parameter interval.

authors.name: Ye Zhou

papers.title: Heavy Quark-antiquark Systems in a Galilean Covariant MIT Bag Model
papers.summary: This work presents a Galilean covariant extension of the MIT bag model to describe heavy quark-antiquark systems within a non-relativistic framework. Using a 5-dimensional formulation of Galilean covariance, a Dirac-like equation governing quark dynamics inside a confining bag is constructed, and the corresponding boundary conditions are derived. Analytical solutions for the spinor wavefunctions and eigenfrequencies are obtained. Numerical results show some agreement with experimental masses and hyperfine splittings for heavy mesons, particularly charmonium and bottomonium states. However, the approach is less reliable for light-quark systems, indicating the limitations of the non-relativistic approximation.

authors.name: G. X. A. Petronilo, M. V. T. Machado, R. R. Luz, A. E. Santana

papers.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
papers.summary: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

authors.name: Lillian Santos-Olmsted, Rebecca K. Leane, Carlos Blanco, John F. Beacom

papers.title: Vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models
papers.summary: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. In these scenarios, LHC data imply lower bounds on the predicted resonances below 2 TeV depending on the scenario. Using $WZjj$ production as a benchmark, we demonstrate that the tails of various distributions nevertheless show significant deviations from Standard Model predictions. This holds in particular for the case of longitudinally polarised vector bosons.

authors.name: Rosy Caliri, Manuel Kunkel, Werner Porod

papers.title: Unveiling the low- and high-energy frontier: a simultaneous SMEFT-PDF fit with parity violation
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive global analysis of Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operators utilising a diverse set of high- and low-energy experimental probes. By systematically matching the SMEFT to the Low-Energy Effective Field Theory (LEFT), we incorporate parity-violating observables into a global fit of 15 independent Wilson coefficients. This low-energy dataset, comprising parity-violation observables, neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decays, as well as leptonic and semileptonic kaon and pion decays, is combined with high-energy measurements including high-invariant-mass Drell-Yan data in both neutral- and charged-current channels, with the latter included for the first time, Higgs boson measurements, Electroweak Precision Observables (EWPOs) from LEP, and diboson production at LEP and the LHC. Crucially, this framework features a simultaneous fit of both the proton Parton Distribution Functions (PDFs) and the SMEFT Wilson coefficients using the public {\tt SIMUnet} framework. We quantify the direct interplay between SMEFT operators and hadron structure, demonstrating the robustness of the SMEFT bounds and the relative stability of the resulting PDFs with respect to the inclusion of SMEFT effects, with only a moderate increase in their uncertainties.

authors.name: Ella Cole, Tom Tong, Maria Ubiali

papers.title: WIMPs as FIMPs: the Inert Doublet Model and low-temperature reheating
papers.summary: Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) are conventionally assumed to acquire their dark matter relic abundance through thermal freeze-out. However, this association relies on assumptions concerning the thermal history of the early Universe. We revisit the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), a representative WIMP framework in which dark matter interacts with the Standard Model through electroweak gauge interactions, even when its Higgs-portal coupling vanishes. We demonstrate that sufficiently low reheating temperatures can prevent chemical equilibrium, allowing a genuine WIMP to acquire its relic abundance through freeze-in rather than freeze-out. Considering both instantaneous and finite-duration reheating, we identify different production histories, including freeze-out during radiation domination, freeze-out during reheating, and freeze-in with potentially significant annihilation backreactions. These scenarios open regions of the IDM parameter space that would otherwise be excluded by dark matter overabundance. Our results demonstrate that WIMPs can behave as FIMPs, depending on the thermal history of the Universe.

authors.name: Genevi\`eve B\'elanger, Nicol\'as Bernal, Andreas Goudelis, Alexander Pukhov, Thomas Reggio

papers.title: TeV-Scale Leptogenesis in the Linear Seesaw Framework
papers.summary: The linear seesaw mechanism relates the smallness of neutrino masses to the mass splitting within a quasi-Dirac pair of heavy neutrinos, thereby providing a natural framework for realising resonant leptogenesis at low energies. We investigate this possibility within its simplest effective realisation, in which neutrino masses are mediated by a quasi-Dirac pair at the TeV scale. We estimate the generation of the baryon asymmetry in the purely flavoured and strong-washout regimes, identifying phenomenologically viable parameter regions and benchmark scenarios in which the heavy-neutrino decays are dominated either by the SM Higgs doublet or by a second, leptophilic scalar doublet responsible for neutrino mass generation. We find viable leptogenesis solutions both near and away from the resonant maximum and discuss complementary phenomenological probes of the framework.

authors.name: A. E. C\'arcamo Hern\'andez, J. Echeverria-Puentes, Stephen F. King, Jos\'e W. F. Valle

papers.title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
papers.summary: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.

authors.name: Giorgio Arcadi, Michele Benaco, Mattia Di Mauro, Sami Nurmi, Kimmo Tuominen

papers.title: The Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at isospin density in closed form: what a regularization can change
papers.summary: At zero temperature, the mean-field thermodynamic potential of the two-flavour Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model at isospin chemical potential reduces to a divergent momentum integral of two quasiparticle levels. In practice this integral is cut off at momenta not far above the chemical potentials being probed. We evaluate it exactly, at an arbitrary cutoff, using the Hermite reduction. The result is an algebraic boundary term and three incomplete elliptic integrals, one of each kind. Their modulus, parameter and amplitude at the end of the path are fixed by the triangle formed by the two levels at zero momentum. The power divergences reside in the boundary term, while the remaining divergence is logarithmic: the momentum axis is an open path on an elliptic curve, and the ultraviolet is the puncture at which it ends. The closed form makes the role of regularization explicit. As the cutoff is removed, sharp and smooth cutoffs acting on the momentum alone differ only by an additive constant and by two terms that the vacuum inputs fix. The medium separation scheme reproduces the resulting potential up to an additive constant. By contrast, a cutoff applied separately to the two levels generates an isospin density below the onset of condensation and violates the Silver Blaze property. The closed form gives the state that continues the vacuum along the isospin axis without numerical momentum integration. With the same vacuum fit, a cutoff kept finite gives a visibly different state. The two differ by explicit terms that vanish only as the cutoff is removed: they are different models, not two regularizations of one.

authors.name: T. G. Khunjua

papers.title: Timelike electric dipole form factors of the baryon octet: short-distance kernels and baryonic rescattering
papers.summary: We calculate the leading-twist contribution of quark electric dipole moments (EDMs) to the timelike form factors of the baryon octet at the $J/\psi$ mass using lattice light-cone distribution amplitudes. For a strange-quark EDM $d_s$, the short-distance $\Sigma/\Lambda$ ratio is $-0.080^{+0.037}_{-0.098}$ over the lattice input ranges. This range lies above the nonrelativistic quark-model value $-1/3$. In the meson-exchange model, kaon exchange feeds the large $\Xi$ source into the $\Sigma$ channel and makes the $\Sigma$ and $\Lambda$ form factors comparable in magnitude. The short-distance $\Lambda$ form factor is about $5\times10^{-4}d_s$. The BESIII measurement then gives $|d_s|<1.3\times10^{-15}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at 95% confidence level. With rescattering at a $1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ cutoff, joint fits to projected $\Lambda$, $\Sigma^+$ and $\Xi$ sensitivities lower the $\Lambda$-only upper limits by more than 25% at BESIII and the Super Tau-Charm Facility. Renormalization-scale variation changes the projected limits by about a factor of two.

authors.name: Chao-Qiang Geng, Xiang-Nan Jin, Chia-Wei Liu

papers.title: Probing tensor-polarized gluon TMDs through \texorpdfstring{$J/\psi$}{J/psi} electroproduction off the deuteron
papers.summary: We investigate tensor-polarized gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs) in semi-inclusive $J/\psi$ electroproduction off the deuteron. At leading order in the color-octet channels of nonrelativistic QCD, we derive the cross-section contributions associated with longitudinal-longitudinal ($LL$), longitudinal-transverse ($LT$), and transverse-transverse ($TT$) tensor polarization and define ten normalized observables for unpolarized and longitudinally polarized electron beams. Using gluon TMDs obtained in a spin-1 spectator model, we study their $q_T$, $y$, $Q^2$, and collision-energy dependences. The observables involving $f_{1LL}^g$, $f_{1LT}^g+h_{1LT}^g$, and $f_{1TT}^g-h_{1TT}^{\perp g}$ depend directly on ratios of gluon TMDs. The moments involving linearly polarized gluons exhibit a common zero at $Q^2=M_\psi^2$ for the adopted long-distance matrix elements, whereas the beam-helicity-dependent sine moments probe the T-odd distributions $g_{1LT}^g$ and $g_{1TT}^g$. We present fixed-scale model estimates that neglect transverse recoil from soft radiation and quarkonium formation.

authors.name: Xiupeng Xie, Zhun Lu

papers.title: Strong First-Order Phase Transition in a Pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson Model
papers.summary: We propose a novel, calculable model for realizing strong first-order phase transitions in the early Universe, in which the phase transition occurs along a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson (pNGB) direction. The model involves two scalar fields whose interactions exhibit collective symmetry breaking, protecting the pNGB potential from quadratically divergent radiative corrections induced by these interactions. This structure allows strong first-order phase transitions to be realized without severe parameter tuning while maintaining perturbative control. We investigate the finite-temperature effective potential and bubble nucleation dynamics, identifying parameter regions where strong first-order phase transitions can successfully complete. The strength and characteristic time scale of the transitions are evaluated, and the resulting gravitational-wave (GW) spectra are computed. The predicted GW signals can fall within the sensitivity ranges of planned GW experiments.

authors.name: Yuichiro Nakai, Masanori Tanaka, Yaoduo Wang

papers.title: Emerging Topics for Hard Probes
papers.summary: These proceedings present a personal selection of emerging topics in jet and heavy-flavor physics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, based on a plenary talk delivered at Hard Probes 2026 in Nashville (USA).

authors.name: Carlota Andres

papers.title: Study of the $N^*(1535)$ and $N^*(1650)$ resonances from $\pi N$ $S_{11}$ scattering data and lattice QCD spectra
papers.summary: We investigate two of the lowest-lying odd-parity nucleon resonances, $N^*(1535)$ and $N^*(1650)$, within a nonperturbative Hamiltonian framework (NPHF). The coupled-channel model contains two three-quark bare states with total quark spins $1/2$ and $3/2$, together with four meson-baryon channels: $\pi N$, $\eta N$, $K\Lambda$, and $K\Sigma$. Constraints from SU(3) flavor symmetry and the bare-state spin wave functions are imposed on the bare-state-channel vertices and the channel-channel Weinberg-Tomozawa interactions. This substantially reduces the number of free parameters. We combine fits to infinite-volume $\pi N$ $S_{11}$ scattering data with finite-volume lattice QCD spectra. We use Hamiltonian eigenvectors to analyze the model-basis compositions. A contamination function then compares the resulting operator-mixing pattern with lattice correlation-matrix eigenvectors. Within the scenarios considered, both bare states and coupled-channel interactions play important roles in describing the two resonances. From our combined infinite and finite volume analysis, in contrast to conventional quark-model expectations, the spin-$1/2$ bare state is heavier than the spin-$3/2$ bare state. The contamination analysis is consistent with the associated operator assignment and with a recent analysis of the relativistic wavefunctions associated with these states. The symmetry-constrained NPHF provides a unified description of the two $S_{11}$ resonances. The combined analysis also constrains their model interpretation.

authors.name: Zhi-Xuan Li, Derek B. Leinweber, Anthony W. Thomas, Jia-Jun Wu

papers.title: Evolution and Prospects of Higgs Boson Searches Beyond the Standard Model
papers.summary: The search for Higgs bosons Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) began intensively at the Large Electron-Positron (LEP) collider (1989-2000), continued at the Tevatron (2001-2011), and entered a new era with the start of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in 2010. While the discovery of a Higgs boson in 2012 established the Standard Model mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking, it also opened a wide landscape of open questions that motivate ongoing BSM Higgs searches. This review traces the evolution of these searches across experiments, highlighting both experimental techniques and underlying theoretical ideas in an accessible manner. Emphasis is placed on how different collider environments shaped search strategies and how seemingly subtle experimental effects, such as small excesses, non-standard decay topologies, or suppressed couplings, can provide insight into the possible structure of extended Higgs sectors. By connecting historical developments with current analyses and future prospects, this article aims not only to summarise results but also to provide students and newcomers with intuitive insight into how Higgs searches are designed, interpreted, and continuously refined. It illustrates how experimental challenges translate into physics opportunities, thereby inviting the next generation of researchers to contribute to one of the central questions in particle physics: whether the Higgs sector is minimal or part of a more complex structure.

authors.name: Andre Sopczak

papers.title: Neutral and Charged Pion Modes in Magnetized Quark Matter with Chiral Imbalance
papers.summary: We investigate neutral and charged pion correlations in a two-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model at finite temperature in the presence of a uniform magnetic field and a prescribed chiral chemical potential $\mu_5$, using the mean-field approximation and the single-channel random phase approximation (RPA). The pion masses are defined by the selected positive-energy zeros of the real parts of the corresponding inverse propagators. We demonstrate that, at zero external spatial momentum, the complete Dirac trace in the neutral channel eliminates mixed-branch contributions, thereby precluding a finite-energy Landau cut. In contrast, the charged channel allows non-diagonal Landau-level transitions and exhibits both pair-production and thermal-scattering contributions. With increasing $\mu_5$, the neutral-pion mass exhibits only a weak variation at low temperature, while the rapid decrease of the mass shifts toward higher temperatures. The charged-pion mass decreases with increasing $\mu_5$ over the selected solution segments. This behavior may help account for the lattice QCD results. At zero temperature and fixed $\mu_5$, increasing the magnetic field lowers the neutral-pion mass but raises the charged-pion mass.

authors.name: Shijie Zhai, Lang Yu, Jie Mei, Mei Huang

papers.title: A billion colour states: exact soft-gluon evolution beyond leading colour for many-jet QCD
papers.summary: We present a new method, and its implementation, for constructing orthogonal colour bases and computing colour factors for any process with quarks, antiquarks and gluons, and use it to compute one-loop soft-gluon evolution exactly in full colour, keeping all colour interference. Each basis vector is labelled, independently of $N_c$, by the sequence of colour representations that appear when the partons are coupled one at a time. We derive a closed formula for the norms of the basis vectors, and colour operators act only on the part of a label between the partons involved, through small tables. Basis vectors can therefore be generated and used one at a time, without listing the complete basis: norms and matrix elements of single basis vectors are obtained for $10^4$ gluons in seconds. The same locality lets the soft anomalous dimension act on colour states without being stored. This allows optimised implementations on CPUs and GPUs, with which we evolve colour states exactly for up to fourteen gluons on a single GPU and for fifteen gluons, a colour space of $827\,888\,726$ dimensions, on a single compute node. We validate the basis and the evolution against independent codes and published results for processes with few partons, the only ones for which such results are available. We then measure the accuracy of leading colour as a function of the number of partons. For exclusive jet rates with a veto on soft radiation outside the jets, at a ratio of about 14 between the hard and the veto scale, leading colour overestimates the full-colour result by a median factor of 1.3 for eight partons, 1.8 for ten and 6.6 for fourteen. Pairs of hard jets are in a colour singlet with probabilities of several per cent, which vanish at leading colour. The formal $1/N_c^2$ suppression of subleading colour therefore does not make it small for many-jet final states.

authors.name: Bakar Chargeishvili

papers.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
papers.summary: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.

authors.name: Jialiang Shao, Andrea Addazi, Xinran Wang, Guanwen Fang, Yi-Fu Cai

papers.title: Infrared divergences in the $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s v^2)$ corrections to exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction
papers.summary: We investigate the infrared structure of exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction, $\gamma p\to J/\psi p$, up to relative order $\alpha_s v^2$ within the frameworks of generalized parton distribution (GPD) and nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization. By analyzing the singular loop-momentum regions, we extract the soft and collinear singular terms and identify residual infrared poles at relative order $\alpha_s v^2$ after QCD renormalization, collinear factorization into the GPDs, and NRQCD matching. These poles originate from incomplete cancellation of soft-gluon exchange between the heavy-quark pair and the target-collinear partons. We verify the pole coefficients through a complete one-loop calculation. We examine the local NRQCD operator basis and find no additional independent vacuum-to-$J/\psi$ matrix element that can absorb these poles. These findings motivate further investigation of factorization in exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction.

authors.name: Zi-Qiang Chen, Long-Bin Chen

papers.title: Neutron lifetime puzzle and Dicke coherence in spontaneous decays
papers.summary: The long-standing discrepancy between beam and bottle measurements of the free-neutron lifetime---known as the neutron lifetime puzzle---remains an open anomaly in nuclear and particle physics. Here, we investigate whether collective quantum synchronization via macroscopic Dicke superradiance can influence free-neutron decay or mediate the relaxation of hypothetical excited neutron states. We show that superradiance is fundamentally obstructed in standard three-body weak beta decay by continuous final-state phase space and fermionic antisymmetrization, and remains inactive in terrestrial ultracold neutron traps due to low particle densities, even within the Koch--Hummel excited-neutron model. Extending this analysis to the primordial plasma prior to Big Bang nucleosynthesis, we demonstrate that rapid $e^\pm$ collisional dephasing and intense thermal photon backgrounds prevent a superradiant purge and instead enforce thermal detailed balance. Consequently, across the entire parameter space unconstrained by terrestrial experiments, an excited neutron state inevitably thermalizes before weak freeze-out, increasing the effective neutron statistical weight and severely overproducing primordial $^4\text{He}$, thereby excluding the standard realization of the Koch--Hummel hypothesis.

authors.name: Z. K. Silagadze

papers.title: Package feyn.gle for drawing Feynman diagrams, version 1.2
papers.summary: As compared to the previous version, there is one backward-incompatible change and many new kinds of lines and other objects.

authors.name: Andrey Grozin

papers.title: Diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC
papers.summary: We compute the cross section for coherent diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral lead-lead and proton-lead collisions (UPCs) at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) within the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective field theory. We include both the exclusive production of a charm-anticharm pair and diffractive production with an additional semi-hard gluon, described in diffractive transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. We show that the diffractive channel, although suppressed by the strong coupling, dominates at large transverse momentum, where the exclusive channel is suppressed by color transparency. Furthermore, we quantify nuclear effects at the parton level with a nuclear modification factor $R_{pA}$ at fixed photon energy, which shows a mild suppression for the diffractive channel and an enhancement growing with transverse momentum up to about a factor of 2 for the exclusive one. We also use the diffractive cross section to correct our inclusive $D^0$ predictions to the CMS event selection, which requires the target nucleus to break up, and compare them with the data. Finally, we provide predictions for inclusive $D^0$ photoproduction in proton-lead UPCs.

authors.name: Paul Caucal, Patricia Gimeno-Estivill, Tuomas Lappi, Farid Salazar

papers.title: Pseudoscalar Yukawa Preheating via Effective Action Approach
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate helicity-dependent fermion production driven by a pseudoscalar Yukawa interaction within the one-loop effective action framework. By integrating out the fermionic fields and employing the Schwinger proper time representation, we derive an analytical expression for the fermion pair production probability near each zero crossing of the oscillating inflaton field. We further introduce a helicity transfer matrix to describe the evolution of fermionic modes through successive non-adiabatic production events. For an undamped inflaton background, the temporal symmetry around successive zero crossings leads to the cancellation of helicity-mixing contributions after an even number of events, preventing the accumulation of helicity asymmetry. We then extend the analysis to a damped oscillatory background, in which the decreasing inflaton amplitude breaks this temporal symmetry and modifies the transfer matrix at each crossing. The resulting non-commuting transfer matrices produce a persistent helical spectrum, as demonstrated by the probabilities as a function of momentum obtained after successive scattering events. A comparison with scalar Yukawa preheating further confirms the role of helicity mixing in generating the helical asymmetry induced by pseudoscalar mechanism. These results establish an effective action framework for studying helicity asymmetry during fermionic preheating and provide insight into the influence of the inflaton's dynamical evolution on particle production.

authors.name: Xi-Bin Li, De-Tian Zhao, Ke Fu, Jun-Yang Jiao

papers.title: Two-loop correction to the complex-bion amplitude in a quasi-exactly solvable sextic oscillator
papers.summary: In this study, a quasi-exactly solvable sextic potential is analyzed by two diagrammatic calculations. At positive coupling, factorization fixes the ground-state energy $E_0$ exactly and forces every perturbative coefficient to vanish. Using only Feynman diagrams, we verify this cancellation explicitly through third order. After continuation to negative coupling, the formal zero mode becomes nonnormalizable. A real instanton remains, but its one-instanton contribution to \(E_0\) vanishes. In particular, the leading shift in energy arises from a complex neutral bion. Taking an exact constrained family, we calculate its local median amplitude through two loops. The direct diagrammatic sum gives $c_{\rm 2L}^{\rm diag}=-0.750000(5)$, in excellent agreement with the exact-WKB value $-3/4$.

authors.name: Adrian M. Escobar-Ruiz

papers.title: Magic Production and the Fundamental Forces of Nature
papers.summary: Quantum magic is a resource for universal quantum computation and may also provide a probe of fundamental interactions. We study its production in forward scattering of two distinct Standard Model fermions in the chirality basis. In the single-mediator-exchange approximation, magic production vanishes for gluon, photon, W-boson, Higgs-boson, and graviton exchange. For Z-boson exchange in purely leptonic scattering, it also vanishes at $\sin^2\theta_W = 1/4$, close to the phenomenological value. By contrast, Z-boson exchange involving elementary quarks generally produces nonzero magic. These patterns raise the question of whether the construction of the fundamental forces encodes, at least in some channels, a tendency to suppress magic production.

authors.name: Jiunn-Wei Chen, Yu-Hao Li

papers.title: Few-gluon interactions in high-energy collisions
papers.summary: A conventional narrative developed for high energy heavy ion collisions prior to the RHIC program assumed hadron production dominated by hot and dense QGP formation, expansion and freezeout. Proposed diagnostics included detection of elliptic and radial flows via correlation and spectrum analysis and jet quenching in a dense medium via rescaled spectrum ratios. The validity of that narrative has come into question in recent years with detection of similar features in data from small collision systems. In response, several recent observations hint at a strongly modified narrative. Study of p-Pb spectra has revealed that the Glauber Monte Carlo estimation of A-B collision geometry is quite misleading. Collision geometry should instead be inferred by inverting ensemble-mean $\bar p_t$ data. A method has been developed to transform $v_2(p_t)$ data to quadrupole spectra $\bar \rho_2(p_t)$ that provide new insights into the true correlation mechanism. Accurate $p_t$-integrated $v_2$ vs $n_{ch}$ measurements for p-p collisions reveal a cubic trend suggesting a three-gluon interaction as the true mechanism. The p-p $v_2(n_{ch})$ trend has been generalized to describe all A-B collision systems in common in terms of an extensive measure $V_2^2 \equiv \bar \rho_0^2 v_2^2$ (number of correlated pairs). A similar program has been applied to jet-related contributions to spectra and angular correlations with a comparable result, a quadratic trend on $n_{ch}$ as expected for two-gluon interactions. Those new results suggest that the relevant data features actually represent multipole (color dipole and quadrupole) radiation from few-gluon interactions within a low-density system.

authors.name: Thomas A. Trainor

papers.title: Flavor-resolved screening length of a moving quarkonium in a lattice-calibrated holographic QCD plasma
papers.summary: We compute the screening length \(L_s\) of a moving heavy quark-antiquark pair in a lattice-calibrated Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton background for pure-glue, two-flavor, and \(2+1\)-flavor matter. Parallel and perpendicular orientations are considered at finite temperature, baryon chemical potential, and rapidity. \(L_s\) decreases monotonically with \(T\) and \(\eta\) in every flavor sector, and for the flavored systems also with \(\mu\). The perpendicular screening length is systematically smaller than the parallel one. At zero density and \(T=0.3\ \mathrm{GeV}\), the ordering \(L_s^{(N_f=0)}>L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\) holds in this calibration, and a lattice check of the static flavor dependence is proposed. At finite density the two-flavor and \(2+1\)-flavor curves cross along a line in the \(T\)-\(\mu\) plane; below the line \(L_s^{(N_f=2)}>L_s^{(N_f=2+1)}\), while above it the ordering reverses. The crossing follows from the competition between the two-flavor crossover temperature and the density coupling, and its location depends on the fitted parameters. These results provide a flavor-resolved reference for moving quarkonium screening in the baryon-rich regime probed by beam energy scans.

authors.name: Huwei Zhu, Zi-qiang Zhang

papers.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
papers.summary: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration $1/\beta$, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield $Y_X\simeq6.8\times10^{-3}(H/\beta)(T_{\rm reh}/M_{\rm P})^3$, where $H$ is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, $T_{\rm reh}$ the reheating temperature and $M_{\rm P}$ the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near $(H/\beta)M_{\rm P}/\nu^2$, where $\nu$ of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about $10^{17}$~GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.

authors.name: Cheng-Wei Chiang, Van Que Tran

papers.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
papers.summary: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $\beta$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $\sigma$, $\zeta$, and $\delta$, and vector fields $\omega$ and $\rho$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^\mu$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids interact only through gravity and are treated within a two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff formalism. We examine the resulting mass-radius relation and tidal deformability, along with the gravitational redshift, to investigate the effects of DM on neutron star structure and observable properties. The inclusion of $U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$ stiffens the EOS, whereas increasing the DM fraction generally softens the EOS and modifies the mass-radius relation, tidal deformability, and gravitational redshift. The magnitude and nature of these modifications depend on the DM particle mass and mediator interactions, which determine whether the resulting configurations exhibit compact DM cores or extended DM halos.

authors.name: Hrishika P, Arvind Kumar

papers.title: Pion scattering in finite volume within the Inverse Amplitude Method: Extension to moving frames
papers.summary: We study the leading exponentially suppressed finite-volume corrections to $\pi\pi$ scattering near threshold in moving frames. Using the one-loop Inverse Amplitude Method (IAM), we compute the $I=0$ and $I=2$ amplitudes in a box with total momentum $\vec P=2\pi\vec d/L$, including the left-hand cut and the $t$-, $u$-channel and tadpole contributions neglected in L\"uscher's quantization condition. We derive the resulting correction to the near-threshold energy levels and measure its size relative to the L\"uscher term. We find that it becomes comparable to the latter for $m_\pi L\lesssim 1.5$--$1.7$ at rest, and that it is larger in moving frames, reaching $m_\pi L\lesssim 2.8$ for $\vec d=[002]$. The corrections become negligible only for $m_\pi L\gtrsim 5$.

authors.name: Juli\'an A. S\'anchez, Raquel Molina, \'Angel G\'omez Nicola

papers.title: Towards a Global CE$\nu$NS Picture
papers.summary: We present a general framework for extracting and interpreting the Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering (CE$\nu$NS) differential cross-section from experimental data. A generalized parametric basis, constructed from common kinematic terms recurring in generalized neutrino interaction models, is employed to numerically constrain the shape and normalization of the observed CE$\nu$NS response. The framework was applied to the COHERENT CsI and liquid argon datasets using Bayesian inference, yielding normalization constraints comparable to those reported by the Collaboration while providing additional constraints on the correlated spectral shape. A combined analysis was also performed, exploiting the complementary sensitivities of the two datasets to constrain features of the differential cross-section that are less accessible to either dataset individually. The framework has been implemented in the open-source Julia package Newtrinos.jl, which supports modular forward modeling, parallel computation, and automatic differentiation.

authors.name: Heerak Banerjee, Philipp Eller

papers.title: Construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor of the Skyrmion coupled to additional dynamical degrees in the large-$N_c$ expansion
papers.summary: We formulate an order-by-order construction of a conserved energy-momentum tensor (EMT) in the large-$N_c$ expansion of the model where the Skyrmion is coupled to additional dynamical fields. We show that, expanding the equations of motion and the EMT in powers of $1/N_c$, the inclusion of the backreaction to the Skyrmion from the additional fields is essential for achieving the conservation law of the EMT, which is contrasted with the fixed-background approximation where the effects of backreaction are neglected. We apply the construction to the model for hyperons based on the Callan-Klebanov bound-state approach, where the antikaon is bound to the Skyrmion, to obtain the EMT up to next-to-leading order of the $1/N_c$ expansion. We explicitly show that the divergence of the EMT from the backreaction for the Skyrmion exactly cancels that of the kaon to achieve the conservation of the total EMT. We find that the conserved EMT gives a negative hyperon D-term whose magnitude is smaller than that of the nucleon D-term and radii of gravitational form factors for the hyperon smaller than those for the nucleon, which implies that the hyperon is more compact than the nucleon.

authors.name: Mitsuru Tanaka, Yasuhiro Yamaguchi, Masayasu Harada

papers.title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
papers.summary: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces. Unlike in previous works, we consider the full fifteen-layered setup of CANNEX, as opposed to treating the plate and wall as single uniform objects. Doing so revealed an increase in the induced chameleon pressure of up to $\sim 7 \%$. However, the resulting gain is insufficient to probe new regions of parameter space at the projected sensitivities.

authors.name: Chad Briddon, Mario Pitschmann

papers.title: A general formalism for electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon
papers.summary: We develop a general formalism for the electromagnetic production of two mesons on the nucleon, $\gamma_{\rm v}N\to\Phi_1\Phi_2B$, that can be used in single-channel as well as coupled-channel analyses over a wide range of energies. In the spirit of the decomposition introduced by Berends et al. for single-meson electroproduction, the hadronic current is expanded in a set of 16 gauge- and Lorentz-invariant matrices, four of which vanish for real photons. The corresponding Lorentz-invariant (Dirac) amplitudes can be obtained from any reaction model and are mapped onto 16 CGLN-like Pauli amplitudes, from which the five-fold differential cross section and its transverse, longitudinal, and interference response functions follow directly. Although these matrices are not all linearly independent, they follow directly from the covariant decomposition of the current, so the amplitudes can be read off from the Feynman diagrams and the observables take a simpler, more symmetric form. As a first application, we calculate the $\gamma p\to\pi^0\pi^0p$ and $\gamma p\to\pi^+\pi^0n$ reactions near threshold from tree-level nucleon Born terms. This example shows explicitly how the Dirac amplitudes are read off from Feynman diagrams and how gauge invariance, which is violated by the individual diagrams, is restored in the total amplitude and preserved when hadronic form factors are included. The formalism thus provides a versatile basis for future theoretical and phenomenological studies of double-meson photo- and electroproduction. A more complete abstract is provided in the paper.

authors.name: Reddy Malik Priandika, Samson Clymton, Terry Mart

papers.title: Light on GeV-scale seesaw
papers.summary: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. However, the tiny active-sterile mixing predicted by the minimal seesaw mechanism is expected to remain out of reach. Oscillation data require at least two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, which may couple to the photon through a transition dipole. Such a coupling can radically change the picture, both by strongly enhancing sterile-neutrino production and by opening new decay channels. We identify charged-lepton pairs produced by an off-shell photon as the most promising experimental signature. We show that the seesaw band can be probed by the T2K near detector for sterile-neutrino masses $m_N\lesssim 500$ MeV, and by SHiP for $m_N\lesssim 5$ GeV. For a sufficiently large dipole, $d\gtrsim (10~\mathrm{TeV})^{-1}$, SHiP can selectively measure decay channels that require nonzero active-sterile mixing. This would give rise to a distinctive hierarchy of signatures, providing a direct test of the seesaw mechanism.

authors.name: Enrico Bertuzzo, Michele Frigerio, Salvador Urrea

papers.title: Fermionic dark linear seesaw with an anomalous Majoron
papers.summary: We propose a minimal fermionic realisation of the $\textit{dark}$ linear seesaw with spontaneous breaking of lepton number. The small lepton-number-violating parameter responsible for linear-seesaw neutrino masses is generated radiatively by a $\textit{dark}$ sector consisting of a singlet and a doublet fermion, together with scalar singlets. The global U(1)$_L$ symmetry is broken to a residual $\mathcal{Z}_2$ under which the $\textit{dark}$ sector is odd. This breaking yields a Majoron $J$ and makes the lightest $\textit{dark}$ particle stable. The charged $\textit{dark}$ fermion acquires its mass solely from U(1)$_L$ breaking and thus induces an anomalous Majoron coupling to photons. Current bounds on this coupling exclude a massless Majoron for TeV-scale U(1)$_L$ breaking. We add a linear term that breaks lepton number softly and gives the Majoron a GeV-scale mass. Such a Majoron decays into two photons and can be probed at beam-dump experiments. We study the dark matter phenomenology, focusing on the case where the stable particle is a fermionic weakly interacting massive particle. We analyse how the framework can be tested through charged-lepton flavour-violating decays such as $\mu \to e\gamma$, which receive contributions from both the $\textit{dark}$ and the seesaw sectors. Moreover, both sectors enhance the Majoron couplings to charged leptons, so that the Majoron-emitting decays $\tau \to \ell J$ ($\ell = e,\mu$) typically exceed $\tau \to \ell\gamma$ by orders of magnitude and can probe parameter space beyond the reach of $\mu \to e\gamma$.

authors.name: A. Batra, H. B. C\^amara, F. R. Joaquim

papers.title: Diffractive Photoproduction of High $p_T$ Photons in Ultraperipheral Collisions at the LHC
papers.summary: We investigate diffractive photoproduction of large-transverse-momentum photons in ultraperipheral collisions at the LHC, considering different collision systems and alternative descriptions of the BFKL Pomeron. We estimate cross sections and differential distributions including NLO corrections to the BFKL characteristic function and assess the prospects for measuring this process in ultraperipheral pp, pPb, and PbPb collisions. We find that the cross sections are sizable, and that future measurements in this channel can help constrain BFKL dynamics and improve our understanding of high-energy QCD.

authors.name: Jo\~ao V. Bulh\~oes, Victor P. Goncalves

papers.title: Kaon-pair production with NNLO effects
papers.summary: The Monte Carlo framework McMule has been extended to support the processes $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ and $e^+\,e^-\to K^0\,\bar{K}^0$. Our results include NNLO initial-state QED corrections together with NLO mixed corrections. The latter are evaluated in the FsQED approach, using disperon QED. The implementation is fully differential and can be used with any kaon form factor. We present the total cross section for energies relevant to the CMD-3 experiment and observe very large corrections. For $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ we also present selected differential observables for energies around the $\phi(1020)$ resonance.

authors.name: Yizhou Fang, Sophie Kollatzsch, Adrian Signer

papers.title: A proposal for an LHC search for baryon number violation in complementarity with trilepton nucleon decay searches
papers.summary: We investigate the compatibility of existing limits on trilepton nucleon decay by the Super-Kamiokande (Super-K) experiment with Baryon Number Violation (BNV) at the TeV scale and motivate a dedicated search using existing data at the LHC. Working within an effective field theory framework, we derive model-independent constraints on higher-dimensional operators associated with $B - L/3$ conserving texture of BNV. We demonstrate that existing Super-K limits on loop-level trilepton nucleon decay provide significantly stronger constraints compared to tree-level charm-baryon decays induced by these operators. These constraints translate into bounds of $O(1-30)$ TeV on the BNV scale, leaving open the possibility of an LHC search for $B - L/3$ type BNV. Motivated by this complementarity, we investigate the collider phenomenology of a representative UV completion featuring an $s$-channel diquark resonance that decays into a leptoquark--dilepton pair, producing a distinctive final state containing an anti-top quark, two charged anti-leptons, and missing transverse energy. Our results indicate that, although same-sign dilepton searches by ATLAS and CMS already place indirect constraints on this model, a dedicated analysis based on the selection cuts we develop significantly extends the reach for our chosen benchmarks. In particular, using only Run 2 data, we demonstrate complementary reach to limits on trilepton nucleon decay searches set by the Super-K experiment and to the projected reach of Hyper-Kamiokande. The selection cuts are applicable beyond our representative model.

authors.name: Amit Bhoonah, Francis M. Burk, Da Liu, Tong Ou, Deepak Sathyan

papers.title: Photomeson-threshold origin of the TeV break in astrophysical neutrinos: Spectrum, flavor, resolved sources, and the ultrahigh-energy landscape
papers.summary:
IceCube observes a break near 30 TeV in the diffuse astrophysical neutrino spectrum. We interpret it as the photomeson ($p\gamma$) threshold. Accelerated protons interact with the soft x rays of accreting black holes through the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance. One kinematic relation sets the break energy from the target field's lowest photon energy, the seed scale $\varepsilon_0$. The measured break fixes $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.13$ keV and supplies the low-energy suppression no sum of falling power laws can produce. Building on the $\Delta(1232)$ identification of Khatee Zathul, Fang, Halzen, and Hooper and the single-source-class photo-pion fit of Winter, Fiorillo, and Buson, we give closed-form relations that invert the four broken-power-law parameters to the source physics with no remaining freedom, namely, $\gamma_2=s$ and $\gamma_1=s-(\alpha_x-1)$ ($s$, $\alpha_x$ the proton and target photon indices), and $E_{m br}\propto[(1+ ar z)\varepsilon_0]^{-1}$. The break width bounds the total smearing to $\sigma_s\le0.235$ dex (68% CL), no broader than redshift alone must make it, and the seed scale is the same across sources to within a factor $\lesssim$1.5, which mean-spectrum fits do not provide. Below-break neutrinos are predicted to come on average from higher redshifts than those above. The threshold also fixes the flavor and $
u/ ar
u$ composition, including the energy-dependent $ ar
u_e$ fraction and the Glashow-resonance discriminator of Winter et al., matching current flavor data. Inverted source by source, the relation gives each resolved IceCube source its target photon scale, from the keV coronae of NGC 1068 and PKS 1424+240 to the $\sim$20 eV jet of TXS 0506+056. That two-decade spread means they cannot supply the homogeneous break, which requires a separate, fainter population. KM3-230213A points to a warm-dust target, $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.02$ eV, unless cosmogenic.

authors.name: Vernon Barger

papers.title: Early Evolution of Strange Quark Stars Admixed with Fermionic Dark Matter
papers.summary: We study strange quark stars admixed with fermionic dark matter (DM) in three quasistatic stages of their early evolution: the neutrino-trapped stage, the heated stage after deleptonization, and the cold stage. Quark matter is described by the MIT bag model at finite temperature with thermal gluons, a repulsive vector interaction, and, in the first stage, trapped neutrinos. The DM is modeled as a cold, asymmetric gas of fermions with masses $m_\chi = 0.3$, $1$, and $3$ GeV, with and without a repulsive self-interaction, and interacts with the quark matter only through gravity. Using the two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we compute the structure, the maximum masses, and the tidal deformability of the stars in each stage for DM mass fractions $F_D$ up to $5\%$, and we follow individual stars at fixed numbers of baryons and DM particles. The effect of DM is nearly the same in the three stages: for $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the maximum mass by about $8\%$ and the tidal deformability of a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star by about $26\%$ in each stage, whereas the stage itself changes these quantities by only a few percent. Heavy DM forms a compact core; for $m_\chi = 3$ GeV without self-interaction, the mass limit of this core can set the maximum mass of the star. Light DM can form an extended halo, which does not increase the maximum mass for the fractions considered. For $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the largest baryon mass of a newborn star by about $0.23\,M_\odot$, but this limit increases from the neutrino-trapped to the cold stage in all cases considered, so that DM does not cause a delayed collapse to a black hole. In our model, pulsars of about $2\,M_\odot$ require a stiff quark equation of state and restrict the DM fraction to a few percent unless the DM is light.

authors.name: Rajasmita Sahoo, Mrutunjaya Bhuyan

papers.title: Regge-eikonal description of high-energy proton-proton elastic scattering: a single-channel Gaussian benchmark confronted with TOTEM data at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV
papers.summary: A single-Pomeron Regge Born amplitude with a Gaussian dependence on the momentum transfer is eikonalized in impact-parameter space, and the resulting single-channel, purely absorptive amplitude is evaluated in closed form. The total, elastic and inelastic cross sections and the forward slope are expressed through the entire exponential integral Ein(a) and a related series $I_1(a)$, and the closed forms are verified against direct numerical integration and against the weak-coupling Born limit. Two parameter choices are confronted with the TOTEM measurements at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. With the Donnachie-Landshoff trajectory and a normalization fixed at 7 TeV, the model gives $\sigma_{tot}=139.2$ mb against the measured $110.6\pm3.4$ mb and places the first diffractive zero at $|t|=0.244$ GeV$^2$ against the measured dip at 0.47 GeV$^2$. Calibration of the two parameters to the measured $\sigma_{tot}$ and $\sigma_{el}/\sigma_{tot}$ describes the differential cross section to within five per cent for $|t|\lesssim0.1$ GeV$^2$, but places the zero at 0.315 GeV$^2$ and overestimates the cross section at the measured dip by more than an order of magnitude. A single Gaussian opacity therefore cannot simultaneously accommodate the integrated cross sections and the position of the diffractive dip. Restoring the signature phase gives $\rho=0.098$, in agreement with the TOTEM and ATLAS measurements, and fills the zero without moving it; a two-component opacity reduces the excess at the dip from a factor of 15 to a factor of 2 without reproducing the dip-bump structure and the large-$|t|$ tail simultaneously; a two-channel Good-Walker eikonal on a Gaussian profile moves the minimum further away from the measured dip.

authors.name: Ji Li

papers.title: Exploring the phase diagram of dense and hot matter with HBT interferometry
papers.summary: We investigate the HBT radii of pions produced in Au+Au collisions at selected energies from the STAR-BES program, using an event-by-event hybrid model that combines AMPT initial conditions, 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic evolution with a QCD equation of state at finite baryon chemical potential, and hadronic transport with SMASH. The goal is to explore the source's space-time structure and its possible connection to the structure of the QCD phase diagram. The hybrid chain was first validated by comparing identified-particle spectra and anisotropic flow, yielding a globally consistent description of the experimental data, with more evident discrepancies at the lowest energies.

authors.name: Vin\'icius S. Fran\c{c}\~ao, Fr\'ed\'erique Grassi

papers.title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
papers.summary: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass.
