Its low nuclear mass leads to substantial recoil energy, limiting measurements with both molecular tritium ($T_2$) and atomic tritium bound to a substrate. With a beta-decay endpoint energy and half-life similar to those of tritium, but a much larger nuclear mass, $^{241}$Pu may offer an interesting alternative. Its principal challenge is background from the beta decay of $^{237}$U. We discuss strategies for suppressing this background and compare the projected neutrino-mass sensitivities of $^{241}$Pu and tritium as a function of the background suppression.

authors.name: Mustafa Anaam (Radboud University), Nicolo de Groot (Radboud University), Inge van Rens (Radboud University)

papers.title: Hadron spectroscopy of QC2D at finite density
papers.summary: We investigate the chemical-potential dependence of hadron masses in two-color QCD (QC$_2$D) at low temperature using lattice Monte Carlo simulations. We calculate all possible meson and diquark correlation functions, including disconnected diagrams, on a $32^4$ lattice at $T\approx40\,\mathrm{MeV}$. In the hadronic phase, we obtain a meson mass hierarchy similar to that of three-color QCD. After the superfluid transition, the ordering changes: the $\sigma$ and $a_1$ channels become lighter, while the pion mass increases with density. We also examine the diquark source dependence of the Nambu--Goldstone mode of $U(1)_B$ symmetry breaking and find an almost vanishing mass in the superfluid phase after extrapolation to zero source. Finally, we compare correlation functions for chiral partners and discuss indications of partial chiral-symmetry restoration. This contribution is based on our recent study of hadron spectra in dense QC$_2$D~\cite{Iida:2026dmw}.

authors.name: Kei Iida, Etsuko Itou, Kotaro Murakami, and Daiki Suenaga

papers.title: Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential
papers.summary: Superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes can produce clouds of ultralight bosons bound by the black hole's gravitational field. A binary companion can ionize these clouds by driving transitions into continuum states in the black hole's 1/r gravitational potential, extracting energy and angular momentum from the orbit. We investigate how a companion-sourced Yukawa interaction modifies this process. At weak coupling, the interference term between the gravitational and Yukawa transition amplitudes provides the leading correction to the ionization power. For the orbital frequencies here, an attractive interaction enhances continuum ionization and accelerates the inspiral, whereas a repulsive interaction has the opposite effect. At larger coupling, the pure Yukawa contribution to the ionization power becomes increasingly important and can compete with the gravitational contribution, particularly for lighter mediators. Comparing continuum ionization with off-resonant bound-state mixing, we find that continuum ionization can halt superradiant growth at a substantially smaller Yukawa coupling. At their respective critical couplings, the Yukawa interaction provides the dominant contribution to cloud depletion in both channels. Finally, we calculate the phase correction to gravitational waves due to continuum ionization and characterize how the chirp-rate response varies with frequency near the thresholds at which successive orbital harmonics open continuum-ionization channels.

authors.name: Yi Wang, Jiayi Yao

papers.title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
papers.summary: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.

authors.name: A. S. Dmitriev, D. G. Levkov, A. G. Panin, I. I. Tkachev

papers.title: Revealing Nuclear Shape through Identified-Hadron Flow Decorrelations
papers.summary: Relativistic nuclear collisions encode nuclear shape in collective flow, yet the potential of identified hadrons to disentangle deformation modes remains largely unexplored. Using event-by-event viscous hydrodynamics coupled to hadronic transport, we investigate momentum-dependent elliptic-flow decorrelations of pions, kaons, and protons in central $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions at 193 GeV and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions at 5.36 TeV. The identified species exhibit distinct momentum- and deformation-dependent responses, with nuclear-shape information persisting in their relative correlations even when individual deformation effects are weak. We introduce crossing coordinates $(P_{\rm cross},R_{\rm cross})$, defined by the intersection of pion-kaon and pion-proton flow-factorization ratios. Variations of quadrupole deformation and triaxiality generate distinct trajectories in the crossing plane, offering complementary constraints on both nuclear-shape parameters. The corresponding behavior persists in higher-moment correlations, while an energy comparison in Ne+Ne reveals the influence of collision dynamics. Our findings establish identified-particle flow decorrelations as a complementary approach to probing and constraining intrinsic nuclear geometry.

authors.name: Hadi Mehrabpour, Abhisek Saha, Li Yan

papers.title: Unbinned Likelihoods for Probability Densities with Poles
papers.summary: Unbinned likelihood fits to detector-level data become prohibitively expensive when narrow resonances interfere with a nonresonant amplitude. The convolution of the truth-level probability density with the detector resolution must then resolve the resonances, whose widths are much smaller than the resolution. We propose a simple approach that subtracts one simple-pole term per resonance from the probability density. This term captures the resonant contribution in closed form, and the smooth remainder is convolved numerically on a grid whose spacing is set by the resolution alone. The approach applies to multidimensional densities and to densities known only on the real axis. Using two benchmark problems, we quantify the accuracy, computational cost, and statistical impact of the approach. We emphasise that the subtraction is a general approach to the computational problems of unbinned likelihoods in the presence of poles in their probability density and that it is applicable to a wide variety of problems in experimental particle physics.

authors.name: M\'eril Reboud, Danny van Dyk, Matteo Verzeletti

papers.title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
papers.summary: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.

authors.name: Randall H. V. Pradinett, Theo F. Motta, Gast\~ao Krein

papers.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
papers.summary: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

authors.name: Ilumi Chavez, Aditya Ghosh, Chris Kelso, Dan Hooper, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Ethan O. Nadler

papers.title: Precise predictions for double-Higgs production via vector-boson fusion
papers.summary: Theoretical predictions with next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD accuracy combined with the next-to-leading order (NLO) electroweak (EW) corrections are presented for differential observables of the double-Higgs production process via vector-boson fusion. While the QCD corrections were previously known, the EW ones are computed here for the first time. The numerical results are obtained for a realistic experimental set-up at the LHC and are presented in the form of fiducial cross sections and differential distributions. Within this setup we find that the VBF approximation employed in the NNLO QCD correction is accurate at the sub-percent level. We find that the NLO EW corrections within the fiducial volume are $-4.8\%$, making them of almost the same order as the NLO QCD corrections. In some kinematic regions they can grow as large as $-30\%$ making them the dominant radiative corrections. When the EW corrections are combined with the NNLO QCD corrections we find a total correction of $-14.8\%$. The results presented here thus comprise the state-of-the-art theoretical predicition for the double-Higgs production via vector-boson fusion, which will be of value to the high-luminosity programme at the LHC.

authors.name: Fr\'ed\'eric A. Dreyer, Alexander Karlberg, Jean-Nicolas Lang, Mathieu Pellen

papers.title: Soft photon corrections in $B \to K^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ and $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda^{(\ast)} \ell^+ \ell^-$ decays
papers.summary: We calculate QED corrections to the semileptonic decays $H_1\to H_2\ell^+\ell^-$ where $\ell=e, \mu$ and $H_{1,2}$ are hadrons. The soft and/or collinear divergences are regulated in a gauge-invariant manner and demonstrably cancel, leaving behind a finite residue that depends on the (infrared) momentum cutoff below which a photon is considered to be indistinguishable. On resumming, the said sensitivity reduces drastically, {\em i.e.}, for the NLL result as compared to the NLO one. The overall correction is negative and its magnitude is larger for a lighter lepton. The corrections are presented for $B\to K^{(*)}$ and, for the first time, for $\Lambda_b\to\Lambda^{(*)}$ decays. Given that QED final-state radiation is routinely incorporated in experimental Monte Carlo simulations, for example through PHOTOS, our results provide an important theoretical framework for assessing the accuracy and limitations of these simulations and their impact on LFU observables such as $R_{K^{(*)}}$.

authors.name: Debajyoti Choudhury, Diganta Das, Jaydeb Das

papers.title: The Chiral Lagrangian of CP-Violating Axion-Like Particles
papers.summary: We discuss the construction of the most general CP-violating chiral Lagrangian for an axion-like particle (ALP). Starting with an effective Lagrangian containing light quarks and gluons, we provide its matching onto a chiral effective Lagrangian at $\mathcal{O}(p^2)$ described in terms of mesons and baryons, identifying the correspondence between the Jarlskog invariants of the two theories. After deriving the ALP interactions with mesons and baryons, we analyse a few relevant phenomenological implications such as the permanent electric dipole moments of nucleons and the CP-violating ALP and kaon decays.This work provides the necessary tools for further phenomenological analyses connecting low-energy observables with the couplings of the underlying ultraviolet complete theory.

authors.name: Luca Di Luzio, Gabriele Levati, Paride Paradisi

papers.title: Local-equilibrium theory of neutrino oscillations
papers.summary: Miscidynamics describes coarse-grained neutrino transport under the assumption that flavor mixing is in local equilibrium. Here we introduce the concept of turbulent flavor-wave viscosity and develop techniques for including it in miscidynamics. This extension of the theory is necessary when neutrinos develop weak flavor instabilities as a result of astrophysical driving. The flavor-wave dispersion relation is obtained using a new and more general form of linear analysis, which does not require small flavor coherence. Flavor-wave transport is then approximated using wave kinetics and geometric optics. We hypothesize that the dynamical emergence of local oscillation invariants restricts the extent of flavor thermalization. In this view, flavor evolution is sculpted by both entropy-increasing and order-promoting factors.

authors.name: Lucas Johns, Anson Kost

papers.title: Integrated subtraction terms and finite remainders for arbitrary processes with massless partons at colliders in the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme
papers.summary: We present integrated subtraction terms and finite remainders for arbitrary processes with massless partons at hadron and lepton colliders in the context of the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme. These results provide the very last ingredients needed to make this scheme a fully local, analytic and process-independent framework for treating infrared singularities at next-to-next-to-leading order in perturbative QCD. The explicit infrared finiteness of all required contributions, as well as their process-independence, puts these results on par with subtraction schemes developed for next-to-leading order computations and opens up a clear path towards the automation of next-to-next-to-leading order computations in QCD.

authors.name: Federica Devoto, Kirill Melnikov, Raoul R\"ontsch, Chiara Signorile-Signorile, Davide Maria Tagliabue, Matteo Tresoldi

papers.title: A Coupled Source Description of Pseudorapidity Distributions from RHIC to LHC: Emergent $1/\mu_B$ Scaling and Limiting Fragmentation
papers.summary: One of the most remarkable observations in heavy-ion collisions is the systematic regularity exhibited by pseudorapidity distributions of charged particles across collision energies. While single-source models fail at higher energies and independent multi-source approaches do not reproduce the central dip observed at LHC energies, a unified description across the full RHIC-LHC energy range remains elusive. These distributions from Au+Au collisions at RHIC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 19.6--200 GeV) and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76--5.36 TeV) are analyzed using a novel parametrization based on coupled Gaussian sources where the interaction strength is quantified by parameter $\lambda$. This coupled two-source model captures the interaction between forward and backward sources through the medium formed in the collision. Remarkably, $\lambda$ exhibits empirical scaling behavior resembling $1/\mu_B$, suggesting sensitivity to baryon stopping and the strongly-interacting medium. All fitting parameters follow systematic energy trends, with the peak-to-peak distance and chemical freeze-out temperature exhibiting identical exponential saturation patterns, indicating that geometric expansion and thermal evolution share a common underlying dynamics governed by QCD phase structure. Furthermore, the approach naturally preserves limiting fragmentation behavior across all energies, in contrast to independent source models that suggest its violation at LHC energies. Although the theoretical basis requires further investigation, these empirical correlations successfully unify charged particle production across nearly two orders of magnitude in collision energy, revealing fundamental connections to underlying collision dynamics.

authors.name: Neeraj, Md. Kaosar Ali Mondal, Amal Sarkar

papers.title: Event-by-Event Multiplicity Cumulants as Probes of Partonic Energy Loss and Phase Structure in Au+Au Collisions within a Modified HIJING Model
papers.summary: Event-by-event fluctuations of charged hadron multiplicity, net-proton, and net-electric charge are investigated in central Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} =$ 20-200 GeV using a modified HIJING Monte Carlo generator. The model incorporates QCD-inspired partonic energy-loss formalisms in hot (quark--gluon plasma) and cold media, reducing reliance on the default HIJING energy-loss parameter. At energies above 100 GeV/nucleon, multiplicity and net-charge fluctuations show sensitivity to the assumed medium properties, while net-proton results provide an additional comparison with available STAR measurements. By introducing a probabilistic distribution for a first-order phase transition, we find within the present modified-HIJING framework that multiplicity cumulant ratios ($\sigma^2/M$ and $S\sigma$) show a pronounced non-linear response to the adopted phase-allocation ansatz near the selected binodal energy, whereas net-charge and net-proton fluctuations remain relatively insensitive. Furthermore, expanding the kinematic acceptance enhances the sensitivity of multiplicity fluctuations to the selected transition region in the present phenomenological ansatz.

authors.name: Y. A. Rusak, L. F. Babichev

papers.title: Axionlike Particles and Lepton Flavor Violation in Muonic Atoms
papers.summary: We explore the potential of the Mu2e experiment to probe the lepton-flavor-violating process $\mu^- e^- \to e^- e^-$ in a muonic atom within a simplified axion-like particle (ALP) framework featuring flavor-violating $e$-$\mu$ couplings and a flavor-diagonal pseudoscalar coupling to electrons, which also allows for possible invisible ALP decays into a dark sector. We compute the ALP-mediated contribution to the transition rate and show that, at fixed couplings, the branching ratio increases for lighter mediators and scales as $(Z-1)^3$, favoring heavier nuclei. We compare the model against constraints from $\mu\to e\gamma$, $\mu\to 3e$, $\mu\to e\gamma\gamma$, $\mu\to e+\mathrm{inv}$, and muonium-antimuonium conversion, as well as from the anomalous magnetic moments of the electron and muon. Additional astrophysical and beam-dump limits on the electron coupling are also discussed. A key result is that $\Delta a_e$ provides one of the most stringent probes of the parameter space and, in the global scan, excludes the largest fraction of sampled points. After applying the laboratory constraints used in the scan, the viable branching ratio for $\mu^- e^- \to e^- e^-$ in aluminum drops to at most $\mathcal{O}(10^{-20})$, while the resonant region $2m_e<m_a<m_\mu-m_e$ is much more heavily suppressed. The highest achievable values are closely tied to $\mathcal{B}(\mu\to 3e)$ near its current limit, indicating that the upcoming Mu3e experiment will explore the most promising region relevant for this muonic-atom signal. Our analysis shows that, although a light ALP can parametrically enhance $\mu^- e^- \to e^- e^-$ at fixed couplings, existing bounds -- especially $\Delta a_e$, $\mu\to 3e$, $\mu\to e\gamma$, and muonium oscillations -- severely limit the observable rate.

authors.name: Girish Kumar, Alexey A. Petrov

papers.title: A High-Precision Statistical Analysis of the SN1987A Neutrino Temporal Distribution
papers.summary: The interpretation of the SN1987A neutrino data remains limited by significant absolute timing uncertainties across independent detectors and a long-standing tension in the angular distributions. This work presents a high-precision statistical framework that resolves these issues by formalizing the mathematical distinction between intrinsic and relative timing offsets (ITOs and RTOs). By performing a simultaneous $\chi^2$-alignment of the Kamiokande-II and Baksan data with the IMB clock, we systematically incorporate non-Gaussian statistical correlations, reducing the temporal uncertainty by two orders of magnitude to the sub-second level. The $\chi^2$-analysis shows that Baksan's absolute timestamps require an advancement of $30.4\,\rm s$, while those of Kamiokande-II require a delay of about $6.4\,\rm s$. Establishing this unified, high-precision timeline is critical to test the physical nature of the first Kamiokande-II event (K1), specifically whether its distinct angular features signal the onset of the prompt neutronization burst. Previous literature often assumes that K1 originated from inverse beta decay (IBD) on qualitative grounds. By contrast, our multidimensional likelihood analysis incorporates energy, direction, and MSW flavor-conversion effects to provide the first quantitative constraint on its origin. We find a likelihood ratio of 3-6 in favor of an accretion-phase $\bar{\nu}_e$ origin over a neutronization-burst origin, thereby turning a traditional assumption into a statistically bounded physical inference. This framework provides the most stringent constraints to date on the chronology of SN1987A and establishes a precise methodology for future multimessenger observations of Galactic supernovae.

authors.name: Riccardo Maria Bozza, Vigilante di Risi, Veronica Oliviero, Giulia Ricciardi, Francesco Vissani

papers.title: Forward hadron production in pp collisions at LHC energies from an event generator based on the color glass condensate framework
papers.summary: We investigate inclusive forward single-hadron production in high-energy proton--proton collisions using a CGC-inspired Monte Carlo event generator, MC-CGC. We carried out a systematic study of the sensitivity of the running-coupling Balitsky-Kovchegov (rcBK) evolution equation to its initial conditions by comparing three parameterizations: the McLerran-Venugopalan (MV) model and its two HERA DIS-constrained variants, MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$. Our results indicate that the current LHCb data favor the MV$^\gamma$ and MV$^e$ models, while the differences from the original MV model become more pronounced at higher transverse momentum and at mid-rapidity. As a complementary analysis, we also compared the dilute-dense (DHJ factorization) and dense-dense ($k_T$ factorization) frameworks. We found that the $k_T$ factorization framework provides a better description of the particle production spectra at mid-rapidity than the DHJ framework, where both the projectile and target are in the dense regime at LHC energies. Predictions for the FoCal measurements at ALICE, including the production of identified neutral mesons and jets, are also presented.

authors.name: Hirotsugu Fujii, Tetsufumi Hirano, Kazunori Itakura, Yasushi Nara, Shujun Zhao

papers.title: Modern Determination of Pion and Kaon Fragmentation Functions from SIA and High-Precision COMPASS SIDIS Multiplicities
papers.summary: We present two separate determinations of charged-pion and charged-kaon fragmentation functions (FFs), denoted HAPS-PiFF1.0 and HAPS-KaFF1.0, at next-to-leading order (NLO) and within a next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) perturbative QCD setup. The analysis combines single-inclusive electron-positron annihilation (SIA) data with charge-separated semi-inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering (SIDIS) multiplicities from HERMES and COMPASS. A central goal of this work is to incorporate the modern COMPASS SIDIS input, namely the COMPASS 2025 proton-target multiplicities and the COMPASS 2026 revised isoscalar-target multiplicities, into a common charged-pion and charged-kaon FF analysis and to assess their role in the resulting flavor separation. The revised isoscalar data supersede the earlier COMPASS measurements used in previous global fits. The charge-separated pion multiplicities provide important constraints on favored and unfavored light-quark fragmentation, while the kaon measurements enhance the sensitivity to light-quark, unfavored, and strange-to-kaon fragmentation channels. In both analyses, the gluon FF remains indirectly constrained in the present SIA+SIDIS framework and should be interpreted with appropriate caution. The extractions are carried out using the publicly available MontBlanc framework, and the resulting HAPS-PiFF1.0 and HAPS-KaFF1.0 replica sets are provided in the standard LHAPDF format.

authors.name: HAPS Collaboration, Maryam Soleymaninia, Hamzeh Khanpour, Hubert Spiesberger, Majid Azizi, Michael Klasen, Hadi Hashamipour

papers.title: Chirality Observables in Vector-Like Lepton Doublet Pair Production with Polarized Beams at a 3 TeV Lepton Collider
papers.summary: We study how pair production of a mass-degenerate weak-isodoublet vector-like lepton (VLL) depends on longitudinal beam polarization at the 3~TeV Compact Linear Collider (CLIC), for VLL masses of 1.1--1.4~TeV and mixing in the tau sector. The charged pair $e^+e^-\to\tau'\bar\tau'$ proceeds through photon and $Z$ exchange, the neutral pair $e^+e^-\to\nu'\bar\nu'$ through $Z$ exchange alone. For the baseline electron polarization $P_{e^-}=-0.8$, the tree-level rates at $\mvll=1.2$~TeV are 15.77~fb (charged) and 4.75~fb (neutral). For an optional positron polarization $P_{e^+}=+0.3$, the left--right configuration $(-0.8,+0.3)$ raises the two rates by factors of 1.95 and 1.38 relative to unpolarized beams. The charged--neutral rate contrast reaches $D_\sigma=0.546$ there, compared with $0.08$ for the opposite configuration, and the observed left--right asymmetries are 0.57 (charged) and 0.12 (neutral). These normalized quantities are independent of the VLL mass at Born level because both channels share the same phase-space factor. Unpolarized rates at a 3~TeV muon collider coincide with the unpolarized CLIC rates to within 0.2\%, as expected from lepton universality. A counting estimate gives a Gaussian separation of the two asymmetries of $Z_A\simeq9$ for a visible fraction of $10^{-1}$ and $Z_A\simeq2.7$--$2.9$ for $10^{-2}$ at $1~{\rm ab}^{-1}$. All results are tree-level, fixed-energy, production-level quantities; initial-state radiation, beamstrahlung, detector effects and backgrounds are not included, and no exclusion or discovery reach is claimed.

authors.name: Haroon Sagheer, Ijaz Ahmed, Jamil Muhammad

papers.title: Three-body forces in the quark model
papers.summary: We review the connection between constituent-quark Hamiltonians and QCD and investigate the long-standing difficulty of describing meson and baryon spectra with one common two-body interaction. A Hamiltonian calibrated to ground-state mesons leaves systematic baryon mass residuals, largest in the light-quark sector and decreasing toward heavier flavors. We show that a short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction substantially reduces this incompatibility. Mass-scaled finite-range profiles yield high-accuracy baryon spectra, whereas flavor-independent common-range profiles do not remove the residual flavor pattern. The result is tested on additional ground-state baryons outside the calibration set and through meson--baryon compatibility analyses across several alternative quark-model Hamiltonians. We also benchmark radial and orbital excitations to identify the regime in which a static compact valence Hamiltonian remains reliable, and provide explicit color-spin matrix elements for two- and three-body operators in baryons and multiquark configurations. Within the tested valence-space representations, the results indicate that a mass-dependent short-range connected three-quark interaction provides the missing contribution required for a consistent simultaneous description of meson and baryon ground-state spectra.

authors.name: Jongheon Baek, Aaron Park, Emiko Hiyama, Sungsik Noh, Hyeongock Yun, Kyong Chol Han, Su Houng Lee

papers.title: Strangeness, entropy, and chemical non-equilibrium from p+p to Pb+Pb: the $K^+/\pi^+$ horn on the system-size axis
papers.summary: The maximum ("horn") of the $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ excitation function in central Pb+Pb collisions near $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.6$ GeV is interpreted as the competition between strangeness production and the faster rise of entropy production at the onset of deconfinement. Statistical hadronization analyses by Letessier, Rafelski, and collaborators have shown that the horn is described quantitatively only if the light-quark phase-space occupancy $\gamma_q$ is free, with $\gamma_q$ near the pion condensation limit from 30$A$ GeV upward. We carry this analysis along the system-size axis provided by NA61/SHINE (p+p, Be+Be, Ar+Sc, preliminary Xe+La) and NA49 (Pb+Pb). Our main new result is the first non-equilibrium analysis, to our knowledge, of the Be+Be and Ar+Sc $4\pi$ multiplicities, published in 2021 and 2024: in Ar+Sc, chemical equilibrium of light quarks ($\gamma_q = 1$) is disfavored, but through the $K^+/K^-$ asymmetry rather than the pion yields, while the Be+Be data do not discriminate. For central Pb+Pb, our fits to the final NA49 data confirm the earlier result, most robustly at 30$A$-80$A$ GeV; the preference rests on the excess of produced hadrons per net baryon and on the Bose-Einstein enhancement of pions. Decomposing $\langle K^+\rangle/\langle\pi^+\rangle$ into strangeness and pion yields per wounded nucleon, we find that the step between Be+Be and Ar+Sc is carried by a doubling of strangeness per participant, whereas the horn appears only in Pb+Pb, where the pion yield per participant is suppressed at 20$A$-40$A$ GeV. Parton-hadron transport (PHSD) reproduces the Pb+Pb horn but predicts one also in Ar+Sc and Xe+La, where none is observed.

authors.name: Neeraj, Amal Sarkar

papers.title: Analysis of the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states in QCD sum rules
papers.summary: In the present work, we study the two-body strong decays of the hidden-charm pentaquark states with the quark content $uudc\bar c$ and the quantum numbers $I(J^P)=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{2}^-)$ in the framework of the three-point QCD sum rules. The initial pentaquark states are described by four local diquark-diquark-antiquark type interpolating currents with definite isospin. We construct the three-point correlation functions for the decay channels $P_c\to \eta_c p$, $J/\psi p$, $\Lambda_c\bar D$, $\Lambda_c\bar D^{*}$ and $\Sigma_c\bar D$, and derive the corresponding QCD sum rules for the strong coupling constants. At the hadron side, the correlation functions are expressed in terms of the hadron masses, pole residues, decay constants and strong coupling constants. At the QCD side, they are calculated by carrying out the operator product expansion with the full quark propagators, where the vacuum condensates up to dimension 10 are taken into account. After matching the two representations and performing the double Borel transformations, we extract the strong coupling constants from the selected Lorentz structures. With the obtained coupling constants, we evaluate the partial decay widths and discuss the possible assignments of the corresponding pentaquark states. The numerical results indicate that two of the compact hidden-charm pentaquark states can be related to the $P_c(4312)$ and $P_c(4457)$, respectively, while the other two lower-mass states may be regarded as possible hidden-charm pentaquark candidates to be searched for in future experiments. The present results may be useful for identifying the hidden-charm pentaquark states in future experiments.

authors.name: Zi-Hao Chen, Han-Xiong Huang, Jie Lu, Xiao-Song Yang, Zhi-Gang Wang, Guo-Liang Yu

papers.title: Measuring Dual-Superconductor Length Scales in the QCD Vacuum at HERA
papers.summary: In the dual-superconductor picture, the QCD vacuum behaves like a superconductor for chromoelectric fields, with characteristic penetration and coherence lengths. These scales have so far been studied primarily through lattice calculations of static flux tubes. We show that they are also imprinted on exclusive diffraction, where the transverse profile of a gluonic hotspot reflects the response of the vacuum to a localised colour source. Using the Clem vortex profile, we fit all 104 H1 and ZEUS measurements of exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction and find $\chi^2/{\rm ndf}=0.72$, the penetration depth $\lambda=0.19(2)~{\rm fm}$, the hotspot core size $\xi_v=0.087(14)~{\rm fm}$, and the Ginzburg--Landau parameter $\kappa=2.6(8)$, placing the effective vacuum description in the type-II regime. The corresponding vector mass $1/\lambda=1.03(11)~{\rm GeV}$ agrees with the lattice gluelump mass, and the extracted parameters reproduce the QCD string tension.

authors.name: Tobias Toll, Nahid Vasim

papers.title: Production of the weakly bound $T_{cc}^+$ state combining the coalescence model with its mass spectrum
papers.summary: We investigate the production of the doubly charmed molecular state $T_{cc}^+$ within the coalescence model. The formation probability is evaluated with the Wigner distribution function. In contrast to previous studies, which usually adopt a Gaussian wave function, we obtain the molecular wave function by numerically solving the coupled-channel Schr\"odinger equation with the one-boson-exchange potential fitted to the mass spectrum of $T_{cc}^+$. The resulting wave function is the universal form of a weakly bound $S$-wave molecule in momentum space (a Yukawa-type exponential in coordinate space), dressed by the dipole form factor of the OBE interaction, and is thus more suitable for such a state. As the input of the coalescence model, we use the transverse-momentum distributions of the constituent $D$ and $D^*$ mesons fitted to the ALICE and LHCb data, and also generated by PYTHIA for comparison. We compute the transverse-momentum distributions of $T_{cc}^+$ in $pp$ and Pb-Pb collisions. The two collision systems differ in which part of the wave function is probed: for the extended Pb--Pb source the universal pure-Lorentzian form suffices, whereas for the compact $pp$ source the short-distance part of the wave function, captured by the dipole form factor, becomes relevant. These results provide a theoretical reference for future experimental measurements of $T_{cc}^+$.

authors.name: Ao Wang, Yu-Shan Ren, Zhi Yang

papers.title: Inelastic Kinetic Decoupling in WIMP Leptogenesis: A Minimal $Z_4$ Model
papers.summary: We study a minimal $Z_4$-symmetric extension of the Standard Model in which a singlet Dirac fermion $\chi$ constitutes dark matter, whose annihilations generate a lepton asymmetry through WIMP leptogenesis. Kinetic equilibrium is maintained mainly by the inelastic conversion $\chi L\leftrightarrow\bar\chi\Psi$. Compared with the near elastic regime, a sizable mass gap suppresses the conversion rate more rapidly as the Universe cools. This naturally drives kinetic decoupling to earlier times, even away from resonance. Starting from the full inelastic collision operator, we derive an effective momentum transfer rate for kinetic decoupling. We then solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the dark matter abundance, its temperature $T_\chi$, and the $B-L$ asymmetry. Early kinetic decoupling can significantly modify the relic abundance, although near resonance this modification can be reduced by annihilation-induced heating. The $B-L$ asymmetry can be affected when asymmetry production overlaps with a substantial departure from kinetic equilibrium. In our scan, the largest deviations occur mainly for $x_{\rm lep}\gtrsim x_{\rm cd}$. After imposing our constraints, asymmetry production typically ends before chemical decoupling, leaving the final asymmetry essentially unchanged. For indirect detection, we generate the photon spectrum with Pythia and evaluate the Fermi-LAT dwarf spheroidal likelihood.

authors.name: An Liu, Hong-Hao Zhang

papers.title: RG evolution of the $B$-meson LCDA and radiative jet function at three loops
papers.summary: We calculate the three-loop evolution kernel of the light-cone distribution amplitude of the $B$ meson, together with the radiative jet function in the leptonic radiative decay $B^-\to\gamma\ell^-\bar\nu$ for the first time. Representing the light-cone distribution amplitude as the discontinuity of a matrix element containing an inverse differential operator, we compute the partonic matrix element in momentum space with a novel method of infrared subtraction. We show that its infrared singularities are governed by the same anomalous dimension as that of the heavy-light quark form factor, so that they can be subtracted without introducing any infrared regulator, thereby preserving gauge invariance and avoiding additional complexity in the Feynman integrals. Based on the renormalization-group invariance of the factorization theorem, we derive the renormalization factor of the radiative jet function, and confirm that it removes all divergences of the bare three-loop radiative jet function. Our results enable renormalization-group improved predictions for exclusive $B$ decays at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order.

authors.name: Ze Long Liu, Guang Tang, Zhe-Yu Wang

papers.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
papers.summary: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $\zeta_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

authors.name: Ke-Xin Zeng, Peng Cheng, Yang Yu, Daniele Binosi, Craig D. Roberts

papers.title: Search for Heavy Charged Higgs Bosons in Boosted Top and Bottom Quark Final States at a 1.4 TeV Future Lepton Collider
papers.summary: The discovery potential for heavy charged Higgs bosons $H^\pm$ decaying into a top-bottom quark pair is investigated at a future $e^+e^-$ collider operating at $\sqrt{s}=1.4~\mathrm{TeV}$. The study considers charged Higgs masses between 200 and 600 GeV within all four Yukawa types of the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM). The boosted $tb$ final state is explored using complementary cut-based and machine-learning analyses based on boosted decision trees (BDT). The expected signal significance and sensitivity contours in the $(m_{H^\pm},\tan\beta)$ plane are obtained for each Yukawa type. The resulting sensitivity extends to regions of the 2HDM parameter space beyond the projected reach of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC), demonstrating the complementary potential of a future high-energy lepton collider to probe heavy charged Higgs bosons.

authors.name: Majid Hashemi

papers.title: $X(2370)$ without exceptionalism from reanalyzing $J/\psi \to \gamma + 3P$ data
papers.summary: Motivated by recent BESIII claims that $X(2370)$ is a pseudoscalar glueball candidate, we reanalyze several radiative $J/\psi$ decays into three pseudoscalars, $J/\psi\to\gamma PPP$, with emphasis on the $X(2370)$ region. A simultaneous analysis of the three invariant-mass projections in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\eta^\prime$, including the pseudoscalar states $X(1835)$, $X(2120)$, $\eta(2225)$, $X(2370)$, $X(2500)$, and $\eta_c$, reproduces the observed dip near $2.2~\mathrm{GeV}$ and the enhancement near $2.4~\mathrm{GeV}$ through coherent interference, without invoking the additional broad $X(2800)$ component employed in the BESIII partial-wave analysis. We further analyze $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0\eta$ and $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ by including both pseudoscalar and axial-vector contributions, and show that multiple excited meson states collectively describe the data. The absence of a prominent $X(2370)$ signal in the $K^*(892)$ region can be understood from differing orbital angular-momentum requirements rather than flavor-singlet suppression alone. Our results indicate that $X(2370)$ is not exceptional compared with the other reported pseudoscalar states in this mass region. Therefore, interpreting $X(2370)$ as a glueball-dominated state should be treated with caution.

authors.name: Tian-Cai Peng, Xiang Liu

papers.title: Chiral QCD phase in equilibrium with Hadron Gas and the location of the critical point
papers.summary: We develop a description of the equation of state of QCD matter with restored chiral symmetry, which is in thermal and chemical equilibrium with the hadronic phase. The hadron gas is described with thermodynamically consistent volume corrections. The chiral phase is composed of a set of few quark condensates, each of which corresponds to a family of hadrons with specific quark content. On the boundary between the two phases we apply the requirement of conservation of particle numbers per family. We use lattice calculations for temperatures below the transition curve to determine hadronic volumes. We find that the pion system plays decisive role in the shift of the transition from higher order (crossover) to first order. For four volume models and five hadron sets we calculate the location of the critical point as function of critical temperature $T_c$ at vanishing baryon density. Among other acceptable solutions, if we additionally impose the equality between the densities of quarks contained in mesons and baryons, we find a critical point residing in the interval of baryon chemical potential $\mu_B \simeq$ 234-279 MeV and of temperature $T \simeq$ 148-156 MeV. We propose as signal of approach to the critical point the determination of the chiral pion mass through experimentally measured pion multiplicities in heavy-ion collisions.

authors.name: N. G. Antoniou, F. K. Diakonos, A. S. Kapoyannis

papers.title: CMB constraints on $U(1)$ axion warm inflation
papers.summary: In this work, we propose a model of warm inflation driven by axion-like particles interacting with $U(1)$ gauge fields, with implications for the early universe's thermal evolution. By extending traditional warm inflation models, we introduce a dissipation mechanism through the thermal fluctuations of electromagnetic fields, leading to a non-trivial back-reaction on the inflaton's dynamics. Our results are consistent with CMB observations, even for a natural sub-Plankian Axion decay constant $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$. We present precise constraints on the model's free parameters, using CAMB and CosmoMC codes. These findings offer new insights into the thermal history of the universe and the nature of inflationary dynamics.

authors.name: Asma Alaei, Sukannya Bhattacharya, Vahid Kamali

papers.title: Effects of dark dipole radiation on eccentric supermassive black hole binary inspirals
papers.summary: The final-parsec problem has long posed a central challenge in understanding the merger of supermassive black hole binaries. In this paper, we investigate a scenario in which a dark scalar or vector field is sourced by eccentric binaries, leading to accelerated mergers through additional dipole radiation, and thereby extending the range of masses for which the binary can merge within a Hubble time. The Newtonian-order radiation fluxes from an eccentric charged Keplerian binary are derived using general results for localized periodic sources in flat spacetime. We find that dipole radiation, although insufficient to fully resolve the final-parsec problem, can alter the low-frequency spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background from supermassive black hole binary inspirals. We construct a simplified model for the spectrum and perform a Bayesian analysis using the current pulsar timing array data.

authors.name: Mu-Chun Chen, Yan Cao

papers.title: How Bright in Gravitational Waves are Millisecond Pulsars for the Galactic Center GeV Gamma-Ray Excess? A Systematic Study and Implications for Dark Matter
papers.summary: The existence of dark matter (DM) is supported by various macroscopic observations, but its microscopic nature remains elusive. The Galactic Center GeV gamma-ray excess (GCE) has been a leading candidate signal for particle DM annihilation. However, an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the bulge provides the alternative explanation for the excess. Identifying these MSPs in electromagnetic bands is difficult due to source confusion, pulse broadening, and extinction. Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a complementary probe: a steadily rotating, non-axisymmetric MSP emits a nearly monochromatic GW signal in the sensitive band of ground-based detectors, with amplitude set by its ellipticity. In this work, we systematically investigate the GW emission from the MSP population proposed to explain the GCE and its detectability with current and future detectors. We consider three major scenarios for the origin of ellipticity and model the population properties of these MSPs. We also consider both isolated MSPs and MSPs in binary systems, as well as Doppler effects in the detection. We find that while the signal is below the reach of current interferometers, next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) may detect a fraction of those MSPs, offering a novel test of the MSP interpretation of the GCE. Future directed searches toward the Galactic Center may either uncover this long-sought MSP population or place stringent constraints on bulge MSP properties. Continued improvements in detector sensitivity will provide increasingly stringent tests of the MSP interpretation, with growing power to distinguish between the astrophysical and DM interpretations of the GCE.

authors.name: Ming-Yu Lei, Bei Zhou, Xiaoyuan Huang

papers.title: Characterizing entanglement dynamics in QED scattering processes
papers.summary: We study the entanglement among helicity degrees of freedom in quantum electrodynamics (QED) scattering processes at fixed momentum, modeled as quantum maps whose spectral structure determines the associated entanglement dynamics. We show that, for fermion-fermion scatterings, parity invariance preserves maximal entanglement and generically leads to entanglement saturation under iterations of the maps. The structure of the maps also provides an accurate description of the entanglement dynamics in processes involving both fermions and photons.

authors.name: Massimo Blasone, Silvio De Siena, Gaetano Lambiase, Bruno Micciola, Kyrylo Simonov

papers.title: Polarized Nuclear DVCS at the EIC
papers.summary: The Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will enable a series of measurements at unprecedented energies and luminosities, providing new opportunities to investigate the microscopic structure of nucleons and nuclei at small $x_B$. Exclusive processes such as Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering (DVCS) offer unique access to the three-dimensional structure of hadrons through Generalized Parton Distributions (GPDs), while polarized electron and ion beams further enable detailed studies of spin-dependent structure. A model for coherent DVCS on polarized $^3$Heis developed and applied to simulations of for $9\times166$-GeV $e^3$He collisions at the EIC. Using this framework, the statistical precision achievable is estimated for measurements of beam-spin asymmetries and for the extraction of the Compton Form Factors (CFFs) $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$. Early EIC data are found to enable precise differential measurements of the unpolarized CFF $\mathcal H_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ and to provide significant constraints on its real and imaginary components. By contrast, meaningful constraints on the polarized CFF $\tilde{\mathcal H}_{^3\mathrm{He}}$ require substantially larger integrated luminosities. The kinematics of the recoil $^3$He nucleus are also examined, and the advanced far-forward detector capabilities at the EIC required to tag the intact nucleus and perform fully exclusive measurements of coherent nuclear DVCS are discussed.

authors.name: Jackson R. Pybus, Xuan Li, Liliet Calero-Diaz

papers.title: Articulating Assumptions in AI-Generated Scientific Analyses through Task Decomposition
papers.summary: Scientific results produced by LLM generated analysis code must be understandable and reproducible. However, uncertainty can arise at different stages of the process, both in the original natural language specification and in the generated implementation. As a result, even executable code may not provide a clear understanding of which quantities are being computed or which assumptions determine the final results. To address this challenge, we introduce quantity grounded semantic differencing, a multi-agent framework for analyzing and comparing scientific programs generated by LLMs. The framework assigns code generation, execution, tracing, and validation to separate agents, allowing it to reconstruct how key output quantities are produced and to identify differences between the intended analysis and the implemented code. We also introduce a module that inspects ambiguities in the initial user instruction and suggests alternative rewrites before code generation. Its modular design enables application to different scientific domains by replacing domain specific resources while preserving the same workflow. We validate the framework on representative collider physics analyses. The results demonstrate that the modular task decomposition enhances both transparency and reliability relative to the previous single prompt approach, while enabling substantially smaller models to execute the complete workflow.

authors.name: Ahmed Hammad, Mihoko Nojiri

papers.title: Forward deuteron breakup on carbon and hydrogen: Coulomb effects and the high-momentum excess
papers.summary: We investigate whether recoil and the Coulomb interaction can explain the excess of protons at large longitudinal momenta in $^{12}$C(d,p)X. We calculate the spectrum in the Glauber--Sitenko model, retaining longitudinal momentum transfer and the transverse momentum of the detected proton. At a beam momentum of 9.1 GeV/c and a longitudinal proton momentum of 0.325 GeV/c in the rest frame of the incident deuteron, the invariant differential cross section with recoil is 2.8--3.6 mb/GeV$^2$, against 18.5 mb/GeV$^2$ in the published spectrum. The Coulomb correction to the channel sum is small in this region. Near the main peak at zero proton angle, the coherent cross section rises by 4--12%, while the sum of coherent breakup and neutron removal changes by less than 0.2% in the transverse approximation. At 3.5 GeV/c we compare the calculated carbon and hydrogen spectra with Sitnik's measurements for several transverse cuts. The effects considered here do not account for the high-momentum excess. Further observables are needed to establish whether it has a quark origin.

authors.name: Yaroslav D. Krivenko-Emetov, Boris I. Sydorenko

papers.title: Pretraining on boosted boson decays for polarization tagging of hadronic $W$ bosons
papers.summary: Longitudinally polarized weak bosons probe the unitarization of vector-boson scattering. At large boosts, longitudinal and transverse $W$ bosons produce jets with the same mass and two-prong structure, distinguished only by the decay angle. Longitudinal bosons are rare in $W$+jet events at these large boosts. We ask where the polarization information of a boosted $W$ boson lies and how much a tagger can recover. Requiring both decay quarks within the jet truncates the decay-angle distribution at an edge set by $m/(p_T R)$, which, as we show, bounds any hadronic polarization tagger. Within this acceptance, the decay angle carries nearly all the polarization information of a jet in $W$+jet events. Whether pretraining retains the decay angle is not obvious, so we pretrain a point-edge transformer on $10^7$ unpolarized boosted-boson, top-quark and QCD jets and fine-tune it with $10^3$ to $5\times10^4$ labeled jets per class. With the fewest labels, a boosted decision tree on substructure observables performs best; with the most labels, the strongest networks come within 0.003 in AUC of the ideal decay-angle tagger. Pretraining saves a factor of about two to three in labels, and our boson pretraining improves on a generic one by a few thousandths in AUC, more with frozen transformer blocks. Student networks with a few hundred times fewer parameters, distilled with unlabeled jets, match their teacher. More information lies outside the jet. The production angle, reconstructed with the recoiling jet, improves every tagger. In diboson production and vector-boson scattering at matrix-element level, the production kinematics carry more information than the decay angles of both bosons. Trading the generality of a jet tagger for an event-level tagger trained on the process thus brings large gains, which measurements of longitudinal vector-boson scattering could exploit.

authors.name: Saptaparna Bhattacharya

papers.title: Precision measurement of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering at a nuclear reactor by CONUS+
papers.summary: We report the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) from reactor antineutrinos, using the CONUS+ germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields a signal with high statistical significance, corresponding to $1565 \pm 155$ CE$\nu$NS events, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events within 0.5 $\sigma$. The flux-averaged cross section is $(0.57 \pm 0.09)\times10^{-40}$ cm$^{2}$, and the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV is $\sin^2\theta_W = 0.226 \pm 0.022$.

papers.title: Design of a Resonator Array Axion Haloscope and its Projected Sensitivity from 2 to 4 GHz
papers.summary: The QCD axion is a dark matter (DM) candidate particle which can also solve the long-standing strong charge-parity problem. The Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) searches for resonantly-enhanced conversion of axion DM into photons in a strong magnetic field. Previous versions of the experiment probed most QCD axion DM from 2.7 $\mu$eV to 4.2 $\mu$eV, with ongoing and planned runs poised to cover up to 8 $\mu$eV (2 GHz). We present the design of a haloscope with 18 cavities 1 m in length read out using individual low-noise amplifier chains and digital coherent signal combination called ADMX extended frequency range (EFR). We discuss details on magnet and cryogenic infrastructure, cavity design, cold electronics and efficiency of coherent signal combination. We use detailed cavity and electronics simulations, as well as diagnostic data from previous ADMX runs, to estimate frequency-dependent instantaneous scan rate. When paired with a comprehensive study of experiment downtime, a projection of final axion coupling sensitivity is produced. Under the stated assumptions, the projected sensitivity is projected to reach below the DFSZ axion benchmark model from 8 $\mu$eV to 16 $\mu$eV (2 GHz to 4 GHz) in 36 months.

papers.title: Lorentz-invariant fiducial decay selection for the ATLAS $H\to ZZ^{*}\to 4\ell$ STXS measurement
papers.summary: ATLAS measurements of Higgs boson production-mode cross-sections and Simplified Template Cross Sections (STXS), $\sigma\cdot B$, in the $H\to ZZ^{*}\to 4\ell$ decay channel rely on selection factors that fold in a decay-side fiducial acceptance evaluated with Standard Model decay kinematics. In an effective-field-theory interpretation that acceptance depends on the Wilson coefficients themselves. We recast these production-side $\sigma\cdot B$ results into a single Lorentz-invariant fiducial (LIF) decay region defined by the $H\to 4\ell$ decay, absorbing the EFT-dependent fiducial acceptance into the signal parametrisation, while the remaining reconstruction-efficiency corrections are shown to be largely EFT-independent. Using the Higgs boson signal Monte Carlo simulation at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 165 fb$^{-1}$, the LIF acceptance in the Standard Model is found to be $A^{LIF}_{SM}=0.8546$, production-independent to 0.07% and stable across STXS bins to 0.19%. Less than 1% of the reconstructed signal events originate from outside the LIF region, and the reconstruction efficiency for events in the region changes by at most 6% over the probed ranges of the EFT Wilson coefficients, as in the fiducial phase space of the published analysis. Consequently, the existing inclusive STXS cross-section measurements can be rescaled to the corresponding LIF fiducial phase space, allowing for EFT interpretations without EFT-dependent corrections for the reconstruction efficiency.

authors.name: ATLAS Collaboration

papers.title: Distillation of a Normalising Flow into a Compact Symbolic Expression for Real-Time Anomaly Detection at the LHC Level-1 Trigger
papers.summary: At the CERN Large Hadron Collider, anomaly detection techniques are becoming popular alternatives to traditional signature-aware new physics searches. For this approach to avoid any bias induced by the real-time event selection applied in the trigger system of ATLAS and CMS, it should be implemented before the first stage of selection, the Level-1 Trigger. This requires deciding to accept or reject each collision within a few microseconds, a latency budget that excludes the most expressive anomaly-detection models. Knowledge distillation has successfully addressed this issue by replacing a complex anomaly-detection model with a lighter student network. This work takes the compression one step further, distilling an anomaly detection model based on a normalising flow into an explicit mathematical formula. Using the SymbolNet symbolic-regression framework with adaptive pruning, the student is a learned functional form based on a chosen subset of the inputs, providing at once feature selection and compression through knowledge distillation. The final expression contains 577 operations and matches the teacher's discrimination on a test dataset, generalising to four benchmark new physics scenarios. Implemented on a Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ VU13P FPGA, the symbolic student has a nine-cycle latency, corresponding to 42.8\,ns at the post-route maximum clock frequency, and uses 0.81\% of the device's LUTs and 0.44\% of its DSP slices.

authors.name: Justin Bollhalder, Florencia Canelli, Valentina Guglielmi, Roope Oskari Niemi, Maurizio Pierini, Chang Sun, Francesco Vaselli

papers.title: Underlying-event properties in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV measured with the ALICE detector at the LHC
papers.summary: This contribution reports measurements characterizing the underlying event at midrapidity in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV, based on LHC Run 3 data collected by ALICE. The charged-particle number and summed transverse-momentum densities are measured as a function of the leading-particle transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}$) in the toward, transverse, and away regions, defined relative to the azimuthal direction of the leading charged particle. The particle densities in the transverse region are observed to increase steeply at low $p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}$, followed by a plateau for $p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}>5$ GeV/$c$. The results are compared with measurements at lower center-of-mass energies to illustrate the energy dependence of the underlying-event activity, and with predictions from PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4.

authors.name: Jes\'us Eduardo Mu\~noz M\'endez (for the ALICE Collaboration)

papers.title: Probing CP violation in weak radiative and dielectron decays of $\Lambda$ and $\Xi^-$ hyperons
papers.summary: The rare decays $\Lambda\to ne^+e^-$ and $\Xi^-\to\Sigma^-e^+e^-$ can serve as sensitive probes of $CP$ violation, especially that induced by interactions from beyond the standard model. We demonstrate that this is so because the dominant long-distance components of these processes provide sizable absorptive phases that can give rise to significant $CP$ violation via interference with potential new-physics effects. Treating the new contributions model-independently, we find that this leads to $CP$-odd rate asymmetries that are currently allowed by kaon and hyperon data to reach the 10% and 20% levels in the $\Lambda$ and $\Xi^-$ cases, respectively. Interestingly, we obtain comparable outcomes for the related weak radiative modes $\Lambda\to n\gamma$ and $\Xi^-\to\Sigma^-\gamma$. These results are testable at future high-statistics hyperon facilities.

authors.name: Xiao-Gang He, Jusak Tandean, German Valencia

papers.title: A Positron Spectral Dip near 20 GV in Selected Orbital Projections of AMS-02 Data
papers.summary: We analyze more than a decade of public Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS-02) data (2011-2021), matching daily electron and positron spectra to the orbital record on 3268 common dates. For each sky window we weight the spectra by the time the orbital zenith spends there and divide each rigidity bin by its all-date mean. At 16.6-22.8 GV, the normalized positron flux dips below its neighboring bins in several projections. At the Galactic center and the Crab, the positron dip exceeds the electron dip by $3.04\pm1.19$ and $3.57\pm1.22$ percentage points, respectively (statistical errors). A scan centered on 1177 Fermi-LAT catalog sources also finds dips at PKS~0301$-$243 and PKS~1424+240. At fixed rigidity, 13.8\% of trials that shift the spectra relative to the orbit produce a dip somewhere in the catalog at least as deep as the observed maximum. An isotropic intensity with the measured daily spectra reproduces every projection exactly. In a zenith pencil-beam model, direct positron annihilation on a common cold-electron column at the Galactic center and the Crab produces less than 0.10 percentage points of dip depth in either projection.

authors.name: Yi Yang

papers.title: Search for Axion-like Particles using Blazar Observations with the HAWC Observatory
papers.summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can mix with photons in astrophysical magnetic fields, modifying the propagation of very-high-energy gamma rays from distant blazars and producing an energy-dependent enhancement of the observed flux relative to the standard expectation from absorption on the extragalactic background light (EBL). We search for this signature through a joint likelihood analysis of seven TeV BL Lac objects at redshifts $z = 0.14-0.60$, combining approximately 3,000 days of HAWC observations with published High Energy Spectroscopic System (H.E.S.S.), Major Atmospheric Gamma Imaging Cherenkov Telescopes (MAGIC), and Very Energetic Radiation Imaging Telescope Array System(VERITAS) spectra. We find no statistically significant ALP signal and derive exclusion limits using the $\mathrm{CL}_s$ method. We exclude photon-ALP couplings at the 95% $\mathrm{CL}_s$ level down to $5.5 \times 10^{-12}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for $m_a \lesssim 4$ neV and $4.6 \times 10^{-12}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ near $m_a \approx 6-9$ neV. The systematic uncertainty on the excluded parameter-space area is $-36.5\%$ to $+32.6\%$, dominated by the choice of EBL model. Because the survival probability oscillates with the coupling, the excluded region is not simply connected, and we quote at each mass the lowest excluded coupling rather than an upper bound. The combined limit is set almost entirely by the highest-redshift detected source, PG 1553+113.

papers.title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $\sigma_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $\tau_R$ and $\alpha$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(\zeta/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.

authors.name: Allan E. F. G. Ferreira, Thiago S. Domingues, Matthew Luzum, Cesar A. Bernardes

papers.title: Transverse single-spin asymmetry of forward $\eta$ mesons in $p^{\uparrow}+ p$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 200$ GeV
papers.summary: Utilizing the 2012 transversely polarized proton data from the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider at Brookhaven National Laboratory, the forward $\eta$-meson transverse single-spin asymmetry ($A_N$) was measured for $p^{\uparrow}+p$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=200$ GeV as a function of Feynman-x ($x_F$) for $0.2=0.086 \pm 0.019$), agreeing well with previous measurements of $\pi^{0}$ and $\eta$ $A_N$, but with reach to higher $x_F$ and $p_T$. The contribution of initial-state spin-momentum correlations to the asymmetry, as calculated in the collinear twist-3 framework, appears insufficient to describe the data and suggests a significant impact on the asymmetry from fragmentation.

papers.title: Unsupervised Machine Learning for Anomaly Detection in LHC Collider Searches
papers.summary: Searches for new physics at the LHC at CERN traditionally use advanced simulations to model Standard Model and new-physics processes in high-energy collisions and compare them with data. The lack of recent direct discoveries, however, has motivated the development of model-independent approaches in HEP to complement existing hypothesis-driven analyses, particularly Anomaly Detection. A review of the latest efforts in BSM searches with anomaly detection is presented in these proceedings, focusing on contributions within the ATLAS collaboration at LHC and discussing Variational Recurrent Neural Network, Deep Transformer and Graph Anomaly Detection applications.

authors.name: Antonio D'Avanzo (on behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration)

papers.title: A Multimodal Domain-Adversarial Network for Fragmentation Background Suppression in AMS Heavy Nuclei Measurements
papers.summary: The Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer (AMS) aboard the International Space Station provides high-precision measurements of cosmic-ray nuclei fluxes from charge Z=1 to Z=28 and beyond. With negligible charge confusion from non-interacting nuclei, the precision of nuclei flux measurements is primarily limited by fragmentation backgrounds originating from heavier cosmic rays interacting within detector materials, particularly between tracker Layers 1 and 2 (L1-L2). As AMS extends its measurements to heavier and rarer nuclei, these fragmentation backgrounds become increasingly dominant, necessitating advanced background suppression methods. To address this challenge, we introduce a Multimodal Domain-Adversarial (MDA) neural network designed to effectively suppress these interaction backgrounds. The MDA model fuses heterogeneous data from the silicon tracker and time-of-flight detectors using specialized sub-networks combined via multi-head attention. Crucially, a domain-adversarial training strategy is employed to learn invariant representations, enabling the model, which is trained on Monte Carlo simulations, to be reliably applied to flight data. Using phosphorus (P) as a benchmark, we demonstrate its background suppression capabilities. This approach provides a robust, generalizable framework applicable to the measurement of other rare cosmic-ray nuclei with AMS.

papers.title: CKM determination from $W$ decays with jet flavor tagging at CEPC
papers.summary: This study investigates the sensitivity of the CEPC to CKM matrix elements $|V_{ij}|$ in semileptonic $W$-pair decays using simulated $e^+e^- \to W^+W^- \to \mu\nu \bar{q}q^\prime$ samples corresponding to $21.6\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$ at $\sqrt{s}=240\,\mathrm{GeV}$, with $|V_{ub}|$ not extracted because of the negligible expected $\bar{u}b$ yield. The projected statistical precisions reach $0.59\,\%$ for $|V_{cb}|$ and $0.01\,\%$ for $|V_{cs}|$, indicating that the CEPC can provide direct, high-precision, and largely model-independent determinations of CKM matrix elements from hadronic $W$ decays. The main sources of systematic uncertainty are discussed, and further improvements are expected from both experimental and theoretical developments, including dedicated data-driven calibrations of detector response and jet flavor tagging performance, as well as more precise higher-order calculations of the relevant electroweak and QCD corrections. Such measurements would provide stringent consistency tests of the Standard Model charged-current flavor structure and offer sensitivity to possible new physics effects through deviations from the Standard Model expectations.

papers.title: Charged-lepton identification at Belle II
papers.summary: Effective particle identification capabilities are a strategic priority for the physics program of the Belle~II experiment. We describe the algorithms used at Belle~II for identifying electrons and muons and separating them from charged hadrons. We present the performance obtained by the experiment during Run 1, which consists of 428 fb$^{-1}$ of data collected at the energy-asymmetric $e^+e^-$ collider SuperKEKB between 2019 and 2022 at center-of-mass energies near the mass of the $\Upsilon(4S)$.

papers.title: A First Indication of Low-Energy Solar Neutrino-Electron Scattering with PandaX-4T Run 2 Data
papers.summary: We report a search for the solar proton--proton ($pp$) neutrino flux via neutrino--electron elastic scattering using the PandaX-4T Run 2 data set collected between 2024 and 2026, corresponding to an exposure of 1.9 tonne$\cdot$yr. Before Run 2 data taking, the detector underwent a series of upgrades to improve its response and background conditions. Time variations of radioactive noble-gas impurities are constrained using the physics data themselves, complemented by measurements from the gas-assay system. The analysis introduced improvements in the data processing chain, detector response characterization, and background models. A blind spectral analysis was then performed on the electronic-recoil data across a wide energy range from 20 to 1000 keV. In combination with the Run 0 data published earlier, the pp neutrino flux is derived to be $(8.5 \pm 3.5)\times 10^{10}$ $\mathrm{cm^{-2}s^{-1}}$, consistent with the prediction of the Standard Solar Model. The combined dataset yields a $2.2\sigma$ statistical significance for solar neutrino-electron scattering, representing the first positive indication obtained using data below the Borexino analysis threshold of 165~keV.

papers.title: First measurement of the forward rapidity dependence of $W$ boson transverse helicity fractions
papers.summary: The transverse helicity fractions of $W$ bosons are measured as a function of the $W$ boson rapidity, $y_{W}$, in the range $0 \leq y_{W} \leq 5$ using $W\to\mu\nu_{\mu}$ decays in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV recorded by the LHCb experiment and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $5.1$ fb$^{-1}$. The fractions are extracted from a template fit to the muon transverse momentum and pseudorapidity. The results show a strong rapidity dependence and agree with next-to-leading-order Standard Model predictions, providing the first determination of the transverse helicity fractions of $W$ bosons in the forward region.

papers.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
papers.summary: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.

authors.name: Joe Wiedemann, Roman Kolevatov, Jianyang Fu, Joelle-Marie Begin, Nate Otto, Felix St-Amour, Lyman Page, Henry LeDuc, Peter Day, Saptarshi Chaudhuri

papers.title: Fermionic 2+1D SU(2) quantum link models: an ED/DMRG reliability study
papers.summary: Non-Abelian lattice gauge theory with dynamical fermions is a central target for tensor-network and quantum-simulation methods, but controlled reliability studies on small systems are scarce. We benchmark two complementary Hilbert-space approaches for a 2+1D SU(2) quantum link model with one staggered fermion flavour on small two-dimensional lattices: sparse exact diagonalization (ED) and matrix-product-state density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG). The link variables use the five-state $\{5\}$ truncation, and fermions are represented by two-colour four-state sites. We implement ED with explicit cross-site Jordan--Wigner strings and DMRG with total-fermion-number conservation and a matrix product operator (MPO) built from local terms. We validate the link algebra, Gauss-law commutation, Hermiticity, the pure-gauge limit, and the MPO against ED component by component. The $2\times2$ methods agree to $10^{-13}$ and the $2\times3$--$2\times5$ ladders are controlled at or below the $10^{-5}$ level. The $3\times3$ geometry illustrates the role of colour neutrality: at half filling the odd fermion number makes $G^2=3/4$ the exact lower bound, while one hole or one doublon restores neutrality and lowers the residual to $\sim2\times10^{-5}$ at $\chi=2048$. An independent exact-Gauss fPEPS provides a reference for the even-filling $3\times2$ sector. The results define a reproducible reliability envelope for non-Abelian gauge-fermion benchmarks and show where larger-scale simulations require larger bond dimensions or different tensor-network geometries.

authors.name: Daming Li

papers.title: Progress on finite temperature Sp(4) lattice gauge theory with matter fields
papers.summary: We explore the finite temperature behaviour of the Sp(4) lattice gauge theory coupled to two dynamical Wilson fermions transforming in the fundamental representation. The continuum theory provides a realisation of composite dark matter within the Strongly Interacting Massive Particle (SIMP) paradigm. Its thermal phase transition in the early universe might have generated an observable relic stochastic gravitational wave signal. Evaluating the sensitivity of future gravitational wave experiments to this signal requires knowledge of the strength of the phase transition. We explore the two dimensional parameter space of the theory, defined by the bare fermion mass and inverse gauge coupling. For this exploratory study we focus on lattices with a small number of sites in the temporal dimension. We analyse the finite volume scaling behaviour of Polyakov loop observables. Specifically the scaling of the peak of the susceptibility, informed by multiple histogram reweighting, is used to discriminate between the presence of a phase transition or crossover. In the light fermion mass regime we find strong indications of a crossover, while for heavy fermions we find preliminary evidence of a first-order phase transition. These findings motivate further studies of the continuum limit for this and other Sp(2N) gauge theories.

authors.name: Alexis Verney-Provatas, Chris Allton, Ed Bennett, Luigi Del Debbio, Ryan C. Hill, Deog Ki Hong, Jong-Wan Lee, C. -J. David Lin, Biagio Lucini, Maurizio Piai, Davide Vadacchino

papers.title: Identifying the conformal window by chiral phase boundaries
papers.summary: Once the number of massless fermion flavours reaches a critical value $N_f^*$, many-flavour QCD enters the conformal window, where chiral symmetry remains unbroken in the vacuum. At non-zero quark mass, chiral symmetry is explicitly broken, and thermal chiral crossovers can also occur for $N_f\geq N_f^*$. Their presence alone therefore does not distinguish a QCD-like theory from a mass-deformed conformal theory. They differ, however, in whether a thermal transition persists in the continuum chiral limit. To address this, we map out the chiral phase boundaries of unimproved staggered fermions in the bare lattice parameter space $(N_\tau,\beta,am,N_f)$, comparing $N_f=7$ and $N_f=8$. Our results indicate that the thermal chiral transition persists in the continuum chiral limit for $N_f=7$, whereas the massless continuum theory with $N_f=8$ remains chirally symmetric in the vacuum.
