Furthermore, we demonstrate that the pseudo-critical surface for eight flavours observed for finite quark masses is consistent with conformal hyperscaling, providing further evidence that eight-flavour QCD lies within the conformal window and suggesting $7<N_f^*\leq8$.

authors.name: Jan Philipp Klinger, Reinhold Kaiser, Owe Philipsen, Jonas Schaible

papers.title: Leading-order dynamical QED corrections to the thermodynamics of isospin-asymmetric QCD
papers.summary: We present a first lattice calculation of the leading-order effect of dynamical photons on the thermodynamics of QCD at nonzero isospin chemical potential $\mu_I$, across the onset of charged-pion condensation. In QCD this onset is a second-order transition, which dynamical photons are expected, on general grounds, to drive first order. However, a direct simulation is not possible since unequal quark charges render the QCD+QED action complex at nonzero $\mu_I$. We therefore expand the free energy density $f$ in the electromagnetic coupling $e$ around $e=0$, where the sign problem is absent. The leading-order expansion coefficient, $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$, is the convolution of the photon propagator with the electromagnetic current-current correlator, which we measure with a newly proposed planar source on existing (2+1)-flavor pure-QCD ensembles at nonzero $\mu_I$ and pionic source $\lambda$. At physical quark masses and a single lattice spacing, after extrapolating to vanishing $\lambda$, we find that $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$ is, within errors, independent of $\mu_I$ below the onset and rises sharply across it.

authors.name: Gergely Endr\H{o}di, \'Ad\'am Fischer, Wei-Ping Huang, Gergely Mark\'o

papers.title: Lattice Configuration Generation with a Self-Learning Diffusion Model
papers.summary: We show that a diffusion model for lattice field theory can be trained by self-learning, without configurations from a separate simulation, and used as the generator of an exact Markov chain. Training starts from exact samples at $\beta=0$, and along a ladder of couplings the model's own chain at each coupling, weighted by the action difference, trains the score at the next. A Metropolis-Hastings test on each proposal and its noising path keeps the sampled distribution exact for any network, so that network errors affect only the acceptance and autocorrelation times. In the two-dimensional compact XY model up to $\beta=1$, on the high-temperature side of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition, ladders at $L=4$ and $8$ reproduce exact and reference values of the energy density and helicity modulus at every coupling, and the generator trained from $\beta=0$ at $L=8$ has the same acceptance as one trained on an exact chain at $\beta=1$. The acceptance follows the relation known from hybrid Monte Carlo, with terms set by the number of noise levels and by the network error per site, and a network trained at $L=4$ generates up to $L=16$ when the number of levels grows with the volume.

authors.name: Akio Tomiya

papers.title: Unveiling the Eigenvector 1 Sequence in BZQ Blazars. I. Mg II and Ultraviolet Fe II Emission in the UV Main Sequence
papers.summary: We investigate the location of flat-spectrum radio quasars confirmed as blazars (BZQ-C), Fanaroff-Riley type II radio-loud (RL) quasars (FRII-Q), and radio non-detected quasars within the ultraviolet (UV) Eigenvector 1 (E1) plane defined by the Mg II line width (FWHM Mg II) and the UV Fe II strength (RFeUV). This represents the first systematic comparison of BZQ blazars with their proposed parent population in the UV E1 framework. To minimize selection biases, we construct statistically representative control subsamples and perform matched-subsample analyses in redshift and Mg II luminosity. Population differences are assessed using one- and two-dimensional non-parametric tests, including the Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling, Mann-Whitney U, and Fasano-Franceschini statistics. We find that the three AGN populations occupy statistically distinct regions of the UV E1 plane. The dominant separation is driven by FWHM Mg II, with BZQ blazars systematically exhibiting narrower line profiles than FRII-Q quasars, while radio non-detected quasars lie between both populations. In contrast, RFeUV provides only limited discrimination between the RL subclasses, although it separates radio-loud from radio non-detected quasars at the population level. The observed ordering demonstrates that the UV E1 plane preserves the physical sequence expected from RL AGN unification. Inclination-dependent projection provides a natural first-order explanation for the Mg II line-width ordering. Additional differences in intrinsic BLR structure or accretion properties may contribute to the observed distributions, although the present analysis does not allow these effects to be separated independently from orientation.

authors.name: T. M. Buendia-Rios, V. Chavushyan, V. M. Pati\~no-\'Alvarez, J. U. Guerrero-Gonz\'alez, M. Mart\'inez-Burelo, C. A. Negrete

papers.title: Why High-Spin Prograde MAD States Are Not Realized for AGN in Nature: Consequences for AGN Phenomenology
papers.summary: Quasar-like and other bright active galactic nuclei are typically radio quiet despite strong evidence that many host rapidly spinning black holes. In contrast, general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations show that high-spin prograde black holes in magnetically arrested disk (MAD) states produce the most powerful relativistic jets. We show that these results are not in conflict but instead correspond to physically distinct and mutually limiting evolutionary pathways. If accretion proceeds through radiatively efficient thin disks, then as the innermost stable circular orbit decreases with increasing prograde spin, radiative output and radiation pressure rise sharply, driving strong disk winds that remove the conditions required for effective jet formation. In this branch, high-spin prograde systems are therefore expected to be jet-suppressed. Alternatively, if accretion transitions to radiatively inefficient flows capable of producing MAD states, then the spin-up to near-maximal prograde rotation proceeds on timescales that exceed the age of the universe for the relevant systems, preventing the realization of the extreme high-spin prograde MAD configurations explored in GRMHD simulations. Within this framework, powerful jets need only be produced efficiently in counterrotating systems, not maximized there, preserving the time-dependent spin evolution central to the counterrotation versus corotation paradigm of Garofalo et al. (2010). We thus reconcile GRMHD results with observations and provide a unified interpretation of the radio-loud/radio-quiet dichotomy and the cosmic evolution of powerful radio sources.

authors.name: David Garofalo

papers.title: Spectral evolution and secular shift of the Z source GX 340+0: an interpretation in the spreading layer paradigm
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive spectral and timing study of the bright neutron star low-mass X-ray binary and Z source, GX 340+0, using broadband X-ray observations with AstroSat in 2020 and 2024, focusing on the evolution of physical parameters along the Z track and the origin of secular shifts of this track across different epochs. The spectra are consistently described by the same model, comprising blackbody emission from a spreading boundary layer near the neutron star surface, an accretion disk, and a Comptonizing corona. We observe a significant decrease in the blackbody temperature from ~1.2 keV on the horizontal branch (HB) to ~1.0 keV on the normal branch (NB), which likely contributes to the harder spectra on the HB and softer spectra on the NB. At the same time, the blackbody normalization varies substantially from ~440-860, indicating changes in the effective emitting area. Within the spreading layer framework, this evolution reflects changes in the extent of theradiating layer, while the large absolute normalization values suggest an additional contribution from the boundary layer. We also detect variations in the absorption column density, suggesting structural changes in the inner accretion disk, possibly linked to radiation driven puffing-up. The Comptonized flux shows a branch-dependent behavior, remaining relatively stable along the HB but decreasing along the NB. We interpret these results within a unified framework where the boundary layer, corona, and inner disk evolve coherently with accretion rate, explaining both the Z-track behavior and its secular shifts.

authors.name: Aman Kaushik, Yash Bhargava, Sudip Bhattacharyya

papers.title: Light Shining Through the Moon: A Lunar-Occultation Helioscope for Solar Axions
papers.summary: We propose a lunar-occultation helioscope in which the Moon suppresses the direct solar x-ray beam before solar axions enter the terrestrial magnetosphere, where they may reconvert into keV photons. We evaluate the conversion with a geomagnetic model combining the IGRF-14 internal contribution and the Tsyganenko T89 external magnetospheric contribution, retaining the two signed transverse components in the oscillation amplitude. As an explicit realizability test, we propagate a circular near-600-km polar orbit through the 12 August 2026 occultation. A $4'$-radius region around the solar center remains lunar occulted for about $470$ s while the sunward line of sight stays clear of the Earth; the coherent magnetic lever arm spans $69.1$--$96.4~\mathrm{T\,m}$ with $\mathcal I_{B,\mathrm{rms}}=76.9~\mathrm{T\,m}$. A B16-AGSS09 Primakoff calculation shows that this aperture contains $97.4\%$ of the 3--15 keV axion flux. For an explicitly specified NuSTAR-like detector benchmark, the propagated single-event exposure gives an expected low-mass 95\% C.L. sensitivity of $g_{a \gamma}=1.31\times10^{-10}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. The proposal therefore establishes the plausibility of a distinct experimental channel for solar-axion searches, characterized by a lunar-defined spatial and temporal window and by a predictable geomagnetic modulation. A future detection would additionally provide directional access to the axion-emitting solar core, opening a complementary probe of the solar interior.

authors.name: D. Su\'arez-Fontanella

papers.title: Making Reconnection Cooler: A relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics model for radiative collisionless reconnection
papers.summary: Relativistic magnetic reconnection around astrophysical compact objects is a likely site for particle energization and multiwavelength emission. Kinetic theory has substantially modelled such collisionless radiative relativistic reconnection using a radiative drag force countering the acceleration of the particles. Here, we systematically derive an energy-momentum sink term in relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD), informed by kinetic theory and coupled with a charge-starved resistivity prescription which reproduces the fast reconnection rate seen in kinetic calculations, to model radiative losses. We show that our radiative loss term accurately captures important macroscopic properties -- including the temperature in the reconnection layer and the bulk motion energy distribution of the out-flowing plasma -- for inverse Compton cooling applied to two-dimensional RRMHD simulations of a reconnection layer and benchmarked to kinetic simulations. Our results hold in various cooling regimes with a one-to-one mapping to kinetic theory. Our radiative model lays a foundation for future RRMHD simulations of plasma in the relativistic radiative regime, such as in reconnection sites in a local turbulent flow or globally in the magnetospheres of black holes and neutron stars.

authors.name: Alicia M. Savelli, Daniel Groselj, Bart Ripperda, Amir Levinson, Alexander Philippov, Norman Murray

papers.title: On the Sensitivity of Fermi-LAT Maximum Likelihood Stacking
papers.summary: Stacking sub-threshold gamma-ray sources has become common practice for understanding high-energy emission processes at the population level. In this procedure, one co-adds log-likelihood ratios, called TS values (TS = 2ln$(L_1/L_0)$), for a source class of interest. It is best practice to compare the population of sub-threshold targets against a population of control field test sources (CFs) selected to represent the unmodeled \gray\ background. Determining the significance of a TS measurement stack has typically been difficult. In this work, we find the necessary cumulative TS value ($\Sigma$TS) of a sub-threshold population of $N$ targets to achieve a $5\sigma$ separation from a like-sized population of CFs. We find that the $\Delta (\Sigma$TS) needed to achieve a $5\sigma$ separation is $\sim 70$. In taking this measurement, we characterize the source distribution corresponding to the measured $\Sigma$TS for a significantly detected stack and even predict new individual source detections in larger stacks.

authors.name: Owen K. Henry, Timothy A. D. Paglione, Joshua Tan, David Zurek, Thyra Eysselinck

papers.title: Tearing stability of pulsar equatorial current sheets
papers.summary: Harris-type current sheets have been studied extensively with particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. These local configurations generally contain no systematic magnetic-field component normal to the current sheet. Such a component develops naturally in a global pulsar magnetosphere because reconnecting field lines connect the northern and southern magnetic hemispheres. We investigate how the normal field component affects the tearing stability and dissipation of the pulsar equatorial current sheet, and we examine the consequences for the global magnetospheric configuration. We combine the tearing-stability condition for a current sheet threaded by a normal field with the electromagnetic relations imposed by the surrounding ideal force-free magnetosphere. We also formulate a dissipative equatorial boundary condition and incorporate it into a global force-free model solved with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). For realistic Lundquist numbers the normal magnetic field can suppress the tearing instability. Preliminary solutions indicate two distinct magnetospheric configurations: a nearly ideal CKF-like state with negligible equatorial dissipation, and a strongly dissipative state resembling the solutions of Contopoulos et al. (2014) and Cerutti et al. (2015). The reconnection rate in the pulsar equatorial current sheet cannot be inferred from local Harris-type current sheet calculations because it depends on the global magnetic topology. Present global 3D PIC simulations operate at effective Lundquist numbers far below astrophysical values, and may therefore exhibit tearing that in a real pulsar magnetosphere would be strongly suppressed.

authors.name: Ioannis Contopoulos, Spyros Rigas

papers.title: Probabilistic foreground diagnostics from dispersion measure excess in individual fast radio bursts
papers.summary: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide a unique probe of diffuse baryons through their dispersion measure (DM), but interpreting a large DM for an individual burst is limited by the uncertain contribution from its host galaxy, which is hard to directly observed. We address this gap with a source-level diagnostic framework that treats $\mathrm{DM_{host}}$ as a latent variable drawn from a shared lognormal population, thereby marginalizing over the uncertain host contribution. Applying an expectation--maximization (EM) inference scheme to 92 localized FRBs, we jointly estimate the host-DM population and obtain a model-conditioned host-DM distribution for each burst. We propagate these distributions into an excess cosmological DM for each sightline, quantifying both its uncertainty and the probability that a positive excess remains after accounting for the host contribution. FRBs previously reported to show evidence for foreground or intervening contributions preferentially exhibit high probabilities of retaining such an excess, indicating that this source-level probability can provide a useful statistic for prioritizing foreground follow-up observations. Using this diagnostic, we identify 18 additional localized FRBs as high-priority candidates for follow-up searches for possible intervening galaxies, groups, clusters, or large-scale structure.

authors.name: Qi Zhou, Ran Gao, Zhengxiang Li, Zong-Hong Zhu

papers.title: Probing Accretion Disk Dynamics of GS 1354-64: Insights from 2025$-$2026 Complex Outburst
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive spectro-temporal study of the 2025--2026 outburst of the Galactic black hole X-ray binary GS 1354$-$64 using observations from MAXI/GSC, Insight-HXMT, and NuSTAR. The source underwent a $\sim126$ day outburst characterized by an `unusual' sequence of spectral states driven by three short X-ray flares ($\sim2$, 5, and 7~days), likely triggered by episodic enhancements in the Keplerian flow. These flares produced rapid spectral softening and delayed the outburst decay. The MAXI/GSC light curves show soft X-ray dominance during the intermediate $\sim90$ days of the outburst. Corresponding minima in the hardness ratio and forward-to-backward loops in the hardness--intensity diagram indicate repeated spectral softening and episodic changes in the accretion flow. Low-frequency type-C QPOs exhibit a three-phase evolution, with frequencies increasing from $0.07$ to $5.76$~Hz, decreasing from $6.14$ to $3.26$~Hz, and rising again to $6.25$~Hz with a sporadic detection of type-B QPOs in the intermediate state. The propagating oscillatory shock model successfully reproduces this evolution through inward shock propagation during the rising phase, followed by rapid outward and gradual inward motion during plateau-1, tracing changes in the Comptonizing corona. Broadband ($2-70$~keV) spectral analysis reveals coupled evolution of the thermal (diskbb: $T_{\rm in}=0.25$--$1.04$~keV) and Comptonized (thcomp: $\Gamma_{\rm th}=1.69$--$2.66$, $f_{\rm cov}\sim0.02$--$0.97$) components. Relativistic reflection is well described by the relline model, while an additional powerlaw above $\sim50$~keV in the initial hard state suggests a high-energy component, possibly associated with synchrotron cooling. Strong correlations between QPO frequency, photon index, and hardness ratio constrain the evolution of the accretion flow geometry and Comptonizing corona.

authors.name: Dipak Debnath, Rahul Bhowmick, Hsiang-Kuang Chang, Anuj Nandi

papers.title: Updated View on Titan's Habitability: Interior and Surface Aqueous Environments
papers.summary: Saturn's moon Titan is the only world beyond Earth where abundant organic molecules and liquid water are expected to interact. Crucially, these interactions yield prebiotic molecules central to terrestrial biochemistry. Characterizing this prebiotic chemistry is one of the main science goals of NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission. Here we synthesize the current state of knowledge on the habitability and prebiotic potential of Titan's three aqueous settings: its interior hydrosphere, its putative cryovolcanic flows, and its impact-melt pools. For each setting, we identify the enabling factors and the principal bottlenecks that limit prebiotic complexification. Titan's interior is likely pervaded by liquid water in contact with organic material delivered from the surface and released from the core, though the longevity of its liquid water has recently been called into question. Cryovolcanic regions transiently expose surface organics to ammonia-bearing aqueous melts but are constrained by short freezing timescales. Impact-melt pools, by contrast, are warm and long-lived environments whose prebiotic chemistry is limited by the scarcity of ammonia. Dragonfly will return ground-truth data not only for Titan's habitability, but also for organic-rich aqueous environments across the Solar System and beyond. The years before its arrival are the last in which predictive work can still shape Dragonfly's investigations.

authors.name: Diogo Gon\c{c}alves, L\'igia F. Coelho, Catarina Miranda, Zita Martins

papers.title: From Surface Lakes to Subsurface Signatures in Antarctica with BIOMASS P-Band TomoSAR
papers.summary: Spaceborne remote sensing of the cryosphere is fundamental to map ice structure and dynamics. Accurate mass balance estimation requires a better understanding of melt/refreeze processes and firn hydrology, whereas spaceborne optical and Radar sensors are mostly limited to near-surface observations. The BIOMASS P-band Synthetic Aperture Radar, launched by European Space Agency in 2025, provides an unprecedented opportunity to gain a more direct access to englacial processes, thanks to the 70 cm wavelength paired with polarimetry, interferometry and tomography. This paper investigates subsurface beneath a region of historical supraglacial lake activity with BIOMASS tomography, at the Riiser-Larsen Ice Shelf in East Antarctica. The main result is that subsurface scattering appears to be related to historical supraglacial lake recurrence, with structural and depth variations over time. This suggests that recurrent supraglacial lake activity may leave persistent hydrological signatures within the firn. Overall, this study highlights the potential of gaining valuable insights into ice sheet hydrology with P-band.

authors.name: Francesco Banda

papers.title: Hot Jupiter TOI-1333 Ab is apparently aligned with its star's spin, but misaligned with its wide binary companion
papers.summary: We present the detection of the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect for TOI-1333 Ab, a short-period gas giant ($P=4.72$ days) orbiting one component of a wide stellar binary (570 AU). Planets in wide binary systems like TOI-1333 Ab offer an opportunity to not only test for alignment between the planet's orbit and the star's spin, but also the orbit of the binary companion. We use radial velocity observations from the Tillinghast Reflector Echelle Spectrograph (TRES) to measure an aligned projected spin/orbit angle of the system $\lambda = 7.74^\circ \pm 20.70^\circ$. However, the inclination of the wide binary companion shows a significant misalignment (likely more than $\approx 30^\circ$) with the planet's orbit, which makes understanding the formation of the system challenging. We propose three different explanations for TOI-1333 Ab's unusual architecture, but cannot confidently distinguish between them. Ultimately, more observations of similar systems are needed in order to understand how hot Jupiters in binary systems form, evolve, and impact their stars.

authors.name: Yadira S. Gaibor, Andrew Vanderburg, Jack Schulte, Joseph E. Rodriguez, Samuel N. Quinn, Juliette C. Becker, Perry Berlind, Allyson Bieryla, Michael L. Calkins, Gilbert A. Esquerdo, David W. Latham, Malena Rice, Benjamin Tofflemire, Jon M. Jenkins, Kevin Burdge, Sam Christian

papers.title: Quasi-hostless LRDs with intrinsically red, faint UV continua
papers.summary: High-redshift objects characterised by very weak UV relative to their strong, red rest-optical continua, with broad Balmer lines, appear to represent little red dots (LRDs) in their purest form: sources dominated by emission from their central engine (CE), sometimes dubbed black hole stars (BH*s). Previous work has selected BH*-dominated objects, where a BH* template dominates the rest-optical emission; this remains agnostic to the rest-UV. We therefore select low FUV-to-optical continuum ratio ($L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}6$ and one at $z\sim3$. The UV slope reddens as the NUV- ($L_{\rm 3500}$) and FUV-to-optical ratios fall, with $\beta_{\rm UV}$ rising from $-1.8$ at $L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}\sim 0.5$ to $-0.5$ at $L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}<0.03$, beyond values typically seen at these redshifts. As the UV-to-optical ratio weakens, gas-enshrouded BH emission appears to dominate, leading to the quasi-hostless regime: a weak, red UV continuum emerges alongside extreme Balmer decrements and weak forbidden line emission. This reddening could be reproduced by a simple model of a blackbody and hydrogen nebular emission leaking through a high column density screen of neutral hydrogen in the $n=2$ level ($N_{\rm H,\,n=2}\approx10^{17}\,{\rm cm^{-2}}$), combined with a relatively weak host galaxy, although alternative CE scenarios may also reproduce this reddening. The host galaxy's growing FUV contribution in this model results in a testable UV morphological evolution with wavelength. This work identifies a family of quasi-hostless LRDs that share a common, intrinsically red, rest-UV continuum originating from their central engine.

authors.name: Callum Witten, Andrea Weibel, Pascal A. Oesch, Rohan P. Naidu, Jorryt Matthee, Alba Covelo-Paz, Romain A. Meyer, Albert Sneppen, Parker Fairfield, Anna de Graaff, Christina C. Williams, Zhiyuan Ji, Pratika Dayal, Yoshinobu Fudamoto, Garth Illingworth, Cristian Carvajal-Bohorquez

papers.title: Resolved internal dynamics of a globular cluster candidate in a cosmological simulation at cosmic dawn
papers.summary: Globular clusters (GCs) are among the oldest and densest stellar systems in the Universe. Their compact sizes and old ages imply they must have assembled rapidly in the early Universe, yet the detailed physical mechanisms responsible for their formation remain uncertain. Although several scenarios have been proposed, cosmological simulations have so far been unable to resolve their detailed formation and internal dynamical structure at birth. Using a cosmological simulation that uniquely combines sub-parsec resolution with the formation of individual star particles, we follow the gravitational collapse and assembly of a compact stellar system with GC-progenitor mass and size, while directly resolving its internal dynamics and tracing the build-up of its angular momentum. The system assembles most of its stellar mass within 3 Myr, at $z\simeq10.5$, it rapidly becomes gas-poor, star-dominated, and develops ordered internal rotation acquired largely through the hierarchical assembly of distinct stellar subsystems. It forms as a satellite of a larger stellar complex within the virial radius of the $M_{\rm vir}\simeq1.73\times10^8\,M_\odot$ dark-matter halo hosting it. Its density, size and mass overlap with those of compact stellar systems recently observed by JWST at high redshift. These results indicate that GC progenitors can have well-defined internal kinematic structures already after their formation.

authors.name: Raffaele Pascale, Francesco Calura, Enrico Vesperini, Alessandro della Croce, Joakim Rosdahl, Alessandro Lupi

papers.title: Long-Term Evolution of Hills-Captured Stars with TDE Disk Collisions: Links to Repeating Nuclear Transients
papers.summary: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) and repeating partial tidal disruption event (rpTDE) candidates are widely interpreted as being powered by a star on an hours-to-years orbit around a massive black hole (MBH). Every such orbiter model presupposes a star delivered onto an extraordinarily compact orbit without being destroyed, but it is unclear whether this is achievable. We follow the coupled orbital and stellar evolution of stars captured by the Hills mechanism, combining gas drag and per-collision mass loss from recurrent TDE disks with gravitational-wave (GW) orbital decay and stochastic two-body relaxation in a Monte Carlo model. Conventionally, the EMRI-formation criterion is based on comparing the timescales of GW decay and orbital angular momentum relaxation. We find that this criterion severely overestimates the EMRI rate: for relaxation timescales shorter than a Hubble time, most Hills-captured stars are tidally disrupted before GW emission can circularize the stellar orbit. Instead, TDE-disk drag plays a crucial role in the orbital evolution and can boost the fraction of stars reaching QPE orbits by an order of magnitude or more, assuming that the disk aspect ratio is relatively large $H/r \sim 0.1$. We also find that collisional ablation imposes a minimum orbital period that rises with MBH mass and precludes sub-day orbits for $M_{\rm BH} \gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$, unless GWs alone can drive orbital decay faster than orbital relaxation. This can explain the observed preference of short-period QPEs for low-mass MBHs. Most known rpTDEs lie below the Hills-capture period minimum and thus require additional orbital decay, which TDE-disk drag can plausibly supply. These results support the viability of the orbiter model; our predictions of the MBH mass and orbital period distributions can be used to further test this model.

authors.name: Howard Hao-Tse Huang, Philippe Z. Yao, Wenbin Lu, Eliot Quataert

papers.title: Empirical Mass and Radius Relations for Main-sequence Stars from Detached Eclipsing Binaries
papers.summary: Detached eclipsing binaries have long served as fundamental calibrators for stellar models because they provide precise measurements of stellar masses and radii. Given a sample of detached eclipsing binaries, we can derive empirical relations between spectroscopic parameters (effective temperatures, surface gravities and abundances) and stellar masses and radii. We use a sample of 605 stars (330 with metallicities) in detached eclipsing binaries to update and refine these empirical models for main-sequence stars. An eight-term polynomial model reproduces the radii and masses of the eclipsing binary calibrators with an RMS scatter of $\sigma_{\log R} = 0.0161$ dex (3.8%) and $\sigma_{\log M} = 0.0322$ dex (7.7%), respectively. Most of this scatter is explained by the parameter uncertainties - the estimated intrinsic scatters in the radius and mass are only $\sigma_{\rm int}=0.0085$ and $0.017$ dex (2.0% and 4.0%). The predicted mass and radius of the Sun are $(1.028\pm0.004)\ M_\odot$ and $(1.014\pm0.002)\ R_\odot$. A 14-term model, while formally preferred, explains little more of the intrinsic scatter. We additionally provide the equivalent relations in terms of the mean stellar density instead of the surface gravity for use with exoplanet host stars. If we compare the 8-term model to MIST and PARSEC model stars with closely matched spectroscopic parameters, we find systematic differences. For example, the radii of hot (cool) stars are systematically over- (under-)estimated in both models by several percent.

authors.name: D. M. Rowan, C. S. Kochanek

papers.title: Scintillation arcs for fast pulsar binaries: the Double Pulsar
papers.summary: The double pulsar PSR J0737-3039A is a prime system for tests of gravity. A precise distance would strengthen these tests and also open up the possibility to measure the fast pulsar's moment of inertia, allowing a direct constraint on the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. Current parallax estimates from pulsar timing and very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) are in tension, which motivates complementary constraints. Information about distances is encoded in pulsar scintillation, but a complication for the double pulsar is that rapid orbital motion makes the interpretation difficult. We introduce an orbital motion ``resampling'' technique to overcome this complication, and use it to determine the properties of the principal scattering screen and the pulsar binary. Our fits yield a pulsar distance, of $781^{+62}_{-94}{\rm\,pc}$, in better agreement with the VLBI-based distance, but find that the nearly edge-on orbit precludes a precise measurement. For the principal screen, we infer a distance of $270^{+24}_{-23}{\rm\,pc}$, an orientation of $73.1^{\circ}\pm2.6^{\circ}$ E of N, and a transverse speed of $-15.2\pm1.0{\rm\,km/s}$. We also demonstrate the presence of a second screen, whose properties we can only partially determine: it is oriented roughly perpendicularly to the first screen and at a larger distance, of $\gtrsim\!547{\rm\,pc}$. To benchmark our technique and its uncertainties, we develop simulations of the system, generating artificial data that match the characteristics of the observed ones. We also discuss how future improvements to the method and use of the second screen could enable a more precise distance measurement.

authors.name: Diego Montalvo, Marten van Kerkwijk, Ashley Stock, Daniel Baker, Ue-Li Pen, Jacob Askew, Daniel J. Reardon, David J. Champion, Michael Kramer

papers.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.summary: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $\phi_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $\phi_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.

authors.name: Vikram Manikantan, Vasileios Paschalidis

papers.title: Fast Radio Bursts Co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 from 400 to 1530 MHz
papers.summary: We present a sample of $15$ fast radio bursts (FRBs) that were co-detected by the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-110) and the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) between 2022 and 2024, of which $12$ have channelized voltage data from both instruments and 9 have secure redshifts. All but one are as-yet-non-repeating. Most bursts span the entire bandwidth of each instrument (400-800 MHz for CHIME, 1280-1530 MHz for DSA-110), significantly expanding the number of FRBs known to emit across $>1$ GHz of spectral bandwidth and constraining the spectral evolution of energy and propagation effects. On average, the FRBs exhibit higher spectral energies (up to a factor of $\sim10$) in the CHIME band but are lower in peak flux density due to substantial pulse broadening. The sample mean (median) spectral index $-0.4\pm0.4$ ($-0.3\pm0.4$) is shallower than previously reported spectral indices, likely a selection effect. A third of the sample shows evidence for a spectral turnover, comparable to that seen in GHz-peaked pulsar and magnetar spectra. Joint scintillation and pulse broadening constraints indicate that nearly all bursts encounter multiple scattering screens, with pulse broadening originating within their host galaxies. The co-detected bursts are among the most scattered in the CHIME/FRB sample, while being the narrowest in the DSA-110 sample, indicating that CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 select different subsets of the FRB population; the interplay between intrinsic burst width, scattering, and the FRB search time resolution creates a narrow window of sensitivity to co-detected FRBs, providing a blueprint for future ultra-wideband FRB surveys.

authors.name: S. K. Ocker, K. Nimmo, J. Faber, K. Shin, V. Ravi, F. Verdi, N. Jain, Z. Pleunis, A. Pandhi, M. Sherman, D. Jow, S. Pradeep E. T., D. Amouyal, L. Connor, A. Curtin, M. Fine, B. M. Gaensler, J. W. T. Hessels, V. Kaspi, A. Khan, C. Law, R. Main, K. McGregor, A. B. Pearlman, M. Sammons, P. Scholz, K. Sharma, K. Smith, I. Stairs

papers.title: Spectropolarimetric properties of fast radio bursts co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110
papers.summary: We present spectropolarimetric analysis of twelve fast radio bursts (FRBs) co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110, eleven of which are apparently non-repeating. We obtain broadband spectral coverage (400-1530 MHz) for these FRBs and constrain propagation effects in their polarized spectra. We observe two notable spectral features: (i) in three FRBs, we find decreasing linear polarization fraction with increasing frequency and, (ii) in seven FRBs, we find that the linear polarization fraction decreases with decreasing frequency. The former spectral signature is commonly observed in radio pulsars and is suggestive of magnetospheric emission, where either the mixing of orthogonally polarized modes or incoherent summing of unresolved burst components may cause depolarization at high frequencies. The latter is consistent with depolarization due to multipath propagation. We report the first statistically significant correlation (3.5-3.9$\sigma$) between the extent of depolarization and amplitude of Faraday rotation arising from FRB host galaxies, implying that the two effects likely arise in the same turbulent, magnetoionic environments around FRB sources. The prevalence of depolarization in our sample suggests that turbulent environments that have, thus far, been predominantly associated with some repeating FRBs, may also be commonly present around a subset of apparently non-repeating FRBs. We highlight a systematic bias for detecting a disproportionately high fraction of constant polarization angle (PA) profiles in low-frequency FRB surveys due to amplified scatter broadening, which we also observe in two of our co-detected FRBs.

authors.name: Ayush Pandhi, Myles Sherman, Jakob Faber, Ziggy Pleunis, Kenzie Nimmo, Stella Ocker, Dylan Jow, Liam Connor, Alice P. Curtin, B. M. Gaensler, Jason W. T. Hessels, Victoria Kaspi, Afrokk Khan, Casey J. Law, Robert Main, Ryan Mckinven, Mason Ng, Aaron B. Pearlman, Vikram Ravi, Mawson Sammons, Paul Scholz, Kritti Sharma, Kaitlyn Shin, Kendrick Smith, Ingrid Stairs

papers.title: The FRB Population Revisited: Rate, Energy, Evolution, and Host-DM Constraints from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
papers.summary: We present a study that simultaneously fits for key fast radio burst (FRB) population properties using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog while calibrating for instrumental selection effects. Our inferred volumetric rate at $z=0$ is $1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\times 10^{5}\,{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ above an isotropic-equivalent energy of $10^{39}$ erg and below a scattering timescale of 30 ms at 600 MHz. The evolution of the FRB rate relative to the cosmic star formation rate remains statistically unconstrained. Assuming a Schechter function for the energy distribution, isotropic emission, and 1-GHz emission bandwidth, we find a characteristic maximum energy of $2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0} \times 10^{41}$ erg and a differential power-law index of $-1.41\,^{+0.27}_{-0.21}({\rm stat.})\,\pm\,0.35({\rm sys.})$. The host galaxy contribution to the observed dispersion measure (DM) is modeled as a log-normal distribution; assuming a total Galactic contribution of 80 $\text{pc cm}^{-3}$, we find a median host-galaxy DM contribution of $199^{+34}_{-36}\;\text{pc cm}^{-3}$ in the rest-frame. Finally, we find that the average FRB spectrum, described by a spectral index of $\alpha=-1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$, is inconsistent with being flat at the $\sim2\sigma$ level. We note an excess of high-S/N bursts at low DMs in the observed sample that is not predicted by the best-fit model. Testing alternative models does not alleviate this tension; future population studies may mitigate this limitation by incorporating robust fluence and redshift measurements.

authors.name: Naman Jain, Kaitlyn Shin, Mawson Sammons, Kyle McGregor, Victoria Kaspi, Kiyoshi W. Masui, Alice P. Curtin, Matt Dobbs, B. M. Gaensler, Jason W. T. Hessels, Afrokk Khan, Adam E. Lanman, Calvin Leung, Lluis Mas-Ribas, Daniele Michilli, Juan Mena-Parra, Kenzie Nimmo, Ayush Pandhi, Aaron B. Pearlman, Ziggy Pleunis, Aniket Prasad, J. Xavier Prochaska, Paul Scholz, Vishwangi Shah, Seth R. Siegel, Kendrick Smith, Ingrid Stairs, Habtamu Menberu Tedila, Michele Woodland

papers.title: Multiplicity of Normal A-Type Field Stars of Low Projected Rotational Velocity
papers.summary: While nearly all rapidly rotating (vsini > 120 km/s) A stars are observed to have normal spectra, a significant fraction (~43%) of slow rotators have peculiar spectra although many do not. For over 30 years, we conducted a radial velocity survey of 119 non-peculiar, slowly rotating dwarf or subgiant A stars. We determined orbital elements and related parameters for 43 systems and along with known visual binaries, common proper motion companions and stars with proper motion anomalies, find a multiplicity fraction of 0.64. We compared our results to recent findings concerning similar stars. We also examined whether the slow rotation of our sample of could have been caused by tidal interactions in short-period binaries. Of the 80 stars that we determined to be at least binary in nature or to show other evidence of having companions, only 6 have periods < 10 days. Thus, a large majority have periods that are much too long for tidal forces to have reduced their rotation rates while they are on the main-sequence. We also observed a small sample of rapid rotators (vsini = 125-230 km/s) over a shorter time interval to judge the accuracy of our measuring techniques on A stars with very broad lines. Orbital elements for 5 non-survey A-type stars, also with low vsini, are listed with our results, but are not included in the statistical discussion.

authors.name: Daryl W. Willmarth, Francis C. Fekel, Helmut A. Abt

papers.title: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
papers.summary: Recent observations of supermassive black hole jets extending up to the typical sizes of cosmic web filaments challenge our current understanding. In particular, the overall jet size of J152932.16+601534.4 ("Porphyrion") reaches $\sim 7$ Mpc at redshift 0.896. Magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) models of relativistic jets have never been successfully applied to such extraordinary distances, requiring demanding jet-environment and flow stability conditions. By using state-of-the-art numerical simulations of 3D relativistic-MHD jets, we show that Porphyrion's observational properties can be successfully modelled in a realistic scenario, involving a jet kinetic power of $3.5 \times 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and an external medium of a low-density galaxy group. We find that the pair of jets expands to $\sim 9$ Mpc in about $20$ Myr, implying that the jet grows with relativistic speeds for most of its evolution. Comparing this case with other jets of similar power propagating in substantially denser cosmic structures, we find much slower outflows that can only reach a few Mpc, consistent with the bulk of the observed population of giant radio galaxies. Our results make a testable prediction, i.e. future detections of even larger-scale jets in upcoming surveys and database searches will be invaluable in studying the demographics and feedback of the poorly known population of powerful jets, particularly in under-dense regions of the cosmic web.

authors.name: Gourab Giri, Marco Tavani, Dario Borgogno, Andrea Botteon, Rossella Cassano, Valerio Vittorini, Claudio Gheller, Gianfranco Brunetti, Paul J. Wiita, Tiziana Venturi, Bernie Fanaroff, Andrea Mignone, D J Saikia, Somak Raychaudhury

papers.title: The JWST Resolved Stellar Populations Early Release Science Program. X. Cross-Observatory Proper Motion Measurements with HST and JWST
papers.summary: We present the first absolute systemic proper motion (PM) of a galaxy measured by combining Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and JWST imaging. The PM of WLM, an isolated dwarf galaxy at $\sim$1 Mpc, is measured against background galaxies with Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) F814W imaging from 2015 and 2024 and NIRCam imaging from 2022 and 2024. The two ACS epochs give a systemic PM of $(\mu_{\alpha}^*, \mu_{\delta}) = (+0.087 \pm 0.019, -0.079 \pm 0.017)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 145 galaxies over 8.93 years, which agrees with previous Gaia-based PMs to within 0.4$\sigma$ and is the most precise PM of WLM. For the HST-to-JWST PMs, we fit each NIRCam detector separately, match the point-spread functions with empirically derived convolution kernels, and correct biases with injected galaxies. With an F090W second epoch, the PM is $(+0.081 \pm 0.045, -0.113 \pm 0.046)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 43 galaxies over 7.02 years, which, like the F150W PM, agrees with HST-to-HST over the same area to within 1$\sigma$, while F200W differs by $\sim$2$\sigma$. The long-wavelength F250M and F430M PMs are consistent to within 1$\sigma$, though less precise. Fewer galaxies can be used at wavelengths farther from F814W. A cross-observatory systematic of $\sim$0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ cannot be ruled out over 7 years. At equal baselines, an F090W second epoch is at least as precise as our second ACS epoch over the same area. We recommend the NIRCam filter closest in wavelength to the first-epoch filter, though the long-wavelength filters show promise for closer targets or longer baselines.

authors.name: Jack T. Warfield, Nitya Kallivayalil, Sangmo Tony Sohn, Christopher T. Garling, Andrew B. Pace, Roeland P. van der Marel, Daniel R. Weisz, Mark A. Fardal, Niusha Ahvazi, Jay Anderson, Kaia R. Atzberger, Paul Bennet, Martha L. Boyer, Roger E. Cohen, Andrew A. Cole, Matteo Correnti, Andrew E. Dolphin, Marla C. Geha, Mario Gennaro, Kevin A. McKinnon, Kristen B. W. McQuinn, Max J. B. Newman, Ekta Patel, Karin M. Sandstrom, Alessandro Savino, Evan D. Skillman, Eduardo Vitral, Laura L. Watkins, Benjamin F. Williams

papers.title: The Most X-ray Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient at Early Times: AT 2024qfm and Inefficient Reprocessing of Its High-Energy Emission
papers.summary: We present comprehensive multiwavelength (X-ray, UV, optical, and radio) observations of the Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient (LFBOT) AT 2024qfm. At $z = 0.227$ and reaching $L_{\rm x}\approx 10^{44}\,\rm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, AT 2024qfm is the most X-ray luminous LFBOT at $\delta t 10000$ K until $\delta t \approx 14$ days. AT 2024qfm shows luminous radio emission that is broadly consistent with the interaction of a fast ($\Gamma \beta c \approx 0.2$ c) shock wave with a dense medium ($n_{\rm CSM} \approx 6 \times 10^{4}\, \rm cm^{-3}$ at $R \approx 1.3 \times 10^{16}$ cm). Interestingly, the radio spectra do not evolve between $\delta t \approx 40-58$ days, indicating multiple outflow components shocking the surrounding medium. Peculiar to AT2024qfm is that this LFBOT reaches $L_{\rm x} \approx L_{\rm opt}$ at much earlier times ($\delta t \approx 7$ days) than observed for AT 2018cow and AT 2024wpp, suggesting less efficient re-processing of X-rays. Finally, a compilation of the X-ray spectral properties of all known LFBOTs shows that they consistently exhibit harder X-ray spectra than GRB afterglows, indicating a different emission mechanism and/or regimes between the two source classes.

authors.name: A. J. Nayana, Raffaella Margutti, Ryan Chornock, James F. Steiner, Erica Hammerstein, Anna Y. Q. Ho, Assaf Horesh, Brian D. Metzger, Daniel A. Perley, Michael Bietenholz, Peter Craig, Mark Gurwell, Garrett K. Keating, Natalie LeBaron, Kevin S. McCarthy, Giulia Migliori, Jean Somalwar, Daniel Stern, Ramprasad Rao, Jay Strader, Huei Sears, Itai Sfaradi, Ryan Urquhart, Eli Wiston

papers.title: Age dependence of the radial metallicity gradient in the Galactic disc with LAMOST and Gaia
papers.summary: We investigate the stellar radial metallicity ([Fe/H]) gradient--age relation (MGAR) of the Galactic disc using a solar-neighbourhood sample of 580\,037 F-, G-, and K-type (FGK) dwarf and turn-off stars from LAMOST DR7, Gaia Data Release3, and the corrected StarHorse age catalogue. The fiducial MGAR is non-monotonic, with relatively strong negative gradients at intermediate ages followed by substantial flattening towards older populations. The most negative gradient occurs at $6$--$8$ Gyr in the adopted 2-Gyr bins, although the $4$--$6$ Gyr slope is statistically similar, indicating a broad intermediate-age turnover rather than a sharply defined transition. The flattening persists within the low-$\alpha$ population, indicating that chemical-population mixing alone cannot explain the full-sample relation, and is also recovered under alternative guiding-radius definitions, radial fitting ranges, vertical-orbit selections, propagation of the reported random age uncertainties, and an alternative stellar-age scale. In contrast, controlling the age-dependent $T_{\rm eff}$--$\log g$ distribution substantially reduces the absolute gradient amplitudes and modifies the younger-age behaviour. A same-star comparison with APOGEE DR17 further shows that the broad age dependence of the controlled MGAR is recovered using an external [Fe/H] scale. We therefore identify the intermediate-to-old-age flattening as the most robust feature of the observed MGAR, whereas the precise location and depth of the intermediate-age minimum and the detailed younger-age morphology are less stable. These results indicate that stellar-parameter selection can contribute to the diversity of MGAR morphologies reported in previous studies.

authors.name: Yi-De Jing, Duojie Jia, Bin Wang, Yulong Gao, Liyuan Lu, Zheng-Jun Du, Zenghui Zou

papers.title: Scalar dynamics in a subclass Ia mimetic DHOST bounce
papers.summary: We study scalar perturbations in a quadratic subclass Ia degenerate higher-order scalar-tensor (DHOST) realization of a nonsingular bouncing cosmology previously analyzed in higher-derivative mimetic gravity. After a constant rescaling of the scalar potential, the subclass Ia model reproduces the same scale-factor history as the original model, although the associated mimetic Lagrange multiplier generally differs. For the comparison with the original mimetic model, we focus on the branch $0<\gamma<2/3$, for which the scalar sound speed of the original model is positive. We perform an ADM and Hamiltonian reduction of the scalar sector and show that, imposing the mimetic and momentum constraints, the reduced canonical scalar mode contains no spatial-gradient contribution. The physical scalar sound speed therefore vanishes, $c_s^2=0$, in agreement with the known vacuum behavior of the \(\alpha_L=0\) mimetic-DHOST sector. On the matched bouncing background, the resulting effective frequency squared is independent of the comoving wavenumber and approaches zero from below in the remote contracting phase. Consequently, the asymptotic oscillatory regime used in the previous mimetic model to impose positive-frequency initial conditions is absent. Although canonical normalization can still be imposed through the Wronskian condition, it does not select the initial state uniquely. Without an additional state prescription, the asymptotic dynamics therefore does not uniquely determine the primordial scalar spectrum.

authors.name: Idaiane L. Machado, Yi-Fu Cai

papers.title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
papers.summary: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datasets that benefit from longer observational baselines and advances in statistical modeling and noise characterization.

authors.name: Jackson D. Taylor, Emmanuel Fonseca, Joseph Glaser

papers.title: Chemical structure of the solar neighbourhood with DESI DR1
papers.summary: We analyse the chemical, spatial, and kinematic properties of stars in the solar neighbourhood using DESI Data Release 1 combined with Gaia astrometry. A high-quality FGK dwarf sample is separated into low-$\alpha$ and high-$\alpha$ populations using Gaussian mixture modelling in the [$\alpha$/Fe]--[Fe/H] plane. The low-$\alpha$ population is more metal rich, dominates near the Galactic mid-plane, and shows negative radial and vertical metallicity gradients. The high-$\alpha$ population is more metal poor, has a steeper vertical metallicity gradient, an approximately flat radial metallicity profile, and dynamically hotter kinematics. Despite these differences, the two chemically defined populations overlap substantially in velocity space. These results indicate distinct chemical enrichment histories for the low-$\alpha$ and high-$\alpha$ populations, while showing that chemical classification does not map uniquely onto present-day kinematic components. The observed chemo-dynamical structure is consistent with the combined effects of chemical enrichment, radial redistribution, and secular dynamical evolution in shaping the Galactic disc.

authors.name: Yi-De Jing, Duojie Jia, Yulong Gao, Zheng-jun Du, Zenghui Zou, Liyuan Lu

papers.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
papers.summary: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $\gamma = 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $\delta\Phi_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

authors.name: Alejandra Rosselli-Calderon, Morgan MacLeod, Enrico Ramirez-Ruiz

papers.title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
papers.summary: Designing low-thrust multi-asteroid rendezvous missions requires the coupled selection of asteroid sequences, encounter epochs, and low-thrust trajectories. Lambert transfers support rapid beam search but do not directly describe thrust-limited transfer capacity or propellant consumption. This paper develops two complementary low-thrust neural approximators. The first directly predicts the continuous maximum admissible initial mass from numerically optimized low-thrust transfers, providing a transfer-capacity estimate for comparison with the current spacecraft mass. The second predicts mass-dependent propellant consumption and propagates spacecraft mass to subsequent legs. With the carefully-designed input features and network structure, the approximators reduce mean absolute errors by 72.2% and 75.5%, respectively, relative to conventional deep neural network baselines. These predictions are incorporated into a Lambert-ranked beam search through resource filtering and recursive mass propagation before final beam selection. The method is evaluated on fixed-visit, maximum-visit, and deployment-collection missions. Across the tested cases, the proposed resource filtering increases the fraction of candidate sequences that yield accepted low-thrust solutions, raises the maximum validated asteroid-visit count by up to 15.4%, and improves the best mission objective by up to 17.8%. These results demonstrate that continuous transfer-capacity and propellant predictions can improve finite-width sequence search.

authors.name: Xingyu Zhou, Roberto Armellin, Jack Yarndley, Xiangyu Li

papers.title: Reassessment of Planetary Parameters and Statistical Validation of 187 Kepler Habitable-Zone and Near Habitable Confirmed and Candidate Planets
papers.summary: Confirmed and candidate planets in the Habitable or near-Habitable Zones (HZ) orbiting Sun-like stars are crucial not only for the search for life beyond the Solar System, but also for understanding the architecture and formation of other solar systems and for conducting demographic studies. Current analyses of such planetary systems are limited both by the small sample size revealed by Kepler as well as by uncertainties in system parameters. Although a larger sample of HZ and near-HZ planets must await new observations from wide-field, space-based surveys, follow-up analyses and observations with existing facilities can improve the precision on stellar and planetary parameters, enable more accurate planetary classification, and a more reliable assessment of whether candidate systems are true planets or merely astrophysical false positives. Here, we present a homogeneous transit light curve analysis of 187 HZ and near-HZ systems discovered by Kepler. Our analysis incorporates the latest Gaia DR3-derived stellar parameters, and we also present a statistical validation effort for all targets. The result is a uniform set of planetary radii, instellation fluxes, and orbital ephemerides suitable for prioritizing and scheduling follow-up observations to improve our understanding of planets in this regime. We show that longer-period (>300days) systems would particularly benefit from transit follow-up: just a single transit from facilities such as the 6m James Webb or the planned 3m Lazuli space telescopes could provide ~2 times tighter precision on planet radii than four years of Kepler photometry, thereby dramatically shrinking relevant parameter uncertainties and allowing more confident planet/false-positive assessments.

authors.name: Md Abdullah Al Zaman, Ian J. M. Crossfield, Ekrem Murat Esmer, Jason S. Pero

papers.title: Evaluating VLT SPHERE for Probing Diffuse Circumstellar Regions of Evolved Stars
papers.summary: Red and Yellow Supergiant stars, generally found in late evolutionary stages with high mass loss, provide test cases for evaluating high-contrast imaging performance. Determining how well adaptive optics combined with coronagraphy isolates faint circumstellar emission allows us to define its true sensitivity limits for evolved stars and refine future high-contrast observing strategies. We conducted a pilot study of seven nearby (within 0.8 kpc), bright (V-band magnitude of 10 or less) evolved red and yellow supergiants. We selected these targets to evaluate the ability of the VLT's SPHERE/IRDIS high-contrast imaging instrument to detect faint, diffuse circumstellar emission in four infrared filters (J1, J2, K1, and K2). We processed the data using RDI to remove the stellar PSF, AO speckles, and diffraction patterns. We extracted radial profiles and performed Radon transform analysis to search for faint extended emission around each target. We detect no extended circumstellar emission in our high-contrast images or clear infrared excess in the SEDs of our seven targets. Injection-recovery tests demonstrate sensitivity to diffuse emission at contrasts of approximately 3.5 mag in the J1 and approximately 2.0 mag in K1 relative to the residual coronagraphic PSF halo. This study provides the first results that elucidate the observational conditions under which SPHERE/IRDIS fails to recover low surface brightness emission and highlights the observational factors that most strongly control detectability, including filter choice, sky calibration, and reference-star matching. Our results motivate future studies to prioritize targets with infrared excess and optimize observing strategies to improve sensitivity to faint circumstellar emission around evolved massive stars.

authors.name: Priyadarshini Gokuldass, Saida M. Caballero-Nieves, Alex Carciofi, Bruce Gendre, Tajan H. de Amorim, Keefe J. Kamp, Justyn Maund, N. Brice Orange, Maddalena Reggiani

papers.title: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
papers.summary: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions of the Universe that encode valuable information about its large-scale structure and evolution. By extending spherical voids into overlapping sphere structures, the Popcorn Void Finder demonstrated an improved statistical characterization of cosmic void populations. However, its origin as a research prototype progressively hindered its maintainability and extensibility. Moreover, post-publication algorithmic modifications have not been systematically evaluated, leaving their statistical and computational consequences insufficiently characterized. In this work, we present a comprehensive reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder, prioritizing algorithmic transparency, maintainability, and reproducibility. We document the complete identification procedure, revisit the original algorithmic choices, and evaluate their statistical and computational consequences. Comparisons between implementations revealed a significant change in the behavior of the Void Size Function, which is now characterized by a power-law regime transitioning to a Schechter-like distribution. These changes not only provide a better characterization of void sizes, but enable a new and more robust method to the determination of the shot-noise dominated regime, without implicit dependencies on internal finder parameters present in previous works. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a 1.62x speedup in spherical void identification and a substantial improvement in overlap-removal throughput. We determined the Popcorn algorithm to be negatively affected by load imbalance, and found a speedup of 63x in a tested configuration with a newly introduced early growth termination criterion. These results establish a more maintainable and reproducible foundation for popcorn void identification, while clarifying the statistical and computational trade-offs that govern its performance.

authors.name: Alvaro Roy Schachner, Dante Javier Paz, Juan Antonio Rico Gallego, Carlos Mauricio Correa, Andr\'es Nicol\'as Ruiz, Sebasti\'an Rogelio Gualpa, Juan Bautista Cabral

papers.title: DIPS-OjOS I: Project Design and Science Validation
papers.summary: Automated pipelines and machine-learning algorithms are efficient at detecting standard planetary transits, but can miss subtle, non-periodic morphological anomalies. We present the pilot phase of DIPS-OjOS (Detecting Irregular Photometric Signals - Oj\'imetrO Survey), a professional-amateur collaboration designed to develop and validate a scalable workflow for identifying irregular photometric signals in exoplanet transit light curves through trained visual inspection. The project targets starspot-crossing events, stellar flares, circumplanetary structures, exomoon-like signatures, and transit-duration or timing anomalies overlooked by automated searches. We built the infrastructure required for a controlled visual-inspection experiment: simulated control light curves, preparation and detrending of real short-cadence Kepler data, a transit-modeling pipeline that computes an optimized average transit profile for each light curve, and a web-based classification platform. The real sample was deliberately restricted to 51 well-characterized Kepler systems. Collaborators inspected 917 transit events: 555 real transits and 362 simulated controls. The simulated sample quantified observer performance and calibrated a weighted consensus scheme; collaborators recovered injected signals with an average efficiency of 87.6%, while the null-case false-positive rate was 15.3%. After expert validation, we retained 88 viable candidate anomalies from the real sample, including 26 starspot-crossing event candidates across eight targets, seven stellar flares, 31 systematic transit-duration deviations motivating refined orbital parameters in four systems, and a mutual transit event in Kepler-89. Recovering candidate signals in this well-studied sample validates the sensitivity of DIPS-OjOS and establishes the basis for future applications to Kepler, TESS, PLATO, and ground-based datasets.

authors.name: E. D\'iez Alonso, S. Iglesias Alvarez, J. Men\'endez Blanco, J. Collada B\'arcena, A. Coya Lozano, J. M. Fern\'andez D\'iaz, D. Garc\'ia, F. Garc\'ia de la Cuesta, N. G\'omez Hern\'andez, \'A. J. Gonz\'alez Ord\'o\~nez, R. Hevia D\'iaz, R. Pardo Silva, J. Polanco, A. Quijada Espina, J. Rodr\'iguez Rodr\'iguez, N. Villanueva Fern\'andez, F. J. de Cos Juez

papers.title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
papers.summary: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. Eleven of the 13 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations, for seven- and nine-parameter solutions alike, and the dynamical companion masses agree with the photometric estimates where the photocenter conversion is well determined. Independently of the fits, 33 of the 43 plausible systems with a usable position angle (77%) have the acceleration directed within 45 degrees of the primary-companion axis, against 50% for a control sample: DR3's measured accelerations point in the directions of the cataloged companions.

authors.name: Qier An, Timothy D. Brandt

papers.title: Probabilistic Inversion of Strong Gravitational Lenses with Flow Matching Priors
papers.summary: Strong gravitational lensing reveals important information about the universe, but reconstructing the source image and lens properties requires solving an ill-posed inverse imaging problem. Generative image models serve as powerful data-driven priors in Bayesian inverse problems. Diffusion models have been used widely, but they are computationally costly. Flow matching has emerged as a promising alternative to diffusion models, with easier training, efficient sampling, and better-quality data generation. In this work, we present Blind-FlowSGS, a principled blind posterior sampling method using flow matching priors, enabling efficient posterior sampling for non-blind and blind inversion of strong gravitational lenses. On simulated Euclid data, we demonstrate our method's improvement over diffusion-based methods in both efficacy and efficiency. Our method shows promising capabilities to accurately process strong lensing data from modern sky surveys at scale. Our code and data are available on our project page.

authors.name: Tianao Li, Jimena Gonz\'alez, Xinfeng Xu, Aggelos K. Katsaggelos, Rebecca Willett, Aleksandra \'Ciprijanovi\'c, Tjitske Starkenburg, Emma Alexander

papers.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
papers.summary: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)\rho(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(\chi)\rangle =\langle \rho(\chi)\rangle \langle \sigma_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $\chi$ is the scale of the system under study and it can describe cosmological or galactic scales and $\sigma_{DM}$ is the characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter at the relevant scales. This results to the entropy function behaving universally as $K(\chi)=\langle \sigma_{DM}^2\rangle$. We investigate the cosmological implications of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter, and we conclude that this scale-dependent equation of state dark matter cannot be the sole component of dark matter in the Universe. Also the second aim of this work is to provide a sufficient explanation for the question why $K_0$ changes for each galaxy, where $K_0$ is the value of $K(r)$ at intermediate and large radii from the core of the galaxy. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of having distinct dark matter components which cluster differently, and thus controlling differently the dynamics of the Universe at various scales. Scale-dependent equation of state dark matter can control the galactic scales, while another component can dominate at cosmological scales and thus control the Universe at cosmological scales.

authors.name: V. K. Oikonomou

papers.title: Identifying Distant and Highly Reddened Star Clusters: 486 Open Clusters and Candidates in the Dusty Galactic Disk
papers.summary: The Gaia mission has transformed the census of Galactic star clusters. Most discoveries were based on Gaia DR2 and EDR3, and the rate of new large cluster catalogues has declined since 2023. The distant and dusty part of the disk is still poorly sampled because optical data are strongly affected by extinction. We search for star clusters in the Galactic disk using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, together with 2MASS near-infrared photometry. We scan trial cluster centers in Galactic position, proper motion, and parallax space, assign a Bayesian membership probability to each star, construct a relative density map, and use DBSCAN solely to separate neighboring peaks. We identify 486 clusters and candidates with astrometric quality comparable to that of previously reported clusters. Of these, 450 have no literature counterpart, while 36 are known clusters that were not recovered in earlier Gaia cluster searches. The median distance is 6.9 kpc, and 39% of the objects lie beyond 8 kpc. The median extinction is Av = 5.10 mag, and 16% of the objects have Av > 8mag. The new objects fill a sparsely sampled region of the distance--extinction plane. Their distribution reveals the north--south displacement of the Galactic warp, and high-latitude objects are on average farther, older, and less extincted. Gaia DR3 still offers room for distant, dust-obscured clusters, and this sample provides a baseline for Gaia DR4. All cluster parameters, member star information, spatial distribution maps, and color-magnitude diagrams can be downloaded from https://zenodo.org/records/24431850.

authors.name: Zhihong He, Xiaoping Wang, Qian Cui, Yangping Luo, Kun Wang

papers.title: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
papers.summary: We formulate the dissipation due to sound-wave emission from a Keplerian binary embedded in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background at rest in the binary center-of-mass frame within linear perturbation theory. Rather than starting from the local wake force, we treat the binary as a localized periodic mass source and compute the sound-wave fluxes carried away by the medium. The time-averaged energy, linear-momentum, and angular-momentum fluxes are obtained from Noether currents of the fluid perturbations. For a classical inviscid barotropic Newtonian fluid, retaining the self-gravity of density perturbations while adopting the Jeans prescription, we derive explicit flux formulas for circular and eccentric binaries with arbitrary mass ratio. This formulation also clarifies the ultraviolet behavior of point sources: in a nondispersive fluid, the harmonic sum becomes cutoff-sensitive precisely when at least one component becomes supersonic. We examine explicitly how finite source size removes this divergence using a uniform-sphere model and relate the resulting regularization to a corresponding effective harmonic cutoff. The associated secular eccentricity evolution exhibits circularization in the subsonic regime when the fluid self-gravity is sufficiently weak but can change sign outside this regime, with eccentricity growth in the strictly supersonic UV limit. For a Schr\"odinger-Poisson quantum fluid, quantum pressure instead softens the high-frequency contribution and renders the point-source fluxes UV finite within the nonrelativistic regime; our numerical results further indicate eccentricity growth due to sound radiation over the parameter space explored. Finally, we translate orbital-decay measurements of two binary pulsars into order-of-magnitude bounds on the homogeneous quantum-fluid density surrounding each system.

authors.name: Yan Cao, Mu-Chun Chen

papers.title: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
papers.summary: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $\gamma=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $\rho_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1\sigma$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $\rho_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$, respectively. The leading halo monopole in the first two metrics is degenerate with the central mass. At fixed dynamical mass, their leading radial profile correction produces retrograde precession. The $\gamma=5/2$ metric introduces an additional angular deficit contribution, which enhances the precession response and accounts for its smaller parameter limits.

authors.name: Qi Qi, Qiang Wu, Xiao-Mei Kuang

papers.title: Insights on Three Distinct Types of Energetic Particle Flux Variations Ahead of ICME-driven Shocks Observed by ASPEX on board Aditya-L1
papers.summary: We investigate upstream energetic-ion transport associated with ten interplanetary coronal mass ejection (ICME)-driven shocks observed near 1 au using multidirectional measurements from the Suprathermal and Energetic Particle Spectrometer (STEPS) onboard Aditya-L1. Based on energy-dependent intensity profiles and onset times, the events are classified as dispersed, dispersionless, or mixed. We combine pitch-angle anisotropy, minimum variance analysis, reduced magnetic helicity, two-dimensional Grad-Shafranov reconstruction, quasi-linear transport diagnostics, shock parameters, and energetic-ion spectral fits to characterize each category. The seven dispersed events exhibit energy-dependent arrivals, generally intermittent magnetic-helicity signatures, and larger parallel mean free paths, consistent with less restricted particle propagation. In contrast, the two dispersionless events show nearly simultaneous enhancements across energy channels, extended intervals of enhanced reduced magnetic helicity, and closed magnetic flux contours in Grad-Shafranov reconstructions. They also exhibit shorter parallel mean free paths, higher pitch-angle diffusion coefficients, and comparatively strong shocks. The mixed event transitions from dispersed arrivals to nearly simultaneous enhancements as the shock approaches, accompanied by evolving anisotropy and distinct scattering properties. Spectral indices range from approximately -2.38 to -0.86 for dispersed events and from -0.82 to -0.26 for dispersionless and mixed events, indicating harder spectra in the latter groups. These results reveal systematic associations between energetic-ion transport, magnetic structure, shock conditions, and spectral hardness, suggesting that shock-associated energization and energy-dependent transport jointly shape the observed signatures, while magnetic topology may regulate particle propagation and confinement.

authors.name: Aakash Gupta, Dibyendu Chakrabarty, Yogesh, Anshu Kumari, Shivam Parashar, Jacob Sebastian, Amrit S. Mishra, Bijoy Dalal, Santosh Vadawale, Shiv Kumar Goyal, M. Shanmugam, Anil Bhardwaj, Vipin K. Yadav, Srikar P. Tadepalli

papers.title: Asteroseismic investigation of intermediate age open star cluster NGC 2126
papers.summary: We present a preliminary asteroseismic investigation of the pulsating stars in the intermediate-age open cluster NGC 2126. The TESS Full Frame Images and ground-based photometry from the previous study, Dileep et al. (2025), were used to identify the pulsation modes of {\delta} Scuti member stars using period-luminosity relations and pulsation modelling.
