Our analysis resulted in a tentative identification up to the first radial overtone in stars N1, N2 and ZV1. Additionally, the second radial overtone was secured in N1. The disentangled pulsation and eclipse light curves of the binary star V551 Aur (V6) from our previous research were employed to study pulsation amplitude and phase modulations across the orbital period. The primary component of V6 exhibits pulsations showing amplitude and phase modulations, indicating tidal influence on the oscillations. Modelling the pulsation as the fundamental radial mode reveals that in order for the mode to be radial, the star must be significantly brighter than observed. Hence, the mode is not the fundamental radial mode or the overtones. Low-resolution spectroscopy was used to search for chemical peculiarities in the pulsating members, and we found that star ID 143 has features similar to an Am star.

authors.name: Athul Dileep, Santosh Joshi, Patricia Lampens, Chenglong Lv, David Mkrtichian, Peter De Cat, Abhay Pratap Yadav, Arjun Dawn, Ali Esamdin

papers.title: Outflows and Young Stars in the Auriga-California Giant Molecular Cloud
papers.summary: The Auriga-California Molecular Cloud (AMC) is a nearby star-forming region with a moderate level of star formation activity. Previous infrared surveys have shown that its young stellar population is concentrated along a dense filament extending north of NGC 1579. We searched for new manifestations of ongoing star formation in the AMC by identifying optical and molecular outflows, H{\alpha} emission-line stars, and young stars associated with reflection nebulae. Narrowband H{\alpha} and [SII] imaging, together with slitless spectroscopy, were obtained with the 1-m Schmidt telescope of the Byurakan Observatory. The optical data were complemented by near-infrared images from the Spitzer Enhanced Imaging Products (SEIP) and by WISE/unWISE archival data. We discovered seven new Herbig-Haro (HH) objects and outflows associated with several young stellar objects, including deeply embedded infrared sources and stars surrounded by compact reflection nebulae. Nearly all of the optical HH objects have molecular hydrogen counterparts, and several additional candidate H2 outflows without optical counterparts were identified. Particularly noteworthy is a compact region around V347 Per that appears to host at least three molecular outflows. We also present a list of newly identified H{\alpha} emission-line stars and a catalogue of stars associated with optical reflection nebulae. Both populations are concentrated primarily along the northern dark filament of the cloud. The spatial distribution of the newly identified HH objects, molecular outflows, emission-line stars, and nebulous young stars confirms that the northern filament is the principal site of ongoing star formation in the AMC. The close correspondence between the optical and molecular outflowsfurther suggests that most of their driving sources are deeply embedded Class 0/I young stellar objects.

authors.name: T. A. Movsessian, T. Yu. Magakian

papers.title: Integrated Study of NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437 Open Clusters: from Stellar Parameters to Orbital Trajectories Utilizing Gaia DR3 Archive
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive photometric, astrometric, and dynamical study of four Galactic open clusters, NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437, using Gaia DR3 data. Probable cluster members were identified through astrometric and photometric criteria. Radial density profiles were modelled with a King-type surface-density distribution to derive structural parameters. Mean parallaxes and proper motions yielded astrometric distances of 410 +/- 12 pc (NGC 1662), 1761 +/- 335 pc (NGC 1778), 477 +/- 18 pc (NGC 2422), and 1681 +/- 172 pc (NGC 2437). Fundamental astrophysical parameters were estimated through Bayesian isochrone fitting using PARSEC evolutionary models within an MCMC framework. The resulting ages (log(t/yr)) are 8.91 (-0.33/+0.24), 8.20 (-0.11/+0.18), 7.80 (-0.11/+0.06), and 8.56 (-0.34/+0.27), respectively. Luminosity functions were transformed into present-day mass functions using an isochrone-based mass-luminosity relation. The derived mass-function slopes are broadly consistent, within uncertainties, with the classical Salpeter form. Mean systemic radial velocities from Gaia DR3 and complementary spectroscopic surveys enabled the determination of Galactic space velocities (U, V, W) in the Local Standard of Rest frame. Backward orbital integrations over 3 Gyr were performed using galpy with the MWPotential2014 Galactic potential. The resulting orbits are nearly circular (e <= 0.106), with limited vertical excursions (Z_max < 0.3 kpc), consistent with thin-disc kinematics. Inferred birth radii suggest possible outward radial displacement for NGC 2422, NGC 2437, and NGC 1778, and inward displacement for NGC 1662. Overall, all four clusters appear to have evolved within relatively stable Galactic disc orbits.

authors.name: R. Canbay, W. H. Elsanhoury, D. C. \c{C}{\i}nar, S. Ta\c{s}demir, A. Haroon, M. S. Alenazi, M. I. Elashiry, A. Ahmed

papers.title: On the subtleties of statistical isotropy in cosmic topology
papers.summary: The cosmological principle assumes homogeneity and isotropy on the largest scales for which the cosmic microwave background (CMB) provides the best testing grounds. Here, an analysis of the statistical isotropy for the CMB in the case of the cubic 3-torus topology is presented. Since the statistical anisotropy in the CMB 3-torus sky maps is very tiny, the analysis requires very large ensembles consisting of 100000 CMB simulations in order to reveal deviations from the isotropy. Orbit sum rules, which also have applications in quantum chaos, are used to describe the anisotropy structures found in the torus ensembles. They relate the length of orbits, which connect a given point on the surface of last scattering with the topological mirror points of the CMB observer, to the anisotropy pattern. It is found that the positions on the surface of last scattering which are closest to mirror observers possess the largest deviations from the statistical isotropy. Furthermore, the anisotropy of the normalised modulus of the gradient of the CMB temperature field is discussed.

authors.name: Ralf Aurich, Martin J France, Frank Steiner

papers.title: On extracting Science information from a large data set of RXTE X-ray binary spectra using KDE technique
papers.summary: Machine Learning/Neural Networks have been successively and extensively used in Astronomy (and other subjects) for class identification of objects based on large data sets. However, it remains difficult to extract other science information, such as what the characteristics of the class are that allow for definite identification, and whether there are objects in the sample that are unique and hence of possible science interest. An alternate approach based on rank ordering of variables and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) may be used for class identification and to infer such science information. We test the method on a previously analyzed data set of RXTE spectra of low-mass X-ray binaries and find that black hole and neutron star systems can be distinguished at an accuracy level of ~93%, which is comparable to deep learning techniques. The soft state spectra of black hole systems are distinct from neutron star ones. For the whole sample, observations of the pulsar 4U 1907+097 (which was inadvertently introduced into the data set) were clearly found to be unique. The previously reported hyper-soft states of GRO J1655-40 and XTE J1550-564 are found to be unique among black hole spectra. For the rest of the neutron stars, the method identifies some unreported spectra of EXO 1745-248 as unique because they seem to be relativistic reflection-dominated spectra. We discuss the potential and scalability of this method.

authors.name: Ranjeev Misra, Akash Garg, Aman Kumar, Ajit Kembhavi

papers.title: Modeling the chemical impacts of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes
papers.summary: Some protostars undergo episodic accretion, resulting in luminosity outbursts that heat their envelopes. The increase in temperature alters the position of the snowlines, which return to their original locations on different timescales depending on the species. However, the chemical effects of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes, including their long-term consequences, remain poorly explored. We investigate the chemical impact of luminosity outbursts on the envelope of a solar-type protostar, accounting for its dynamics, and identify trends in the molecular response relative to both ongoing and past outburst activity. We combined the dynamic semi-analytic code APE with the three-phase chemical model NAUTILUS to predict the time evolution of 83 molecular abundances between 10 and 10,000 au in the collapsing envelope. The outburst was parameterized by increasing the protostellar luminosity by a factor of 100 for 100 years. The outburst shifts molecular snowlines outward by up to a factor of ten, thus enriching the gas phase through thermal desorption. Most species return to their pre-outburst state within a few thousand years at most for r$\leq$1000 au and remain in that state thereafter. However, eight molecules (HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, C2H5CHO, OCS, SO2, C2S, C3S, and HC3N) show abundance deviations 10$-$50 kyr after the outburst in the warm inner regions (T$\geq$100 K), due to the inward transport of chemically altered material. Eight other species (CH3O, C2O, NH2, HCCO, HCNO, HNO, NO, and NCO) show enhanced gas-phase abundances at intermediate radii ($\sim$300$-$1500 au). Overall, most molecules are impacted by outward snowline shifts. With the exception of HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, and C2H5CHO, all complex organic molecules (COMs) are expected to exhibit similar abundances in the warm inner regions of protostars (hot corino), regardless of whether they undergo outbursts.

authors.name: Antoine Espagnet, Audrey Coutens, Pierre Marchand, Jean-Christophe Loison, Fernando Cruz-S\'aenz de Miera, Valentine Wakelam

papers.title: Survey of Compact Sources for Pulsars and Exotic Objects-II. Precision Timing of Millisecond Pulsar J1840+1102
papers.summary: We present the timing analysis of the eclipsing millisecond pulsar PSR J1840+1102, discovered in the Survey of COmpact sources for Pulsars and Exotic objects (SCOPE) using the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT). PSR J1840+1102 has a short spin period of 1.60 ms and an orbital period of 1.68 days, with a dispersion measure (DM) of 98.8 pc cm$^{-3}$. We report timing analysis over a 2.7-year baseline, yielding a phase-connected solution with a post-fit residual RMS of 2.1 $\mu$s. Enabled by the timing solution, we report discovery of pulsed gamma-rays from PSR J1840+1102, with the gamma-ray peak aligned with that of the radio profile. PSR J1840+1102 also exhibits remarkably short eclipses, lasting only around $0.4\%$ of the total orbit at 650 MHz. Based on optical searches, the orbital parameters, short eclipses, and comparison with the known binary pulsar population, we infer a Helium white dwarf (He-WD) surrounded by plasma to be the most likely companion. Furthermore, using GMRT observations covering 300 to 750 MHz, we present a study of the interstellar medium properties towards PSR J1840+1102 including refractive scintillation, DM variations and scattering, and report a very low scattering index of $1.65\pm0.15$. The low timing residuals and lack of any prominent orbital parameters or DM variations support the overall suitability of PSR J1840+1102 for inclusion in the pulsar timing array campaigns.

authors.name: Ayushi Shrivastava, Yogesh Maan, M. A. Krishnakumar, Banshi Lal, Joeri van Leeuwen

papers.title: Discovery of Two Hyperluminous Infrared Galaxies at $z\sim6$
papers.summary: Hyperluminous infrared galaxies (HyLIRGs) at cosmic dawn are key to understanding the formation of the first massive galaxies. We report the spectroscopic confirmation of two unlensed HyLIRGs at $z\sim6$ in the COSMOS field, AzTECC63 and S2COS-84, originally selected from single-dish AzTEC and SCUBA-2 surveys. Using ALMA and NOEMA observations, we robustly detected CO and [CII] lines in both galaxies and unambiguously confirmed their redshifts to be $z=6.092$ and $z=5.90$, respectively. Panchromatic SED fitting reveals dust-obscured star formation rates of $\approx1000$ and $\approx2300\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, ranking them among the most intensely star-forming systems known at $z \gtrsim 6$. High-resolution ALMA observations reveal an extremely compact morphology for S2COS-84, with a dust-continuum effective radius of $\approx0.3$ kpc, implying a star-formation rate surface density above the Eddington limit. The far-infrared SEDs of both galaxies, together with the compact size of S2COS-84, indicate warm dust ($T_{\rm dust} \approx 80$ K) that is likely optically thick at far-infrared wavelengths. Both galaxies exhibit an extreme [CII] deficit, with $L_{\rm [C\,II]}/L_{\rm IR} \approx 10^{-3.7}$, an order of magnitude below that of normal star-forming galaxies. Their molecular gas masses, derived consistently from both [C\,{\sc ii}] and dust, together with their IR-derived SFRs imply short gas depletion times of $\approx$40--60 Myr, making them plausible progenitors of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies found at $z\sim5$.

authors.name: Shuowen Jin, Georgios E. Magdis, Raphael Gobat, Eva Schinnerer, Emanuele Daddi, Herv\'e Dole, Aurelien Henry, Daizhong Liu, Benjamin Magnelli, Francesca Rizzo, Nikolaj B. Sillassen, Sune Toft, Francesco Valentino

papers.title: Finite-temperature quark dynamics in proto-neutron stars: Maximum baryonic mass and radial oscillations
papers.summary: Finite-temperature quark dynamics can significantly alter proto-neutron star evolution even when the cold equation of state remains unchanged. We quantify this sensitivity by comparing a purely hadronic baseline with two hybrid models incorporating quark matter via the Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (PNJL) framework and its entanglement extension (EPNJL), which isolates the role of finite-temperature chiral-deconfinement coupling. Employing bulk Gibbs constructions for both nuclear liquid-gas and hadron-quark phase coexistence, we compute equilibrium configurations across hot neutrino-trapped, hot neutrino-free, and cold stages, alongside linear radial oscillations of selected hot neutrino-free stars. Introducing quarks lowers the maximum baryonic mass at every stage and reverses its evolutionary ordering: whereas the maximum baryonic mass increases toward the cold limit in the purely hadronic model, it decreases progressively in both hybrid models, opening mass windows for delayed collapse. Crucially, despite sharing the same cold limit, PNJL and EPNJL yield distinct baryonic-mass intervals for mixed-core survival across stages: only EPNJL permits configurations that retain mixed cores across both hot stages, whereas only PNJL allows hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars to possess cold equilibrium counterparts. All tested hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars remain linearly stable, yet their fundamental radial frequencies differ substantially. These findings demonstrate that finite-temperature quark dynamics imprints distinct evolutionary constraints and pulsation signatures on proto-neutron stars beyond cold-matter descriptions.

authors.name: Xuefeng Ma, Jingdong Shao, Kun Xu, Mei Huang

papers.title: Temporal Evolution of Inner Circumstellar Geometry in Herbig Ae/Be Stars Revealed by Multi-epoch $H\alpha$ Spectropolarimetry
papers.summary: We present multi-epoch $H\alpha$ spectropolarimetric observations of three Herbig Ae/Be stars, HD 58647, MWC 120, and MWC 147, obtained at epochs separated by $\sim$1-1.3 yr. By combining $H\alpha$ line profiles with velocity-resolved linear polarization and $Q$-$U$ diagrams, we investigate temporal changes in their inner circumstellar environments. The $H\alpha$ profiles retain broadly similar morphologies and overall velocity extents between epochs, although noticeable variations in line strength and peak intensity are observed. In contrast, the polarization spectra and $Q$-$U$ trajectories exhibit pronounced changes in morphology, orientation, and velocity-dependent behavior. The three sources display distinct temporal characteristics: HD 58647 evolves from a compact, relatively weakly structured trajectory to a pronounced, predominantly linear excursion; MWC 120 exhibits open, structured trajectories at both epochs, with changes in their orientation and distribution; and MWC 147 evolves from a complex, vertically extended trajectory to a more confined and comparatively coherent, approximately linear arrangement. In HD 58647, strong velocity-dependent variations in polarization across the $H\alpha$ profile suggest a structured spatial relationship between the line-emitting and scattering regions. These source-dependent variations demonstrate that substantial changes in velocity-resolved polarization morphology can occur without corresponding changes in the overall $H\alpha$ velocity extent. This indicates that the projected polarization structure can evolve independently of the kinematic extent of the $H\alpha$-emitting region. Multi-epoch, velocity-resolved spectropolarimetry therefore provides a sensitive probe of temporal variations in the innermost circumstellar environments of intermediate-mass young stars, revealing variations that may not be apparent from spectroscopy alone.

authors.name: L. K. Dewangan, Arijit Maiti, Sube Singh Gurjar, Mudit K. Srivastava

papers.title: Using fixed $w$ to reproduce evolving $w_0$-$w_a$ dark energy at the field level
papers.summary: Recent results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) hint at dynamical dark energy, making the accurate modelling of such cosmologies increasingly important for future analyses. In this work, we show that because, when written in superconformal time $\tau$, the $N$-body equations of motion depend on the background cosmology only through the expansion history $a(\tau)$, matching $a(\tau)$ allows us to map one cosmology onto another. As a first, observationally relevant, application of this new method, we match a Chevallier--Polarski--Linder (CPL) cosmology to a constant-$w$ cosmology with the closest $a(\tau)$. This allows us to use a single fixed-$w$ simulation to reproduce the simulation predictions of the target CPL cosmology at the field level at redshifts $0\le z\le3$. We validate this matching with 100 pairs of CPL and fixed-$w$ \textsc{mg-glam} simulations, spanning $0.1\le\Omega_{\rm m}\le0.5$, $-1.4\le w_0\le-0.5$ and $-1.8\le w_a\le-0.15$. For a DESI-like cosmology, the matter power spectra of the matched and target simulations agree to 0.24\% for $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and 0.8\% up to $k\lesssim3\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at $0\le z\le3$, and the density phases are reproduced with a stochasticity below 0.02\%. Displacements, velocities, momenta, redshift-space multipoles, bispectra and the halo and void abundances are similarly well predicted. For most models we consider, we achieve subpercent error in the power spectrum up to scales $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at all redshifts, with density stochasticity below 0.03\% over the same scales. The method allows constant-$w$ simulations and field-level emulators to be used for CPL cosmologies, and generalises to any cosmology with no additional scale dependence.

authors.name: Yuxi Meng, Daniela Saadeh, Cheng-Zong Ruan, Baojiu Li, Kazuya Koyama

papers.title: Velocity-Window Dependence of the Broad H$\alpha$ Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots
papers.summary: Broad Balmer emission lines probe black hole masses and nuclear kinematics in high-redshift active galactic nuclei (AGNs). In JWST "little red dots" (LRDs), integrated broad-H$\alpha$ widths span a remarkably narrow range at fixed line luminosity, raising the question of whether this tightness persists once outer-wing emission is included. Holding each object and its broad-H$\alpha$ luminosity fixed, we measure the finite-window line dispersion $\sigma(V)$, the flux-weighted second-moment width within $\pm V$, from $V = 1500$ to $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in JWST/NIRSpec spectra and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Type-1 AGNs. Across 20 high signal-to-noise LRDs, the observed scatter in $\log_{10}\sigma(V)$ at fixed $L_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}$ rises from 0.036 to 0.084 dex between $V = 2500$ and $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, a paired increase of 0.048 dex with a 95% bootstrap interval of 0.026-0.064 dex, compared with 0.020 dex across 167 broader SDSS AGNs. Injecting synthetic profiles into the empirical noise of the same 20 spectra shows that single-Gaussian and core-plus-wing models both accommodate this rise, leaving intrinsic wing diversity, truncation, and wing noise unseparated. In the clearest dual-line spectrum, RUBIES-EGS-55604, H$\beta$ strengthens relative to H$\alpha$ from line center to wing under two spectral decompositions of the same grating spectrum. Alongside integrated widths in JWST, SDSS, and 334 Euclid DR1 AGNs, these results show that the observed tightness of the H$\alpha$ scaling depends on the velocities included in $\sigma(V)$, requiring mass and kinematic models to match both transition and velocity interval.

authors.name: Haoyu Wang

papers.title: Reliability of Fermi/GBM spectral-catalogue parameters for gamma-ray burst population studies
papers.summary: The Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor (GBM) spectral catalogue contains measurements affected by model uncertainties, different peak-flux (PFLX) integration times, and changes in catalogue processing. We examine which quantities describe spectral shape and which reflect brightness or measurement conditions. We analysed 3337 of 3378 GRBs with spectral-fit data and identified a catalogue transition at GRB180712358. We compared the two periods using rank-based tests, regressions, and catalogue model-selection rules, and assessed duration classification by repeated cross-validation. PFLX measurements at 64 and nominal 1024 ms were analysed separately; short-long comparisons used fluence (FLNC) measurements only. The transition coincides with changes in catalogue version, fit statistic, and fit fields. In the nominal 1024 ms sample, all ten COMP A-B rank-biserial effects have absolute values below 0.10. In the 64 ms sample, COMP shape parameters are similar, but amplitudes, fluxes, and fluences are higher in the later period. The origin of this difference is unknown. In the earlier period, brighter bursts have smaller parameter errors but larger reported fit statistics and stronger evidence for spectral curvature. The FLNC PLAW index measures broad-band hardness. BAND alpha and Epeak can describe spectral shape when their errors are controlled, but beta is often poorly constrained. Adding PLAW or BAND to COMP provides little additional duration-classification information in matched samples. We interpret the A-B division mainly as a catalogue-processing transition, not population evolution. Fit statistics, errors, metadata, and model labels describe measurement conditions and should not be treated as independent physical variables. Correlated model parameters should not be treated as independent.

authors.name: Istvan Horvath

papers.title: Unresolved binaries from Gaia XP to SPHEREx
papers.summary: Unresolved companions alter the luminosity and spectra of a star, but a colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) reveals them only when the system is over-luminous, and a Gaia photocentre orbit constrains only a combination of the mass and flux ratios. We fit the absolute Gaia BP/RP (XP) and SPHEREx spectra (XPS) of about 71,000 low-mass stars in the Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars with the J-CaPS XPS emulator, which predicts single-star and coeval-binary spectra on an absolute flux scale. First, more than half of known binaries lie within the main-sequence (MS) band of the CMD, because the companion is faint or lifts a metal-poor primary onto the single-star ridge. XPS recovers 86 per cent of the binaries that a CMD cut finds and 44 per cent of those it misses. Second, a small photocentre motion can come from a faint companion or a luminous one of nearly equal mass. XPS distinguishes them and recovers the mass ratios of double-lined binaries. Among substellar candidates with radial-velocity follow-up, it ranks all 11 binaries above all 16 confirmed brown-dwarf or planet hosts. The public package spbin provides this check before follow-up. Third, where XPS detects no companion light, we place an upper limit on the light of an MS companion. Among Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits with clean spectral fits, 2841 require more companion mass than XPS allows for a single MS star. Within 200 pc, their companion masses cluster at those of typical white dwarfs, and nearly circular orbits support this interpretation. Of 24 companions that joint radial-velocity and astrometric orbits show to be faint, XPS recovers 22, compared with 14 selected by the absence of a colour excess. Applied to forthcoming Gaia DR4 orbital solutions, XPS can help distinguish luminous binaries from substellar companions and identify candidate compact companions whose dynamical masses exceed the limits allowed by their light.

authors.name: Jiadong Li, Hans-Walter Rix, Johanna M\"uller-Horn, Kareem El-Badry, Ben Pennell, Xiaoying Pang, Chao Liu

papers.title: Multiphase Gas in the Ram-Pressure-Stripped Elliptical Galaxy NGC 1404
papers.summary: Galaxy groups and low-mass galaxy clusters are major sites of environment-driven galaxy evolution. NGC 1404 is an X-ray-bright early-type galaxy traveling through the intracluster medium of the nearby low-mass Fornax Cluster, and it hosts off-center warm ionized gas. With minimal ongoing stellar feedback and negligible active galactic nucleus feedback, NGC 1404 provides an ideal laboratory for constraining the impact of environmental processes on the thermodynamics of the interstellar medium. We analyzed VLT/MUSE, 506 ks Chandra ACIS, and 119 ks XMM-Newton RGS observations to quantify gas motions in both the hot and warm phases of NGC 1404. We probed the kinematics of the warm gas by deriving the velocity structure function (VSF) from MUSE H$\alpha$ integral-field spectroscopy. To measure the kinematics of the hot gas, we derived the power spectrum of X-ray surface brightness fluctuations from the Chandra data, and independently constrained galaxy-scale hot gas motions by measuring Fe XVII resonant scattering and turbulent line broadening with RGS. Our RGS spectral analysis gives a three-dimensional Mach number of $0.48^{+0.22}_{-0.14}$, consistent with the power-spectrum results from Chandra for the same extraction region, and corresponding to a turbulent-to-thermal energy density ratio of $\sim0.13$. The warm-gas VSF follows the expectation for Kolmogorov turbulence and is broadly consistent with the hot-gas kinematics. The off-center warm gas in NGC 1404 may have formed through radiative cooling of the hot interstellar medium, triggered by the uplift of low-entropy hot gas during ram pressure stripping. Our study suggests that ram pressure stripping can drive substantial gas motions and reshape the thermodynamic state of the interstellar medium of cluster member galaxies.

authors.name: Ryan Eskenasy, Yuanyuan Su, Qinnan Zhu, Charles Romero, Junjie Mao, Yuan Li, Tirso Marin-Gilabert, Romana Grossov\'a, Valeria Olivares, Ming Sun, Elke Roediger, Ralph P. Kraft, Sheng-Chieh Lin, Aaron Burke

papers.title: py4radiation: a framework for generating heating/cooling functions and ion fractions from custom radiation fields for astrophysical simulations
papers.summary: Modelling multiphase gas in and around galaxies is key to understanding the baryon cycle in galaxy evolution. Modern simulation codes rely on heating/cooling functions and ion fractions to capture the thermodynamics and chemistry of such gases, but coupling all physical factors remains challenging. We present a new Python-based, parallelised package that acts as an integration framework, connecting well-established astrophysical codes and models to produce self-consistent heating/cooling functions and ion fractions from custom ionising UV/X-ray backgrounds. The package returns multi-dimensional tables that can be readily coupled to hydrodynamic and post-processing codes to study radiative processes and extract observables, as we demonstrate with static cloud simulations. Our simulation suite studies the thermodynamic history of a static circumgalactic cloud with smoothed edges subjected to meta-galactic and starburst heating. We find that the clouds experience damped pulsations regulated by strong cooling-driven inflows and heating-driven outflows that constantly overshoot pressure equilibrium. Meta-galactic heating is weak and produces a confined and dense cloud, while starburst heating is strong and sustains large clouds only a little smaller than those obtained with the standard $10^4\,\rm K$ cooling floor. Starburst radiative heating acts as a damping agent, thereby reducing mixing. py4radiation comes with extensive documentation and a sample catalogue of heating/cooling functions and ion tables for a selected set of input meta-galactic and starburst spectral energy distributions. The code is publicly available and can be easily expanded.

authors.name: Daniel Villarruel-Y\'anez, Wladimir E. Banda-Barrag\'an, Benedetta Casavecchia

papers.title: $w_0$ Is All You Need: Field-Level Matching of General Dark Energy Models to $w_0$CDM Simulations
papers.summary: We show that clustering in general dynamical dark energy models $w(z)$ can be predicted with constant dark energy $w_0\text{CDM}$ models at the field level via spectral equivalence. The prescription of this method requires equating comoving distances to the last scattering surface between predictor and target models, which is equivalent to requiring equal recent background expansion history averages. Dark energy models with the same distance thus form approximate equivalence classes, with nearly identical matter fields. To test the precision of spectral equivalence beyond the CPL parametrization, we run $N$-body simulations with various dynamical dark energy models, including spline-based $w(z)$, all matched to a single $w_0\text{CDM}$ run. Our measurements show that the power spectra of all matched dark energies agree with the predictor within $0.2\%$ up to $k = 0.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and within $0.6\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We also compare the non-Gaussian information contained in the simulated fields. Bispectra differ by at most $0.26\%$ across all runs up to $k = 0.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and $1.75\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, while wavelet scattering transform coefficients are all within $0.05\%$. The decorrelation, $1 - r^2$, between each matched field and the predictor stays below $0.006\%$ up to $k = 1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. We run a toy power spectrum analysis in the CPL parametrization demonstrating that a $w_0$-only emulator could produce the same posterior without any knowledge of the full $w_0w_a$ model. This matching prescription thus offers a new tool to constrain dynamical dark energy models with arbitrary equations of state at the field level, without running additional simulation suites.

authors.name: Pavel Demidov, Carolina Cuesta-Lazaro, Peter L. Taylor

papers.title: A Tributary of Tucana III? The Sutlej Stellar Stream in DELVE DR3
papers.summary: We present the first analysis of the Sutlej stellar stream using deep DECam photometry from the third data release of the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey (DELVE DR3). Sutlej was discovered in Gaia DR3 as two parallel branches of old, metal-poor stars in projection near the SMC. Our DELVE DR3 sample reaches $\sim$2.5-3.5 mag below the main-sequence turnoff of Sutlej, and with a main-sequence matched filter built from an isochrone fit to Sutlej, we recover both previously identified branches, and find additional structure between them and at the periphery of the stream, occupying a region of $\sim$11$^\circ$ $\times$ 7$^\circ$ scattered at $\sim$23-33 kpc. We investigate this region by separating it into four segments that have Sutlej-like properties. The isochrone is also consistent with the nearby ultra-faint satellite Tucana III (Tuc III), and the two systems have similar distances and proper motions. $N$-body simulations of a Tuc III-like satellite show that, once the passage of a massive LMC is accounted for, Tuc III's preceding pericentric passage was deep enough to strip most of the progenitor. The encounter with the LMC then spreads the debris across the Sutlej field at the observed distances and proper motions, though the models do not recreate the observed discrete overdensities. We find that Sutlej is compatible with a Tuc III origin.

Carlin, William Cerny, Denija Crnojevi\'c, Alex Drlica-Wagner, Denis Erkal, Alexander P. Ji, Guilherme Limberg, Pol Massana, Noelia E. D. No\"el, Andrew B. Pace, Alexander H. Riley, David J. Sand, Guy S. Stringfellow, Julio A. Carballo-Bello, Anirudh Chiti, Yumi Choi, David J. James, Clara E. Mart\'inez-V\'azquez, Gustavo E. Medina, Bur\c{c}in Mutlu-Pakdil, Mahdieh Navabi, David L. Nidever, A. Katherina Vivas, Alfredo Zenteno

papers.title: Predicting the Orbital Retention of Habitable-Zone Planets Following Stellar Flybys Using Machine Learning
papers.summary: Stellar flybys can significantly alter the orbital configurations of planetary systems, potentially displacing planets initially located within the habitable zone (HZ) of their host stars. In this study, we investigate the dynamical effects of stellar encounters on HZ planets using a large suite of three-body N-body simulations. We examine how the properties of the host star, passing star, planetary orbit, and encounter geometry influence the final orbital configuration. A planet is considered to retain an HZ orbit only if it remains bound to its original host and its entire final orbital range, from periastron to apastron, lies within the HZ boundaries. Based on the simulation results, we develop an XGBoost classifier to predict the final HZ status of planets following stellar encounters. The model achieves an accuracy of 0.90, an ROC-AUC of 0.97, and a PR-AUC of 0.97 on the test set. Feature importance analysis identifies the encounter-impulse parameter as the dominant predictor of the outcome. The classifier provides a computational speedup of approximately 74 compared with direct N-body simulations. We further evaluate the model using an independent dataset representing a globular-cluster environment, where approximately 20 per cent of planets retain HZ orbits. Despite the naturally imbalanced class distribution, the model achieves an accuracy of 0.87, an ROC-AUC of 0.92, and a PR-AUC of 0.77. These results demonstrate the potential of machine learning for efficiently predicting the dynamical retention of HZ planets following stellar encounters and for investigating their outcomes in dense stellar environments.

authors.name: Fatemeh Rahimi, Ahmad Farhani Asl

papers.title: Binning is Sinning: Absolution for the Unbinned Supernova Hubble Diagram
papers.summary: Cosmological analyses of Type Ia supernovae use a covariance matrix to describe statistical noise and systematic uncertainties. To fit a Hubble diagram with an unbinned covariance matrix, the CPU cost scales as O(N^3) for N supernovae, which has motivated compression into bins that loses information and reduces self-calibration power. To remove the need for lossy compression, we present a method that greatly reduces CPU time for matrix inversion and cosmology fitting, as well as matrix storage. For systematic covariances constructed from K per-supernova distance-shift vectors, we retain the exact representation C = D + U U^T, with diagonal statistical covariance D, and use the Woodbury factorization identity to efficiently invert C, significantly reducing computing time and disk storage without losing information. We implement this method in SNANA and validate it on simulated samples for LSST (N ~ 5,300, K = 18), Roman+LSST (N ~ 15,000, K = 30), and 10-yr LSST (N ~ 134,400, K = 18). For 10-yr LSST, matrix inversion and cosmology fit time is ~10 weeks using a dense (unbinned) matrix with 18 billion elements, and is reduced to ~1.5 hr using the factorization method. It also reduces covariance matrix disk storage by a factor of 1,800 (36 GB to 20 MB). In all validation tests, the best-fit cosmological parameters are nearly identical to the unbinned fit, and the dark energy figure of merit (FoM) agrees to better than 0.1% accuracy; the small differences are likely due to numerical artifacts in the pipeline. For the LSST and Roman era, this factorization method enables large unbinned supernova analyses with significantly reduced computing resources compared to previous analyses using a dense matrix, while preserving all information in the covariance model.

authors.name: Ayan Mitra, Anish Mukherjee, Richard Kessler

papers.title: The XRISM view of the front and rear ejecta dynamics in Tycho's SNR
papers.summary: We present a line-of-sight dynamics study of Tycho's supernova remnant (SNR) with XRISM/Resolve, based on five pointings obtained during the first two years of the mission. Thanks to a spectral resolution better than 5 eV, the spectra reveal a clear Doppler splitting of the Si, S, Ar, Ca and Fe emission lines towards the center of the remnant, allowing us to study the front and back sides of the shocked ejecta independently for the first time. Using a phenomenological Gaussian line model and a Bayesian fitting method, we analyze the broadband spectra of each pointing and of 149 individual pixels. We derive the dynamics and flux of the front and back sides for each element, as well as a global line broadening. The dynamics of Tycho's SNR are asymmetric, with the back side expanding faster than the front side for Si, S and Fe. We reveal a line-of-sight stratification of the elements, with Fe at lower velocities than Si and S. Si shows a strong front/back flux asymmetry, the front side being up to twice as bright as the back side in the northeastern part of the remnant. A similar but weaker asymmetry is found for S. For Fe, the flux ratio varies spatially, with either side dominating. These measurements allow us to reassess the average line-of-sight kinematics obtained at CCD resolution, which is affected by the flux asymmetry between the front and back sides and not only by a velocity asymmetry. Combining our line-of-sight velocities with Chandra proper motions, we reconstruct the three-dimensional dynamics of Tycho's SNR. Finally, we discuss the constraints these results set on the explosion model and the progenitor system.

authors.name: L. Godinaud, A. Decourchelle, R. Giuffrida, T. Tanaka, C. Badenes, G. Ferrand, J. Ballet, T. Holland-Ashford, A. Bamba, B. J. Williams, T. Mizuno, F. Acero, J. Vink

papers.title: Modelling of post-reconstruction galaxy clustering with a hybrid bias expansion
papers.summary: Density-field reconstruction sharpens the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature and recovers part of the cosmological information lost from two-point statistics through nonlinear evolution. Exploiting reconstructed clustering beyond BAO measurements requires modelling nonlinear evolution and galaxy formation physics. We extend the hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion to post-reconstruction galaxy clustering in configuration space and determine its range of validity. We apply a single reconstruction displacement to each Eulerian basis field of a second-order hybrid expansion, retaining the same bias parameters before and after reconstruction. We fit the correlation-function multipoles of subhalo abundance-matching mocks in real and redshift space, considering RecIso and RecSym, and use a Fisher analysis to forecast constraints on $\sigma_8$ and $\Omega_{\rm m}$. The model reproduces the pre- and post-reconstruction multipoles for $r>35 h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ with a single set of Lagrangian bias parameters. For a $3 h^{-3}\mathrm{Gpc}^3$ volume at $z\simeq0$ with $\bar{n}=5\times10^{-4} h^3\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, post-reconstruction clustering (POST) alone tightens the marginalised constraint on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ by a factor of $\sim1.3$ relative to pre-reconstruction clustering (PRE), but slightly weakens that on $\sigma_8$ when the reconstruction bias is inferred from the observed clustering amplitude. Combining PRE and POST reduces both marginalised uncertainties by about one third and increases the figure of merit by a factor of $\sim2.2$, mainly by breaking degeneracies between bias and cosmology. Pre- and post-reconstruction clustering contain complementary cosmological information and can be modelled within the same hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion. The framework is well suited to emulation and future joint full-shape analyses of galaxy surveys.

authors.name: Vicente Izzo Dominguez, Raul E. Angulo, Antonio D. Montero-Dorta, Marcos Pellejero-Ib\'a\~nez

papers.title: Detection of a warm absorber in a highly variable low-redshift quasar
papers.summary: { 3XMMJ115535.8+232723 (z=0.136) is a low-redshift radio-quiet quasar, which shows an unusual spectral nature. The X-ray properties and variability of this source have never been studied.} {Using numerous X-ray observations, this study aims to perform a detailed spectral analysis for 3XMMJ115535.8+232723. Having produced spectra from different flux states, the aims of the study is to investigate long-term spectral behaviour in a single object outside the local group of AGNs.} { We used {\it XMM-Newton} and {\it Chandra} observations of quasar 3XMMJ115535.8+232723 obtained between 2000 and 2008 to derive the spectroscopic details. We analyzed 0.3--10 keV spectra using an absorbed powerlaw model in combination with a warm absorber component.} {The first spectroscopic analysis of 3XMMJ115535.8+232723 reveals that the X-ray spectrum imprints a strong absorption feature, prominent at $\sim 0.7$ keV, which has been interpreted to be due to absorption in a partially ionized material (a.k.a. warm absorber). The column density and ionization parameter of the warm absorber vary by more than an order of magnitude for different observations. The results are consistent with high density clouds located ($\sim 1000$ gravitational radius) from the central region and another set of low density clouds further away. The intrinsic flux and spectral shape of the source also varies significantly over the observations.}

authors.name: SH. M. Shehata, Samuzal Barua, Ranjeev Misra

papers.title: Performance of attention-based deep-learning models in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor measurements
papers.summary: A systematic performance evaluation of attention-based deep-learning models for wavefront reconstruction in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor (SHWFS) systems is presented. While deep learning has been extensively applied to pyramid and focal-plane wavefront sensing, its application to standard SHWFS configurations remains relatively underexplored. A simulation dataset consisting of 3.5 million open-loop uncorrelated turbulent phase and image pairs modeled after the Subaru Telescope pupil was generated. The dataset spans four pupil-sampling cases (8$\times$8, 16$\times$16, 20$\times$20, and 32$\times$32 subapertures) under realistic conditions. A custom Vision Transformer (ViT) which incorporates features such as rotary positional embeddings, register tokens, and a cross-attention decoder, is benchmarked against a fully convolutional U-Net and a classical Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) linear reconstructor. The results show that the ViT architecture yields the lowest overall residual phase variance across all tested subaperture configurations, demonstrating a robust capability to model global spatial correlations and spot-to-spot cross-coupling across the pupil. While the U-Net performs competitively by capturing localized features, it exhibits $\sim1.5$ times more residual variance per mode than the ViT, which is relatively significant in high-order modes. This study represents a key step toward implementing attention-based models for high-order wavefront sensing and telemetry-assisted data reduction in next-generation instrument suites like ULTIMATE-Subaru.

authors.name: Matias Marambio-Jimenez, Yosuke Minowa, Yoshito Ono, Hajime Ogane, Shin Oya, Yusei Koyama, Masayuki Akiyama

papers.title: XRISM view of a featureless cluster Abell 1060: Revealing the advection of a diffuse radio source by ICM motions
papers.summary: Abell 1060 is a nearby, dynamically relaxed galaxy cluster hosting the extended radio structure Flying Fox (FF) near its center. We used high-resolution XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy to measure intracluster medium (ICM) motions and velocity dispersion. Spatially resolved analysis reveals a velocity gradient of approximately 100 km/s along FF and enhanced velocity dispersion near the brightest cluster galaxy NGC 3311, suggesting turbulence generated by galaxy-ICM interactions. These results and the compact extent of FF favor fossil plasma supplied by past activity of the brightest cluster galaxy and transported by ICM motions. We also tested whether the measured turbulence could generate or maintain the nonthermal components of FF. For a velocity dispersion of $96.7^{+23.9}_{-24.6}$ km/s and an assumed turbulence scale of 50 kpc, comparable to the Resolve field of view and approximately half the cluster core radius, the turbulent energy flux is approximately $3.49 \times 10^{-28}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. Although this flux may weakly reenergize pre-existing relativistic electrons, the acceleration timescale of approximately 2.5 Gyr exceeds the synchrotron and inverse Compton cooling timescale of approximately 210 Myr. The present turbulence is therefore insufficient to accelerate electrons to high energies. In situ turbulent reacceleration is unlikely to dominate the generation of FF, although it may help maintain fossil electrons supplied by past AGN activity. These results link ICM dynamics to the origin of nonthermal emission and support a time-evolutionary picture of particle acceleration in galaxy clusters.

authors.name: Kohei Kurahara, Kazuhiro Nakazawa, Yuki Omiya, Daisuke Ito, Kosuke Nishiwaki, Andrea Botteon, Takuya Akahori, Noriko Y. Yamasaki, Liyi Gu, Kosuke Sato, Takayuki Tamura

papers.title: Radiation-Hydrodynamical Modeling of Accretion Columns in Ultraluminous X-ray Pulsars
papers.summary: Ultraluminous X-ray pulsars (ULXPs) provide a unique laboratory for studying accretion-column physics under strongly magnetized super-Eddington conditions. In this work, we employ a one-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamical model to investigate the vertical structure of ULXP accretion columns, applying it to NGC 300 ULX-1, Swift J0243.6$+$6124, and SMC X-3. We solve the coupled conservation equations for the inflowing gas and radiation field in a dipole-funnel geometry, allowing the velocity, density, gas pressure, radiation pressure, total energy transport rate, radiation sonic surface, and thermal mound location to be determined self-consistently. We find that radiation pressure naturally produces an extended sinking region above the stellar surface, where the inflowing gas is gradually decelerated and its kinetic energy is converted into radiation energy that partly escapes through the column walls. Despite their different luminosities, magnetic fields, and column geometries, the radiation sonic surfaces are tightly clustered near $15$ km, indicating a similar large-scale radiative deceleration structure. These results show that ULXP accretion columns develop extended radiation-dominated structures regulated by the mass accretion rate, magnetic scattering opacity, and column geometry. The dynamical profiles obtained here provide a physical basis for interpreting radiation-dominated accretion columns in ULXPs and for future physics-based spectral modeling.

authors.name: Hong-Bo Li, Ziming Wang, Bo-Yan Chen, Shu Zhang, Ren-Xin Xu

papers.title: Environmental dependence of the properties of H$\alpha$ emitters in the extremely massive galaxy protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 at $z = 2.24$
papers.summary: Protoclusters, the progenitors of galaxy clusters, provide ideal laboratories for studying how high-density environments influence galaxy formation and evolution at early cosmic epochs. It remains unclear whether environmental effects on galaxy properties over scales of $>30$ cMpc are already in place at $z > 2$ and how these effects depend on the evolutionary stage of large-scale structures. We investigate the physical properties of H$\alpha$ emitters (HAEs) in two extremely overdense protoclusters, BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, at $z = 2.24$, and explore the environmental dependence of galaxy properties at this redshift. In BOSS1244, we find a clear color-density and stellar mass-density relation. HAEs in higher-density regions are significantly redder in $z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}$ and more massive than those in lower-density regions. In contrast, BOSS1542 shows weak or no such correlations. Red HAEs $(z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}>2.5)$ in both fields are preferentially located in the densest cores, have high stellar masses $(>10^{11}\,M_{\odot})$, high SFRs, and are $4-7$ times more abundant than in general fields. The irregular morphologies observed in some red HAEs are consistent with ongoing mass assembly and may be associated with dust-obscured star formation or galaxy interactions. Both protoclusters broadly follow the star-forming main sequence, but BOSS1542 exhibits a steeper slope, indicating more active star formation in massive galaxies. Our results demonstrate that environmental effects on galaxy properties operate over scales of $\sim39$\,cMpc at $z=2.24$, but their manifestation is strongly dependent on the evolutionary state of the large-scale structure. BOSS1244 appears more evolved, with ongoing galaxy merging and possible quenching, while BOSS1542 remains in an early, filamentary, gas-rich phase.

authors.name: Dongdong Shi (AUST), XianZhong Zheng (SJTU), Zheng Cai (Tsinghua), Xiaohui Fan (UA), Xin Wang (UCAS), Helmut Dannerbauer (IAC), Fangxia An (YNAO), Zhizheng Pan (PMO), Yuheng Zhang (NJU), Run Wen (SJTU), Shuang Liu (CHNU), Yongming Liang (NAOJ)

papers.title: No Evidence of Cold Trapping in the Dayside Atmosphere of WASP-33 b
papers.summary: Ultra-hot Jupiters allow simultaneous measurements of volatile molecules and refractory metals, providing constraints on atmospheric chemistry and refractory-element sequestration. We reanalyze the previously published Gemini-N/IGRINS-2 dayside emission spectra of WASP-33~b, extending the analysis to neutral refractory species. Using cross-correlation (CC) and likelihood-based (LL) detection methods, we recover the strongest species detection signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) from CO ($\rm CC~S/N=5.29,\ LL~S/N=5.62$). \ion{Mg}{1} ($\rm CC~S/N=3.88,\ LL~S/N=4.73$) and OH ($\rm CC~S/N=3.88,\ LL~S/N=3.89$) are recovered at lower significance in both metrics. H$_2$O remains marginal, appearing only in the cross-correlation analysis ($\rm CC~S/N=3.24$), while \ion{Ti}{1} ($\rm LL~S/N=3.70$) and \ion{Ca}{1} ($\rm LL~S/N=2.98$) show tentative signals. We do not detect \ion{Fe}{1}, \ion{Si}{1}, and \ion{V}{1} in this dataset. A chemical-equilibrium retrieval with a flexible Bezier-spline pressure--temperature profile yields ${\rm C/O}=0.65^{+0.09}_{-0.10}$ and $[{\rm M/H}]=-0.48^{+0.24}_{-0.18}$, and a refractory-to-volatile ratio of $[R/V]_{\rm p}=-0.15^{+0.24}_{-0.23}$. The corresponding stellar-normalized value is $[R/V]_{\rm p/ \star}=0.37^{+0.38}_{-0.36}$, but this value is sensitive to the stellar oxygen abundance. We find that the atmospheric Ti/Mg and Ca/Mg ratios of WASP-33~b are consistent with their respective stellar values within 68\% confidence. This is in contrast to other ultra-hot Jupiters with lower equilibrium temperatures that often show depleted Ti abundances compared to other metals, indicative of cold-trapping. This would suggest that even the nightside of WASP-33~b is too hot for significant condensation and sequestration to occur. Comparison with disk-chemistry models remains exploratory because the carbon-to-refractory posterior overlaps several formation scenarios.
