Hayward, Hyewon Suh, Jen Miller, Siyi Xu, Emanuele Paolo Farina, Charlie Figura, Teo Mocnik, Zachary Hartman, Mark Rawlings, Andrew Stephens, Bryan Miller, Kathleen Labrie, Paul Hirst

papers.title: Shifting the snow line in protoplanetary disks by planet-induced multiple spiral shocks
papers.summary: The snow line location provides important constraints on rocky planet formation. Recent magnetohydrodynamical simulations suggest that Joule heating associated with gas accretion is so inefficient that the snow line can be located inside 1 au around a solar-type star. This challenges in-situ formation of the terrestrial planets in the solar system unless other internal heating processes are present. Previous studies have proposed that spiral shocks induced by an embedded planet potentially shift the snow line outward. In this study, we investigate the impact of shock heating induced by a giant planet on the location of the snow line in two steps. First, we perform two-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of a disk with a giant planet to model shock heating rates. We construct an empirical formula for total entropy jumps due to multiple spiral shocks interior to the planetary orbit. Second, we calculate the radial temperature profile based on the thermal balance with the modeled shock heating rates. We find that shock heating can substantially increase the disk temperature in inner regions far from the planet when the planetary mass and disk optical depth are sufficiently high. For example, assuming a fixed surface density profile and an opacity of $\kappa = 1~\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}$, a planet with one-third of Jupiter's current mass at 5 au can shift the snow line outward beyond 1 au. Our results suggest that the early formation of proto-Jupiter in the solar nebula may have enabled rocky planetesimals and protoplanets to form in the present-day terrestrial planet region without invoking additional water removal processes.

authors.name: Shizu Shimizu, Ryosuke T. Tominaga, Satoshi Okuzumi, Takayuki Muto

papers.title: Continuum Pumping Revises Metallicity in the Orion Nebula
papers.summary: The enrichment of heavy elements in the interstellar medium is central to understanding galaxy evolution. Oxygen, the most abundant element after H and He, provides the principal tracer of gas-phase metallicity, typically measured using nebular emission lines in star-forming regions. However, a long-standing issue-the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF)-produces a $\sim 0.25$ dex offset between metallicities derived from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs). We present deep spectroscopic observations of the Orion Nebula (M42), and use them to assess the contribution of the often neglected continuum pumping process. We find that the continuum pumping effect is at least a factor of two stronger than previously expected. After accounting for the flux contribution from continuum pumping, the RL metallicity is consistent with the CEL metallicity, thus explaining the bulk of the ADF. Reassessing O/H measurements in five literature star-forming regions using the same method, we similarly find a systematic reduction of RL-based metallicities. These results indicate that RL metallicities, which have previously been considered more reliable than CELs, are subject to potentially large bias from continuum pumping. This study provides a foundation to correct this bias and establish accurate element abundance scales throughout cosmic time.

authors.name: Yuguang Chen, Tucker Jones, Ryan Sanders, Paige Kelly, Zhuo Cheng, Xuan Fang, Sunny Rhoades, Keerthi Vasan GC, Fabio Bresolin, Rodrigo Herrera-Camus, Erin Huntzinger, Xiao-Wei Liu, Peter Senchyna, Charles Steidel, Renbin Yan, Danielle Berg, Dario Fadda, Ryan Rickards Vaught, Guido Roberts-Borsani, Daniel Stark, Jessica Sutter, Bejamin Weiner

papers.title: Revisiting Evidence of Temperature Fluctuations in H II Regions. I. Interionic temperature differences
papers.summary: The oxygen abundance of H II regions is a fundamental tracer of chemical enrichment and gas cycling and is now routinely measured across a broad range of cosmic time. A persistent complication is the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF): the O$^{++}$/H$^+$ abundance inferred from optical recombination lines (RLs) is systematically higher than that inferred from collisionally excited lines (CELs). Small-scale temperature fluctuations within the O$^{++}$-emitting gas are among the most widely discussed explanations for this discrepancy. However, the recent identification of a substantial continuum-pumping contribution to the O II spectrum of M42 motivates a renewed assessment of which observations uniquely favor a temperature-based interpretation and which are also compatible with other mechanisms. In this first paper of a series, I examine the relation between the inferred temperature-fluctuation parameter, $t^2$, and interionic temperature differences, focusing on $\Delta T_e=T_e([OIII])-T_e([NII])$. Photoionization calculations show that ionization stratification naturally produces systematic temperature differences between the low- and high-ionization zones. Meanwhile, the conversion from an ADF to $t^2$ is strongly temperature dependent because CEL emissivities are nonlinear functions of electron temperature. I show that these two effects can account for much of the observed $t^2$-$\Delta T_e$ relation without requiring the interionic temperature difference itself to trace fluctuations within the O$^{++}$ zone. This result does not exclude temperature fluctuations in H II regions. Instead, it indicates that interionic temperature differences should be interpreted with care and, on their own, provide limited discrimination among proposed origins of the ADF.

authors.name: Yuguang Chen

papers.title: Offsets in gravitational wave burst timing in eccentric black hole binaries with stellar-mass tertiaries
papers.summary: At present, the formation scenarios producing observed compact binary coalescences (CBCs) are relatively unconstrained. Such mergers are thought to occur efficiently in hierarchical triple systems, with three-body dynamics and stellar interactions from the tertiary inducing mergers in the inner binary. Deducing the presence of a tertiary in an observed gravitational wave (GW) signal from a merging binary would be a smoking gun for this specific formation scenario, offering constraints on the evolution of CBC progenitors and multiple star systems. We present a fast model for the effect of tertiary perturbation on observed GW signals from generically-oriented eccentric inner binaries. We apply the model to two populations of triples with merging inner binaries: (1) a group of wide triples whose inner binary was driven to merger through excitations of the inner eccentricity due to three-body dynamics and von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai (ZKL); and (2) compact triples with chemically homogenously evolving (CHE) inner binaries that merge after experiencing mass transfer from the tertiary companion. When viewed face-on, the expected offset in the burst arrival time for the compact (CHE) triples varies by orders of magnitude depending on the properties of the triple system, with the majority of systems having an offset between $10^{-2}$ to $10^2$ seconds. A smaller fraction of the population with the highest inner eccentricities show the largest offset at $10^3$ to $10^6$ seconds. For the wide (ZKL) systems, the vast majority experience negligible perturbation from the tertiary. With an inclination of $\pi/2$ with respect to the observer both the compact and wide triple populations are expected to have offsets on the order of $10^3$ to $10^4$ seconds.

authors.name: C. W. Bruenech, I. Romero-Shaw, N. Loutrel, S. Toonen

papers.title: Interpreting the $\gamma$-Ray Emission of the Cygnus X region with a Combined Cygnus OB2 and Cygnus X-3 Scenario
papers.summary: The recent detection of high-energy $\gamma$-ray emission up to PeV energies from the Cygnus X region points to the presence of a PeVatron therein. This region hosts notable candidates such as the Cygnus OB2 association, which may be associated with PeV $\gamma$-photons detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO). The X-ray binary Cygnus X-3 also lies along the line of sight to the Cygnus X region, and LHAASO has observed modulated PeV $\gamma$-ray flux from its direction, indicating that its contribution is also non-negligible. Here, we attempt to interpret the $\gamma$-ray emission of the Cygnus X region using a combined scenario. Assuming a hadronic origin, we consider contributions from Cygnus OB2, Cygnus X-3, and Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs). Our results show that Cygnus OB2 alone, or its combination with the GCR component, is insufficient to account for the multiwavelength observations, whereas including the $\gamma$-ray emission from Cygnus X-3 naturally explains these observations. This suggests that the $\gamma$-ray emission from the Cygnus X region has a more complex origin, necessitating a joint consideration of Cygnus OB2 and Cygnus X-3. The expected neutrino flux from hadronic interactions extends into the GeV band and can help reveal the radiation mechanism of Cygnus X-3, underscoring the need for high-sensitivity GeV neutrino observatories.

authors.name: Caijin Xie, Zhihao Ouyang, Yudong Cui, Lili Yang

papers.title: Centimetre-sized meteoroids from the active asteroid (3200) Phaethon: lunar impact flashes during the 2018 and 2025 Geminids
papers.summary: Centimetre-sized meteoroids released by the active asteroid (3200) Phaethon, parent of the Geminid meteor shower, probe the ejection of refractory material from a comet-asteroid transition object and the age of the stream; lunar impact flashes (LIFs) are the only ground-based technique that samples this size range. We determine the impact flux, mass and size distributions, and expected crater sizes of Geminid meteoroids on the Moon from campaigns at the 2018 and 2025 maxima, and test the stability of the centimetre-sized population over seven years. Both campaigns used the Nihon University 0.40 m "GUNDAM" telescope with CMOS video cameras at 60 fps, with candidates validated at independent stations; a common aperture-photometry pipeline calibrated in the Cousins R band gave peak magnitudes to 0.1-0.25 mag. Eleven LIFs were detected in 3.3 h in 2018 and nine in 2.2 h in 2025, all with Geminid probabilities of 0.87-0.96. With monitored areas measured on the video frames, the campaigns give consistent fluxes of $4.2\times10^{-7}$ and $5.2\times10^{-7}$ km$^{-2}$ h$^{-1}$ (merged: $4.6\times10^{-7}$ km$^{-2}$ h$^{-1}$). For a luminous efficiency of $1.4\times10^{-3}$ the impactors have masses of 10-320 g, diameters of 1.8-5.9 cm, and predicted crater rim diameters of 2-5 m. The combined sample gives a maximum-likelihood mass index $s=1.76\pm0.17$ and a population index $r=2.0\pm0.3$, markedly shallower than the NELIOTA all-flash values; a single power law with this slope connects the Global Meteor Network millimetre flux to the LIF centimetre flux. The Geminid stream delivers an excess of large particles relative to the sporadic background, consistent with an asteroidal origin, and its stable centimetre-sized flux over seven years constrains stream-formation models with ages of $2\times10^3$-$2\times10^4$ yr.

authors.name: Shinsuke Abe, Noriaki Arima, Misaki Nishikata, Yuto Araki, Tsubasa Aoki, Shotaro Akutsu, Jungo Okuyama, Ryota Fuse, Daichi Fujii, Shinji Sato, Toshinari Tanaka, Ryuhei Yamada, Satoshi Tanaka, Hiroaki Shiraishi, Keisuke Onodera, Taichi Kawamura, Masahisa Yanagisawa

papers.title: The MeerKAT absorption line survey: Galactic OH absorption at 18 cm
papers.summary: We present a blind search for Galactic OH 18-cm absorption lines towards 19,130 radio sources brighter than 1mJy at 1.4GHz, using 390 pointings of the MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS). We apply an automated line search followed by Bayesian nested sampling to identify OH 1667MHz, 1665MHz and 1612MHz absorption features, using HI emission and absorption profiles as physically motivated priors. We identify 15 confident detections of OH 1667/1665 MHz absorption. The majority of detections are associated with a visual extinction ($A_{\rm V}$) excess and, within the same MALS pointings, with detected CO emission and a high incidence rate of HI absorption, consistent with OH tracing the H$_2$-bearing medium. We also identify 9 candidates of OH 1612MHz satellite line absorption, two of which coincide with OH main line detections and show integrated optical depth ratios well above the LTE expectation of 1:9. As in previous studies, $N(\rm OH)$ shows no dependence on $N$(HI). Accounting for the varying sensitivity across sight lines, we estimate the covering fraction of OH-bearing gas at $\log N(\rm OH) > 12$ to be $C = 0.051 \pm 0.008$, providing an independent and a more precise estimate than previous measurements of the diffuse molecular gas. We also find qualitative evidence for a decrease of the covering fraction with Galactic latitude. Stacking reveals a clear OH absorption signal that becomes increasingly prominent when sight lines are weighted by $A_{\rm V}$ excess, independently confirming the association of OH with diffuse molecular gas. Modeling of the physical conditions yields hydrogen number densities of 10-100 cm$^{-3}$, typical H$_2$ column densities $\log N(\rm H_2) > 21$, and UV-flux to number density ratios of 0.01-0.3 Mathis cm$^{3}$, typical of the CNM.

authors.name: S. A. Balashev, N. Gupta, H. -W. Chen, F. Combes, J. Kerp, H. -R. Kl\"ockner, D. Kosenko, J. -K. Krogager, P. Noterdaeme

papers.title: Non-Equilibrium Steady States in Nucleosynthesis
papers.summary: Steady-state behavior underlies many nucleosynthesis processes in which the population number of nuclei can remain nearly constant despite the rapid nuclear reactions. While existing theoretical descriptions largely focus on established chemical equilibrium, as in nuclear statistical equilibrium (NSE) and quasi equilibrium (QSE), non-equilibrium steady states (NESSs) can form in process-specific approximations such as classical $\beta$-flow $r$-process. We develop a general framework for describing NESSs in nuclear reaction networks by formulating the steady-state condition as a balance of reaction flows within a reduced linear description of the relevant network subset. We apply the framework to four representative nucleosynthesis scenarios spanning different steady-state regimes: disequilibrium between nucleons and $\alpha$ particles during $\alpha$-rich freeze-out, the classical $\beta$-flow steady state, the neutrino-assisted $\nu r$-process, and the fission-cycling phase of the $r$-process. In particular, the fission-cycling scenario is described by a quasi-steady-state (QSS) approximation maintaining the population ratios between two nuclei while not conserving the total number of nuclei. The framework reproduces the characteristic abundance pattern for each case while providing a unified interpretation of the underlying steady-state behavior. The eigenvalue spectrum reveals network structure and characterizes the relaxation timescales of abundance distributions. These results establish a general approach for analyzing nucleosynthesis beyond the condition of chemical equilibrium and provide a foundation for extending graph-based methods to complicated nuclear reaction networks.

authors.name: Zewei Xiong, Gabriel Mart\'inez-Pinedo

papers.title: Lithium rich stars in M67: Searching for hot companions through UV observations
papers.summary: Lithium-rich (Li-rich) stars are a rare class of objects characterized by an abnormally high Li abundance in their atmospheres. Although several explanations, including binary interactions, have been proposed, their origin remains uncertain. We aim to search for hot companions to the known Li-rich stars in M67, characterize these stars, and evaluate the binary hypothesis as a possible explanation for their Li enhancement. We combined archival ultraviolet photometry from UVIT/AstroSat, GALEX, and Swift/UVOT with optical and infrared photometry to create multiwavelength spectral energy distributions (SEDs) and search for hot companions. We also used high-resolution archival UVES spectra to look for chemical signatures of past binary interactions. Two known Li-rich stars in M67, WOCS6008 and WOCS2003, show a significant far-UV excess relative to a single-star SED fit, attributed to a companion in the former and to stellar activity in the latter. We thus report the first detection of a hot companion to the Li-rich star, WOCS6008, in M67, offering direct evidence of the role of binary interactions in its Li enrichment. The companion is found to be an extremely low-mass (ELM) white dwarf (WD) of $\sim 0.16\pm0.01 M_{\odot}$, consistent with its kinematic mass, and an age of 2.5 Gyr. We find no enhancement of Na or s-process elements and no depletion of C or Mg in WOCS6008, suggesting that mass transfer during the asymptotic giant branch or red giant branch stage is unlikely. Its derived abundances support a scenario in which this star is the accretor in a binary system that underwent early Case B mass transfer. Our results support previous suggestions that stellar rotation is the most favored mechanism for the Li enrichment in this post-interaction system. Overall, the available evidence supports the case for binary interactions as one of the channels to form Li-rich stars.

authors.name: S. Rani, E. Pancino, D. Alvarez Garay, C. Watts, A. Avdeeva, M. Echeveste, E. I. Leitinger, S. Nedhath, E. Reggiani, N. Sanna, S. Saracino, L. Steinbauer, A. Turchi

papers.title: Deep UV Spectroscopy of an Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxy at z = 5.725
papers.summary: We present deep X-shooter follow-up spectroscopy of AMORE6, an exceptionally metal-poor galaxy at z = 5.725. The new spectrum provides stringent upper limits on rest-frame ultraviolet metal lines, including NV, CIV, NIV], NIII], and OIII]. The non-detection of CIV breaks the density-metallicity degeneracy present in previous analyses based on the [OIII]/Hbeta ratio, excluding the high-density, chemically enriched gas scenario and strengthening the evidence for an extremely metal-poor environment. The X-shooter spectrum also reveals a narrow Lyman-alpha line with a velocity dispersion sigma_v = 23.2 +/- 0.5 km/s and a nearly symmetric profile centered at the systemic redshift measured from Hbeta. Combining the Lyman-alpha line width with the measured source size, we infer a dynamical mass M_dyn = (1-22) x 10^7 Msun, assuming that the line width traces gravitational motions. Spectral energy distribution modeling using Pop III and Pop II stellar population libraries yields stellar masses (1-5) x 10^5 Msun. Although all models reproduce the observed blue UV continuum and Halpha equivalent width (EW), none simultaneously reproduces the Hbeta luminosity and EW, with the observed Hbeta luminosity exceeding the model predictions by up to 3.7 sigma. Possible explanations include departures from standard recombination conditions or limitations in the adopted stellar population models. We discuss possible interpretations of AMORE6, including massive-star formation in an atomic-cooling halo and a gravitationally bound star cluster.

authors.name: Takahiro Morishita, Massimo Stiavelli, Zhaoran Liu, Matteo Messa, Eros Vanzella

papers.title: Dynamical calibration of a metallicity-dependent stellar mass--luminosity relation from Gaia wide binaries
papers.summary: The mass of a main-sequence star is usually estimated from its luminosity through a mass--luminosity relation (MLR). This relation depends on metallicity, and its empirical calibration relies on few stars with measured masses. We calibrate the MLR of single main-sequence stars in the Gaia $G$ band as a function of metallicity with $10\,559$ wide binaries. The projected relative speed and separation of a wide binary constrain its total mass statistically. We describe the stellar mass as a monotone function of absolute magnitude and metallicity and fit this function to all pairs. The metallicities come from Gaia low-resolution (XP) spectra and are calibrated by requiring that both stars of a pair have the same metallicity. The likelihood includes the measurement noise, the selection of the sample and pairs with an undetected close companion. The data constrain the MLR over $3.7\lesssim M_{\mathrm{G}} \lesssim11.8$\,mag and $-0.5\lesssim\ \mathrm{[M/H]} \lesssim0.4$, with a median statistical uncertainty of $2.5\%$ in mass. Tests of the model assumptions indicate an additional systematic uncertainty of up to $5\%$. At solar metallicity the MLR agrees with the PARSEC models to within $5\%$. At the faint end, the MIST, BaSTI, Dartmouth and BHAC15 models predict masses 8 to $22\%$ below our MLR. Published masses from orbits, eclipsing binaries and asteroseismology lie within about $10\%$ of our MLR for $M_{\mathrm{G}}<10.5$ mag. For fainter stars they are about $17\%$ lower. The origin of the difference at the faint end is not yet understood. Because a shift of $0.1$ dex in metallicity changes the mass by up to $5\%$, MLRs should be compared on a common metallicity scale.

authors.name: Yu-Ting Wang, Hans-Walter Rix, Yuan-Sen Ting, Jiadong Li, Chao Liu

papers.title: Luminosity function of millisecond pulsars in globular clusters from their gamma-ray emission
papers.summary: Millisecond pulsars (MSPs) are widely believed to be responsible for the gamma-ray emission of globular clusters (GCs), yet the underlying MSP gamma-ray luminosity function remains uncertain. Existing GC-based determinations of the latter often rely on external prescriptions for the number of MSPs in each cluster. In this work, we constrain the MSP gamma-ray luminosity function in Milky-Way GCs directly from gamma-ray spectral energy distributions (SEDs), establishing an inference strategy that remains computationally viable for joint analyses of large GC samples. We construct a forward model in which each GC hosts a population of MSPs whose luminosities are drawn from a universal log-normal luminosity function. Synthetic GC SEDs are generated by summing individual MSP spectra, and we infer posterior distributions using first a likelihood-based nested sampling method and then a simulation-based inference (SBI) approach. We show how the likelihood-based method becomes rapidly impractical as the number of jointly modelled clusters (and cluster-specific latent parameters) increases, whereas the SBI approach scales mildly with sample size and reproduces the likelihood-based posteriors in regimes where direct sampling is feasible. We then apply the SBI pipeline to Fermi-LAT SEDs from the 4FGL-DR4 catalog for a sample of 36 GC-associated sources, augmented by dedicated phase-resolved ON/OFF SEDs for two clusters hosting individually detected MSPs. For the real data sample, we obtain informative constraints on the luminosity-function parameters consistent with previous analyses that constrain the cluster-specific MSP counts via complementary multi-wavelength information.

authors.name: Francesca Calore, Christopher Eckner, Silvia Manconi, Francesco Xotta, Gabrijela Zaharija\v{s}

papers.title: A Cross-Domain Simulator and Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Global 21-cm Inference
papers.summary: End-to-end uncertainty propagation in scientific inference often requires repeated evaluation of coupled simulators spanning multiple physical domains, often at prohibitive computational cost. Global 21-cm cosmology is an extreme example: a millikelvin cosmological signal must be separated from radio foregrounds and instrumental effects four orders of magnitude larger, making inference acutely sensitive to model misspecification. Reliable recovery is therefore contingent on an exceptionally accurate model that jointly propagates uncertainty through the complete observational chain. We present a differentiable, GPU-accelerated hybrid forward model combining neural emulation of the cosmological signal, a physics-informed multi-resolution parameterisation of the galactic foregrounds, and a linear surrogate model of the antenna. This unifies simulators spanning astrophysics and computational electromagnetics while reducing evaluation time by a factor of $7.2\times10^{7}$. Using GPU-accelerated Nested Slice Sampling, we benchmark the framework across 100 unseen signal realisations and find that 94 injected profiles lie entirely within their corresponding 95% credible bands. Together, the simulator and reference Nested Slice Sampling results provide a demanding benchmark of posterior calibration, mode coverage, and evidence accuracy across next-generation stochastic samplers, simulation-based inference, and variational inference frameworks.

authors.name: Jacob Tutt, Harry Bevins, James Alvey, Dominic Anstey, John Cumner, Eloy de Lera Acedo, Anastasia Fialkov

papers.title: Estimating M Dwarf Ages using their Transiting Brown Dwarf Companions
papers.summary: Determining M dwarf ages remains challenging because of their slow main-sequence evolution. We investigate using transiting brown dwarfs to constrain system ages through their measured masses and thermal emission. We report Palomar/WIRC secondary-eclipse observations of two close-in brown dwarfs, LP 261-75C and AD 3116B, measuring eclipse depths of $6.1 \pm 0.3$ parts per thousand (ppt) in $K_s$ and $9.1 \pm 0.6$ ppt in $J$, respectively. Combining these observations with space-based transit photometry, radial velocities, and host star spectra, we infer brown dwarf internal luminosities and, assuming coevality, host star ages using five sets of atmospheric and evolutionary models. For LP 261-75C, model-dependent median ages span 1.3-2.9 Gyr, substantially older than the previously proposed age of 0.1-0.2 Gyr based on presumed membership in the AB Doradus moving group. This result, the host star's high metallicity, and the companion's measured radius disfavor AB Dor membership. The revised age implies a mass of $\approx 62$-$68$ $M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$ for the wide-orbit companion LP 261-75B, compared with an earlier estimate of $\approx 21$ $M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$. AD 3116B, a member of the 0.6-0.8 Gyr Praesepe cluster, provides a test of brown dwarf evolutionary models through independent constraints on its mass, age, and luminosity. Its inferred age depends strongly on cloud treatment, spanning 0.4-0.6 Gyr for cloudy models and 1.0-1.3 Gyr for cloudless models. Among the models considered, Sonora Diamondback, which includes cloud condensation and cloud clearing across the L/T boundary, provides a plausible simultaneous match to the observed eclipse depth and radius. These results demonstrate a new method to constrain M dwarf ages using emission observations of their brown dwarf companions, while highlighting the sensitivity of the inferred temperatures and ages to evolutionary model differences.

authors.name: Aryan Gupta, Steven Giacalone, Joshua N. Winn, Gregory J. Gilbert, Zafar Rustamkulov, Luke B. Handley, Andrew W. Howard, Jonathan Gomez Barrientos, Heather A. Knutson, Morgan Saidel

papers.title: Tidal effects of bulk viscosity in neutron stars
papers.summary: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter provides a temperature-dependent mechanism for tidal dissipation. In this study, we investigate the impact of bulk viscosity on the dissipative tidal response of neutron stars composed of neutrons, protons, and electrons. Employing cold equations of state derived through the momentum-dependent interaction model, we examine the bulk viscosity arising from the direct Urca process, which acts to restore chemical equilibrium. The temperature dependence is incorporated through the weak-interaction rate, allowing us to explore the behavior of bulk viscosity in the neutrino-transparent regime at temperatures up to a few MeV. To account for the spatial distribution of bulk viscosity within neutron stars, we introduce the effective bulk viscosity, a volume-averaged quantity over the region where direct Urca process operates, and establish a connection with the bulk viscosity. Specifically, we investigate its implications for tidal quantities, including the lag time and dissipative deformability, highlighting their dependence on temperature and stellar compactness. We find that the dissipative tidal effects become maximal at a temperature approximately coinciding with the one of maximum bulk viscosity on the onset of direct Urca. Additionally, these effects are more pronounced in intermediate neutron star masses compared to maximum ones. Finally, for both canonical $1.4\;M_\odot$ and maximum-mass neutron star configurations, we derive causality-based upper bounds on these quantities, providing theoretical benchmarks for assessing the potential observability of bulk-viscous effects in gravitational-wave signals from binary neutron star inspirals.

authors.name: A. Kanakis-Pegios, P. S. Koliogiannis, Ch. C. Moustakidis

papers.title: Interactions between the magnetised jets in the twin radio galaxy J104455+354055
papers.summary: Pairs of galaxies in which both objects host kiloparsec-scale radio jets are extremely rare. Such systems provide unique opportunity to study the formation of relativistic jets and their resistance to side-way collisions with each other prior to their eventual merger. We analyse the radio data for the twin radio galaxy J104455+354055 associated with a pair of distant elliptical galaxies (z=0.163). The radio jets of both sources avoid disruption/merging for the initial tens of kiloparsecs. We investigate the role of the magnetic fields in the propagation of these radio jets. We used VLA radio data at high frequencies in both compact and extended array configurations to obtain sensitive high-resolution polarimetric data and study the properties of the magnetic fields in all jets. Polarisation data suggest shearing of the magnetic fields at points where the jets bend. The orientation of the magnetic field parallel to jet axis helps confine the jet. Such field configuration in two adjacent jets seems to prevent them from merging. The strength of the magnetic field slightly increases in jet bends and the associated shearing enhances the ordered component of the magnetic field. The more diffuse radio plumes at the end of each jet have comparable strengths and energies of the magnetic field. The twin radio galaxy J104455+354055 provides a unique possibility to study the interplay of radio jets of two radio galaxies. The analysis of the properties of the magnetic fields observed along the radio jets suggests that the wiggles and bends of these jets, caused by the likely interactions of the host galaxies, could be also governed by the magnetic fields that may prevent them from merging. The derived strengths and energies of the magnetic field in different parts of the jets should allow us to improve the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of radio galaxies.

authors.name: M. Wezgowiec, R. Joshi, Gopal-Krishna, M. Jamrozy, S. Mondal, L. C. Ho, G. Giri

papers.title: Cross-calibration of Hera/HyperScout-H with MRO/CRISM and MEx/OMEGA based on Mars observations
papers.summary: On March 12, 2025, Hera, the European Space Agency's planetary defense mission, performed a Mars flyby en route to the asteroid system (65803) Didymos-Dimorphos. During this event, HyperScout-H (HS-H), the spacecraft's hyperspectral imager, acquired five high spatial resolution images over the southern hemisphere of Mars. These observations provide an opportunity for systematic cross-calibration of HS-H with two established Mars orbital instruments, Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM) on board the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (Murchie et al., 2007), and Observatoire pour la Min\'eralogie, l'Eau, les Glaces et l'Activit\'e (OMEGA) on board Mars Express (Bibring et al., 2004). This study evaluates the performance, reliability, and readiness of HS-H for the forthcoming asteroid observation phase by comparing it with CRISM and OMEGA data. We selected 21 surface regions spanning diverse terrain types from three HS-H images in which the Martian surface fills the entire field of view. These images were corrected, calibrated, and co-registered to associate each pixel with latitude and longitude. The relative inter-channel correction factors are close to unity for bands 3-25 (0.688-0.952 {\mu}m), with standard deviations of 0.52% for OMEGA and 0.62% for CRISM, indicating good agreement in spectral shape. Bands 1 and 2 show a systematic mismatch of 4.7% and 3.6%. The absolute flux correction factors reveal offsets of 8% relative to OMEGA and approximately 0.7% relative to CRISM, with mean inter-image standard deviations below 2%. These results confirm the radiometric stability of HS-H and establish a calibration framework for future Didymos-Dimorphos observations.

authors.name: A. Farina, M. Popescu, M. Lazzarin, J. de Le\'on, G. Prodan, B. A. Dumitru, F. La Forgia, G. Poggiali, M. K\"uppers, G. Kov\'acs, B. V. Nagy, B. Grieger, O. Barnouin, E. Tatsumi, \"O. Karatekin, P. Michel

papers.title: Characterization of solar background signatures in IXPE gas pixel detectors through laboratory measurements
papers.summary: We present a laboratory to in-flight comparison of the IXPE background signatures, using the spare Detector Unit (DU), identical to the three flight units, exposed to a Co-60 radioactive source, historically adopted as a proxy for solar-induced X-ray background. Co-60 emits 1.17 MeV and 1.33 MeV photons which undergo Compton scattering in the DU structures, producing a degraded spectrum extending down to the keV range after ADC counts to keV conversion via Fe-55 (charging measurement) calibration. The source was placed on the top and side of the DU; event tracks were reconstructed to extract spectral and morphological observables (track size, energy fraction in the track's main cluster, number of pixel triggered per event). Laboratory spectra and parameter distributions are compared with IXPE in-flight in-eclipse (Earth occultating the sun) and in-sun backgrounds from two observations (NGC 2110, RCW 86). We discuss how the in-flight and on-ground spectral and modulation properties of the background compare to each other.

authors.name: Simone Pagliarella, Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Paolo Soffitta, Enrico Costa, Alessandro Di Marco, Nicolas De Angelis, Alessandro Lacerenza, Fabio Muleri, Stefano Silvestri

papers.title: Two-Component Model for the Unidentified Extended Fermi-LAT Source 4FGL J1908.6+0915e / FL16Y J1908.6+0915e in the SGR 1900+14--W49A Sky Region
papers.summary: Galactic PeVatrons are expected to be powerful sources of non-thermal high-energy (HE, $E>100$ MeV) and very-high-energy (VHE, $E>100$ GeV) $\gamma$-ray emission as a manifestation of acceleration processes in supernova remnants (SNRs), star formation regions (SFRs), and pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe). In the sky region containing the magnetar SGR 1900+14 and the young massive star cluster (YMSC) W49A, there is one recently identified point-like source FL16Y J1910.2+0903, and there are three unidentified gamma-ray sources: the Fermi-LAT extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e, the HAWC extended source 4HWC J1908+0845, and the LHAASO point-like source LHAASO J1907+0913. We investigate the possibility of explaining the HE and VHE $\gamma$-ray emission from the SGR 1900+14--W49A sky region using a model of the Fermi-LAT extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e as superposition of two extended sources -- a potential SNR/PWN associated with the magnetar SGR 1900+14 and the stellar-wind superbubble adjacent to the YMSC W49A complex. To this end, we simulate the observed $\gamma$-ray emission in hadronic and leptonic models using the open NAIMA code and show that it consists of two extended regions: the stellar wind superbubble in W49A region -- an analog of the Westerlund 1 superbubble -- powered by the YMSC W49A (the southern part of the extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e); and the SGR 1900+14 region, powered by a potential SNR/PWN associated with the magnetar (the northern part of the extended source FL16Y J1908.6+0915e). However, due to the considerable distance to the magnetar ($d=12.5$ kpc), the required cosmic-ray energy budget in both hadronic and leptonic scenarios corresponds to a hypernova explosion and/or a powerful magnetar wind nebula created by a newly born millisecond magnetar with a rotational energy of the order of $10^{52}$ erg.

authors.name: Vadym Voitsekhovskyi, Roman Hnatyk, Bohdan Hnatyk, Lidiia Zadorozhna, Anastasiia Sokareva, Valentyna Babur, Olexandr Gugnin

papers.title: A Log-Normal Timing Likelihood for Direction Reconstruction of Ultra-High-Energy Gamma-Ray Air Showers
papers.summary: Ultra-high-energy $\gamma$-ray observations provide a direct probe of Galactic PeVatrons. Extending measurements to multi-PeV energies requires characterizing extensive air showers over large lateral distances, where the arrival-time distribution of secondary particles becomes broad and strongly asymmetric. Conventional direction reconstruction methods approximate the shower front as a deterministic surface and minimize a $\chi^2$ function of timing residuals. Because this implicitly assumes symmetric Gaussian errors, far-axis timing information is poorly utilized. \textsc{CORSIKA} simulations show that the arrival-time distribution of $\gamma$-induced secondary particles in the shower plane at a given lateral distance is positively skewed and closely follows a log-normal function. Using this property, we develop a likelihood-based direction reconstruction method that directly models the empirical arrival-time distribution and its radial dependence while accounting for multiple particles triggering the same detector unit. Applied to simulated $\gamma$-induced air showers, the log-normal likelihood consistently improves angular resolution compared with conical and parabolic wavefront fits, with the largest relative gains for high-energy events spanning wide lateral extents. We also show that independent readout of individual detector units yields better angular resolution than merging their signals into a single station-level measurement.

authors.name: Jun-Yu Shen, Yi Zhang, Jia-Yin He, Xing-Yu Li, Shi-Ping Zhao, Qiang Yuan

papers.title: X-ray polarimetry of a magnetar in the aftermath of an anti-glitch: Revisiting 1E 2259+586 with IXPE
papers.summary: Magnetars display timing anomalies such as glitches and anti-glitches. 1E 2259+586, whose properties in the X-ray band were recently investigated through a joint XMM/IXPE observation campaign, has been observed to have multiple glitches and three anti-glitches, the most recent occurring in May 2025. Although the X-ray emission is currently decaying, the flux, which roughly doubled at the onset of the anti-glitch, had not yet returned to its original level at the time of the IXPE observation, and the pulse profile has also shown significant evolution. We present an analysis of the recent IXPE observation of 1E 2259+586 from late April to early May 2026. We compare the post-anti-glitch polarisation results with those obtained from the previous IXPE observation in 2023. This provides an unprecedented opportunity to monitor the spectro-polarimetric evolution of a magnetar in the wake of a hallmark event such as an anti-glitch. A dedicated 400ks IXPE DDT observation was approved to track possible changes in the polarisation with respect to the pre-anti-glitch campaign. Spectral and polarimetric properties were jointly modelled within the xspec and ixpeobssim suites, and the analysis was further expanded using a maximum-likelihood technique. No significant detection was found in the phase-averaged and energy-integrated spectrum of this observation. However, despite the significantly shorter exposure, polarisation was clearly detected in the phase-resolved spectrum and the degree of polarisation was found to have a higher best-fitting value, though still statistically consistent, than the previous measurement from 2023, reaching a level >30% in correspondence to the pulse profile minimum. In spite of some slight differences between the two observations, the polarisation trends remain largely consistent and indicate that the source has mostly returned to its pre-event state.

authors.name: Ruth M. E. Kelly, Roberto Taverna, Roberto Turolla, Lorenzo Marra, Swati Ravi, Jeremy Heyl, Silvia Zane, Mingyu Ge, Hanlong Peng, Hua Feng, Sandro Mereghetti, Herman Marshall, Alice Borghese, Michela Rigoselli, Shuang-Nan Zhang, Gian Luca Israel

papers.title: Redshift-space 3$\times$2pt statistics of galaxy clustering and intrinsic alignments at one-loop order
papers.summary: Intrinsic alignments of galaxies, long regarded as a systematic in weak lensing, are now recognized as a cosmological probe complementary to galaxy clustering. Exploiting them with spectroscopic surveys requires accurate models in redshift space beyond the linear regime. In this work, we derive the galaxy density--shape cross-power spectrum and shape auto-power spectra at one-loop order in redshift space. We consider two models, one based on the effective field theory (EFT) and the other on the Taruya--Nishimichi--Saito (TNS) prescription. They share the bias expansion but differ in how they treat small-scale velocities along the line of sight. The EFT model expands the effects of these velocities perturbatively and absorbs their sensitivity to small scales into counterterms. We show that, for the sky-projected shape field, this model requires six renormalized bias parameters and two counterterms. Up to order $k^2$, the stochastic terms require two parameters for the cross spectrum and four parameters for the auto spectra. The TNS-based model keeps the one-point velocity dispersion in an unexpanded damping factor and treats it as a single free parameter. We extend our previous linear-bias TNS-based model of the cross spectrum to nonlinear bias and the shape auto spectra. We find that all loop integrals reduce to those already used for shape spectra in real space and galaxy clustering in redshift space, and we evaluate them with FFTLog. We compare both models with power spectra measured from halos in $N$-body simulations and find good agreement on mildly nonlinear scales. These models provide a basis for joint cosmological analyses of galaxy clustering and intrinsic alignments with imaging and spectroscopic galaxy surveys, in which intrinsic alignments are utilized as a cosmological probe.

authors.name: Toshiki Kurita, Atsushi Taruya, Teppei Okumura

papers.title: Stars on the ascending helium giant branch: II. A metal-rich luminous helium sdO gone astray
papers.summary: Hot subdwarf stars with masses above $\sim0.7~M_\odot$ expand after core helium exhaustion and ascend the helium giant branch before entering the white dwarf (WD) cooling track. In the first paper of this series, we identified the luminous helium-rich hot subdwarf HE~1518-0948 (HE~1518) as the product of a massive He-WD+He-WD merger in this evolutionary phase. Here we present a detailed analysis of a second luminous helium-rich O-type hot subdwarf (He-sdO), Gaia~DR3~5369742867090186624 (G5369). We derive an effective temperature of $55~000\pm2500$~K, a surface gravity of $\log g = 4.85\pm0.15$, and an upper limit on the hydrogen abundance of $\log (n_\mathrm{He}/n_\mathrm{H})>2.5$. The close similarity of its atmospheric parameters and its helium and carbon abundances to those of HE~1518 indicates that G5369 is also likely the product of a massive He-WD+He-WD merger. In contrast to HE~1518, G5369 is metal-rich, with an iron abundance of about twice solar. The metallicity-adjusted abundance pattern of G5369 for the elements C, N, O, and Ne is broadly consistent with the nucleosynthesis predictions of a composite He-WD merger model and is similar to the observed abundances of R~CrB stars, extreme helium stars, and the O(He) star KPD~0005+5106. The kinematics of G5369 place it near the boundary between the thick disk and halo. Its orbit, with a pericentre of $\sim$3.5 kpc, together with its high metallicity suggests that G5369 most likely originated in the inner Galaxy.

authors.name: M. Pritzkuleit, M. Dorsch, M. Miller Bertolami, S. Geier, C. W. Bradshaw, S. Nepal, N. Reindl, H. Dawson

papers.title: Accuracy, Convergence and Consistency of Dark Matter Evolution with the PhotoNs-3 Code
papers.summary: We systematically investigate the accuracy and convergence of PhotoNs-3, a cosmological N-body code employed for the HyperMillennium simulation. In particular, we examine its convergence with respect to parameters that affect the accuracy of the force calculation and the time evolution, such as the softening length and the adaptive time-stepping scheme, and find that it converges very well. Furthermore, using GADGET as the benchmark, we design four sets of simulations to compare the mutual consistency. We compare the power spectrum of the density field, halo density profiles, and the halo and subhalo mass functions. The difference between PhotoNs-3 and the Gadget codes is at the same level as that between Gadget-3 and Gadget-4. Meanwhile, PhotoNs-3 generally achieves a significant computational speedup. This work establishes that the accuracy and reliability of PhotoNs-3 and its simulations are sufficient for Stage IV galaxy surveys.

authors.name: Xiaoyang Zhang, Ming Li, Qiao Wang, Liang Gao

papers.title: Reconstructing the depth of first interaction in extensive air showers from fluorescence detector profiles with a physics-motivated neural network
papers.summary: We present a physics-motivated neural network that reconstructs, event by event, the depth of the first interaction of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays from longitudinal profiles measured by fluorescence detectors. The network couples a convolutional encoder to a decoder that implements the Gaisser-Hillas function and predicts quantiles of the target, providing a per-event uncertainty estimate. It is trained and evaluated on four million proton- and iron-induced showers between $10^{18}$ and $10^{20}$ eV, simulated with the hadronic interaction models EPOS LHC-R and Sibyll 2.3d and processed by an end-to-end simulation of the fluorescence detector response. Despite detector effects, the reconstruction retains useful information for protons, achieving a mean absolute error of about 21 g$\,$cm$^{-2}$ for primary energies around $10^{19}$ eV, whereas for iron most of the information is lost. The reconstructed distributions preserve the exponential shape of the true ones, so the proton-air interaction length can be recovered from their tail with a model-related systematic uncertainty of approximately 4%. This value is limited mainly by the choice of the hadronic interaction model and is nearly insensitive to iron contamination. These results show that the depth of the first interaction can be reconstructed under realistic detection conditions, offering a complementary route to measurements of the proton-air cross section and mass-composition studies.

authors.name: Marcos Olegario, Vitor de Souza

papers.title: Cold CCH and warm CH3CCH: complementary tracers in the massive star-forming complex RCW122 (NE & SW)
papers.summary: AIMS: By combining CH3CCH and CCH, we present a first multi-transition analysis of the RCW122-NE and RCW122-SW regions in the massive star-forming complex RCW 122. The aim is to investigate and to constrain the nature, chemistry, and evolutionary stage of each region. METHODS: We performed observations with the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX). The analysis is based on 39 CH3CCH lines with J=10-9 to 20-19 (170.8-341.8 GHz) and four hyperfine components of the CCH N=4-3 transition (349.1-349.6 GHz). We estimated excitation conditions using both local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and non-LTE methods, with rotational-diagram analysis and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) calculations. Gas-grain chemical models were performed with the Nautilus code to reproduce the observed abundances over timescales characteristic of high-mass YSO evolution. RESULTS: The excitation analysis of CH3CCH indicates two physical components suggestive of a thermal gradient. The NE region yields T~41-61 K and N_tot~1x10^{16} cm^{-2}, while SW exhibits T~33-48 K and N_tot~7x10^{15} cm^{-2}. In both regions, CCH traces cold gas below 15 K with an H_2 density of 0.5-4x10^6 cm^{-3}. The detection of the ^{13}C isotopologues of CCH indicates that C^{13}CH is more abundant than ^{13}CCH. Chemical models at various evolutionary stages, with cosmic rays as a key parameter, reproduce the observed CCH and CH3CCH abundances, although the two species form through chemically distinct routes. CONCLUSIONS: We provide a coherent scenario in which CCH traces colder gas at an early evolutionary stage, whereas CH3CCH traces a region characterized by a warmer temperature gradient, associated with chemically more evolved gas at a later stage. These results constrain the conditions governing the origin and survival of interstellar species in a thermally and chemically stratified medium.

authors.name: Edgar Mendoza, Nicolas Duronea, Leonardo Bronfman, Xiaohu Li, Martin Ortega, Xia Zhang, Ricardo Finger

papers.title: The EX~Lupi Asymmetric Micro-jet Revealed with Spectro-astrometry
papers.summary: EXor variables are a class of young pre-main-sequence stars that show repeated brightenings,likely caused by sudden increases in accretion. Studying their outflow properties, especially during periods of increased activity offers a unique perspective on the accretion-ejection connection in young stars. The aim is to detect and characterise the jet from the prototype EXor variable EX Lupi. Evidence of an outflow driven by EX Lupi has existed for some time but prior to this work, but the jet properties were unknown. This YSO has been monitored for over 100 years and during this time it has undergone increases in magnitude of between 1 and 5 mags which have been connected to increases in the mass accretion rate onto the star. A further aim of this work is to investigate if the jet can be connected to specific accretion events. Spectro-astrometry was applied to UVES spectra collected in 2021 and 2022. HIRES spectra with a similar wavelength range, taken in 2003, 2008 and 2010 were obtained from the Keck Observatory Archive and also analysed with spectro-astrometry. The spatial and kinematic properties of the EX Lupi optical bipolar jet are revealed for the first time. In 2022 the blue-shifted jet is compact.In the same year the red-shifted jet extends to approx 60 au. This finding is significant as it identifies a source that can be used to study the impact of episodes of intense accretion on jet launching. The strongest detection of the jet is in 2010, between the 2008 outburst and the 2022 burst, which points to a new ejection event triggered by the 2008 outburst. Evidence of enhanced ejection connected to a 2002 burst is also presented. No change in the jet is observed during the 2022 burst. However, we are hindered here by the limitations of the technique.

authors.name: A. Unni, E. T. Whelan, N. Otten, S. Mills, A. Banzatti

papers.title: Archival X-Ray Observations of the Eclipsing Algol-type Binary TV~Cassiopeiae
papers.summary: TV~Cassiopeiae (TV~Cas) is an eclipsing Algol-type binary with a B9\,V primary and an evolved late-type secondary in a 1.81-day orbit. We examine six serendipitous Chandra and two XMM-Newton observations spanning 2003--2012. The supplied Chandra spectra show thermal plasma near 1~keV and sub-solar fitted abundances, with an additional hotter component in one observation. EPIC-pn fits improve substantially with two temperatures: approximately 0.74/1.39~keV in 2003 and 0.87/2.16~keV in 2012. At 240~pc their nominal intrinsic 0.3--8~keV luminosities are $7.1\times10^{30}$ and $1.2\times10^{31}$~erg~s$^{-1}$, but residual structure, particularly in 2012, and response-calibration uncertainties limit physical interpretation. A prominent flare-like event occurs in Chandra ObsID 08458 (2006-11-04). The longest observation carried out in 2012 pn light curve spans approximately 82\% of an orbit and shows no conspicuous deep eclipse at the predicted secondary conjunction. An exploratory multi-epoch fold contains apparent troughs, but heterogeneous responses, intrinsic variability, and ephemeris uncertainty prevent a unique orbital interpretation. Thermal spectra and flare-like behavior favor a magnetically active secondary corona. The available products do not securely determine a coronal scale height, an orbital modulation amplitude, elemental abundance changes, or the fractional contributions of other unresolved emitters.

authors.name: Jun Yang

papers.title: The system initial mass function of Orion OB1b from probabilistic Gaia DR3 memberships
papers.summary: [ABRIDGED] Context: Whether the initial mass function (IMF) varies with environment remains a central question in star formation. The multiple populations of Orion OB1b provide an ideal laboratory to test possible IMF variations. Aims: We aim to characterise the stellar populations of Orion OB1b by identifying its constituent groups, assigning membership probabilities to individual sources, and determining their IMFs. Methods: Using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, we identified stellar groups through clustering analysis and assigned membership probabilities with a probabilistic mixture model. Stellar masses were derived from extinction-corrected photometry using pre-main-sequence evolutionary models. Results: We identified eight kinematically distinct groups and a non-clustered population, deriving ages and IMFs spanning ${\sim}0.08$--$10\,M_\odot$ for six groups, all consistent with being gravitationally unbound. Each IMF was fitted with a lognormal distribution below $1M_\odot$ and a power law above. The high-mass regime is statistically indistinguishable across all groups, while four groups also exhibit consistent IMFs over the full mass range. The remaining two groups show differences that may reflect membership uncertainties rather than intrinsic IMF variations. The combined IMF is characterised by $m_c=0.27^{+0.02}_{-0.02},M_\odot$, $\sigma=0.45^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$, and $\Gamma=1.85^{+0.16}_{-0.14}$. The non-clustered population exhibits a broader and more uncertain IMF, although residual field contamination cannot be ruled out. Conclusions: Our results support previous evidence for the complex internal structure of OB1b. The IMF in OB1b appears broadly consistent across its kinematically distinct groups and compatible with other young populations in Orion.

authors.name: Rodrigo Cabral, Juan Jos\'e Downes, Rafael Bertolotto-Stefanelli, Genaro Su\'arez

papers.title: Constraining Gamma-Ray Emission Beyond the TOV Limit: A Targeted Fermi-GBM Search for Counterparts to 39 LVK Gravitational-Wave Candidates in GWTC-5.0
papers.summary: We present a systematic search for sub-threshold gamma-ray counterparts within a one-day time window of 161 gravitational-wave (GW) events from the GWTC-5.0 catalog, whose inferred source masses exceed the adopted Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) limit, using the Gamma-ray Targeted Search (GTS) pipeline. The search identifies 39 candidate GW--gamma-ray pairs satisfying the adopted joint likelihood-ratio thresholds. None of these candidates exhibits a temporal offset compatible with the prompt-emission delay observed for GW170817 ($\sim 1.7$ s); the smallest temporal separation is 17 min 17.976 s, ruling out GW170817-like prompt temporal associations in our candidate sample. Several candidates nevertheless show substantial spatial consistency. In particular, the most spatially consistent pair has a joint localization overlap of 95.4%, despite a temporal separation of 13 h 19 min 8.85 s, illustrating that high spatial agreement can occur by chance in the absence of temporal consistency. Among the sub-threshold gamma-ray candidates, we further identify an anomalous event with an exceptionally large single-instrument significance of log LR = 5250.84. For comparison, the adopted $3\sigma$ threshold corresponds to log LR $\approx 9$. The extreme likelihood ratio of this candidate motivates further investigation of trigger sensitivity, onboard veto configurations, and the statistical interpretation of sub-threshold events. Overall, we find no physically viable multi-messenger associations between the GWTC-5.0 events and the searched gamma-ray candidates, and derive corresponding upper limits on prompt high-energy emission from GWTC-5.0 progenitors.

authors.name: Navya Raj

papers.title: Geneva seven-colour synthetic photometry from Gaia DR3 spectrophotometry
papers.summary: The well-established calibrations of astrophysical parameters derived from classical photometric systems (e.g. those of Johnson, Stromgren-Crawford, and Vilnius) are rarely applied at present. Instead, spectral energy distribution fitting techniques and the very broad Gaia photometric system are typically employed. However, these approaches have proven highly inaccurate for upper main-sequence stars. In this work, the Geneva seven-colour photometric system was synthesised from flux-calibrated low-resolution Gaia spectrophotometry (BP/RP spectra). The available ground-based observations have made it the most homogeneous dataset, offering a number of astrophysical calibrations and applications. The GaiaXPy Tool was used to synthesise the seven filters. The original Geneva U had to be exchanged with the SDSS u because it is found to be significantly blueward of the cut-off of the BP/RP spectra. The ground-based observations were used to correct for offsets and the known temperature dependence of the effective temperature in the ultraviolet region of the BP/RP spectra. The test using well-known effective temperature and metallicity calibrations on the synthetic photometry (with 21 080 stars) demonstrated the high accuracy of this approach. Further checks for possible correlations between the projected rotational velocity and binarity yielded negative results. As a direct application, the metallicity of 630 open clusters (and, thus, the radial Galactic metallicity gradient) was determined. Finally, we compiled a catalogue of 25 881 397 objects. This work demonstrates that alternatives exist to the widely used three-band Gaia photometric system. The Geneva seven-colour approach can help calibrate and analyse astrophysical parameters, especially those of upper main-sequence stars.

authors.name: E. Paunzen

papers.title: Early Realignment of Eccentric Planetary Orbits without Orbital Decay
papers.summary: Warm Jupiters are, on average, more closely aligned with their host stars than hot Jupiters, even at high eccentricities. The low projected obliquities of eccentric warm Jupiters on the tidal migration track are difficult to reconcile with high-eccentricity migration (HEM) pathways that excite large misalignments. We examine whether tides acting on the star can realign initially misaligned systems before their orbits circularize. We extend a frequency-dependent tidal model to arbitrary eccentricities and focus on the $(1,0)$ obliquity tide. This component is stationary in the inertial frame, dissipates stellar rotational energy, and can change spin obliquity while leaving the semimajor axis and eccentricity unchanged. Its forcing frequency in the stellar rotating frame coincides with that of the rigid spin-over mode, which is non-dissipative. The strength of dissipation by non-rigid motions at this same frequency remains uncertain. In our models, enhancing the dissipative response by a factor of $10^7$ produces appreciable obliquity damping for Jupiter-mass planets. The stronger damping for more massive planets suggests that an enhancement of $10^6$ may suffice for super-Jupiters. Realignment can outpace circularization if the planet is already on an eccentric warm orbit while the star is still inflated and rapidly rotating during the pre-main sequence (PMS). If alignment occurs then, present-day stellar effective temperature may be a weak predictor of obliquity. In binary-driven HEM runs initialized at the zero-age main sequence, orbital circularization outpaces realignment in systems with sustained eccentricity forcing. The stellar quadrupole scaling suggests substantially stronger suppression of eccentricity excitation for PMS starts. These results cast doubt on binary-driven HEM as the origin of such aligned eccentric warm Jupiters, even when they lie along the tidal migration track.

authors.name: Diego J. Mu\~noz

papers.title: An Intergalactic medium centred parametrisation of the 21-cm power spectrum from the Epoch of Reionization
papers.summary: The 21-cm signal from the intergalactic medium (IGM) is a key probe of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR). In this work, we present a model of the 21-cm power spectrum centred on the state of the IGM. The framework combines aspects of perturbation and percolation theory to deduce a physically informed parametrisation of the power spectrum. Moreover, it complements classical interpretation methods, centred on modelling the properties of the first ionising sources. We define the IGM parameters driving the shape and amplitude of the 21-cm signal, from the globally averaged volume- and mass-weighted ionisation fractions ($\bar{x}_{HII}$ and $\bar{x}_{HIIm}$), the clustering of sources, through the halo bias ($b_{\mathrm{h}}$), and the characteristic sizes of ionised regions ($R_{i}$) and neutral islands ($R_{n}$). We extend this analysis to model the redshift dependence of the power spectrum, constraining parameters such as the midpoint and duration of reionization. We test the IGM framework on three reionization simulations (C2-Ray, 21cmFAST, and POLAR) with varying cosmologies, astrophysics, and numerical assumptions. The framework constrains the IGM parameter space, recovers the midpoint and duration of the EoR as well as the minimum mass of halos hosting ionising sources $M_{\mathrm{min}}$, and the redshift evolution of the global ionisation fraction, the evolution of ionised and neutral regions (measured with the radial mean free path method by Georgiev et al. (2026b, submitted)). Moreover, the IGM framework lends itself to joint analysis with other EoR probes, such as high-redshift galaxies and quasars and the Cosmic Microwave Background.

authors.name: Ivelin Georgiev, Saleem Zaroubi, Raghunath Ghara, Abinash Kumar Shaw, Garrelt Mellema, Benedetta Ciardi, L. V. E. Koopmans, Anshuman Acharya, Sambit K. Giri, Ilian T. Iliev, Qing-bo Ma

papers.title: Radial mean free path bubble size distribution (RMFP-BSD) from the Epoch of Reionization
papers.summary: Among the many statistics used to characterise ionised regions during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), we introduce one which, while closely related to the mean free path bubble size distribution method from Mesinger et al. 2007, is analytically tractable and substantially less dispersive than that method. The radial mean free path (rmfp) method casts six rays along the Cartesian axes in a 3D volume from a random origin to a neutral hydrogen island. This allows us to better quantify the role of overlap during the EoR, identify isolated or interconnected clusters in the simulation, and study the characteristic peak in the ionisation power spectrum, which is important for 21-cm studies of the intergalactic medium. Moreover, we find the method informative about the properties of neutral H I islands during the final phases of the EoR. We also show that applying both methods in tandem can further improve our insight into the morphology of reionization.

authors.name: Ivelin Georgiev, Robert Crawford, Saleem Zaroubi, Raghunath Ghara, Abinash Kumar Shaw, Garrelt Mellema, Benedetta Ciardi, L. V. E. Koopmans, Anshuman Acharya, Sambit K. Giri, Ilian T. Iliev, Qing-bo Ma

papers.title: Joint Flow-Matching Posteriors for Overlapping LISA Galactic Binaries
papers.summary: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe millions of galactic binaries (GBs) at once, thousands of them resolvable, with signals that overlap in frequency. Separating them requires a global fit, a joint inference of all sources, which today takes Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers hours to days on a cluster and is repeated for each new stretch of data. We adapt recent advances in large-scale diffusion models, flow matching with a multimodal transformer, to learn the joint posterior once and then draw from it in a fraction of a second. We evaluate our approach on a realistic simulator, with full instrument response and noise, priors fitted to a simulated Galactic catalogue, and sources sampled anywhere in the entire 0.1 to 16 mHz frequency band. We demonstrate that the approach is scalable to up to 15 653 sources fitted simultaneously, evaluating calibration and coverage w.r.t. the MCMC baseline. The results show that this approach could be realistically scaled to tackle the full global fit problem.

authors.name: Davide Sartor, Giorgio Mentasti

papers.title: Extragalactic carbon-monoxide (CO) as a CMB foreground: an analytic halo model for the CO auto-spectrum and its correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background
papers.summary: Context. Carbon Monoxide (CO) lines emitted by star-forming galaxies are redshifted into the frequency bands of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments. Their correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background (CIB) may be a non-negligible small-scale foreground. Aims. We develop an analytic, full-shape halo model framework for the CO auto-spectrum and for the CO$\times$CIB cross-spectrum in CMB bands, and assess its impact on current and future high-resolution CMB experiments. Methods. We use a luminosity-weighted halo model with separate occupation distributions of central and satellite galaxies for CO and CIB emitters, CO transitions up to $J=13$, and all auto- and cross-frequency spectra. Line and infrared luminosities derive from the same star formation rate. We perform Fisher analysis for ACT-like and CMB-HD-like experiments. Results. At $\ell=3000$, the CO$\times$CIB contribution to the sky power is 0.4, 0.7, and 1.9 $\mu$K$^2$ at 90, 150, and 220 GHz, and the CO auto-spectrum is $\simeq0.02\,\mu$K$^2$. For an ACT-like experiment, the CO occupation parameters are essentially unconstrained, and neglecting CO leaves the cosmological parameters unbiased, but shifts the radio and SZ parameters by $\sim2\sigma$ and $\simeq1\sigma$, respectively. For a CMB-HD-like experiment, CO is detected with high significance and the minimum halo masses of CO and CIB emitters are constrained; neglecting CO biases the cosmological parameters up to $\sim2\sigma$ when all multipoles are used in the analysis. Conclusions. CO should be included in the foreground model of future high-resolution CMB analyses; our framework describes it analytically and consistently with the CIB, and the code implementing it is publicly available.

authors.name: Giorgia Zagatti, Marian Douspis, Giulio Fabbian, Laura Salvati

papers.title: Radial and vertical structure of accretion discs around magnetized stars
papers.summary: The ubiquity of accretion discs around magnetized stars motivates studies of the structure of these discs, in particular in whether the external magnetic field changes the radial and vertical profiles of pressure, temperature, and other quantities. We study the effects of the magnetic field of a central star on a steady accretion disc under the assumption that the magnetic field of the central star is able to partially penetrate the disc, with a degree of penetration quantified by a single parameter. We construct an analytical model of the interaction between the disc and the star's magnetic field. The equations of motion are modified to take the magnetic field into account. We solve the vertical structure of the disc assuming tabulated opacities and incorporate the magnetic field in order to determine the radial and vertical distributions of the disc parameters. The inner radius of the accretion disc, the viscous stress tensor, and the spin-up torque on the central object follow from the obtained distribution of the magnetic torque. In the limit where the stellar field is expelled from the disc, the inner radius scales with the Alfven radius, whereas when the external field penetrates the disc, the inner radius behaves in a more complex way, remaining within a few corotation radii. The normalized vertical profile depends only weakly on the radius and magnetic field. Nevertheless, the magnetic field can significantly modify the viscous stress tensor, radial structure, spectrum of the disc, and its thermal-equilibrium curves. The publicly available code AlphaDiSC now includes discs around magnetized stars.

authors.name: Aleksei Kuzin (Institut f\"ur Astronomie und Astrophysik, Universit\"at T\"ubingen), Galina Lipunova (Dr. Karl Remeis-Observatory and Erlangen Centre for Astroparticle Physics, Friedrich-Alexander Universit\"at Erlangen-N\"urnberg, Max Planck Institut f\"ur Radioastronomie)

papers.title: A data-driven absolute amplitude calibration for the Radio Neutrino Observatory Greenland (RNO-G)
papers.summary: The Radio Neutrino Observatory Greenland (RNO-G) aims to detect ultra-high-energy neutrinos (E $\geq 100\,$PeV) through the nanosecond-long coherent radio pulses produced by the Askaryan effect when neutrino-induced particle cascades develop in the Greenlandic ice sheet. Precise calibration of the analog signal chain of each antenna channel is essential for accurate reconstruction of neutrino-induced events and their physical properties. In this work, we present a data-driven calibration method based on measurement of the ambient radio background. By combining first-principles simulations of the physical noise contributions with a parametric model of the detector response, we determine the absolute gain of each antenna channel. The resulting calibration provides a season-averaged gain for every channel with an accuracy of approximately 0.5\,dB (better than 5\%), while the investigated systematic uncertainties associated with the noise signal-model were found to be negligible. This work represents the first application of an ambient-noise-based calibration that utilizes a multi-component model for the ambient noise, originally developed for radio air-shower experiments, to an in-ice radio neutrino detector.
