We ask whether information represented across two alternative measurement contexts can bridge this gap without assigning a joint distribution to their outcomes. Building on the relative-entropy-based projection method introduced by Harder et al., we define the directed posterior novelty of each record relative to the other, and an associated total-information quantity. For posterior-orthogonal records, this quantity equals the sum of the two record mutual informations. For finite-dimensional classical--quantum ensembles, we prove that optimizing this quantity over pairs of POVMs yields a value between the accessible and Holevo information. The upper bound follows by showing that the directed posterior novelty provides a lower bound on the infimum of the measured-relative-entropy recovery error. The uniform BB84 ensemble provides an example in which the quantity saturates the Holevo information while strictly exceeding the accessible information. Finally, we analytically establish the quantum validity of a redundancy-based information causality condition, resolving a question that has remained open since the condition was introduced.

authors.name: Baichu Yu, Zhang Zhou, Zhiyuan Li, Jiajun Zhang

papers.title: Increasing Quantum LDPC Code Distance through Explicit Extensions
papers.summary: We give an explicit construction of quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes without searching for candidates at each size. A fixed pair partition (PP) and fixed integer parameters determine the parity-check matrices at a specified size. Using affine permutation matrices (APMs), we construct a $[[3072,772,32]]$ code with column weight 3 and check weight 8 in each of the X and Z parity-check matrices. A construction based on circulant permutation matrices (CPMs) gives $[[1270,260,\ge34]]$, with column weight 4 and check weight 10. We prove that the construction yields commuting checks and verify the resulting distances using exhaustive search and logical operators. For the main construction, we conjecture the existence of a finite structural distance upper bound and distance improvement toward that bound as the size increases.

authors.name: Kenta Kasai

papers.title: The resource--invariant gap: a protected Floquet invariant need not protect Wigner negativity
papers.summary: Topological invariants constrain a driven Floquet generator, yet whether they protect a transient nonlinear bosonic resource remains open. We track boundary Wigner negativity of an even cat state in a chiral Floquet Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with boundary Kerr nonlinearity and structured loss. The quasienergy windings remain quantized at every chain length, yet the matched sector contrast flips sign when the chain grows under index-end shielding and is null within $3\times 10^{-5}$ under uniform loss at $t=T$ for $d\le 0.5$. Prepared and shielded on the physical dangling end, the contrast remains positive, modulated by local dimer return rather than set by the invariant. A three-site causal light cone and a boundary-Laplacian erosion law trace the flip to strong-bond bulk exposure: the sign is set by where the bulk-rate loss sits relative to the prepared site, not by chain length. We call this decoupling the resource--invariant gap.

authors.name: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorw\'e, Nsangou Mama, S. G. Nana Engo

papers.title: Long-time dynamics of open quantum systems: mathematical and physical aspects
papers.summary: Quantum channels provide the mathematical framework for describing the evolution of open quantum systems, i.e., quantum systems interacting with an environment. This review focuses on the long-time or asymptotic dynamics of open quantum systems, a topic of growing interest due to its relevance for quantum information theory and noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. We present a comprehensive analysis of homogeneous evolutions in both discrete and continuous time, treating the dynamics in full generality within the Schr\"odinger and Heisenberg pictures. By systematically studying the spectral properties of quantum channels, we present general structure theorems that characterize asymptotic behaviour, illustrated through several paradigmatic examples. We further discuss how the asymptotic dynamics can be exploited for dissipative state engineering, the identification of decoherence-free subspaces, the design of quantum error-correction schemes, and the evaluation of the asymptotic capacities of quantum channels.

authors.name: Daniele Amato, Paolo Facchi, Giovanni Gramegna, Arturo Konderak

papers.title: Non-Abelian Twist Defects in Bivariate Bicycle Codes
papers.summary: Bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity-check codes combine efficient quantum storage with a rich Abelian anyon structure, providing a compelling platform for exploring the interplay between quantum error correction and topological order. A central challenge is how to realize domain walls that host non-Abelian twist defects at their endpoints. Here we explicitly construct electric-magnetic duality walls for arbitrary bivariate bicycle codes with finite anyon content using composite, interblock, and patch checks. These checks remove the unwanted local modes while preserving charge conversion, ensuring that topologically contractible closed ribbons act trivially on encoded states. For each fixed code, check weights and interaction ranges remain bounded independently of wall length. The wall endpoints have quantum dimension $2^{Q/2}$, where $Q$ counts the independent generators in each electric or magnetic charge space. As an application, we illustrate measurement-only braiding for $Q=3$ under the correspondence between measurements and defect transport. Our construction provides a valuable basis for exploring non-Abelian defect physics and developing logical operations in quantum low-density parity-check codes with Abelian topological order in future.

authors.name: Rui Zeng, Li-Wei Yu

papers.title: Q-TRACE: Physics-based zero-day attack detection for decoy-state quantum key distribution
papers.summary: Practical quantum key distribution (QKD) is secure only while its devices match the assumptions of the security proof, and implementation attacks exploit mismatches while keeping the quantum bit error rate (QBER) low. We formulate attack detection in decoy-state BB84 as a sequential test against the honest-device manifold, the set of receiver statistics an attack-free link can produce under arbitrary channel loss. The resulting monitor, Q-TRACE (Quantum Telemetry Residuals Against Calibrated Expectations), calibrates a physical model of each link on commissioning data, profiles out the transmittance, and combines omnibus residual, physics score and setting-allocation tests with drift-robust references; no attack data are used. The formulation also yields a detectability exponent D* that lower-bounds the delay of any telemetry monitor and vanishes for a Trojan-horse probe with filtered back-reflection. On a count-level twin with model mismatch, over five held-out seeds and at a per-window false-alarm rate of 10^-3, Q-TRACE detects 63.6% of links under known attacks, 28.0% under unseen attack families and 65.3% under composite attacks, versus at most 51.2%, 6.7% and 42.3% for industry monitors, unsupervised and quantum-kernel detectors and a supervised classifier. Its delay attains the bound for strongly detectable attacks. On 33 parallel BB84 links of the IBM Heron processor ibm_marrakesh with physically executed entangling and amplitude-damping eavesdroppers, the measured information-disturbance relations agree with theory; a commissioning reference acquired under different operating conditions triggers alarms in every monitor tested, while a condition-matched reference detects a probe with 0.3% ideal QBER increase on 14 of 14 link-epochs with no false alarm on 66 honest ones.

authors.name: Sumit Tapas Chongder (Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur, Jodhpur, India)

papers.title: On locked states for damped driven Jaynes--Cummings equations
papers.summary: We consider damped driven version of the Jaynes-Cummings equation which describes quantised one-mode Maxwell field coupled to a two-level molecule. The pumping and dissipation operator are polynomial in the creation and annihilation operators. The structure of the dissipation operator corresponds to the theory of completely positive trace preserving operators due to Lindblad, Kossakowski and others. We construct examples of {\it locked states} which are stationary states of the corresponding averaged dynamics in the interaction picture. The states are nonnegative Hermitian density operators with finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The calculations rely on the recurrence equation for diagonal entries.

authors.name: A. I. Komech, E. A. Kopylova

papers.title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
papers.summary: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.

authors.name: Laureline Polli

papers.title: A Frequency-Learning Interpolation-Based Coordinate Descent Method to Optimize Parameterized Quantum Circuits on Quantum Hardware
papers.summary: Structure-aware optimizers have been the focus of recent study for the optimization of parameters in variational quantum circuits. Many of these optimizers follow a coordinate-based paradigm, making single parameter updates by using classical approximations to the cost function generated from quantum sampling. However, the performance of structure-aware optimizers on real quantum hardware at large system size has yet to be demonstrated. Recently, Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (ICD) has been proposed to unify many of these optimizers into one framework. ICD requires a preset frequency set for interpolation, which can be theoretically derived, but for which the cost function is generally sparse over and may require manual tuning. To address these issues, we propose Frequency-learning Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (FLICD) to adaptively learn frequencies online, allowing easier scaling up to larger systems. We demonstrate that our algorithm is more accurate than an existing zeroth-order method COBYLA and requires fewer quantum resources than ICD on simulator. Using IBM quantum hardware, we execute FLICD on systems up to 100 qubits and observe robust performance with an increasing number of layers.

authors.name: Jack Mandell (Department of Mathematical Sciences, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Adam Leicester (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Zixu Wang (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Jian Shi (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Department of Physics, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Haimeng Zhang (IBM Quantum, IBM T.J. Watson Research Center), Yangyang Xu (Department of Mathematical Sciences, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute)

papers.title: Compact and Long-Term Stable Polarization Entangled Photon-Pair Source
papers.summary: We present a robust, compact polarization-entangled photon-pair source based on bulk optics that achieves long-term stability, a spectral pair generation rate of $4.24 \times 10^6$ pairs s$^{-1}$ mW$^{-1}$ nm$^{-1}$ constant for pump powers up to 700 mW, an intrinsic heralding efficiency of 59.8% , and a polarization contrast visibility of 99.6%. The source is mechanically designed for vibrational robustness, employing an engineered base plate and a reduced optical layout for less alignment sensitivity and complexity. It operates at telecom wavelengths in C-band with a typical type-0 SPDC spectral output of 70 nm width. We demonstrate its integration into a deployed entanglement-based QKD system that bridges the gap between laboratory prototypes and practical quantum communication hardware.

authors.name: Mirela Selimovi\'{c}, Josip Bajo, Mikl\'{o}s Horv\'{a}th, Juan Jos\'e Romero, Thomas Heine, Philip Walther, Rupert Ursin, Sebastian Philipp Neumann

papers.title: Single-Phonon-Gated Pair Charging of Quantum Batteries
papers.summary: Charging a quantum battery requires both an energy source and access to a channel through which that energy can be transferred. If that access depends on a quantum state, charging becomes conditional on the state while the external controls remain unchanged. We show that a single phonon in a common mechanical mode enables a second-order resonant pair transition in a two-cell battery formed by the electronic spins of two nitrogen-vacancy centers, whereas the mechanical vacuum supports no corresponding resonance. At fixed controls and mean phonon number, the final stored energy and ergotropy reached with a one-phonon Fock state are unattainable with any classical mixture of coherent states. An energy balance shows that the microwave drives supply nearly all of the stored energy, while the phonon contributes only a small fraction. Our results open a route to quantum-state-conditioned charging in quantum batteries under experimentally feasible parameters.

authors.name: Xiaolong Zhao, Yazhuang Miao, Shuo Liang, Tianhui Qiu, Libin Fu

papers.title: Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers
papers.summary: Below a threshold noise rate, error correction lets larger quantum memories store a qubit for longer, without limit. Can the noise rate alone tell us whether a given noisy circuit does this? We construct fixed local circuits for which no algorithm can, already in one dimension under single-qubit noise. Each circuit is translation-invariant and time-periodic, with depolarizing noise on every wire after every layer, including all classical control. A computable list of disjoint rate intervals is indexed by the inputs $n$ of a universal Turing machine; local noise statistics select the input that the circuit simulates, and halting triggers erasure. If the machine runs forever on $n$, a qubit is stored throughout the $n$-th interval at entanglement fidelity at least $15/16$ for a time that grows without bound with size: linearly on rings, exponentially in six dimensions. The encoding and decoding maps are noiseless and global; they depend on $n$, the system size and, for decoding, the time, but not on the rate. If it halts, the fidelity of every encoding falls below $1/2+\eta$, for any fixed $\eta>0$, after a time independent of size and rate. The labels of the intervals with unbounded storage form a $\Pi^0_1$-complete set, and intervals of both kinds accumulate at zero, so these circuits have no noise threshold. Without rate selection, the ring construction is a translation-invariant, time-periodic memory: from an initialized classical hierarchy it stores a qubit for a time linear in the ring length at every sufficiently small rate, addressing the memory part of a one-dimensional question raised by D\"unnweber, Styliaris and Trivedi. These are existence results: registers and interaction ranges are very large and the rates astronomically small.

authors.name: Seth Douglas, Nidhal Mghirbi

papers.title: Where to Hide the Traps: Robust Placement in Verifiable Blind Quantum Computation
papers.summary: Trap-based verification of blind quantum computation hides test qubits among the positions of a measurement pattern, and existing protocols choose the trap configuration without regard to the delegated computation. We model trap placement as a zero-sum game between a client, who chooses a trap distribution, and a server, who chooses where to apply a Pauli deviation, with a damage profile $w$ and a per-trap detection constant $c$. Since the client cannot know how damage from several positions combines, we solve the game for all monotone subadditive damage functions consistent with $w$ at once. In a single round, placing traps in proportion to $w$ guarantees soundness error $1-c/\|w\|_1$ and is optimal up to a factor $1+\max_iw_i$, while the optimistic solution can fail completely. Over $T$ test rounds, the error decays exponentially against a server that repeats the same deviation, but a general server can keep it at $\Theta(\|w\|_1/(cT))$, and against such servers the damage-weighted placement is exactly optimal. Damage profiles follow from the flow of the pattern: for brickwork patterns with $m=4h+1$ columns, only $(2h+1)^2$ positions can affect a decision qubit, whatever the width. With $k$ traps per round, placing them on this set reduces the number of test rounds by the same factor as for a single trap; with unrestricted trap sets and flat damage we recover the known optimality of fractional coloring. Finally, trap statistics certify the aggregate damage with a number of rounds independent of the number of positions $N$, whereas locating the damage requires $\Omega(N\epsilon^{-2}\log\delta^{-1})$ rounds.

authors.name: Noureldin Mohamed, Saif Al-Kuwari

papers.title: Quantum Geometric Tensor in Parameter-Dependent Quasi-Hermitian Systems
papers.summary: A parameter-dependent physical inner product makes the comparison of quantum states at different parameter points non-unique. We formulate two geometric prescriptions for this comparison in quasi-Hermitian systems. The Type I QGT is defined by an inner-product-compatible covariant derivative and horizontal projection. It is a Hermitian, positive-semidefinite Gram tensor, and, for any normalized solution of the inner-product-preserving dynamics, its tangential component equals the physical energy variance. The Type II QGT is constructed from the endpoint overlap of physical dual states and is invariant under local $GL(1,\mathbb{C})$ rescalings. We show that, on a normalized section, it coincides with the established left--right (LR) QGT, while providing an endpoint-overlap interpretation of that tensor. Our central result is an exact relation between the two constructions: in the positive Dyson frame, the Type I QGT is the positive Gram block of the dressed-derivative sector, while the real symmetric part of the Type II QGT is this metric minus a positive-semidefinite contribution from the metric connection; the full complex tensor also contains cross terms. This relation clarifies the origin of the possible indefiniteness of the Type II metric and separates it from the positivity of the physical Hilbert-space metric. We further distinguish instantaneous Dyson mappings from the fixed inner-product-preserving dynamics and characterize the conditions under which the corresponding QGTs agree. Three two-level models illustrate these results. The physical content of the two tensors is then identified through the energy uncertainty and evolution speed for Type I, and the symmetrized endpoint overlap, complex holonomy, and signed dynamical response for Type II.

authors.name: Ming-Zhang Wang, Xu-Yang Hou, Hao Guo

papers.title: Approximation of Semigroups of Random Processes on a Hilbert Space
papers.summary: This paper develops Chernoff-type approximation methods for strongly continuous and bi-continuous semigroups of operators arising in the stochastic dynamics of quantum systems. The main focus is on applying Chernoff iterations to Markov semigroups of multiplicative random processes on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The justification of the passage from discrete quantum measurements to continuous ones depends essentially on the choice of topology and function spaces. We propose conditions for convergence to bi-continuous semigroups on subspaces that weaken the classical requirements of the Chernoff theorem. The existence of the limiting bi-continuous semigroup is established in each of the three cases: commutation of the approximating operators, their asymptotic commutation, and uniform convergence of difference quotients over a family of approximating operators. For diffusive models with a generator having bounded coefficients, the derivative of the approximating function is computed explicitly on the subspace of test functions with rapidly decreasing second derivative; the limitations of applicability of this result are discussed. Applications to generalized models of continuous imprecise quantum measurement with unbounded observables, as well as to Poisson and diffusion processes, are outlined as directions for further research.

authors.name: A. V. Utkin

papers.title: Optimizer or physics? Machine-learning surrogates for collision-based preparation of multipartite entangled quantum states
papers.summary: Repeated partial-SWAP collisions can prepare symmetric Dicke states, including the $W$ state, without measurement or postselection. The collision sequence uses only two global collision angles, and its fidelity is evaluated after a final layer of local phase rotations is optimized numerically, so each candidate pair requires a many-qubit simulation and a phase fit. We study when learned surrogates reduce the number of such evaluations, and what limits the best-found fidelity, for 65 Dicke targets with 11--20 qubits in noiseless simulations. At 50 evaluations per target, Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (GP-BO) exceeds fixed Sobol and grid designs by 0.088 and 0.063 in mean best-found fidelity. Bounded Nelder--Mead reaches 0.760 against 0.762 for GP-BO, and has the higher three-seed mean on 41 of the 61 targets with a reference value; in this two-parameter problem, adaptivity matters far more than the choice between the two methods. A neural-network ensemble pretrained on 750 observations from smaller systems needs 32\% fewer new evaluations per target than GP-BO at comparable fidelity, but the full neural search takes 1.6 times the wall time of GP-BO in our implementation. In a separate source-only test, the best of five neural proposals per target exceeds the best of five population-model proposals by 0.070 in mean fidelity. Exact symmetries and state diagnostics help explain why the leading adaptive methods reach similar family-mean fidelities. The collisions conserve the magnitude of the bare Dicke overlap and the total-spin weights, and for the best controls on a 12-target diagnostic panel, 79% of the infidelity is an amplitude deficit that a final phase layer cannot remove, which motivates interleaved phase control.

authors.name: Duc-Kha Vu, Minh Tam Nguyen, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustacapl{\i}o\u{g}lu, Fatih Ozaydin

papers.title: No-Go Theorems for Transversal and Automorphism Clifford Gates on Prime-Dimensional Qudit Stabilizer Codes
papers.summary: Logical Clifford gates are a basic primitive of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For stabilizer codes on qudits of prime dimension $p$ that encode $k\geq 2$ logical qudits, we prove that Clifford gadgets that are transversal with respect to a fixed partition of the physical qudits into blocks of fewer than $k$ qudits cannot realize the full logical Clifford group, and that this block size is tight. Code automorphisms, which combine single-qudit Clifford gates with qudit permutations, also fail for every $p$. Both obstructions come from prime-order logical Clifford elements that these gadgets cannot reach.

authors.name: Yuchen Zhan, Qi Ye, Dong-Ling Deng

papers.title: Multi-port few-photon diodes
papers.summary: We investigate single- and two-photon scattering dynamics in a system comprising two one dimensional chiral waveguides coupled to a dissipative Rydberg atom pair. By employing the Laplace transform method, we analytically solve the scattering problem and characterize the transport properties. Our results demonstrate robust perfect single-photon diode effects in this system with or without dissipation, exhibiting unity transmittance in the forward direction and zero transmittance in the backward direction. Unlike previous studies where perfect nonreciprocity requires a specific dissipation rate, our scheme achieves this effect without fine-tuning such parameters. Furthermore, we extend the nonreciprocal transport to multi-port configurations at the one and two-photon levels. The system exhibits pronounced photon nonreciprocal behavior in lossy and lossless scenarios, without the need for precise parameter matching. This work provides a robust platform for on-chip nonreciprocal photonic devices.

authors.name: Teng-Fei Xiao, Liang Li, Renli Xu, Tiantian Li, Junlong Tian, Jinlei Tan, Jie Peng

papers.title: Scaling of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence
papers.summary: Phase rigidity vanishes as a power law near exceptional points, reflecting the coalescence of eigenstates at these points. In this Letter, we show that non-Hermitian skin effects induce distinct asymptotic behaviors of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence. To demonstrate this, we derive exact analytical results for three non-Hermitian chain models and verify them numerically. For the ordinary skin effect, phase rigidity decays exponentially with increasing system size $N$, as the right and left eigenstates are exponentially localized at opposite boundaries. For the scale-free skin effect, phase rigidity exhibits an $N^{-2}$ power-law approach to a nonzero constant as the right and left eigenstates have decay lengths proportional to $N$. For the algebraic skin effect studied here, phase rigidity can exhibit an $N^{-1/2}$ power-law decay to zero, with the right eigenstate algebraically localized near a boundary and the left eigenstate spread across the chain. These findings show that non-Hermitian skin effects govern phase-rigidity scaling by shaping the spatial profiles of the right and left eigenstates, enabling control of eigenstate nonorthogonality without exceptional points.

authors.name: Shang-En Xie, Li-Mei Chen, Yao Zhou, Peng Ye

papers.title: A single-photon quantum sensor via single-atom cavity-QED
papers.summary: We describe a cavity-QED sensor using an optical probe with exactly one photon per pulse. This has a better sensitivity than a coherent pulse with the same average power when no global coherent phase reference is available. The sensor measurement is based on the estimation of the Raman-controlled absorption probability of a single-photon pulse. We use the Fock state master equation to determine the dynamics and performance of the Raman-controlled absorption of a single photon pulse and optimise the sensitivity using machine learning. Two examples are presented; (1) the target parameter is the detuning of the two-level system itself, and (2) the target parameters describe a remote reflecting cavity. In the second case, the scheme does not require a shared coherent phase reference.

authors.name: Joshua Burns, Mattias Keller, G J Milburn

papers.title: Unveiling the Action of Randomized Compiling on Quantum States: A Geometric Perspective
papers.summary: Randomized compiling (RC) converts coherent errors into stochastic Pauli noise, but this conversion alone does not imply isotropic contraction of the output state. Here we use the generalized Bloch vector (GBV) representation to examine the cumulative effect of RC on state purity and orientation in multi-layer circuits. For the independent, isotropically distributed weak coherent errors considered here, the accumulated ensemble-averaged RC channel lies close to the depolarizing direction, producing a state-level near-isotropic contraction that sacrifices a small amount of purity to achieve a substantial suppression of orientational deviation. When dephasing coexists, RC suppresses the coherent-error contribution but leaves a residual deviation dominated by dephasing, setting a limit that we term the "dephasing wall". We experimentally validate these findings on a superconducting quantum processor through GHZ state preparation and phase estimation in a simulation of topological braiding. The results confirm that RC's effectiveness stems from its ability to suppress the orientational bias of coherent errors---a structural transformation not resolved by fidelity alone but directly visible through GBV diagnostics.

authors.name: Kai Tang, Chao Zhan, Yao Song, Peiling Huang, Yuxuan Zhou, Song Liu, Junkai Zeng, Jiansheng Wu, Tongxing Yan, Xiu-Hao Deng, Yuanzhen Chen

papers.title: Interaction-Driven Photocurrent Enhancement in a Quantum Photocell with Opposite Transient and Steady-State Responses
papers.summary: We study photocurrent control in a quantum photocell with interacting qubit-qutrit donors coupled to an acceptor. We show that stronger Heisenberg exchange coupling and anisotropy increase the transient photocurrent but reduce its steady-state value, whereas the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction favors steady-state output at the expense of transient enhancement. This reversal highlights the need to distinguish rapid current generation from sustained operation when tuning quantum photovoltaic devices. Analysis of donor purity further reveals that the qutrit's local purity tracks the photocurrent trends in both regimes. These results demonstrate that the effects of donor interactions depend crucially on the timescale of operation, suggesting a strategy for tailoring the response of hybrid quantum photocells to different operating regimes.

authors.name: Abbas Shokri, Esfandyar Faizi, Mohammad B. Arjmandi

papers.title: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer
papers.summary: We propose a superconducting circuit QED source of on-demand frequency-entangled microwave photon pairs, with one photon emitted into each of two separate waveguides, enabling individual manipulation. The design is based on a transmon-resonator dimer, which consists of two transmon-resonator subsystems coupled through a cross-Kerr interaction. We outline a viable circuit-QED realization in which the required cross-Kerr interaction is implemented using Josephson-junction couplers. To analyze the emission dynamics, we derive and numerically solve the set of evolution equations that enable tracking the evolution of the joint spectral intensity of photons. We characterize the resulting photon-number correlations, frequency anticorrelation, and spectral entanglement. By varying the coupling strengths, we obtain biphotons with distinct joint spectral intensities and Schmidt spectra, ranging from broadly distributed multimode entanglement to states dominated by two nearly equally weighted Schmidt contributions. In the latter regime, optimizing the transmon-resonator coupling and detuning yields an output biphoton state that has fidelity $F \approx 0.956$ with a two-dimensional maximally entangled state. Restricting the local target modes to separated frequency bins yields a fidelity $F_\mathrm{bin} \approx 0.949$, indicating that the output state closely approximates a frequency-bin Bell pair. Thus, the proposed microwave biphoton source provides a route toward distributing frequency-encoded quantum resources between remote superconducting nodes.

authors.name: E. V. Stolyarov, O. V. Kliushnichenko

papers.title: Differentiable collision-model control for multipartite state engineering: reachability, geometry, and preparation cost
papers.summary: We study a differentiable control architecture for multipartite state engineering in which partial-SWAP collisions, a Heisenberg exchange, are interleaved with layers of local phase rotations. Singular collision angles confine the evolution to invariant supports, impose exact fidelity ceilings, and generate an inverse-distance lower bound on the preparation time nearby. Away from them, numerical certificates show that the sampled couplings reach the whole fixed-excitation sector for sector dimensions up to 21, and optimizations reach fidelities above 0.999 for dimensions up to 1716. At generic couplings the number of rounds needed for a given Dicke fidelity, measured by the ratio of independent phase controls to the projective dimension, is nearly independent of the system size, and the quantum Fisher information spectrum is close to that of a random Gaussian Jacobian. Near full SWAP, a slow-time theory, the sharp form of the inverse-distance bound there, predicts microscopic hitting times without fitted parameters: the distance from the singular point sets the clock and its direction selects the effective control geometry. A detuning sweep along two rays shows that the Dicke horizon follows this law up to a detuning of 0.1, where it is two to five times shorter than at a generic coupling in sectors of dimension 70 to 252, while phase-uniform, random-sign, and Haar-random targets are delayed; beyond a detuning of about 0.3 all targets return to the generic cost. The slow-time value for the Dicke target is nearly the same for sector dimensions from 35 to 252. The exchange graph of the effective theory offers an interpretation of this ordering. Counted in two-qubit gates, generic-coupling preparation is costlier than known Dicke circuits; the architecture offers fixed global couplings, local phase rotations as the only control, and no measurement.

authors.name: Minh Tam Nguyen, Duc-Kha Vu, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu, Fatih Ozaydin

papers.title: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
papers.summary: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Finite-size security analyses of high-dimensional protocols fix the dimension in advance, and the dimension-adaptive schemes reported so far have been analyzed only asymptotically. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. Each block is therefore a standard fixed-length protocol, and composable finite-key security against coherent attacks follows from sequential composition; an inaccurate channel model reduces the key rate but does not weaken security. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel--Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31\%--47\% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8\% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario, while every fixed dimension drops to 73.5\% or less in at least one scenario. Running the link's measurement statistics on a superconducting quantum processor shows device errors close to a constant offset; with these errors included, the best daytime dimension changes from eight to four, and the controller adjusts accordingly.

authors.name: Murtuza Lemonwala, Laxima Niure Kandel

papers.title: Just another Markovian embedding for open quantum systems
papers.summary: In this work, I present one more method for analysis of non-Markovian open quantum systems by embedding them into larger Markovian systems. As many other approaches, this method starts from finding a rational approximation for the bath correlation function in the frequency domain, the difference is that I retain $\omega \to -\overline \omega$ symmetry for the poles of the approximation. This allows to reduce the dimension of embedding from one- to half-degree-of-freedom per pole. In case of odd number of poles, the resulting equation describing dynamics of the system turns out to be not a Lindblad, but a hybrid quantum-classical master equation.

authors.name: Vasilii Vadimov

papers.title: Network contextuality beyond binary outcomes
papers.summary: Can a joint measurement reveal nonclassical behaviour in independently prepared systems that share no entanglement? We study network contextuality by extending the two-qubit test of bi-contextuality [G. Ruffolo et al., arXiv:2507.08461 (2025)] to projective measurements with more than two outcomes. In one laboratory, an observer measures the systems individually or jointly performs two compatible global measurements constructed from them. The individual probabilities constrain the possible classical correlations at each source. For our preparations, every noncontextual model with outcome-deterministic and source-independent assignments predicts a nonzero average product of the two global outcomes. The joint quantum measurement gives zero. We construct explicit product states realizing this contradiction for $N=d$ independent sources, each preparing one $d$-dimensional system, with $2\leq d\leq9$. We derive an inequality in observed probabilities, prove its single-source bounds are exact for these preparations, and give sufficient thresholds for violations under independent depolarizing noise. For this family of preparations the dimension range is sharp: for every $d\geq10$ the individual probabilities admit a zero assigned average, so the certificate fails. The same data admit a noncontextual explanation when source independence is relaxed.

authors.name: Hao Zhang, Gerard John Wong Zhongwei, Rafael Rabelo, Gabriel Ruffolo, Pawe{\l} Kurzy\'nski, Dagomir Kaszlikowski

papers.title: Direct quantum simulation of compressible Navier-Stokes flow via finite homotopy linearisation
papers.summary: We develop a direct quantum simulation algorithm for finite homotopy approximations to the non-isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations. A primitive-variable formulation gives polynomial residuals in the fields and their spatial and time derivatives, including density-weighted time derivatives. On a periodic grid, applying each spatial stencil uniformly to every factor in a shifted product preserves the dynamics of the finite homotopy hierarchy in an affine linearisation. Because each deformation equation depends only on lower homotopy orders, the lifted generator matrix is strictly block lower-triangular and hence nilpotent. The resulting finite-polynomial solution evaluates the final state directly without time-stepping error, while explicit short-time convergence conditions bound the homotopy truncation error on a fixed grid. In two-dimensional Taylor-Green flow, initial pressure balance removes the leading longitudinal acceleration and delays the onset of dilatational kinetic energy from quadratic to quartic in time. At Mach numbers 0.2 and 0.4, the fifth-order hierarchy reproduces viscous dissipation over a longer interval than pressure-dilatation at the same relative tolerance. We identify auxiliary variables representing the same evolving product, compile the finite-polynomial evolution into logical quantum circuits, and recover a signed velocity Fourier mode via Hadamard interference. Together, the Taylor-Green energy budgets quantify the accuracy windows of each homotopy order, while coarse-grid circuits verify the signed readout and measure gate counts. For higher-order evolution on finer grids, merging coincident stencil terms and combining block-encoded products along strictly increasing homotopy-order paths substantially reduce the predicted normalisation cost.

authors.name: Ming-Yang Tan, Guo-Ping Guo, Zhao-Yun Chen

papers.title: Quantum tomography of ququart states of optical vector vortices based on measurements in mutually unbiased bases
papers.summary: In this paper we present an original method for quantum state tomography of vector optical vortices with an axially symmetric transverse polarization profile. We present an interference technique which allows one to distinguish states of vector vortices with a fixed topological charge with high accuracy. We also demonstrate the feasibility of experimental quantum tomography of the density matrix in the logical ququart space built on vector vortices, with high fidelity for all 20 basis states. It is shown that the proposed tomography scheme provides a uniform characterization of states in all mutually unbiased bases of the ququart space.

authors.name: D. D. Reshetnikov, E. V. Maliutina, T. K. Korol, E. A. Vashukevich, T. Yu. Golubeva

papers.title: Extraction erases the gain: cavity loss bounds dynamical-Casimir metrology at ultrastrong coupling
papers.summary: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling dresses the vacuum with virtual photons whose response to the coupling strength exceeds that of any coherent probe, yet these photons never leave the cavity and cannot be detected. A parametric drive at the dynamical-Casimir resonance converts them into real photons that a detector can collect. We show that this conversion is self-limiting: converting the virtual photons of an ultrastrongly coupled probe into real, extractable photons opens the cavity port that removes them, so the retained metrological gain is set by the accumulated cavity loss rather than by the pure-state ceiling. In the driven quantum Rabi model the pure-state quantum Fisher information on the coupling reaches $1.7\times10^{5}$ times the coherent baseline; at a cavity linewidth of $246$~MHz, typical of coplanar-waveguide flux-qubit circuits, master-equation dynamics retain $0.96\%$ of it. In a 32-qubit Dicke model the retained fraction is $2.6\%$ at the largest photon basis computed. Eighteen lossy configurations from both models fall on one curve of the accumulated loss, the product of linewidth and interrogation time, which halves the retained information at $0.13$. The extraction cost, not the lossless ceiling, is the figure of merit for any protocol that reads bound vacuum correlations through a lossy port.

authors.name: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorw\'e, Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo

papers.title: Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks for Power Grid Analysis under N-x Contingencies
papers.summary: The combinatorial growth of network configurations under N-x contingencies presents significant computational challenges for power system analysis. In this work, we introduce a quantum algorithm based on Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CCTQWs) that evolves a quantum walker conditioned on a contingency register held in a uniform superposition of all x-line outage configurations representing the contingency scenarios. The proposed framework encodes transmission line availability in a quantum register and employs controlled Hamiltonian evolution to account for topology changes induced by contingencies. We develop a gate-based implementation using Trotter-Suzuki product formulas and investigate the associated approximation errors and computational requirements. As a demonstration of the proposed methodology, we introduce a contingency-averaged occupation centrality measure derived from quantum-walk measurement statistics. Numerical experiments on an 8-bus power network under N-2 contingencies demonstrate the implementation of the algorithm and characterize the convergence of the resulting centrality estimates with respect to the observation window, sampling and Trotter steps. Comparison with established classical centrality measures shows a qualitatively consistent characterization of network structure, particularly in identifying the most central nodes. The proposed framework establishes a methodological foundation for quantum-walk-based analysis of power networks under contingencies, providing a starting point for future investigations of quantum algorithms for power system security assessment.

authors.name: Mahesh N. Jayakody, Ruben Kara, Carsten Hartmann, Andrea Benigni

papers.title: Local redundancies are necessary for long-lived memories in finite spatial dimensions
papers.summary: We prove a no-go theorem for exponentially long-lived thermal memories, based on the structure of redundancies among Hamiltonian terms. For local stabilizer Hamiltonians in finite spatial dimensions, the absence of local redundancies---relations in which the product of a small number of Hamiltonian terms equals the identity---is known to preclude bulk thermodynamic phase transitions. Yet glassy dynamics can still sustain long-lived memories even without a thermodynamic transition, as demonstrated by LDPC codes on non-Euclidean graphs. A longstanding question, exemplified by Haah's cubic code, is whether such a mechanism can also support passive (quantum) memory in finite-dimensional Euclidean systems. We show that this route fails for local stabilizer Hamiltonians without local redundancies: at any constant nonzero temperature, local heat-bath dynamics is fast mixing, with $O(N)$ mixing time, where $N$ is the number of qubits. We establish this by proving a strong decay of correlations property of the thermal Gibbs state. We further prove rapid mixing with $O(\log N)$ mixing time under a stronger condition on induced redundancies in suitably chosen regions. This stronger result applies to several well-studied examples, including Haah's cubic code and its generalizations, as well as three-dimensional layer codes. Our work identifies redundancy structure as a key property for understanding thermal memories.

authors.name: Chao Yin, Yaodong Li, Benedikt Placke, Vedika Khemani

papers.title: What can a quantum network promise about the entangled pairs it delivers?
papers.summary: Quantum networks will give users entangled pairs of qubits, the resource behind teleportation and quantum-secure keys. But a user cannot check a pair without destroying it, so networks promise the quality of each pair, its fidelity, from a physical model rather than from a measurement. If the model is too optimistic, the delivery rule alone may miss the error. We ask: what can a network actually guarantee? Our main result has two sides. By testing some pairs at random, in secret, users can put a lower bound on the average fidelity of the pairs they keep, without any model and at every moment. But when they test only a small fraction and keep most pairs, the tests cannot reliably show that every kept pair meets a fidelity threshold: a rare bad pair can still slip through. A promise about every single pair therefore rests on a model, and we give a rule that bounds each user's risk of ever receiving a bad pair under any data-driven routing, as long as the model is not optimistic or a large enough margin is declared in advance. Real data show calibration noise beyond chance, and in simulated networks a model error of the size seen in one experiment breaks the per-pair promise unless the margin was declared. On real data from trapped-ion and diamond links, the number of pairs decided how strong the certificate was: with about 3,000 pairs of a kilohertz link and 20% tested, the median certificate was 0.818, against the 0.817 we predicted in advance. We then ran the protocol ourselves on a 36-qubit trapped-ion processor in 50 pre-registered jobs. The certificate came within 0.003 of the measured fidelity, dropped by the predicted amount when we secretly damaged a third of the pairs, and, without changes, certified three- and four-qubit entangled states. The same tests also catch an optimistic model, but slowly. We pre-registered every confirmatory analysis and report the failures too.

authors.name: Tanish Singh Rajpal, Michael Mattarock

papers.title: Stopping-Time Leakage in Blind Quantum Delegation
papers.summary: Blind quantum computation lets a client delegate a computation while hiding it from the server, up to a declared leakage. Its security definitions cover a single round. A variational quantum algorithm, however, delegates many rounds, and its classical optimizer decides from private data when to stop. We study what the resulting round count tells an honest-but-curious server. For protocols with one-time-padded transcripts and fresh randomness in every round, we prove that the server's best distinguishing advantage over the whole sequence equals the total-variation distance between the stopping-time distributions, so the round count is the only residual channel in this model. We also show that soundness composes as $\delta\,\mathbb{E}[T]$ under adaptive stopping, given a conditional per-round soundness property that composably secure verifiable protocols provide. In simulated delegated eigensolvers for the transverse-field Ising chain, the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz ratio measured in iterations 5 to 15 predicts the noiseless stopping round with a leave-one-out error of 1.7 iterations, compared with 10.3 for a constant predictor. Across 14 configurations that differ in optimizer, stopping rule, initialization, system size, shot budget and problem family, the leakage is significant in 12 and ranges from 0.14 to 1.68 bits, and a maximum-entropy bound estimated on held-out sessions lies above it in all of them. For defense, we show that any mechanism acting after the stopping decision can only add rounds, and that differentially private padding costs the full adjacency radius. A fixed public iteration budget removes the channel completely; set at the median run length, it costs 10% of the remaining energy gap. A differentially private stopping rule based on AboveThreshold protects every pair of instances, but it must often stop too early, which makes it costly.

authors.name: Noureldin Mohamed, Saif Al-Kuwari

papers.title: Joint Dynamics of Spins and Frequency-Resolved Bosonic Occupations: A Projection-Operator Approach
papers.summary: We derive weak-coupling kinetic equations for frequency-resolved bosonic mode occupations in the spin--boson model. Rather than integrating out the bath completely, we retain these mode occupations as independent dynamical variables whose equations are coupled to those for the spin observables. A projection-operator construction closes the dynamics on a product-spin ansatz and an undisplaced Gaussian environment with a diagonal covariance matrix. The equations are obtained to second order in the interaction parameter $\lambda$ for an arbitrary number of spins within this factorized closure, and are solved numerically for a single spin. A fixed-truncation calculation using the hierarchical equations of motion provides a benchmark for the spin dynamics with the Drude--Lorentz spectral density. The numerical results reveal a redistribution of bosonic mode occupations concentrated near the spin transition frequency $\Omega=\sqrt{\Delta^2+h^2}$. We also examine the response of the coupled spin--boson system to structured spectra, nonthermal initial occupations, and slow modulation of the coupling. The calculated mode occupations also allow changes in the bath-side occupation and energy densities $p(\omega)\delta\langle N_\omega\rangle(t)$ and $\omega p(\omega)\delta\langle N_\omega\rangle(t)$ to be obtained without requiring an exponential decomposition of the bath correlation function. Its scope is restricted to weak coupling, diagonal Gaussian bath states, and, for time-dependent couplings, the adiabatic regime.

authors.name: Khazret Sh. Meretukov, Alexander E. Teretenkov

papers.title: Quantum-Memory Forensics for Tampered Quantum Seals: Resource-Dependent Sample Gains
papers.summary: Quantum seals reveal that an object was disturbed, but not where, with which tool, or when the tool changed. We study quantum-memory forensics for sealed items returning through an untrusted network where one tool opens many. Each seal cell is half of a Bell pair whose partner the verifier keeps in a protected quantum memory, a secret Pauli frame turns any attack into a Pauli channel, and a three-tier report localizes the tampering, learns a hidden-parity fingerprint of the tool and detects a tool switch in arrival order, not necessarily in attack order. Attribution concerns attackers who do not erase that fingerprint, which a random Pauli layer would do cheaply. Each result is stated within one of four verifier classes. For per-unit verifiers, which never couple two seal units and hold no untouched reference, the sample separation is asymptotically exponential, by reduction from a known lower bound for one parity of strength up to 1/3. On ten tampered cells it is proved to be at least \qnProvedUniformMin-fold against non-adaptive stabilizer probes and observed in simulation at \qnEoneRatioFine-fold. Against an implemented self-referencing strategy the simulated gain is about twice the inverse squared strength. The value also depends on the attack: destroying the untouched cells makes the reference necessary, whereas copying errors exposes the fingerprint to reference-free probes. We derive the vault's qubit inventory and simulate a seal requirement curve: ten times more seal noise lengthens the seal's lifetime \qnSealLifeGainFive-fold at \qnSealRhoFive{} times the attribution cost at $r=10$.

authors.name: Jaeyun Jeong, Zehua Wang, Lilia Tightiz, Ki-Woong Park, Victor C. M. Leung

papers.title: Generalized Bloch Oscillations of Doublon Defect in One-dimensional Antiferromagnetic Atomic Spin Chain under Linear and Quadratic Magnetic Gradients
papers.summary: We investigate generalized Bloch oscillations of a single doublon defect in a one-dimensional antiferromagnetic $t$-$J_{\rm{z}}$ chain subjected to linear and quadratic magnetic field gradients. By mapping the spin-charge coupled many-body dynamics onto an effective single-particle model, we reveal how the N\'eel background mediates parity-dependent coupling between the defect and the external fields. The linear gradient induces a staggered potential that splits the Wannier-Stark ladder into two intertwined subladders, producing a characteristic beating pattern in the center-of-mass motion with a subband offset accurately captured by third-order perturbation theory. The quadratic gradient generates sublattice-dependent tilts that shear the ladder into a scissor-like profile, yielding site-dependent beating periods that encode the nonlocal spatial averaging of the defect wave function. When both gradients coexist, their interplay is fundamentally nonadditive: the quadratic gradient breaks the two-site periodicity that forbids second-order linear responses, unlocking a dominant cross-coupling proportional to $B_{\rm{z,1}}B_{\rm{z,2}}$. This leaves distinct fingerprints on the Bloch-oscillation spectrum---a rigid baseline hift of the fundamental doublet and asymmetric broadening of the first harmonic. These predictions are quantitatively corroborated by exact many-body simulations of the real-time density evolution and center-of-mass dynamics. Our work establishes a gradient-induced unlocking mechanism for multi-gradient defect spectroscopy in quantum magnets, offering a framework for probing parity-protected selection rules and their controlled breaking via generalized Bloch oscillations in tunable quantum simulators.

authors.name: Xiang Gao, Xing Deng, Wei Xiao, Chunhua Zhang, Xingxing Wang, Xueting Fang

papers.title: Proposal for a cat-cluster-state machine gun
papers.summary: Non-Gaussian bosonic states such as the Schr\"odinger cat states are essential for continuous-variable quantum-information processing. A convenient and deterministic process for generating cat states is through the use of a Rabi interaction between a single bosonic mode and a spin which facilitates a state-dependent displacement. The lack of a Rabi interaction for propagating optical photons has rendered optical cat states elusive. Here, we show that the complex nonlinear scattering dynamics of a single-mode squeezed-vacuum state interacting with a quantum emitter can be engineered to produce a Rabi interaction between a quantum emitter and a propagating photon mode while the contributions from other orthogonal modes destructively interfere. Our protocol can deterministically prepare large-scale high-fidelity squeezed cat states from squeezed-vacuum pulses and is robust to photon loss due to spontaneous emission to non-guided modes. Extending to scattering multiple input squeezed-vacuum pulses off the quantum emitter, we propose generating linear cluster state strings with logical qubits encoded as squeezed cat states, which we refer as the cat cluster state. Our interaction scheme can potentially produce strings of entangled cat states at GHz rates using semiconductor quantum dots.

authors.name: Haoyuan Luo, Hugo P. Stackhouse, Sahand Mahmoodian

papers.title: Cqlib: A High-Performance Software Stack for Quantum Computing
papers.summary: This paper presents Cqlib, a high-performance software stack for quantum computing built around a unified quantum circuit model. Its native Rust core provides efficient implementations of circuit processing, quantum-state and operator computation, compilation, and optimization, while Python and C interfaces support algorithm development and system integration. Cqlib covers quantum program construction, simulation, analysis, compilation, device adaptation, and result processing under consistent program semantics. Through OpenQASM and the Quantum Control Instruction Set (QCIS), Cqlib supports program representation and hardware-oriented execution. Cqlib further provides backend interfaces for device execution, with Cqlib-Tianyan serving as one implementation for QCIS-compatible quantum hardware. Evaluations using parameterized compilation tasks from Benchpress and related tests show that Cqlib achieves good functional coverage, compilation correctness, and execution efficiency within the evaluated task scope. We develop Cqlib-Algorithm as a modular library of reusable operators and composable components for widely used quantum algorithms, including quantum search, phase estimation, and variational algorithms, with additional support for error mitigation. To complement these building blocks with domain-specific workflows, we further develop Cqlib-VQE, Cqlib-QAOA, and Cqlib-QML for application-level studies in quantum chemistry, combinatorial optimization, and quantum machine learning, respectively. Cqlib also integrates source-grounded Skills and MCP-based tools to support agent-assisted program generation, backend execution, and result-guided workflow refinement. Overall, Cqlib provides a unified and extensible software foundation that connects quantum algorithm development, simulation, compilation, and execution on QCIS-compatible quantum hardware.

authors.name: Tianyan Quantum Group

papers.title: Multiphoton Electronic Coherences in Molecules
papers.summary: We investigate multiphoton electronic coherences in a series of gas-phase atomic and molecular systems with increasing complexity. Our measurements are driven by pairs of phase-locked, deep-ultraviolet pulses with independent control of the relative phase and time delay. By combining the ionization yields measured at specific relative phases between the pulses, we can isolate different multiphoton orders and enable measurements of coherences between specific pairs of electronic states. We measure electronic coherences between states separated by zero-photon (i.e. within our laser bandwidth), one-photon and two-photons, resulting in signals with modulation periods ranging from 430 attoseconds to several femtoseconds. Fast electronic dynamics are tracked simultaneously with the accompanying nuclear motion. Additionally, we derive analytic expressions for the measured ionization yield as a function of pump-probe delay and demonstrate their use as a quantitative tool for isolating individual photon-order contributions within the total yield.

authors.name: Loc Thi-Hoang Ngo, Brian Kaufman, Varun Makhija, Ryan Cloughly, Javin Ohara, Julia Codere, Scott Liguori, Sameer Singh, Martin Cohen, Matt Bain, Brett Pearson, Ruaridh Forbes, Thomas Weinacht

papers.title: Spin-adapted state preparation for quantum chemistry
papers.summary: Quantum phase estimation for strongly-correlated molecules requires an initial state of high overlap with the true ground state, and preparing one is a significant fault-tolerant cost. Matrix product states (MPS) produced by the density matrix renormalisation group (DMRG) are a leading choice, yet existing circuits treat their tensors as dense or do not use the full symmetries present in molecular electronic Hamiltonians. In quantum chemistry, DMRG also exploits total spin, a non-abelian symmetry, storing one amplitude per spin multiplet instead of one per state. We show that the reduced tensors of such a spin-adapted MPS, labelled by the steps of the unitary group approach, form an abelian-symmetric MPS, which existing block-sparse preparation protocols can load at a cost set by the multiplet count. One state-independent rotation per site, determined by a Clebsch-Gordan coefficient, then returns the state to the occupation basis. We provide resource estimates for our circuits on singlet ground states of active space models of iron-sulphur clusters, finding improvements in Toffoli count up to $135\times$ compared to dense methods and $4.9\times$ compared to block-sparse methods applied to the same states, with up to $3.7\times$ fewer ancilla qubits required.

authors.name: Matthew L. Sims-Goh, Fredrik Hasselgren, Hamza Jnane

papers.title: Quantum Amplitude Estimation for Ligand and Pose Index Retrieval
papers.summary: Structure-based virtual screening spans a combinatorial configuration space, motivating a quantum screening framework that targets threshold-qualified configuration indices without reconstructing a complete interaction-score table. Quantum amplitude estimation based on quantum phase estimation (QAE/QPE) supplies finite-resolution phase information to a reversible comparator that writes its decision to FLAG, while optional Grover-style quantum selection (QSEL) amplifies FLAG-selected outcomes and selector measurements identify the ligand, receptor state, rotation, and translation. In an ideal logical benchmark using AutoDock grid interactions as a proof-of-concept model, we evaluated initial FLAG acceptance probability, classification precision, shots required for 95% FLAG detection, and logical Q-operator calls across eight receptor systems and nested libraries of up to 1,024 ligand occupancies. Higher QAE/QPE resolution generally improved classification precision at additional evaluation cost, whereas suitably chosen QSEL iteration counts reduced required shots without improving classification precision, revealing selection and resource trade-offs for extending coherent index retrieval to more physically detailed molecular evaluation models.

authors.name: Pei-Kun Yang

papers.title: Positive-partial-transpose structure of completely entangled subspaces and their complements
papers.summary: A completely entangled subspace (CES) contains no product vectors, so every state supported on it is entangled. Whether such a subspace can support states with positive partial transpose (PPT) is a more subtle question. The normalized projector onto a CES may be NPT even if there exist PPT states supported on the CES. We investigate this distinction using a semidefinite criterion that optimizes the smallest partial-transpose eigenvalue over all supported density operators. For two- qutrit states supported on CESs, this leads to a complete characterization: a CES supports PPT states exactly when it is four-dimensional and related by invertible local transformations to the complement of an unextendible product basis (UPB). We also establish restrictions on PPT states whose ranges contain only vectors of Schmidt rank at least three, ruling out their existence in $3\otimes n$, $4\otimes4$, and $4\otimes5$, and showing that any such state in $4\otimes6$ must have rank eight. An interesting structure emerges when two orthogonal completely entangled subspaces together span the full Hilbert space, which we term \textit{complementary CESs}. Explicit constructions in $3\otimes4$ demonstrate that both subspaces can support PPT entanglement even when their normalized projectors are NPT. In $4\otimes4$, we construct a complementary pair whose normalized projectors are themselves PPT entangled. These constructions offer an alternative route to obtaining PPT entangled states, beyond the familiar approach based on UPB complements.

authors.name: Gurvir Singh, Arvind

papers.title: Remote Charging of Quantum Batteries via a Multimode Resonator
papers.summary: We study the remote charging of a qubit battery by a qubit charger coupled through a finite multimode resonator. The charging protocol uses time-shifted coupling pulses that account for the spatial phases of the resonator modes. We compare the energy stored in the battery with its ergotropy, the maximum work extractable by a local unitary operation. In the single-excitation regime considered here, the battery stores energy at any nonzero excited-state population, but its ergotropy is positive only when that population exceeds one half. In the absence of loss, stronger coupling brings the battery above this threshold earlier, while the final charge remains nearly complete across the coupling range studied. For the parameters considered, qubit relaxation suppresses ergotropy more strongly than resonator loss at comparable decay rates. After the battery is disconnected, relaxation causes its stored energy to decay exponentially, yet its ergotropy vanishes at a finite time while half of its energy capacity remains occupied. For a fixed storage interval, disconnecting at the population maximum therefore preserves the most extractable work.

authors.name: Maryam Hadipour, Soroush Haseli

papers.title: 500 Hz atom-atom entanglement distribution over metropolitan-scale fibers
papers.summary: Quantum networks and repeaters are among the most promising routes to scale up quantum information systems. Nevertheless, various aspects still require significant improvement to achieve practical realization. Multiplexing can enhance the performance in many fundamental steps, thus emerging as a critical strategy for the realization of quantum repeaters. Currently, a major bottleneck in realizing functional quantum repeaters is heralded entanglement distribution over longdistance elementary links, as neither of the two dominant protocols-single-photon nor two-photon interference-can simultaneously achieve high efficiency and strong robustness. Here, we address this challenge by experimentally realizing a method that unifies the efficiency and robustness. By harnessing two 15 * 15 quantum memory arrays, we generate remote matter-matter entanglement at a rate of 546 Hz over 20 km of fiber without active phase stabilization. This rate exceeds that of two-photon and single-photon schemes by factors of 75,932 and 23, respectively, establishing a new benchmark for entangling speed over metropolitan-scale distances and enabling semi-deterministic entanglement distribution. Inherently compatible with multiplexed quantum repeater architectures, our scheme offers a promising approach towards the realization of future high-performance distributed quantum systems.

authors.name: Jixuan Shi, Yuedong Sun, Yibo Liang, Sheng Zhang, Pingyuan Liu, Zhaibin Cui, Luming Duan, Yunfei Pu

papers.title: Observable-Level Expressivity in Fixed-Readout Quantum Neural Networks
papers.summary: A central question in quantum machine learning is which functions of an input state a model can represent when its measurement is fixed by hardware or by experimental design. We address this question for quantum neural networks with a fixed readout observable, where the trainable pre-measurement dynamics determine the effective observable in the Heisenberg picture and the scalar output is the measured expectation value itself, without trainable affine post-processing. We characterize the reachable effective observables under three physical resource classes: unitary evolution, which preserves the spectrum of the readout; mixed-unitary evolution, which relaxes this to a majorization constraint while preserving the trace; and completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) evolution, whose Heisenberg adjoint is unital rather than trace-preserving and therefore lifts the trace constraint inherited at the mixed-unitary level. The three reachable sets are a fixed-spectrum orbit, its convex hull, and an operator interval, and the inclusions are strict for any readout that is not proportional to the identity. The separation is witnessed locally: for a fixed Pauli readout $Z_j$ on an arbitrary number of qubits, the amplitude-damping observable $\gamma\id+(1-\gamma)Z_j$ lies outside the mixed-unitary level for every $\gamma>0$. We realize the CPTP level with a Stinespring-channelized circuit and derive closed-form loss floors, $4\gamma^2/3$ and $\gamma^2$ for the unitary and mixed-unitary levels and zero at the CPTP level, which the numerics reproduce within precision. Structured-observable, R\'enyi-moment and classification experiments illustrate how the hierarchy manifests in finite-depth ans\"atze. The results identify which spectral constraint each physical resource relaxes, framing reachable-observable classes as a resource for expressivity rather than an architectural advantage.

authors.name: Iqra Bashir, Yuanfeng Wang, Mingda Huang, Keren Li, Qi Qin

papers.title: Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models
papers.summary: Quantum impurity models, which describe a small but strongly-interacting subsystem coupled to a large noninteracting bath, are the computational core of dynamical mean field theory and play an important role in simulating strongly correlated materials. We develop quantum algorithms for efficiently simulating these models at low temperatures and with high precision. For any impurity model on $n$ fermionic modes with fixed impurity size: (1) We give a quantum algorithm that prepares the thermal state at inverse temperature $\beta$ to precision $\delta$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta))$. This algorithm is the first to achieve both polynomial scaling in the inverse temperature and polylogarithmic scaling in the precision. When the Hamiltonian has an inverse-polynomial spectral gap, our quantum algorithm prepares its ground state to precision $\delta$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log(1/\delta))$. (2) We further give a quantum algorithm that prepares a purification of the thermal state in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\beta,\log(1/\delta))$. Using this purification, we estimate static and dynamical properties with error $\delta$ in time polynomial in $n$ and $\beta$ and linear in $1/\delta$ up to polylogarithmic factors, achieving the Heisenberg scaling. Our algorithms build on quantum Gibbs samplers, which are quantum analogues of Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. By using global jump operators instead of local ones, we avoid the $\exp(\beta)$ overhead commonly associated with quantum Gibbs samplers, making them efficient for impurity models even at low temperatures.

authors.name: Jiaqing Jiang, Nathan Ju

papers.title: Combining Schr\"odinger and Heisenberg Evolution to Extend Quantum Many-Body Simulations
papers.summary: Classical simulations of quantum many-body dynamics face complementary limitations: entanglement growth restricts state evolution in the Schr\"odinger picture, while operator spreading makes Heisenberg-picture calculations increasingly expensive. Here, we combine both approaches by evolving quantum states and observables independently and joining their dynamics through massively parallel tensor-network contractions. We implement this strategy using tree tensor networks and sparse Pauli propagation, extending evolution times beyond those reached by either method separately in our calculations. For a quench of the two-dimensional transverse-field Ising model at the critical field, we simulate the magnetization of an $11\times11$ open lattice up to $t=1.20$ by combining state and operator evolution over intervals $t_S=t_H=0.60$. We compare the dynamics with iPEPS, numerical linked-cluster expansion, and X-truncated sparse Pauli dynamics results. We also combine exact state evolution on small clusters with operator propagation on a larger lattice, improving agreement with iPEPS relative to cluster evolution alone. We further derive error bounds showing how the state can suppress operator errors and the evolved observable can reduce sensitivity to state errors.

authors.name: Zhigang Hu, Igor Ermakov, Yauheni Talochka, Biao Wu, Oleg Lychkovskiy

papers.title: Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error
papers.summary: Subentropy gives a tight spectral lower bound on the accessible information of ensembles of pure states. We prove its subadditivity for arbitrary bipartite states in finite dimensions and derive a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and the minimum discrimination error. This relation strengthens a conjectured comparison with conditional min-entropy. Its inverse gives the strongest universal lower bound on the error determined only by conditional subentropy and the number of labels. Both main results follow from a comparison of conditional subentropy with the average subentropy of measurement posteriors, valid for mixed signal states and every finite measurement. We characterize all equality cases in these two results and bound posterior deviations near equality. We also determine the optimal Lipschitz constant in trace distance for conditional subentropy on classical-quantum states, including the exact constant when the quantum marginal is fixed. A determinant inequality strengthens subadditivity and proves strong subadditivity for classical distributions, while an exact counterexample shows that strong subadditivity fails for quantum states. Lean 4 proofs of all theoretical results are available at https://pratikpatil.io/lean/subentropy/

authors.name: Pratik Patil

papers.title: Privacy-Enhanced Distributed Sensing Network via Causal-Order Switching and Probe Squeezing
papers.summary: As sensor networks become more interconnected, sensitive information sharing among multiple users poses potential risks of information leakage, making privacy protection a critical challenge. To address this challenge, we quantify network privacy using the maximum information leakage ratio (MILR) and propose a protocol that enhances privacy through causal-order switching and probe squeezing. Causal-order switching harnesses intrinsic network propagation dynamics for privacy encoding, while probe squeezing suppresses information leakage through quantum channels and increases the information available for estimating the global parameter. These mechanisms enable an asymptotic exponential enhancement on the privacy with the squeezing rate. We experimentally demonstrate this mechanism in distributed beam-tilt sensing using spatially structured light without requiring nonclassical light sources. Our work identifies intrinsic network propagation dynamics as a resource for privacy protection and opens a new avenue for continuous-variable sensing networks that combine high precision with enhanced privacy.

authors.name: Zhaotong Cui, Binke Xia, Yuxiang Yang, Hongjing Li, Jingzheng Huang, Guihua Zeng

papers.title: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction
papers.summary: Bosonic quantum error correction relies on an accurate description of single-photon loss dissipation using an ideal annihilation operator, under which correctable loss errors act equivalently on different logical code states. In realistic weakly nonlinear bosonic modes, however, coupling to a structured environment can render photon loss Fock-state dependent, thereby modifying the effective dissipation operator and deforming the associated error space. Here, we experimentally investigate this effect in a three-dimensional circuit quantum electrodynamics system. By injecting spectrally engineered environmental noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator, we observe pronounced frequency selectivity in the measured Fock-state dynamics. While the long-time transition rates converge to the Markovian limit, the transient dynamics display distinctly non-Markovian behavior, in quantitative agreement with a second-order time-convolutionless theory. By applying narrowband noise to a binomially encoded logical qubit, we further demonstrate Fock-state-dependent dissipation channels that drive logical states beyond the nominally correctable error space. These results establish structured environmental noise as a mechanism for deforming photon-loss errors in weakly nonlinear bosonic systems and highlight the need to incorporate realistic, state-dependent dissipation into the design and characterization of bosonic quantum error correction.

authors.name: Guoyu Shu, Ling Hu, Hongbo Wu, Zhongchu Ni, Yanyan Cai, Xiaowei Deng, Pan Zheng, Pengbo Li, Fei Yan, Song Liu, Dapeng Yu, Yuan Xu

papers.title: Exact finite-sample and loss limits of squeezed-vacuum phase estimation
papers.summary: We settle the dispute over squeezed-vacuum phase estimation by exact computation of the finite-sample errors, resource-fair scaling, phase window, and loss ceilings. A fixed overhead of ten repetitions sets the attainable finite-sample frontier; the repetitions cancel from the resource-fair bound, so Heisenberg scaling survives; the operating window holds a repetition-set number of resolvable points and needs one bit of branch prior; and fixed loss caps the per-photon advantage at a value set only by transmissivity, already reached by the reported record.

authors.name: Wangjun Lu, Qing Yu

papers.title: Liouvillian Quasiparticle Spectroscopy
papers.summary: Quasiparticles play a central role in understanding closed quantum many-body systems, as they reduce complex many-body problems to effective single-particle descriptions and connect directly to spectroscopic measurements. In open quantum systems, the interplay between coherent dynamics and dissipation gives rise to unique phenomena, such as the Liouvillian skin effect and strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. This raises a fundamental question: how can the quasiparticle picture be extended to open quantum systems to account for such phenomena and enable the experimental probing of quasiparticle spectra? Here we introduce coherent and incoherent Liouvillian quasiparticles, defined by responses to perturbations acting on one side and both sides of the density matrix, respectively. We propose spectroscopy protocols that couple the system to auxiliary levels, either coherently or via a dissipative pulse, to measure the corresponding complex quasiparticle energies. Numerical simulations of Liouvillians with skin effects validate these protocols, revealing nontrivial spectral winding associated with unidirectional transport in real space. Notably, coherent and incoherent quasiparticles can propagate in opposite directions within the same system. Furthermore, in models exhibiting weak and strong-to-weak $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking, our results unveil gapless Nambu-Goldstone modes in the coherent and incoherent quasiparticle spectra, respectively; the other quasiparticle spectrum remains gapped in each case. Our work provides a unified framework for theoretically describing and experimentally probing coherent and incoherent quasiparticles in open quantum many-body systems.

authors.name: Kai Li, Masahito Ueda

papers.title: Universal stabilizer correlations in chaotic eigenstates
papers.summary: Entanglement and nonstabilizerness provide complementary perspectives on quantum-state structure.
