In this work, we find that the stabilizer correlation, defined as the difference between the R\'enyi-$2$ mutual information and the mutual stabilizer R\'enyi entropy, approaches a universal constant for chaotic eigenstates. This constant is determined solely by the symmetries, and quantifies the correlation that does not contribute to nonstabilizerness. We identify this universal stabilizer correlation analytically via random-state ensembles, which give $\log_2 7$ (GOE) and $\log_2 4$(GUE) without extra symmetries, $\log_2 14$ and $\log_2 8$ under spin-inversion parity or half-filling magnetization. While imposing reflection or translation symmetry leaves these values unchanged. Exact calculations for a chaotic mixed-field Ising chain confirm the predicted plateau and finite-size approach. Integrable free-fermion and strongly disordered eigenstates behave qualitatively differently. This universal stabilizer correlation reveals a characteristic structure of chaotic eigenstates beyond entanglement or nonstabilizerness alone.

authors.name: Zhi-Han Liu, Hao-Yue Qi, Wei Zheng

papers.title: Binary-Tree Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for the Maximum $k$-Cut Problem
papers.summary: The maximum $k$-cut (Max-$k$-Cut) problem, as a natural generalization of the maximum-cut (MaxCut) problem, has broader applications in practical engineering. To solve this problem on quantum devices, existing studies typically encode the $k$ possible subset assignments of each vertex within the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA), which directly causes the required quantum resources to grow substantially with $k$. Here we propose a binary-tree quantum approximate optimization algorithm (BT-QAOA), which solves the Max-$k$-Cut problem by applying standard MaxCut QAOA to at most $2k-3$ subproblems. Specifically, after solving MaxCut once on the full vertex set, each subsequent step splits only the subset that yields the largest cut-value gain. This process is equivalent to constructing a binary tree whose leaf nodes after $k-1$ steps form an approximate solution to the Max-$k$-Cut problem. Furthermore, we derive a theoretical lower bound on the approximation ratio in terms of the single-step splitting quality, showing that the overall approximation ratio does not decay exponentially across multiple splits. Numerical simulations show that BT-QAOA substantially reduces the single-circuit qubit and gate overhead while maintaining a high approximation ratio, improving the estimated success probability of a single compiled circuit by orders of magnitude. This work effectively expands the practical reach of QAOA on near-term quantum hardware, offering a new route for solving more complex real-world optimization problems with limited quantum resources.

authors.name: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, Hong-Fu Wang

papers.title: Quantum Imaging of Nonlinear Magnetization Reversal and Dissipative Domain Dynamics
papers.summary: To investigate the rich nonlinear dynamics of magnetic materials, we introduce a stroboscopic quantum diamond microscopy technique to probe the dynamic AC response of a Pt/Co/Pt thin film using nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond. By overcoming the limited dynamic range of conventional optically detected magnetic resonance based imaging, our approach enables the observation of magnetization reversal under various large-amplitude sinusoidal and square wave excitations. The observed phase delay between the applied field and the sample response reveals information about the energy dissipated within the material. The temporal evolution reveals magnetization reversal through domain nucleation and growth also demonstrating isolated bubble domains associated with the defects. Furthermore, the detection of higher order harmonics provides access to the nonlinear AC susceptibility. These results establish stroboscopic quantum diamond microscope as a promising tool for spatially and temporally resolving nonlinear magnetization dynamics, with potential applications extending beyond ferromagnetic systems to complex magnetic crystals, magnetic phase transitions and superconductor vortex dynamics.

authors.name: Manali Verma, Dasika Shishir, Prajna Shubhranshu Mahaku, P. S Anil Kumar, Kasturi Saha

papers.title: Floquet dark-mode manipulation in a three-mode optomechanical system
papers.summary: We propose a Floquet sideband method to manipulate the dark-mode effect in a three-mode optomechanical system consisting of a single cavity mode coupled to two mechanical modes. We introduce a periodic frequency modulation for one mechanical mode to generate the Floquet sidebands, one of which is selected to match the resonance frequency of the other mechanical mode, allowing complete destructive interference to produce a mechanical dark mode decoupled from the cavity mode. The semiclassical operating point is determined self-consistently within the framework for linearization of optomechanical interaction, and the linear stability is examined under the rotating-wave approximation. We evaluate the validity of the approximate Hamiltonian by examining the fidelity between the states governed by the approximate and exact Hamiltonians. We further demonstrate dark-mode control by inspecting the bright/dark-mode populations of the system, when a frequency detuning is introduced suddenly. These results may provide a basis for further study of quantum-state storage using the Floquet mechanical dark modes.

authors.name: Mian Mao, Jin-Feng Huang, Jie-Qiao Liao

papers.title: Quantum Cyclic XYZ Stabilizer Codes
papers.summary: XYZ codes generalize the Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) framework by adding $\sym{Y}$-type stabilizers to the usual $\sym{X}$- and $\sym{Z}$-type ones. We study XYZ codes whose three classical component codes are binary cyclic codes of odd length~$n$. Assigning disjoint sets of irreducible factors of $x^n-1$ to the three Pauli types fixes the number of encoded logical qubits and ensures that the row spaces of the three parity-check matrices intersect pairwise trivially. Then, a coprimality condition between the factors assigned to each type and the reciprocals of those assigned to the others guarantees the required orthogonality. Cyclotomic cosets give a complete and explicit description of the resulting family. We show that, for odd~$n$, a cyclic stabilizer code admits an XYZ representation with cyclic component codes iff its stabilizer generators are invariant, up to a phase, under the qubit permutation $i\mapsto 2i\bmod n$. By fixing the length and the dimension of the code, the proposed cyclic XYZ codes attain the best known minimum distance of stabilizer codes, exceed the minimum distance of the underlying CSS codes, and even exceed the linear-programming upper bounds for general CSS codes.

authors.name: Alessio Baldelli, Francisco L\'azaro, Davide Orsucci, Massimo Battaglioni

papers.title: Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization
papers.summary: Here we present an approach to quantifying superposition of nonorthogonal reference states through quantum coherence. No change of basis achieves this: every orthonormal basis makes some superposition-free states appear coherent. We show that orthogonalization succeeds instead as a measurement mapping every reference state onto a multiple of a basis vector in each outcome; such measurements are exactly the free operations that convert superposition into coherence. The largest average coherence they extract from a state, which we call its degree of superposition, turns every coherence measure into a superposition measure with the same operational meaning. An interference term becomes coherence at most with the probability of unambiguously discriminating its two reference states, a bound attained when there are no others and, for positive coefficients and nonnegative overlaps, exactly when the overlaps are probabilities of a random grouping. Maximal degree means conversion into a maximally coherent state with certainty, possible for up to three reference states but not in general. Each coherence measure gives its own degree; when two degrees order two superpositions oppositely, neither converts into the other with certainty, and we find such pairs already for two reference states, unlike in qubit coherence. For equal positive overlaps, in-phase superpositions are rigid: deterministic conversions that keep all components can only permute their coefficients. As the reference states merge, the degree stays bounded where widely used measures can diverge, and at every amplitude a rotation-symmetric cat state attains its maximum. Our results quantify superposition operationally and reveal conversion constraints created by nonorthogonality.

authors.name: G\"okhan Torun

papers.title: THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
papers.summary: The quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architecture is a promising approach to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing, enabling flexible qubit interactions by transporting ions between dedicated trap zones. Programs for such systems require operations beyond conventional circuit primitives: ion shuttling, physical SWAPs, trap splitting and merging, and cooling. Motional excitation accumulated during transport increases the mean phonon number of ions and degrades the fidelity of the two-qubit Molmer-Sorensen gates. However, existing quantum error correction (QEC) simulation frameworks do not jointly track per-ion motional excitation and explicitly schedule cooling operations with their transport time and heating costs. We develop a full-stack software framework for QEC experiments and simulations on linear QCCD systems with a single ion species, comprising an intermediate representation (IR) supporting QCCD-native operations, a compiler that translates syndrome-extraction circuits into the IR, and a heating-aware noise-injection pipeline that generates noisy Stim circuits. The compiler updates the mean phonon number of each ion throughout the schedule, and the pipeline derives gate-dependent error rates from the tracked phonon states and per-ion timing, enabling the evaluation of finite-size logical-error scaling of the rotated surface code under transport- and heating-aware noise. We show that transport-induced heating prevents logical error rates from decreasing with increasing code distance under the evaluated conditions, and that indirectly cooling the ion pairs involved in two-qubit gates, by merging them with precooled coolant ions immediately before each gate, restores this decrease. By sweeping the duration and post-cooling mean phonon number of an abstract cooling instruction, we characterize their trade-off and identify the region in which logical-error scaling is maintained.

authors.name: Eitaro Ishikawa, Noah Hirai, Koichiro Miyanishi, Hana Ebi, Kazufumi Tanji, Isamu Kudo, Kenji Toyoda, Masahiro Takeoka, Hiroki Takahashi, Takahiko Satoh, Shin Nishio

papers.title: Coherence transfer under bounded channel capacity
papers.summary: We investigate quantum coherence transfer between two parties whose local reference bases are misaligned, under a constraint on the capacity of the quantum communication channel. Within the resource theory of coherence, we formulate the task as maximizing the coherence received by Bob when Alice is restricted to Maximally Incoherent Operations (MIO) in her local basis. We first analyze two single-shot protocols, based on direct and locally entangled transmission, and derive their phase-optimized coherence yields. We further investigate their performance when Bob's reference basis is unknown, averaging over uniformly distributed basis configurations. In the asymptotic regime, we exploit the reversibility of coherence under MIO to characterize achievable transfer rates in terms of Alice's initial coherence. For single-qubit transmission, we derive an analytical lower bound using pure-state conversions and identify a regime in which the optimal yield saturates the channel capacity.

authors.name: Dhruv Baheti, Karol Horodecki

papers.title: Geometric properties of concatenated geometric and holonomic quantum gates
papers.summary: We investigate the geometric properties of concatenated quantum gates, focusing on the distinction between geometric and holonomic quantum computation. We show that, although individual gates may be purely geometric, their concatenation does not generally preserve this property, since the cyclic states of the composite operation can accumulate nontrivial dynamical phases over the course of the concatenated evolution. In contrast, we demonstrate that concatenations of arbitrary single-qubit holonomic gates remain holonomic, provided that the parallel-transport condition holds throughout the evolution and the computational subspace undergoes cyclic evolution. The preservation of geometric or holonomic character under concatenation is an important prerequisite for extending arguments underlying geometric protection from individual gates to complete quantum circuits.

authors.name: Rasmus Wallentin, Erik Sj\"oqvist

papers.title: Efficient Shot Allocation and Spectral Reconstruction for Real-Time Quantum Krylov Diagonalization
papers.summary: We develop analytical and statistical methods to improve the energy estimate from the real-time quantum Krylov diagonalization under a fixed measurement budget. We first express the leading energy variance as a function of the number of shots assigned to each circuit setting, accounting for both the sensitivity of the energy to the measured moments and the correlations among outcomes recorded in the same shot.We use an initial batch of measurements to choose how to allocate the remaining shots. Under fixed-model regularity assumptions, the resulting generalized least-squares energy estimator attains the minimum leading mean-square error (MSE) coefficient within the prescribed allocation class, with the initial measurements included in the total shot budget. Furthermore, we use the same data to reconstruct the Hamiltonian and overlap moments jointly by fitting them to a common nonnegative spectral measure. For asymptotically Gaussian moment errors, we characterize precisely when this reconstruction lowers the leading energy MSE in the case where two linearly independent inequalities describe the feasible moment perturbations to first order. Numerical experiments on spin and Hubbard models show that learned allocation can improve Ritz energy estimates at fixed total shot cost. The experiments also illustrate that enforcing spectral consistency can further reduce the energy estimation error.

authors.name: Pegah Mohammadipour, Xiantao Li

papers.title: Dephasing-Powered Autonomous Quantum Engine with Time-Crystalline Work Cycles
papers.summary: Autonomous quantum engines seek to convert energy supplied by environments into useful work, yet dephasing is usually regarded as detrimental noise. Here we show that local dephasing can instead power a quantum engine: by disrupting ferromagnetic correlations in an interacting spin-$1/2$ ensemble, it injects energy that can be transferred through an LC resonator to a passive load. Remarkably, without any external periodic driving, the coupled system can self-organize into a time-crystalline work cycle that delivers sustained, reproducible power. Within homogeneous mean-field dynamics, we identify two distinct routes to such operation. At weak spin--resonator coupling, the dissipative time crystal of the unloaded working medium survives loading and drives the receiver. At stronger coupling, resonator backaction can disrupt cyclic operation, whereas appropriate load damping restores a stable, self-consistent periodic cycle of the composite system. Finite-size spin-diffusion simulations further reveal rapidly increasing uninterrupted operating times with different size dependences in the two regimes. Our results demonstrate how an autonomous quantum engine can self-organize its collective dynamics through interactions and load feedback to harness environmental noise for sustained cyclic work output.

authors.name: Zhen-huan Yang, Dan-Bo Zhang

papers.title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
papers.summary: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.

authors.name: Hanieh Najafzadeh, Radmehr Jafari, Abdollah Langari

papers.title: Optimal fidelity over zero-capacity erasure channels
papers.summary: Antidegradable quantum channels have zero capacity for reliable quantum communication. However, they can nevertheless transmit quantum information with nontrivial fidelity. This raises the question: how well can quantum information be preserved through such channels? In this work, we exactly characterize the optimal asymptotic entanglement fidelity of quantum erasure channels throughout the antidegradable regime. Specifically, we show that it equals $\gamma+\frac{1-\gamma}{d}$ for transmission probabilities $0<\gamma\le \frac{1}{2}$ and logical dimension $d$. We use fractional extendibility to establish an upper bound on the entanglement fidelity achievable by arbitrary error-correcting protocols. Furthermore, we construct a family of permutation-invariant codes that asymptotically saturates this bound.

authors.name: Camilo Castro-Landolt, Rabsan Galib Ahmed, Graeme Smith

papers.title: Mitigating drift in spin-qubit control with calibration-insensitive pulses
papers.summary: Silicon spin qubits offer fault-tolerant control fidelities in a platform that is compatible with commercial foundries, but device calibration drifts and control parameters must be retuned every few hours. Here, we replace conventional square control pulses with two drift-resilient pulse families: the adiabatic BIR-4 and the composite CORPSE. In a Si/SiGe quantum-dot device, we benchmark single-qubit gate sets built from each pulse against deliberate miscalibration. We find that BIR-4 offers a 99% Clifford fidelity over a factor of 2 change in drive power and CORPSE maintains similar fidelity over +/-0.9MHz of offset. When fully calibrated CORPSE offers a 99.97% fidelity per gate, on par with a calibrated square pulse. Starting with tuned pulses, we then track errors using gate-set tomography for ten days without recalibration. BIR-4 holds its rotation angle to 0.3 degrees throughout, including across a 1.3MHz frequency jump. Our results demonstrate that these pulses can maintain high-fidelity operations without constant recalibration, mitigating the need for constant tuning, which is a key bottleneck in scaling quantum-dot-based quantum processors.

authors.name: Mridul Pushp, Jonathan Hess, Seong Woo Oh, Vatsal K. Bandaru, Shize Che, Noah D. Johnson, Anthony J. Sigillito

papers.title: Linear entanglement suffices for $f$-routing
papers.summary: In $f$-routing, Alice receives an $n$-bit string $x$ and an unknown qubit, and Bob receives an $n$-bit string $y$. They share a state prepared in advance and exchange one simultaneous message each. The party selected by the Boolean function $f(x,y)$ must then recover the unknown qubit without further communication. To perform $f$-routing successfully, Alice and Bob need to share entanglement that scales with $n$ for some functions $f$, but the lower and upper bounds for the entanglement are not tight. This paper shows that $2n+2$ shared EPR pairs suffice for every function $f$. The best previous bound that holds for all functions is a shared state of $2^{O(\sqrt{n\log n})}$ qubits. The new strategy moves the cost from the shared state to the messages: Alice sends an exponentially long message of $2^{n+1}+1$ qubits, while Bob sends only classical bits. When the messages are counted towards the resources as well, the previous strategy remains the cheapest known. The result also limits lower bounds that count only the shared state: they cannot exceed a linear number of EPR pairs. The result is formalized in Lean.

authors.name: Kevin Bogner

papers.title: Wigner negativity costs phase-space area: A conjectured refinement of the Lieb--Solovej inequality at R\'enyi order one half
papers.summary: We conjecture that the Wigner logarithmic negativity of any single-mode state is bounded by the amount by which the R\'enyi-$1/2$ entropy of its Husimi function exceeds the coherent-state value, with equality only for coherent states. If true, this refines the Lieb--Solovej (generalized Wehrl) inequality with a remainder term that is a resource monotone, and it implies that heterodyne statistics alone certify an upper bound on the classical-simulation cost of a state. We show that it suffices to prove the conjecture for pure states, since the negativity is convex and the squared $L^{1/2}$ norm of the Husimi function is concave. We prove the conjecture up to an additive constant $\ln 2$ for all states, and identify where the factor of two is lost: For pure states the Wigner function is the wavefunction of a two-mode state obtained by passive operations, and over generic two-mode wavefunctions our constant is already optimal, so that a proof of the sharp bound must exploit the product structure of that state. Finally, we show with an explicit superposition of the vacuum and a distant coherent state that the analogous inequality fails for the Wehrl entropy and for higher R\'enyi orders, meaning that the conjecture is not a consequence of the majorization relation underlying the Lieb--Solovej theorem.

authors.name: Christos N. Gagatsos

papers.title: Solving the Traveling Salesman Problem Using Quantum Devices: QUBO and HOBO Formulations
papers.summary: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) forms the foundation for many logistics and optimization tasks. At the same time, this problem is NP-hard and requires significant computational resources. Quantum computing promises to substantially accelerate computations or increase solution accuracy. The TSP can be conveniently mapped onto the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulation, which in turn can be solved using variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) methods, but this mapping requires a quadratic number of qubits. The higher-order binary optimization (HOBO) formulation requires significantly fewer qubits, but it contains higher-order terms. In our work, we thoroughly investigate both formulations and provide a practical recipe for solving the TSP. We give a comprehensive study and compare in detail QUBO and HOBO formulations.

authors.name: G. V. Shuvalov, E. N. Krivtsova, A. V. Kapranov, M. A. Remnev

papers.title: Quantum Approximation and Integration in Sobolev Spaces -- Low Smoothness
papers.summary: We study the complexity of approximation and integration in Sobolev spaces in the quantum setting of information-based complexity theory (IBC). Previous results have been obtained under the assumption that the embedding condition holds. Here we drop this assumption and use a quantum version of a previously developed stochastic discretization technique.

authors.name: Stefan Heinrich

papers.title: Resilience of Entangling Gates to Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise
papers.summary: As quantum processors scale, spatially and temporally correlated noise is emerging as a limiting factor in the fidelity of multiqubit gates. Here we show that this makes the choice of entangling operation a first-order design decision: for two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, the CZ and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates exhibit a pronounced resilience to correlated noise relative to the SWAP gate, even though correlated fluctuations of the entangling interaction can degrade gate performance to a level comparable to that of local noise. We trace this hierarchy to the redistribution of noise-sensitive channels away from zero frequency and show it to hold for noise spectra dominated by low-frequency weight, including $1/f$ and Lorentzian. These results follow from a general expression, derived here, for the average gate infidelity under arbitrary spatiotemporal noise correlations, valid for generic multiqubit systems and system-environment coupling structures. The infidelity takes the form of a spectral overlap between the noise correlation matrix and a gate-dependent filter function, in which the coherent dynamics of the gate itself shapes the spectral window through which correlated fluctuations enter. The framework converts measured noise correlations into quantitative error budgets and provides a concrete design principle for selecting entangling operations in scalable quantum architectures.

authors.name: Xinru Tang, Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Stefano Bosco, Jelena Klinovaja, Daniel Loss

papers.title: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula
papers.summary: We construct a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects the critical-line zeros of a regularized zeta function within a continuous spectrum. Starting from the exact Riemann--Siegel integral representation, we define $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ by subtracting the contribution of the pole at the origin. The two remaining contour integrals supply the interfering amplitudes. A Dirichlet heat filter suppresses high spatial frequencies, and an arithmetic dressing has a profile generated by prime-power dilations. These transformations map the dilation generator to a self-adjoint, parity--time ($PT$) symmetric Hamiltonian on a physical Hilbert space with a positive metric. Its spectrum is real and continuous. The computed lower critical-line zeros of $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ lie close to the corresponding Riemann zeros and exhibit spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.

authors.name: Germ\'an Sierra

papers.title: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
papers.summary: Modular exponentiation dominates the logical cost of factoring 2048-bit RSA integers (RSA-2048) with Shor's algorithm. Recent approaches based on approximate residue number systems (RNS) sharply reduce the required logical qubits, yet still demand billions of Toffoli gates. Optimizing these circuits is difficult because shared ancilla qubits and measurement-based uncomputation tightly couple the arithmetic stages, while rare overflows in compressed registers occur too infrequently for random simulation to detect. Here we use large language model (LLM)-driven search to redesign the RNS pipeline across stages and build a deterministic compiler that produces a Pareto frontier of RSA-2048 circuits. We bound rare overflow probabilities analytically and verify the resulting elementary gate sequences across all constituent RNS primes on representative circuits. Relative to Gidney's 2025 baseline under matched adder accounting, our frontier cuts the minimum qubit-Toffoli product by 70.1% and lowers expected factoring Toffolis by up to 78.6% at matched accumulator precision, bringing RSA-2048 factoring below one billion Toffolis for the first time.

authors.name: Xiaodi Li, Yuqing Wang, Xue Chen, Yang-Yang Tang, Linghui Chen, Tao Zhang

papers.title: Floquet spectra and parameter sensitivity of entanglement in the quantum kicked top
papers.summary: We investigate the relationship between the Floquet spectrum and the sensitivity of the entanglement landscape to parameter and initial condition change in the quantum kicked top. We focus on the case of four qubits and on locating degeneracies in its Floquet eigenphases using the resultant of its characteristic polynomial $p$ and its derivative $\partial_{\lambda}p$ and quantitatively map the sensitivity of the entanglement landscape to changes in kicking strength over the sphere of spin coherent initial states. We find that prominent sensitivity maxima coincide with either Floquet eigenphase degeneracies or kick strengths exhibiting short-period quantum revivals, with some points satisfying both conditions. These results establish a connection between the spectral structure of the Floquet operator and entanglement landscape sensitivity, demonstrating the utility of the resultant in studying the dynamics of small-$j$ quantum kicked tops. Since this structure extends to all values of $j$, the central lessons apply completely generally.

authors.name: Dyari Jarvis, Peter A. Rose, Arjendu K. Pattanayak

papers.title: Self-guided estimation of the stabilizer fidelity with single-copy Pauli measurements
papers.summary: The stabilizer fidelity quantifies the non-stabilizerness of pure states, but it is hard to estimate because it requires optimizing over $2^{O(n^2)}$ stabilizer states for $n$ qubits. Here, we propose a self-guided estimation protocol for the stabilizer fidelity of an unknown state, pure or mixed, which requires only Pauli measurements on single copies. The protocol moves through the graph of neighboring stabilizer states, obtains the fidelities of a whole stabilizer basis from a single direct fidelity estimation, and reuses previous outcomes, which also provide a restart point that mitigates the barren plateau of a random start. In addition, it certifies the global optimum when the lower confidence bound of the estimated fidelity exceeds $\cos^2(\pi/8)$. In numerical simulations of up to 14 qubits, the protocol reached the optimum in all runs, with the number of iterations remaining small and increasing only slightly with $n$.

authors.name: M. Torres, J. Gidi, L. Pereira

papers.title: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
papers.summary: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.

authors.name: Bikun Li, Guo Zheng, Liang Jiang

papers.title: Small-world networks yield tunable quantum codes at short circuit depth
papers.summary: Monitored random quantum circuits naturally generate quantum error-correcting codes. We generate quantum codes with tunable properties by implementing random Clifford circuits on Watts--Strogatz `small-world' networks and tailor code properties via three knobs: nonlocal graph rewiring, measurement rate, and circuit depth. On fully rewired networks, circuits of logarithmic depth produce codes with a finite rate and an extensive mean contiguous distance with failure probability substantially lower than codes produced from local circuits. These small-world codes form at a circuit depth growing as $\ln n$ compared to polynomial depths required for codes produced from local networks. Rewiring also moves the purification transition to higher measurement rates and changes its critical exponents. Connectivity is thus a knob for designing codes.

authors.name: Samuel Bevins, Gregory Bentsen

papers.title: Two messages suffice for quantum interactive proof systems
papers.summary: Quantum interactive proof systems can be parallelized to three messages, as shown by Kitaev and Watrous (STOC 2000), perhaps their most striking distinction from classical counterparts. In this work, we establish that any quantum interactive proof system can further be parallelized to two messages, with the verifier sending halves of EPR pairs (``quantum public coins'') and, after the prover's response, using only stoquastic verification. Technically, we strengthen ${\sf QIP}(3) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}$ of Jain, Ji, Upadhyay, and Watrous (JACM, 2011) and fully characterize two-message quantum interactive proof systems by proving \[ {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf StoqAM} = {\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf QAM} = {\sf QIP}(2) = {\sf QIP} = {\sf PSPACE}. \] Our main technical contributions show that Close Image to Uniform (CIUniform), which is naturally in the stoquastic version of ${\rm qq}\text{-}{\sf QAM}$, is $\sf PSPACE$-hard via transforming the sum-check protocol of Shamir (JACM, 1992) and Shen (JACM, 1992) into a CIUniform instance consisting of an efficient sampler whose image distribution is exactly uniform for some input distribution when the underlying quantified Boolean formula is true.

authors.name: Yupan Liu

papers.title: Experimental Demonstration of 7-Dimensional N-Vector Model with Dimensional Inflation and Annealing
papers.summary: We report the first experimental realization of a physical system described by a high-dimensional Hamiltonian comprising up to seven dimensions. Our setup is based on a holographic optical computer, which realizes a dimensional inflation by spatial and temporal multiplexing of lower dimensional systems. We demonstrate an $N$-vector model, with applications in field theory and computing. The approach is scalable and enables table-top implementation of high-dimensional theoretical models, and novel methods for combinatorial optimization. We experimentally demonstrate dimensional annealing: by dynamically reducing the number of dimensions, the ground state of an Ising model is found in complex graphs by an adiabatic evolution from high-dimensional spaces.

authors.name: Daniele Veraldi, Marcello Calvanese Strinati, Paolo Charlesworth, Matteo Spaziani, Silvia Gentilini, Davide Pierangeli, Claudio Conti

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Risk Portfolio Optimization via Exponential Tilting
papers.summary: Financial portfolio optimization is often framed through mean-variance objectives, yet real profit-and-loss (P&L) scenario distributions are typically discrete and non-Gaussian. To explore realistic P&L distributions, we propose an objective function based on exponential tilting and certainty equivalent under constant absolute risk aversion. We then derive a second-order approximation, recovering a quadratic optimization problem solvable through mixed integer quadratic programming (MIQP) and quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO). Constraints in the QUBO formulation are incorporated via Lagrangian relaxation and slack variable approaches, enabling a direct comparison between classical constrained MIQP and quantum-inspired methods. In order to study how exponential tilting affects mean, standard deviation, and tail-risk measures such as Value at Risk and Conditional Value at Risk, we design an experimental protocol based on scanning a grid of tilt parameters and solving the associated optimization problems. The results on a realistic trading portfolio show how the tilts can be tuned to optimize different risk-return profiles while remaining competitive with those found using other state-of-the-art approaches. Moreover, performance analysis suggests that, even using classical solvers, the QUBO formulation with Lagrangian relaxation scales better than the MIQP approach, providing the best constraint encoding strategy.

authors.name: Fabio Vitale, Francesca Cibrario, Davide Veronelli, Chiara Vercellino, Valeria Zaffaroni, Giacomo Vitali, Gregorio Antonio Polito, Emanuele Dri, Carla Monferrato, Olivier Terzo, Davide Corbelletto, Marco Bianchetti

papers.title: The Thue-Morse route to chaos in the open quantum baker map
papers.summary: We study the resonances of the quantum baker map opened by a window of width $w$ centred at $q_c$. For $q_c=1/2$ the survivor set of the classical doubling map with a hole goes from zero to positive topological entropy along the Thue-Morse route, and we find numerically, for $N$ up to $2^{25}$, that the resonance spectrum follows this route step by step, also where the entropy is zero. Below the threshold $w_c=4a^*-1$, with $a^*$ the Thue-Morse constant, the surviving cycles have periods $2^\nu$ and their thresholds accumulate doubly exponentially. Each cycle gives, as isolated orbits do, a multiplet of resonances close to modulus $2^{-1/2}$, with phases set by its action. Since a cycle is resolved only if its period is shorter than about $\log_2 N$, twice the Ehrenfest time, about $\log_2\log_2 N$ steps are resolved, four at our largest sizes. Near $w_c$ the 16-cycle perturbs the 8-multiplet through a return path that classically opens only at $w_c$. Cutting a few sites of this path removes the perturbation. At $w_c$ the leading resonance jumps within one or two lattice sites, since a window one site wider than the threshold already has an entropy of order $1/\log_2 N$. One site or more above $w_c$ it lies between 0.93 and 1.00 times the value set by the topological pressure, with no free parameter. There the Walsh eigenvalue count grows with the fractal Weyl exponent, and the Fourier count with an exponent a few hundredths smaller at the sizes we reach.

authors.name: Leonardo Ermann

papers.title: Wireless readout and control of cavity magnon-polaritons via photonic modes delocalised across a gap
papers.summary: In cavity magnonics, photon-magnon hybridisation is typically detected by measuring the cavity response (i.e. measuring cavity resonance shifts through its reflection or transmission spectra). While a large body of work in the field has focused on three-dimensional cavities, a variety of two-dimensional resonators have also been explored as hosts for photonic modes due to their compatibility with on-chip integration. Nevertheless, the readout approach remains largely unchanged. Here, we demonstrate remote excitation and readout of cavity magnon-polaritons using two spatially separated, wirelessly coupled ring resonators. Through inductive coupling, energy is transferred between the resonators, enabling the magnonic system to be excited by one resonator while its hybrid-mode spectrum is detected through measurements of the other. We demonstrate wireless readout of cavity magnon-polaritons at separations ranging from millimetres to centimetres, identifying their characteristic response in the remotely measured spectrum. This establishes wireless resonator coupling as a route to remote interrogation of hybrid photon-magnon systems.

authors.name: Alban Joseph, Ryan D McKenzie, Amy Eden, Morven Last, Shannon Howard, Alzbeta Oravcova, Mawgan A Smith, Robert L Stamps, Rair Macedo

papers.title: A High-Frequency Flux-Driven DC-SQUID Threshold Detector at the Single-Microwave-Photon Energy Scale: A Numerical Feasibility Study
papers.summary: In our recent work (Phys. Rev. B \textbf{113}, 224503 (2026)), we showed numerically that rapidly sweeping the bias current of a current-biased Josephson junction threshold detector (CBJJ-JTD) drives it out of equilibrium. This substantially reduces the effect of thermal noise on microwave detection and may enable threshold detection near the energy of a single microwave photon. The scheme requires very low damping ($\beta \leq 10^{-4}$) and a very fast bias-current sweep ($v/\beta \geq 1$), both of which are difficult to achieve with available junctions and low-pass-filtered cryogenic measurement lines. Here we propose a more experimentally accessible nonequilibrium threshold detector based on a high-frequency flux-driven direct-current superconducting quantum interference device (DC-SQUID) and investigate it by numerically solving the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) equations. The applied flux drives a circulating supercurrent and sustains nonequilibrium phase dynamics throughout the bias-current sweep, removing the need for a fast sweep or for transient oscillations set by the initial phase. Using typical experimental device parameters, we calculate switching-current distributions (SCDs) with and without a microwave input for both driven and undriven SQUIDs. We quantify detection performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and their area under the curve (AUC). The simulations show that high-frequency flux drive reduces the impact of thermal noise and enables statistical discrimination of weak microwave pulses at the single-photon energy scale. We also numerically estimate detector characteristics such as phase selectivity and dynamic range.

authors.name: M. Y. Wang, Y. Q. Chai, S. N. Wang, L. F. Wei

papers.title: Feshbach resonances of the second order in a Friedrichs model
papers.summary: We consider an extended version of the matrix Friedrichs model that may produce Feshbach resonances of the second order. In this model, under enlarging of the coupling constant, a pair of eigenvalues of the unperturbed Hamiltonian embedded into the continuous spectrum first transforms in resonances of the first order. At some moment later on, these two resonances merge into a single resonance but of the second order, and we fix conditions for this event. Being based on the operator interpretation of resonances, we found that, in the case under consideration, the operator roots of the transfer function have a very particular structure.

authors.name: Dmitry S. Grudko, Alexander K. Motovilov

papers.title: Path Integrals on Functional Lattices
papers.summary: Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a Galerkin argument. The limit is independent of the compatible functional lattice: any sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces dense in the quadratic-form domain converges to the same continuum covariance and generating functional. A direct Minkowski construction is obtained at fixed Feynman regulator $i\epsilon$, followed by the distributional limit $\epsilon\downarrow0$. For interacting theories, each truncation gives an ordinary non-Gaussian integral. At fixed perturbative order, convergence follows when the finite-resolution graph integrands converge pointwise and admit an integrable majorant independent of the functional resolution. Numerical results for one-dimensional $\phi^4$ theory approach the known first- and second-order mass-gap coefficients, while four-dimensional calculations exhibit the expected mass divergence and logarithmic wave-function renormalization. Thus functional lattices provide a continuum-space approach to path integrals with mathematically controlled limits in the cases considered here.

authors.name: Alexey A. Kryukov

papers.title: Constraint-Preserving Quantum Circuit Compilation for Graph Independent Sets via Persistent Occupancy Encoding
papers.summary: Constraint-preserving mixers for graph independent sets repeatedly evaluate overlapping neighborhood conditions, increasing CX costs across ordered quantum optimization circuits. We propose a structure-aware compiler that reuses these conditions through persistent occupancy encoding. Exploiting mutual exclusion within true-twin classes, our reversible encoding stores class occupancy on the original data register across mixer operations and cost layers. Local mixers are synthesized using target compensation, blockwise parity queries, and coherent restoration; nonuniform cost phases are preserved by an exact coefficient transformation. We prove that the compiled circuit reproduces the original program's unitary action on the feasible subspace for any prescribed operation order and independent layer parameters, and establish exact separability of source-level caching costs under a fixed synthesis recipe. Across 134 evaluation programs and 72 independent confirmation programs, total CX counts fall by 22.61% and 19.87%, respectively, relative to the best of six reference implementations selected per program. Against a matched no-cache implementation, persistent encoding yields additional reductions of 4.10% and 9.13%.

authors.name: Zhiyi Wang, Xiaorui Xue, Xiaoxing Liu

papers.title: Quantum coherence and entanglement of mixed states in relativistic settings
papers.summary: States prepared in laboratory experiments are generally mixed because of imperfect preparation and residual coupling to the environment, whereas pure initial states represent an idealized limit. Motivated by this distinction, we investigate quantum entanglement and coherence in a pair of Unruh-DeWitt detectors initially prepared in a general two-qubit X state. One detector remains inertial and uncoupled, while the other undergoes uniform acceleration and interacts locally with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We obtain the reduced detector state within a perturbative treatment and evaluate its concurrence, $l_1$ norm of coherence, and relative entropy of coherence. For the initial-state families considered, the resulting expressions exhibit entanglement sudden death at finite acceleration, with larger initial entanglement associated with a higher threshold. Both coherence measures remain nonzero beyond this threshold and approach zero in the formal infinite-acceleration limit of these expressions. We also examine the dependence of these resources on the detector energy gap and interaction duration. The results distinguish the persistence of coherence from that of entanglement in the mixed-state detector model and identify initial mixedness as a relevant ingredient in relativistic quantum information.

authors.name: Xing-Le Zhao, Zhen Yang, Shu-Min Wu

papers.title: Reconstruction and geometry of $4\times4$ quantum Sudoku
papers.summary: We study the reconstruction and geometry of $4 \times 4$ quantum Sudoku, viewed as arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks decompose the identity. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for two prescribed opposite blocks to admit a completion, prove its uniqueness, and obtain explicit reconstruction formulas, also expressed in the language of quantum logic. The sixteen overlaps between these blocks determine the unitary equivalence class of the grid, while the number of nonzero overlaps equals its cardinality. Using a matrix representation, we parametrise the equivalence classes by five closed squares, with the sides of one square identified with the diagonals of the other four. The quotient by classical cell symmetries is a closed disc containing exactly two classical classes. Finally, measurement in the basis of the first block gives a fractional Sudoku that retains the full unitary class and is a convex combination of at most four classical grids. This measurement map embeds the five-square model into a seven-dimensional polytope whose vertices are the twelve classical Sudoku.

authors.name: Fabio Deelan Cunden, Paolo Facchi, Roberto La Scala, Marilena Ligab\`o, Karol \.Zyczkowski

papers.title: Analytic continuation of the T- and S-matrices to unphysical sheets in a multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model
papers.summary: We consider a matrix multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model. First, we formulate conditions on the kernels of the potential matrix that guarantee for the T-matrix (and then for the S-matrix) the existence of analytical continuation to unphysical energy sheets. We also obtain explicit representations for the analytically continued T- and S-matrices on unphysical sheets in terms of these matrices themselves, but only taken in the physical sheet. From the explicit representations obtained, it follows that the resonances on a certain unphysical sheet are nothing but the points at which the corresponding truncation of the scattering matrix in the physical sheet has an eigenvalue of 0.

authors.name: Mikhail V. Kremenetsky, Alexander K. Motovilov

papers.title: Ground-State Manifold Curvature and Phase Transitions in the Kitaev Honeycomb Model
papers.summary: The Kitaev honeycomb model is an exactly solvable spin model whose ground state realizes a quantum spin liquid with gapped Abelian phases and a gapless phase that becomes a non-Abelian phase in a magnetic field. Here we study its phase transitions through the geometry of the ground-state manifold, using the Ricci scalar of the quantum metric. In the three gapped phases we obtain closed-form expressions for the curvature, which is negative and diverges at the critical lines; the three phases are related to one another by an exact change of coordinates. In the gapless phase, the curvature of the infrared-regularized metric is positive and decays inversely with the logarithm of the system size, with a size-independent amplitude that diverges at the phase boundaries, with an exponent different from that of the gapped side. The change of sign and the divergences together reproduce the complete phase diagram. A magnetic field gaps out the gapless phase and plays the role of the infrared cutoff, so that away from the critical lines the curvature of the non-Abelian phase becomes finite and positive, while around the critical lines it opens a crossover region whose width scales quadratically with the field. Since divergences of geometric quantities are often regarded as signatures of phase transitions, the divergence of the Ricci scalar at the critical lines provides a geometric signature of these transitions.

authors.name: Omid Yahyayi Monem, Setare Bashari, Hosein Mohammadzadeh

papers.title: Exact many-body scars of generic spin models from singlet covers
papers.summary: The square-lattice transverse-field Ising model has exact zero-energy eigenstates at any field: products of singlets on alternate plaquette diagonals. A longitudinal field isolates them from a symmetry-protected degeneracy. The mechanism is that a site coupled equally to both ends of a singlet annihilates it. The result thus holds for any spin $s$, anisotropic exchange, a large class of bond disorder and certain three-spin terms. This mechanism decides which lattices host such states: two of the 11 Archimedean lattices (four at $s=1/2$), bcc and quasicrystals with spins on the edges. Singlet pumping cools any state into them.

authors.name: Camilla Polvara, William Witczak-Krempa

papers.title: Modulation equations and coherence dynamics in a qubit chain coupled to a circulating fluxon
papers.summary: We derive modulation equations for the joint quantum amplitudes of a circulating fluxon and an exchange-coupled qubit chain whose endpoint interacts with the field. A unitary passage operator combines the translational packet, vacuum dressing, and discrete oscillatory modes. A resonant normal form separates the slow amplitude evolution from nonresonant corrections. Ordered emission and return amplitudes generate a second-order correction that changes the population and coherence of an internal qubit. The next ground-band coefficient gives compensating diagonal and near-resonant off-diagonal contributions to the accumulated error. We bound the state error a posteriori. At a velocity-selected resonance, direct propagation over 81 passages gives a mode contribution of order $6\times10^{-8}$; the cubic ground-band approximation agrees with an expanded full calculation to $1.5\times10^{-9}$ in the tested observables. The equations describe how the source profile and field memory affect coherence inside the chain.

authors.name: O. M. Kiselev

papers.title: Geometric Polarization-Virial Theorems for Field-Induced Dipolar Interactions and Force Reversal
papers.summary: Electric fields can turn attraction into repulsion between far-separated atoms, yet the complete angular mechanical structure governing this reversal has remained unknown. Here, we uncover an entropy-like geometric structure: the cubically weighted interaction free energy, r^3 F(r), is nondecreasing under physical dilation. This structure unifies two exact polarization-virial theorems for arbitrary stable quasistatic dipole assemblies and fully retarded dipole pairs under stated conditions. Consequently, the free energy has at most one zero and energetic cancellation precedes mechanical cancellation. A force zero retains strictly positive energy, whereas an energy zero retains an attractive force. The resulting analytical angular fine structure is resolved by a quantum harmonic oscillator pair, yielding the complete arbitrary-angle interaction energy and radial force that recover quantum-perturbative results. The conventional dipolar magic angle splits into strictly ordered energy- and force-zero angles; the latter uniquely bounds the radially repulsive sector and carries a positive energy barrier. Derived scaling laws and finite-sphere calculations provide experimentally testable signatures from microscopic dipoles to macroscopic polarizable bodies.

authors.name: Shuze Zhu

papers.title: Domain advantage in two-dimensional quantum-device design with multi-modal agentic harness
papers.summary: High-quality two-dimensional quantum devices are commonly fabricated from mechanically exfoliated crystals, whose irregular shapes and placement require a lithographic layout tailored to each specimen. Drawing these layouts remains largely manual. We introduce qlaybench, a benchmark that tests whether language-model agents can turn microscope images and experimental requirements into device layouts that fit the specimen. Agents with conventional tools often construct devices when material outlines are supplied, but struggle to identify those outlines from images. Modelled on the human workflow, qlaybot, a multimodal agentic harness, connects image interpretation to the tools used to align images, draw device features and inspect the resulting layout. We evaluate each layout with checks drawn from practical design experience, asking whether it fits the specimen and connects its intended components. With greater computational effort, an agent using qlaybot passes 81.5% of the benchmark tasks, compared with 24.1% when it uses conventional tools. This domain advantage highlights the importance of connecting scientific interpretation of a specimen to geometric design and provides a route towards reducing manual effort in two-dimensional quantum-device fabrication.

authors.name: Shenhao Miao, Yizhou Li, Liqiao Xia, Ruihao Liu, Dingke Wang, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero, Eli Zeldov, Jiaqi Cai

papers.title: Critical Topology: A New Perspective for Phase Transitions
papers.summary: Critical topology has emerged as a form of quantum criticality beyond the Landau paradigm, challenging conventional approaches to classifying universality classes by introducing topological properties as an additional criterion. Despite substantial progress over the past five years, several fundamental questions remain open. Theoretically, can we establish a general criterion for the emergence of critical topology? Can a unified theoretical framework be extended beyond one-dimensional quantum many-body systems? What efficient numerical methods can be developed to investigate critical topological states in higher-dimensional strongly correlated systems? Experimentally, research has so far focused primarily on single-particle critical topology. An important next step is to realize and characterize many-body critical topology in quantum systems using platforms such as Rydberg atom arrays, superconducting quantum processors, and quantum materials. Major advances in statistical physics often arise from re-examining fundamental concepts. The theory of critical phenomena developed by Landau, Ginzburg, and Wilson, together with the topological phase transitions pioneered by Kosterlitz and Thouless, has now inspired new discoveries in artificial acoustic metamaterials. These experimental observations mark a beginning rather than an endpoint for research on critical topology, and further advances in this direction are anticipated.

authors.name: Xue-Jia Yu

papers.title: Universal thermodynamics and BKT transition of the planar Bose gas from weak to strong interactions
papers.summary: We compute the universal thermodynamics of the dilute two-dimensional Bose gas at weak and strong coupling using the functional renormalization group (FRG). We employ an approximation that retains the full field dependence of the effective potential and spatial derivative terms, extending previous FRG calculations. We find that the equation of state is remarkably insensitive to the approximation scheme, with differences of only a few percent even at strong coupling. By contrast, the improved approximation substantially improves the description of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition, reproducing the universal jump of the superfluid density and the critical anomalous dimension to within a few percent. At weak coupling, our results agree very well with classical-field Monte Carlo simulations, while at stronger coupling we observe deviations from classical-field scaling, valid at weak coupling. Our approach thus provides a quantitative description of the thermodynamics and superfluid density across the BKT transition, including in the strong-coupling regime where classical-field methods are no longer reliable.

authors.name: Yaniss Rabahi, Ivan Balog, Adam Ran\c{c}on

papers.title: For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory
papers.summary: State update rules and their behaviour in Bell tests play an important role in the study of measurement schemes and quantum information. We consider the state updates of the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory using their connection to the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We focus on a set of observables of the form $A(f_i)^*A(f_i)$, where $A(f)$ is the (complex) smeared field operator for any theory induced by a formally hermitian, Green hyperbolic differential operator, and where the $(A(f_i))_{i=1, \dots, m}$ are assumed to be normal and mutually commuting. Under the assumption that these operators have a sufficiently nice representation on a bosonic Fock space, we derive the joint moment generating functional and the unique joint probability distribution for the observables $(A(f_i)^*A(f_i))_{i=1,\dots,m}$. As an application of these results, we construct a model of a Bell inequality test within quantum field theory using a recently developed coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements. We show that our Bell test model can violate the CHSH inequality, approaching Tsirelson's bound for maximally entangled states in the limit where vacuum effects are perfectly rejected. These results show that the state update rules derived in the Fewster-Verch framework are compatible with strongly quantum correlations. They also support a viewpoint in which state updates should be understood in relation to available information.

authors.name: Christopher J. Fewster, Christiane K. M. Klein

papers.title: An Alphabet-Size Bound for the Information Bottleneck Function
papers.summary: The information bottleneck function gives a measure of optimal preservation of correlation between some random variable $X$ and some side information $Y$ while compressing $X$ into a new random variable $W$ with bounded remaining correlation to $X$. As such, the information bottleneck has found many natural applications in machine learning, coding and video compression. The main objective in order to calculate the information bottleneck is to find the optimal representation on $W$. This could in principle be arbitrarily complicated, but fortunately it is known that the cardinality of $W$ can be restricted as $|{\cal W}|\leq|{\cal X}|+1$ which makes the calculation possible for finite $|{\cal X}|$. Now, for many practical applications, e.g. in machine learning, $X$ represents a potentially very large data space, while $Y$ is from a comparably small set of labels. This raises the question whether the known cardinality bound can be improved in such situations. We show that the information bottleneck function can always be approximated up to an error $\delta(\epsilon,|{\cal Y}|)$ with a cardinality $|{\cal W}| \leq f(\epsilon,|{\cal Y}|)$, for explicitly given functions $\delta$ and $f$ of an approximation parameter $\epsilon>0$ and the cardinality of ${\cal Y}$. Finally, we generalize the known cardinality bounds to the case were some of the random variables represent quantum information.

authors.name: Christoph Hirche, Andreas Winter

papers.title: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in transport through interacting quantum dots
papers.summary: We investigate electronic transport through a two-terminal Aharonov-Bohm interferometer with two quantum dots in the presence of finite intra-dot Coulomb interactions. With the help of a diagrammatic technique, we derive, within linear perturbation theory in the tunnelling-coupling strength, analytic expressions for the occupations, current, and interferometric visibility in terms of a coherence measure that involves the sum of four off-diagonal elements of the reduced density matrix. The latter are calculated numerically from a master equation for arbitrary settings of the system parameters. For some symmetric setups, we obtain closed-form expressions for the linear conductance. We systematically analyse the impact of a finite Coulomb interaction on the interferometric visibility, and reveal a rapid suppression of destructive interference upon breaking of system symmetries. Our results are supported by alternative methods, including the TraSPI method.

authors.name: Oliver Oing, Alexander Hahn, J\"urgen K\"onig, Alfred Hucht

papers.title: Coherent Recovery of Nested Codes over the Quantum Erasure Channel Using Erasure Decoding and Quantization
papers.summary: Motivated by quantum capacity results, we revisit nested binary linear codes for the quantum erasure channel through a packing-covering viewpoint: the outer code supports erasure reconstruction, while the inner code performs erasure quantization. We turn this perspective into two explicit decoder architectures. Architecture I requires no stabilizer-syndrome measurements and combines a classical peeling decoder and erasure quantizer with corresponding coherent quantum reconstruction and cleanup operations that disentangle the logical state from inaccessible erasure-environment branches. Architecture II goes one step further and implements erasure belief propagation directly through reversible ternary quantum gates, providing quantum state healing that reconstructs erased symbols while leaving unerased code states unperturbed. We establish sufficient conditions for exact recovery of arbitrary logical states, and illustrate both architectures using the Steane code, including explicit scheduling procedures and coherent quantum circuits.

authors.name: Aditya Guhagarkar, S. Sandeep Pradhan, Achilleas Anastasopoulos

papers.title: Protected Charge Readout Scheme Utilizing Nonlinear Resonators
papers.summary: Charge detection of nanoscale quantum devices commonly relies on dissipative sensors, where signal absorption causes measurement backaction. Recently, nonlinear resonators showed a near-unity readout signal through an induced frequency shift. We show that this frequency shift protects the sensor, as it detunes the resonator from the measurement signal. The resonator excitation reduces while an enhanced readout signal is maintained. Our results, supported by numerical modeling, show that nonlinear resonators can combine strong readout contrast with reduced measurement-induced backaction.

authors.name: Andrea Cicovic, Harald Havir, Pierre Glidic, Samuel Andersson, Sebastian Lehmann, Kimberly A. Dick, Claes Thelander, Ville F. Maisi

papers.title: A resource theory of asynchronous quantum information processing
papers.summary: In standard quantum teleportation, the receiver must wait for a classical message from the sender before subsequently processing the transmitted quantum information. However, in port-based teleportation (PBT), this local processing can begin before the classical message is received, thereby allowing for asynchronous quantum information processing. Motivated by resource-theoretic considerations and practical applications, we propose different communication models that progressively allow for more powerful decoding strategies while still permitting asynchronous distributed quantum computation, a salient feature of standard PBT. Specifically, we consider PBT protocols augmented by free classical processing and/or different forms of quantum pre-processing, and we investigate the maximum achievable teleportation fidelities under such operations. Our analysis focuses specifically on the PBT power of isotropic states, bipartite graph states, and symmetrized EPR states, and we compute tight bounds on the optimal teleportation fidelities for such states. We finally show that, among this hierarchy of communication models consistent with asynchronous quantum information processing, the strongest resource theory is equally as powerful as any one-way teleportation protocol for surpassing the classical teleportation threshold. Thus, a bipartite state can break the one-way classical teleportation threshold if and only if it can be done using the trivial decoding map of discarding subsystems.

authors.name: Chloe Kim, Eric Chitambar, Felix Leditzky

papers.title: Channel coding against quantum jammers via minimax
papers.summary: We study classical communication over fully quantum arbitrarily varying channels, in which a jammer can prepare an arbitrary state entangled across channel uses. We formulate assisted codes as joint input-output maps and apply Sion's minimax theorem to exchange optimization over codes and jamming states at fixed message size. Combining this reduction with one-shot coding bounds and a generalized quantum asymptotic equipartition property yields a single-letter formula for the entanglement-assisted classical capacity, a single-letter formula for the shared-randomness-assisted capacity of classical-quantum channels, and a regularized formula for general quantum input channels. For entanglement assistance and for shared-randomness-assisted classical-quantum channels, we extend the capacity formulas to arbitrary jammer Hilbert spaces while keeping the sender and receiver systems finite-dimensional. The extension uses finite-dimensional approximations at each blocklength, a uniform bound on the change in coding error, and compact closures of finite-dimensional output-state sets. These arguments avoid de Finetti reductions and establish equality with the corresponding compound-channel capacities in these two settings.

authors.name: Michael X. Cao, Yongsheng Yao, Mario Berta

papers.title: Tutorial: Understanding quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno regimes
papers.summary: The quantum Zeno effect is a striking feature of quantum mechanics with foundational implications and practical applications in quantum control, error suppression, and error correction. In recent years, the effect has branched off into a variety of different interpretations, making it easy to miss its underlying unifying features. In particular, the quantum Zeno effect has been studied in the context of both selective and nonselective measurements; for both pulsed and continuous interactions; for suppression and enhancement of decay (Zeno / anti-Zeno effects); and even in the absence of measurement entirely. This tutorial presents a unified picture of these effects by examining how they all arise in the pedagogical example of a driven qubit subjected to measurements or dissipation. Zeno and anti-Zeno effects appear as regimes of a unified effect that appears when a measurement-like process competes with non-commuting evolution. The current landscape of Zeno and anti-Zeno effects is examined through this unifying lens, with a focus on experimental applications and implementations. Thus, this tutorial is ideal for new researchers interested in learning about cutting-edge tools in quantum control and measurement, while remaining highly relevant to quantum computing specialists aiming to understand the quantum Zeno effect's applications in adjacent subfields or apply it in a novel way in their own research. The quantum Zeno effect is found to be both ubiquitous and essential for the future of near-term quantum computing.

authors.name: Sacha Greenfield, Archana Kamal, Justin Dressel, Eli Levenson-Falk

papers.title: Fermion-to-Fermion Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
papers.summary: Simulating fermionic systems on qubit-based quantum computers often demands significant computational resources due to the requirement to map fermions to qubits. Thus, designing a fault-tolerant quantum computer that operates directly with fermions offers an effective solution to this challenge. Here, we introduce a protocol for fault-tolerant fermionic quantum computation utilizing fermion-to-fermion low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. Our architecture employs a fermionic LDPC memory, which transfers its state to fermionic color code processors, where logical operations are subsequently performed. We use odd-weight logical Majorana operators to encode fermionic information in the LDPC memory and provide an algorithm for identifying these operators. Explicit code examples exhibit logical failure rates substantially below the physical error rate. We further develop two fermionic lattice surgery protocols to enable state transfer between the memory and processors. Finally, we demonstrate effective error suppression in a simulation of fermionic dynamics using the proposed protocol.

authors.name: Chong-Yuan Xu, Ze-Chuan Liu, Yong Xu

papers.title: Construction of Kochen-Specker Sets from Mutually Unbiased Bases
papers.summary: We give a constructive analysis of Kochen-Specker (KS) contextuality at the level of complete orthogonal bases (contexts). In dimension three, three noncomputational mutually unbiased bases generate a union of 165 rays and 130 contexts. Exact provenance accounting gives a symmetric decomposition: the three 69-ray lineages share 21 rays and 10 contexts, while each contributes 48 exclusive rays and 40 lineage-specific contexts. Each 69-ray, 50-context lineage is a KS configuration; as a hypergraph it is the 69-50 KS set reported earlier by Pavicic and Megill. This framework clarifies the relation among the Yu-Oh, Harding-Salinas Schmeis, Pavicic-Megill, and Cabello constructions. In dimensions four and five, we give parametrized orthogonality gadgets whose connector contexts force a central ray to be maximally unbiased relative to the computational basis. For the concrete four-dimensional example, the 20-ray gadget and the Cabello 18-ray set are informationally equivalent subsets of the 24-ray Peres-Mermin eigensystem, although their context hypergraphs have different two-valued-state behavior. The results show why both the rays and the complete incidence structure of their contexts are needed in assessments of KS contextuality.

authors.name: Mirko Navara, Karl Svozil

papers.title: A Rigorous Quantum Framework for Inequality-Constrained and Multi-Objective Binary Optimization: Quadratic Cost Functions and Empirical Evaluations
papers.summary: The prospect of quantum solutions for complicated optimization problems is contingent on mapping the original problem onto a tractable quantum energy landscape, e.g. an Ising-type Hamiltonian. Subsequently, techniques like adiabatic optimization, quantum annealing, and the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can be used to find the ground state of this Hamiltonian. Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) is one prominent problem class for which this entire pipeline is well understood and has received considerable attention over the past years. In this work, we provide novel, tractable mappings for the maxima of multiple QUBO problems. Termed Multi-Objective Quantum Approximations, or MOQA for short, our framework allows us to recast new types of classical binary optimization problems as ground state problems of a tractable Ising-type Hamiltonian. This, in turn, opens the possibility of new quantum- and quantum-inspired solutions to a variety of problems that frequently occur in practical applications. In particular, MOQA can handle various types of routing and partitioning problems, as well as inequality-constrained binary optimization problems.

authors.name: Sebastian Egginger, Kristina Kirova, Sonja Bruckner, Stefan Hillmich, Richard Kueng

papers.title: Secure PAC Learning: Sample-Budget Laws and Quantum Data-Path Admissibility
papers.summary: Security in machine learning is fragile when data are exfiltrated or perturbed, yet existing frameworks rarely connect data-path security to learnability. In this work, we develop an operational theory of secure learning grounded in the probably-approximately-correct (PAC) viewpoint. An explicit stopping time combines the event that a trained hypothesis attains a target accuracy with the event that a run-based validation gate halts within a finite sample budget. We derive a closed-form sufficient budget requirement for this joint PAC-within-budget guarantee under an admissible random-classification-noise channel. We then specialize the construction to a BB84-like quantum label path. Under the stated ideal single-qubit, authenticated-classical-channel, memoryless, basis-symmetric, collective-attack, asymptotic, and one-way-reconciliation assumptions, the standard Holevo bound gives the protocol-specific information-advantage criterion $1-2h(\eta) > 0$, with the threshold $\eta_{\mathrm{BB84}} \simeq 0.11$. The quantum layer is not invoked to reduce distribution-free PAC sample complexity; rather, it turns a designer-chosen classical noise tolerance into a physically testable, protocol-dependent security condition by linking information acquisition to observable disturbance. Below the threshold, the PAC and information-advantage conditions provide complementary statistical and physical guarantees; at or above it, the present protocol and proof no longer certify the latter. Basis sifting is incorporated explicitly in the conversion from sifted-sample budgets to expected raw channel uses.

authors.name: Jeongho Bang

papers.title: Addressable gate-based logical computation with quantum LDPC codes
papers.summary: Quantum computing relies on quantum error correction for high-fidelity logical operations, but scaling to achieve near-term quantum utility is highly resource-intensive. High-rate quantum LDPC codes can reduce error correction overhead, yet realizing high-rate fault-tolerant computation with these codes remains a central challenge. Lattice surgery remains the main approach for addressable logical computation but at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d)$ time overhead. Other approaches rely on low-rate code switching methods or high space overhead homomorphic CNOT. In this work, we introduce a gate-based protocol for addressable single- and multi-qubit Clifford operations on individual logical qubits encoded within one or more quantum LDPC codes. Our scheme leverages logical transversal operations via an auxiliary -- a Bacon-Shor code or an unrotated surface code -- to perform logical operations with constant time overhead enabled by teleportation. We demonstrate the implementation of an overcomplete logical Clifford gate set and perform numerical simulations to evaluate the error-correction performance of our protocol. Additionally, our scheme can also realize any joint Pauli product measurement natively. Finally, we observe that our scheme can be integrated with magic state cultivation protocols to achieve universal, gate-based, and fully addressable quantum computation.

authors.name: Laura Pecorari, Francesco Paolo Guerci, Hugo Perrin, Guido Pupillo

papers.title: Local causal consistency as a foundational principle for indefinite causal order
papers.summary: Quantum processes with indefinite causal order challenge the description of physical experiments as globally ordered networks while retaining causality within each local laboratory. Whether and how this local causal requirement constrains the information flow in such quantum processes remains unclear. Here we formalize the principle of local causal consistency through experiments in which each laboratory performs two sequential operations and may use the earlier outcome to choose the later operation. The principle is equivalent to a set of parity-erasure conditions: the joint earlier outcomes for any set of laboratories reveal no information about the parity of the corresponding independent, uniformly random binary settings. We show that these conditions precisely characterize, via local process tomography, the multipartite channels representing valid quantum processes; characterize classical process-matrix correlations through local readout of outcome tables; and, together with the gentle-measurement property, constrain general quantum correlations with indefinite causal order. Moreover, these results extend naturally to a vast class of theories beyond quantum theory. Our findings provide an operational account of how causality within local laboratories shapes indefinite causal structure and the correlations it supports, revealing a fundamental constraint on information exchange through indefinite causal structure.

authors.name: Zixuan Liu, Ognyan Oreshkov

papers.title: Spin-1 quantum annealing with anisotropy-controlled intermediate-state pathways
papers.summary: Quantum annealing offers a promising strategy for solving complex optimization problems by encoding the solution into the ground state of a problem Hamiltonian. While most implementations rely on spin-$1/2$ systems, we explore the performance of quantum annealing on a spin-$1$ system where the problem Hamiltonian includes a single ion anisotropy term of the form $D\sum (S^z)^2$. Our results reveal that for a suitable range of the anisotropy strength $D$, the spin-$1$ annealer reaches the ground state with higher fidelity. We attribute this performance to the presence of the intermediate spin level and the tunable anisotropy, which together enable the algorithm to traverse the energy landscape through smaller, incremental steps instead of a single large spin flip. This mechanism effectively lowers barriers in the configuration space and stabilizes the evolution.
