These findings suggest that higher spin annealers offer intrinsic advantages for robust and flexible quantum optimization, especially for problems naturally formulated with ternary decision variables.

authors.name: M. Haider Akbar, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

papers.title: Chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing via flux-mediated transmon mechanical coupling: Theory and device requirements
papers.summary: Measurements of local gravitational acceleration support geophysics and inertial navigation. We develop a circuit-level model of a chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing head that longitudinally couples a nanomechanical beam in a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) loop to an independently flux-biased transmon. The interaction encodes changes in gravitational acceleration in the qubit Ramsey phase. We derive the phase response and evaluate the quantum Fisher information of the reduced qubit state and the classical Fisher information accessible through Ramsey readout. The model includes qubit relaxation and dephasing, mechanical damping, flux noise, readout infidelity, and cycle overhead. With other model inputs fixed, the competition between phase gain and responsivity-dependent decoherence yields a finite optimal transmon frequency responsivity to mechanical-loop flux. The decoherence model includes dephasing from low-frequency flux noise in the mechanical SQUID loop and coupling-dependent qubit dephasing from the mechanical bath. For the prospective integrated-device parameter set, Ramsey readout at the first mechanical revival gives a conditional projection of the sensing head's sensitivity of $1.1\times10^{-5}$ m s$^{-2}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ at an interrogation time of 10.0 $\mu$s. This estimate uses the single-cycle-equivalent Fisher-information rate for statistically independent cycles. A separate analysis identifies the joint mechanical, circuit, flux-noise, coherence, timing, and readout parameters needed within the model to reach $10^{-6}$-class internal sensitivity. These results specify the design tradeoffs and component requirements for Ramsey gravimetry in the proposed SQUID-transmon electromechanical sensing head.

authors.name: Salman Sajad Wani, Mughees Ahmed Khan, Abrar Ahmed Naqash, Saif Al-Kuwari

papers.title: TopoLS: Lattice Surgery Compilation via Topological Program Transformations
papers.summary: Lattice surgery is a leading approach for implementing fault-tolerant logical operations in surface code quantum computing. Current compilers largely treat lattice surgery as a layout problem downstream of a gate-level circuit; this circuit-centric view hinders a substantial optimization opportunity: lattice surgery computations are topological programs whose semantics are determined by connectivity, so different concrete space-time realizations may implement the same computation while offering different space-time volumes. Circuit-centric compilers, however, commit to fixed realizations throughout the program. We tackle this problem by presenting TopoLS, a topology-centric compiler that uses ZX diagrams as the intermediate representation (IR) for automated lattice surgery compilation. Compiler transformations on this graph preserve its semantics, and the backend must produce a valid pipe diagram, i.e., a 3D space-time layout of the lattice surgery program, with the same semantics. TopoLS first simplifies the graph and slices it into layers, and then uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to place the graph's nodes as cubes in a 3D grid and to route its edges as pipes. To scale to large circuits, TopoLS partitions the graph so that each search step routes a bounded number of connections. Across evaluated benchmarks, TopoLS reduces space-time volume by 46% on average over prior circuit-centric compilers, with improvements ranging from 25% to 90%, while exhibiting strong empirical scalability on large benchmark families.

authors.name: Junyu Zhou, Yuhao Liu, Ethan Decker, Justin Kalloor, Mathias Weiden, Kean Chen, Costin Iancu, Gushu Li

papers.title: Gradually opening Schr\"odinger's box reveals a cascade of sharp dynamical transitions
papers.summary: Quantum mechanics predicts that unobserved systems may exist in a superposition of states, yet measurement produces definite outcomes, a tension at the heart of the quantum-to-classical boundary. How the transformation between these opposing regimes unfolds as observation strength increases has remained experimentally elusive. Here, by continuously tuning the measurement strength on a superconducting qubit, we reveal that measurement-dominated dynamics emerge not gradually but through multiple sharp transitions marked by the halting of coherent oscillations, state freezing near an attracting state, and the onset of quantum Zeno dynamics. Decoherence, rather than washing out this structure, reshapes it, reordering the transitions and decoupling signatures that coincide in idealised models. These results establish that the passage from quantum dynamics to measurement-dominated behaviour unfolds through a sequence of distinct transitions governed by the interplay between observation and environment.

authors.name: Barkay Guttel, Danielle Gov, Noam Netzer, Uri Goldblatt, Sergey Hazanov, Lalit M. Joshi, Alessandro Romito, Yuval Gefen, Parveen Kumar, Kyrylo Snizhko, Fabien Lafont, Serge Rosenblum

papers.title: Intractability of Witnessing an Entangled Measurement Device Independently
papers.summary: Protocols have been previously proposed to certify that a measurement is entangled in a fully device-independent manner. Here, I provide models for these protocols in which the claimed measurement is not entangled, and demonstrate it is always possible to displace entanglement from a given measurement to the measured state for a general class of device-independent scenarios. This indicates that no black-box measurement scenario requires a specific chosen measurement to be entangled in order to replicate its behavior, which is relevant to our fundamental understanding of this phenomenon and how to witness it.

authors.name: Peter Bierhorst

papers.title: Landscape-Similarity-Guided Optimization in Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
papers.summary: Divide-and-conquer strategies mitigate hardware constraints for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices by partitioning large interaction graphs into smaller, hardware-compatible sub-problems. However, this approach introduces a severe classical training bottleneck: a decomposition across $m$ boundary nodes generates $2^m$ distinct sub-problems that typically require independent optimization. In this work, we quantify correlations between reduced QAOA energy landscapes using a landscape-overlap measure $q$ and Pearson correlation $r$, and investigate their usefulness for parameter transfer. For $p=1$ on the studied long-range percolation graphs with $L=50$--$400$, the displayed $q(s)$ curves cross near $s\approx0.6$. This observation on finite systems does not establish a thermodynamic phase transition. Exploiting these correlations, we introduce Doubly Optimized QAOA (DO-QAOA), which fully optimizes one representative reduced instance and transfers its parameters to the remaining frozen assignments, with target-specific refinement when required. We evaluated DO-QAOA on more than 6,000 circuits under the realistic noise model, DO-QAOA uses approximately $285$--$386\times$ fewer quantum shots and has approximately $6.5$--$23.9\times$ shorter runtime than FrozenQubits, with equal or lower dataset-averaged Approximation Ratio Gap (ARG).

authors.name: Sokea Sang, Leanghok Hour, Sanghyeon Lee, Aniket Patra, Hee Chul Park, Moon Jip Park, Youngsun Han

papers.title: Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution with Majorana Memories
papers.summary: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) certifies secrecy from Bell nonlocality and has been demonstrated with ions, atoms, and photons. Majorana parity qubits are proposed as network memories, but their operations and noise have not been connected to device-independent security. We show that Clifford-only Majorana operations cannot violate the CHSH inequality on a heralded pair, so a node needs a non-Clifford resource, which we confine to one party's test rounds. Because quasiparticle poisoning flips the total island parity, a parity flag read before the inputs are drawn preserves device independence and turns the poisoning distance cutoff into a rate penalty; flag errors restore part of the loss in proportion to the miss probability. We derive closed-form Bell statistics for realistic heralding and anisotropic Majorana noise, instantiate a block-based finite-size key length, and find that 2025 tetron prototypes cannot yet certify a key. We identify the hardware milestones that would.

authors.name: Noureldin Mohamed, Saif Al-Kuwari

papers.title: Uncertainty Relations and Quantum Speed Limits for Lattice-Regularized Fractional Kinetic Operators
papers.summary: We study a ``hybrid'' kinetic operator on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ that combines a lattice-regularized momentum, with lattice constant $a$, and a fractional (L\'evy-type) power $\alpha\in(1,2]$. It is a bounded Fourier multiplier whose symbol is a fractional power of the central-difference Laplacian symbol; equivalently, it is a long-range hopping model with algebraically decaying hops. We prove that the kinetic operator is bounded and self-adjoint with purely absolutely continuous spectrum $[0,E_{\max}]$ (for every $\alpha\in(0,2]$), and that $\hat K+V$ is self-adjoint on $\mathcal D(V)$. The main new technical result is an exact position--momentum commutator with domain control for the singular multiplier it produces when $\alpha\in(1,2)$, and the resulting Robertson-type uncertainty relation together with its joint weak-lattice, weak-fractionality expansion. For $\alpha=2$ the uncertainty relation reduces to a known lattice result, which we attribute. For quantum speed limits we recall the bandwidth bound $\tau_\perp\ge\pi\hbar/E_{\max}$, a direct consequence of the Mandelstam--Tamm bound, and evaluate the Mandelstam--Tamm and Margolus--Levitin bounds for Gaussian states in closed form, including their crossover as a function of $\alpha$. To leading order the lattice reduces the energy variance of a Gaussian state and therefore raises the Mandelstam--Tamm bound; the effect of the fractional order is controlled by the width of the state relative to a reference momentum $p_0$ through an explicit crossover width $\sigma_*$. For $\hat H=\hat K-F\hat x$ we show that $\ave{\hx}(t)$ is exactly periodic for every state, and discuss ion-chain realizations.

authors.name: M. W. AlMasri

papers.title: Semiclassical Ehrenfest paths in open quantum systems
papers.summary: We study the semiclassical Ehrenfest trajectories in open quantum systems. Using the Fokker--Planck equation for the Gaussian mixing measure, we embed the generalized Ehrenfest theorem recently obtained for open quantum systems into this phase-space picture and study the time evolution of the expectations of observables with respect to the Gaussian mixture. We show how the coherent and irreversible contributions are separated in the frictionless harmonic regime relevant to the semiclassical approximation. Our work provides a transparent phase-space interpretation of the emergence of classical trajectories in open quantum dynamics.

authors.name: Xiao-Kan Guo

papers.title: Temporal State Tomography via Quantum Snapshotting the Temporal Quasiprobabilities
papers.summary: Quantum tomography is a cornerstone of quantum information science, enabling the reconstruction of states and channels from experimental data. Here we introduce a new paradigm, temporal state tomography (TST), for reconstructing quantum processes across multiple times. Our approach is based on temporal quasiprobability distributions (TQDs), which, in the informationally complete setting, provide a complete description of multi-time quantum processes and uniquely determine temporal states. We formulate TST as a unified framework for reconstructing both density operators and quantum channels within a single scheme. We show that any TQD can be obtained via classical post-processing of measurement outcomes generated by a fixed set of quantum instruments, thereby establishing a direct operational route to accessing TQDs experimentally. For informationally complete TQDs, the associated temporal state can be reconstructed via a temporal Bloch-type representation. Leveraging this correspondence, we derive the sample complexity of TST, thereby quantifying its statistical efficiency.

authors.name: Zhian Jia

papers.title: Molecular Attoscope: Pulse Shape Spectroscopy of Electronic Coherence
papers.summary: Tracking the coupled motion of electrons and nuclei on their intrinsic timescales is essential to understanding and controlling photochemical transformations. While attosecond techniques have provided unprecedented insight into electronic dynamics, they have largely been restricted to ionic systems, with nuclear motion often neglected or indirectly inferred. Here, we demonstrate a ``molecular attoscope", which uses shaped laser pulses in the deep ultraviolet to perform a coherent measurement of electronic and nuclear dynamics in an entangled wave packet in neutral benzene. This enables us to trace both the 856-attosecond-period electronic motion and the 36-femtosecond-period nuclear motion. We observe electronic coherence persisting over hundreds of optical cycles, modulated by nuclear dynamics. Our holographic approach is general, and lays the groundwork for coherent measurements capable of visualizing the evolution of the coupled electronic-nuclear wave function in real time.

authors.name: Loc Thi-Hoang Ngo, Julia Codere, Javin Ohara, Brian Kaufman, Martin G Cohen, Scott Liguori, Varun Makhija, Tamas Rozgonyi, Philipp Marquetand, Matthew Bain, Brett J Pearson, Ruaridh Forbes, Thomas Weinacht

papers.title: An extensive theory of nonlinearly intercoupled pseudomodes for noise model reduction in circuit QED
papers.summary: Superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamical (cQED) platforms present a persistent modeling challenge: the intrinsic nonlinearity of the Josephson potential couples to a dissipative electromagnetic environment in ways that resist both perturbative treatment and naive Markovian reduction. Standard approaches either scale poorly with system size or absorb undeclared approximations about the noise structure into their master equations. In this work, we generalize Garraway's pseudomode construction to accommodate nonlinearly intercoupled auxiliary modes, providing a nonperturbative and systematically reducible framework for open-system cQED dynamics. The key observation is that pseudomode elimination is not fundamentally tied to linearity but to representability: any eliminated sector whose influence on the retained subsystem admits a rational self-energy can be replaced by a finite set of damped auxiliary modes, independent of the internal nonlinear structure of the retained Hamiltonian. We develop the general theory in the Heisenberg picture via a Dyson equation for the retained-mode Green's function, then demonstrate closed-form elimination for two-, three-, and four-mode Kerr-coupled systems with bilinear exchange and three-wave mixing interactions. The resulting framework substantially reduces the computational overhead of open-system cQED modeling while remaining faithful to the underlying physics, provided the spectral description of the eliminated sector is chosen to match the experimentally measured response functions of the hardware.

authors.name: M. Gabriela Boada G., Nicolas Dirnegger, Andrea Delgado, Prineha Narang

papers.title: C-Phase-Aware Compilation for Efficient Fault-Tolerant Quantum Execution
papers.summary: Achieving practical quantum advantage on fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQC) is fundamentally constrained by significant spatial and temporal overheads required to execute logical operations on physical hardware. Existing compilers fail to exploit the connection between algorithmic structure and fault-tolerant execution primitives, leaving substantial optimization opportunities unrealized. Additionally, they often rely on coarse-grained, slice-based abstractions that ignore microarchitectural overheads, leading to poor resource utilization. We present a microarchitecture-aware compilation approach that integrates algorithmic structure directly with lattice surgery (LS) execution. By leveraging the commutativity of C-Phase operations, the method transforms inherently sequential gate sequences into concurrent multi-target interactions, effectively removing artificial dependencies and exposing significant instruction-level parallelism. To enable this, we design a dynamic, event-driven scheduling strategy that accurately models spatial layout and routing constraints, allowing operations to overlap in time while minimizing contention. Compared to the state-of-the-art compiler, our work achieves up to 24.5$\times$~(geomean~3.7$\times$) reduction in execution time, up to 20.8$\times$~(geomean 2.9$\times$) reduction in space-time volume, and up to 2.7$\times$~(geomean 2.4$\times$) reduction in program-failure probability across three regimes of magic-state production. By co-optimizing the circuit reordering and LS primitives, we make executing fault-tolerant programs faster, cheaper, and more reliable on the same hardware.

authors.name: Dhanvi Bharadwaj, Siddharth Dangwal, Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

papers.title: Worst-Case Sample Complexity Bounds for Distributed Inner Product Estimation with Local Randomized Measurements
papers.summary: We study distributed inner product estimation for $n$-qubit states using local randomized measurements, for which rigorous worst-case guarantees are less understood. We first reduce the minimax kernel optimization to Hamming-distance kernels. Within this class, unbiasedness fixes a unique kernel. For this kernel under local Clifford sampling, we prove a fourth-moment bound for arbitrary inputs. This yields a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{5.25^n})$ copies per party at fixed additive error and failure probability. For the same kernel under local Haar sampling, we prove a local twirling identity that compares its fourth moment with the Clifford fourth moment. A direct bound on the Haar fourth moment shows that $\mathcal(\sqrt{4^n})$ copies per party suffice. We also show that independent single-qubit Pauli shadows have a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{7.5^n})$ for large $n$.

authors.name: Zhenyuan Huang, Kun Wang, Ping Xu

papers.title: GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery for Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes
papers.summary: Efficiently realizing logical operations on general stabilizer codes remains a long-standing challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing. While code surgery provides a general framework with provable guarantees through joint logical measurements, existing constructions are largely theoretical and incur substantial ancilla overhead in practice. We present GeneCS, a resource-efficient synthesizer of code surgery protocols for arbitrary stabilizer codes, designed for the backend of fault-tolerant quantum compilers. Our approach leverages structure-aware optimizations to eliminate redundancy in graph construction, dynamically balance expansion and congestion, and incorporate code degree constraints. Experimental results show that GeneCS reduces ancillary qubits and checks by over 85\% on average for both single-code and cross-code logical operations, while the optimized constructions exhibit logical-error-rate behavior comparable to the baseline under BP-OSD (belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding). On surface-code stress tests with more than $10^4$ physical qubits, one independent synthesis run takes about one second on average. These results enable practical logical operations and efficient cross-code communication for modern QLDPC (quantum low-density parity-check) codes and heterogeneous code systems.

authors.name: Junyu Zhou, Ali Javadi-Abhari, Gushu Li

papers.title: Optimal work extraction in measurement-based quantum Otto engines: Non-adiabaticity and generalized measurements can be beneficial
papers.summary: Measurement-based quantum heat engines have attracted significant interest as alternatives to conventional thermal engines, as they replace the hot thermal reservoir with quantum measurements, thereby offering greater controllability and simpler implementation. Motivated by these advantages, we investigate a measurement-driven quantum Otto engine with a qubit working substance and study the optimal work extractable from such engines along with the corresponding efficiency, including whether their performance can surpass that of conventional quantum Otto cycles. We analyze the engine in both the infinite-time (adiabatic) and finite-time (non-adiabatic) regimes, considering two distinct implementations obtained through optimization over all projection-valued measurements (PVMs) and over all two-outcome positive operator-valued measurements (POVMs). We show that measurement-based engines can outperform conventional quantum Otto engines within specific parameter regimes and that POVM-based engines can yield higher optimal work extraction than PVM-based ones. Furthermore, by incorporating the thermodynamic cost associated with resetting the auxiliary system required for POVM implementation, we demonstrate that the resulting net work output can still exceed that of PVM-based engines under suitable conditions on the spectral gaps and cold bath temperature. We also identify regimes in which non-adiabatic implementations can yield higher work output and efficiency than their adiabatic counterparts. Our study provides operational guidelines for designing improved measurement-driven quantum Otto engines.

authors.name: Arunabha Das, Sayan Mondal, Debarupa Saha, Ujjwal Sen

papers.title: Two Operational Principles Single Out Quantum Theory
papers.summary: Within a finite-dimensional causal operational-probabilistic theory (OPT), we show that adding just two postulates, local equivalence and purification, suffices to derive the mathematical structure of quantum theory as a whole, without separately assuming quantum rules for states, measurements, composites, or transformations. This resolves the question raised by Chiribella, D'Ariano, and Perinotti (CDP) [Phys. Rev. A 81, 062348 (2010)]. The key step is to establish homogeneity of state cones by combining infinitesimal cone-preserving deformations obtained from these postulates with geometric optimization. CDP purification requires every normalized state to be purifiable and purifications of the same state on any common ancilla to be related by a reversible channel on that ancilla. Our alternative assigns each system one operationally equivalent ancilla that purifies all its normalized states, requiring such reversible equivalence only there. Together with local equivalence, this condition also yields quantum theory.

authors.name: Kenji Nakahira

papers.title: Soft information from neural-network logits and correlation-aware matching gaps
papers.summary: To utilize quantum error-correcting codes, a decoder must infer the logical sector from the measured syndrome. Beyond producing a hard logical decision, some decoders provide soft information that estimates the reliability of that decision. For minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM), a common confidence measure is the complementary gap. Neural-network decoders trained with binary cross entropy naturally output a different confidence score, the logit, whose usefulness for post-selection has already been demonstrated. Here, we compare the logit of a pretrained graph neural-network (GNN) decoder with the complementary gaps of uncorrelated and correlation-aware MWPM, evaluated on identical syndromes from rotated-surface-code memory experiments under circuit-level noise. Incorporating correlations substantially improves matching-based hard decisions, post-selection performance, and calibration, reversing the GNN's advantage at larger code distances while leaving it superior at smaller distance. Exchanging confidence scores shows that their ability to rank logical failures is decoder-relative. An exact-posterior comparison at small distance, together with larger-distance log-loss measurements, further shows that neither score universally provides the closer approximation to posterior soft information. These results reveal that much of the apparent advantage of learned confidence over the standard matching gap arises from correlations omitted by the matching model. Nevertheless, learned logits provide useful soft information without requiring an explicit detector error model or competing-sector matching calculations at inference, offering an alternative where matching-based confidence is costly or unavailable.

authors.name: David Dentelski

papers.title: A Dynamical Spacetime Hypothesis for Quantum Entanglement with a Proposed Experimental Test
papers.summary: Quantum entanglement is a central resource of quantum information science, yet its correlations are ordinarily treated as properties of the quantum state rather than as the outcome of an underlying physical process. Here we explore the hypothesis that these correlations are mediated dynamically by a field propagating locally at finite velocity through an extension of ordinary spacetime, extending the kinematic proposal of Physical Review Research 7, 013261 (2025) to a constrained bulk-field dynamics. Motivated by the constraints imposed by no-signaling on finite-speed hidden-influence models, we consider a warped five-dimensional spacetime with an additional timelike coordinate. We show that the five-dimensional Einstein equations determine the warp factor within a symmetric ansatz, requiring a positive bulk cosmological constant. We show that null trajectories propagating through the additional timelike dimension can project onto arbitrarily large spatial distances at the same ordinary time, although these trajectories do not themselves connect separated points on the brane. Spectral analysis of a minimally coupled bulk scalar reveals a tachyonic four-dimensional continuum. We isolate a normalizable zero-mode sector with stable, retarded effective dynamics in ordinary brane time and obtain an exact solution for a suitably distributed source. Building on these results, we formulate an equal-time contextual coupling and Bohm-Bub-inspired outcome dynamics as additional hypotheses, subject to Born-rule compatibility and multipartite no-signaling. We propose an experiment involving two independently prepared Bell pairs to test for departures from their expected statistical independence. Under specified assumptions on the field covariance and detector response, we derive a conditional inverse-square decay of correlations between the two pairs joint measurement outcomes at large separations.

authors.name: Marco Pettini

papers.title: Quantum Otto engine powered by an anisotropic Heisenberg XYZ model under independent local magnetic fields
papers.summary: We study a quantum Otto heat engine whose working substance is an anisotropic two-qubit Heisenberg XYZ model. Independent local magnetic fields are used to control each spin individually. The influence of the longitudinal coupling, anisotropy, transverse coupling, and local fields on the net work output and efficiency is systematically examined. Reducing the longitudinal coupling is found to markedly improve both the maximum work and the peak efficiency. The engine performance reaches an optimum at a particular value of the anisotropy parameter. A local work analysis clarifies how work is produced during the cycle. Because of the asymmetric local fields and the intrinsic spin-spin interaction, the two qubits play markedly different thermodynamic roles; the interaction term itself contributes crucially to the total work. We further analyze the variation of quantum entanglement, quantified by concurrence, along the cycle. The results indicate that a pronounced change in entanglement between the hot and cold isomagnetic strokes is closely correlated with the efficiency enhancement. This work offers new insight into the operating principles and control of quantum Otto heat engines.

authors.name: Meiru Li, Maimaitiyiming Tusun, Fang Zhao, Hasiyatihan Abudoula, Tongcheng Wei

papers.title: Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Mutually Unbiased Operator Frames
papers.summary: We develop an operator-frame formulation of entropic uncertainty relations in the Hilbert-Schmidt space of operators. For general continuous indexed operator frames, we derive an entropic uncertainty relation for the associated coefficient distributions by combining endpoint norm estimates with Riesz-Thorin interpolation. We then identify a distinguished class of mutually unbiased operator frames, defined through constant-modulus trace overlaps. Under suitable structural conditions, the corresponding coefficient amplitudes are related by a bilinear Fourier transform, leading to a stronger Hirschman-Beckner-type entropic uncertainty relation. As canonical realizations, we consider Weyl displacement operators and Wigner kernels, as well as Cartesian dyadic frames generated by position and momentum eigenstates. These examples recover familiar continuous-variable Fourier dualities while extending entropic uncertainty relations beyond measurement outcomes to operator representations themselves.

authors.name: Jesni Shamsul Shaari, Stefano Mancini

papers.title: Electrical-Circuit Simulation of the Uhlmann Phase
papers.summary: The Uhlmann phase extends the concept of geometric phases to mixed quantum states through a parallel-transport condition on purification amplitudes, but its experimental realization has so far required sophisticated quantum platforms with carefully engineered auxiliary degrees of freedom. In this work, we reformulate the Uhlmann parallel-transport condition as a linear matrix differential equation and vectorize it to obtain an effective dynamical generator. This generator can be directly mapped onto the admittance matrix of a classical RC circuit, thereby translating the Uhlmann dynamics into the evolution of circuit node voltages. We illustrate the mapping using the equatorial-loop model and, via a rotating-frame transformation followed by a real decomposition, derive a time-independent, real-valued dynamical system suitable for analog implementation. LTspice simulations of the resulting active RC network faithfully reproduce the Uhlmann geometric phase and its topological transition at the critical purity, demonstrating that classical electrical circuits offer a simple and accessible platform for probing mixed-state geometric phases.

authors.name: Yu-Huan Huang, Yu Wang, Jia-Chen Tang, Xu-Yang Hou, Hao Guo

papers.title: Unbiased Estimation of Conditional Covariance for Quantum Optomechanics
papers.summary: Continuous measurements can prepare macroscopic mechanical oscillators in conditional quantum states, but their covariance is difficult to verify. For each quadrature, the conventional retrodictive estimator is unbiased exactly when the conditional and future-likelihood variances are equal, and it needs a separate rule for the position-momentum cross covariance. Here, we derive an estimator that recovers all three independent covariance entries using one exact identity for linear-Gaussian models. It combines the forward trajectory, a future-likelihood center, and the smoothed trajectory. Using these three trajectories, we reconstruct the covariance of the center-of-mass motion of a 7.71-mg suspended mirror. This covariance describes a thermally squeezed conditional state with a principal-variance ratio of $4.7\pm0.7$. The reconstructed covariance and the measured bias difference between the conventional and three-trajectory estimators agree with the model predictions within propagated uncertainties. Varying the upper band edge resolves changes in all three covariance entries. For upper edges up to 1 kHz, the measured changes agree with the finite-band predictions. Every experimental record covers only a finite frequency band; these results show how such records can be used to characterize conditional mechanical states and provide a basis for future tests of macroscopic entanglement.

authors.name: Katsuta Sakai, Nobuyuki Matsumoto

papers.title: Approximate Virtual Quantum Recovery
papers.summary: The recovery of quantum information after subsystem loss is a central challenge in quantum information processing. However, some quantum states remain beyond the reach of any recovery strategies. Here we identify the algebraic origin of virtual irrecoverability, the \emph{ghost information}---correlations present in the global state that leave no trace on any accessible subsystem. We introduce a scalar measure to quantify its magnitude and prove a universal error floor below which no virtual recovery map can operate, irrespective of resource investment. In such cases only \emph{approximate} virtual recovery is available. We derive upper and lower bounds on the sampling overhead for approximate virtual recovery. Moreover, we show that conditional mutual information, the standard entropic diagnostic, does not determine the sampling overhead. Our work thus establish an algebraic framework of information recovery beyond entropic criteria.

authors.name: Yuan Liu, Linhan Lin, Ke-Mi Xu

papers.title: Quantum States over Spacetime Can Hide Setting-Dependent Dynamics
papers.summary: Determining whether correlations across quantum events arise from one physical process is essential for interpreting quantum states over spacetime (QSOSTs). Yet separately realizable settings can share the same unconditional QSOST without admitting a common process, because compression hides distinctions between underlying dynamics. Using least positive lifts, we derive an exact joint-domination criterion for conditioned data to admit a common deterministic parent. A reset-dephasing example and a sparse interferometric witness make this obstruction testable under trusted readout assumptions. We further establish a minimum-five-reference theorem: for two laboratories with qubit inputs and outputs, any four fixed local product-unitary reference groups cannot universally identify deterministic processes from exact joint data, whereas a specified set of five suffices. These results establish when reconstructed temporal correlations support interpretation as alternative readouts of one stable quantum process, making preparation-readout separation a testable physical property.

authors.name: Jianqi Sheng

papers.title: Later Information Can Outperform Earlier Information in Query-Assisted Quantum State Discrimination
papers.summary: Classical partial information about the states can increase the success probability in quantum state discrimination. An important aspect is its timing, whether it is given before or after the measurement. One might expect that later information is less useful than earlier information, because earlier information can still be stored and exploited at a later stage. Surprisingly, we show that the classical information can be more useful if it arrives after the measurement. We present a framework for state discrimination in which the sender provides classical information in response to a request from the receiver, which we refer to as a query. In some cases, nonorthogonal states can be perfectly discriminated when the query is allowed to depend on the measurement outcome. We give a general method for finding the optimal strategy in this setting, which turns out to be the standard minimum-error discrimination problem for an auxiliary ensemble. We show that for any number of states greater than two, there exists a qubit ensemble exhibiting an advantage of later information.

authors.name: Hanwool Lee, Teiko Heinosaari

papers.title: Fidelity-Based Robustness Margins for Quantum Control
papers.summary: We develop certified lower bounds on structure-specific fidelity-threshold robustness margins for finite-dimensional closed quantum systems under piecewise-constant coherent control. A scalar physical parameter may perturb the drift, a control Hamiltonian, or another declared Hamiltonian component across the control horizon. A differential sensitivity bound for the trace-amplitude gate fidelity yields a threshold-dependent Lipschitz constant on the nominal connected safe parameter component and hence a certified finite perturbation radius. Recentering this certificate produces an iterative one-dimensional method whose finite runs return lower bounds on the distance to the first threshold contact. The fidelity may touch the threshold without falling below it. A three-qubit gate-control example shows that the returned bounds vary by up to a factor of three across controllers of comparable nominal fidelity and contain structure-dependent information not captured by nominal differential sensitivity alone.

authors.name: S. P. O'Neil, F. C. Langbein, C. A. Weidner, E. A. Jonckheere, S. Schirmer

papers.title: Spin-coherent quantum designs
papers.summary: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify finite sets that represent spin observables exactly. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases already exist. Here we address a more specific problem: preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. For a spin-$J$ system, the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-$S$ irreducible tensor sector exactly if and only if the sampling directions form a spherical $(2J+S)$-design and the corresponding coherent-state projectors then form a spin-coherent quantum design. We also give an explicit Gauss-Legendre construction which leads to weighted spherical designs. These results provide a systematic way to determine spin-operator moments from finite coherent-state POVMs without full state tomography, with practical protocols for polarimetry and magnetometry. Presented construction can be extended to other compact symmetry groups.

authors.name: Marcin Rudzi\'nski, Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andrei B. Klimov, Luis L. S\'{a}nchez-Soto, Karol \.Zyczkowski

papers.title: Micromotion and topological constraints on Floquet-state quantum geometry
papers.summary: The quantum geometry of Floquet-Bloch states in periodically driven crystals evolves throughout each drive cycle. We show that Floquet topology and micromotion constrain this evolution. Using a projector formulation that separates stroboscopic and micromotion contributions, we bound the deviation of the integrated quantum metric of any Floquet-band subspace from its stroboscopic value and derive a geometric speed limit on its evolution. In chiral Floquet systems, these bounds extend the topological lower bounds set by the $0$- and $\pi$-gap invariants at two symmetry-selected times into finite intervals of the drive, a dynamical topological obstruction. When both invariants are nonzero, it can force a minimum intra-period change in the metric, driven by micromotion. Because the integrated metric is a periodic lower bound on the total spread of time-evolved Wannier functions, such a change can make this spread breathe. An exactly solvable driven spin chain realizes this obstruction and further hosts a flat-band point where each band's metric equals the breathing of its compact localized state. This equality provides a direct geometric characterization of local micromotion, accessible through local spin correlators.

authors.name: Arpit Raj, Johannes Mitscherling, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

papers.title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution Arbitrarily Close to Local Correlations
papers.summary: Recently, Wooltorton et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210802 (2024)] and Farkas [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210803 (2024)] have exhibited the mismatch between Bell inequality violations and their cryptographic application in device-independent quantum key distribution, by showing that arbitrarily close to the set of local behaviours there exist quantum correlations guaranteeing a constant rate of secret key. While these results require correlations attaining the maximum quantum value of a suitable Bell observable (aka the Tsirelson bound) and rely on a kind of ideal self-testing of a maximally entangled state and associated Bell measurement, here we show that the effect is robust: for every one of the Bell inequalities considered by Wooltorton \emph{et al.}, a constant rate of secret key ensues if the observed Bell violation is sufficiently close to the respective Tsirelson bound. For these and also the Bell inequalities of Farkas, we furthermore present numerical results based on semidefinite relaxations of the minimum min-entropy consistent with a certain Bell violation, which demonstrate that small but nonzero key rates can be guaranteed (in principle) by practical and efficient means.

authors.name: Hari Krishnan SV, Andreas Winter

papers.title: The inverse eigenvalue problem for Partial Transposes of Two-Qubit States and Sharp Entanglement Bounds from Their Low-order Moments
papers.summary: The negativity of a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho$ can be determined without full state tomography by measuring sufficiently many partial-transpose (PT) moments on multiple copies of $\rho$. When the available copies allow only low-order PT moments to be estimated reliably, how tightly do these moments bound the negativity? For two-qubit states, we answer this question by solving the inverse eigenvalue problem for their partial transposes: an ordered eigenvalue list $(x,y,z,-q)$, with $x\ge y\ge z\ge0$, $q>0$, and $x+y+z-q=1$, occurs as the spectrum of $\rho^{\Gamma_B}$ for some two-qubit state $\rho$ if and only if $q\le y$ and $qy\le xz$. The quantum steering ellipsoid of the $X$ state constructed to prove sufficiency gives a geometric interpretation of the two equality cases. We use these inequalities to determine the exact range of negativity compatible with the two lowest nontrivial PT moments, $p_2=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^2]$ and $p_3=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^3]$. We also compare our sharp negativity bounds with estimates from several existing methods and quantify how much the inverse eigenvalue constraints narrow the negativity interval as a function of $p_3$ at fixed $p_2$. Beyond negativity, we extend this approach to derive attainable bounds for the maximal CHSH value and directional coherent information at fixed $p_2$ and $p_3$. Our result establishes the strongest possible bounds on the negativity of an unknown two-qubit state from just two experimentally accessible PT moments, and shows the potential for obtaining similarly sharp bounds from low-order PT moments by solving the corresponding inverse eigenvalue problem for higher-dimensional bipartite states.

authors.name: Ruoting Dou, Shengjun Wu, Zeng-Bing Chen

papers.title: Coherence-generating power deviation: Fluctuations and input selectivity beyond average coherence generation
papers.summary: Coherence-generating power (CGP) tells how much coherence a quantum process produces on average from incoherent inputs, but an average can hide where that coherence comes from. We introduce the coherence-generating power deviation (CGPD), the standard deviation of the generated Hilbert--Schmidt coherence over the uniform simplex of incoherent states. CGPD turns coherence generation into a landscape: a small value signals robust production across input populations, whereas a large value reveals selective conversion of particular population imbalances. By representing unitary coherence generation as a quadratic response on population space, we obtain exact first and second moments in arbitrary finite dimension. We prove that every nontrivial unitary generator must fluctuate, and we separate this unavoidable isotropic fluctuation from excess anisotropy. The resulting distinction between average strength and input selectivity has direct consequences for benchmarking, reliability guarantees, input-ensemble susceptibility, and four-copy measurement protocols; it also extends naturally to unital quantum channels. Matched quantum-walk and quasiperiodic-transport examples show that topology and localization can leave CGP unchanged while substantially changing CGPD, revealing structure invisible to the mean alone.

authors.name: Kyoungho Cho, Jeongho Bang

papers.title: A Few Reveal Many: Constraint-Enhanced Learning of Many-Body Quantum Systems
papers.summary: Discovering properties of many-body quantum systems is challenging due to the large number of parameters involved. Here, we show that harnessing fundamental constraints among quantum observables improves quantum learning, enabling the inference of exponentially many quantities from a linear number of direct measurements. We leverage this result to design constraint-enhanced algorithms for evaluating key quantum features such as Entanglement and Magic in 100-qubit simulators. At a fixed number of measurement shots, they achieve up to an 83% reduction in relative error compared with protocols based on constructing "classical shadows" of quantum states. Quantum constraints themselves are therefore a resource for exploring large quantum systems, guiding the allocation of the measurement budget to highly informative observables.

authors.name: Matteo Tedde, Davide Girolami

papers.title: Measurement-induced dynamics and emergent symmetries of particles moving in a one-dimensional lattice
papers.summary: Continuous measurements simultaneously reveal and modify the dynamics of a quantum system. In this work we consider the tunneling motion of particles between the sites of a one-dimensional lattice. We investigate how weak continuous probing of the occupation of a single lattice site induces entanglement and selects definite values for system properties such as wave function parity and permutation symmetry. Our simulations show how continuous measurement can steer systems of two and three particles, with no prior permutation symmetry, into stable bosonic, fermionic and parastatistical symmetry sectors.

authors.name: Salvatore Di Lorenzo, Klaus M{\o}lmer

papers.title: Optimal Resource Scaling for Early Fault Tolerant Iterative Quantum Phase Estimation under Cost Error Tradeoffs
papers.summary: The iterative quantum phase estimation algorithm (IPEA) is better suited for NISQ and early fault-tolerant hardware compared to the original algorithm, which requires the inverse quantum Fourier transform. However, current error mitigation and correction implementations lead to imperfect unitaries, causing erroneous phase feedback in IPEA. To improve the reliability of phase bits is to repeat the k^th iteration for the 2^k-th power of the unitary $N_k^*$ times, followed by a majority decision. However, due to variations in their circuit complexities, different iterations incur varying resource costs ($w_k$) and different per-shot error probabilities ($q_k$). Given tight resource constraints, we ask what the optimal number $\{N_k^*: 1\le k \le L\}$ of shots per bit is: $$\arg \max_{\{N_k\}} \mathbb{P}(\text{all } L \text{ bits correct}) \text{s.t.} \sum_{k=1}^L w_k N_k \le W$$ We construct upper and lower surrogate objectives via concentration and anti-concentration inequalities and prove an asymptotic optimality guarantee for whenever the budget satisfies $W = \sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}(\ln L + \omega(1))$, where $c_k=-\ln\left(2\sqrt{\left(1-\frac{q_k}{2} \right) \frac{q_k}{2}}\right)$, which, for $q_k\ll 1$, is proportional to $\ln\frac{1}{q_k}$. Optimizing the tractable lower surrogate yields a true success probability within a $(1-o(1))$ factor of the exact optimum. We observe that when resources are abundant, $W \gg \ln(L)\sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}$, optimal allocations are proportional to $\ 1/c_k$. However, when resources are sufficient but not abundant, $(\ln(L)+\omega(1))\sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\le W \le O\left( \ln(L)\cdot \sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\right)$, an additional $-\frac{1}{c_k}\ln\frac{w_k}{c_k}$ correction accounts for error propagation from less-significant to more-significant bits.

authors.name: Mrudula A Mahindrakar, Avhishek Chatterjee

papers.title: Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory
papers.summary: A streaming algorithm can keep classical or quantum memory, and its input arrives in adversarial or random order. Each resource alone is known to beat the basic model exponentially, but it was not known whether random order can help a quantum algorithm. We compare the four models by exponential space separations: every pair is separated on some problem and tied on another, and the two models with one resource each beat each other on different problems, one direction for random inputs, by concurrent work of Bouland, Ding, and Jain. The new phenomenon is that quantum memory and random order together can be exponentially stronger than each alone. We show this on a streaming version of Hidden Matching in which the bits of $x\in\{0,1\}^N$ arrive many times and $m\le\sqrt{N}$ matching requests must be answered on arrival. In random order a quantum algorithm uses $O(\log N\log m)$ space, while classical algorithms need $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$, and quantum algorithms need $\Omega(m)$ when all data comes before the requests. Two properties explain this. Consumability: answering a request destroys the quantum state. Replenishment: the state can be rebuilt from bits that keep arriving, which random order supplies and a data-first order does not. We prove that one quantum message answering $m$ Hidden Matching requests needs $\Omega(m)$ qubits, a conjecture of Gilboa, Jain, and McClean, for $m\le N^{1/2-\delta}$. The rest comes from Noisy Gap Cycle, a problem of Assadi and Sundaresan: tell whether a graph is a union of cycles of length $k$ or $2k$. With long cycles it needs linear space in all four models: we extend their random-order lower bound to quantum algorithms and obtain the first quantum random-order lower bounds for natural graph problems. With short cycles, $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ classical bits suffice in random order, but adversarial order requires polynomial quantum space.

authors.name: Nadezhda Voronova

papers.title: Towards the Geometry of Quantum Optical Measurements: Kraus Trajectories in the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg Group Manifold
papers.summary: Since ancient Greek times, geometry has been a method by which humans can make inferences, by the use of similar triangles, about the world far beyond their immediate senses. Similarity plays an equally important role in quantum measurement, except that instead of between triangles on wax tablets and in the sky, the similarity is between the infinitesimal generators of transformation (i.e. rotation, affine canonical transformation) on the page and within the atom. For many quantum optical measurements of a single mode, these generators produce Kraus operators that are contained within a twelve-dimensional Lie group: the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg group manifold ($\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$). In particular, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is general enough to include all diffusively generated 'dyne measurements. In this paper, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ will be used to develop two more general classes of 'dyne measurement: one that interpolates between diffusive homodyne and diffusive heterodyne (``slomodyne'') and one that adds to 'dyne measurements adaptive squeezing and displacement. Our analysis uses an approach known as the Instrument Manifold Program (IMP). In particular, a Harish-Chandra-like decomposition of $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is used to calculate the vielbein transformation from a right-invariant basis to the corresponding coordinate basis, allowing us to universally and autonomously navigate $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ and locate the Kraus-operator of whatever selective process is being considered as it evolves in time according to the measurement record.

authors.name: Tzula B. Propp, Chris S. Jackson

papers.title: Quantum-classical algorithm interpolation for spatial search
papers.summary: Quantum-walk algorithms can quadratically reduce the dependence of spatial search on the classical hitting time $\mathrm{HT}$. Realising this speedup using standard quantum-walk algorithms, however, requires deep coherent circuits, limiting their applicability on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum devices. We derive a parameterised family of hybrid quantum-classical spatial search algorithms that continuously interpolates between the classical and fully coherent quantum regimes, trading off circuit depth for total query complexity. For any $\gamma\in[0,1]$, our algorithms use circuits of depth $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{\gamma/2})$ and find a marked vertex with constant success probability at total cost $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{1-\gamma}\mathsf{S} + \mathrm{HT}^{1-\gamma/2}(\mathsf{U} + \mathsf{C}))$, where $\mathsf{S}$, $\mathsf{U}$, and $\mathsf{C}$ denote the setup, update, and checking costs, respectively. We also derive an optimal continuous depth-query trade-off for fixed-point amplitude amplification, providing a potential building block for other hybrid designs.

authors.name: Diogo Ramos, Duarte Magano

papers.title: Local failure of disjoint additivity
papers.summary: Local Gauss constraints can prevent commuting regional algebras from generating the full algebra assigned to their union. We investigate disjoint additivity on the full magnetic physical subspace of finite-group quantum-double models while keeping the original lattice edge supports fixed. Every finite non-Abelian group exhibits a counterexample on vertex-disjoint regions contained within a contractible disk on a regular square torus. For a fixed eight-edge loop and a specified peripheral contact family, additivity fails if and only if the group is non-Abelian and the selected contacts cover all four interior faces of the loop. Leaving an inner face uncovered restores additivity; for the same loop, so does any second region avoiding the specified testing neighborhood. A peripheral projector restricts the exterior tests on a loop transition, allowing their product to preserve the constraints even when the loop factor does not. We construct union observables that deterministically separate orthogonal relative-sign superpositions that yield identical outcome statistics under every measurement whose effects lie in the generated regional algebra. For a separate wrapping pair, we also determine the complete matrix-block inclusion, identifying missing center-orbit coherences, and construct an independent regular-torus counterexample for the eight-dimensional Kac-Paljutkin Hopf algebra.

authors.name: Yi Liang

papers.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
papers.summary: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers under conditions on local mixing and local energy estimates. We verify these conditions for one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature and for finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.

authors.name: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding, Jianfeng Lu

papers.title: Universality in Quantum Many-Body Spin Ratchets
papers.summary: We consider a class of quantum circuits, known as quantum many-body spin ratchets, which act on alternating spin chains with two distinct spin types on even and odd sites. This setup breaks parity symmetry and exhibits chiral transport. It has been shown that the drift velocity in the case of integrable, SU(2)-symmetric quantum spin ratchets is universal, and conjectured that the same holds in the non-integrable case. Here, we prove that this universal drift is exact at all times, requiring only translation invariance and U(1) symmetry. Furthermore, we prove that it is sufficient for the circuit to be translation-invariant on average by deriving the same result in the random case. Finally, we demonstrate that breaking translation invariance immediately results in deviations from this universal prediction.

authors.name: Andrea Azzali, Marko Ljubotina

papers.title: Attainable and unattainable gauge-dependent quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling
papers.summary: In this paper, we study the gauge dependence of quantum precision in ultrastrongly coupled light--matter systems. The unitary between gauges carries the coupling $g$, so each truncation defines a different family. The quantum Fisher information traces an exact parabola across frames. Harmonic matter minimizes it at a universal $\theta_\ast=\Omega/(\Omega+\omega)$, set by the matter and cavity frequencies. Only the minimal-coupling bound is attainable. Frames differ by a factor $9.6$ with opposite trends. Diverging virtual-excitation gain at the Dicke point is a gauge artifact and saturates.

authors.name: Wangjun Lu, Qing Yu

papers.title: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory
papers.summary: Local measurements and feedback can autonomously prepare and stabilize entangled many-body states. In frustration-free control, the target manifold is fixed by local constraints, whose violations are detected by measurement and removed by feedback. We develop an exact theory of this mechanism for Dicke states of $N_q$ qubits, which span the permutation-symmetric subspace with one Dicke state per magnetization sector. Local singlet projectors define the constraints and detect departures from permutation symmetry. The dynamics closes exactly on the span of the $N_q(N_q-1)/2$ singlet-pair projectors and maps onto a classical first-passage process: measurements move the pair endpoints, while feedback absorbs pairs on measured bonds. The closure reduces the exponentially large many-body Liouvillian to a generator of polynomial size, fully quantifying the preparation process. In one dimension we solve it in closed form. Its slowest rate, $\Lambda_{\rm pair}=2[1-\cos(\pi/N_q)]$ in units of the measurement rate, is the full Liouvillian gap. For any such scheme, the relaxation time is bounded below by the inverse fraction of pair configurations on which feedback acts; local feedback reaches $O(N_q)$ of $O(N_q^2)$ configurations and thus needs a time at least linear in $N_q$. A second exact closure gives the final state for any initial condition. Extensions to modified transport, restricted feedback, and physical errors yield an exact transport-to-absorber crossover, geometric preparation laws, and a bound on the stationary leakage. An exact second-moment closure determines the ensemble fluctuations: measurement noise is conserving, while feedback generates the shot noise of removal and correlations between pairs. Preparation, acceleration, robustness, and fluctuations are thus all governed by one exactly solvable process: the transport and absorption of local constraint violations.

authors.name: T. D\"orstel, T. C. Lang, T. Iadecola, J. H. Wilson, M. Buchhold

papers.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
papers.summary: Non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems arise from memory effects in the environment. Crucially, this memory can often be explained classically and does not require the storage of quantum information. The presence of genuine quantum memory can be certified by existing criteria that compare the evolution of the system at two different times. We show that quantum memory can remain hidden from all such pairwise tests and become detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. We derive an analytical three-time witness and use it to certify quantum memory in a minimal qubit example in which every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, thus establishing a strict hierarchy of quantum memory effects. Genuine multi-time quantum memory does not rely on fine-tuned time-dependent Hamiltonians or gate-based evolution. We experimentally demonstrate the hierarchy of quantum memory in a time-continuous realization on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings.

authors.name: Konstantin Beyer, Valentin Link, Surihan Sean Borjigin, Qian Cao, Orion Lee, Kater Murch, Igor Pikovski, Philip Taranto

papers.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
papers.summary: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. For reversible local binary-spin dynamics, we establish volume-uniform $O(\varepsilon)$-$L^2(\pi)$ approximation bounds for local observable dynamics using connected-cluster spaces with neighborhood radius $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ and cluster order $O(\log^2(1/\varepsilon))$. We further establish error bounds for repeated one-step propagation using exact moment matrices and their sparse-plus-rank-one compressions, uniformly in the time step and number of iterations.

authors.name: Yuehaw Khoo, Bowen Li, Yuguan Wang, Siyao Yang

papers.title: Quantum sine imaginary-time evolution: sequential and QSVT implementations of a probabilistic ground-state filter
papers.summary: We propose quantum sine imaginary-time evolution (QSITE), a quantum algorithm for preparing ground states of a Hamiltonian. QSITE approximates imaginary-time evolution through an exact sine filter. We give two circuit implementations of this operator: a sequential one that applies it as a concatenation of linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), reusing two ancilla qubits across steps via mid-circuit measurement, and a coherent one based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). A telescoping identity shows the two prepare the same state and succeed with identical probability, differing only in how that probability can be boosted. QSITE belongs to the family of ancilla-based probabilistic imaginary-time filters and we state rigorous convergence guarantees: we prove that the QSITE operator converges uniformly to the exact ITE operator, that the prepared state converges to the ideal ITE state, and that the filter probability increases monotonically with each concatenation step. Although the construction applies to an arbitrary Hamiltonian, we specialize it to optimization Hamiltonians, and this specialization is what exposes its structure more easily. Since MaxCut eigenvalues are integers, the probability of failure is periodic in the evolution time, yielding safe zones, the first located analytically and the second numerically. For MaxCut we further show that, when the tolerated energy error is a fixed fraction of the ground-state energy, the probability of failure can be bounded below 1/2 with concatenation steps growing linearly with the number of qubits in the first safe zone. We present numerical results for random Erd\"os-R\'enyi instances with up to 24 qubits and benchmark QSITE against QAOA.

authors.name: Victor A. Penas, Tamara Bottazzi, Marcelo Losada, Diego Tielas, Federico Holik

papers.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.summary: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(\pi/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\frac{\pi}{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $\pi/2$ and $\pi/4$, respectively.

authors.name: Lijun Wang

papers.title: Entanglement Geometry Beyond Polygons: Graph-Theoretic Entanglement Inequalities
papers.summary: Entanglement entropies of pure multipartite states can be constrained by organizing subsystem cuts as edges (hyperedges) of graphs (hypergraphs). Starting from the one-party entanglement polygon inequality, we derive these constraints from strong subadditivity and pure-state complementarity, with optimal coefficients and explicit equality conditions. Our central result determines, for a distinguished two-party cut and an arbitrary weighted family of cuts, the optimal polygon coefficient: the smallest total weight of the cuts separating a member of the distinguished pair from a remaining party. A refinement involving three mutual information terms gives the exact minimum of the weighted sum at fixed entropies of the two parties and of their union, attained by at most three independent bipartite pure states. The analogous coefficient is also optimal for a distinguished one-party cut and for any distinguished cut that the family does not split. This criterion recovers the cycle and complete-graph inequalities and shows that uniform incidence parity, which we prove sufficient for polygon inequalities on hypergraphs, is not necessary. Averaging strong subadditivity over both sides of a bipartition gives a sharp $k$-marginal inequality with coefficient $2\binom{n-2}{k-1}$, and we determine uniformly optimal coefficients for collective hyperstar inequalities. For paths and overlapping hyperchains, the deficits are exact sums of conditional mutual information terms; genuinely multipartite entangled cluster states saturate the hyperchain inequality while the chain inequality remains strict. We characterize pure chain equality states, bound the trace distance to cycle equality states independently of the number of parties and local dimensions, and obtain bond-dimension bounds for matrix product states and sequential-recovery error estimates.

authors.name: Masoud Gharahi

papers.title: Quantum dynamical transitions when the corresponding classical phase space has a separatrix: extension of the QKNH theorem beyond double wells
papers.summary: In classical Hamiltonian systems with a slowly time-dependent parameter, adiabaticity breaks down at a separatrix, leading to probabilistic post-adiabatic transitions between different phase-space regions described by the Kruskal-Neishtadt-Henrard (KNH) theorem. Quantum mechanically, dynamical tunneling allows adiabaticity to persist where it breaks down classically, making the quantum-classical correspondence for separatrix crossing non-trivial. We recently established a quantum version of the KNH theorem (QKNH) by introducing the concept of a sweep-rate-dependent quantum separatrix in the instantaneous energy spectrum of the time-dependent system. The QKNH theorem relates the splitting of a quantum ensemble between the outgoing dynamical sectors at the quantum separatrix to their relative growth rates, and thus provides a quantum analog of the classical KNH rule. Here, we demonstrate that these findings are not restricted to double-well systems with tunneling through a potential barrier. We investigate a slowly driven quantum pendulum, in which the avoided crossings arise from above-barrier reflection. The resulting Landau-Zener probabilities have the same local lattice form as in the double-well problem, allowing the application of the QKNH theorem.

authors.name: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin

papers.title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
papers.summary: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.

authors.name: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin

papers.title: Direct electron cooling at millikelvin temperatures with quantum-well heat pump
papers.summary: Unconventional solid-state cooling is proposed whereby the electron subband degeneracy of a semiconductor quantum well is cycled at cryogenic temperatures. By "expanding" electrons to higher subband degeneracy and "compressing" to lower degeneracy in an Otto cycle, a stack of ultra-wide 150 nm GaAs quantum wells filling a 1 cm3 volume could be operated as a heat pump to pump 26 uW at 100 mK. Operated as a refrigerator, it can piggy-back onto dilution refrigerators to cool from T_base to T_base/4. Possible cooling applications include quantum computers and infrared detectors.

authors.name: Chulin Wang, Thomas Douglas, Matthew A Grayson

papers.title: Glued tree lattices with only compact localized states
papers.summary: Flat band physics is a central theme in modern condensed matter physics. By constructing a tight--binding single particle system that has vanishing momentum dispersion in one or more bands, and subsequently including more particles and interactions, it is possible to study physics in strongly interacting regimes. Inspired by the glued trees that first arose in one of the few known examples of quantum supremacy, we define and analyze two infinite families of tight binding single particle Bose--Hubbard models that have only flat bands, and only compact localized states despite having any nonnegative number of translation symmetries. The first class of model that we introduce is constructed by replacing a sufficiently large fraction of the edges in a generic countable graph with glued trees modified to have complex hoppings. The second class arises from thinking of complex weighted glued trees as rhombi that can then be used to tile two dimensional space, giving rise to the familiar dice lattice and infinitely many generalizations thereof, of which some are Euclidian while others are hyperbolic.

authors.name: Andrew Osborne, Ciro Salcedo, Andrew A. Houck

papers.title: Effective Dynamics for Weakly Interacting Bosons in an Iterated High-Density Thermodynamic Limit
papers.summary: We study the time evolution of weakly interacting Bose gases on a three-dimensional torus of arbitrary volume. The coupling constant is supposed to be inversely proportional to the density, which is considered to be large and independent of the particle number. We take into account a class of initial states exhibiting quasi-complete Bose-Einstein condensation. For each fixed time in a finite interval, we prove the convergence of the one-particle reduced density matrix towards the projection onto the normalised order parameter describing the condensate - evolving according to the Hartree equation - in the iterated limit where the volume (and therefore the particle number), and subsequently the density go to infinity. The rate of convergence depends only on the density and on the decay of both the expected number of particles and the energy of the initial quasi-vacuum state.

authors.name: Daniele Ferretti, Kalle Koskinen

papers.title: Classification of Thouless pumps with non-invertible symmetries and implications for Floquet phases
papers.summary: We study symmetry preserving adiabatic and Floquet dynamics of one-dimensional systems. Using quasiadiabatic evolution, we establish a correspondence between adiabatic cycles and invertible defects generated by spatially truncated Thouless pump operators. Employing the classification of gapped phases by module categories, we show that the Thouless pumps are classified by the group of autoequivalences of the module category. We then explicitly construct Thouless pump operators for minimal lattice models with $\text{Vec}_G$, Rep($G$), and Rep($H$) symmetries, and show how the Thouless pump operators have the group structure of autoequivalences. The Thouless pump operators, together with Hamiltonians with gapped ground states, are then used to construct Floquet drives. An analytic solution for the Floquet phase diagram characterized by winding numbers is constructed when the Floquet drives obey an Onsager algebra. Our approach points the way to a general connection between distinct Thouless pumps and distinct families of Floquet phases.

authors.name: Yabo Li, Matteo Dell'Acqua, Aditi Mitra

papers.title: Symmetry-Protected Bipartite Entanglement in Hopf-Linked Quantum Rings
papers.summary: We study two interacting electrons in Hopf-linked quantum rings, one electron on each ring. In the absence of the inter-ring interaction, the two lowest orbital states on each ring have the same energy. For the ideal geometry, the Fourier coefficients of the three-dimensional Coulomb kernel satisfy $V_{1,0}=-V_{0,1}$, making the positive-parity block of the four-state Hamiltonian diagonal in the Bell basis. Unitary symmetries of the full orbital Hamiltonian preserve the parity sectors under virtual transitions. For pure states odd under ring exchange followed by a half-turn on each ring ($\mathcal Y=-1$), the Schmidt weights occur in equal pairs, giving at least one bit of entanglement between the rings. An elliptic deformation changes the Coulomb selection rule to first order while preserving the link. Finite-basis diagonalization shows that higher orbitals can reduce the probability of obtaining the encoded Bell pair by projection onto the two lowest orbitals of each ring even when the entanglement between the rings remains close to one bit.

authors.name: V. Yogesh, Prosenjit Maity

papers.title: Quantum resetting with memory
papers.summary: We introduce a quantum stochastic resetting protocol with uniform memory, in which each resetting event returns the system to a state visited at a time chosen uniformly from its entire history. The resulting dynamics is nonunitary, non-Markovian and a direct quantum generalization of the classical preferential relocation model. Working in the energy eigenbasis, we derive the exact evolution of every density-matrix element for an arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonian and show that the Hamiltonian enters the dynamics only through the corresponding Bohr frequencies. This leads to a natural distinction between two classes of quantum systems: gapped and gapless. In \emph{gapped systems} (systems with a discrete energy spectrum), while the diagonal elements remain unchanged, the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix in the energy eigenbasis decay algebraically with a continuously varying exponent and with an amplitude that oscillates periodically in $\log t$. The system therefore approaches a stationary state that is independent of the resetting rate and retains a strong memory of the initial state. In \emph{gapless systems} (systems with a continuous energy spectrum), arbitrarily small Bohr frequencies prevent stationarity. Instead, the position distribution spreads on the universal (ultra-slow) scale $\log(rt)/r$, independently of the initial state and of the details of the Hamiltonian. We illustrate these results with a two-level system, a harmonic oscillator, and a free quantum particle, and contrast them with their classical counterparts.

authors.name: Gabriele de Mauro, Manas Kulkarni, Satya N. Majumdar

papers.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
papers.summary: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.

authors.name: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

papers.title: Dynamics of R\'enyi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization
papers.summary: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on R\'enyi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we employ spectral representations of reduced density matrix moments (purity and its higher-order generalizations) whose decay through spectral dephasing captures nonequilibrium entanglement growth. These representations closely resemble those governing local-observable dynamics, but involve eigenstates in a replicated Hilbert space and observables are replaced by subsystem permutation operators, such as the swap operator for R\'enyi-2. Focusing on R\'enyi-2, we combine exact random matrix theory calculations, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to formulate ETH-like ans\"atze for subsystem swap matrix elements in the replicated eigenbasis and their cross-correlations with initial-state overlap statistics. In the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is entirely determined by smooth slowly varying functions that emerge from such statistics, paralleling generalized ETH formulations in a single replica.
