By combining the longitudinal response with the antisymmetrized Hall signal, we use a phenomenological current-partition model to estimate the dissipative and superconducting current contributions. From this analysis, we estimate the field-dependent superconducting current together with the Hall-derived effective dissipative carrier density and mobility. We also observe an even-in-field transverse signal whose magnitude depends strongly on the driving current. We discuss this signal as a possible mixed-state response involving the magnetic and supercurrent texture of Abrikosov vortices, vortex dynamics, and Cooper-pair current redistribution. The present measurements do not uniquely distinguish vortex, condensate, or combined contributions. The model provides a practical way to compare the longitudinal and transverse mixed-state responses without implying a direct spatial separation of the two current channels.

authors.name: Sai Vaishnavi Kanduri, Danilo B\"urger, Zichao Li, Mario Ziegler, Detlef Born, Sahitya V. Vegesna, Heidemarie Kr\"uger

papers.title: Sondheimer oscillations in Weyl semimetal films
papers.summary: In conducting films subject to an out-of-plane magnetic field, electron motion between the surfaces gives rise to conductance oscillations periodic in magnetic field, known as Sondheimer oscillations. While this size effect has been investigated in conventional metals, its dependence on the Berry curvature of topological materials remains less explored. In this work, we extend the semiclassical Boltzmann description of Sondheimer oscillations to type-I Weyl semimetal films. We account for the Berry curvature, the orbital magnetic moment and the effect of the Zeeman coupling on the Fermi wavevector and the electronic group velocity. The Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment generate a beating pattern and chirping in the Sondheimer oscillations. In the thick-film and thin-film regimes, we provide analytical expressions for the longitudinal conductivity, which highlight the interplay between electronic band topology and boundary-scattering in magnetotransport.

authors.name: Lucas M\'echet, Louis-Thomas Gendron, Ion Garate

papers.title: Unveiling the Complex high-pressure phases of Sodium at the Melting Curve Minimum via Data-Drive Crystal Structure Prediction
papers.summary: Sodium exhibits a remarkable concentration of complex crystalline phases near its melting-curve minimum, yet the atomic arrangements of several experimentally observed phases remain unresolved. Here, we combine CALYPSO crystal structure prediction with Deep Potential models developed through concurrent learning to explore this structural landscape. Searches over more than 1.6 million configurations recover the previously reported $I4/m$ structure of $tI50$ and identify candidate atomic arrangements for $oC120$ and $aP90$, together with three additional low-enthalpy structures, $tI52$, $oP72$, and $oP92$. The proposed candidates reproduce key features of the experimentally indexed cell geometries. First-principles enthalpy calculations, Gibbs free-energy comparisons, and solid--liquid coexistence simulations reveal close competition among these structures and established sodium phases. Near the calculated reference melting minimum, $tI50$ is favored over $cI16$ and $oP8$, whereas $oC120$ and $aP90$ remain closely competitive, with their relative stability sensitive to model accuracy. These results provide testable structural models for unresolved experimental phases and reveal multiple closely competing low-enthalpy configurations near sodium's melting minimum

authors.name: Zhenyu Wang, Chengqian Zhang, Xiaoyang Wang, Haiyang Niu, Jian Lv, Han Wang

papers.title: Nonmonotonic In-Plane Thermal Transport in Metal-Embedded Graphitic Carbon Nitride
papers.summary: Embedding metal atoms within the intrinsic cavities of graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) modifies its local bonding and vibrational properties, yet its consequences for lattice thermal transport remain poorly understood. Here, we combine a machine-learned potential (MLP) with homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) to investigate in-plane thermal transport in Cu-embedded g-C3N4 across the full range of cavity occupation. The thermal conductivity exhibits a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence on Cu occupation, decreasing at intermediate occupation and partially recovering as the cavities approach full occupation. Frequency-resolved analysis reveals that this behavior originates from the competition between two phonon contributions. The low-frequency vibrations introduced by Cu couple to the intrinsic modes of g-C3N4, reconstructing the phonon dispersion and suppressing thermal transport below 10 THz. With increasing Cu occupation, the collective mechanical response of the N atoms surrounding the cavities is enhanced, accompanied by increased phonon group velocities in the 20-30 THz range and a corresponding recovery of the high-frequency thermal contribution. The competition between the saturating low-frequency suppression and the increasing high-frequency contribution gives rise to the nonmonotonic thermal conductivity. A similar occupation dependence and spectral redistribution are observed for Ag-embedded g-C3N4. These results identify competing phonon contributions as the microscopic origin of nonmonotonic thermal transport in metal-embedded g-C3N4 and suggest that occupation of intrinsic cavities provides a route to redistributing phonon transport in porous crystalline materials.

authors.name: Wenwu Jiang, Hekai Bu, Wei Qiu, Yong Ni

papers.title: Trajectory arclength reveals thermodynamic criticality
papers.summary: Thermodynamic criticality arises at continuous phase transitions, where collective interactions produce non-analytic behavior in equilibrium thermodynamic quantities in the thermodynamic limit. We show that this criticality also leaves an analytically predictable signature in the arclength of microscopic Hamiltonian trajectories. For the attractive Hamiltonian mean-field model, we derive the thermodynamic limit of the equilibrium-averaged arclength, formulated as a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, and demonstrate that it develops a kink precisely at the phase transition. We trace this non-analyticity to spontaneous magnetization and derive the leading critical finite-size correction, scaling as $N^{-1/2}$ with an explicit analytical prefactor. Simulations with up to $10^5$ degrees of freedom confirm both predictions without adjustable parameters. Requiring neither tangent-space evolution nor prior specification of an order parameter for its computation, trajectory arclength provides a simple, quantitative link between microscopic Hamiltonian motion and collective thermodynamic criticality.

authors.name: Jim\'enez-L\'opez, Javier, Garc\'ia-Garrido, V. J

papers.title: Solids activated by multi-body nonreciprocity
papers.summary: Field-mediated forces between particles can be both nonreciprocal and irreducibly multi-body, giving rise to emergent activity in systems of individually passive particles. While prior work extensively studied how multi-body nonreciprocity can activate few-body systems, fuel intermittency, and drive liquid-like behavior, the effect on the solid state of large particle ensembles is less explored. Here we use two-dimensional, close-packed rafts of identical, athermal, acoustically levitated microspheres to show how multi-body nonreciprocity injects activity in solids. At the level of both individual particles and collective dynamics, crystalline rafts exhibit persistent circulations with no net handedness. The rafts also exhibit a phonon-like dispersion relation corresponding to a large Poisson ratio, indicating an induced softness to shear. Within the bulk, lattice symmetry masks microscopic nonreciprocity, although it can manifest in renormalized, reciprocal elastic coefficients. At dislocations and raft edges, where this symmetry is broken, multi-body nonreciprocal interactions act as local generators of activity. A coarse-grained microscopic model of multi-body nonreciprocity, calibrated on three-particle simulations, recovers the rafts' experimentally observed dispersion relations and localized activity. Using these findings, we illustrate how to harness defect-induced activity for programmable movement by arranging microscopic dislocations to drive macroscopic propulsion and rotation of a whole raft.

authors.name: Brady Wu, Daniel S. Seara, Qinghao Mao, Vincenzo Vitelli, Heinrich M. Jaeger

papers.title: NEP-Spin: A spin-dependent neuroevolution potential for large-scale spin--lattice simulations
papers.summary: NEP-Spin is a \glsentrylong{nep} for coupled atomic motion and variable-length magnetic moments. Local bond and spin tensors give an energy invariant under independent spin and spatial rotations without \glsentrylong{soc} and under joint rotations with it. We benchmark energies, atomic forces, and magnetic forces on public datasets for collinear Fe--Al and noncollinear Fe. In multiferroic \glsentrylong{bfo}, the predicted zero-field cycloid period is 69.7~nm, compared with 62--63~nm from neutron scattering. An electric field of 20~mV/\AA{} opposite to the polarization lengthens the period to 93.2~nm, while imposing the same polar displacement at zero field gives 85.1~nm. In a uniform antiferromagnetic cell at fixed lattice vectors, 6~T magnetic fields along orthogonal basal axes reorient the Fe moments and give opposite signs of the ionic polarization change $\Delta P_y$. First-principles ionic relaxations at the predicted moment vectors reproduce both signs. In a 2.79-million-atom ferroelectric twin, the cycloid rotation planes tilt by different amounts from their shared initial plane and remain distinct over 10~ps at 100~K. At 10~ps the propagation axes lie within about $7^\circ$ of their initial directions. With inertial spin dynamics, GPUMD advances a 5.93-million-atom BiFeO$_3$ cell at 21.8 million atom-steps per second on four RTX 4090 GPUs.

authors.name: Chengbing Chen, Zheyong Fan, Ben Xu

papers.title: Valence band, electron correlation, and possible temperature dependent change in the electronic structure near $E_F$ of a candidate of ambient-pressure nickelate superconductors Sr$_3$Ni$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$
papers.summary: Photoemission spectroscopy (PES) studies of Sr$_3$Ni$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$ (Sr3252), a candidate ambient-pressure bilayer nickelate superconductor, have been performed to investigate the electronic structure. Valence band spectra, which are compared with DFT and DFT+U calculations, reveal dominant Ni 3$d$ $t_{2g}$-derived states located around 0.6 eV binding energy with a shoulder around 0.2 eV that can be attributed to states with a dominant Ni 3$d_{3z2-r2}$ character. The overall valence band shape is better reproduced by the simulated spectrum of DFT+U (= 3 eV), providing an experimental estimation of the strength of electron correlation. High-resolution PES near the Fermi level ($E_F$) exhibits marked temperature dependence, which cannot be fully understood by a broadening due to coupling of a photo-hole to phonons alone and suggests change in electronic structure. The results provide fundamental electronic structure information of Sr3252, which is useful to further explore the superconductivity of Sr3252.

authors.name: Ryota Goban, Daiki Ootsuki, Kenichi Ozawa, Akira Yasui, Masayuki Ochi, Kazuhiko Kuroki, Ryo Matsumoto, Kensei Terashima, Yoshihiko Takano, Yuji Muraoka, Takayoshi Yokoya

papers.title: Soliton Propagation of Zero Sound in Superfluid $^3$He-B
papers.summary: Nonlinear equations for zero sound interacting with the B-phase collective modes are derived by treating $^3$He-B as a medium of two-level ``molecules'' (Cooper pairs), The nonlinear equations reduce to known results from kinetic theory in the linear response limit. Soliton solutions to the nonlinear equations are discussed in context with the experiments of Polturak et al.

authors.name: J. A. Sauls

papers.title: Indentation-induced polar domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave semiconductor EuTe4
papers.summary: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarization-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 m$\Omega$cm. Polarized-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarization domains with an approximately 90 $^\circ$ domain configuration. Local indentation with a $\sim$1 $\mu$m-apex-radius needle reconfigures these domains, producing write/erase-like changes in wedge-shaped regions. These results establish local mechanical-field domain engineering in a relatively conducting CDW semiconductor, with possible contributions from both ferroelastic-like and flexoelectric mechanisms.

authors.name: Hidefumi Takahashi, Yuki Umewaka, Kiichiro Yoshida, Ritsuto Nakamura, Akitoshi Nakano, Takao Matsumura, Daiki Sekine, Masakazu Matsubara, Masayuki Ochi, Shintaro Ishiwata

papers.title: Projecting Fermions into Exact Scar Towers: Local Protection across Phase Transitions
papers.summary: We construct exact scar towers in $SO(n)$ ($n\ge3$) spin chains by Gutzwiller projection of $n$-flavor flat-band Kitaev chains. The projected roots have only singlet and antisymmetric components on each bond. These local constraints allow a staggered flavor flip to generate an equidistant tower. The root and its first descendant exhaust the two-site configurations that are visited by the tower, leaving an orthogonal bond subspace unvisited. Deformations within this subspace can break $SO(n)$ symmetry and reshape the low-energy physics without altering the exact scar tower. A polarization-selective deformation drives an exact first-order transition from the symmetry-protected topological phase to a ferromagnetic phase. The tower retains its wave functions and absolute energies across the phase transition, including at the gapless point. Exact scars therefore need not inherit the symmetries, order parameters, or criticality of the ground state.

authors.name: Wenjie Wei, Kun Jiang, Hui-Ke Jin

papers.title: Generation and non-thermal annealing of dislocations and atomic-scale roughness by nonlinear surface acoustic waves
papers.summary: Surface acoustic waves (SAWs) are widely used to probe near-surface material properties and microstructure, but their potential to drive permanent structural modification remains largely unexplored. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations reveal the mechanisms of defect generation and evolution induced by nonlinear Rayleigh waves in Pt. Strong crystallographic dependence of the nonlinear evolution is observed. SAWs on Pt(111) undergo rapid nonlinear sharpening and shock formation, with localized elastic energy and increasing near-surface stresses, whereas much weaker sharpening on Pt(001) allows dissipation to compete effectively with shock formation. For sufficiently strong SAWs on Pt(111), Shockley partial dislocations are emitted from the surface when the resolved shear stress approaches the theoretical shear strength. The highly localized and rapidly changing stress field at the shock front activates multiple slip systems and promotes crossslip and reactions between Shockley partials, producing complex dislocation structures with sessile stair-rod segments. Subsequent SAW interactions activate dislocation sources on slip systems where the stress is insufficient for homogeneous nucleation, leading, in one case, to sequential emission of Shockley partials and formation of a subsurface twinned domain. Repeated SAW passages progressively reduce dislocation density, demonstrating SAW-driven nonthermal annealing. Dislocation interactions with the free surface generate atomic-scale steps, terraces, and other under-coordinated configurations, providing a microscopic pathway for permanent surface modification that may contribute to the acoustically enhanced catalytic activity observed on Pt surfaces. These results establish nonlinear SAWs as drivers of nonthermal defect generation, restructuring, and annealing, opening opportunities for acoustic processing of near-surface microstructure.

authors.name: Yuan Xu, Maxim V. Shugaev, Leonid V. Zhigilei

papers.title: Quantum Geometry Effects in Lattice Dynamics
papers.summary: Quantum geometric effects such as the Berry curvature and the quantum metric are well established in electronic transport, whereas in lattice dynamics the Berry curvature also plays a key role: adiabatically following the lattice, electrons generate a molecular Berry curvature that splits degenerate optical phonons into chiral partners. To determine how the quantum metric affects phonons, we go beyond adiabatic lattice dynamics, identifying Berry curvature and quantum metric contributions to the electronic response of the lattice. Using first-principles calculations in the magnetic topological semimetal EuB$_6$, we find that phonon modes with chiral splitting and those with nonchiral splitting coexist. Unlike the former, which originate from the Berry curvature, the latter arise from the pure quantum metric, while the Berry curvature contribution is forbidden by crystal symmetry.

authors.name: Haoshu Li, Hao Chen, Qian Niu

papers.title: Dynamical evolution and rheological behavior of a sheared compound vesicle with a highly viscous core: a mesoscale particle-based study
papers.summary: We study numerically the dynamics and the rheology of a two-dimensional compound vesicle in wall-bounded shear flow, as a minimal model of a nucleated cell. We consider the configuration in which the annular fluid is iso-viscous with the external one, while the inner core is more viscous. Increasing the core viscosity drives the external vesicle away from steady tank-treading at values $\phi \geq 0.6$. When an internal body is present, the annular fluid partially shields the outer membrane from the viscous core, so that at small filling fractions the external vesicle retains tank-treading with a higher inclination angle and the intrinsic viscosity stays comparatively low. The internal vesicle, by contrast, tumbles and migrates away from the center, and at high $\phi$ this motion couples back to the host, producing intermittent shape excursions of the external membrane. The inner viscous body thus acts as an internal governor of the dynamical state.

authors.name: A. Lamura

papers.title: Anatomy of orbital and spin responses in GaAs and Si: Hall, inverse Faraday, and magneto-optical Kerr effects
papers.summary: Magneto-optical signals in nonmagnetic semiconductors entangle spin and orbital contributions, both in angular-momentum generation and magneto-optical detection. We calculate these contributions for electron-doped GaAs and Si using density-functional theory, linear-response theory, and a second-order density-matrix treatment of the inverse Faraday effect. At small electron doping, the intrinsic orbital Hall conductivity exceeds its spin counterpart in magnitude, while the orbital contribution to light-induced magnetization dominates over broad photon-energy ranges. We show that orbital- and spin-resolved optical Hall and polar Kerr coefficients exhibit stronger sensitivity to orbital moments than to equal spin moments. This contrast reflects direct electric-dipole coupling to orbital motion versus spin-orbit-mediated coupling to spin polarization. Consequently, Si maintains a substantial orbital magneto-optical response despite its weak spin-orbit interaction. At probe energies of 1.5 eV in GaAs and 3.0 eV in Si, the magnitude of the Kerr rotation per unit orbital moment is approximately 5 and 13 times larger than that per unit spin moment, respectively. Combining the calculated Hall conductivities and Kerr coefficients with a phenomenological drift-diffusion model yields predominantly orbital edge signals for the assumed diffusion constants and relaxation lengths. These results indicate that optical detection of induced magnetization in doped semiconductors such as GaAs and Si can be dominated by orbital signals, and therefore cannot be interpreted solely in terms of spin polarization.

authors.name: Sanaz Alikhah, Daegeun Jo, Peter M. Oppeneer

papers.title: Spin-controlled thermophase and noise-optimized thermometry in multiorbital quantum dots
papers.summary: Converting temperature differences into electrical signals underlies both thermoelectric energy conversion and thermometry, which is essential for managing heat in cryogenic quantum technologies. Superconducting circuits typically show a weak thermoelectric response, since their quasiparticle spectrum is nearly particle-hole symmetric. In a Josephson junction, a temperature difference can instead be converted into a superconducting phase difference in an open circuit. We investigate this thermophase effect in a setup where the junction consists of a two-orbital quantum dot with Rashba spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Zeeman splitting. A second orbital near the superconducting coherence peaks supports quasiparticle transport over a broad gate range. Zeeman splitting can enhance the thermophase by suppressing pair transport, while spin-orbit hybridization shifts the orbital resonances and can reverse the sign of the response. We assess the junction as a phase-based thermometer using a noise budget that includes readout and current noise together with fluctuations of the orbital energies and the magnetic field. The optimal operating points do not maximize the thermophase but balance a large quasiparticle response against sensitivity to parameter fluctuations. Under experimentally motivated noise assumptions, we obtain projected noise-equivalent temperatures of order $10\,\mu\mathrm{K}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ and determine the range over which a linear calibration remains accurate. Gate-tunable quantum-dot junctions thus offer a phase-based route to sensing temperature differences in superconducting circuits at sub-kelvin temperatures.

authors.name: Markus Plautz, Jeroen Danon, Jacob Linder

papers.title: Edge-asymmetric magnetism in semi-Dirac quantum dots
papers.summary: In this study, we investigated the electronic and magnetic properties of quantum dots (QDs) throughout the transition from the Dirac limit to the semi-Dirac limit and beyond. When non-interacting semi-Dirac fermions are confined in triangular QDs, the resulting electronic states near the Fermi level are localized asymmetrically among the three edges of these systems. In the presence of electron interactions, we show that these low-energy states favor the formation of edge-asymmetric magnetism in triangular QDs. In particular, the magnetic moments were localized only along a single edge of the zigzag triangular QDs, corresponding to an edge-asymmetric ferromagnetic ground state. For various system sizes, these zigzag triangular QDs exhibit a one-unit increase in the ground-state total spin ($\Delta S_z = +1$) beyond the semi-Dirac limit, revealing a striking result of this transition. In contrast, the remaining two edges are antiferromagnetically coupled in the armchair triangular QDs, indicating an edge-asymmetric antiferromagnetic (AFM) ground state. We further identified the AFM ground states in hexagonal QDs, indicating that these types of asymmetric configurations are not unique to triangular QDs. Collectively, edge-asymmetric magnetism could create potential opportunities for future spintronics.

authors.name: Mustafa Polat

papers.title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
papers.summary: Metal-halide perovskites are promising photovoltaic absorbers whose optoelectronic properties are highly tunable. Epitaxial strain offers a route to stabilize desirable phases, tune band gaps, and reduce energetic disorder, but rational strain engineering requires predictive models. Static, zero-temperature "strained-bulk" density functional theory (DFT) calculations, successful for oxide perovskites, neglect the dynamic disorder and anharmonicity that govern halide perovskites at ambient temperature. Here, we show that molecular dynamics (MD) based on machine-learned force fields trained on-the-fly on DFT reproduces the structural and optoelectronic response of methylammonium (MA) lead iodide (MAPbI$_3$) to epitaxial strain at 300 K. We simulate bulk and free-standing slab models across experimentally accessible biaxial strains by locking the in-plane lattice vectors in nanosecond-long simulations. We predict a tetragonal-to-cubic transition at $\sim$0.5% tensile strain, marked by $c/a = 1$ and the loss of the $a^0a^0c^-$ tilting pattern, in agreement with experiments on epitaxial MAPbI$_3$ films on KCl. MA cations retain preferential orientations in the strain-induced cubic phase, unlike in its temperature-induced counterpart. Bulk and slab models yield consistent trends, with surface effects decaying within a few octahedral layers. Band gaps computed as ensemble averages over MD snapshots blue-shift under tensile strain, consistent with experiment, whereas static calculations on averaged structures predict a red shift. Our study positions MD with constrained lattice vectors as a method for predicting finite-temperature strain phase diagrams and guiding the epitaxial design of perovskite absorbers.

authors.name: Daan Holleman, Luuk Klein Nagelvoort, Monica Morales-Masis, Linn Leppert

papers.title: Manipulation of Ferroelectric Polarization Under Near-Gap Light
papers.summary: Noncontacting light control of ferroelectric (FE) order has been receiving extensive interest in condensed matter physics. In this work, we investigate near-resonant light irradiation that induces structure-dependent photoexcited carrier density along the transition pathway. We combine a minimal Rice-Mele model containing intersite density-density correlations with ab initio calculations for realistic materials such as GeTe and SnTe. If the photon energy is below-gap without carrier excitation, only off-resonant scattering occurs and the FE order tends to be diminished. Slightly increasing photon energy at the near-gap regime would lead to a centrosymmetric non-polar (NP) to FE phase transition, which is not thermally accessible in conventional pressure-temperature phase diagram. This is in contrast to the well-above-gap light situation that tends to suppress the FE order under a fixed amount of photoexcitation. We apply phenomenological Landau theory and show that they belong to the continuous and first-order phase transitions, respectively. The occupation constrained calculations suggest that these reversible NP-FE phase transitions could be triggered under moderate light fluence. Our mechanism provides a potential route to reversible light-stabilized polar phases with reduced lattice heating and marginal lattice damages.

authors.name: Hanli Cui, Jian Zhou

papers.title: Gyroidal Magnetic Order with Weyl Magnons
papers.summary: The gyroid, a triply periodic minimal surface found widely in nature and materials, has remained largely unexplored as a design principle for magnetic order. We introduce gyroidal magnetic order on the hyperoctagon lattice, the skeletal network of the gyroid, in which each magnetic moment points along the local $C_3$ axis that coincides with the local normal to the gyroid surface. The resulting noncoplanar spin texture constitutes a direct magnetic imprint of the gyroid geometry. We show that this order can be stabilized by single-ion anisotropy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, or the symmetric off-diagonal $\Gamma$ interaction combined with the Kitaev interaction, and remains robust against quantum fluctuations. Its magnon spectrum hosts symmetry-enforced pseudospin-1 and pseudospin-1/2 Weyl points that, unlike their electronic counterparts, persist under symmetry-allowed perturbations. Our results establish the gyroid as a geometric platform for magnetic order and symmetry-enforced topological magnon excitations.

authors.name: Kiyu Fukui, Yukitoshi Motome

papers.title: Neutron Spin Resonance as Probe of Triplet Pair Density Waves in CeCoIn$_5$
papers.summary: Spin resonance modes are among the most characteristic collective excitations of unconventional superconductors, yet their microscopic origin remains unresolved. Although commonly interpreted as purely magnetic excitations, this picture does not explain the rich magnetic field evolution of these modes observed in heavy-fermion superconductors. Here we combine inelastic neutron scattering and symmetry analysis to investigate the evolution of the spin resonance modes in the heavy-fermion superconductor CeCoIn$_5$ under an in-plane magnetic field. At high fields, approaching the upper critical field of the superconductor, we discover a third resonance mode with relatively high intensity. We demonstrate that the resonance branches observed experimentally can be interpreted as collective modes of the superconducting condensate involving transitions to excited superconducting states. This framework provides a unified interpretation of the field-induced splitting of the resonance, the newly observed mode at high fields, the relative neutron scattering intensities of each mode, and provides the first direct evidence that a spin resonance mode can be associated with a singlet-triplet excitation of a superconductor.

authors.name: David W. Tam, Ilaria Maccari, St\'ephane Raymond, Barry Winn, Paul Steffens, Arno Hiess, Jacques Ollivier, Dariusz Jakub Gawryluk, Ekaterina Pomjakushina, Aline Ramires, Michel Kenzelmann

papers.title: Scanning nanowire quantum dot with radio-frequency read-out
papers.summary: Scanning single-electron transistors (SETs) are highly sensitive local probes of charge and electric potential, but their integration with robust height control for scanning probe microscopy remains challenging. Furthermore, readout bandwidths are limited to tens of kHz, while characterizing faster charge dynamics is often of interest. Here, we present a scanning SET in the form of a nanowire (NW) quantum dot (QD) integrated at the apex of a non-contact atomic force microscopy (NC-AFM) cantilever. We demonstrate NC-AFM topographic imaging and local electrometry capability by mapping the electrostatic potential generated by a set of nanoscale voltage-biased gate electrodes. Comparison with electrostatic simulations shows agreement with the measured potential profiles. We demonstrate radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry read-out of the sensor, by embedding the QD in an LC-resonator. This platform establishes a route towards high-bandwidth scanning electrometry with simultaneous topographic contrast.

authors.name: Aur\`ele Kamber, Luca Forrer, Valentina Zannier, Fabio Beltram, Lucia Sorba, Martino Poggio, Floris Braakman

papers.title: Exact solution of the long-range voter model in arbitrary dimensions: correlations and effective-dimensional scaling
papers.summary: Long-range interactions can profoundly alter collective ordering and critical behavior, yet exact ana- lytical results for non-equilibrium systems with such interactions remain scarce. We obtain an exact analytical solution for the spatial correlation function of the voter model with long-range interac- tions in arbitrary spatial dimension. Starting from the evolution equation for the Fourier modes, we identify the long-wavelength dispersion generated by the interaction kernel and derive the resulting coarsening and stationary scaling regimes. The solution yields the critical condition separating these regimes, the characteristic coarsening length, and the asymptotic decay of stationary correlations. These results establish an exact effective-dimensional correspondence: the long-range model in dimen- sion d, with interaction exponent \b{eta}, exhibits the same scaling exponents as a short-range voter model in the effective dimension deff = 2d/\b{eta}. The correspondence holds across the coarsening, marginal, and stationary regimes, while the associated scaling functions need not coincide

authors.name: Fabrizio Rippa, Jacopo Alexander Garofalo, Giuseppe Petrillo, Eugenio Lippiello

papers.title: Collective order from language models without communication, memory or shared context
papers.summary: Physical matter orders without a centre: units interact only with neighbours, and fluctuations carry them over energy barriers from a locally stable arrangement to the ordered state. We ask whether language-model agents can do the same, treating each memoryless query as a particle that sees its neighbours but cannot communicate, has no identifier or shared context and receives the same question as all others. Such a particle behaves as if at zero temperature: told a rule or a temperature, it returns the most probable state, and a collective can freeze in a local minimum. We therefore give each particle only a goal and a die whose weights it sets itself, and test several models. Some of them use the die as a noise source even at a local optimum, with weights that fall with the energy cost of the move; on a lattice the energy of one of them climbs over barriers and reaches the ground state, where the noise stops by itself. Particles in three-lane counterflow also order, from mixed traffic into one-way lanes: a spontaneous symmetry breaking. Decentralized collective order can thus arise from disorder without communication, memory or shared context, with noise that the particles choose themselves.

authors.name: Yong Wang

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamics of R-loop Formation in the CRISPR-Cas9 System
papers.summary: The binding specificity of CRISPR-Cas9 is governed by the stepwise formation of an R-loop, in which the sgRNA displaces the nontarget DNA strand and hybridizes with the target strand in discrete base pair steps. Here we develop a nonequilibrium dynamics framework that models R-loop formation as a continuous-time Markov birth-death process over twenty base pairs. Each transition rate is derived from Eyring transition-state theory and the Bell model, and combines three physical contributions, i.e., the torsional strain generated by the B-form to A-form helical conversion at the unwinding front, a base stacking correction that couples neighboring base pairs, and the allosteric work supplied by Cas9 conformational changes. We further derive the entropy production of the process, which is decomposed into activation, stacking, torsional, and allosteric terms. The resulting prediction model uses no external thermodynamic database and reaches Spearman correlations of 0.84 and 0.82 in two independent libraries of dCas9-sgRNA mismatch variants measured in vivo. The mismatch-type dependence is carried by one twist deviation and one pairing weight per type. Our model recovers the seed region sensitivity, the PAM-proximal activity gradient, and the moderate cost of dDrG mismatches, while isolating the high-activity double mismatch tail as the regime in which the present free-energy mapping is inadequate. The framework gives quantitative predictions on how DNA supercoiling and sequence context modulate binding affinity, and provides a mechanistic basis for sgRNA design.

authors.name: Yu Liu, Bing Miao

papers.title: Metal-Dielectric Bilayer Supported Nanoporous Silver Substrates for Ultrasensitive Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
papers.summary: Resolving the chemical footprint of molecules in analytes is of fundamental interest in biosensing and biomedical applications. Surface-enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) spectroscopy is a powerful tool for non-invasive molecule investigation, and there is a continuous effort to develop highly efficient SERS substrates that can be fabricated at low cost and tuned to the desired spectral range of investigation. Here, we show that the Raman signal of porous silver films can be significantly enhanced by integrating a thin dielectric layer and a metallic backreflector underneath the porous metal film. We call this architecture nanoporous metal on dielectric metal (NPMoDM) and show that it leads to much stronger near-field enhancement in the bulk of the film. Additionally, the spectral band of enhanced sensitivity can be tuned by the thickness of the dielectric layer within the visible spectral range. With rhodamine 6G and para-aminothiophenol as target analytes, we demonstrate SERS detection of substrates incubated with zeptomolar concentrations of the analyte, which corresponds to only few molecules present on a mm2 surface area. Our approach introduces a tunable and scalable (lithography-free) platform for ultrasensitive SERS applications, with a readily accessible surface for analyte functionalization.

authors.name: Maryam Naseer, Anastasiia Sapunova, Ali Douaki, Vincenzo Caligiuri, Silvia Dante, Denis Garoli, Roman Krahne

papers.title: Correlated chemical and displacive disorder in a lithium-rich disordered rocksalt revealed by electron diffuse scattering
papers.summary: Lithium transport in disordered rocksalt cathodes depends on local cation arrangements and atomic distortions that are hidden from average-structure analysis. Resolving both contributions experimentally remains challenging, particularly in powders where directional information is lost. Here, we use electron diffuse scattering and three-dimensional difference pair distribution function analysis (3D-{\Delta}PDF) to resolve occupational and displacive correlations in the model lithium-rich rocksalt Li{_2.5}TiO{_3}F{_0.5}. We identify an unusual combination of like-cation first-neighbour and unlike-cation second-neighbour preferences with correlated anion displacements towards Ti and accompanying cation displacements. A minimal pair-interaction model incorporating these displacements reproduces the principal diffuse-scattering and 3D-{\Delta}PDF features and improves agreement with powder-PDF measurements. The experimentally constrained cation configurations exhibit an above-random population of 0-TM lithium-migration environments. These results establish electron 3D-{\Delta}PDF as a route to constrain atomistic models incorporating chemical order and local relaxation, providing a foundation for assessing their combined influence on lithium migration in disordered rocksalt materials.

authors.name: Sam Y. Thompson (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark), Kristoffer A. H. St{\o}ckler (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark), Nikolaos Zacharakis (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark), Rebekka Klemmt (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark), Ella M. Schmidt (Faculty of Geosciences, MARUM and MAPEX, University of Bremen, Germany), Sandro Wieser (Institute of Materials Chemistry, TU Wien, Austria), Nico Unglert (Institute of Materials Chemistry, TU Wien, Austria), J{\o}rgen Skibsted (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark), Espen D. B{\o}jesen (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark), Georg K. H. Madsen (Institute of Materials Chemistry, TU Wien, Austria), Bo B. Iversen (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark), Dorthe B. Ravnsb{\ae}k (Center for Sustainable Energy Materials, Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, Denmark)

papers.title: Electric Field Assisted Charge Transfer Mediated Electronic Coupling in Ferromagnetic/Multiferroic Hetero-structure
papers.summary: The strongly coupled ferromagnet-multiferroic material could be a better alternative to complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS) based data storage device or rather lone multiferroic oxide materials because it offers the electric field controlled conductivity and large magnetisation at the interfaces, but choosing a proper system is still very much challenging. In the present scenario, an interionic charge transfer from Co ion to Fe ion via oxygen is observed at the interfacial region of LaCoO3 (LCO)/BiFeO3 (BFO) grown on SrTiO3 substrate, leading to induce multivalency in Co, Fe ion and also induces exchange biasing in the system. The charge transferring between Co and Fe ions gets further enhanced by electric biasing across the bilayer in the low temperature region, which affects the polarisation behaviour of BFO layer. This confirms the electronic coupling between the ferromagnetic LCO and the multiferroic BFO layers, useful for the making of voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) systems.

authors.name: Subho Saha, Sourav Chowdhury, Suryakanta Mondal, Kartick Biswas, Deepak Prajapat, Andrei Gloskovskii, Suresh Bharadwaj, Mukul Gupta, Pavan Nukala, Bhagwati Prasad, Ram Janay Choudhary

papers.title: Coupled Altermagnetic and Valley Physics in Monolayer VBiSe$_3$
papers.summary: The interplay of compensated magnetism, spin--orbit coupling (SOC), and valley degrees of freedom provides a promising route toward spin--valley control without conventional ferromagnetism. Here, using first-principles calculations combined with Wannier-based analysis, we reveal coupled altermagnetic and valley physics in monolayer VBiSe$_3$. In the absence of SOC, the compensated N\'eel antiferromagnetic state, whose opposite-spin V sublattices are related only by mirror operations, exhibits momentum-dependent spin splitting with a characteristic $i$-wave altermagnetic texture. Upon inclusion of SOC, the conduction-band states develop anisotropic Rashba-like spin splitting together with a sizable $K/K'$ valley splitting of about $112.2$~meV. Orbital analysis and an effective SOC Hamiltonian identify the hybridization between SOC-active Se-$p_{x,y}$ states and predominantly V-$d_{z^2}$ conduction-band states as an important microscopic origin of the valley splitting. The two valleys carry Berry curvature of the same sign but different magnitude, unlike the opposite-sign pattern of conventional valley Hall systems, so the large valley splitting, rather than a valley Hall effect, offers a possible route to valley-selective carrier occupation by gating. Moreover, a modest $-1\%$ biaxial compressive strain drives the system into a quasi-half-valley-metallic state with valley-polarized electrons and non-valley-polarized holes. These results establish monolayer VBiSe$_3$ as a promising platform for coupled altermagnetic, spin--orbit, and valley phenomena with strain-tunable electronic states.

authors.name: Divyanshi Tyagi, Saswata Bhattacharya

papers.title: Strain-induced non-trivial band topology and large magnetoresistance in epitaxial SrTaO$_3$ thin films
papers.summary: Epitaxial thin films of complex transition metal oxides constitute an ideal platform for realizing correlated topological phases through strain engineering of crystal symmetry and band topology. Here, we investigate the electronic transport properties and the band structure of the 5$d^1$ paramagnetic metal SrTaO$_3$ thin film under epitaxial compressive strain. The film exhibits a large non-saturating quasi-quadratic magnetoresistance (MR) and a nonlinear Hall effect characteristic of two-band transport, together with the field induced re-entrant metallic behavior. The violation of Kohler's scaling further corroborates the scattering from multiple bands. Semiclassical two-band analysis yields carrier densities and mobilities of the order $\sim 10^{21}~\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $\sim 10^{4}~\mathrm{cm^2 V^{-1} s^{-1}}$, respectively. The observed large mobility and unsaturated MR, indicates the presence of a non-trivial band structure. Consistent with this, results from density functional theory calculations and tight binding model studies reveal that the stable structure has an octahedral rotation $a^0a^0c^+$, where the non-symmorphic symmetry ensures the presence of topological nodal lines yielding finite Berry curvature in the vicinity of the Fermi level. Besides the nodal line, trivial electron and hole pockets exist near the Fermi level, contributing to electron transport. These findings establish that epitaxial strain drives SrTaO$_3$ into a nontrivial topological semimetal, a phase inaccessible in the bulk counterpart.

authors.name: Aditya Mehta, Soumyakanta Panda, Pratik Sahu, Amit Chauhan, Dibyajyoti Sahoo, Shwetha G Bhat, Rohit Soni, Goutam Tripathy, Niharika Mohapatra, B. R. K. Nanda, D. Samal

papers.title: The effect of isotopically-enriched 70Ge on the Raman scattering in Cr2Ge2Te6
papers.summary: The highest-energy A5g Raman-active vibrational mode in chromium germanium telluride (Cr2Ge2Te6, CGT) exhibits a unique lineshape comprising a series of remarkably narrow peaks. While this multiplet was attributed to the natural isotope distribution of germanium affecting Ge-Ge pseudo-molecular vibrations, direct evidence has been lacking. Here, we present a Raman spectroscopy study of CGT isotopically enriched with 70Ge to validate this hypothesis. Upon isotopic enrichment, both the E5g and A5g modes exhibit a pronounced blue-shift. At room temperature, the A5g peak undergoes significant narrowing, while low-temperature measurements reveal a single, well-defined line instead of the previously observed multiplet. These observations align precisely with density functional theory calculations, confirming that the multi-line profile originates from Ge isotope distribution. Our findings demonstrate that similar isotope-induced Raman splitting may occur in other structurally analogous layered tellurides containing Ge or Si.

authors.name: Grzegorz Krasucki, Katarzyna Olkowska-Pucko, Tomasz Wo\'zniak, Mihai I. Sturza, Holger Kohlmann, Adam Babi\'nski, Maciej R. Molas

papers.title: All-in-one Spintronic Sensory Neurons for Magnetic Edge Intelligence
papers.summary: Magnetic fields enable non-contact sensing through nonmagnetic materials, offering opportunities for magnetic edge intelligence in autonomous recognition, navigation, and control. However, directly converting magnetic stimuli into neural spikes for local neuromorphic processing remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate an all-in-one spintronic sensory neuron (SSN) based on spin-transfer-torque magnetic tunnel junctions (STT-MTJs) fabricated using a 40-nm magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) process. By exploiting magnetic-field-modulated stochastic switching, the SSN enables probability-based sensing with an electrically tunable sensitive field window, allowing adaptive operation across different magnetic-field ranges without structural modification. This tunability alleviates the fixed sensitivity-range constraint of conventional tunneling magnetoresistance sensing, providing an accessible sensing range of +/-40 mT with an average probability sensitivity of 2.91%/mT. Importantly, the same stochastic switching process directly transduces magnetic stimuli into binary spike trains, integrating magnetic sensing, nonlinear rate encoding, and spike generation within a single nanoscale device. The resulting sigmoidal spike-rate response enables magnetic-field encoding, experimentally validated using the Neural Engineering Framework. Using experimentally characterized device responses, a simulated 10 x 10 SSN array achieves 90.7% accuracy in contactless magnetic-trajectory recognition with optimized encoding, approaching the software baseline. These results establish a scalable, MRAM-compatible approach to unifying programmable magnetic sensing and neural encoding for sensor-native edge intelligence.

authors.name: Jiajia Jian, Bin Rong, Jiaxin Liu, Fangyi Zhao, Kai Li, Tao Huang, Xue Zhou, Xin Yue, Zeyu Ma, Xuefeng Zheng, Weidong Zhang, Jian Fu Zhang, Yumeng Yang, Zheng Chai

papers.title: Two-dimensional Thyristor
papers.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer a viable platform for next-generation electronics beyond sub-3 nm nodes, yet essential nonlinear circuit elements, such as thyristors, remain unexplored on atomically thin platforms. Here, we report an atomically thin reconfigurable electro-optical thyristor based on a lateral WSe2-MoSe2-WSe2-MoSe2 PNPN heterostructure, directly grown via sequential edge epitaxy. Unlike single-junction 2D diodes, this multijunction architecture exhibits thyristor-like nonlinear switching, including forward blocking, abrupt snapback, bistability, and electrical latching. The device exhibits a forward-blocking voltage of 183 V, corresponding to a critical electric field of 1 MV/cm. Under open-gate conditions, avalanche-assisted carrier multiplication and regenerative feedback are associated with a sharp forward-voltage drop of 175 V, a pronounced current surge, and an ultralow holding voltage. Gate-pulse modulation and temperature-dependent measurements indicate avalanche-assisted thyristor operation and latching behavior. This 2D lateral heterostructure enables a new route to nonlinear and bistable switching, latching, ultralow standby power, and adaptive logic, opening the way for reconfigurable 2D electronics and photonic integrated circuits.

authors.name: Purbasha Ray, Rupali Verma, Biswajeet Nayak, Suman Kumar Chakraborty, Mayank Shrivastava, Prasana Kumar Sahoo

papers.title: Geometry-controlled clogging and transport mechanisms in confined Y-junctions
papers.summary: We investigate transport and clogging of hard particles in a confined symmetric Y-junction using off-lattice Monte Carlo simulations. The geometry is controlled by the channel width w and a truncation parameter s that modifies the inner vertex. The flow probability exhibits a sharp sigmoidal crossover, defining a characteristic width wc that depends non-monotonically on s. This non-monotonic behavior persists under variations of the transverse Monte Carlo step, although the absolute values of wc change. Microscopic analysis reveals two distinct blocking mechanisms: single-particle obstruction at small truncations and collective arch-like structures at larger truncations. Residence-time statistics and particle-order inversions provide additional evidence of this change in transport dynamics. Our results demonstrate that local modifications of junction geometry can strongly affect clogging and particle transport, even in a minimal model with excluded-volume interactions only.

authors.name: Horacio Javier Diaz Carrera, Diego J. P\'erez-Morelo, Sergio J. Manzi, Paulo M. Centres

papers.title: Janus Asymmetry Unlocks Rashba Spintronics and Chiral Phononics in Two-Dimensional Carbo-Chalcogenides
papers.summary: Spintronics and chiral phononics offer complementary routes for nanoscale control, yet realizing both functionalities within a common two-dimensional platform remains challenging. Here, using extensive first-principles calculations, we show that Janus asymmetry simultaneously drives both effects in transition-metal carbo-chalcogenides (JTMCCs) along two chemically distinct routes, through either chalcogen or transition-metal substitution. Remarkably, both Janus routes yield giant Rashba responses, with $\alpha_\mathrm{R}\approx2$ eV {\AA} in Ta$_2$CSSe and NbTaCS$_2$, exceeding those reported for Mo/W-based Janus transition-metal dichalcogenides. Furthermore, Janus asymmetry lifts the degeneracy of opposite-chirality phonons, producing splittings as large as $\approx28$ cm$^{-1}$. More strikingly, asymmetry generates chiral carbon vibrations that were achiral in the centrosymmetric parent compounds, with splittings reaching $\approx8$ cm$^{-1}$. Finally, we show external electric fields tunability over Rashba strength and chiral-phonon splittings, providing a common control knob for electronic spin and lattice angular momentum. Our work offers a unified strategy for realizing spintronic and chiral phononic in two-dimensional materials.

authors.name: Valentina Barreca, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Giovanni Cantele, Ludovica Zullo

papers.title: Perfect Spin-to-Charge Signal Conversion via Inverse Spin Hall Effect in a Superconductor
papers.summary: Spin-to-charge conversion is central to spintronics, but conventional spin Hall mechanisms are intrinsically limited by the small spin Hall angle. Here we show that superconductivity can overcome this limitation and enable near-unity spin-to-charge signal conversion. We consider a nonlocal spin-valve geometry in which a spin accumulation is injected into a superconductor and converted into a transverse charge signal through the inverse spin Hall effect. In the superconducting state, the strongly suppressed quasiparticle conductance below the gap allows the resulting charge imbalance to generate a voltage comparable to the injected spin bias, despite a small spin Hall angle. We derive the full nonequilibrium response including finite spectral broadening and finite temperature, and propose temperature and spin-bias-dependent measurements of the detector voltage to test our predictions.

authors.name: Rodrigo de las Heras, Ilya V. Tokatly, F. Sebastian Bergeret

papers.title: Gallium at germanium surfaces: links to superconducting films and correlated adatom lattices
papers.summary: Epitaxial films grown on Ge(001) show that germanium hyperdoped with substitutional Ga is superconducting. In earlier implanted films, Ga-rich precipitates obscured the origin of the superconductivity. This review examines the sites Ga occupies on Ge(001) and Ge(111) and how it enters the growing film. The Ga fraction expected from the growth fluxes is 17.9\%, yet the distribution of Ga among lattice sites is unknown. Comparisons include Ga on Si(001) and Si(111),In, Sn, Pb, Sb and P on Ge(001), and elemental and two-dimensional Ga. Where its surface coordination has been established, Ga has three bonds, whereas substitutional Ga in the films is fourfold coordinated and acts as an acceptor. Scanning tunnelling microscopy and X-ray standing waves have assigned Ga sites on Ge(111), but the dilute Ga site on Ge(001), where the films are grown, has yet to be measured. On Ge(111), Ga in the substrate may supply holes to the correlated Sn adatom lattice, as B supplies holes to the superconducting Sn lattice on Si(111). Whether Ga can supply holes depends on where it sits and whether it has three or four neighbours. On both surfaces, element-specific measurements and calculations comparing adsorption with substitution could settle the remaining site assignments.

authors.name: Peter Jacobson

papers.title: Altermagnetism of MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 in a wurtzite-based crystal structure
papers.summary: Based on symmetry analysis, the Pna2_1 wurtzite-based crystal structure with Mn as a magnetic group-II element, MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 belong to the class of altermagnets because spin-up and spin-down Mn in the unit cell are related by rotation or mirror plane type operations rather than inversion or translation. Spin polarized density functional theory calculations and quasiparticle self-consistent (QS) GW calculations support the symmetry analysis and identify the lowest-energy spin configuration as Pna'2_1' in agreement with neutron diffraction data. The altermagnetic band splittings allowed for the three different antiferromagnetic ordering patterns are reported and symmetry analyzed. Additionally, spin wave dispersions, chiral magnon spltting, and Neel temperature estimates from the mean-field and random-phase approximations are provided, as well as calculations of the optical dielectric function using the Bethe-Salpeter Equation method. MnSiN2 exhibits both Wannier-type excitons with N-p to Si-s transition character and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons with hole on N-p and electron on Mn-d orbital character.

authors.name: Ilteris K. Turan, Jonathan Agrinya, Walter R. L. Lambrecht

papers.title: Interaction-driven ordering of multiple pseudospins and anomalous Hall metals in Bernal-stacked graphene
papers.summary: Recent observations of anomalous Hall states in Bernal-stacked tetralayer graphene raise a fundamental question: How do electron-electron interactions organize multiple low-energy pseudospin sectors within each spin-valley flavor? Within the Hartree-Fock approximation, we analyze interaction-driven pseudospin ordering and spin-valley polarization as functions of displacement field and carrier density. We find a rich phase diagram shaped by the interplay between the two pseudospin doublets, including mixed flavor orders at charge neutrality and anomalous Hall metals upon doping. In particular, we identify topological states with $\sigma_{xy} \approx 6e^{2}/h$, consistent with recent experimental observations. Our results highlight the central role of multiple pseudospin doublets in the interaction-driven phases of even-layer Bernal multilayers.

authors.name: Jeonghyeon Suh, Kyungjin Shin, Hongki Min

papers.title: Statistical mechanics of noisy collisions in active matter: Dyson-Landau theory
papers.summary: Active systems and other coarse-grained descriptions are often modeled by generalized dynamics, effective equations of motion that are not bound by the constraints of genuinely microscopic physics. In particular, these equations are generally stochastic on the smallest resolved scale. This poses a challenge to first-principles statistical physics, which usually derives emergent noise on larger scales from deterministic interactions. Here, we show how to systematically incorporate microscopic noise into kinetic theory in the limit of weak noise, i.e., high activity. By means of a Dyson expansion of the noisy free propagator, we derive the leading correction to the Landau kinetic equation for weakly interacting systems. We find that the common practice of combining a deterministic collision integral with the diffusive terms of the Fokker--Planck equation is the correct leading order. For dry aligning active matter, however, the corrections are non-analytic in the noise strength, as nearly parallel particles interact for arbitrarily long times. For noise that acts only during interactions, a minimal model of stochastic interactions, noise and collisions do not decouple: the leading corrections are odd in the coupling strength, partly logarithmically enhanced, and amount to an orientation-dependent effective noise strength. Agent-based simulations confirm the predicted dependence on the sign of the coupling. Even in this minimal model, the effect of noise on collisions can thus not be inferred from symmetry alone.

authors.name: Horst-Holger Boltz, Max-Robin Schultz, Thomas Ihle

papers.title: Dirac-like bands and weak-field transverse transport in ABA trilayer graphene
papers.summary: The low-energy electronic structure of ABA trilayer graphene is composed of light and heavy electron branches, which can be altered by an out-of-plane displacement field. Here, we show that, depending on the values of Slonczewski-Weiss-McClure parameters, a displacement field can inflict a band edge inversion, for which we identify the inversion conditions. This inversion is accompanied by a reversal of Berry curvature and giant topological magnetic moments at the band edges. In a weak perpendicular magnetic field, those topological magnetic moments produce valley splitting, giving rise to distinct anomalous transverse electrical and thermoelectric responses. These features offer a potential route to detecting the band inversion and constraining several of the least established tight-binding parameters, such as the on-site energy shift for the dimer pair of carbons $\Delta^\prime$ and the next neighbour hopping parameters $\gamma_2$ and $\gamma_5$.

authors.name: Agustin Montemurro, Fujia Lu, Ellis R. Huntley, Vladimir Fal'ko

papers.title: Generalized dielectric-dependent hybrid functional combining Gaussian and Yukawa screening
papers.summary: We develop a generalized Coulomb-attenuated method (GCAM) for dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals that combines Gaussian and Yukawa-type screening functions to provide an accurate representation of the random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function. Through systematic fitting to RPA dielectric functions of semiconductors and insulators, and to the Lindhard dielectric function of the homogeneous electron gas, we demonstrate that GCAM significantly reduces errors in the model dielectric function across the full momentum range. However, despite this improved physical description of screening, band gap calculations reveal that GCAM yields larger errors compared to experiment than previous CAM approaches for wide-gap materials, but smaller errors for most narrow-gap materials. This counterintuitive result demonstrates that the success of CAM stems not purely from physical reasons, but also from a partial cancellation of errors. In contrast, for optical absorption spectra calculated within a model Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, GCAM systematically outperforms CAM, showing better agreement with the reference spectra obtained with the diagonal RPA screening in both peak positions and relative intensities. Our findings reveal the important role of error cancellation in dielectric-dependent hybrid functionals.

authors.name: Alexey Tal, Fabien Tran, Wei Chen, Stefan Riemelmoser, Alfredo Pasquarello

papers.title: Magneto-ARPES as a direct probe of Berry Curvature and the Orbital Magnetic Moment
papers.summary: The Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment are central to the understanding of electronic transport phenomena such as the anomalous Hall effect, yet measuring these quantities directly with momentum resolution remains experimentally challenging. Here we show that angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements in a weak magnetic field (magneto-ARPES) provide a direct route to both quantities. We develop an analytic theory of photoemission in a weak magnetic field and show that, for any material, the first-order change in photoemission intensity is directly proportional to both the Berry curvature and the orbital magnetic moment, even in the presence of self-energy effects. For linearly polarised light, the matrix elements are unchanged to first order in the field, so the intensity change directly reflects these quantities. Using monolayer WSe$_2$ as an example, we show how both quantities can be extracted in a typical experiment. This finding thus points to magneto-ARPES as a general route for measuring the momentum-resolved Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment in quantum materials.

authors.name: Seohyun Kong, Bernd Braunecker, Luke C. Rhodes

papers.title: Interface-Engineered Piezoelectricity and Electromechanical Coupling in Two-Dimensional van der Waals Heterostructures
papers.summary: Interfaces between dissimilar two-dimensional (2D) materials provide a route to engineer electromechanical responses that are not intrinsic to the individual constituent layers. Here, we use high-throughput density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate 461 van der Waals heterostructures constructed from 57 2D monolayers and establish a materials-design framework linking work-function mismatch, interfacial charge redistribution, dipole formation, and strain-dependent electromechanical response. We find that heterostructure formation generates out-of-plane interfacial dipoles via charge redistribution between the constituent layers, while biaxial in-plane strain systematically modulates them. The resulting heterostructures exhibit two distinct regimes: metallic interfaces with strain-tunable interfacial dipoles and semiconducting heterostructures with well-defined piezoelectric responses. For the latter, Berry-phase (BP) calculations independently validate the charge-density-difference (CDD) approach, which is generally applicable to all representative systems, with piezoelectric coefficients calculated via two methods agreeing to within 10%. Among 24 selected heterostructures, effective biaxial interfacial electromechanical coefficients reach 83.35 pCm-1 . These results demonstrate that the interface can serve as the active element governing electromechanical coupling and provide a computationally guided strategy for designing strain-tunable out-of-plane electromechanical responses in 2D van der Waals heterostructures.

authors.name: Shivanand Yadav, Raihan Ahammed, Umer Ali, B. S. Bhadoria, Yogesh S. Chauhan, Amit Agarwal, Somnath Bhowmick

papers.title: Terahertz detection of magnon chirality in polycrystalline CsCuCl$_3$
papers.summary: In antiferromagnets, the handedness of magnon precession is usually measured on single crystals. In a pressed pellet of the chiral helimagnet CsCuCl$_3$, whose grains carry both structural handednesses and all orientations, we found that, from 5 to 7 T, the sub-terahertz magnon absorbs one circular polarization more than 20 times as strongly as the other, which rules out precession about each grain's own axis. Spin-wave theory attributes this to the Zeeman frequency, here two to four times the exchange-enhanced gap, which locks the precession axis to the field in every grain. Magnon chirality in antiferromagnets is thus accessible without a single crystal.

authors.name: Juan S. Rodr\'iguez-Hern\'andez, Gabriel F. Freitas, Nicolas M. Kawahala, Rafael S. Freitas, Felix G. G. Hernandez

papers.title: Self-consistent Floquet theory of steady-state ordering in driven open systems
papers.summary: Periodically driven open systems have quasienergy bands whose steady-state occupations are set by the drive and reservoir. We formulate a self-consistent Floquet spectral theory of electronic ordering in the weak-reservoir-coupling limit, expressing the nonlinear mean-field equation and the particle-hole response in terms of quasienergies, steady-state occupations, and harmonic matrix elements that account for micromotion. We illustrate the theory in the square-lattice Hubbard model and show how the drive produces `dynamical nesting' conditions and how Floquet resonances produce \textit{hysteretic} responses due to multiple self-consistent solutions. Interestingly, we find that the hysteresis branches exhibit distinct Floquet topologies. Away from half-filling, we find that the combination of drive-induced detuning of the van Hove saddle points and the micromotion leads to the onset of switching between competing incommensurate orders.

authors.name: Srinjoy Ghosh (IUB), Babak Seradjeh (IUB), Arijit Kundu

papers.title: Fast-erasure energy-cost lower bound and its first-order correction under restricted control
papers.summary: Determining the minimum work required for information erasure is central to understanding the energetic limits of fast and reliable information processing. In the fast-erasure limit, we derive an explicit expression for this minimum work in a one-dimensional overdamped isothermal system with control restricted to linear and quadratic additions to a reference potential. For symmetric initial distributions at fixed mobility, the minimum work scales inversely with the erasure duration, with a prefactor determined solely by the second moment and a quantile associated with the target success probability. We further derive the leading finite-time correction at a prescribed success probability and verify both analytical predictions numerically. These results provide an analytical benchmark for fast erasure under restricted control, connecting a universal leading cost with finite-time corrections that account for the detailed form of the memory potential.

authors.name: Yihang Cai (Department of Physics and Shenzhen Research Institute, Xiamen University, Xiamen, China), Yirong Jiang (Department of Physics and Shenzhen Research Institute, Xiamen University, Xiamen, China), Chenlong Huang (Department of Physics and Shenzhen Research Institute, Xiamen University, Xiamen, China), Yue Liu (Center for Gravitational Physics and Quantum Information, Yukawa Institute for Theoretical Physics, Kyoto University, Kyoto, Japan), Dahai He (Department of Physics and Shenzhen Research Institute, Xiamen University, Xiamen, China)

papers.title: LeIFF: A localized-electron and ion force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics
papers.summary: Classical and machine-learned interatomic potentials enable large-scale simulations by replacing electronic structure with an effective energy surface for nuclear motion. This excludes electronic dynamics, electronic excitation and energy exchange between electrons and ions. First-principles electron dynamics can describe these processes, but its computational cost restricts system sizes and simulation times. Electron force fields offer an intermediate description by treating electrons as semiclassical dynamical particles interacting with ions. We introduce the localized-electron and ion force field (LeIFF), a compact physical model for both ground state bonding and excited electron dynamics. Valence electrons are represented by spin-labeled spherical charge distributions with dynamical centers and widths. The energy combines analytic electronic kinetic, Coulomb, and dispersion terms with spline-interpolated short-range interactions fitted to a large molecular data set. The resulting energy surface describes a variety of ground state properties across diverse bonding environments and charge states. It also provides a qualitative description of electronic behavior away from equilibrium. It shows improved robustness, accuracy, and transferability relative to earlier electron force-fields. Without any solid-state training, the same model describes dielectric screening and collective electronic response in silicon. LeIFF thus opens a route to large-scale simulations of nonadiabatic processes in molecules and solids, combining chemical bonding and nonequilibrium electronic motion within a common physical framework.

authors.name: Anthony Mannino, Isidro Losada, Simon Divilov, Michelle Fritz, Younos Hashem, Ashraf Mrabet, Paula Mori S\'anchez, Javier Junquera, Mariv\'i Fern\'andez-Serra, Jose M. Soler

papers.title: Quantum and classical transport in the underscreened Kondo lattice
papers.summary: We investigate quantum effects in high-spin Kondo-lattice transport as resistivity approaches the classical spin-disorder limit. Using dynamical mean-field theory and the numerical renormalization group, we calculate resistivity, the Seebeck coefficient, and optical conductivity for the paramagnetic single-channel Kondo lattice away from half filling. At intermediate temperatures, the resistivity for large local spin $S$ approaches the double-exchange plateau. Thermopower retains a positive quantum excess even where resistivity is nearly classical. The excess arises from the transport kernel's particle-hole asymmetry. Even the full Kelvin approximation, often accurate for incoherent correlated metals, captures only part of it. Incomplete Kondo screening leaves residual moments and leads to singular Fermi-liquid behavior at low temperatures. For $S=1$, the apparent power-law resistivity is consistent with a $1/\ln^2(T_\rho/T)$ asymptote. Above the Kondo scale $T_K$, weak-coupling resistivity follows $1/\ln^2(T/T_K)$. Above the band and exchange scales, the charge susceptibility decreases as $1/T$, while the effective diffusion constant becomes nearly temperature independent, resulting in linear resistivity. A many-body coherent-potential approximation accounts for the spin dependence of the linear coefficient without adjustable parameters.

authors.name: Leo Pintar, Don Rolih, Rok \v{Z}itko

papers.title: Anomalous Field-induced Coherence beyond Single-ion Kondo Physics
papers.summary: The emergence of coherent heavy quasiparticles in Kondo lattices is generally accompanied by a reduction in electrical resistivity at low temperatures. However, certain strongly correlated metals exhibit anomalously large resistivities that persist to very low temperatures, raising fundamental questions about the mechanisms governing charge transport. Here, we report an unusual magnetic field-induced evolution of electronic transport and thermodynamic properties in a Ce-based heavy fermion compound, Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$. At zero field, Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$ undergoes a magnetic transition at $T$$_{0}$ = 0.45 K and exhibits a strongly enhanced low temperature specific heat coefficient, reaching $C$/$T$ = 2.2 J/mol$_{Ce}$-K$^{2}$, but no discernible coherence in its electrical resistivity. Remarkably, applying a magnetic field produces a large negative magnetoresistance and restores coherent metallic behavior, characterized by low-temperature $T$$^2$ resistivity. Although the field dependence of the electronic specific heat coefficient can be described phenomenologically within a single-ion Kondo framework, the same description fails to account for the strong suppression of the residual resistivity and the overall magnetoresistance. These results point to an additional field-sensitive scattering contribution beyond conventional single-ion Kondo physics. The striking resemblance to the long-standing anomalous magnetotransport behavior of UBe$_{13}$, without the complications introduced by superconductivity, establishes Ce$_{2}$Rh$_{3}$Ga$_{5}$ as a platform for investigating the microscopic origin of anomalous scattering and field-induced coherent transport in strongly correlated electron systems.

authors.name: Arushi, Konstantin Semeniuk, Manuel Brando, Javier F. Landaeta, Elena Hassinger, Christoph Geibel

papers.title: A Fractional Chern Semimetal: Exact Wavefunction and Conformal Criticality
papers.summary: Unlike fractional quantum Hall states in uniform Landau levels, fractional Chern insulators can host dispersive anyon bands, raising the question of what happens when the anyon gap closes. We construct an exact finite-bond-dimension tensor-network state for a fractional Chern semimetal by Gutzwiller projecting a critical parton state. This state exhibits divergent correlation lengths in charged sectors but a fractionally quantized many-body Chern number of $1/3$. Although it has one electron per unit cell, its modular $S$ and $T$ matrices and entanglement spectrum match those of the $\nu=1/3$ Laughlin state. We identify a $(1+1)$--dimensional $U(3)_1\times SU(3)_1$ conformal field theory (CFT) governing the wavefunction norm in the infrared, an unexpected result for a state with $U(1)_3$ topology. The $SU(3)_1$ sector is a nonlinear sigma model whose Wess--Zumino level and kinetic stiffness are determined by the parton Chern number and Fubini--Study metric, respectively. Under renormalization, it flows to the conformal fixed point, with an initial distance to this fixed point controlled by the idealness of parton quantum geometry. Favorable geometry enables precise agreement with CFT predictions even on narrow cylinders.

authors.name: Fa-Jie Wang, Yang Qi, Zhi-Da Song

papers.title: Quantum-geometry-tuned Mott transition and emergent heavy fermions in a topological flat band
papers.summary: A flat band with a nonzero Chern number has no localized Wannier orbitals, which raises the question of whether Mott physics is still possible. We place a Hubbard interaction $U$ on coherent orbitals, which are localized but overcomplete, and develop a single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for this model. Within the flat band alone, DMFT reproduces the experimentally observed cascade and inverse-compressibility sawtooth without invoking Dirac revival or remote-band electrons. At nonzero integer filling we find an insulator-to-metal transition tuned by $s^2$, the fraction of the Brillouin zone that carries the Berry curvature. For $N_f=8$ flavors the Mott transition at $\nu=-2$ occurs at $s^2_c\approx0.025$, where the top of the lower Hubbard band reaches the Fermi level and the local moments are Kondo screened, forming a heavy Fermi liquid (HFL). The HFL extends to the hole-doped side, $\nu=-2-x$, but above the small Kondo temperature $T_K$ the state is an incoherent bad metal without a Fermi surface. At low temperature, an anti-Hund's coupling $J_A\sim0.1U$ replaces the HFL with a pseudogap metal that has a small Fermi surface and is dominated by spin-polaron excitations at small $x$. We propose this pseudogap metal as the parent state of superconductivity in TBG. The framework may also be applied to other topological bands, such as those of twisted WSe$_2$.

authors.name: Ya-Hui Zhang

papers.title: Burgers equation from non-thermal stationary states in nearly-integrable gases
papers.summary: When a gas of particles interacts with much a larger reservoir the density dynamics on large scales is typically governed by diffusion. We study this paradigmatic problem for weakly coupled integrable systems and show that this picture gets altered, when transport is investigated on top of long-lived non-thermal states. Remarkably, for states non-invariant under parity we find Burgers equation arising in the hydrodynamic limit. We explicitly compute the diffusion constant and nonlinear advective coefficient of the Burgers equation using a variant of the Chapman-Enskog theory. We find an excellent agreement between our theory and numerical simulations of a simplified model of stochastic two-body collisions. Our conclusions are based only on Galilean invariance, existence of a small system-bath coupling parameter and a small momentum exchange between the system and the bath particles during two-body scattering.

authors.name: Pawe{\l} Lisiak, Maciej {\L}ebek, Mi{\l}osz Panfil

papers.title: From dynamic strain aging to Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi dynamics of propagating Portevin--Le Chatelier bands
papers.summary: Type-A Portevin--Le Chatelier bands are propagating strain localizations whose velocity exhibits strong intermittent fluctuations. We derive a coarse-grained connection between the dynamic-strain-aging model of H\"ahner and Rizzi and the Alessandro--Beatrice--Bertotti--Montorsi (ABBM) mean-field model of avalanche dynamics. A propagating band is reduced to a single phase coordinate while retaining the elastic feedback of the tensile machine. This feedback generates the increasing drive and restoring terms of the ABBM description. A finite-time adjoint calculation determines the stress mobility of the band and is checked independently by direct stress continuation. The mobility is approximately proportional to the hardening parameter, whereas the band speed scales approximately as its square root. Short-range heterogeneity in the plastic strain deposited by the band is converted by the global machine feedback into a Brownian effective force. The resulting reduction provides a microscopic route from dynamic strain aging to ABBM-like avalanche dynamics of propagating PLC bands.

authors.name: Tero M\"akinen, Mikko J. Alava

papers.title: Geometric foundations of mesoscopic nucleation theory: commutativity of kinetic and probabilistic reduction for the Dean-Kawasaki equation
papers.summary: The reduction of a stochastic field equation to a few degrees of freedom is a central problem in many areas of physics, applied mathematics and engineering. In this work we present two routes for the dimensional reduction of conservative stochastic partial differential equations of Dean-Kawasaki type. To our knowledge, such reductions have always been carried out at the level of the trajectories, i.e. on Dean's equation, and never at the level of the probability distribution, i.e. on Kawasaki's equation.
