Our exact-Hessian interior-point solves are up to 27 times faster than those with the sound log-sum-exp robustness in CasADi and IPOPT.

authors.name: Sai Sandeep Damera, Ryan Matheu, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

papers.title: Feedback Completion Certificates for Repeated Dwell Tasks with Time Windows
papers.summary: An inspection robot may owe several measurements at the same station, each with a different window in which a dwell can begin. We ask what a feedback controller must retain about earlier visits to guarantee all remaining deadlines under bounded disturbances. For a common spatial predicate and dwell length, removing redundant windows orders the remaining obligations by both endpoints. On every history without an expired obligation, the served windows form a suffix. One boundary and one capped run length therefore preserve the future satisfaction of the original task. On a verified library of branching motion primitives we use this state to recover a feedback policy. For one task type a scalar threshold per run length suffices, with work linear in the number of listed branches per time layer for fixed dwell. Multiple types require a joint recursion. On a quadrotor inspection library the threshold sweep reduced the cost of constructing a reusable full-domain policy, while a sparse Boolean baseline answered a single initial query faster. In a two-station MuJoCo patrol, three task-aware filters all met every window in twelve paired runs each. Of eight initially certified runs, the completion filter retained the certificate in all eight, compared with three for safety-only filtering.

authors.name: Jiaxun Sun, Yuqi Yang, Senlan Yao, Hengyu Xue, Hongming Fu, Zhimu Zhou

papers.title: Performance Evaluation of Nonlinear Model Predictive and Sliding Mode Controllers on a 4-Cable Spatial CSPR in Simscape
papers.summary: This paper offers a comprehensive comparative study between Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) and Sliding Mode Control (SMC) applied to a spatial Cable-Suspended Parallel Robot (CSPR) actuated by four cables. The robot is modeled in two parallel ways: (i) via an analytical dynamic model with included cable elasticity and frictional losses, and (ii) in MATLAB Simscape Multibody, capturing realistic physical effects. Both controllers are implemented under identical reference trajectories, system constraints, and tuning strategies. Our results show that NMPC achieves superior tracking accuracy and stronger disturbance rejection compared to SMC, but at the cost of higher computational demand. Moreover, both controllers were tested on an analytical model of the robot and a Simscape model. The close agreement between the two, for both control schemes, confirms the accuracy of the analytical formulation and its consistency with the physics-based simulation. The study highlights the value of physics-based simulation as a complementary tool for validating advanced controllers under realistic conditions, and demonstrates that NMPC offers superior performance for the studied high-precision, constrained CSPR.

authors.name: Erfun Bayat Sarmadi, Ali Asadi, Moosa Ayati

papers.title: Context-Aware Proactive Self-Adaptation: A Two-Layer Model Predictive Control Approach
papers.summary: In self-adaptive software systems, the role of context is paramount, especially for proactive self-adaptation. Current research, however, does not fully explore context's impact, for example on priorities of the requirements. To address this gap, we introduce a novel contextual goal model to capture these factors and their influence on the system. Using this, we propose a two-layer control mechanism with a context-aware model predictive control to achieve proactive adaptation for the software system and adaptation for the controller itself. By contextual prediction and a more accurate system model, our approach utilizes model predictive control to facilitate timely and efficient system adaptations, improving both performance and adaptability. Meanwhile, we perform requirement adaptation to update the contextual goal model, which in turn updates the objective function and constraints of the controller. Our experimental evaluations across two scenarios demonstrate the significant benefits of our approach in enhancing system performance.

authors.name: Zhengyin Chen, Jialong Li, Nianyu Li, Wenpin Jiao, Eunsuk Kang

papers.title: Model-Assisted Probability of Detection Studies for Image-Based Human Inspection
papers.summary: Establishing a probability of detection (POD) curve is important for assessing the reliability of components in aging systems. Traditional POD studies rely on physical specimens containing representative flaws and human inspectors who record detection results, making such studies costly. This paper demonstrates how appropriately validated physics-based simulation can substantially reduce, and in suitable applications potentially replace, physical POD experiments. We use XRSIM, an X-ray radiographic simulator, to generate weld images containing cracks of varying size, morphology, and location. Flaw characteristics, locations, and the number of flaws per image were randomized, with images containing zero to three flaws. Each simulated flaw is treated as an observational unit contributing flaw-level hit-miss responses. To capture human inspection variability, the images were presented in random order to five inspectors, each of whom inspected the images twice. The resulting data were analyzed using a repeated-measures binary-regression model accounting for flaw-to-flaw, inspector-to-inspector, flaw/inspector-combination, and inspection-to-inspection variability. Bayesian inference was used to estimate the population-mean POD curve, inspector-specific POD curves, and associated statistical uncertainty. Results show that flaw-to-flaw variability dominates, with appreciable differences among inspectors. The study provides a framework for combining physics-based image simulation with controlled human inspection to estimate POD while reducing the experimental burden of physical specimen fabrication.

authors.name: Qizheng Xia, William Q. Meeker, Joseph N. Gray, Qing Li

papers.title: Value function based Reward shaping for safety in quadrupeds
papers.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has progressed from simple control tasks to complex real-world challenges with large state spaces. While RL excels in these tasks, training time remains a limitation. Reward shaping is a popular solution, but existing methods often rely on value functions, which face scalability issues. This paper presents a novel safety-oriented reward-shaping framework inspired by barrier functions, offering simplicity and ease of implementation across various environments and tasks. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed reward formulations, we conduct simulation experiments on the Unitree Go1 quadruped robot in Isaacgym. The policy was better than the existing baselines and reduced safety violations from 27% to 0.1% without almost any compromise on the performance.

authors.name: Janani S K, Manan Tayal, Shishir N. Y Kolathaya

papers.title: Robust Lateral String Stability and Error Attenuation for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons
papers.summary: Keeping an entire vehicle platoon close to its planned path is essential for navigating road boundaries and obstacles safely. Followers may rely on predecessor information for lateral guidance, which couples their lateral dynamics and allows errors to propagate downstream. This paper develops a robust lateral string stability framework to study this propagation and achieve downstream error attenuation in heterogeneous platoons under varying longitudinal motion and local perturbations. Arc-length-based feedback linearization gives each vehicle the same nominal lateral error dynamics, with parameter uncertainty and external disturbances represented as local perturbations. We define robust $\mathcal L_2$ lateral string stability in terms of platoon-length-uniform error bounds and derive a sufficient condition for achieving it. Furthermore, we show that the same condition guarantees platoon-length-uniform $\mathcal L_\infty$ error bounds. For the considered control formulations, predecessor tracking (PT) can accumulate lateral errors, whereas desired-path tracking (DT) prevents this accumulation. We propose a learn-from-predecessor (LFP) strategy with explicit gains for downstream error attenuation and characterize how intervehicle perturbation differences limit this attenuation. Simulations validate the theoretical findings under vehicle heterogeneity, varying longitudinal motion, and local perturbations.

authors.name: Sixu Li, Swaroop Darbha, Yang Zhou

papers.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

authors.name: Rui Dai, Shunpeng Yang, Zhen Fu, Maolin Lei, Jiaqi Song, Hua Chen, Nikos Tsagarakis

papers.title: Adaptive Beamforming Using One-Bit Data Samples for Covariance Estimation
papers.summary: The use of one-bit quantized complex-valued data samples enables efficient distributed computation of an array data covariance. This reduced complexity covariance estimate can be used for adaptive beamforming, but requires careful diagonal loading and results in lower performance compared to a full-precision approach. Two main approaches are presented: a covariance matrix built out of complex one-bit data samples, and a ``hybrid'' cross-covariance between the one-bit data and the full precision data. Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) estimates for the associated population and finite-sample matrices are derived and compared to the full precision results using tools from linear algebra and statistics. Many strong, well-separated interferers with low overlap with the signal of interest are assumed throughout, none of them dominant.

authors.name: Aaron Kogan, Swaroop Appadwedula

papers.title: Combatting Fraud in Artificial Currency Based Government Benefits Programs
papers.summary: Benefits programs are policy tools for providing targeted aid, such as food assistance or transit subsidies. However, these programs are often susceptible to misreporting fraud, wherein users misreport private attributes to obtain excess aid. To address this problem, we introduce a two-stage audit game between an administrator and users in which the administrator can audit users at a cost and levy fines on misreporting users, with player payoff structures designed to reflect real-world benefits programs. We show that the administrator's least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibria can be computed tractably via linear programming and derive prescriptive bounds on the administrator's excess payments and users' misreporting probability as functions of audit costs and fines. We further establish that, with an appropriately chosen budget level, the reduction in excess payments in any least-favorable Bayesian Stackelberg equilibrium offsets the audit budget required to sustain the mechanism, yielding total costs no greater than those of a baseline without an auditing authority, which we corroborate through a case study of Washington D.C.'s federal transit benefits program.

authors.name: Devansh Jalota, Matthew Tsao, Marco Pavone

papers.title: Range-Only Dynamic Output Feedback Controller for Safe and Secure Target Circumnavigation
papers.summary: The safety and security of robotic systems are paramount when navigating hostile targets. This paper addresses the problem of circumnavigating an unknown target by a unicycle robot while ensuring it maintains a desired safe distance and remains within the sensing region around the target throughout its motion. The proposed controller design is based on a composite Lyapunov framework consisting of: (i) a quadratic Lyapunov function characterizing the target-circumnavigation objective, and (ii) a barrier Lyapunov function-based potential term enforcing the prescribed safety and sensing constraints. A notable feature of the proposed approach is that it relies exclusively on local range measurements between the robot and the target, achieved through a dynamic output-feedback controller that treats the range as the only measurable output. Using Lyapunov-based stability analysis together with an equivalent autonomous reformulation of the closed-loop dynamics, we establish asymptotic stability of the desired equilibrium while guaranteeing satisfaction of the prescribed safety and sensing constraints under the proposed controllers. Restrictive bounds on the post-design signals are also derived, and numerical simulations are presented to validate the proposed approach.

authors.name: Anand Singh, Anoop Jain

papers.title: Prescribed Time Higher Order Control Lyapunov-Barrier Functions
papers.summary: We propose a framework based on Repeated-Root Prescribed Time Higher-Order Control Lyapunov- Barrier Functions (RR-Pxt-HOCL-BF) that guarantees convergence to a safe set/ goal set within user-specified time. Unlike conventional Higher-Order Control Barrier Functions, which does not provide any guarantee on reaching the safe set if the system is initially not in safe set, the proposed method enforces convergence within a prescribed time horizon. This is achieved through a structured differential constraint derived from repeated roots of the characteristic polynomial, leading to closed-form polynomial solutions that ensure convergence at the desired time. Analytical conditions for forward invariance and prescribed-time reachability are derived, with explicit formulations for second-order systems. The approach is validated on an acceleration-controlled unicycle and an inverted pendulum and compared with existing HOCBF methods. Simulation results demonstrate reliable convergence within the desired time horizon, even in scenarios where conventional approaches fail.

authors.name: Janani S K, Manan Tayal, Shishir Kolathaya

papers.title: Stable and Fair Benefit Allocation in Mixed-Energy Truck Platooning: A Coalitional Game Approach
papers.summary: This paper addresses the benefit allocation in a mixed-energy truck platoon composed of fuel-powered and electric trucks. The interactions among trucks during platoon formation are modeled as a coalitional game with transferable utility. We first design a stable payoff allocation scheme that accounts for truck heterogeneity in energy savings and platoon roles (leader or follower), establishing core-stability conditions to ensure that no subset of trucks has an incentive to deviate for greater benefit. To enhance payoff fairness, we then propose a closed-form, Shapley value-based allocation approach that is computationally efficient and independent of the platoon size. Sufficient conditions under which the allocation is both fair and core-stable are provided. In scenarios where the Shapley value falls outside the core, we develop an alternative allocation based on the stable payoff that minimizes the mean relative deviation from the Shapley value while preserving core stability. This deviation is further proved to be upper-bounded by $1$, showing a favorable trade-off between stability and fairness. Finally, extensive numerical studies validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in facilitating stable, equitable, and sustainable cooperation in mixed-energy truck platooning.

authors.name: Ting Bai, Xinfeng Ru, Karl Henrik Johansson, Jonas M{\aa}rtensson, Andreas A. Malikopoulos

papers.title: Chirp-Permuted AFDM: A Versatile and Multifunctional Waveform for 6G
papers.summary: We present a novel multicarrier waveform, termed chirp-permuted affine frequency division multiplexing (CP-AFDM), which introduces a unique chirp-permutation domain on top of the chirp subcarriers of the conventional AFDM. Rigorous analysis of the signal model and waveform properties demonstrates that the proposed CP-AFDM waveform preserves all core characteristics of affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) - including robustness to doubly-dispersive channels, peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC)-enabling full delay-Doppler representation - while introducing a new degree-of-freedom without any loss of these properties. Given this, by exploiting the vast chirp-permutation domain, two selected exemplary multifunctional applications are presented: an index modulation (IM) technique over the permutation domain which achieves significant spectral efficiency gains, and a physical-layer security scheme that ensures practically perfect security through permutation-based keying, without requiring additional transmit energy or signaling over-head. In all, these characteristics establish CP-AFDM as a highly attractive candidate for emerging sixth generation (6G) use cases demanding reliability, sensing-awareness, and multifunctionality.

authors.name: Hyeon Seok Rou, Hanvit Kim, Sunwoo Kim, Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu

papers.title: Transferring the driveshaft inertia to the grid via the DC-link in MV drive systems
papers.summary: This paper investigates a control approach that renders the driveshaft inertia completely available on the grid side and enhances the fault ride-through behavior of medium-voltage (MV) drive systems. Two main contributions are presented. First, we show how the rotational inertia of the driveline shaft can be synchronously coupled to the grid through a modification of the speed control reference signal and through an adapted DC-link control strategy. For the latter, we pursue two alternatives: one based on conventional cascaded control and another based on synchronous machine (SM) model matching. Second, we demonstrate that both the standard phase-locked loop (PLL) and the matching control approach can be interpreted, via the ray-circle complementarity, as feedback optimization schemes with distinct steady-state maps. This perspective allows us to revisit matching control, reveal its embedded PLL, highlight its current-limiting and tracking capabilities, and provide an extensive simulation study.

authors.name: Catalin Arghir, Pieder J\"org, Silvia Mastellone

papers.title: Sparse Neural Approximations for Bilevel Adversarial Problems in Power Grids
papers.summary: The adversarial worst-case load shedding (AWLS) problem is pivotal for identifying critical contingencies under line outages. It is naturally cast as a bilevel program: the upper level simulates an attacker determining worst-case line failures, and the lower level corresponds to the defender's generator redispatch operations. Conventional techniques using optimality conditions render the bilevel, mixed-integer formulation computationally prohibitive due to the combinatorial number of topologies and the nonconvexity of AC power flow constraints. To address these challenges, we develop a novel single-level optimal value-function (OVF) reformulation and further leverage a data-driven neural network (NN) surrogate of the follower's optimal value. To ensure physical realizability, we embed the trained surrogate in a physics-constrained NN (PCNN) formulation that couples the OVF inequality with (relaxed) AC feasibility, yielding a mixed-integer convex model amenable to off-the-shelf solvers. To achieve scalability, we learn a sparse, area-partitioned NN via spectral clustering; the resulting block-sparse architecture scales essentially linearly with system size while preserving accuracy. Notably, our approach produces near-optimal worst-case failures and generalizes across loading conditions and unseen topologies, enabling rapid online recomputation. Numerical experiments on the IEEE 14- and 118-bus systems demonstrate the method's scalability and solution quality for large-scale contingency analysis, with an average optimality gap of 5.8% compared to conventional methods, while maintaining computation times under one minute.

authors.name: Young-ho Cho, Harsha Nagarajan, Deepjyoti Deka, Hao Zhu

papers.title: Self-Aligned Resonant Beams for Adaptive Beamforming in 6G IoT
papers.summary: The integration of communication, sensing, and wireless power transfer (WPT) is becoming an important direction for 6G Internet of Things (IoT). However, conventional beamforming typically depends on channel state information (CSI) acquisition, beam training, and active beam scanning, which can introduce substantial overhead in dynamic or passive-device scenarios. This article reviews the radio-frequency resonant beam system (RF-RBS) as a physical-layer self-alignment mechanism for reducing this dependence. By using retro-directive antenna arrays (RAAs) at the transceivers, RF-RBS can form a cyclic electromagnetic feedback loop in which phase-conjugated waves reinforce a dominant round-trip path. This mechanism enables self-aligned, high-gain beam formation under suitable loop-gain, propagation, and hardware conditions. We discuss the RF-RBS architecture, its operating principles, and its potential roles in WPT, self-aligned communication, and passive positioning. We also examine implementation challenges, including analog hardware integration, multi-user interference, limited coverage, and line-of-sight (LoS) dependence, and outline its potential value for latency-sensitive 6G IoT scenarios such as unmanned systems and industrial automation.

authors.name: Yixuan Guo, Mingliang Xiong, Qingwen Liu, Wen Fang

papers.title: Enhancing time-frequency resolution with optimal transport and barycentric fusion of multiple spectrogram
papers.summary: Time-frequency representations, such as the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), are fundamental tools for analyzing non-stationary signals. However, their ability to achieve sharp localization in both time and frequency is inherently limited by the Gabor-Heisenberg uncertainty principle. In this paper, we address this limitation by introducing a method to generate super-resolution spectrograms through the fusion of two or more spectrograms with varying resolutions. Specifically, we compute the super-resolution spectrogram as the barycenter of input spectrograms using optimal transport (OT) divergences. Our method does not require the input spectrograms to share the same time-frequency grid. The input spectrograms can be computed using any STFT parameters, and the resulting super-resolution spectrogram can be defined on an arbitrary user-specified grid. We explore various OT divergences based on different transportation costs. Notably, we introduce a novel transportation cost that preserves time-frequency geometry while significantly reducing computational complexity compared to standard Wasserstein barycenters. We adopt the unbalanced OT framework and derive a new block majorization-minimization algorithm for efficient barycenter computation. We validate the proposed method on controlled synthetic signals and recorded speech using both quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The results show that our approach combines the best localization properties of the input spectrograms while maintaining a smooth energy distribution, and preserving computational efficiency.

authors.name: David Valdivia, Elsa Cazelles, C\'edric F\'evotte

papers.title: Extracting Exact Lie Derivatives Without Backpropagation: A Dual Compiler for Neural Control Barrier Functions
papers.summary: A safety filter based on a neural control barrier function (CBF) evaluates, at each control cycle, the trained network and its Lie derivatives along the system vector fields. This paper presents a compiler whose emitted C++ code performs this evaluation on embedded processors by forward-mode differentiation with dual numbers. The derivatives are exact in the sense of automatic differentiation, which means that they are free of truncation error and subject to floating-point roundoff. One evaluation of the network in this arithmetic, called a dual pass, returns the barrier value and its Lie derivative along one vector field, and an extension to hyper-dual numbers returns the second-order Lie derivatives of CBFs of relative degree two. Apart from scalar variables, the memory that a dual pass writes is at most four floating-point numbers per neuron of the widest layer and does not depend on the network depth. On an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, we compare the emitted code with code for reverse-mode differentiation (i.e., backpropagation), which is also generated before the program runs and uses fixed-size arrays. In three experiments, the reverse-mode code has a lower execution time than the dual and hyper-dual passes executed one after the other. For single-input networks, the measurements do not establish such an ordering between the reverse-mode code and a variant of the dual pass that propagates the real part once. For networks of increasing depth, the working memory of the dual passes is constant, whereas that of the reverse-mode code increases. While the emitted code runs, no dynamic allocation is recorded. We report the maximum observed execution time of the complete filter step, which includes the dynamics and a breakpoint search for the quadratic program with input bounds and one affine constraint. The compiler and the experiments are open source.

authors.name: Mohammadreza Kamaldar

papers.title: Control and Cryptosystem Co-Design for Encrypted Nonlinear Multi-Agent Coordination
papers.summary: A cloud that must not see the agents' states can steer them on data encrypted under CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic. Its stored estimate admits only so many multiplications before a refresh that costs time and error, and every decrypted command is flooded with noise of a mandated size, constraints no controller designed in exact arithmetic meets. For networked agents with polynomial dynamics, we prove one closed-loop bound tying the controller and the cryptosystem in both directions. If the exact loop contracts on a region, the encrypted loop stays within a certified radius of it, set by the per-cycle and refresh errors, the refresh interval, the flooding and the delay. The errors and the bound's probability are derived from the library's circuits, not measured. Inverted, the bound turns the tolerance and a failure-probability target into the refresh interval, and with it the precision, security parameters and period. Conversely, costs shape the realization: a tracing backend tallies any pipeline's operations before a ciphertext exists, and evaluating the prediction about each agent's reference holds the released error below its sixteen-agent level. A full satellite-train mission encrypted at 128-bit security ran inside its certified radius, and the certificate holds across six graphs and at 32, 64 and 128 agents. Security enters the design twice, in time and precision. The cryptosystem is therefore part of the control design, derived from the same specification and certified by the same guarantee as the controller.

authors.name: Sai Sandeep Damera, Maria Charitidou, Asim Zoulkarni, John S. Baras

papers.title: From Tokens to Energy Flexibility: Quantization-Enabled Demand Response for Data Centers with LLM Inference Workloads
papers.summary: The rapid growth of large language model (LLM) inference is creating significant data-center loads that face increasing energy-management challenges under tightening grid conditions and demand response (DR) requirements. Conventional data-center energy management mainly relies on temporal and spatial workload shifting and campus-level energy asset scheduling, but it usually treats LLM inference demand as an aggregate load. As a result, these approaches fail to exploit the internal characteristics of LLM serving and therefore overlook the flexibility offered by LLM-specific techniques such as model quantization. To unlock this flexibility, this paper proposes a quantization-enabled energy management framework for grid-responsive LLM inference data centers. First, a quantization-to-power model is established to map each model--quantization configuration to a compact set of dispatchable parameters. Second, a two-stage quantization-enabled DR model is developed to account for model instance switching, request routing, and precision selection. Third, a multi-campus co-optimization method is introduced for DR participation by integrating grid-side electricity and carbon signals with the quantization-enabled DR model. Case studies show that the proposed framework reduces total data-center operating cost by 31.8% without curtailing served token volume, validating model quantization as an effective flexibility lever for grid-responsive LLM data-center energy management.

authors.name: Bojun Du, Xiaoyi Fan, Ershun Du, Long Chen, Jianpei Han, Qingchun Hou, Ning Zhang, Chongqing Kang

papers.title: MSU-Bench: Towards Speaker-Centric Understanding in Conversational Multi-Speaker Scenarios
papers.summary: Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) is moving from task-specific pipelines toward large audio language models (LALMs) that generate natural-language responses. However, existing speech benchmarks mainly focus on single-speaker settings or isolated subtasks, leaving speaker-centric understanding in realistic multi-speaker conversations insufficiently evaluated. We introduce MSU-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark for multi-speaker conversational understanding, covering 16 speaker-centric tasks and 2,300 QA instances in a two-tier framework from speaker grounding to dialogue reasoning. We build a Gemini-assisted annotation and QA generation pipeline with human-in-the-loop verification, achieving high QA validity and strong agreement between human answers and verified labels. We further analyze speaker-referencing schemes and diagnostic error types to reveal bottlenecks in speaker grounding and reasoning. Experiments reveal clear gaps across model families, with closed-source systems leading overall but all models still facing challenges in complex speaker grounding and multi-speaker reasoning. The benchmark annotations, metadata, and evaluation scripts will be available at the GitHub repository: https://github.com/ASLP-lab/MSU-Bench.

authors.name: Zhaokai Sun, Shuai Wang, Zhennan Lin, Chengyou Wang, Dehui Gao, Yuang Cao, Chunjiang He, Pan Zhou, Lei Xie

papers.title: Dynamic Constraint Reconstruction Based Control Barrier Functions for Safety-Critical Control of High-Dimensional Manipulators
papers.summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide formal safety guarantees for constrained nonlinear systems, but their effectiveness relies on accurate system dynamics. In high-dimensional manipulators subject to unknown disturbances and model uncertainties, fixed safety constraints constructed from nominal dynamics may become inconsistent with the actual system behavior, leading to safety degradation or excessive conservatism. This paper proposes a dynamic constraint reconstruction based control barrier function (DCR-CBF) framework for safety-critical control of disturbed robotic manipulators. An extended state observer is employed to estimate lumped disturbances online, and the estimated disturbance is incorporated into high-order control barrier functions to reconstruct safety constraints according to the estimated true dynamics. To address estimation inaccuracies, a safety margin is introduced, and a sufficient condition is derived to guarantee forward invariance under bounded estimation errors. Simulation studies on a 4-DOF excavation manipulator demonstrate that the proposed DCR-CBF method achieves zero safety violation under strong unknown disturbances while significantly improving trajectory-tracking performance compared with standard and robust CBF methods.

authors.name: Bingsheng Zhang, Shen Wang, Qiang Wang, Muguo Du, Donghai Shi, Xiaofeng Tao

papers.title: Non-Square UPA-Enabled XL-MIMO Systems: Anisotropic Near-Field Characterization, Fundamental Limits, and Channel Estimation
papers.summary: Extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) is crucial for next-generation communication systems. In practice, the deployment of non-square uniform planar arrays (UPAs) fundamentally alters wavefront characteristics and induces anisotropic beamfocusing capability along different axes due to the aperture disparity originating from the non-square array geometry. To fully uncover the performance impact of such non-square geometry and thus unleash the potential of the non-square UPAs, we investigate the anisotropic near-field characteristics, fundamental limits, and channel estimation for non-square UPA-enabled XL-MIMO systems. First, we derive the effective beamfocusing distances for the long and short axes of the array. Interestingly, the radiation space of a non-square UPA can be partitioned into three regions, i.e., the fully near-field, the anisotropic near-field, and the far-field regions, and the anisotropic region asymptotically dominates the overall near-field space as the array aspect ratio increases. Then, the asymptotic effective degree of freedom for non-square UPA-enabled XL-MIMO systems is provided, which reveals that distance-domain multiplexing is governed by the long-axis aperture in the large array aspect ratio regime. Furthermore, the closed-form Cramer-Rao bound for distance estimation and the three-dimensional (3D) position error bound (PEB) are derived to reveal the geometry-induced performance trade-offs among distance, azimuth, and elevation estimation, based on which the optimal array aspect ratio that minimizes the 3D PEB is determined. Finally, by exploiting the anisotropic wavefront properties, we design a 3D anisotropic near-field codebook to facilitate low-complexity channel estimation for non-square UPAs. Numerical results validate that the proposed codebook achieves comparable accuracy to the 3D polar-domain codebook at reduced complexity.

authors.name: Yilong Liu, Xi Yang, Jing Xu, Jun Zhang, Shi jin

papers.title: A Closed-Loop Thermal Dynamic Model for AI Data Center Cooling Load Simulation
papers.summary: Accurate modeling and simulation of cooling electricity demand is essential for characterizing AI data center loads, but time-synchronized operational measurements are scarce. Constant coefficient-of-performance models can oversimplify cooling behavior, while detailed thermal state-space models are cumbersome to use. This paper proposes a closed-loop simulation framework that couples a linear thermal dynamic model with deadband-based control to capture nonlinear cooling behaviors. The framework is validated against operational data from the Marconi100 supercomputer. Compared with the baseline, the proposed model reduces the mean absolute error from 95.80 to 23.52 kW and the root-mean-square error from 109.79 to 29.91 kW. The statistical evaluation further shows improved reproduction of daily peak demand and intraday variability. The framework provides a computationally tractable approach to generate physically interpretable cooling load profiles for power system studies.

authors.name: Cletus Ngwerume, Lang Tong, Chee-Wooi Ten, Yi Hu

papers.title: Data-Driven Domain of Attraction Estimation via Convergent Koopman-Zubov Approximation
papers.summary: This paper considers the problem of estimating the domain of attraction (DOA) of an asymptotically stable equilibrium, which is characterized by the support of a Zubov function. A Zubov--Koopman operator, i.e., a Koopman operator weighted by an accumulated cost, is defined and shown to be exponentially stable on a space of functions that vanish at the origin at least linearly (whenever the cost is sufficiently large away from the equilibrium). Consequently, the Zubov function is the unique invariant element on this space augmented with constants. Hence, by learning the Zubov--Koopman operator on a suitable reproducing kernel Hilbert space from snapshot data, an explicit kernel expression of the estimated Zubov function and an explicit DOA estimation algorithm are obtained. Such an estimation procedure is a highly efficient convex, closed-form regularized least-squares one, with a provable error bound proportional to the distance from the equilibrium and decreases with the fill distance of the sample. Numerical examples illustrate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the approach in comparison with existing neural network and dictionary-based methods.

authors.name: Wentao Tang

papers.title: Time-Window Noise2Noise: Self-Supervised Blind Denoising of Mechanical Vibration and Impact Signals
papers.summary: Vibration and impact measurements in mechanical systems are invariably corrupted by noise, which degrades every quantity derived from them, such as modal parameters and contact forces. Classical filters rely on assumptions about the noise or the signal, and linear filters cannot remove the noise that shares the frequency band of the structural response. This work presents Time-Window Noise2Noise (TWN2N), a self-supervised method for blind denoising of signals produced by deterministic mechanical systems. The method requires neither a clean reference signal nor paired noisy observations, nor a measured noise variance or distribution: by reconstructing each time instant from its temporal neighborhood while masking the instant itself, a compact autoencoder-based network is encouraged to exploit the coherent temporal and multichannel structure of the measurement rather than the noise. The formulation requires no model of the system and is assessed on two benchmarks with exactly known ground truth: the impulse response of a linear 3-degree-of-freedom system and a nonlinear Hunt-Crossley impact. Over repeated realizations, TWN2N exceeds a zero-phase low-pass filter at low and moderate input signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and gives the largest gain inside the structural band, which a linear filter largely preserves, among the Savitzky-Golay and wavelet references; the advantage vanishes at high input SNR and under brown noise. The benefit propagates to identification: the damping ratio of the weakest mode, overestimated several-fold on the raw signals, is recovered close to its reference value after denoising.

authors.name: Vinicius S. Vianna, Tiago H. Machado, Ilmar F. Santos

papers.title: Advanced 400G-SerDes Modulations and Equalizers for GPU Cluster in AI Era
papers.summary: High-speed GPU cluster interconnects are evolving from 200 to 400 Gbps to meet the growing computing demands of artificial intelligence. We investigate high-order modulation and advanced equalization for 400 Gbps interconnects. Theoretical bit error rate (BER) expressions for 4/8-ary pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) and approximate expressions for six PAM6 formats generated from 32-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (32QAM) are derived. In additive white Gaussian noise, PAM6 generated by framed-cross 32QAM achieves the best BER performance among the PAM6 formats. PAM6 and PAM8 incur peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) penalties of approximately 4.2 and 7.2 dB, respectively, relative to PAM4 at the KP4 forward error correction (KP4-FEC) limit. Simulations compare PAM4, PAM6, and PAM8 at a line rate of 440 Gbps (net rate of 400G) under different bandwidth limitations. As bandwidth becomes more constrained, bandwidth requirements increasingly dominate performance over noise tolerance. PAM4 requires the lowest PSNR to reach the KP4-FEC limit in mildly bandwidth-limited channels, whereas PAM6 performs best under moderate limitations. PAM8 offers a significant advantage under severe limitations because of its lower bandwidth requirement and reduced susceptibility to high-frequency attenuation. With maximum likelihood sequence estimation, PAM6 and PAM8 reach the KP4-FEC limit under all evaluated channel conditions, while PAM6 requires a lower PSNR in most channels, highlighting its potential for 400G-SerDes systems.

authors.name: Sheng Chen, Zhengxiang Cheng, Ji Zhou, Haide Wang, Mengqi Guo, Weiping Liu, Liangchuan Li, Xiangjun Xin

papers.title: Optimal Allocation of Grid-Forming Frequency Shaping Control
papers.summary: Various inverter-based control strategies have been proposed to improve frequency security for power systems with high renewable penetration. Among them, the grid-forming frequency shaping control is particularly promising due to its ability to shape the post-contingency aggregate system frequency dynamics into first-order with prescribed rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and steady-state frequency deviation. Moreover, the shaped aggregate dynamics depends on the harmonic sum of all inverter transfer functions rather than on their distribution. In light of this, here we explore how to allocate shaping control resources to minimize the transient control effort needed to achieve ideal coherent dynamics. We formulate it as a constrained optimization problem by tackling two main difficulties. First, we make the squared $\mathcal{H}_2$ norm legitimate quantification of transient control cost under step power imbalances through a system transformation. Second, we simplify the $s$-domain constraint for Nadir elimination into a standard constraint that is easy to implement in optimization. The resulting non-convex optimization problem can be solved by existing successive convexification method. The effectiveness of the allocation has been verified on the modified Icelandic Power Network test case.

authors.name: Zhaomin Lyu, Ding Zhang, Yan Jiang

papers.title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
papers.summary: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

authors.name: Yunseob Tae, Jeongjae Lee, Songnam Hong

papers.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
papers.summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.

authors.name: Simon Hellmann, Leander Lerch, Terrance Wilms, Moritz Reumsch\"ussel, Alberto Meola, F\'elix Delory, Steffi Knorn, Stefan Streif, S\"oren Weinrich

papers.title: Flux Compensation as a Prerequisite for Temporal CT: Per-Bundle Cram\'er-Rao Floors and Estimators That Reach Them
papers.summary: In Temporal CT (TCT) each detector reading sums the photons of up to three rays. Earlier work measured the resulting per-bundle cost as a Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), using one incident count $N_0$ for all rays and a learned prior trained on one patient; this paper removes both restrictions. N$_0$FC ($N_0$ flux compensation), a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, approximately equalizes each bundle's detected flux. SNN2 is a bias-corrected, box-projected Gauss-Newton Poisson likelihood iteration. V8c, a neural network trained on 19 patients, corrects SNN2. T2bp, an empirical-Bayes post-processor without trained weights, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior from the patient's own bundles. On 23 non-test volumes, N$_0$FC lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cram\'er-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under a flat-fluence baseline to 3.3-6.3 at 35-62% of the baseline's incident photons, near the equal-attenuation 13/3 and 1.4-1.7 times below GE-type bow-ties. For bundles with $X_2<6$ (83%), SNN2 attains this floor (median MSE ratio 1.02); holding air paths at zero, a box-constrained maximum likelihood estimate lowers the ratio to 0.88, and T2bp$\circ$SNN2 to 0.89 (0.74-1.26); T2bp's per-patient prior adds measurably only in the deeper bins (a median 12-29% over all bins). T2bp$\circ$SNN2 beats T2bp$\circ$V8c on three of four N$_0$FC test cells, but trails or ties it on the four N$_0$FC validation volumes. V8c beats SNN2 in distribution under baseline acquisition, gains at most 9% under N$_0$FC (losing 14% on the largest in-distribution test patient), and fails on a patient acquired outside its corpus's exposure rule. Flux compensation, chiefly the bow-tie, is a prerequisite; classical estimation attains the resulting limit. The remaining 3- to 6-fold gap to single-source CT at equal fluence, and the high-attenuation tail, are targets for inter-bundle priors.

authors.name: Guy M Besson

papers.title: QIEN: Quantum-Inspired Energy-Neutral UAV Trajectory for WPT-Enabled Industrial HRLLC
papers.summary: This paper introduces Quantum-Inspired Energy-Neutral (QIEN) UAV Trajectory for WPT-Enabled Industrial HRLLC, a novel framework for mobility-integrated trajectory and resource optimization in solar-powered uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) relay systems supporting autonomous mining robots in post-disaster environments. We formulate a mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) that jointly optimizes UAV trajectory, finite blocklength allocation, transmit power, and wireless power transfer (WPT) over discrete time horizons to maximize aggregate data throughput. The system operates under strict extreme hyper-reliable low-latency communication (HRLLC) constraints, energy sustainability requirements via solar harvesting, and continuous robot power delivery. To solve this large-scale optimization problem, QIEN employs a hybrid Cooperative Quantum-behaved Particle Swarm Optimization (Co-QPSO) algorithm using quantum tunneling mechanisms and a heterogeneous swarm architecture. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed QIEN framework significantly outperforms benchmark algorithms, achieving successful convergence while maintaining energy-neutral operation and satisfying all reliability, power, and mobility constraints.

authors.name: Ali Ranjha, Georges Kaddoum, Halim Yanikomeroglu

papers.title: Stability and Safety of Grid-Following Inverters in Weak Grids via Barrier Function Control
papers.summary: This paper proposes a barrier control approach for the safe regulation of grid-following voltage-source converters (VSC), operating in weak grid conditions. The proposed controller aims to enhance the transient performance and synchronization properties of the VSC, providing frequency and current limiting guarantees by employing smooth control barrier functions. First, a dynamic model is derived that includes the dynamic state interactions that are omitted in quasi-steady-state approaches, revealing the destabilizing elements both during transient and steady-state performance. Then, it is analytically proven that the proposed control law guarantees frequency limitation and inner current evolution in prescribed safety regions, while counteracting the destabilizing strong coupling between PCC voltage and injected current. In addition, sufficient conditions are formulated that guarantee the stability of the closed-loop system with respect to desired operating points. The theoretic results are verified in simulations of case studies operating in varying grid strength.

authors.name: Grigoris Michos, Christos K. Verginis

papers.title: Anomalous Sound Detection Using Separation Features and Paired-Mixture Representation Learning
papers.summary: Acoustic monitoring often relies on normal machine recordings with limited information about operating conditions. We first train a separator to estimate a normal target recording from a mixture of machine sounds. With the separator frozen, we train regional attention on pairs of mixtures that share the target recording and contain different interfering sounds. Differences between the paired embeddings provide the covariance estimate for correction before cosine nearest-neighbor scoring. We evaluate the method on the development-test recordings of seven machine types in the 2022 Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events challenge. We summarize detection performance by the harmonic mean of source-domain, target-domain, and partial areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve. On the original recordings, a separator trained without external pre-training achieved a three-run mean of 64.56%, close to the 64.87% obtained by distillation from a pre-trained audio transformer. Using the same transformer as a frozen encoder gave a mean of 64.88%. With competing machine sounds added to the test recordings, both implementations outperformed distillation at all seven tested interference levels.

authors.name: Seunghyeon Shin, Seokjin Lee

papers.title: Learn Locally, Extend Globally: Koopman Eigenfunctions and the Basin of Attraction
papers.summary: Koopman eigenfunctions associated with the Jacobian eigenvalues of a stable equilibrium are Lyapunov functions defined exactly on its basin of attraction. We turn this into a computational procedure for power systems. Eigenfunctions estimated by extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD) are written as functions of the state, made to vanish at the equilibrium by centering the lifted variable $\cos\delta$, and verified on a grid with the model: two Lyapunov candidates from the EDMD spectrum certify up to 66\% of the basin of a single-machine infinite-bus system from data in the linear region. The Koopman semigroup property then extends the EDMD-Lie eigenfunction to the whole basin, recovered at the grid resolution with its isostables and isochrons.

authors.name: Marcos Netto, Aditya Kale, Bukunmi Gabriel Odunlami, Andrey Bernstein

papers.title: StreamingDPD: A 1.28-GSa/s Instantaneous-Power-Gated Depthwise TCN Accelerator for Real-Time 320-MHz Digital Predistortion
papers.summary: State feedback between successive samples limits the streaming throughput of recurrent neural networks for digital predistortion (DPD). We present StreamingDPD, an accelerator that processes 320-MHz signals at 1.28 GSa/s. Its 207-parameter instantaneous-power-gated depthwise temporal convolutional network (IPG-DWTCN) uses $|x[n]|^2$ to gate feature channels and causal dilated depthwise convolutions to model power amplifier memory. The network maps to a spatially unrolled fixed-point pipeline with shift-based quadratic activations and layer-wise mixed precision, sustaining one complex sample per cycle per lane. Its algorithmic cost is 554 floating-point operations per complex sample, 30.1% fewer than the recurrent baseline with the best linearization performance. In RF playback measurements on three power amplifiers driven by 40- to 320-MHz Wi-Fi 6/7 and 5G NR waveforms, IPG-DWTCN achieves the lowest mean adjacent-channel power ratio (ACPR) and ranks first or ties for first in mean error vector magnitude (EVM) against five neural baselines of comparable size. Four-lane FPGA hardware-in-the-loop tests on a 320-MHz 4096-QAM Wi-Fi 7 waveform achieve -45.82 dBc ACPR and -42.94 dB EVM at 1.28 GSa/s. At the same sample rate, post-layout evaluation of a single-lane 12-nm FinFET ASIC yields a 0.10 mm$^2$ core, a 52-cycle (40.63 ns) latency, and an estimated typical-corner power of 142.21 mW (111.10 pJ/sample). Relative to the prior 22-nm recurrent DPD ASIC, the design provides 5.1 times the throughput at about one-seventh the energy per sample.

authors.name: Yizhuo Wu, Xinling Wang, Chang Gao

papers.title: Trade-off Between Airspace and Channel Capacity for Low-altitude Wireless Network
papers.summary: Communication-serviceable capacity for low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks depends on both spatial occupancy and wireless quality of service (QoS). This paper formulates a communication-feasible occupancy-planning model that maps candidate-grid assignments to concurrent beam loads and per-user rates under fixed-stream and fixed-beam power. With fixed effective noise, per-beam QoS screening determines maximum admission, and an exact dynamic program maximizes aggregate spectral efficiency at that fixed admission. Signal-level simulations validate the SINR expressions, while an explicit-array model examines load-dependent inter-beam leakage. The dynamic program is globally optimal for the separable integer problem, but that guarantee does not extend to the coupled problem. Equal-time orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and ideal-SIC non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) are evaluated through the same local beam reduction under fixed effective noise and fixed per-beam power.

authors.name: Xinyang Zhang, Yuanhao Cui, Xiaotong Zhao, Ningyan Guo, Christos Masouros, Dong In Kim

papers.title: Adaptive Filtering With Reduced Computational Complexity Using SOPOT Arithmetic
papers.summary: Implementing finite impulse response (FIR) adaptive filters by employing the sums of signed-powers-of-two (SOPOT) arithmetic may lead to simpler hardware and consequently reduced power consumption. In this paper, one evaluates the effects of SOPOT arithmetic on the adaptive filter's recursion algorithms. The filters' coefficients and algorithms' underlying variables are fully operated using SOPOT arithmetic in the whole iterative process. More specifically, one evaluates convergence rate, numerical stability, and accuracy since using few signed-powers-of-two (SPT) terms propagates numerical errors during the adaptive cycle that may impair the algorithm behavior. The SOPOT approximations are obtained through the technique known as Matching Pursuits with Generalized Bit-Plane (MPGBP) algorithm, with notable cost-performance trade-off and low computational complexity. Results are provided for the Least-Mean-Squares (LMS), the Normalized Least-Mean-Squares (NLMS) and the Recursive-Least-Squares (RLS) algorithms, considering adaptive filters employed for system identification and change detection.

authors.name: Luiz F. da S. Coelho, Lisandro Lovisolo, Michel P. Tcheou

papers.title: Motion-Sickness-Aware Vehicle Control via DKUC-Based Inverse Design and Iterative Feedback Tuning
papers.summary: Tuning existing vehicle controllers for motion-sickness reduction requires a desired vehicle response that reflects physiological comfort. The six-degree-of-freedom subjective vertical conflict (6DoF-SVC) model can evaluate sensory conflict induced by vehicle motion, but it does not directly provide a target motion for controller design. This paper proposes a 2-step framework to construct such a reference. First, a target SVC trajectory is generated from the baseline response by limiting conflict peaks while imposing a minimum activity level. Second, a lifted linear model identified using Deep KoopmanU with Control (DKUC) is inverted to map the target SVC trajectory to a regularized reference expressed in vehicle-acceleration and angular-velocity coordinates. The resulting motion reference is then used in an Iterative Feedback Tuning (IFT)-style procedure for fixed-structure PI and LQR controllers. In the considered simulation scenario, the selected SVC target reduces the sequence norm by 6.95% relative to the baseline. Controller tuning with reduced response models decreases the regularized PI and LQR objectives by 49.5% and 32.3%, respectively. These results show that a nonlinear physiological comfort objective can be converted into a practical motion reference for tuning fixed-structure vehicle controllers.

authors.name: Uta Kawakami, Kenji Sawada

papers.title: Decision Fusion in Wireless Networks: A Tutorial and Survey of Classical and Learning-Based Methods
papers.summary: Decision fusion combines local decisions from distributed sensors to support reliable detection of phenomena in wireless networks. The effectiveness of decision fusion depends on sensing accuracy, reporting-channel reliability, and available communications and computation resources. This article surveys decision-fusion techniques for wireless sensor networks and emerging communication systems, bringing together their theoretical foundations and practical implementation requirements. We review network architectures and hard, soft, and quantized reporting strategies, and examine statistical, learning-based, game-theoretic, and heuristic fusion approaches. Advanced fusion techniques, including relay-aware combining, link-adaptive regeneration, branch selection, and likelihood approximations, are discussed with emphasis on their assumptions, information requirements, and limitations. The survey examines tradeoffs among detection performance, computational complexity, communications overhead, energy consumption, and latency. The tradeoffs are considered across representative sensing applications and emerging technologies, including massive machine-type communication, ultra-reliable low-latency communication, uncrewed aerial vehicle-assisted networks, and the massive Internet of Things. The reviewed literature highlights the importance of jointly considering sensing quality, reporting reliability, and fusion processing when selecting a suitable strategy. Finally, we identify research directions in resource-aware optimization, uncertainty calibration, and robust learning-based fusion under heterogeneous data, missing reports, and changing wireless conditions. Particular attention is given to convergence, generalization, and the costs of training and inference.

authors.name: Mohamed Abdelkader, Arafat Al-Dweik, Sobia Jangsher, Hamad Yahya, Shihab Jimaa

papers.title: FGAS: Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation
papers.summary: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) has made high-fidelity generated audio widely available across the Internet, driving the advancement of audio steganography. Benefiting from advances in deep learning, current audio steganography schemes are mainly based on encoder-decoder network architectures. While these methods achieve promising perceptual quality, they typically require network pre-training, and maintaining anti-steganalysis performance at high payloads remains challenging. To address these issues, we propose Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation (FGAS). Adversarial perturbations carrying a secret message are embedded into the cover audio to generate stego audio. The sender and receiver independently construct the same fixed decoder from a shared architecture and initialization key, avoiding the transfer of trained decoder parameters. In FGAS, we propose an Audio Adversarial Perturbation Generation (A2PG) strategy with an optional robust extension and design a lightweight fixed decoder. The fixed decoder guarantees reliable extraction of the hidden message, while adversarial perturbations are optimized to keep the stego audio perceptually and statistically close to the cover audio, thereby improving anti-steganalysis performance. The experimental results show that FGAS significantly improves stego audio quality, achieving an average PSNR gain of over 10 dB compared to SOTA methods. Furthermore, FGAS demonstrates strong robustness against common audio processing attacks. Moreover, FGAS exhibits superior anti-steganalysis performance across different relative payloads; under high-capacity embedding, it achieves a classification error rate about 2% higher, indicating stronger anti-steganalysis performance than current SOTA methods.

authors.name: Jialin Yan, Yu Cheng, Zhaoxia Yin, Xinpeng Zhang, Shilin Wang, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang

papers.title: Distributed Constraint-coupled Resource Allocation: Anytime Feasibility and Violation Robustness
papers.summary: This paper considers distributed resource allocation problems (DRAPs) with a coupled constraint for real-time systems. Based on primal-dual methods, we adopt a control perspective for optimization algorithm design by synthesizing a safe feedback controller using control barrier functions to enforce constraint satisfaction. On this basis, a distributed anytime-feasible resource allocation (DanyRA) algorithm is proposed. It is shown that the DanyRA algorithm converges to the exact optimal solution of DRAPs while preserving feasibility of the coupled inequality constraint from a feasible initialization. To address constraint violations caused by external disturbances, we develop a recover-after-violation mechanism using a virtual queue with a minimum buffer, enabling feasibility recovery within a prescribed number of iterations. We characterize the trade-off between convergence accuracy and violation robustness for a fixed positive buffer and establish exact convergence with a suitably decaying buffer. DanyRA is further specialized to coupled equality constraints, with constraint preservation and an explicit linear convergence rate established. Finally, a numerical example is provided for verification.

authors.name: Wenwen Wu, Shanying Zhu, Cailian Chen, Xinping Guan

papers.title: Industrial Viewpoints on RAN Technologies for 6G
papers.summary: Sixth-generation (6G) mobile systems have entered the standardization phase, with commercial deployments anticipated around 2030. This article presents an industrial perspective on the performance targets and key technologies shaping the 6G radio access network (RAN). It examines advances in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), artificial intelligence (AI), waveforms, channel coding, signal constellations, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), and the integration of terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs). Although detailed specification work is still ahead, the scope of the 6G studies has been defined and substantial technical progress has been made. We assess the emerging technologies and design choices from the perspectives of implementation complexity, computational and energy efficiency, interoperability, deployment feasibility, and migration from 5G. By connecting research advances with practical standardization and commercialization considerations, this article aims to inform researchers and industry practitioners developing the 6G RAN.

authors.name: Mansoor Shafi, Erik G. Larsson, Xingqin Lin, Dorin Panaitopol, Stefan Parkvall, Flavien Ronteix-Jacquet, Antti Toskala

papers.title: A Shared-Autonomy Construction Robotic System for Overhead Works
papers.summary: We present the ongoing development of a robotic system for overhead work such as ceiling drilling. The hardware platform comprises a mobile base with a two-stage lift, on which a bimanual torso is mounted with a custom-designed drilling end effector and RGB-D cameras. To support teleoperation in dynamic environments with limited visibility, we use Gaussian splatting for online 3D reconstruction and introduce motion parameters to model moving objects. For safe operation around dynamic obstacles, we developed a neural configuration-space barrier approach for planning and control. Initial feasibility studies demonstrate the capability of the hardware in drilling, bolting, and anchoring, and the software in safe teleoperation in a dynamic environment. Experiment videos and results are available at https://kmk9846.github.io/Construction-Robot/

authors.name: David Minkwan Kim, K. M. Brian Lee, Yong Hyeok Seo, Nikola Raicevic, Runfa Blark Li, Kehan Long, Chan Seon Yoon, Dong Min Kang, Byeong Jo Lim, Young Pyoung Kim, Nikolay Atanasov, Truong Nguyen, Se Woong Jun, Young Ouk Kim

papers.title: Cache-Aided Asymmetric MIMO Communications: Achievable DoF Analysis
papers.summary: Integrating coded caching (CC) into multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications significantly enhances the achievable degrees of freedom (DoF). This paper investigates a practical cache-aided asymmetric MIMO configuration with cache ratio $\gamma$, where a server with $L$ transmit antennas communicates with $K$ users. The users are partitioned into $J$ groups, and each user in group $j$ has $G_j$ receive antennas. We propose four content-aware MIMO-CC strategies: \emph{min-$G$} enforces symmetry using the smallest antenna count among users; \emph{Grouping} maximizes intra-subset spatial multiplexing gain at the expense of some global caching gain; \emph{Super-grouping} aggregates users into optimized \emph{min-$G$}-based super-sets with identical effective receive multiplexing gains before applying \emph{Grouping} across them; and \emph{Phantom} redistributes spatial resources assuming "phantom" antennas at the users to bridge the performance gains of \emph{min-$G$} and \emph{Grouping}. We develop these asymmetric strategies under three reference symmetric CC placement-delivery policies with guaranteed linear decodability: a finite-search DoF-optimized policy attaining the best single-shot achievable DoF lower bound, and two closed-form policies, namely combinatorial and linear cyclic low-complexity constructions, with the cyclic policy attaining DoF performance close to the others in many operating regimes. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate significant DoF improvements across various system configurations, and that policy-strategy combinations offer flexible trade-offs between DoF and subpacketization complexity.

authors.name: Mohammad NaseriTehrani, MohammadJavad Salehi, Antti T\"olli

papers.title: The generalized method of moments is (almost) statistically efficient in low-SNR Gaussian latent-variable models
papers.summary: We study estimation in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regime for a broad class of Gaussian latent-variable models, including Gaussian mixtures and orbit-recovery problems. We show that, in this regime, the generalized method-of-moments (GMoM) matches the first-order asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood. In particular, if the moment features are chosen up to the minimal local order required for identification and are weighted optimally, then the resulting GMoM estimator has the same leading asymptotic covariance as the maximum-likelihood estimator. We further show that this efficiency can be achieved using practical, data-driven weighting schemes and is preserved under a broad class of simpler weighting choices, including the commonly used identity-weighted method of moments, although these may incur larger higher-order efficiency losses. On the other hand, inappropriate weighting or discarding moment entries can lead to persistent efficiency losses even as SNR tends to zero, despite preserving identifiability. These results distinguish the moments required for identifiability from those needed for statistical efficiency, and characterize when moment-based estimation can match the performance of maximum likelihood.

authors.name: Amnon Balanov, Tamir Bendory, Dan Edidin

papers.title: Probabilistic Risk Sensitivity and Loss Aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory
papers.summary: This paper develops a binary-gamble framework for characterizing risk sensitivity and loss aversion in Cumulative Prospect Theory (CPT). The proposed probabilistic risk-sensitivity metric is defined as a probability-threshold ratio that determines acceptance and preference thresholds in choice problems involving either a certain outcome and a binary gamble or two binary gambles. We show how standard notions of symmetric and non-symmetric bet aversion can be recovered within this framework, and we compare the resulting threshold-based conditions with utility premia, probability premia, and Arrow-Pratt curvature measures. The analysis clarifies when these criteria coincide and when they diverge, particularly for increasing aversion conditions, binary gambles with unequal probability distributions, and settings involving probability weighting functions. We also identify technical restrictions that arise when CPT-utility functions are used to represent loss aversion at the reference point. The resulting framework provides a decision-theoretic interpretation of risk sensitivity that is directly tied to probability thresholds and complements existing premium-based approaches.

authors.name: Symeon Vaidanis, Marios Kountouris

papers.title: Supply Chain Networks: Equilibrium, Sensitivity, Dynamics and Shortage Games
papers.summary: We model production in a supply chain network in which every node sets a Newsvendor order target, upstream demand is the sum of downstream orders routed through a substochastic matrix, and every node has a capacity. The clearing vector of production quantities is the unique Nash equilibrium of the ordering game and the unique optimal solution of a linear program, and it has the form of the Eisenberg--Noe interbank clearing model. Nodes that produce their order target are hedged; the others are unhedged. We give comparative statics and a closed form for the stationary covariance of node demands. Inventory drawdown after a capacity shock is a Skorokhod reflection problem with a closed-form solution: the network and the unhedged nodes determine who is eventually rationed and by how much, and inventories determine when. When rationed nodes can inflate their orders, the equilibria never lower aggregate deliveries and can make suppliers with no physical shortage unhedged. With endogenous prices, a per-epoch price equilibrium exists and, under mild conditions, is unique when supply is price-elastic. We illustrate the model on global crude-oil trade.

authors.name: Elioth Sanabria

papers.title: Satellite Infrastructure Sharing: Orbit-Structured Stochastic Geometry Modeling and Connectivity Analysis in Heterogeneous Satellite Networks
papers.summary: This paper develops an analytical framework to evaluate the feasibility and performance of satellite infrastructure sharing among multiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite operators. Motivated by the growing demand for universal connectivity under limited satellite resources, the proposed model captures uncoordinated deployments where independently operated constellations coexist without predefined orbital agreements. To describe such heterogeneous configurations, the spherical Cox point process is employed to jointly generate orbital structures and satellites. Then, each satellite is further assigned a random communication range, reflecting variations in coverage capability across operators. The overall coverage region is modeled through a spherical Cox-Boolean model that captures the spatial overlap of individual satellite spherical footprints on Earth. Using the proposed framework, the feasibility and benefits of satellite infrastructure sharing are mathematically analyzed, and closed-form expressions are derived for key performance metrics such as the connection probability, connection number, and downlink signal characteristics including the nearest serving distance, total received signal power, and the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) distribution in the interference-limited regime. The analytical results, validated through system-level simulations, provide a tractable characterization of how orbital geometry governs coverage, connectivity, and interference, and reveal the inherent trade-offs induced by coverage overlap in heterogeneous satellite constellations.

authors.name: Chang-Sik Choi

papers.title: A complete characterization of sequential testability and change detectability in i.i.d. models
papers.summary: We give qualitative and quantitative necessary and sufficient conditions for sequential testing and change detection in an i.i.d. composite problem. A level-\(\alpha\) test with power one against every alternative exists if and only if the alternatives are separated from the null by a countable family of finite-block events. Equivalent conditions use randomized tests, bounded scores, e-processes, reduced-filtration test supermartingales, and a countable cover with positive finite-block weak-$*$ convex-hull separation. The construction gives pointwise expected sample size \(O_Q(\log(1/\alpha))\). Quantitatively, one e-process attains the intrinsic pointwise growth rate \(\Gamma(Q)\) at every alternative if and only if a countable family of bounded block bets recovers these rates. The same condition characterizes simultaneous attainment of the sharp expected-sample-size coefficient \(1/\Gamma(Q)\); arbitrary attainable lower rate profiles admit an analogous characterization. Total-variation separability of the alternatives suffices for recovery. Weak lower semicontinuity of the KL projection, in particular weak compactness of the null, also identifies \(\Gamma(Q)\) with \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)\). The qualitative and quantitative conditions also characterize change detectability under fixed-time false-alarm bounds \(\Prob_{P^\infty}(T_\gamma\le n)\le n/\gamma\), together with ordinary ARL control. Whenever countable rate recovery holds, for any \(\eta>0\) one calibrated e-detector has robust Lorden delay asymptotic to \((\log\gamma)/\Gamma(Q)\) at finite positive rates, while satisfying the stronger optional-horizon inequality and placing every null ARL in \([\gamma,(1+\eta)\gamma+1]\). Examples exhibit a strict cost of simultaneous optimality and show that ordinary ARL alone supports neither characterization, even with finite, tightly calibrated null means.

authors.name: Aaditya Ramdas

papers.title: The LQ Digital Mode Family: Protocol Architecture and Reference Specification for Weak-Signal Communications
papers.summary: This paper introduces LQ8, an open-source weak-signal digital mode for amateur radio that completes structured two-way contacts in 4 transmissions (60 s), achieving a 1.50x speedup over canonical 6-transmission exchanges (90 s) and 1.25x over 5-transmission RR73 exchanges (75 s) while preserving complete bidirectional exchange of Maidenhead grid locators, signal reports, and mutual acknowledgments. By replacing fixed-width message-type headers with variable-length prefix codes matched to physical-layer bit budgets, LQ8 packs the answering station's grid locator and measured signal report into a single 77-bit reply. In multi-station pileup operations, LQ8 confirms up to two answering stations simultaneously within a single-carrier 50.0 Hz transmission with a 0.0 dB RF power-splitting penalty, achieving a peak rate of 240 QSOs/h in continuous pileup (4x over single-carrier FT8; 480 QSOs/h dual-carrier) while retaining -21.0 dB SNR sensitivity. The protocol family also defines three extended profiles (LQ16, LQ4, and LQ2) tailored for extreme sensitivity, VHF/UHF contesting, and fast-burst channels.

authors.name: Luis Quesada

papers.title: Self-Distilled Pronunciation and Accent Control for Neural Text-to-Speech
papers.summary: Text-to-speech that reads raw text has no lexicon: a rare word is read as guessed, and a native Japanese listener accepts a word only if its reading and pitch accent are both right. A known remedy installs a reading-and-accent channel into a released model, but it needs many recordings. This paper removes the recordings: the frozen backbone reads a sentence containing a common word it already says correctly, and that output serves as the teacher for the same sentence with the word replaced by an annotated reading with its pitch accent. Screened raters judged the tag right on 0.80 to 0.93 of unseen difficult words on four backbones spanning autoregressive, diffusion, and encoder-decoder synthesis; plain kana, which cannot express an accent, got 0.38 to 0.60. On words needing no edit, naturalness is non-inferior on one backbone; on the other three, listeners prefer the unedited rendition by 0.19 to 0.26.

authors.name: Shuhei Kato

papers.title: A Bi-level Co-design Framework for Lunar Monoped with 2D Jump and Landing Control
papers.summary: Legged robots for lunar exploration must be designed for low gravity, where reduced contact forces and long flight phases make leg morphology and controller choice interdependent. We study this for a planar monoped in lunar gravity (1.625 m/s^2) using a bi-level co-design framework: a differential evolution outer loop searches over link lengths, and each candidate is evaluated on a vertical jump by either a quadratic program based task-space controller (QP-TSC) or a direct-collocation based trajectory optimization. The two controllers yield different optimal link lengths, and trajectory optimization outperforms the QP-TSC across most of the design space, with 17% lower Cost of Transport (COT) at their respective optima. We then extend to a 2D jump, where trajectory optimization with centroidal angular momentum regulation produces stable in-place and forward jumps, and an LQR controller absorbs impact and stabilizes the robot after touchdown. This is demonstrated on a baseline morphology with both links 0.3 m long.

authors.name: Sanjay Ramkumar, Suraj Kumar

papers.title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk. Asynchronous early inference can hide latency, but its results may be inconsistent with the arriving actual inputs. Unconditional reuse risks acting on mismatched inputs, whereas full recomputation discards useful precomputation. We propose SR-VLA, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair. During current chunk execution, a lightweight action-conditioned predictor generates next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state. These predictions, together with the task instruction, drive the frozen VLA to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk. After real inputs are available to VLA, predicted--real differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the action chunk or trigger selective KV repair. On LIBERO, SR-VLA achieves $2.67\times$ and $1.27\times$ query speedups over the respective synchronous $\pi_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA-OFT baselines, while maintaining competitive average task success rates. Under target-motion perturbation, success remains baseline-comparable, with $1.52\times$--$1.93\times$ query speedup.

authors.name: Tao Zhang, Yi Zhong, Jinhao Ruan, Yipeng Gao, Linfeng Zhong, Youming Yang, Yuan Wang
